    Chapter 1

    Let's grab a drink, huh?

    Kate Bishop sat hunched over on a bar stool, brow furrowed in concentration, as she tapped intently at her phone. She wasn’t going to let him slip away from her this time. The bar was quiet as it was approaching last orders, and most of Hell’s Kitchen’s financial, political and criminal elite had already decided to call it a night. A few waiting staff were buzzing back and forth from behind the bar and the clinking of crystal punctuated the muted jazz that was in constant battle with the building’s air conditioning, as tables were emptied of empty glasses and unfinished cocktails. Kate had been considering a quick fingered minesweep, but shit had got serious on her phone. Her app pulsed and she crinkled her nose in frustration.

    She glanced up for a moment to see the man in the booth across the bar ordering himself, what she presumed, was one last drink. Of course, he’s going to be here till close, of course he is . Kate sighed and quickly took another sip of her diminishing margarita. At least her evening hadn’t been a total write-off, soon she will have claimed another glorious victory over the dastardly Team Valor. A determined frown darkened her features as she glanced back down to her phone and considered her next move.

    Without a moment’s notice, hot breath tickled the sensitive skin at back of her neck and a warm and accented voice spoke softly into her ear. ‘A woman as beautiful as yourself shouldn’t be drinking alone in a place like this.’ It was safe to say that Kate Bishop almost fell out of her stool.

    Clutching her proverbial pearls, Kate swung around to catch sight of the assailant who had just made a successful attempt upon her social clout. Of course, Kate didn’t have to lay eyes on her ego’s attacker in order to identify her as Yelena Belova, Black Widow, Hot Sauce lover and Assassin Extraordinaire. She’d recognise those dulcet tones anywhere, and weirdly, that scent too. Huh . But that didn’t mean that she’d been prepared for them. Part of her had worried that she’d never see Yelena again, part of her wondered if that was for the best.

    ‘Oh my God, Yelena, where did you come from?’ Kate asked, whilst desperately trying to collect the shattered fragments of her ego and hastily piece them back together. She was an Avenger, now, and it really shouldn’t be that easy to sneak up on an Avenger. Well, an Avenger in training.

    Yelena shrugged with her trademark nonchalance. ‘Istanbul.’

    Kate blinked. ‘No, I mean where did -’

    A smile pulled at the corner of Yelena’s lips and her eyes danced brightly, despite their dimly lit surroundings. ‘Some things should remain a mystery don’t you think?’

    Kate wanted to disagree, fiercely. She wanted to tell her friend (were they even friends?) that no, some things should not at all remain a mystery. Sometimes friends should tell their other friends that they might be disappearing for six months, and if they were planning on doing so, perhaps they should leave a forwarding address, or set up a private insta so they could follow them daily and share funny, intimate anecdotes by DM.

    ‘Well, you are very mysterious,’ Kate offered, as a slightly less hysterical sounding alternative, ‘So this whole appearing out of nowhere thing is very on brand for you’.

    ‘Thank you,’ Yelena smirked, ‘But really I just walked through those double doors.’ The blonde gestured to the bar’s main entryway.

    Kate scoffed, there was no way. No way. Kate was perceptive as they come, she refused to believe Yelena hadn’t used some kind of subterfuge to gain entry into the bar. She was an international assassin after all. ‘No, you didn’t, I would have seen you.’

    ‘The doors just over there. The really big ones that you can see in the mirror behind the bar, you really didn’t see me?’

    Kate had to consider her position here. Continue to protest that there was no way in hell Yelena had entered through the plebs entrance, concede that perhaps she’d been a little too into her phone whilst she was on a job, or deny all knowledge of the doors whatsoever. ‘I don’t know what doors you’re talking about.’ She went with the latter. Perhaps a poor choice.

    ‘They’re big and gold.’ Yelena continued, incredulously, but Kate simply looked at her, blankly. The younger woman had made her position quite clear; she’d had her bed, and now she would have to lay in it. ‘Maybe,’ Yelena continued, taking a step closer to the Bishop heir, ‘You would have seen me come in if you weren’t playing Pokemon Go.’

    Busted.

    ‘I wasn’t playin-’ Kate began to protest, but within a blink of an eye, Yelena had snatched Kate’s phone out of her hand and was holding it up to her as proof of her claims. Indeed, Kate had been playing Pokémon Go, and indeed, she’d probably spent more dollar on Pokécoins than she had on cocktails since entering one of the priciest bars in Hell’s Kitchen.

    Kate flailed helplessly, trying to reclaim her phone, but the Russian was too quick. ‘This place is a gym, okay?’ she tried to explain, unaware that she was almost certainly making the situation worse. ‘And some little Valor shit, PikachuIzMaBish, keeps kicking me off top spot.’

    A stifled laugh escaped the blonde, clearly amused by Kate’s fiery vitriol, and that it had been brought on by what Yelena undoubtedly thought was a dumb game for children. The brunette huffed in response; her passion for Pokémon was something Yelena could never truly appreciate. ‘If you played it, you’d understand, now give it back I need to replenish my potions before the next battle.’

    Yelena deftly avoided another vain attempt from Kate to regain her phone. ‘Don’t you have anything to say?’

    ‘Like what?’ Kate frowned, in frustration. If she knew the magic words that would coerce Yelena into giving her phone back, she would have said them by now.

    ‘Oh, I don’t know,’ Yelena began, an eyebrow raised and her voice thick with sarcasm. ‘Hi Yelena, how have you been? You look nice and healthy. I’ve missed you deeply.’ She rested one hand upon her hip, whilst the other was still clutched tightly around Kate’s Pokédex, and to her credit, Yelena really did look pretty nice and rather healthy. Considering the heat had been in the nineties that day, the blonde didn't look as if she’d broken a sweat making her way through the still bustling streets of New York City.

    If Yelena confiscating her phone hadn’t been so ridiculously irritating, Kate would have even considered complimenting her on her outfit; a plain loose black blouse, a pair of not so unreasonably tight Blackwatch tartan trousers, some chunky oxblood Chelsea boots, and several golden t-bar chains that hung rather audaciously round her neck. Kate found herself wondering if they shared the same shoe size. Considering she was currently looking down at the woman in front of her, it seemed unlikely. Tragic.

    ‘Not really, I just want to play…’ Kate reached again for the phone, one too many times for Yelena's liking, who swiftly placed it in her canvas backpack.

    ‘Nope. Pikachu is my bitch now.’ Yelena said, with a no-nonsense smirk.

    ‘Oh, come on,’ Kate hissed quietly, with a quick glance to the gentleman in the booth. He seemed unperturbed.

    Yelena shook her head with an unforgiving smile. This was a battle Kate wasn’t going to win, she knew she had to play ball. Sadly, she would be forced to concede the gym to Valor that night. You’ve may have won the battle Valor, but you will not win the war.

    ‘Fine, fine. Hi Yelena. Where have you been the last six months? You left without saying goodbye. What are you doing here?’

    ‘Oh, thank you so much for asking, Kate Bishop,’ Yelena responded, her words dripping with sarcasm, ‘But I didn’t realise your ego was so fragile.’ Kate heard the smaller woman mumble a protest about not saying goodbye under her breath before continuing. ‘You went to Missouri out of nowhere,’.

    ‘Wait,’ How does she know about Missouri? ‘How do you know about that?’ She shouldn’t know about Missouri. No one should know about Missouri.

    ‘And I text you, which you left on read by the way.’ Oh shit, I did do that.

    ‘Only for a week.’ A week is bad.

    ‘And if you must know, after a few more days sightseeing, alone ,’ Kate cringed at the thought, ‘I went home to spend Christmas with my family.’

    'Were they pissed that you were so late?’

    ‘We celebrate Christmas in January, dumb ass’.

    ‘Oh. Like in Russia or just your family?’ Kate asked, naively. Yelena didn’t dignify the question with a response.

    ‘But now, seeing as I’m back in New York City, I thought it was time to collect on what is owed.’ Yelena’s eyes narrowed mischievously and Kate swallowed nervously.

    ‘Collect? You’re not here to kill me this time are you?’

    ‘No, you would be dead by now if I were,’ Yelena smiled, sweetly. Kate knew that was 100% true.

    ‘I can’t argue with that’.

    ‘No, no,’ The blonde shrugged off the suggestion jovially. ‘There will be no killing, just drinking. And I believe that you, Kate Bishop, owe me a drink.’ Yelena pointed in Kate’s direction, raised an expectant eyebrow and punctuated her claim with a wink.

    ‘I do?’ Kate frowned.

    ‘Yes, at the party you said, let’s grab a drink’.

    ‘That was back in December. It’s July…’ And Kate was pretty sure that they had vacated the party by that point. Less of a party, more of a fist fight.

    Yelena pouted a little. ‘So, you no longer desire my company? I see.’

    ‘No, no, no, I just…’ Kate waved her hands, to emphasise how much she meant the word no. Of course, she wanted to spend time with Yelena. She’d been weirdly craving the older woman’s company since they’d shared a saucepan of Mac and Cheese together in her burned-out apartment last December, but in that moment, at that bar, really was not the time or place; and not because of Pokémon Go.

    ‘Look it’s nice to see you,’ Kate continued, hoping beyond hope that Yelena would believe her. ‘It really is but, I’m here tailing someone okay? And I’m trying to be inconspicuous.’

    Yelena’s pout quickly turned into a sceptical smirk as she hopped effortlessly up onto the tall barstool that was opposite Kate’s. ‘You are trying to be inconspicuous?’

    ‘Yeah, you know...‘ Kate mirrored her friend but instead leaned easily back onto her stool. ‘It means- ‘

    ‘I know what inconspicuous means, but you and your Pokémons are not the definition of it.’

    Kate scoffed. ‘You don’t what you’re talking about. I’m just a single girl, chillaxing at her favourite cocktail bar.’ Yelena tried to smother a laugh, unsuccessfully. Kate tried not to let Yelena’s obvious amusement derail her. ‘I’m in my favourite Levis, sipping on a marg whilst blasting little kids with my baby Arcanine. I am the epitome of inconspicuous.’

    ‘Firstly, never say chillaxing in my company ever again,’ Yelena visibly shivered, but couldn’t hide the smile that was creeping across her face. ‘Secondly, you, alone, are far more conspicuous than you with company, especially dressed like this.’

    ‘Dressed like what?!’ Kate found herself hissing, again. What was that supposed to mean?’ These were her favourite Levi’s because they were so comfortable and she was happy to admit, made her ass look great too. So what if she was in a fancy bar? Really, what was Yelena’s problem?

    ‘Thirdly, have they not taught you anything at S.H.I.E.L.D.?’

    How did she know about S.H.I.E.L.D.? Come to think about it, how did she know about everything that she knows? Was there a mole in Kate’s life? Someone on the inside? Maybe Yelena got to Lucky. Oh no, not Lucky. ‘How do you know about S.H.I.E.L.D.?’

    ‘How do you think I knew that you were chillaxing in this very cocktail bar?’ Fuck, how did she know that?

    ‘Well…’ Kate thought, she may as well tell the truth, seeing as Yelena knew she was at this very bar, then it stood to reason she knew why Kate was there. ‘I’m not exactly on S.H.I.E.L.D. business’.

    ‘No shit.’ Yep, called it. ‘Then what are you here for?’ Yelena asked, innocently with a flutter of her eyelashes. Oh yeah, she knew.

    ‘This is a favour for a friend’.

    ‘Hmm. This friend. Can you be linked to them?’ Yelena asked.

    ‘No.’ Kate answered, a little too hastily. The Russian gave her a sceptical look. ‘Maybe…we have mutual friends. Why?’

    ‘Because the guy you’re tailing, the one in the booth,’ Yelena nodded towards the guy drinking alone, the one Kate had been keeping tabs on well before the blonde had arrived. ‘He made you five minutes ago.’

    ‘What?!’ Kate asked in a panicked whisper. ‘You weren’t even here five minutes ago.’

    ‘If you believe that than you’re not nearly as smart as I thought.’ Kate frowned. She didn’t know whether to take that as an insult or a compliment. ‘But don’t worry, he’s only suspicious, for now’.

    ‘Shit,’ Kate shook her head with worry and sighed. ‘I can’t screw this up, I promised her I could do this.’

    ‘Are you a trained super spy?’ Yelena asked.

    ‘Not yet.’ Kate shifted a little self-consciously on her stool. Sure, she was an Avenger in training, and yes, she’d been giving it everything she had, but with all her prior experience, there were still areas that she found herself lacking. Most areas really. It was a little hard to admit when sat facing the best fighter she’d ever been punched in the face by.

    ‘Then don’t put too much pressure on yourself, okay?’ Yelena smiled, earnestly, and some of those creeping self-doubts seemed to recede, ever so slightly. ‘Luckily for you,’ the blonde grinned, ‘The best super spy in the world just walked through those double doors and at this very moment, she would do pretty much anything for a drink.’

    'If only you were this agreeable last time, we could have avoided all that drama.’

    Yelena simply ignored Kate’s swipe and continued. ‘You have two options. Make him look or make him look away.’

    Kate frowned. She needed to know more. ‘Could you elaborate, please, for the room?’

    ‘Of course, Kate Bishop. Option one, make him look. Draw attention to yourself, a tail wouldn’t do that.’

    ‘That sounds like a terrible idea, what’s option two’.

    ‘Option two is to make him look away, to convince him that he must have been mistaken, that he is the one prying into your life.’ Kate looked down as she felt rough but tactile fingertips graze gently against her own, before they captured her hand and raised it to their keeper’s lips. Yelena placed a soft, gentle kiss atop of Kate’s knuckles and smiled affectionately. To Kate’s surprise, the blonde’s smile reached her eyes, that again, looked as though they were dancing in the soft mood lighting. Kate’s stomach flip flopped at Yelena’s touch and she found that her words had, quite worryingly, become lodged irretrievably in her throat. Something she very quickly explained away as a very understandable reaction to being blindsided by Yelena’s ultimately fake but very convincing show of affection. The Russian gave Kate’s hand one more gentle kiss before leaning towards the bar keep, her eyes only momentarily leaving Kate’s. ‘I’ll take a White Russian please, on the rocks,’ she asked, and then her eyes were back on Kate’s, and they were saying play along dipshit .

    ‘Seriously?’ Kate whispered, once her frontal left cortex had rediscovered its connection with her vocal cords, ‘A White Russian?’ This was the only thing she was protesting. Not the other thing. Not the other thing at all.

    Yelena simply narrowed her eyes. ‘Indulge me.’ It wasn’t a request, she was telling Kate that she could trust her, that she knew exactly what she was doing, and that she was going to get a free drink out of it.

    Kate gave her friend a small and nearly imperceptible nod, and told the bar keep to ‘Put it on my tab’, without taking her eyes off of Yelena. ‘This is feeling a lot more like option one,’ the brunette whispered, as she imagined the gaze of nearly every pair of eyes left in the bar fall upon her and Yelena.

    The blonde smiled and leant forward, further into Kate’s personal space. Kate supposed to wasn’t the first time they’d both got a little too close for comfort, but this felt very, very different. Yelena lowered her voice and spoke in hushed tones and her breath once again tickled the soft skin of Kate’s neck. Kate considered this extremely unfair but also oddly comforting. ‘One thing that terrifies guys like that more than anything else; real life women who don’t need men for any sexual or emotional satisfaction. They love to watch on their little iPhones and get off but this,’ Yelena kissed Kate ever so gently on the cheek, ‘This is enough to make them very uncomfortable.’

    ‘Errr.’ Frontal. Lobe. Connection. Lost.

    ‘And you apparently.’

    ‘I’m not uncomfortable.’

    Yelena smiled, wryly. ‘Sure,’ she said, but thankfully didn’t tease Kate any further. ‘Is he looking over anymore?’

    Kate glanced nervously in the direction of her mark, but to her surprise, he was now turned with his back to the couple. A surprised ‘Huh,’ escaped the brunette. ‘He now appears to be staring intently at the cocktail menu.’

    Yelena smiled a smug and slightly deranged smile. ‘Hmm, he is terrified.’ She was taking great pleasure in her victory.

    ‘Are you going to let go of my hand now?’ Kate asked, glancing down at fingers that were still laced together.

    ‘What if he looks back over?’ Yelena said, matter-of-factly. Kate had a sneaking suspicion that Yelena was also taking great pleasure in pushing her buttons. Yelena did like to play, that was for sure.

    'Well then, I’d just have to jump you.’ Two can play at that game Yelena Belova, Kate thought, determined to a, prove she wasn’t uncomfortable, it would take more than a little flirting to ruffle her proverbial feathers, and b, show Yelena that she could push back, that she could play too.

    Yelena simply grinned. ‘I’d like to see you try Kate Bishop, but you are learning.’

    Kate blinked. ‘You know what jump means, right?’

    ‘One White Russian,’ came the bar keeps voice, ‘On the rocks.’ Yelena’s eyes lit up as an incredibly decadent looking cocktail, served up in an Old Fashioned glass and poured over ice, was delicately placed in front of her, on a branded paper coaster.

    ‘Ooh thank you,’ the blonde beamed, ‘This looks good,’ she sang excitedly as she shimmied a little atop her stool. Kate couldn’t help but smile at the extremely likeable contradiction in front of her. World’s most dangerous assassin gets giddy over some of life’s simplest things. Mac and cheese, hot sauce, fist fights, vodka, Kahlúa and cream.

    Yelena took a slow first sip of her cocktail. Her eyes closed momentarily, trying to block out all her other senses in an attempt to savour the fleeting moment the rich and alcohol laden liquid danced happily across her tongue. A little moan of pleasure escaped the blonde and her hand tightened, almost imperceptibly around Kate’s. Kate wondered if Yelena had even noticed she’d done it.

    ‘That is a good White Russian,’ Yelena declared, her happiness evident.

    ‘This is a great bar, what can I say?’

    ‘Did you know that White Russians aren't Russian at all?’ Yelena asked. ‘They just call them that because they have vodka in?’

    ‘I did not know that. What is the world coming to?’ Kate shook her head in faux dismay.

    ‘I know!’ Yelena threw her spare hand in the air, dramatically, joining in Kate’s admonishment. ‘Americans,’ she muttered afterwards, which earned her an eye-roll from Kate.

    ‘So,’ the brunette began, ‘Did you come all the way from Istanbul for some russki cocktail?’ This earned Kate an eye-roll and a sarcastic, ha , but the dig was worth it, and also, she really did want to know what had brought Yelena back to New York City. It couldn’t have just been to collect on a drink that was owed. That would have been one really expensive drink, for Yelena and for the Amazon Rainforest.

    ‘Would you believe me if I told you I came to see you?’ Yelena asked, eyebrow raised.

    ‘No. Not at all actually.’ Kate replied, smoothly. She wasn’t going to allow herself to be fooled, especially by such an obvious set up. That wasn’t to say that secretly she was maybe hoping the answer would be yes. World’s greatest assassin travels half the world to come and see you and it’s NOT to take your life? Seems like a pretty exclusive club to be in.

    But Yelena smiled, and let Kate down softly. ‘You would be correct. It’s a nice thought though, isn’t it?’

    Dammit, this woman can read my mind. ‘No,’ Kate said, a little too quickly, as a tiny stubborn frown turned her smile upside down, and she dragged her eyes from Yelena’s. A soft touch and rough fingertips turned her face back towards the blonde, Kate told herself that Yelena was almost certainly still in character. Gotta keep up that façade.

    ‘Do you not want to know why I am here?’ Yelena asked, like butter wouldn’t melt.

    ‘Nope. Not at all. I have absolutely no desire to be complicit in your next pay per kill’.

    The Russian grinned knowingly. ‘Then you will be pleased to know that’s not what brings me to New York.’

    Kate blinked in surprise, and maybe a little in disappointment. ‘Oh, and it’s not me?’

    ‘No. In fact, I had a job interview.’ Yelena explained, proudly.

    ‘Oh… I didn’t know assassins had job interviews,’ Kate said, facetiously.

    Yelena rolled her eyes. ‘No assassinations. Similar set of skills, different outcome.’

    Kate’s eyes grew wide and she suddenly gripped Yelena’s hand in excitement. ‘Oh my god, are you going into bounty hunting? Love that journey for you.’

    Yelena scoffed, with absolute disdain. ‘No, fuck that.'

    ‘Why not?’ Kate asked, slightly taken a back and perhaps just a little insulted. ‘What’s wrong with bounty hunting?’

    ‘What’s wrong with bounty hunting?’ Yelena responded incredulously. ‘Did you just ask what’s wrong with bounty hunting? What isn’t wrong with it? Bounty hunters are the worst. Have you ever met one?’

    ‘I…I’ it was at this moment Kate knew; she’d fucked up. ‘I don’t think so...’ She winced, preparing for the inevitable tirade, which came, like an avalanche.

    ‘God, they’re so pretentious. In my line of work, it’s all about the job. Nothing else matters. But with bounty hunters, it’s all about the brand.’ Kate nodded and hmmd her agreement, it seemed like the safest thing to do. ‘It’s all about them and their clothes and their sunglasses and their hats and their cars and their websites and their Instagrams. Who is this Mr Dog Hunter hmm? Does he not hunt people?’

    ‘Dog the Bounty Hunter, have you met him!?’ Kate might have let her momentary excitement get the better of her, but Yelena didn’t seem to mind, it simply gave her more ammunition.

    ‘No! And if I did that would end badly for him. He is all talk, all bullshit. Blah blah, tv show blah. Do you think an assassin could have a TV show?’

    ‘Pfft, no,’ Kate agreed, animatedly. What were friends for?

    ‘Do you think an assassin would announce that they are coming for you on the TikTok? They wouldn’t make very good assassins.’ To Yelena’s credit, she was making a lot of fair points, if not rather dramatically.

    ‘Wow. I did not know you felt this way. This is awkward. I’m going to have to return that Dog the Bounty Hunter calendar I bought for your-’ Yelena gently smacked Kate on the arm and the pair laughed together.

    ‘Cyka,’ the blonde grumbled, with a teasing frown.

    ‘Hey, look, I thought he was your kinda guy.’

    ‘Shut up,’ Yelena smirked into her White Russian, as she took another sip.

    ‘So,’ Kate begun, whilst trying to tear the massive grin from her face, ‘If you’re not here for nefarious reasons, then why are you here?’

    ‘Well…’ Yelena took a pause, for dramatic effect, which Kate appreciated. ‘I actually had a meeting with your bosses today.’

    Bosses. By bosses, did Yelena mean S.H.I.E.L.D.? She couldn’t have meant S.H.I.E.L.D. The idea of Yelena agreeing to even meet with an American Government agency was laughable, let alone the Government agency that so famously turned against her sister. ‘Voluntarily?’ Kate asked.

    ‘Uh huh,’ Yelena confirmed, nonchalantly. Okay, maybe not so laughable.

    ‘You… working with S.H.I.E.L.D.?’

    ‘Well, that bit is up to you. And please, at least try a little harder to hide your scepticism. I can play nice when I want to.’

    ‘Uh huh, like you played nice with me?’ Kate prodded.

    Yelena gasped a little, offended. ‘I do play nice with you; I am very nice with you. Which is why they want me to team up with you, to help you.’

    ‘W...what?’ Kate stuttered. Yelena, at S.H.I.E.L.D., with her, every day? This evening had taken a turn, and it was rather wonderful. Yelena, back in her life. Learning from Yelena, working with Yelena, fighting with Yelena, goofing off with Yelena, sharing food with Yelena, buying drinks for Yelena, holding hands with-. No, scrap that last one.

    ‘I said I’d only considered it for you,’ Yelena explained, and took another sip of vodka, cream and coffee liqueur, cool as you like whilst Kate’s brain was quickly turning to mush. ‘Not for anyone else.’ The brunette felt a heat rise in her cheeks; she was blushing. Good lord she was blushing.

    ‘We would be partners?' Kate’s excitement was showing.

    ‘And we could train, regularly, because my god you are rough around the edges.’

    ‘Ignoring that malicious slander, bit of a leap, isn’t it? Red Room to S.H.I.E.L.D.?’ Kate asked.

    ‘S.H.I.E.L.D. has its benefits,’ The blonde offered with a smile, and Kate was struck with the inescapable thought that Yelena was maybe, just maybe, referring to her. Yep, she was still blushing alright. Thank goodness the cocktail bar’s lighting could be described as moody. ‘And besides, it’s...’ Yelena continued, only to pause and catch herself. She swallowed, as a flicker of sadness crossed her warm and jovial features. She was searching for the words, for different words, words that weren’t, it’s what Natasha would have wanted. Kate found herself gently squeezing Yelena’s hand as the Russian looked up at her with a small smirk. ‘You guys have a lot of cool shit.’ She’d found the words, and so Kate doubled down. That’s what friends were for.

    ‘Oh my god, the amount of cool shit. Yelena, you would not believe. They’re legit letting me work on this trick arrow that delivers nano technol-’

    ‘You probably shouldn’t tell me that,’ Yelena cut her off quickly, with a laugh. ‘I haven’t accepted the job yet.’

    ‘Oh,’ Of course, Kate had got ahead of herself. She was one of the world’s greatest archers for sure, one of the world’s greatest adults, not so much, and to say she was easily excitable was one of the world’s greatest understatements. But surely if Yelena wasn’t taking the job she wouldn’t be sitting here now, right? Unless this was all just a big fuck you. You kicked my ass, so now I’m going to kick your heart into a thousand pieces kind of thing. Of course, Kate hadn’t really kicked Yelena’s ass, but selective memory is a funny thing. ‘But you will accept it… right?’ Kate asked, hoping to high water that her voice didn’t sound as desperate to Yelena as she did to herself.

    Yelena nodded her head, side to side, as if weighing something up. As if working out how much needed to be said, how much she needed to reveal, and how much Kate deserved to hear. A little exhale told Kate that she had settled upon something, and the little frown that worried the blonde’s brow told Kate that she was determined to say it. ‘I haven’t accepted yet because I think you should get a say in who you partner up with.’ Their eyes met, and Yelena’s were dark, darker than they were a few moments earlier. ‘You should get a say about who trains you, who you learn from. My entire life for nearly twenty years was training. Not once did someone ask me what I wanted. How best I learned, what I enjoyed and what I didn’t, or if I wanted to train at all. No one asked me if I wanted to be a killer. I never had choice. I would like to give you the choice I never had, Kate; it shouldn’t be prescribed to you.’

    Wow . That was pretty much the only thought that Kate could muster. Just wow. She looked down at their hands clasped together, her thumb was soothingly moving across Yelena’s knuckles. Yelena hadn’t seemed to noticed. Neither had Kate.

    She’d known a little about Yelena’s time with the Red Room, as Clint had filled in a couple of blanks for her since December prior, but hearing it from Yelena, in her voice, in her own words, really put into perspective what a remarkable young woman she was. A young woman with strength that Kate could only dream of, with courage she could only admire, let alone aspire to have, and an empathy that most people would lose after living just a day in her shoes. To learn from Yelena, to have the chance to emulate her, that was everything that Kate wanted. It was like Christmas in July.

    ‘Yelena, of course I’d choose you! I mean, we’re a good fit right?’ Yelena raised an eyebrow, ‘We have fun,’ and smirked sceptically. ‘I’m the funny one, you’re the serious one, like a proper double act. Apart from the assassin thing, you’re pretty much everything I wish I could be.’ Kate realised that her excitement was getting the better of her again, and perhaps after such a heartfelt admission from Yelena, Kate should follow it up with one of her own. ‘It would be the privilege of my life to have you as my partner and to learn from you, thank you for giving me the choice.’ And she meant it.

    ‘Eh,’ Yelena shrugged, ‘Most of the killing was whilst brain washed anyway. And I’m pretty sure I’m the funny one.’

    ‘You were BRAINWASHED!?’ Kate gasped.

    ‘Yes,’ replied Yelena, matter-of-factly. ‘When I was working for the red-‘

    ‘THAT IS SO COO-’. The blonde raised a silencing eyebrow and Kate caught herself. ‘Awful. That is so awful. How could they dream of taking of advantage of you in that way. I’m so angry for you. Is there someone I can write an angry letter to?’ Smooth Kate, you styled that out.

    ‘No, they are all dead now,’ Yelena said, with another dispassionate shrug and a sip of her cocktail. Talk about styling it out.

    ‘Wow, okay. You are a badass.’

    ‘Thank you. You have a lot of badass potential.’

    Kate grinned at the compliment. ‘You really think so?’

    ‘I do.’ Yelena smiled, earnestly, and Kate felt as though she might faint. This was almost as good as the time Clint conceded she was a pretty great archer, almost.

    ‘Then it would be an honour to be your partner and padawan. Just to clarify, you won’t be my boss, right?’ Kate asked, her nose scrunched in a sign of displeasure.

    ‘Unsure,’ Yelena shrugged.

    ‘Because this right here,’ Kate gestured subtly to their entwined fingers. ‘Feels like an HR- able offence.’

    Yelena rolled her eyes. ‘It worked, didn’t it?’ And just like that, they were back to where they started. Being pricks to each other.

    Kate stole a glance towards the booth where her mark had been sitting. The empty booth in which her mark had been sitting. Fuck . ‘Wait…He’s gone!’ He can’t be gone. This was a disaster. This was the first time Jenn had asked her to do anything remotely interesting, and she was about to fuck it all up.

    ‘Oh, yeah’ Yelena said, coolly. ‘He left a while ago. This,’ she waved her and Kate’s clasped hands into the air goofily, ‘Was super effective.’

    ‘What?! Why didn’t you tell me?’ Kate practically yelped with exasperation.

    ‘Would I be a very good teacher if I held your hand through every test? Figuratively speaking of course.’

    ‘But he’s gone!’ Kate was quickly regretting agreeing to work with Yelena, quickly regretting buying her a drink and quickly regretting thinking she looked pretty hot in her outfit.

    ‘This is your first lesson. Don’t let pretty things distract you.’ The smugness that was Yelena’s face made Kate want to burn the entire cocktail bar to the ground. Fuck that, the entire block.

    ‘I wasn’t distracted,’ Kate managed, through gritted teeth. ‘You were talking to me and you are not pretty.’

    ‘Wow,’ Why did I say that? Kate thought, as Yelena rather dramatically extracted her hand from Kate’s. ‘That cuts deep Kate Bishop. Maybe I should just get on my plane and fly home to my Mamma and Pappa.’

    ‘No, no,’ appealed Kate, panicked. Yelena simply smiled mischievously, she was taking a lot of pleasure in Kate’s miniature meltdown. ‘Look, you’re super-hot but I’m mad at you, okay?’

    ‘You should be mad at yourself,’ Yelena said, plainly. And although incredibly stubborn, Kate couldn’t help but agree.

    ‘Okay, it’s all my fault, can we move on? What do we do now?’ Kate asked.

    ’Lesson number two, if all else fails, smile and play dumb.’ Yelena dropped this solution on Kate’s lap as if she’d just dropped the mic.

    ‘Is that it? I’m actually really good at that.’ Kate didn’t feel as if this was something she should be proud of, but it really was quite the talent.

    ‘You don’t say,’ Yelena quipped, before she turned to the bar keep, inviting him to join their conversation, a conversion Kate didn’t know they’d been having, as if it was the most natural thing in the world. ‘Yes, it was the guy in the booth who just left, I swear he lives in our building. Don’t you recognise him darling?’ she asked, as she turned back to Kate.

    Kate blinked for a moment. Darling. Who’s darling? You’re darling dipshit, came Yelena’s voice from inside her own head. Kate quickly caught up and determined that she’d better join the rouse or risk blowing it. ‘He looked a little familiar, but I can’t place him, babe.’

    ‘We’re up at 62 nd ’ Yelena explained, leaning her body back towards the bar keep ever so slightly. For someone who could kill you with a paper clip, she sure knew how to be charming. Her body language manipulation was off the charts good.

    ‘Nah,’ said the bar keep, whilst polishing down the bar before them. ‘I think he’s down towards Penn, comes here a few nights a week and heads out same way every time.’

    ‘That’s so weird, he looks so familiar,’ Yelena said, smiling and playing dumb. ‘Ah well, so much for serendipity. I suppose we should be leaving; it’s closing time after all and you probably want to get on home.’ Yelena caught Kate’s eyes and glanced subtly towards the door. It looked as if their night wasn’t going to end there. They were going on a little adventure. Their first mission. Together. As partners. Kate could feel the excitement begin to build in her again, she was going to learn so much fucking good stuff.

    ‘Thank you so much for the cocktail, it was wonderful, truly.’

    ‘No problem,’ the bar keep beamed. ‘Remind you of home?’

    ‘No, the Big Lebowski.’ The bar keep couldn’t hide his confusion as Yelena hopped down from the dizzying heights of her bar stool, swung her backpack across her shoulder and made towards the big gold double doors. ‘Can you grab the bill, darling?’ She called back to Kate, ‘I’ll fetch the bike round.’

    ‘Darling, that’s me,’ Kate pointed to herself with pride, just to make sure there were no misunderstandings. Yelena was her fake girlfriend. Hers. And her partner, and teacher and probably soon to be best friend.

    But wait... ‘Did she say bike?!’

    B&E, Vodka and Ice Cream Chapter Summary Kate and Yelena track their mark to his apartment, where they put their newly formed partnership to the test.

    Kate sums it up pretty well. B&E, vodka and ice cream.

Absolutely not. ‘Come on Kate, just pull the cushions out. You can do, I believe in you. It’s the last place to check. Remember your friend...?’

    But Yelena had been right. In amongst the hair and the dust bunnies, the crumbs and the suspicious substances, was a small, red burner phone. ‘Ha ha!’ Kate exclaimed, throwing her hands in the air in celebration.

    ‘Well then, Kate Bishop, seasoned B and E master’ Yelena said, laughter still thick in her voice,, with one hand on the handlebars of her scrambler, the other on her hip, ‘Where to next?’

    ‘First thing’s first, I should probably drop this to Jen.’

    ‘Probably,’ Yelena agreed, ‘But also, you probably shouldn’t tell anyone else her name.’ Ignoring her clear and obvious error, Kate continued. ‘And theeeen, there’s this cute little ice cream place just down from her apartment.’

    ‘Ice cream?’ Yelena’s eyes lit up. Kate made a mental note to try and replicate that as much as possible too.

    ‘Uh huh,’ Kate said, with a grin. She was getting excited again, and why not? ‘And I’m talking gelato, sorbets, sundaes, dairy free stuff, sprinkles, hot caramel, chocolate, marshmallows. This shit is the real deal.’

    Yelena sighed, dreamily and Kate made another mental note. ‘You know what? I have a feeling that this is going to be a beautiful relationship.’

    They were both sat on Yelena’s bike, feet firmly on the sidewalk, faces lit by the bright lights of Amorinos ‘No,’ Yelena scolded, as she knocked Kate’s spoon away with her own for the second time. ‘But the rum and raisin is really good,’ Kate appealed, and she was not wrong. The rum and raisin was the third best flavour at Amorinos.

    Yelena shrugged. She gave zero fucks. ‘If you wanted it so badly, you should have gotten your own.’

    ‘But I didn’t need a third scoop,’ Kate explained. Surely Yelena could see sense here. Kate only wanted a taste. ‘I just need a little... If I could just...’ Kate made a third attempt on the rum and raisin but Yelena deftly batted her away once more. Kate frowned and threw out her lower lip for good measure. ‘I thought we shared food.’

    ‘My mother always taught me to say please and thank you,’ Yelena warned, ‘But I suppose your mother was just used to taking what she wanted.’

    Okay, okay, Kate got it. She was being called out and she was being called spoiled. Yelena wasn’t exactly wrong either, Kate was willing to admit. Yes, they were both highly trained martial arts experts. Her mother had paid for it with their considerable fortune and probably a little blood money. Yelena had paid for it with her freedom, her mental health and her literal blood. So, perhaps Kate could learn to say please once in a while.

    ‘Please , may I have a small taste of your rum and raisin, Yelena Belova, Queen of Assassins, Mother of Dragunovs.’

    ‘I will take your request into consideration,’ said Yelena, regally, as one should. ‘Please, just a tiny bit.’ Yelena was clearly enjoying watching Kate beg, and Kate would continue to give her that enjoyment until Yelena relented. ‘Please?’

    After a torturous pause, Yelena raised a solitary eyebrow and extended her small tub of ice cream towards Kate, whose eyes light up with delight. ‘Thank you!’ Kate exclaimed with unabashed merriment, before diving into her rum and raisiny prize. Kate took a modest amount of ice cream, being careful not to incur the wrath of of her partner, and tasted it with glee. ‘Oh, this is good,’ she practically moaned in delight, ‘You chose so well, this is so good. Tomorrow, we are coming back,’ Kate had decided. The decision had been made. Done, dusted, definitive.

    Yelena shifted a little uncomfortably on her bike. ‘I won’t be here tomorrow,’ she explained. ‘I’m flying back to Istanbul. There are a few things I need to sort out before I sign my life away to a shady faction of the American Government.’

    Kate’s smile dropped a little, but only a fraction. ‘Oh, oh well that’s cool. When you’re back then.’ She could wait for full time Yelena, of course she could. Yelena would be worth it. ‘Definitely, when I’m back,’ the assassin smiled, ‘And I will be back,’ Yelena made sure to impress, and Kate appreciated it. She’d just got Yelena back, and the last thing she wanted was another extended period of radio silence.

    ‘It’s a date then,’ Kate smiled as she nudged Yelena affectionately in the side. ‘It is not a date,’ Yelena said, matter-of-factly.

    Well, of course it wasn’t a date date. ‘I didn’t mean...’

    ‘I don’t date,’ clarified Yelena, whilst taking another small scoop of rum and raisin. ‘Oh, I see. Sure, you’re a straight to the point kind of gal.’ Kate nodded her enthusiastic approval for any choices that Yelena may have been making with her own body. ‘No shame in that. None whatsoever. Actually, I support that, if it's your thi-’ ‘I do not do that either,’ the blonde cut in to save Kate any additional embarrassment as the brunette continued to nod.

    ‘Cool, cool, cool. And I take it you’re not a real... lesbian? ’Kate inwardly cringed, was lesbian even the right word anymore? ‘Despite being pretty convincing.’ ‘Nope. Are you?’ Yelena asked with a smirk.

    ‘What?! Me?! Ha,’ Kate laughed, nervously and no doubt blushed profusely. She was giving up on trying to hide it at this stage. Yelena Belova seemed to have been put on this earth to embarrass her. ‘No, no, not gay. No. I mean, I went to college, if you get my meaning but-‘ ‘Nope.’ Case in point. Yelena seemed to really enjoy making Kate uncomfortable and all the brunette could do was laugh. She glanced to the blonde who was smiling into her ice cream. It had been a good evening. Actually, scratch that. What had started out as a pretty mediocre evening, had quickly evolved into a pretty fucking awesome evening, due to one secret ingredient. And that ingredient was sat just to Kate’s left, animatedly recounting the time she’d been sent to intercept an assassination attempt at Oxford University, and offering Kate more rum and raisin from her waning tub of ice cream. An offer Kate happily accepted. ‘See what we can achieve with more than one piece of cutlery?’ Yelena asked, earning herself an eye roll from Kate. Yep, a pretty good evening all round. Pokémon, drinks, scramblers, B&E, vodka and ice cream. Kate could get pretty used to nights like this. And to top it all off, it turned out that Amorinos was in fact an Instinct occupied gym, was being the operative word.

    'Thanks for saving my butt earlier.’

    ‘It’s a butt worth saving,’ Yelena quipped.

    Kate groaned in good humour. ‘Why do you say these things?’

    ‘Well,’ Yelena tilted her head to one side, considering her words. ‘There is an element of truth to most things that I say, apart from when I lie, of course.’

    ‘That makes no sense.’

    ‘But you are worth saving.’

    ‘I like to think so,’ Kate smiled, and was met with a small, soft smile of Yelena’s own. ‘So, what now? I’d say we should find somewhere that’s still serving but you’ve got to ride me home and maybe one more is one too many.’

    ‘Presumptuous, that I am taking you home,’ Yelena said, eyebrow raised. ‘After saving my butt, you’d leave me to get the Metro, at this time of night, all by my lonesome?’

    Yelena smirked, knowing full well that Kate was more than capable of looking after herself. The bruises that marked her body after their fight were testament to that, as they weren’t all from Clint. ‘Is there vodka in your apartment?’ Yelena asked.

    ‘Yes.’

    ‘Is there Kahlua?’

    ‘Yes.’

    ‘Cream?’

    ‘For the dog but I’m sure he could spare you some.’

    ‘And is that dog up there?’ Kate smiled gleefully. Yahtzee ! She knew the answer to this dealbreaker.

    Kate nodded, smugly. ‘Lucky is in residence.’

    ‘Then yes, Kate Bishop, I will be taking you home.’

    Chapter End Notes Next up, IKEA.

    1 Fork More Chapter Notes Wow what an incredible response so far. Thank you all so much for reading. This is a lighter chapter to prepare us for our next full chapter which I can guarantee you will be angst laden. Enjoy!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes “So, you are telling me that I must walk all the way around this place?”

    “Yes! That’s the whole idea. It’s cool, right?” Kate Bishop had been struggling to contain her excitement. For one, she was shopping, which wasn’t something she’d really been able to do properly since her credit cards were cancelled last Christmas. Secondly, she was shopping with Yelena, something she’d been looking forward to since she’d learned that the Russian was moving in with her. And lastly, but not leastly, she was shopping in the Scandinavian paradise bazaar that was IKEA. Yelena didn’t seem to share Kate’s enthusiasm for the venture, but the youngest and only Bishop child would soon make her see otherwise.

    “You walk round,” Kate continued with unmatched enthusiasm, “Check out the rooms, get some inspo, eat some meatballs. You have to have the entire IKEA experience.”

    “Will this take the whole day?” Yelena asked. Her apathy palpable. Kate would have to up her game.

    “Picture yourself hosting around this beautiful kitchen island,” she said, as she draped herself seductively across the piece of furniture. “Admire the complexity, elegance and efficiency of these quaker style storage solutions.” Kate ran her fingers across the veneered wood as Yelena crinkled her nose, probably at the thought of how many grubby hands had gone before. If the Russian wasn’t sufficiently repulsed, her disgust grew deeper as Kate grabbed her by the wrist and pulled her towards a staged living room set. “Sit back, relax on one of the many textiled couches and take the weight of your feet whilst you contemplate life, Swedishly.”

    Kate released her friend and threw herself into a wingback chair. “Look, cool chair huh? I look smart in this chair.”

    Yelena simply shrugged. “But we are not here for a chair. You already have chairs and average smarts. We are here for cutlery. Where is the cutlery?”

    “Yelena, I admire how to straight to the point you are, I really do. There’s never any bullshit with you, but you see, IKEA is a journey, and you need to give yourself up to that journey.”

    “You are going to ignore that average smarts jibe?”

    “Gotta choose my battles,” Kate explained, shrewdly.

    Yelena’s eyebrow quirked as she tried to hide a smile; Kate had defied her expectations. FUCK. YESSSSS. Like a fucking boss boi. “You surprise me every day Kate Bishop. Not always in a good way, but you surprise me none the less.”

    “Well, how about you surprise me and just embrace this journey, just a little more. For me. Embrace the IKEA life.”

    “Like I embraced Pokémon for you? Like I embraced working for a US Government Agency, like I embraced leaving my family and relocating to the USA, like I embraced leaving my dog behind for you so that your dog could be happy, like I embraced pineapple pizza because you didn’t want to pay extra for half and half?”

    Don’t be drawn offside, she’s living with you rent free. In your apartment and elsewhere.

    “Yes, just like that.” Kate smiled sweetly. What had Yelena taught her, smile and play dumb?

    Yelena sighed. “Fine,” she said through gritted teeth. “I will embrace this IKEA life you speak of. Now, where is the cutlery?”

    “Oh, it’s in the market hall,” Kate explained.

    “Where’s that?” Yelena asked.

    “Umm,” Kate glanced with trepidation at the one-way system marked upon the floor, “It’s at the end of the one-way system.”

    “It’s one way?” Yelena asked, incredulously.

    “Yes,” Kate mumbled, preparing herself for the inevitable show of impatience.

    “There are no short cuts?” Kate could hear the desperation rising in her friend’s voice.

    You can do this Kate; you can manage this. “Well, I’m not gonna lie to you, there are short cuts. But do you really want to take your life into your own hands like that?”

    “Are you threatening me Kate Bishop?” And there was the inevitable show of impatience.

    “No, all I’m saying is that shortcuts are a dangerous business in IKEA,” Kate reasoned, and she wasn’t wrong. She remembered one disastrous trip from her childhood, which ended in tears. Not only did Kate miss out on adding to her tiny pencil collection, but she managed to avoid the kid’s bedroom section entirely. It was a dark day.

    “Ee-kay-ah" Yelena corrected. A correction Kate promptly ignored.

    “You could cut through kitchens simply to find bathrooms, but end up in picture frames pushing a trolly laden with lint rollers and ice cube trays, and completely bypass the kid’s stuffed toys.”

    “Why would you want to check out the stuffed toys?” Yelena asked, quite heartlessly in Kate’s opinion.

    “It’s okay Kate,” the brunette whispered to herself in dramatic fashion, as she clutched her chest, “She knows not of what she speaks.”

    There was a pause, a moment. Kate spared a glance back at Yelena. Her jaw was tight with frustration and indecision. Kate could tell her friend wanted to relent, but she also knew that it went against every fibre of Yelena’s being. She was stubborn, set in her ways and, and lived and died for efficiency; three things that Kate loved about her. Kate also loved that when she asked the scary Russian Assassin for something, and when she smiled sweetly, the scary Russian Assassin would acquiesce her request. And as if on cue...

    “Fine, we will walk round,” The Russian relented, and Kate gave an internal and external victory whoop. “But please, please promise you are not going to sit in every brightly coloured chair that catches your eye.”

    “I can’t make you that promise Yelena,” Kate admitted, theatrically. The weird sets and bright lights of IKEA seemed to bring out the performer in here.

    Yelena was done, she’d had enough. The blonde rolled her eyes, turned her back on the Bishop heir and started to make her way around the one-way system. “When I see a chair I like,” Kate called after her, “I just have to sit on it!”

    “Strandmon, Strand-mon. Strandmon?...” Yelena leaned in to inspect the label of the product in front of her. “What does it mean? I have not heard this word.”

    Kate shrugged, unhelpfully. “It’s Swedish, or it’s made up, or a weird combination of the two. Like higee.”

    “Hygge is a real word.”

    “No, it’s not, you can’t even say it right.”

    “I can. It’s Hoo-guh. And it’s Danish, not Swedish.”

    “I didn’t mean you,” Kate pouted, “I meant you.” She waved her hands out in front of her, a gesture that she was sure effectively indicated the general populace.

    Yelena chuckled warmly. It was a sound that was so lovely, Kate didn’t particularly care that it was at her expense. Of course, she wasn’t going to tell Yelena that.

    “And you’re laughing at me. Great.”

    “Only because it is so easy to laugh at you,” the blonde smiled, teasingly. Kate gave her a look of faux admonishment and turned on her heel to head further down the one-way system, but before she could take two steps, Yelena’s hand had wrapped tightly around her wrist.

    “No, wait,” The blonde said. “I like this one.” Yelena pointed matter-of-factly to the chair in front of her.

    “You like this chair?” Kate asked. Okay, maybe her faux admonishment wasn’t so faux after all, because that temperature rise felt very, very real.

    “Yes,” came Yelena’s straightforward response. Clearly the Russian hadn’t grasped that she was the reason for Kate’s building annoyance. Or perhaps she was grasping it all too well.

    “But a minute ago you said I looked dumb in that exact same chair.” Was Kate hurt? Yes, she was hurt.

    Yelena frowned a little, perplexed. “No, I didn’t,” the blonde protested. It only took a moment for Yelena to realise the confusion. She rolled her eyes and attempted to explain. “Not that one, that one.” Yelena pointed away from a wingback chair identical to the one Kate had thrown herself in ten minutes before, this time upholstered in a vivid forest green, and drew Kate’s attention to the chair next to it. It was practically alike in every way, but this chair was half the size.

    “The tiny one?” Kate asked, exasperated.

    “Yes, the tiny one,” Yelena confirmed, softly.

    Kate’s hands went to her hips and she huffed dramatically, sending the errant hairs that had fallen in front of her eyes straight into orbit. “I hate to break it to you, I know your like… 4,11 or something,” Yelena sent Kate a stern look but the brunette continued unphased, “But that peach of yours is not fitting into that chair.”

    The stern look on the Russian’s face quickly softened to one of sincere and utter gratitude. “Thank you,” Yelena said, softly.

    “You’re welcome,” came Kate’s earnest response. The two locked eyes, and neither could hold back the grins that were spreading across their faces. Kate loved this; she loved how easy it was with Yelena. Even when they were bickering, they were never really at odds, they were just pushing and prodding, finding out how far they could push the other and how much they’d need to push to get their own way.

    “As much as I’d love to discuss the benefits of front squats,” Yelena said, a conspiratorial grin spreading from ear to ear, “I wasn’t actually thinking about me.” The blonde paused for dramatic effect. Kate was on tenterhooks. Who was she thinking about? Did they know any children, and would they want any children in their home? It was maybe a little to early to be thinking about adoption. Or would Kate bear their kids? If Yelena meant Scott, that chair was going to need to be a hundred times smaller. Unless... no she couldn’t be, she couldn’t be thinking about... “I was thinking about Lucky.” And there it was, the answer, the answer to the ultimate question of life and the universe.

    Kate found it hard to contain her excitement. “Oh my god. Oh my god you’re right. He would look so smart in that chair.” Breathe Kate, breathe. “Get a pencil Yelena, you beautiful human being, get a pencil now. Go, go!” Kate slapped her friend’s arms in an attempt to agitate her towards the nearest pencil dispenser but to Kate’s dismay, when she needed her friend the most, the ex-assassin didn’t budge, she simply narrowed her eyes.

    “I’m not getting you a pencil until you admit that I’m 5,3.”

    “What am I looking at?” Yelena asked, brow furrowed.

    “This is a…” Kate got a little closer to read the mattress’ label. “Ho-bag,” Kate said, enunciating the syllables with relish.

    Yelena sighed. Kate was busted but Kate did not give a fudge. “That is not what it says.”

    “True,” Kate responded without inflection, “It says hövåg but I just wanted to say it.”

    “And why are we looking at this, ho-bag?”

    Kate snickered, she said hobag. Pull it together, Kate. “Well, I thought that since Lucky and I were making a little space for you, that maybe you should you know, have your own bed, as well as your own fork. We can’t share everything,” Kate shrugged.

    “Oh, okay,” came the rather muted response from Yelena. It wasn’t the response Kate had been expecting.

    “I mean, not that I haven’t enjoyed the additional warmth that you bring to the bed situation, but it’s August.”

    “I am warm,” Yelena agreed with a nod.

    “You are indeed.”

    “Like a furnace,” Yelena whispered, intensely.

    “Dipped in the deepest of magmas” Kate’s eyes went wide as her imagination momentarily transported her to the fiery hellscapes of Mount Doom.

    “I understand,” came Yelena’s voice, from across the misty mountains. The brunette blinked, as the spell was broken, and just like that Kate was home, safe in the Shire. “This will do then I suppose?” Yelena gestured to the mattress before them, her lips downturned in stoic approval.

    Kate nodded. “A wise choice, it’s certainly well reviewed.” Kate hoped Yelena wouldn’t question why she had such extensive and well researched IKEA mattress knowledge, she also hoped she wouldn’t spy on the last five days of her browsing history. “But,” Kate continued, “You should try some others. See what you like.”

    “There is a choice of mattress?” Asked Yelena. The tiniest hint of wonder and excitement danced in Yelena’s eyes and Kate’s heart soared. Yelena was starting to believe in the IKEA journey, Kate could sense it. Oh yes, she was well and truly on the path.

    Kate grinned, she was about to rock Yelena’s world. Not like that. “Yes, oh yes. THIS is Ikea. Just hop on and see which one you like best.”

    “What if I don’t know what I like?” Yelena asked. It was the first time Kate had heard anything like what she’d just heard in her friend’s voice. She’d heard uncertainty, perhaps the most un-Yelena like quality. The blonde normally knew what she liked, she knew herself, and if she hadn’t tried something before she was the type of person who would jump straight in, headfirst without a thought and with no fucks given. The dark and mysterious world of mattresses, Yelena was unsure of, so naturally, Kate decided to hold her hand through the entire process.

    “Well,” she began, throwing her arm around Yelena’s shoulder. To her surprise, the blonde didn’t shrug it off. “What mattresses do you normally go for? Firm or soft?”

    “I like yours,” Yelena sheepishly answered. Kate glanced down at her friend. Something beautiful yet terrifying had happened. Yelena Belova, Queen of Assassins had metamorphosised in front of her eyes, into a puppy. A real-life puppy. Her eyes were dark and unsure, her brow creased with indecision, and suddenly Kate was struck with a thought. Maybe it wasn’t just Kate that needed Yelena.

    “Okay, okay,” Kate sprung to action, as she squeezed her friend’s arm with encouragement, and then dashed amongst the mattress on show, eyes scanning each label quickly and efficiently. “Mine’s got a little memory foam,” she explained and poked the mattresses as she went, in hope of finding something similar. Her eyes lit up when they fell upon exactly what she had been looking for. “This,” Kate pointed, triumphantly, “Has a memory foam topper.”

    “Okay. That one is fine,” Yelena shrugged, clearly not mirroring Kate’s passion for mattress shopping. Well, what a disappointment that was.

    But Kate didn’t relent, Yelena just needed a nudge in the right direction, she was sure of it. If this was all new, Yelena just needed to be enlightened of the possibilities. “Do you not want to get on it?”

    “I can do that in the store?” Yelena asked, with the same apprehension. The Russian glanced down at the mattress before her, sizing it up. Her eyes narrowed as she continued her cross examination. “But if I can do that, then other people will have also done that, and that is disgusting.”

    Kate rolled her eyes and decided that the best way forward was to simply force Yelena’s hand, that’s what friends were for, and so Kate hopped up, onto the mattress and patted the spot next to her, demandingly. “Will you just get on.” It wasn’t a request.

    “Eta devushka, someone’s cranky.”

    “Someone simply appreciates the benefits of having a mattress that suits and wants to extol them upon you. Is that too much to ask?” Kate fixed her friend with a look; it was clear that Kate’s question wasn’t anything but hypothetical.

    With a tiny groan of protest, which didn’t go unnoticed by Kate, Yelena perched on the mattress. “No… I guess I could be a little more agreeable.”

    “I guess you could,” Kate agreed, signalling to Yelena that it would be best for her health if she embraced her IKEA journey and just lied the fuck down. After a beat, Yelena sighed and then relented, despite both friends knowing the older woman was not afraid of the younger’s retribution.

    The two women lay, side by side, both pairs of eyes fixed high up into the warehouse rafters. Kate heard Yelena sigh once more, quieter this time, as if releasing a breath she hadn’t realised she’d been holding onto. Kate stole a glance at her friend. Her body looked tense, despite being on one of the most comfortable and expensive mattresses in the store, and a muscle ticked in her jaw as she eyes never left the rafters above. On instinct, Kate reached for Yelena. It was involuntary, or at least it had felt that way. She captured the blonde’s hand in hers and squeezed. To Kate’s surprise, Yelena didn’t pull away.

    “I’ve never chosen a mattress before, as a kid I didn’t really get that luxury,” Yelena spoke quietly, as if prompted by Kate’s touch, and didn’t take her eyes from the IKEA ceiling. “And the last few years, I’ve never been in one place long enough to even think about going out and buying my own. It’s always been hotel rooms or safe houses, or my mother’s house,” she added the last with just the slightest bit of disdain. “This would be my first.”

    “Do you like it?” Kate asked, gently.

    “How much is it?”

    “Doesn’t matter.” Yelena turned to Kate and raised a sceptical and surprised eyebrow. She obviously wasn’t used to gifts either. Kate guessed that in Yelena’s line of work, nothing ever came for free. “What?” A small laugh escaped Kate as Yelena began to grin, “It doesn’t matter. What matters is that you like it. Do you like it?”

    “I like it,” Yelena confirmed, softly.

    “Yesssss!” Exclaimed Kate, in victory, as she propped herself up on her elbow and properly turned to face her friend. “You will not regret this. You are going to be so well rested, and so limbered up that you’re going to be an even better assassin than you were before you made this trip today.”

    Yelena shook her head, coolly. “Not possible.”

    “Totally possible, with the power of IKEA.”

    “Ee-kay-ah"

    “Whatever.” Kate said, dismissively, as she flopped back down onto her back and stared back up to the ceiling, trying to avoid looking directly into the bright lights that she found here. They lay in comfortable silence as the world shuffled by. Couples, families, singletons, each on their individual IKEA journeys.

    “Do you think they would sponsor me? When I become a famous Avenger.” Yelena asked, quite out of the blue.

    “IKEA?” Kate asked, to clarify.

    “Yes. I could do a cool new series for them. Ten ways to kill someone with a miniature pencil. Sheets or curtains, how to strangle a man in less than sixty seconds.” Kate didn’t quite know whether Yelena was being serious or not, put it on the list of one of the many things Kate Bishop loved about Yelena Belova.

    “Could you speak any louder about this?” Kate asked, conscious of the perfectly regular civilians, milling around them.

    “It’s okay,” Yelena reassured her, “People just tend to think I’m crazy.”

    “Wow, that’s unfair of them.” Kate’s sarcasm wasn't given the time of day.

    “Oh, and I have some fantastic tips on how to get blood out of upholstery.”

    “Actually, could you share those with me? I think most women in the world would open to hearing about those.”

    Yelena’s face contorted, as something over Kate’s shoulder caught her eye.

    “What are you looking at?” Yelena raised her voice and Kate inwardly cringed as she pictured the shocked faces that were stood behind her. “Can’t two women share a bed? It’s 2025!” The Russian had a point, shame Yelena was probably off the mark.

    “I think it might be the murder talk,” Kate whispered, hastily. “You know, and not a gay thing?”

    “We are not gay.”

    “Okay, babe,” Kate nodded and she hopped of the mattress. “But you are a murderer,” she said, as she grabbed Yelena’s arm and pulled her up and away from the small group of onlookers. Kate didn’t let go of her friend’s arm until she’d managed to stash her away in a darkened faux bedroom set up.

    “I am not a murderer,” Yelena reasoned, “If I kill people-”

    “If, that’s hilarious.”

    “If I kill people, they are bad people.”

    “Keep telling yourself that babe, whatever helps you sleep at night.”

    Yelena’s eyes darkened, as Kate become painfully aware of how close they were standing; how close she was standing to one of the world’s most prolific and efficient killers. Whilst brainwashed, Kate added as mental note. Yelena took a step closer, squared up to Kate and gazed directly up, into Kate’s eyes. Her heart picked up its rhythm and her breathing became shallow. A smile pulled at the corner of Yelena’s lips, could she tell, could Yelena hear the way Kate’s body had reacted? It didn’t seem that far fetched. Kate didn’t know if she was intimidated or excited to go toe to toe with Yelena again. Scratch that, she did know. She was almost certainly excited. Maybe a little too excited. Was IKEA the best place for an all out play fight? Arguments could be made for and against.

    For one long moment, Yelena’s eyes washed up and down Kate’s body as she sized up the taller woman up. “Now I have that great mattress, I could kill you just like that,” the Russian snapped her fingers and Kate jumped, unconsciously, “And would still get a full eight hours, no problem.”

    A moment’s silence hung between the two partners. Kate quirked a come at me bro eyebrow as Yelena’s small, smug smile turned into a broad grin. “Well, in that case, we should pick out a bed, don’t you think? Just to make sure.”

    The next half an hour was spent was spent browsing bedroom layouts, beds, linen, bedside tables and the like. You name it, they browsed it. Yelena would systematically pick things up and appraise them, or take bed linens between her fingers and rub delicately, making unspoken judgement calls on their quality. Kate found it hard to decipher whether an item had left Yelena impressed or unimpressed, as every judgement would be punctuated with a downturned little pout of approval or disapproval. She was quite something to behold, deadly assassin checking the thread counts under the bright lights of IKEA.

    It became quite apparent to Kate that the mattress wasn’t the only first for Yelena. The entire experience was new. Shopping for life, mundane, boring life. Kate felt her heart ache a little as Yelena explored all the storage possibilities. The shelves, the drawers, the baskets, the tiny jewellery stores, the mirrors, the handle selections. The blonde’s eyes were alive as she explored the kid’s bedroom department. She’d asked Kate more than once if she could change her mind on the simple but stylish metal bed they’d picked out for her and trade up to a bunk bed, or a loft bed. The brunette felt pretty awful reminding her that her bed would sit underneath the balcony of Kate’s duplex, and so wouldn’t be afforded enough height. Yelena had pouted, stuck a wolf cub plushie under her arm, and stalked off to check out the gaming chairs. Kate couldn’t keep the smile from her face at the innocence of it all, at how care free Yelena was in those moments, at how open to possibility she was, but then her thoughts shifted. She wondered how many stuffed toys Yelena had been afforded as a child, how many times she’d be encouraged to discover, how much room she’d been afforded to dream. Kate’s smile faltered, but they continued.

    After what had been a genuinely life changing IKEA journey, and after Kate had persuaded her friend that they didn’t need a pop art mural of Audrey Hepburn, Yelena and Kate’s feet brought them safely to their ultimate destination. The two stood, wide eyed and if not a little exhausted, before a large yellow and blue sign; they had made it to the market floor.

    “Be prepared,” warned Kate. “You will want to buy everything.”

    “I believe you.”

    “But we are strong.”

    “The strongest.” Yelena nodded in agreement. “Wait, are those scented candles?”

    “So, I get the impression you like IKEA, right?” Yelena asked.

    “Love, love, love it,” responded Kate, jovially.

    “And you come here often?”

    “Not all the time, but maybe once a year to load up on Daim bars and eat mash potatoes, which we have to do once we’re finished by the way.”

    “Oh, one hundred percent a yes from me on the potatoes.”

    “You know we were meant to be, right?”

    “I know.”

    “But even though I will happily hold my hands up and say today has been less painful than I expected it to be, there’s just one thing that doesn’t make sense to me about this place.”

    Kate frowned. It all seemed pretty self-explanatory. See shit you want. Pick up shit you want. Buy shit you want. And always, ALWAYS eat the shit you want. “What is it?”

    “How do you only have one fucking fork when I am literally surrounded by cutlery right now?”

    Kate cast her eyes in all directions. Yelena was not wrong. The shelves had cutlery, the walls had cutlery, even the floor had cutlery; not on purpose, but it had cutlery all the same. But this was where Kate and Yelena were different. Yelena took what she needed, first and foremost. She saw a need and she fulfilled it. Kate identified what she wanted and bought it, all of it. If she didn’t want it she wouldn’t buy it. As simple as that. Never let it be said that Kate Bishop never followed her heart.

    “That’s like asking, how have I not found a boyfriend in New York City when I’m literally surrounded by eligble bachelors? Well, let me tell you Yelena, maybe I just haven't found the right partner for my fork yet,” Kate said pointedly, with one hand on her hip and the other serving what she thought was ostentatious attitude.

    Yelena looked perturbed. “A fork is just a fork,” she said, plainly.

    “Woah, woah, woah, I’m going to pretend I didn’t just hear that.” Kate couldn’t believe what she was hearing. Since when was a fork just a fork.

    “It’s pointy, you poke things with it, you put them in your mouth. Done. What more do you need from a fork? It’s is a vehicle for my food, from my plate to my mouth. Apart from this one time I killed a girl with one, a fork serves one purpose, and that is it.” Yelena seemed quite sure of these spurious lies, but she was quite, quite wrong.

    “You’ve obviously never been to one of my mom’s benefit dinners,” Yelena frowned in disgust. “And by the look on your face, you obviously never will”.

    “Look,” Yelena appealed, as she picked up a set of cutlery and placed it in Kate’s hands. “This set is called Dragon. Stupid name but you like Dragons, right?”

    “I do,” Kate confirmed, thoughtfully. It was a measured response. She needed to at least look like she was weighing up her options and making sensible decisions, but if Kate Bishop didn’t want something we all knew it wasn’t getting bought. “Dragons are super cool,” she reasoned, and they totally were. “But these forks are just…” she sighed and shook her head, as she placed them back on the shelf. “They’re too curvy, I dunno.”

    Yelena bit back her annoyance and persevered. “Okay, how about these? ‘TILLGAD’. They’re black, like my heart,” she quipped, with a smile, hoping that Kate would warm to the cutlery like she’d warmed to Yelena herself, despite her shades of grey.

    Her efforts were futile. “I just feel like they’re trying too hard. Look at me, I’m black and contemporary,” she said as she stood in black DMs, black jeans, and a black band t-shirt. Not to mention the black nail polish. Yelena’s sigh was now a groan. “Oh! Oooh, these are cool,” Kate exclaimed, as she picked up a container of colourful utensils.

    “These,” Yelena grabbed the cutlery from Kate and waved them in front of her. “These are plastic… and they are for children.”

    “Perfect for your tiny hands.”

    The Russian’s eyes narrowed. “Remember what I said about the mattress Kate. I’d sleep easy.”

    Kate was quickly learning that Yelena’s love language was threatening behaviour. She would narrow her eyes and get all serious. Her voice would drop a pitch or two lower and she’d say something oh so scary. It would never fail to make Kate feel something, apart from fear of course. The brunette stopped being genuinely afraid of Yelena a long time ago.

    “Oh, look at these!” Kate pointed to a set behind her friend like a kid in a candy store, and Yelena rolled her eyes.

    “You are a puppy.”

    “Upphjod.” Kate attempted in her best, but not good, Swedish accent. “Metal and plastic, colour and classic. The perfect partnership.”

    “Are you suggesting that this cutlery is like us.”

    “Yes.” Yelena raised a judgemental eyebrow. “No. But they have an anti-slip surface that’s comfortable to hold. Ergo-nomic. Ergo... we get them?”

    Yelena could only shake her head at the ridiculousness of the entire situation. “Yes! Please just put them in the basket and let’s bust this joint.”

    They smiled, easily. “You’ve enjoyed this though; I know you have.” Kate teased.

    “I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Yelena said, slyly. “However, I am happy with our cutlery selection. Comfort is always important, but anti-slip might be the difference between life and death. Smart Kate Bishop.”

    Kate frowned. “What?”

    “Well, if someone broke into your home, what are you using to defend yourself?”

    “Er,” was this like, a trick question? “My bow and arrow, obviously.”

    “Oh sure,” Yelena said, her voice dripping with sarcasm, “I’m sure your intruder will gladly wait for you to retrieve your quiver.”

    “Pfft,” Kate was having none of this. “I mean, I’m fast.” Yelena smirked. The blonde’s silence was doing nothing to hide her scepticism, as Kate took her bag from her shoulder and started to root around inside for her wallet. “Deceptively fast,” she argued as she retrieved her wallet, only to find it stripped empty of all its credit cards. “What?” came Kate’s disbelieving voice. How did she…?

    “Okay Kate Bishop, you are dead. Bye bye, nice knowing you, thank you for the credit card.”

    Kate’s nose crinkled as she pouted and frowned, all at the same time. “I don’t feel as if you take my skills seriously enough.”

    “I take your skills very seriously. You are a very good Robin Hood,” Yelena smirked as she grabbed Kate’s wallet and began returning all of her bank cards to their rightful places.

    “Case in point,” Kate protested, as she dumped her basket down onto the self-checkout and started scanning all their small items through, before they could go to the collection point for Yelena’s bed and mattress, and Lucky’s chair.

    “Robin Hood was a cool dude. Rob from the rich, give to the poor. He’s like, a big a hero of mine.”

    Kate’s eyes lit up. No way, I love her, this is why we’re going to be best friends. “Really? I do kind of lov-”

    “No,” Yelena answered, shortly, as she handed Kate her most coveted credit card back. Kate’s heart sank, she should have seen that coming. The brunette huffed and frowned once more.

    “Remember who’s paying for this,” She warned, as she waved the card at Yelena in what she thought was an intimidating fashion.

    “Crime? Blood? The citizens of New York City?” Yelena quipped.

    “Seems fitting for you then, doesn’t it?” Kate snapped back. Quite suddenly and without realising, the pair were back how they’d found themselves two hours before; squared up, with Kate towering over the smaller but no less intimidating Yelena. The tension was palpable, at least for the poor IKEA sales assistant who was marshalling the self-checkouts.

    “Um, ma’ams, is everything okay?” The sales assistant was met with silence. The two women were too lost in each other’s eyes to care.

    After what felt like forever, Yelena spoke, quietly, not taking her eyes from Kate’s. It was practically a whisper. The kind of whisper that managed to send Kate’s stomach into flip flops. “You were right, I have enjoyed this.”

    Kate tried to remain cool, she really did, but hearing that admission was suddenly all Kate cared about, all she desired, all she wanted in life. After one more, final beat a hearty “Yes!” erupted from the brunette as she punched the air. The startled, if not slightly relieved, sales assistant returned to helping people with unexpected items in their bagging areas. “I knew you would! I knew it!” Kate exclaimed, pointing at Yelena as the Russian batted her hand away. “That wallet trick was pretty cool though.”

    “Oh, thank you. In my old line of work, bow and arrows are not cool. But you are making them cooler. For me, anyways.”

    “Really?” Kate asked, as she tapped her card on the card reader, clearly delighted and clearly more than willing to get her hopes up despite an unprecedented possibility of having them dashed again if Yelena was true to form.

    This time however, Yelena smiled an earnest smile, one that reached her eyes and then some, and answered. “Really.” Kate’s chest felt hot, and tight as her breath caught in her throat. Their daily push/pull for Yelena’s approval had yielded results, the best kind of results. Warms eyes, small smiles and honest words; things that Yelena Belova didn’t afford to just anyone.

    Maybe Kate really was in an exclusive club. Yes, Yelena was going to teach Kate how to survive, but Kate was going to teach Yelena how to live.

The update might take a little while longer as it’s an important chapter. This phone call takes place the evening on the IKEA trip.

    Again, thank you all so much for reading, kudosing, and commenting. Enjoy! P.S. I love Carol, don’t hate me.

    Birthdays Are For Children Chapter Notes Well, this one was a bit of an epic in my end. It’s longer than usual and I really hope you enjoy it.

    Thank you all so much for your kind comments and kudos. And thank you for reading. And a special thank you to Kristin for painstakingly proof reading this to help me get it out the door.

    Kate stared at her recent outgoing calls list.

    Yelena Belova-lova 08:53 Yelena Belova-lova 09:05 Yelena Belova-lova 09:27 Yelena Belova-lova 09:32

    Four unanswered calls. FOUR. That was the most in history. Yes, their history as a pair had been short, relatively speaking, but never had Yelena let four calls go unanswered, or at least unacknowledged. Normally if Yelena was too busy to take a call from Kate, she’d send a text or pick up and let her know she’d give her a call back when she was available. So, you see, for unanswered calls was rather unprecedented, and if not a little anxiety inducing.

    Kate had woken up in her bunk at the Avenger compound, Yelenaless. Neither of the friends were really known as morning people, especially as they spent their nights chatting shit, watching shit and eating enough shit to compensate for the amount that they were burning in the day time.

    Since Yelena had been inducted at Avengers HQ, Kate’s activity levels had gone through the roof. If they weren’t training in combat, they were in the gym or at the firing range, or running situational simulations in the war room. Being a hero was serious shit, and turns out, much to Yelena’s chagrin, there were particular ways you were supposed to go about things. Kate had already lost count of the number of times Yelena had told Carol that she wasn’t a hero, and being a hero wasn’t what she signed up for; she was far more effective than that. Kate had also lost count of the amount of ranty tirades Yelena had subjected the heavy bag to.

    Last night, after their mandatory Facetime with Lucky via Grills, they’d settled down to watch a couple of episodes of Blue Planet in their bunks, and shortly after Kate drifted off to sleep to the welcomed sound of Yelena’s rasping chuckles. She’d recently taken to watching mixed martial arts, and was going through a phase of binging hours and hours' worth of compilation videos such as ‘MMA’s most horrific injuries’ and ‘UFCs most devastating bone breaks’ before bed. Of course, she found them all highly amusing, and would often quietly chide the fighters for their stupidity. Yelena Belova wasn’t one for constructive criticism. Unless your name was Kate Bishop.

    But to Kate’s surprise, upon her waking that morning, no Yelena Belova did she find in the bunk next to hers, much to Kate’s frustration.
