And what made it even weirder, was that the bed was made, Yelena’s bed was never made. A small act of non-conformist rebellion after years under a strict regime. So, why today? Kate had made sure to fall asleep before Yelena and she’d made sure to wake up before Yelena normally rises, and yet, there was no Yelena.

    Kate’s brow furrowed with indecision as she stared at her phone once more and chewed nervously on her bottom lip. How could she have miscalculated so badly, and how had her friend managed to elude her so comprehensively. It was almost as if she hadn’t wanted to wake Kate. It was almost as if... her Yelena was avoiding her. Of course, that was a stupid though, Kate told herself. Sure, they’d spent a lot of time together recently, which was probably an understatement, but Yelena had shown no signs of fatigue or annoyance, in fact, they had grown closer and closer as time had gone by. So why today of all days, could Kate not find her friend?

    The time stood at 09:45. Was it too early to call her friend again? Some might say yes, some might say leave it alone you needy bitch, but today wasn’t a normal day, and their friendship wasn’t a normal friendship.

    “Fuck it.” Kate whispered to herself, and hit the call button. Yelena’s phone rang once, then twice, then three times then-

    "Hello?!” Came Yelena’s voice, loud and clear above the cacophony of noise on the other end of the line. Kate practically jumped out of her skin with relief and excitement.

    “Hey! It’s me!” Kate shouted down the phone, clearly pretty elated.

    “Hello Kate,” was Yelena’s terse response. Kate frowned, it was unlike Yelena to be short with her. Well, that wasn’t entirely true. It was unlike Yelena to be short with her when she wasn’t doing something the Russian deemed immature or dangerous; and Yelena didn’t frown on all things dangerous.

    “You okay? you sound a bit-”

    “I’m fine.” Yelena barked down the phone, over the thumping and whirring in the background.

    “You don’t sound-”

    “I’m running!” Yelena explained, loudly, a little exasperated. Running, of course she was running. That explained the thumping and the shouting and the whirring. But it didn’t explain why Yelena was there in the first place. Nearly all gym sessions were done together, even if they worked in silence with their headphones in and nearly all gym sessions were done in the afternoon.

    “Oh. Cool. You at the gym because I thought th-” The thumping increased and the whirring intensified. What the fuck was going on? Was Yelena really at the gym or had she joined Vin Diesel for a twenty-six-mile grand theft auto along an airstrip in Spain? Kate sighed, audibly, not that her friend would ever hear her. “You’re doing intervals, of course you are.” After a few more seconds of very patient waiting from Kate, the sound of the treadmill begun to wane, and so Kate decided to persevere.

    “You there?” the brunette asked.

    “Yep,” Came Yelena’s slightly breathless response.

    “And you’re sure you’re okay?” Kate persisted, “Because I didn’t hear you leave this morning.”

    “I’m fine.” Yelena didn’t sound fine, Yelena sounded agitated. Had Kate done something without realising? She knew that she’d accidentally spoiled the Lion King for her the day before yesterday, but that certainly wasn’t the first and wouldn’t be the last thing Kate would spoil for her friend, because Kate was quickly making it a habit.

    Kate sighed, perhaps it would be better to simply let Yelena run and punch her frustration out, irrespective of what had caused it. “Okay. Well, good, good. Erm, well I guess I was really just phoning to say Ha-’

    “Look Kate,” Yelena interjected, as the revs of the treadmill began to increase; here came another interval. “Do you need anything? Because intervals are tough at the best of times but I think doing them without music goes against the Geneva Convention!” The Russian practically shouted.

    “Oh my goodness, you are totally right. I’m sorry.” And she totally was totally right. There was a reason Kate avoided intervals at all costs, and it was because they were hard and unpleasant and needed to be erased from time and space. There really was only one thing to be done. “How about I see you down there okay? Catch you in ten.”

    “Kate-” Yelena began, and Kate could hear the warning in her voice, but it was too late, she’d already hung up and she’d already made her decision. If Yelena was feeling shitty, it was Kate’s job as her best friend, to make her feel not shitty, especially on her Birthday.

    The automatic doors to the gym slid open, just like every door did in the Avengers Complex did, and Kate hurried through, in fear of them closing abruptly in her face. There, at the end of the gym, was her best friend, and she was still running. That meant Yelena had been doing interval training for at least twenty minutes, because although Kate had said ten minutes, she’d most definitely mis-estimated. This was all, quite frankly, sickening. How was she still alive? How was she still running so fast? Was that the interval? The treadmill began to speed up and Yelena picked up her pace. Shit, that wasn’t the interval? Yelena was going hard that day. What a way to spend your birthday.

    Kate made her way past the free weights, mats, squat racks and benches and hopped up on the treadmill next to Yelena. The blonde was focused, headphones on, as she ran, eyes out across the complex. Her hair was scooped back into a messy, high ponytail, her skin was flushed, and she was dressed in her typical gym garb. Black cycling shorts, black vest, black in ear headphones and black Nike Zooms. Kate blinked at the sight, and swallowed, hard. Wow, she is sweaty.

    “You are glistening!” Kate shouted enthusiastically, a little too enthusiastically. Perhaps it was for the best that Yelena couldn’t hear Kate's attempt at a compliment over the sound of the treadmill, her thumping footsteps and her undoubtedly ear-splitting Finnish metal. Despite that, Kate had certainly meant it. Yelena mid anything that raised her heart rate was a thing to behold, and Kate was slowly realising that beholding Yelena do any kind of exercise could quite easily raise her heart beat too. Was it the sweating? Maybe. The outfits? Perhaps. The general badassery? Almost certainly.

    The machine beeped twice and began to power down to a slow walking speed. Yelena’s interval torture protocol had ended. The Russian glanced over to Kate, who in true Kate Bishop style was wearing a baggy looking purple t-shirt over a tight black crop top and some black leggings, all of which looked perfectly regular but were probably cobbled together by Balenciaga. Yelena didn’t so much as offer her friend a weak smile. Kate frowned. Okay, this was becoming less fun now. She’d woken before her, snuck out to the gym without her, and now Yelena wasn’t even acknowledging her friend’s existence. That smarted a little.

    Usually, if Kate had pissed her Russian friend off, Kate would soon know about it. Don’t pull your punches, don't act like a fucking baby, I've done the washing up every night this week. And so on and so on. But these were all trivial, in the grand scheme of things, or at least that’s what she told Yelena about the washing up, they’d never had a genuine falling out. Perhaps not until now.

    With a push of a button and a flick of her smartwatch, Yelena turned abruptly, stepped off the treadmill and headed towards the squat racks. This was normally Kate’s second favourite Yelena gym activity, but today, the prospect of seeing a short-ass woman squat twice her body weight didn’t seem to be having quite the same effect.

    Yelena sighed a little as she shook and stretched off the lactic acid build up in her quads and calves and then began to shift the weights around on the bar. “Who here squats a hundred pounds?” The blonde muttered to herself, probably a little louder than she intended due to the heavy metal destroying her ear drums. That squatter would be Kate, yesterday afternoon, when Yelena was too involved in annihilating the heavy bag to pay attention to what her charge was doing. “Pussy,” came Yelena’s rather scathing verdict.

    “Cool. Thanks, babe,” Kate whispered to herself, despite there being next to zero risk that Yelena would overhear.

    Kate huffed a little as she hopped off the treadmill and made her way over to her friend. Was she fighting a losing battle? Perhaps. Would she persevere? Absolutely. If her friend was upset, she needed to fix it, if she’d upset her friend, she needed to fix it. “You need a spot?” Kate asked, loudly, as she tried to find Yelena’s eyes with her own.

    “Hmm?” Yelena sounded, loudly, and glanced up. Their eyes did eventually find each other, and Kate made a note, this was her first victory of the day. She was certain there would be many more, with what she had planned, there couldn’t not be. She just needed to get over this first hurdle. A grumpy Yelena sized hurdle.

    Kate pointed to her own right ear, gesturing to Yelena that removing her in-ear headphones might be conducive of a more constructive conversation. Yelena’s stoic face was unreadable, almost innocent, as if she’d been completely unaware that her friend had been desperately trying to gain her attention, with an almost puppy-like quality for the last couple of minutes. To Kate’s delight, Yelena complied with her request, and removed her right headphone. Victory number two!

    “Do you need a spot?” Kate asked again, with a small smile.

    “No, thank you.” Yelena said, as she popped her headphone back in place, secured the final disk weights, and dipped under the bar. Victory number two had been called too early, evidently. Classic Kate. The battle had been lost, and to win the war, Kate realised she may have to retreat and lay down arms, at least for the time being. With a wistful sigh, Kate trudged back over to her treadmill and set it to a slow walking pace. She glanced up at the large glass panel windows in front of her, to catch sight of Yelena and her gloomy disposition in their reflection. Something wasn’t right, and although Kate knew that the entire world did in fact revolve around herself, she couldn’t help but think that Yelena’s mood had been triggered by something or someone else entirely.

    A fleeting thought crossed Kate’s mind, perhaps Yelena just didn’t like birthdays. But who didn’t like birthdays. Child assassins who were raised on a diet of abuse, neglect and trauma? Kate studied her friend’s face. Her brow was furrowed and her eyes dark, not an unusual look for the new Avenger, but she felt smaller today. For such a small human being, Yelena always took up space with her energy and her being. She was confident, gregarious and effervescent, and for the most part, didn’t give a fuck. But today, today her energy was dark and diminutive. Today, she didn’t want to be here, and that worried Kate. So, the brunette decided that she had to get closer for a better look.

    She brought the treadmill to a stop, slunk over to the free weights, pulled up a bench and a couple of ten-pound dumbbells and got to work. A few curls, followed by a glance over to Yelena, followed by a scroll on Twitter, then a few curls more. The blonde dropped the bar, unceremoniously onto the rack causing it to clank loudly. Kate jumped a little and glanced up from her newsfeed. Yelena was switched up her weights as she discarded some lower weighted disks to go heavier. She was certainly on one today. “Are you actually going to work out?” She called, quite suddenly towards the free weights area, headphones removed, “Or are you just going to make dog eyes at me?” Was she talking to Kate? Couldn’t be, as Kate’s eyes were perfectly normal looking and were certainly not doggish. In fact, on more than one occasion, she’d been told she had beautiful eyes. On one particularly special occasion, it had been Yelena who had remarked.

    “Oh no, I’m still sore from yesterday.” Kate explained. And she certainly was. But she also had next to no real interest in working out.

    “Well,” Yelena continued, and gestured to the smaller disks that lay discarded on the floor, “That makes sense.” Her tone was dismissive, and was missing her usual playful lilt. This wasn’t banter, Yelena was being mean. Yelena was never mean, not her Yelena anyways. Kate felt a small pang of hurt, but decided to persevere. She’d made plans. Her friend was having a shit day? Well, she would remedy that, no matter how disparaging she was of how much, or little, she’d squatted yesterday. Just to be clear, her max squat was far more impressive, but toning was important too. Maybe not for Avenger purposes, but for other... reasons.

    “I just thought we could hang out,” Kate explained. “You know. As it’s your-”

    “I do not want to hang out,” Yelena said, abruptly, as the bar clattered down into the rack once more. “All I want is to work out. You do not need to be here for that.” Wow, stone cold. And there it was again, the meanness. Meanness that had never been reserved for Kate before. Kate bit the inside of her lip despondently, as Yelena began to wrap her hands, ready for some heavy bag work. Just what this conversation needed, more aggression. At least Yelena’s anger would be worked out on the bag, rather than on Kate’s precious purple heart.

    Kate sighed and put the dumbbell down. “You don’t like birthdays, do you?

    “I don’t... dislike... birthdays,” Each word was punctuated by a punch and a grunt, “I just don’t do them.”

    “Is that why you’re trying to punch the living shit out of that bag?” Kate asked, suddenly very appreciative of the existence of punch bags.

    Yelena didn’t dignify Kate’s question with an answer, she simply continued to pepper the bag with jabs as she worked around it. Every once in a while, she’d deliver a thunderous blow with a hook or a body shot, and then reset deftly with her feet to begin her persistent tattoo.

    Kate got to her feet and made her way over to where Yelena was working on the bag. The brunette put a firm hand onto the back of the bag, steadying it for her friend. This wasn’t normally something one would have to do with a heavy bag, but today seemed to be an exception. As Yelena moved swift footedly, left and right, around the bag, Kate adapted and shifted to accommodate. She’d gotten pretty good at anticipating Yelena’s feints and attacks over the last month or so, not that she would be sharing that titbit of information with Yelena anytime soon.

    “I get it,” Kate said, softly.

    “Do you?” Yelena asked, not taking her eyes from the bag. It was a decent question, did she? Could she ever really hope to truly get Yelena. Of course, she could try, she could learn to anticipate her needs, understand the roots of her behaviours and the reasons for her pain, but could she ever truly get it? Probably not. That didn’t mean that she wouldn’t continue to try.

    Yelena struck a final blow that reverberated through Kate, and then dropped her guard as she breathed heavily, lungs on fire. “You don’t need to stand here you know?” Yelena explained, through ragged breaths.

    Kate shrugged, stubbornly. “But I want to.”

    “Fine,” Yelena muttered, with a shrug of her own. “Do whatever you want.” Punches began to pepper the bag again, then knees, and elbows, and jabs. A snap kick flashed high and Kate quickly pushed back, off and away from the bag.

    “Woah,” she said, with a faltering smile. “You really don’t like birthdays.”

    Within a flash, Yelena’s hands were on her, quicker than she’d ever experienced before. Kate was thrown to the mat with a vicious efficiency that said Yelena wasn’t playing anymore. Had they really been playing for the last few months?

    A forearm was pressed tightly under Kate’s chin, a strong hand pinned her right arm to the floor, and Yelena’s right knee pinned her left arm down. Sure, she was aware that threatening behaviour was her friend’s love language, but Kate got the feeling that this strayed a little outside of both of their comfort zones.

    “Do you want to fight?” Yelena asked, her voice much lower than it had been a moment earlier. She was close. Incredibly close. Yelena’s hot and angry breath tickled Kate’s now rather hot and angry cheeks.

    “Like a spar or a fight?” Kate managed; her voice much higher than it had been a moment earlier. Yelena was on her. She should have been scared. No, scratch that, she should have been pissed, but she wasn’t. She was distracted. Distracted by Yelena’s mindboggling flexibility, distracted by her incredibly impressive show of strength and distracted by exactly where she was sitting. “Come to think of it, a spa day might be a good way to work off some this bad juju you’ve got going on.” And maybe they could work out some other things too.

    Yelena’s nose crinkled in frustration, and her elbow thrust a little higher, up and underneath Kate’s chin.

    “Woah, woah, okay, okay! Truce,” Kate appealed, waving her pinned hands in surrender. “I won’t mention it again, okay? I’m sorry.” And Kate really was sorry. Sorry she’d even fucking bothered. Sorry she’d looked up her best friend’s birthday on the Avenger’s database, sorry she’d planned ahead, sorry she’d made plans and planned surprises, sorry she’d researched Russian birthday traditions, sorry she’d ordered food and gifts and experiences, sorry she’d wanted to give Yelena just a slice of the type of birthday she was used to.

    Yelena’s eyes were dark as she fell silent, and then the smallest flicker of realisation flashed across her features as her face softened. Her breathing slowly returned to a more normal rhythm and the elbow at Kate’s neck seemed to relent slightly. As quickly as she’d taken Kate down, Yelena had clambered off of the young Avenger and put some distance between herself and her friend. She began to unwrap her hands, back turned and in silence.

    “No need to be such a hurtful bitch about it.” Kate’s words echoed through the gym. They were met by silence from Yelena. Kate saw her friend shake her head, almost imperceptibly, as her chest heaved with a sigh.

    Kate swallowed the lump that had been building in her throat. Don’t get upset, don’t get upset. She isn’t worth it. But that was the problem, she was worth it, or at least that was what Kate had thought.

    “I’m sorry. I...” Yelena sighed once more and turned to face her friend. The hurt that she found in Kate’s eyes, in her face, in the way that she had unconsciously wrapped her arms around herself, stopped her in her tracks. Her body softened, her eyes filled with regret, and she quickly closed her difference between herself and Kate, as she reached for her friend, but Kate stepped back. “Shit, Kate, I am sorry. I shouldn’t have-”

    ‘No, you shouldn't have.”

    “I’m not good at...” Yelena paused, hoping to find the right words that would somehow make the situation okay again, make them okay again. “I just wish this day didn’t exist. Sometimes, I just wish it had never happened at all, you know?” Their eyes met again and Yelena smiled sadly. Kate hadn’t known that Yelena felt that way. “You’re teaching me how to be happy, and be normal and be more alive, but I don’t know how to be mad yet. I don’t know how to do that, if it’s not killing people.”

    “I would prefer it if you didn’t try and kill me.” Kate spoke, quietly with a small attempt at a smile. Yelena was grateful, her friend had given her an out. It was small, but it was there.

    “I’ll make a note for next year,” Yelena offered, before Kate closed the distance between the pair and folded her friend into a desperate hug. At first, Yelena’s body stiffened instinctually, not used to such intimate physical contact. Physical contact that was usually initiated for murder purposes only, but this, this was very different. Kate doubled down on her venture, drew Yelena even closer to her and stooped a little so that her chin gently brushed her friend’s shoulder. To Kate’s surprise, Yelena didn’t resist. The blonde’s body softened as she breathed out. Two hands came to rest in the small of Kate’s back as Yelena relaxed into the crook of her neck, her warm breath softly tickling the sensitive skin there.

    And there they stood. Two friends and two partners. Kate had never considered herself much of a hugger. Hugs had been hard to come by in the Bishop household. In fact, Kate would go as far to say that hugs had become some form of social currency, rather than a freely given show of comfort of affection. So, if Kate wasn’t used to hugging, she couldn’t imagine how much of a foreign concept it must have been for Yelena.

    “Can you forgive me?” Yelena mumbled, sheepishly into Kate’s neck. Kate wanted to scream. How could a person go from being so fucking terrifying to so fucking adorable within the space of two minutes.

    “I will forgive you on three conditions.”

    “Anything.”

    “Number one. Never do that again. I’m serious. I know I’m not often serious, but I am about this. That cannot happen again, do you understand?”

    “I understand. It will not happen again.” Yelena’s arms tightened around Kate and the tip of her nose brushed softly against Kate’s pulse point.

    “Number two, if you ever feel shitty about your existence on this Earth, you come to me. Agreed?” This time Yelena only managed to nod into their embrace. That was enough for Kate.

    “And thirdly,” Kate began, “You have to forgive for what I've done to your locker.”

    With a bewildered frown, Yelena pulled away from Kate, and their embrace was broken. “What have you done to my locker?”

    Yelena stared with dismay at her gym locker. “What did you do?” she asked, disbelievingly.

    “It’s your birthday.” Kate shrugged, as if it was the most obvious thing in the world.

    Yelena’s locker hand been filled with balloons, streamers and little pieces of Avenger themed confetti that she’d managed to Prime from the S.H.I.E.L.D. merch store. She thought it had been a pretty inspired purchase, she was beginning to think she’d been wrong.

    “You have to forgive me,” Kate pleaded/

    Yelena couldn’t help the disbelieving laugh that escaped her. “I forgive you,” she said as she shook her head.

    “Okay, good. Now I just need to cancel everything I had planned for today,” said Kate, as she chewed on her bottom lip and hastily scrolled through several rather sizeable orders that she’d place.

    Yelena groaned. Kate could tell that her friend was desperately trying to be more amiable about the whole Birthday situation, she could also tell that she was hating every fucking moment.

    “But I’ll sort it! I’ll sort it,” Kate reassured her, as she tucked her phone into her sports bra and grabbed a small trash can from the corner of the women’s changing rooms. Within moments, the entire contents of Yelena’s locker was in the trash. Easy, job done, Kate thought, as she shot her friend a triumphant smile. The Russian raised one incredibly restrained eyebrow. Oh shit. Kate dived back into the trash in a desperate attempt to retrieve Yelena’s belongings, which once found, were hastily returned to their rightful place. Kate smiled, sheepishly now. “Tada!” Kate gestured, “This is now a birthday free zone!”

    A small smile pulled at the corner of Yelena’s lips. Yelena Belova might not like birthdays, but she sure as hell seemed to like goofy, brunette Robin Hoods, when she wasn’t trying to mount them that was. Oh no, wait, mounting means something else entirely.

    “There is one more thing though…” Kate had to admit it to her friend, but she just knew that she was on safer ground here. If there’s one thing Yelena really couldn’t resist, even at the darkest of times, was a medium sized, incredibly fluffy, one eyed Labrador. “Lucky looks too good in a party hat, so you’re going to have to just put up with it.”

    The purest smile spread across her friend’s features and it did much to erase the heaviness that still weighed on Kate’s heart from their ‘interaction’ in the gym. “That, I can handle,” Yelena confirmed, happily. “I deserve it for trying to kill you.”

    “That was a pretty dick move. Friends don’t kill friends.” Kate was pretty sure they didn’t anyways.

    Yelena cringed, in silent disbelief of her actions. Kate had to admit, regretful Yelena was making her feel all sorts of better about the situation. ‘I just…” Yelena sighed as she struggled to find any words that would explain away the situation. She gave up with a groan and threw herself down on one of the changing room benches. “God, I just really don’t like birthdays. “

    “I knew it!,” Kate exclaimed, triumphantly, forgetting herself for a moment. “I knew you didn’t lik-” A sharp look from Yelena and the brunette quickly remembered herself again. Kate grimaced. “Sorry.” She just really enjoyed winning.

    The Russian smiled and nodded toward the space next to her on the bench. “Enough sorrys.”

    Kate plonked herself down next to her friend. “Sorry,” she whispered.

    Yelena rolled her eyes, “Idiot,” she muttered, good-naturedly, rested her head gently upon Kate’s shoulder and released a long, cathartic sigh. She fit, perfectly, Kate thought. She was really sweaty, but she fit, perfectly.

    Kate glanced down to where Yelena’s hand was resting, palm up, again the top of her thigh. She smiled at the simplicity of it, the ease of it. How had they become this familiar, how had it come this easy for an ex-child assassin and a rich kid from New York City? And it had been easy since the start, hadn’t it? Something had just fit from the moment they’d laid eyes on each other up on that roof, from the moment Yelena had wordlessly told her to hold her shot. They’d just fit. So, Kate gently wove her fingers between her friend’s and traced her thumb, soothingly across her palm.

    They both sat there, for quite some time, comfortable in the silence than passed between them. At some point, Yelena’s eyes had closed and her body had relaxed into Kate’s side. The silence was broken, however, when, to Kate’s surprise, Yelena went to speak.

    “When I was a kid, I had a few good years. I don’t remember all of it, I was little, but have a few really clear memories. Some good, some not so good.” Kate felt Yelena scoff a little, as if remembering a particularly nostalgic moment.

    "I broke my arm once, just playing on the swings with Natasha. My father was afraid to take me to the hospital. At the time I didn’t know why but looking back, he was probably afraid that our cover would be blown. He waited until my mother got home to take me, I was in so much pain and she was so angry,” Yelena laughed a little at the memory of her mother. From what Kate knew of her, Melina was a pretty fierce individual, Alexei perhaps not so much.

    “My best memory,” Yelena continued, a smile now evident in her voice, “My absolute best memory was my sixth birthday. I don’t have a birth certificate, not a real one, but my forged papers said that I was born October 14th, 1989. My Papa still insists he chose the date but he’s probably the biggest bullshitter you will ever meet.”

    “Sounds like the biggest asshole I’ll ever meet,” Kate muttered and Yelena pulled on her hand playfully. Their eyes met and for a fleeting moment, Kate could have sworn she’d seen Yelena’s eyes fall to her lips. No, Kate. That is irrational. And needy. And hopeless. And lovely.

    “He might be an asshole, but he’s my asshole.”

    “That’s awful, please never say that again.”

    “If I agree, can I go back to baring my soul to you?” Yelena asked, sardonically.

    “Oh, is that what you were doing? I didn’t know you had one,” Kate grinned.

    Bemused, Yelena shook her head and extracted herself from Kate. Never letting go of Kate’s hand, she repositioned herself on the bench by putting one knee up and the same foot tucked underneath. They were facing each other now, and Kate was just as happy about this situation as she was the previous one.

    The Russian glanced down at their entwined hands and smiled, melancholically. It was crazy how Yelena could get inside her head, read her thoughts, anticipate her next move or know the next dumb thing she’d say. She’d know when to encourage and when to comfort and she’d also know when a little tough love was needed; all because she could read Kate Bishop like a book. Kate’s problem was that the book of Yelena Belova was only published in Russian, and she only knew some swears.

    “We didn’t have a lot when we were in Ohio, but it was enough” Yelena explained, breaking the momentary silence. “My mother and Natasha made a cake. They even put my name on it, I loved it, I thought it was so special.” Yelena smiled and it was the purest thing Kate had ever seen. She found herself smiling along with Yelena, as if the memory were her own. “And my father spent what felt like hours outside with me, just flying me around like an aeroplane. Just stupid stuff you know?” Kate did know, her father had done the very same thing with her at their family home. Funny how they had lived very different lives, but love had touched their lives in very similar ways.

    “I got to drink soda and my papa gave me a sip of his beer, it was the best thing, it was so cool.” Kate’s heart felt giddy and tight with feeling. They were close; they shared food, space, dogs, beds and more and more often, they’d shared touch, but Yelena had never, ever shared her past. Perhaps the book of Yelena Belova wasn’t so unintelligible after all.

    “Natasha did my hair in all these crazy different styles, I’m sure it looked awful but I loved it. We felt like real sisters.” Yelena paused for a moment to catch herself as a rush of emotion threatened to wrestle her control from her. This was the first time Kate had seen her friend this way. She was vulnerable. “It all felt so real,” said Yelena, quietly, and Kate did the only thing she thought she could; she squeezed the blonde’s hand and grazed her thumb across her knuckles. “They even let me stay up late to watch a dodgy version of Jurassic Park on VHS. I fell asleep on the couch with my mother.” Yelena paused once more and her eyes met Kate’s. “For my next birthday, I was in the Red Room. I don’t dislike birthdays, Kate,” Yelena smiled, sadly, “But all I have is this memory. My only birthday. It’s special to me.”

    And just like that, Kate got it. She got it completely, and now she felt like a fucking idiot. “You’re worried that if you make new memories, this one won’t be special anymore?”

    Yelena nodded, slowly.

    “Weirdly, I kind of get that.” Kate said, and she did. She knew what it was like to be terrified of forgetting. She knew what it was like to have her most cherished memories stuck in the past, and it seemed only right that as Yelena had shared, as she’d made herself vulnerable, Kate should offer the same in return. That’s what a partnership was, right?

    “When Jack was with my mom, I was so resistant, I wanted him to be a bad guy so I could justify keeping him at arm's length. And that is because every year I remember less and less of my dad. I try to remember the big stuff still, and some of the little stuff too, but each year I lose more and more detail. Sometimes I forget that his eyes were blue like mine, not brown. Sometimes I smell his cologne when I’m out and I can’t remember the reason why it makes me feel so safe. And what if creating new memories with someone else forces those old memories out? What if there’s not enough room? What if, eventually, I can’t close my eyes and see his face or his smile? What if I forget him?” Kate asked, quietly as Yelena found her eyes. She gave Kate’s hand a squeeze and offered her a reassuring smile.

    “That is what photographs are for,” Yelena said, as her smile quickly turned into a grin and Kate couldn’t help but laugh at the absolute cheek of it. But the look in Yelena’s eyes, the way her hand was still clasped around Kate’s, the way she’d sat in earnest and listened to Kate’s testament, that told Kate that she had been heard. That wasn’t to say that Kate wouldn’t attempt to make Yelena feel bad for her comment.

    “You’re insensitive. I am hurt!”

    “Me, I am the insensitive one? That is hilarious.”

    “Yes, yes, and you’re super gross right now actually,” Kate said, nose wrinkled as she wrestled her hand out of Yelena’s and wiped it on her leggings, all the while failing to hide the mischievous smile that had invaded her features.

    “What? I thought you liked me sweaty.” Okay, they were in full blown banter mode now. But what was the saying? Many a true word is spoken in jest. Don’t blush, Kate. Don’t blush. Just think of a clap back, you got this.

    “Errr.” Terrible, okay, Plan B, change the subject. “Well, in the spirit of sensitivity,” Kate triumphantly segued.

    “Uh huh.”

    “There may be a few birthday things that I can’t really cancel for later.” And just like that, Kate changed the subject to a potentially even more awkward one.

    Yelena narrowed her eyes, sceptically. “Okay…” she said, prompting Kate to elaborate.

    “One of them is a surprise.”

    “Why can’t you cancel it?”

    “Because…” Kate realised this was an atrocious explanation, but also, any explanation she did give would give the surprise away, and she really, really didn’t want to do that.

    “Have you paid any money?”

    “No, but-”

    “Then cancel it.” Yelena said, matter-of-factly, as if, just like that, Kate could cancel a birthday surprise five weeks in the making. There was a slight pause where Kate considered her position. Cancel it, that was probably a no because the alternative was scary. Lie about cancelling it, those consequences were scary too. Or bide time, which was really just a fancy way of saying, ‘put off having to make the decision’.

    “You know what,” Kate said, quickly, “I’ll see what I can do.” Yelena’s eyes narrowed even more and Kate could only manage an unconvincing smile.

    “Hmm?”

    “What are the other things? You said a few things.” Nothing got past Yelena Belova, she wasn’t just a pretty punch-in-the face.

    “Well,” Kate began, cautiously. “There’s already a freezer full of frozen margaritas, I bought extra cream for White Russians, and Lucky looks really cute in a party hat so I won’t lie to you, I love you but I won’t be accepting any push back there.”

    There was a moment of quiet, as Yelena seemed to be weighing up whether to murder Kate or humour here. She sighed a little, and to Kate’s relief, relented. “Fine. That does actually sound pretty cute.”

    “Argh,” Kate exclaimed in untamed excitement. “You won’t regret this. HE. IS. ADORABLE.”

    “Don’t make me regret it,” Yelena warned, now with a wagging finger and frown that couldn’t compete with her smile. Kate grinned; she had a feeling that today was going to be a good day. It was going to be the best non birthday Yelena had ever had.

    “Now get up, come on,” Kate grabbed Yelena by the wrist and pulled, hard. Yelena didn’t budge. “Come on,” Kate pulled again, and received a look that said I will murder you and hide your body in the lockers. The brunette just rolled her eyes at her friend who was still sat, stubbornly on the benches. Yelena was a puppy, not a Kate Bishop killer. “Get a shower and let’s get home. I promise you, you’re going to enjoy today so much that you’re totally going to forget it’s your birthday.”

    “Kate,” Yelena warned. Kate was having none of it.

    “Just shower and meet me when you’re ready,” Kate said, before leaning down and placing a gentle kiss atop Yelena’s head. The taste of salt immediately invaded Kate’s senses, but it was worth it to see Yelena’s stubborn face soften. “I’ll be in the breakout room, Samus Arun is calling.”

    “Who?” Yelena asked, perhaps a little too quickly.

    “My girlfriend,” Kate explained, as if it was the most natural thing in the world.

    Yelena’s brow wrinkled in amusement. “Huh, I didn’t know you had a girlfriend.”

    “She’s super-hot.”

    “Uh huh.”

    “And a total badass.”

    “Wow,” Yelena said, her voice thick with sarcasm, as she peeled off her sweat laden black vest to reveal a plain black sports bra underneath. Yelena was quite a fan of black, so was Kate it seemed as her eyes refused to fall anywhere but the item of clothing in question. “Could I take her?” Yelena asked and Kate couldn't help but smile at how quickly her friend had wanted to resort a physical show of dominance.

    “That is a great question,” And it really was. Kate’s second favourite fictional alien killer vs Kate’s first favourite ex-assassin. She took a moment to mull it over before answering. “You know what? I'm really not sure but I know I would pay to see that fight.”

    Kate turned the key in the lock and cautiously peered round the door into her apartment? She’d panic texted Grills whilst Yelena had been in the shower, Abort decorations, abort decorations. Fanny Lover does not do birthdays, I repeat, Fanny Lover does not do birthdays. To her relief, the apartment, which Kate had begged Grills to decorate, was absolutely, one hundred percent decoration free.

    The familiar scratching of doggy claws across hardwood floors brought a huge smile to Kate’s face as she pushed her way into the apartment, followed by Fanny Lover herself. The one-eyed golden retriever closed the difference between him and his momma, and leapt up, whining in joyous delight.

    “Oh, good boy,” Kate gushed, as she threw her holdall to the floor and sunk to her knees to dote on her baby more effectively. “Hello baby hello, I know, I know, it’s been too long, I know,” Kate cooed into fur and kisses. “Your mommas will get a car soon and then we can have all the adventures.” Yelena dumped her bag down next to Kate’s tearing Lucky’s attention from the brunette. Kate signed and rolled her eyes. Their moment had passed and the usurper’s time had come. “Yes, yes, your favourite is home too.”

    “Hello boy!” Yelena said, through surprised little laughs as Lucky made several excited attempts to jump into her arms. She leant down and brought him into a tight hug, in which he licked her ear, hair and side of her face uncontrollably. “You are a good boy and your momma was right, you do look very cute in a party hat.”

    “Right? I just can’t bring myself to take it off of him. Don’t make me,” Kate turned to Yelena and begged, her bottom lip quivering dramatically. “You’re not that much of a bad person, are you?”

    Yelena weight up Kate’s request with a little teasing, downturned smile. “Hmm. It’s borderline but no, the hat can stay.”

    “You hear that baby,” Kate said, holding Lucky’s wonderfully happy face in her hands, “Your hat stays.” Yelena rolled her eyes and grabbed Kate’s bag from the floor to lug it upstairs. “She’s soft really,” Kate whispered to her golden boy with a little mischievous smile.

    “Right, first things first,” Kate called up to Yelena with a wiggle of her eyebrows that went unseen, “Margarita?

    “I should probably eat first,” the blonde called down, and she was right, she probably should after the kind of session Yelena had put in at the gym, but and it was a big but, it was her non birthday and there was a lot of frozen margaritas in the freezer.

    “But it’s your b-,” Nope Kate, stop. “It’s your body and of course you need to look after it, so, will grab some...pizza.” It wasn’t exactly my-body-is-a-temple fare but with the amount of sprints Yelena had done, Kate was pretty sure she could afford the calorific intake, and she was also prety sure that the Russian deserved the indulgence. “I will be back, ten minutes tops, I promise,” Kate called, as Yelena made her way back downstairs. “Pepperoni? All the meats? Extra cheese? All of the above?”

    “No pineapple?” Yelena asked, a little surprised at Kate’s omission.

    Kate shook her head, hands on hips. “Don’t make me say it.”

    “Say what?” Yelena asked, not so innocently, and shrugged.

    “That is not fair, I am going now,” Kate said, as she grabbed her keys and wallet from the side. “Can you pick out something you want to watch, whilst I’m down there?” She called, behind her.

    “I will certainly do my best,” Yelena agreed.

    “Okay. Bye, bye, bye, bye.” Kate said as she rushed out the door, and made her way downstairs to Herman’s. After careful consideration at the counter, Kate decided that the best decision was to make no decision, and got an extra-large pizza with as much on as possible, plus cheesy garlic bread, stuffed jalapenos, and some loaded fries. There was a lot of cheese involved, thankfully cheese was one of Yelena’s favourite things.

    With her coveted bounty in hand, Kate quickly made her way back upstairs, and let herself into the apartment with her and Yelena’s food carefully balanced in one hand. To Kate’s surprise, Yelena had already made herself comfortable on the coach, feet up underneath a fleecy purple blanket, with Lucky draped lazily across her lap, laptop set up on the coffee table, and a margarita in hand. Kate raised a questioning eyebrow.

    Yelena shrugged. “I just thought, fuck it, you know?” The blonde said, hosting the cocktail in the air nonchalantly.

    “Yeeeessss,” Kate said with glee as rushed to the freezer, loaded up her arms up with even further indulgences, captured a cup between her teeth and hustled over to where Yelena was sat.

    “Lucky has settled,” Yelena pointed out, “And you know what they say about letting sleeping dogs lie, so, you will now have to bring me whatever my heart desires.”

    “Anything for you,” Kate smiled and earned a happy smile in return.

    “Pizza?” Yelena asked, her excitement for meaty, cheesy goodness dancing in her eyes.

    “Starting with pizza.”

    Three quarters of a pizza, an entire cheesy garlic bread, several jalapeno poppers and three episodes of Queer Eye later, Kate and Yelena sat, snuggled into each other’s sides, full, satiated and if not a little tipsy. Kate smiled. All things considered, Yelena’s non birthday was turning out to be a pretty great day. Apparently, all one needed to make a day special was good food, good drink and good company. She felt her phone begin to buzz insistently inside her hoodie pocket, and fished underneath the blankets to dig it out. With a glance to the screen her stomach dropped. Shit. Shit, shit, shit. She’d completely forgotten. Well, perhaps not completely, but when Yelena had said to cancel all surprises, there was one specific surprise that Kate was more terrified to actually cancel, than face the wrath of Yelena for not doing so.

    Yelena noticed the change in her friend’s demeanour and turned to face her. “Everything okay?”

    Kate grimaced. They’d got home, they’d got pizza, they’d got a little drunk and then she’d completely forgotten there was no way out of it. She was going to have to come clean. It had been a good job she’d set an alarm the night before, because the last thing she’d want to do was miss a call from Yelena’s mother. That woman terrified her.

    “So, you remember that surprise you told me to cancel.”

    “There was no specific surprise. Just all of them,” Yelena shrugged, as if it were easy to cancel surprises that had been planned months in advance.

    “Well, there was one that I couldn’t actually cancel” Kate admitted, with an inward cringe.

    Yelena’s brow furrowed in confusion, a frustration. “But I asked you,” she said, in a way that made Kate’s heart break, just a little. The last thing today was about, was upsetting, but they had just been so excited.

    “I know and can we just say that I fucked up and move on?” Kate asked, a little desperately. “They were so looking forward to it I kind of feared for my life cancelling on them.”

    Yelena’s eyes narrowed in suspicion. “Kate, what did you do?”

    Kate laughed a little, nervously as her phone began to vibrate in her hand once more. This time, it wasn’t an alarm. She looked down at it in trepidation, the caller ID was blocked. Kate?” came Yelena’s questioning voice yet again.

    The brunette swallowed, steeled herself and swiped. “Hi!” she exclaimed, down the phone, with a nervous cheer as she extracted herself from Yelena on the couch, apologised profusely to Lucky for disturbing his snooze, and clambered forward towards the laptop. “Right on time.” Yelena threw Kate a questioning look and tried to listen, intently.

    “Is that-?”

    Kate took the phone from her ear and stuck it on speaker. “I’m just going to put you on speaker. Did you get my link?”

    “Yes, Kate Bishop. Thank you,” came Melina’s voice down the phone. Melina had only ever referred to Kate as Kate Bishop, and that hadn’t surprised her one bit.

    “Mom?!” Yelena asked, disbelievingly as Kate navigated through an obscenely large number of open tabs to the encrypted chat window that she’d conspired with Happy to get set up. With a quick refresh, and a tap on the ‘join call’ button, Kate dialled them into the waiting room.

    “You just need to press the button, Alexei,” Came Melina’s voice from Kate’s phone. “Hello, darling. Yes, it’s me. Alexei, the big green button. Click on it.”

    “I’m trying,” Yelena grinned at the sound of her father’s voice, and shook her head, fondly.

    “Click the button!” Said Melina in exasperation. Kate chanced a look at her friend amongst the chaos. Yelena’s cheeks were a little flushed from the alcohol, but her eyes were alive, moving between Kate’s phone and the laptop screen, waiting with anticipation, for her parents’ faces to appear on the screen before. That was the moment Kate knew she had done good. Birthday or no birthday, Yelena Belova was happy and that was all that mattered.

    The call flickered to life, and two curious faces appeared on Kate’s laptop screen. They were huddled together, lit in the relative darkness, by the light of whatever devices they were using to connect to the call.

    “Fanny, Fanny come here!” Melina called to Yelena’s dog, who must have been somewhere offscreen.

    “My girl!” Boomed Alexei.

    “Alexei, get Fanny,” Melina gave her partner a forceful shove. Before he could protest, she administered another more insistent nudge and shooed him away. “Go, go.” He went off screen with all the enthusiasm of a teenager being forced to take his little sister to Homecoming.

    Yelena shuffled to the front of the sofa, with Lucky still lounged across her lap, and leaned closer to the screen. “Hey mama,” she said softly, as Kate found her hand had come to rest, quite inadvertently, in the small of her back.

    “Hello, darling,” Melina smiled.

    "You look so little.”

    “Are we on the television?”

    “No, you’re on Kate’s laptop,” Yelena turned to Kate. “Would this work on a TV?”

    “I guess so, I’m sure we could make it work,” Kate shrugged.

    “We should get a TV.” Wow, from no surprises to we should get a TV. Keeping up with these Black Widows was hard work, for both herself and Alexei it seemed.

    “Where is your father?” Melina muttered to herself. “One moment. Alexei!” Yelena’s mother shouted into the darkness. “Alexei! How long does it take to find a dog in a bungalow?”

    Yelena could only grin wider and shake her head.

    “We’re coming, we’re coming!” Alexei could be heard calling, before he reappeared next to Melina with an incredibly excited American Akita. “Yelena! How good it is to see you!” Alexei said, speaking far more loudly than he needed to for video call, but Yelena only had eyes for Fanny.

    “Fanny!” Yelena practically screamed with delight at seeing her dog. “Hello! What a beautiful girl, I miss you so much!” Getting Fanny to the United States and acclimating her and Lucky had immediately become Kate’s next mission. “This is Lucky look,” Yelena took the Pizza Dog’s paw and waved it, rather adorably, at the screen. “You are going to be best of friends, I promise.” And just like that, Kate Bishop died of assault to the heart. Rest in Peace Kate, rest in peace. “I do hope mama and papa are taking good care of you.”

    “The best care, aren’t we darling,” Melina said, as she leaned in and wrapped her arms around Fanny. Yelena’s dog seemed suitably pleased with the attention.

    “Yelena, it’s your father, Alexei.” The rather large, bearded fellow waved from the screen, trying to elbow his way into the conversation with his daughter. “Yelena? Hello?”

    “Oh, hey papa.” Yelena said, before placing a small kiss atop of Lucky’s head, and fussing with his ears.

    “Kate here tells us it’s your birthday!” Alexei boomed, once more, clearly quite oblivious of how awful that sounded. Kate cringed, inwardly, at the B word, but to her relief, Yelena simply rolled her eyes.

    “Which of course we knew darling,” Melina jumped in, trying but failing to cover for Alexei’s mistake, “We just wanted this to be a surprise.”

    “You’ve never known before,” Yelena said, indifferently.

    “That is not true!” Alexei protested, “I have your birthday, tattooed on my back!

    “No you don’t.”

    “I do!” Alexei declared, as he tore his shirt off, much to everyone else’s dismay, turned his back to the camera and pointed aggressively to an array of tattoos on his back.

    Yelena sighed and went back to fussing Lucky. “That is not my birthday.”

    “Of course, it is. You think I don’t know my own daughter’s birthday?” Oh no. Kate tried not to let her inward cringe become an outward cringe. This call, which she had previously been giving herself a pat on the back for setting up, was going south, and quick.

    “That is the day the USSR was dissolved,” Yelena explained coolly, with an amused smile. Well, maybe not that far south.

    “Why would I have that on my back?” Melina could only roll her eyes, much like her daughter.

    “Because you’re an idiot?” Yelena retorted, as her smile grew wider, and Kate breathed a little easier.

    “I think now is probably a good time for me to erm, leave you guys to it.”

    Yelena turned to her and blinked. “You’re going?’

    “It’s your family time,” Kate explained, with a reassuring smile, which earned her an understanding one in return.

    ‘’Just give me a call when you’re done okay?” Kate asked. Yelena nodded gladly as Kate got out from under the blanket again and placed another kiss upon Yelena’s head. This time, she tasted of sandalwood and shea butter, rather than sweat and indignation.

    Kate turned to the laptop and gave Yelena’s parents a small wave and a broad smile. “Lovely to meet you, as long as I don’t get suspended by S.H.I.E.L.D. for breaking a tonne of protocols, maybe we can speak again soon.”

    “Goodbye Kate Bishop!” Came Alexei’s thundering voice.

    “A pleasure to put a face to the name, my dear, hope to speak to you soon” smiled Melina, and after a few more waves and goodbyes, Kate collected one more slice of pizza and padded her way up the stairs to her bed. She threw herself down and grabbed her headphones, so that Yelena and her family could talk in private. Just before she opened up Netflix on her phone and toggled the noise cancelling function of her headphones, she heard Melina’s voice ring through the apartment.

    “That girl is far too sweet for you.”

    Take your headphones off.

    Kate blinked as the text pinged up on screen part way through her third episode of Blown Away. What a fucking show that was by the way. She clicked her phone shut, sat up and whipped her headphones from her ears.

    “Kate! Kate!” Came Yelena’s insistent voice.

    With a frown, Kate hopped off her bed and looked down over the balcony to the far side of her apartment. There was Yelena, sat on her sofa, her arms outstretched with a large golden retriever sprawled out across her lap.

    “Please free me,” Yelena appealed. Evidently, her call had ended a while ago. Kate grinned in amusement and the blonde pouted.

    “You could just move him,’ Kate suggested, rather unhelpfully.

    Yelena gasped in shock at the suggestion. “I could never move him, look at him he is sleeping.”

    Kate chuckled as she made her way downstairs towards her friend. “He is not asleep,” Kate said a she took the final slice of pizza from the box, “Watch.” Kate waved the slice of pizza a little out of the dog’s reach. “Hey, Pizza dog,” she whispered, as Lucky’s one eye peeked open, “Pizza for you.” In an instant Lucky was up and pushing himself off Yelena, who made a few unhappy grunts at being trodden on. He trotted over to Kate and snapped the pizza from her hands happily. Yelena on the other hand frowned unhappily.

    “Wow,” Kate said, as she made her way into the kitchen and to the cupboard under the sink, “Your shirt is like a carpet.”

    “Well, he’s your dog.” Yelena muttered back as Kate returned from the kitchen, lint roller in hand, and started in an attempt to lift the dog hair from the blonde’s upper torso.

    “What are you doing?” Yelena asked, perturbed.

    “I’m lint rolling you,” and just as the words had left her mouth, Kate realised how ludicrous they had sounded. “And I’ll stop, I’ll stop that.” She put the lint roller on the coffee table, under Yelena’s watchful stare, and retreated to the kitchen in hope that she could distract Yelena with more booze. “More margarita? I’ve got some classic, wild berry, ooh there’s a watermelon left.”

    Yelena threw the blanket off and followed Kate into the kitchen. “I’m not mad at you. You do not need to hide from me. It’s just that no one has ever tried to lint roller me before.”

    “So… watermelon?” Kate asked, nervously.

    Her friend smiled, warmly. “Yes, watermelon is very nice, thank you.” And just like that, before Kate could even comprehend what was happening, they were hugging again. This time, Kate could tell that Yelena was up on her tip toes, and again sandalwood and shea butter gripped her senses. “This is all very nice,” Yelena spoke softly, into Kate’s shoulder and gripped Kate a little tighter. They held each other for a moment longer, and Kate took another opportunity to simply breath Yelena in. Since when had she become so soft? Sure, Kate Bishop wore her heart on her sleeve, it was kind of her super power; her openness, her willingness to talk to anyone and her ability to empathise with everyone. But that had always been people letting her in, never the other way round.

    After small moment longer, both women broke their hug, and Kate hurriedly delved into the freezer to retrieved the watermelon margs.

    “Your parents were okay?” Kate asked, as she handed Yelena a fresh drink.

    “Thank you, and yes, they were tolerable as always,” Yelena quipped as she leaned back against Kate’s fridge.

    “Your dad is quite the character.”

    “My dad is an asshole but-”

    “He’s your asshole?” Kate grinned and Yelena shook her head. “Yeah, I know the feeling.”

    “At least your mom has credit cards.”

    "To absent mothers!” Kate raised her cocktail.

    “To absent mothers!” Yelena chimed in, with a rasping laugh. The blonde thrust her watermelon marg into the air and then took and hearty sip of it. She was enjoying herself, on her birthday and Kate was grateful. So grateful that really, Yelena had embraced all of it. The video call with the parents, the drinking, the food; Yelena had embraced every second. But Kate had one more surprise for Yelena, a surprise that she wasn’t sure she should give.

    “More Queer Eye or...?” Yelena started but glanced round to find Kate deep in thought. “Is everything okay, Kate?”

    “What?” Kate blinked, she hadn’t realised she’d gotten so lost in thought. “Fine, fine, I er...”. Just ask her Kate, ask her, if she doesn’t want it, she says no and that’s that. Kate sighed. “I actually had another surprise lined up. It’s something that I’ve been thinking about giving you for a while and I thought that today would be the best day for that but obviously, I was totally wrong,” Kate explained, in a bit of a whirlwind.

    Yelena raised an eyebrow and Kate realised that she’d stopped breathing. The Russian really did have a pretty incredible hold on her. “Pour me a second margarita and let’s get this over with." Kate’s face lit up with a mix of extreme happiness and disbelief.

    “Really?”

    “Do you want me to change my mind?” Yelena asked, only half joking.

    “No, no, I’ve just got to grab it, I’ll be back. One second. You get comfortable. Eat pizza. Get drunk.” Kate called behind her as she dashed upstairs to root around for the surprise.

    Yelena frowned. “Is it really going to take you that long to-”

    “Got it!” Kate came racing back down stairs, holding a small packet, triumphantly above her head. Yelena met her at the couch and Kate nervously placed a carefully wrapped gift onto the coffee table. Kate breathed out heavily in trepidation. This was a risk, she knew it. This was a huge risk, but there was something about it that just felt too right to not go through with it. Kate swallowed as she and Yelena retook their seats, next to each other on the couch.

    “I’m going to be straight with you, this is didn’t cost me anything,” Kate felt the need to explain. “The other stuff that I’d planned was the expensive stuff, so I don’t want you to think that I didn’t spend-”

    “Kate,” Yelena stopped her with a hand upon her knee, “I don’t care about how much things cost.”

    Kate bit her lip nervously as her friend smiled and began to carefully unwrap the gift. This is a bad idea, this is a bad idea.

    “I just hope it’s okay. With everything that you’ve said today, I’m not sure that…” Shit, this was dumb. “Maybe you should open it another time,” Kate wrung her hands together, itching to snatch it away from Russian hands and hide it and herself upstairs, under her bed for good.

    “I’m sure anything you get me will be...” The wrapping paper fell open, revealing some slightly beaten-up packaging, and inside lay a perfectly preserved Natasha Romanoff action figure. “Perfect,” Yelena’s voice fell and her hands froze. Silence filled the room and Kate felt the need to explain, to make this okay.

    “She was mine but er, I thought it was maybe more fitting for you to have her.” Once more, Kate was met with deafening silence, as Yelena reached out to take the boxed figure in her hands. “I think it’s pretty hard to get hold of now,” Kate swallowed, anxiously, “They didn’t make that many of Clint and Natasha.” Kate thought she heard a small murmur of disappointed agreement, but she couldn't be sure. Yelena turned the box over in her hands, her face unreadable, apart from her eyes. Her eyes were dark with emotion, and were working at a million miles per hour to take in every inch of the packaging that lay before her. Kate thought it best to continue.

    “My mom got me Hawkeye for Christmas,” Kate explained. “But like the prick kid I was, I decided that Clint Barton by himself wasn’t good enough, I wanted the deadly Black Widow too so I could play with them together. That poor woman,” Kate laughed a little to herself, ruefully, “I dragged her all over New York City to find a Black Widow. We were out for hours the day after Christmas. Ended up finding her in Long Island. Say what you want about Eleanor Bishop but that is one dedicated mom.” Kate stole another glance at Yelena. She released the cardboard from the bottom of the box and slid the plastic tray that held the collectible, out.

    “I know that you were probably still with the Red Room when all this stuff came out, after New York was invaded?’ Yelena nodded slowly as if she had heard Kate from a great distance away. “So, I thought that maybe you’d never had the chance to get your hands on one, and they’re pretty much a collector's items now so, you should have mine. It’s only right.” Kate smiled, a smile that went unseen. Yelena’s eyes never left the figurine. “Oh,” Kate remembered, a little too excitedly, “And what’s really cool is if you press the button that back she er, she, says stuff.”

    Yelena’s eyes flashed to meet Kate’s. The desperate grief that Kate found there was heart breaking. “Really?” Yelena whispered. “Is it her?”

    ‘Oh totally,” and Kate was sure of it, she remembered the commercial as if it were yesterday. “When you put her with Clint, it unlocks a couple of unique phrases which is actually really kinda cool. Do you wanna hear it?” Kate asked.

    “I don’t…” Yelena caught herself, before her emotion got the better of her. “I don’t know.”

    “Well,” Kate placed a reassuringly gentle hand upon Yelena’s knee. “You don’t have to. And you don’t have to keep her, if it’s not what you want. You get to decid-”

    < Thank you for your cooperation>

    Natasha Romanoff’s voice echoed through Kate’s apartment and Yelena choked back a shuddering breath.

    “It sounds like her,” Yelena whispered, as dark eyes began to fill with tears.

    “It does?” Kate asked, warmly.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded as her emotions got the better of her and sobs began to wrack her body. Kate quickly scooted closer to her friend and engulfed her into what she hoped was the warmest most comforting hug that had ever been hugged. Tears fell upon Kate’s shoulder, as she rested her cheek atop Yelena’s head. “It’s her stupid voice,” Yelena laughed through her tears and Kate didn’t think she could hold Yelena any tighter. What a revelation she was turning out to be.

    Yelena must have pressed the button again as < Avengers do whatever it takes > sounded from in-between the two of them. The meaning wasn’t lost on Kate. Natasha had done whatever it took to save the world and to save her sister. She felt Yelena’s right hand grip her back, as another wave of sobs broke over her body.

    “I’m sorry,” Kate whispered. “I didn’t mean to upset you.” And it was true, she hadn’t. Of course, she’d know there had been potential, giving a friend an action figure of their dead sister would probably stir a few emotions no matter what day of the week it was, but until that day, Kate had never known Yelena to be so vulnerable.

    “No, no,” Yelena pulled back quickly, sniffing and hastily wiping her eyes. “This is sweet, I love it, I do.” Yelena ran her fingers across the figure, taking in every jump and ridge, every contour of her sister’s face, as if committing it to memory all over again. “I’m just so proud. That she is my sister,” Kate nodded, and smiled. “She was my hero you know?” Another flurry of tears began their hot decent across Yelena’s flushed cheeks.

    “Hey, hey come here. I got you.” Kate pulled Yelena into her once more, and that’s how the two of them sat, for some time; as Yelena’s sobs grew less frequent, and the emotion that had gripped the Russian’s body had somewhat subsided. Kate sighed into their embrace. They really did just fit.

    After a few moments longer, Yelena released her grip on Kate and pulled away ever so slightly, sniffing somewhat fiercely. “Here you are trying to do a nice thing and here I am crying all over you.” She looked sheepish, it was cute.

    “I hate to break it to you, but badass bitches gotta cry too. Especially when they lose people they love.”

    “Am I snotty? Do I have snot?” Yelena asked, crinkling her nose.

    “No, you’re perfect,” Kate smiled. What the fuck was happening to her? Why did she say these things?

    “Because you can tell me if do.”

    Kate chuckled. “I promise to always tell you if you have booger, but right now? You do not.” Yelena smiled and they fell back into each other’s embrace momentarily.

    “Oh!” Kate remembered, suddenly. “I have something else for you, it’s in the kitchen.” Kate dragged herself away from Yelena, it was possibly one of the hardest things she’d ever had to do in her entire life. Kate could practically feel Yelena’s eyeroll as she pottered into the kitchen. Now, where had Grills hidden it? She opened her top cupboards and glanced inside. These were the obvious places to hide something from a short ass person, but obviously Grills did not share her logic. Kate frowned, after searching a few more cupboard and coming up with nothing. Maybe Kate would have to drop him a text. “I’m sorry babe!” Kate called, as she turned to-

    Lips, lips were on hers. Lips that belonged to a 5’3, blonde, Russian ex-assassin. For a moment Kate couldn’t think, or act or do. She couldn’t move. Yelena was kissing her. Her Yelena. Her Yelena was touching her face. Her Yelena was stood on her tip toes, reaching for her lips again, and so Kate let her take them. She stooped down to breathe her in, to wrap her arms tightly around her waist, to kiss her back. But just as quickly and unexpectedly as it had started, the kiss was over.

    “I’m going to go to the bathroom,” Yelena said, almost inaudibly, and then she was gone.

    Fuck, what just happened? No, seriously, what just happened? Her friend, she kissed her friend. Or her friend had kissed her? That was right, right? Her friend who wasn’t into women kissed her, the not gay one. That wasn’t confusing. No, not at all. Just like how everything Kate had been feeling toward Yelena over the last two months hadn’t been confusing. Kate needed to breathe, she needed to do something, not Yelena, something else. Kate, stop. But Kate couldn’t stop. Her brain was a runaway train, and her mental capacity was tied to the tracks.

    Was Yelena okay in the bathroom? Should she go and check? Kate, stop. Would they get to kiss again, or what that it? What if she comes back through that door and says it was a mistake, or that she was drunk or emotional and they have to go back to how it was before? And what if they couldn’t? And why had it felt like they fit? Fuck.

    The bathroom door opened. Kate’s heart stood still as an apprehensive Yelena stepped out. She’d neatened her eye make-up, which had run a little from her previous crying. She still looked beautiful. She smiled a small, nervous smile, and Kate’s stomach flip flopped. The brunette looked down at her hands; somehow, she was holding more margarita mix.

    “Um,” Kate swallowed. “Do you want another drink?”

    Yelena shook her head. “I still have plenty,” she explained, quietly, as she pointed to the glass and a half of watermelon, slowly melting on the coffee table.

    “Oh, no problem,” Kate said, smiling awkwardly.

    "I’m sorry I did that.” And there it was, the regret. Kate’s heart began to ache.

    “No, don’t be,” the brunette blurted.

    “I should have asked.” Kate’s runaway train brain slammed on the brakes. If Yelena regretted not asking, did that mean that she didn’t regret the kiss itself?

    “I mean, consent is important...”

    “I just felt…” Yelena caught herself, she shook her head. “But you are straight and I am complicated.”

    “Yelena, I’m just gonna put something out there, okay?” The blonde nodded, uncertainly, and Kate steeled herself for what she was about to say. She was pretty straight, a lot of the time. Men were hot, and sometimes women were hot too but mainly men. Sure, she’d been with women, and sure, it had been a pretty great experience, both times, but she’d always gravitated back towards guys. That was until Yelena had physically forced her way into Kate’s life. Everything about her was attractive, and beautiful and exciting and smart and sexy and yes, hot too. Everything about her had challenged her expectations of what she wanted, and it turned out that what Kate wanted more than anything was the connection that they shared. This inexplicable connection. All Kate wanted to do was explore it, together. Just spit it out, Kate. She took a moment, and then jumped. “When you kissed me, I didn’t feel that straight.

    Yelena blinked, was it hope that danced in her eyes. “You didn’t?”

    “No, you idiot, that’s why I kissed you back.”

    ‘So, it’s okay?” Wow, she was adorable.

    “Yeah, totally, it’s totally okay.” Kate thought to take Yelena’s hands in hers but realised she was still holding the damn bags of frozen margaritas.

    “You just don’t seem okay.”

    “I mean, I was a bit surprised. You surprised me. It was a good surprise,” Kate explained hastily, “But er, as surprises go, weirdly, probably the biggest of the day.”

    A small laughed escaped Yelena, and Kate felt the worry around her heart recede further. “But a good surprise, right?” The blonde asked.

    “Oh, yeah, really good.” It was really good. "Unexpected, but not unwelcome,” Kate clarified, dorkily. Kate looked at the distance between them. It was too great, and that needed to be rectified, stat. “Do you want to sit and watch a movie?”

    Yelena nodded, with a little tired smile. She had been through a lot today. “Sounds good.”

    “And if I kissed you during the movie, would that be okay?” Kate asked, as she dumped the margarita mix on the side and led a nodding Yelena slowly back to the couch. Fuck the margaritas, let them melt.

    Metamorphosis: One Chapter Notes Welcome to the mind of Yelena Belova. And here’s your accompaniment.

    https://open.spotify.com/track/66TMmu4ve50PliM4314Vqd I wrote a little something this evening, it’s an absolute change of pace but will hopefully keep you intrigued and satisfied until the next proper update! Apologies for the angst, I can’t help it.

    Thank you to everyone for reading and commenting. I’m so grateful. Enjoy! See the end of the chapter for more notes A light flickered at the end of the darkened corridor. Yelena shielded her eyes from the visual assault. Every flicker was blinding, every rhythmless pop and buzz of electricity made her flinch as the sound crawled underneath her skin. The moment her eyes would adjust to the darkness, the fluorescent light would flash brightly overhead once more, and her vision would burst brightly with stars, only to fall quickly into a state of absolute, blinding darkness. The assassin pressed herself against the wall, she would have to feel her way to the door that she knew was there, the door that she could see in her mind’s eye. Even if her eyes refused to show it to her, it couldn’t elude her; she’d walked through it many times before. She reached with a bloodied, outstretched hand, flat against the wall, fingertips taking in the rough and familiar wallpaper. Next was a light switch. She knew that flicking it would be no good, she knew what would happen, but her left hand fought against her logic. Flip the switch, you’ll be able to see her if you just flip the switch. As always, Yelena couldn’t resist the compulsion.

    The explosion shattered her senses, and she cried out as crystalline teardrops rained down violently from above. Instinctually, she dropped to the floor and threw her arms up in a desperate attempt to protect herself from the barrage. Ice cold droplets bombarded her skin, soaked through her tactical gear, through her flesh, through her bones. Her chest became tight as her body temperature plummeted, and Yelena could see her breath clearly. Get up. You know you can get up. She rose to one knee, put a steadying hand against the wall and began to haul herself to her feet.

    Another flash of white and another flood of light burned her retinas, but it wasn’t going to stop her. She’d been here before, so many times. Everything was familiar, but everything was unexpected.

    Just find the door, she’s here, just find the door, Yelena told herself as she urged her body to move further down the corridor. With her eyes closed, her hands felt for the picture rail which was now wet with rain or her own blood. Yelena wasn’t quite sure which. It wouldn’t matter anyways. All that mattered was finding her.

    The sound of gunshots rung through the air as the light flashed once more. But it was no longer the flash of a fluorescent light, it was a muzzle flash. Another concussive shot reverberated down the corridor and a wave of sound threatened to send Yelena back to where she’d started. But in the flash of the muzzle, she’d seen it. She’d seen the door. Yelena wasn’t turning back. Another flash and it was clearer this time, as the light escaped momentarily from under the doorway. She had to persevere, just like she always did. She would reach her, this time she would reach her in time.

    Yelena staggered forward against the shock and awe that was bombarding her body, with new found purpose. She could make it, she could. Another flash and the door was closer, another shot and the handle was just within her reach.

    Brass found her fingertips. The corridor fell silent. The light flickered for the last time and then fell to black. Yelena took a steadying breath, gripped the handle with intent, and turned it. Once released the door swung open. She could hear her heart, it beat slowly, always slowly. She’d been here so many times, nothing came as a surprise anymore. The kitchen stood empty and still. Crockery lay smashed, cutlery littered the floor. The gas hob was still lit, and flickered in the breeze from the smashed windows, but the water, and the pot intended for it, lay discarded and pooling on the linoleum floor. Water met red watercolour, and the two danced and intertwined, until they became one whole, in the shadow of the last chair left standing.

    She was too late. Just like she always had been, just like she always would be. Too late. She blinked and she was sat. The chair was cold, hard and unforgiving. As she held her head in her hands, her reflection peered back at her from the standing water on the floor. She was flushed despite the cold and young despite her years. Blood framed her delicate features, and heavy droplets escaped her nose, rippling and then dispersing to mix with her mother’s hues. Her knees dropped to the floor before her. The organic cocktail soaked through the cotton of her suit and bloodied her knees, like a kid in the playground. The gas burner flickered out as the wind picked up strength. She would have to leave soon.

    Yelena searched for her reflection once more but was still only met by her own eyes, staring back. Hands met water in an attempt to wash those eyes away, to sweep them aside, to find her beneath. To find a flicker of a smile, the corner of her mouth, a small piece of the flush of her cheek. If she could find one piece, maybe just one piece, she could find them all. It was just one piece she needed. Surely, she could find one piece.

    She scratched and swept with increasing desperation at her reflection, but could dig no further than the linoleum that lay beneath her knees. Her fists beat and her nails clawed and her nose streamed. The smell of gas mixed with the taste of iron, and Yelena’s vision began to blur. Fumes infiltrated her mind and the vignette of darkness began to grow. Just one piece, just one, she thought despairingly, as her body began to fail her. A force pulled her to her feet, violently. It was time to leave. She would resist, she always resisted. Her clouded mind told limp legs to kick, and tired arms to scratch and thump and blow. If she’d had more time, she’d have found her. If she’d just had more time. She was dragged backwards, out of the kitchen, just as it started, just as it always did. His distant, melodic voice, distorted and amplified, rose from the muted and desperate silence. His melody reverberated viscerally around the blood-soaked kitchen that was rapidly fading from sight, and against the peeling walls of the shattered corridor as Yelena was dragged through the rain, the glass and the rubble.

    Yelena thrashed and screamed, and her voice tore at her throat, but her screams fell silent. There was only his voice. Only his voice.

    Yelena woke with a start. Her skin was wet with sweat, but cool, as the breeze from an open window danced across it. An open window, Yelena mused, it didn’t take much to trigger her subconscious anymore, not that it had ever needed much persuading. She felt a pair of arms tighten around her, it seemed as if it didn’t take much to trigger Kate’s subconscious either. Yelena turned her head to one side, to better view the sleeping woman. The apartment was dark, but not completely pitch black. New York really was the city that never slept, and the light from the still busy street below was casting indistinct light and shadow across Kate’s delicate features. It felt cliché to say, but she always looked so peaceful when she was sleeping. No cogs turning, no over thinking, no anxiety tugging at her brow or biting at her lip. Just freedom; a deep, dark, thought free pit of freedom. Freedom from the worries of twenty-three-year-old life when you’re an Avenger. Yelena smiled sadly to herself. With all the training, and fighting and the running of end of the world simulations, she sometimes she forgot how young Kate really was. How innocent she was. How naïve she was. She allowed herself a few more seconds to study the other woman’s features. She was beautiful, that was for certain, but the peace of sleep was just a mask for chaos. Yelena gently negotiated Kate’s arms from around her waist, placed a lingering kiss upon her forehead, and then silently slipped out from underneath the covers, careful not to wake the sleeping dog at their feet. Kate's wasn’t the face she needed to see that night. Yelena padded across the balcony to dig around in her hold-all. She quickly found her prize, a crumpled pack of Winstons with a lighter, tightly bound to it with a couple of old hairbands. She pocketed her cigarettes momentarily whilst she threw on an oversized sweatshirt, and then made her way down the first flight of stairs to the open window. She settled on the window’s edge with a sigh and pinched the bridge of her nose with an unsteady hand. It had been some time since she’d had that dream, and she knew that in reality, it wasn’t really a dream at all, it was a nightmare, but it was a nightmare that she’d had so many times before. When the nightmare had first come to her, as a child, she’d awake in horror. Melina would often find her in the night, inconsolable and in tears. She’d hold her until the tears passed, and stayed with her until morning. But in the Red Room, she had to face the horrors alone, so now, now all she felt upon waking was dread.

    With a shake of the head to scatter her thoughts, Yelena took one of the old hairbands bound around the Winstons and scooped her hair back into a messy ponytail. After a few goes, the lighter burst into life, and Yelena put a cigarette to her lips and then held it to the open flame. As she drew on it, it burned brightly and its illumination danced in her dark, sleep deprived eyes. The slightly stale smoke filled Yelena’s lungs, it burned and cloyed satisfyingly as the nicotine hit her bloodstream. She exhaled with a shudder, and took another long draw that burned her throat. She would never get used to this, but that was kind of the idea. She heard the familiar sound of Lucky rousing, she’d woken him. Pizdets. The familiar clip clip clip of pawed feet pattered across the balcony and down the stairs. Yelena sighed and turned from the window and was met by the ever-loving eye of Lucky the Pizza Dog. “Go away, Lucky,” Yelena whispered, trying to shoo the golden retriever, but he simply sat and cocked his head to one side. These tactics would not work on Yelena Belova, hardened assassin and experienced dog owner. “Go back to sleep. You stay here much longer and she will smell this on you, and then I am in big trouble.” Lucky responded the only way a dog knew how. He padded forward and rested his head, gently upon Yelena’s lap. She sighed, quite clearly defeated by cuteness, and scratched his head affectionately. Yelena glanced over at Kate’s sleeping form once more, resting on one side with her hair tide back.
