How she loved to run her hands through that hair. In the light from the window, she could make out the dip of her waist and the rise of her hip, and the rise and fall of her chest. She really was beautiful, in many ways. Kate Bishop was chaotic and boisterous, generous and brave. And Yelena was willing to admit that Kate could also be quite funny, at times, too. But the young Avenger could also be idealistic, brash and over confident, all in ways that could get you killed in a fight and tomorrow, tomorrow would be their first real fight. Yelena took another long drag on her cigarette in an attempt to quell the incessant tapping of her foot. Kate’s first mission started in the morning, and what had they done in preparation? Half read their briefings and then made out whilst watching, or at least attempting to watch, the fourth John Wick movie. Yelena groaned and rubbed her temples. What a ridiculously fucking stupid idea this had been.

    She knew they’d had a connection, from the first moment their eyes had met on that rooftop, but she’d come back to New York for Kate, despite it. Or because of it. She knew they had a connection when she’d surprised Kate in that cocktail bar, she knew it when she’d taken the job at S.H.I.E.L.D., when she’d moved in with her, when she’d played house with her. She knew she was fucked from the start, because Kate was open with her heart, gentle with her touches, delicate with her kisses. Kate was too good. Too beautiful. And beautiful, gentle, delicate things had a habit of getting spoiled, usually by people like her. She knew she was complicated, and she hadn’t found the right way to articulate that to Kate yet, she hadn’t ever really known how to articulate for herself. She’d never had to before, because Kate was the first. But Kate never pushed, never complained, Kate let Yelena come to her and in that they’d struck the right balance. For the time being. She just hoped Kate would be able to separate the person from the trauma. The trauma didn’t trust and the person didn’t lust, and those two things that were mutually exclusive but together were not a recipe for a healthy relationship, but quite suddenly, Yelena Belova had found herself in one. Yelena took another drag on her cigarette and held the hot smoke in her lungs for longer than she should. The pleasurable, familiar burn made way for a harsher, sharper pain, and her body screamed to be replenished with oxygen – Yelena acquiesced momentarily. She took another fierce drag, and then another, quickly depleting the waning cigarette, but still the sense of dread remained. Up until this point, they hadn’t been living their real lives, their real purpose. IKEA, forks, beds, Netflix, takeout and kisses; all these things would feel different after tomorrow, their relationship would feel different tomorrow. It would feel different when Kate understood Yelena’s real purpose, it would feel different after Kate killed someone for the first time, it would feel different when Kate finally realised that no matter how long she waited or how understanding and patient she would be, Yelena might never fulfil her expectations of what a relationship was. So, should they be in one?

    Yelena often wondered when the human race had gotten so lost in sexualisation and objectification, when had they lost the ability to appreciate beauty for what it was? Warms smiles, and eyes and touches, smooth skin and kisses and comfort. Exploration of the human form, the appreciation and adulation of freckles and bruises and lumps and bumps. Trust, respect and unwavering and unconditional partnership. These were all expressions of beauty, and with Kate Bishop, Yelena wanted to explore every single one of them. That didn’t change the fact that she didn’t know how. It certainly didn’t change the fact that she doubted she could. Kisses and comfort, certainly, but trust, trust was something that Yelena was in short supply of, even when it came to trusting Kate with her life.

    With one last draw of breath, Yelena dragged her cigarette all the way down to its filter, stubbed it out against the outer wall, and rather irresponsibly flicked it out into the street; anywhere else and Kate would find out. She’d be subject to disapproving looks and disparaging lectures all morning, and probably well into the afternoon. Yelena would roll her eyes and draw her close and kiss her deeply, and then Kate would continue on her tirade after only being momentarily distracted. With another sigh, Yelena patted Lucky on the head, snuck her remaining Winstons back into her bag, and then took the rest of the stairs down to the ground floor of Kate’s apartment, to where her bed stood, cold and unmade. It would have to do. She threw back the covers and crawled inside, Lucky joined her. Kate would pretend to not be jealous in the morning.

    Yelena laid in the darkness. In the quiet of the evening, she could hear Kate’s slow and steady breathing. She took comfort in it. If she was breathing, she was alive. It would be hours before she would fall back to sleep, if she would find sleep again at all. It would be just her and her thoughts. Yelena shut her eyes tightly, and tried once more to picture her face, but there was nothing. Only watercolour eyes on linoleum floors. Maybe another cigarette would help, maybe just one.

    Chapter End Notes Next up, their first mission together! Wonder how it’s gonna go…

    Oh, shoot!

    Chapter Notes And we’re back! Kate and Yelena are on their first mission together and it’s going to go great… just… great.

    Just like the first two chapters, this one is more of a two parter. The second part will come later this week.

    Get ready for some action, some flirting and some unexpected angst! Get through this, and I’ll treat you all to some comfort a little later in the week.

    Thank you so much for all your comments and kudos from the last chapter. I tried something different and you guys were great.

    “Are we... are we there yet?” Kate asked, bent over, hands on knees and completely puffed out. Kate had her reasons, of course. It wasn’t as if she didn’t have a pretty decent baseline fitness, she’d just been working pretty damn hard. The unconscious guards left in her wake were testament to that. But her machine of a girlfriend, on the other hand, hadn’t broken a sweat. Her breathing was regular, her words not broken by the overwhelming need to inhale as much oxygen as humanly possible, and her face was unflushed.

    “No. It says service elevator,” Yelena explained, pointing to the sign written in Russian, matter-of-factly.

    “Oh...Cool,” Kate managed, nodding enthusiastically, in a cover for her complete and utter exhaustion. “Now I see why you’re here."

    Yelena raised an eyebrow, an eyebrow that told Kate she wasn’t a hundred percent sure if she was being serious or not. “To translate for you?” the Russian asked, incredulously. Of course, Kate was joking. A good seventy five percent of the unconscious dudes that lay behind them had been put, rather aggressively, to sleep by the Black Widow, but the brunette wasn’t going to give her the satisfaction of admitting it.

    “Yeah,” Kate said, as she gave the blonde a playful pat on the back and strolled towards the elevator. “You’re doing a great job,” she smiled goofily, and pressed the elevator call button. Yelena shook her head and sighed for effect, but did an absolutely terrible job of keeping a small but affectionate smile from tugging at the corner of her lips. Kate’s heart felt tight, and warm and happy. Apart from the being heinously out of breath thing, this was just how she’d imagined them together. Quipping and flirting and kicking ass. Yep, today was turning out to be pretty perfect.

    Yelena pressed herself against the wall on one side of the elevator’s entrance dramatically and nodded to Kate to do the same.

    Kate frowned. “Why?”

    “Because there could be someone in the elevator,” Yelena explained, as if it were perfectly obvious. To her credit, it was pretty obvious once she’d explained, but Kate simply shrugged. Seeing Yelena in action so far, had been pretty impressive, and pretty hot to boot, but there was no way Kate was going to let her know that either.

    “I just thought you’d wanted to look cool.”

    “You think I do this to look cool?” Perhaps the affection was gradually being replaced with exasperation. It was one hundred percent worth it.

    Kate threw herself against the wall on the opposite of the elevator doors with a flourish. She flicked her hair to gaze, dramatically, at the Russian. “I think you do a lot of things to look cool.”

    “No, I don’t,” Yelena said, indignantly.

    “You know the thing you do when you jump off a roof?” Kate asked, and she knew that she knew.

    “That very practical thing.” There was nothing practical about it.

    “You think you look cool doing it,” Kate insisted, smugly. She was going to win this argument, there was no way in hell Yelena couldn’t concede this.

    The blonde huffed, Kate was on the brink. “Okay, whatever,” Yelena relented. And there it was, a resounding victory for the fighter in the purple corner. “But!” Kate rolled her eyes, there was always a ‘but’. “I look very cool doing it which isn’t my fault, it is just a by- product of being a very cool person.”

    “Uh huh. Sure.”

    With a ding the doors of the elevator pinged open and a moment later a guard stepped out. A stamp to the right knee, a deft shift between standing legs, and a swift kick up and under the chin put the guard down in under two seconds. Yelena stood, stoically over the fallen guard, and raised a solitary eyebrow in Kate’s direction.

    Kate had to admit, “That was pretty cool.”

    “You see?’ Yelena shrugged, clearly satisfied with Kate’s appraisal of her. “By-product.” Kate could only smile. Her girlfriend was very cool. Not that Yelena had said the word girlfriend, but saying ‘seeing each other’ just felt wrong. ‘Seeing each other’ would imply that there were times when they didn’t see each other, but they lived together, trained together, worked together, cooked together, slept together – not like that, and were about to commit to raising two dogs together. They were together, right? So, what did that make them? Some kind of item, surely.

    Kate studied the elevator buttons and hovered her finger over the most worn of the four options. She turned a questioning look to Yelena who nodded her agreement, and then gave the button a shove. Immediately, Kate wished she’d brought some hani sani with her as the control panel was grim af.

    The elevator lurched to life, and to her surprise, it began to move downwards. Kate frowned, a look that was matched by her partner in crime. Yes, it was tacky and clichéd, but Kate liked partner in crime. It was smart because Yelena used to be a criminal, and it also implied fun and hijinks.

    “Did the briefing say down?” Kate asked, with just the smallest touch of apprehension. She was sure it was fine. Probably just a case of reading the map the wrong way round, which was certainly something she’d been guilty of previously, but the fact that Yelena also looked a little surprised, was enough to make her feel the slightest bit uneasy.

    The two took up a similar position to the one they had just moments before, on either side of the elevator door, just as it ground to a halt. The bing of the soviet era elevator sounded again, and doors slowly slid open. Kate studied Yelena, she was listening for any signs of life. Thankfully, she heard nothing. With the smallest of glances from her vantage point, the Russian scanned the corridor and then quietly exited the elevator. She nodded for Kate to follow.

    The brunette glanced around the hall. Everything she saw was unexpected. Of course, there were cameras, but Yelena had already dealt with those on their way in, but the cameras were about the only thing that made sense. The service elevator had been soviet built, as had the foundations of the building. The surveillance system had been slightly higher tech, which was something you’d expect considering it was 2026 and you could buy a 4k internal camera set up with a click of a button from Amazon Prime. But upstairs, the corridors were clean. Smooth lines, smooth glass, modern architecture. There were carpets for pity's sake. Kate swallowed, as plush as she knew the toilets would be in this place if she needed to take a comfort break, this did not bode well.

    “Does this look like a Russian terrorist cell to you?” Kate asked, quietly.

    “Are you asking me because I’m Russian or because I know a lot of terrorists?”

    “A little bit of both.”

    Kate watched as Yelena’s brow and nose crinkled, and her eyes flicked over every detail of the corridor. The blonde was suspicious too, and when Yelena was suspicious, Kate knew she should be worried.

    The Russian tapped her ear-piece. “Sharon?” she whispered.

    “Yes, Yelena. Where are you?” came Carol Danver’s voice from across the Pacific Ocean, into both of their ear pieces. Yelena’s less than sunny disposition became, if possible, even gloomier.

    “Where’s Sharon?”

    “Where are you?”

    Kate could see Yelena’s jaw twitch with irritation. “We’re out of the service elevator and making our way to the lab.”

    “Good. Run into any resistance?” Carol asked, voice crackling with interference.

    “Nothing our Purple Ranger couldn’t handle,” Yelena said, with a wry smile. Kate gave her a look. Yelena thought that it would be funny to call Kate the Purple Ranger ever since she discovered Kate’s childhood love for the Power Rangers. In all honesty, it was quite the inspired name choice considering the purple suit and the bow and arrow, but Kate was Clint’s protégé, and Kate also wanted to be taken seriously. Sadly, Carol had immediately taken to Purple Ranger, and considering it was pretty much the only thing that Carol and Yelena could ever see eye to eye on, it had become a bit of a running joke.

    “This place looks more sophisticated than we expected,” Yelena continued. “No high-level security but it’s all high level. Nice offices, nice interior. This place is well funded. Are we sure this is Red Network?”

    “That’s what the intelligence says,” Carol said, Kate could practically hear her shrug.

    “Could your intelligence be wrong?” Yelena asked, whilst grabbing Kate and quickly pulling her into a dark alcove. They had been out in the open for too long.

    “There’s always the possibility, but it doesn’t matter who these guys are. We need you to recover the asset, that’s the priority.” And she wasn’t wrong. That was the priority, and a pretty big one at that.

    Two nights prior S.H.I.E.L.D. had received word that a British asset had been lost over Russian airspace. Later reports indicated that the asset, being transported from Hong Kong to an airbase in Alaska had been brought down by a surface to air missile, somewhere off the coast of the Bering Sea. Russian Terrorist group, Red Network had claimed responsibility for the missile launch but had made no mention of securing the asset that had been onboard. British and S.H.I.E.L.D. intelligence had evidence to say otherwise, and tracked the cell pretty much all the way back to where Yelena and Kate were standing. Normally, with situations such as this, an organisation like S.H.I.E.L.D. wouldn’t even think about getting themselves involved, but unfortunately for Red Network, the asset that they’d seized was some kind of alien technology that the British had been studying out in Hong Kong. S.H.I.E.L.D. could not let it fall into the wrong hands, even if it fell into the hands of a terrorist cell who didn’t have anywhere near the skills or technology to work with it. Kate glanced around the corridor once more and took in the unexpectedly sophisticated set up, all the more reason to secure what they came for.

    “And that’s exactly what we’re going do,” Yelena assured Carol whilst giving Kate a reassuring smile.

    “Okay. Sitrep in five. Out.” And with that, Carol Danvers was gone. With the slightest of nods, Yelena asked Kate to follow her, and follow her she did. They made their way through the complex, going room to room systematically. Yelena expertly removed guards as she went. The first, she choked out, the second she punched in the gut and then caught with a knee up and under the chin, the third, she struck with the butt of her pistol, a weapon she now only used as a final resort. How S.H.I.E.L.D. life had changed her.

    Kate found herself watching Yelena work, respectfully. When she was in full flow, she was an absolute sight to behold. There was something incredibly attractive about seeing a master at work. She moved purposefully, but with a grace and beauty that Kate could only ever aspire to. She was efficient and powerful. Strong and agile, and knew how to use your own body against you. Kate’s mind had certainly wandered, which, of course, was stupid. They were on a mission, their lives were at risk, and she needed to ensure that she was paying said mission her fullest attention. Sadly, her mission right now seemed to have devolved from ‘secure top-secret asset’ to ‘stare incessantly at your girlfriend’s asset’. She was quite sure that Carol would not approve, and realistically, Yelena probably wouldn’t either.

    Yelena took cover at the end of the hall and threw a momentary glance around the corner. “Two guards, no way to flank them, and what looks like a biometric scanner to access the lab. I need you to take them out, quickly and quietly, okay?”

    Kate smiled. She was being allowed to shoot arrows, real life stealthy arrows. She could do this, but which arrow to go with? There were so many options. Foam arrow, gas arrow, a sonic AOE.

    “Kate,” Came Yelena’s urging voice.

    “Right, sorry, yes. Got it. I got it,” she said, with a nerdy smile as she grabbed a gas arrow from her quiver. Kate was sure that Yelena was smiling too, just on the inside.

    With one swift motion, Kate loaded her arrow into her bow, stepped out from around their cover and released. The arrow struck the ceiling above the guards with a satisfying thunk, and before they’d even had time to react, the sleeping gas began to billow out of it. No sooner had the guards taken a breath to gasp in shock, were they on the floor. That stuff really was fast acting. It was a recipe Kate had been perfecting herself, and she was pretty proud of it. By the look on Yelena’s face, the Russian was pretty impressed too.

    The partners dashed down the corridor, and quickly helped each other to haul one of the passed-out guards to his feet. After both women muttered a number of rather unkind expletives, mostly aimed at the guard in their arms, they managed to hoist his face up to the scanner. An angry red warning flashed up on the screen, < доступ закрыт >. Yelena groaned, audibly.

    “Is that a no?” Kate asked, a little glibly.

    “Yes, it’s a no.” Yelena said with a sigh. “Let’s try the even heavier looking son of a bitch.”

    Kate mustered as much optimism as was possible in a situation such as the one she found herself in. Sometimes she needed to be an optimist enough for the both of them, and that was absolutely a-okay. “Yes, ma’am,”

    With another gargantuan effort, they hauled the guard off of the floor. Kate suspected that it was Yelena doing most of the heavy lifting, but there was no replacement for positive attitude.

    <доступ предоставлен>

    “Oh, thank god,” Yelena said, with relief, as the doors to the lab slid open. She glanced inside, to what looked like a completely empty laboratory, and then let go of the guard, quite unceremoniously. He dropped, face first to the floor with an unfortunate crunch.

    “Ouch, that’s rough. Is he bleeding now?” Kate asked.

    “Probably. I thought you had him, why didn’t you catch him?” The Russian asked, mischievously.

    “Me? Catch this dude? Really? Setting me up for a fall there, don’t you think?”

    Yelena simply shrugged as she grabbed the first guard and dragged him inside the lab. “Maybe you should spend more time in a real-life gym, and less time in a Pokémon gym.”

    “Hey! it is not my fault that Niantic made the Avengers Complex a gym, okay? That place is supposed to be secret. And what else am I supposed to do in-between reps?”

    “I don’t know? Hydrate... a super set...”

    “A super what?”

    Yelena deposited guard number one and came back for the slightly bloodier guard number two. She put her hands on her hips, clearly a little tired. Good, she’s finally broken a sweat. “Are you just going to watch me do this?” Yelena asked in exasperation. She huffed and blew a few loose strands of her hair out of her face.

    “I thought I could deal with the blood,” Kate reasoned. That was an even distribution of work, right? Yelena does the heavy lifting and Kate cleans up after her. Kate rolled her eyes as the Russian continued to look at her disdainfully. After a beat, Kate relented. She supposed it was the reasonable thing to do. “Fine, I’ll help. You’re welcome,” Kate said, with a grin, and Yelena couldn’t help but smile. Kate loved this. She loved being able to work with Yelena, smile with Yelena, fight with Yelena, flirt with Yelena. It all just seemed to fit.

    After they’d hidden the second guard behind a control terminal in the lab they tried their best to wipe away the blood, just on the other side of the door, and then shut the lab doors behind them. As the pair ventured further into the lab, the lights flickered on. They must have been on sensors.

    “Woah...this is huge.” Kate gasped, as the full extent of the lab’s sophistication came into view.

    “This is not a terrorist cell.” Yelena whispered, with trepidation, as she flicked a switch on the main control panel. It was labelled in Cyrillic Russian, but Kate didn’t need to be able to read the language to know what it did. In moments, what looked like blast shields slide up and away, and revealed three large panels of glass beneath them. They were windows, huge viewing windows with thick glass, all of which looked out on the scene below. It was a hangar bay, a busy hangar bay, filled with one-man fighters and larger class vehicles. It all looked pretty high-tech, worryingly high-tech.

    “Or maybe they’re just like… really good terrorists?” Kate wondered, out loud, still a little overwhelmed by the scene before her and not really listening to the words that were coming out of her mouth.

    Yelena shot her an incredulous glance.

    “You know what I mean,” Kate said, dismissively.

    The Russian frowned. She was uneasy. Very uneasy. This wasn’t at all what they’d signed up for, but they were there, and they were far too far down the rabbit hole to turn back. “Let’s just find this thing and go. The quicker we’re out of here the better.” Kate couldn’t agree more.

    “What are we looking for?” Kate asked as she scanned the walls and surfaces, looking for anything that could host the asset. “The briefing said it would have to be kept at low temperatures to remain viable, but I don’t see anything resembling a refrigerat-”

    The sound of hissing made Kate wheel around. A contraption, holding what looked to be a selection of test tubes, rose from the lab station in front of Yelena who had her hands held up, a little startled. Cool vapour escaped the cavity below and billowed its way across the work surfaces.

    “I didn’t touch anything,” the Russian panicked and a small laugh escaped the brunette.

    “I think you found the asset.”

    Yelena nodded, as she reached out and tentatively touched a test tube with the back of her hand, ensuring it was a safe temperature to handle. The tube was cold but not freezing, so Yelena plucked a tube from its holder and held it closer so she could inspect the label.

    “Property of S.H.I.E.L.D.,” Yelena read with a frown. “Well, that’s helpful”.

    Kate frowned too. Didn’t the briefing say the alien tech was a British asset? And would alien tech really come in a test tube? The only tech Kate had ever seen was big, glowing and destructive. What kind of alien technology was this?

    Without warning, sirens blared and an alert in Russian echoed around the lab. Yelena groaned. “Of course,” she muttered, “It’s alarmed”.

    Kate’s eyes went wide, what the fuck were they going to do? Every guard in the entire building would be on their six, in like.... six seconds. That was an exaggeration, but still. Shit just got serious, and this was supposed to be her first time out the gate. “I thought you were a super spy?!” she shouted, across the lab, perhaps a little too shrilly at her girlfriend.

    “Well… I?” Yelena looked up at Kate, a little lost as to what to do. Fucking up wasn’t something the assassin was at all familiar with. Kate would have found it completely adorable if they hadn’t been so royally screwed at that moment. “Let’s just go.” Kate was inclined to agree.

    They began to run, the safest bet was the service elevator, they both knew it. They’d already cleared it, and the service tunnels that ran out to the man-made harbour. They met their first guard fifteen seconds out of the lab. She came from their flank and Yelena put her down. The next guard Kate disarmed with a well-aimed arrow. Yelena then closed the distance and struck him in the stomach with a knee and the back of the head with a sharp elbow.

    They turned the corner and three guards were waiting for them. Yelena struck first with a firm, high foot to the solar plexus. Kate swept his legs and the Russian bounded to her next target, parrying one blow and then another. The third blow she caught, twisted and with it sent the guard to the floor. She delivered a final hard shot to the face and put him down. Suddenly an arrow sailed past, close to her head, and struck the approaching third guard violently in the shoulder, sending her staggering backwards and to the floor. Kate gave Yelena a little saved your life smile, before the Russian rose to her feet and turned on the final guard. “Mne ochen' zhal,” she rasped low and remorsefully, before she delivered a swift roundhouse kick to the guard’s jaw. She went down like a sack of potatoes, a sack of potatoes with a broken jaw.

    Oh, my stars, just rail me, Kate’s mind wandered. It had spent more and more time doing that lately. It had done it when she’d first seen Yelena put on her new black tactical suit, it had done it when she’d taken out the guards on the pier, it had done it when she’d disabled the security system with a few taps of her fingers and it had done it just now. The only problem was, Yelena was probably never going to rail her. Not that it was a problem, per se, Kate was pretty content with satisfying her own needs, for the time being anyways, and calling it a problem really wasn’t very fair to Yelena. Her sexuality wasn’t a problem, it was just not what she was used to, not how her and pretty much everyone else in the world was conditioned into thinking relationships should work. Which begged the question, was it really society and its patriarchal, heteronormative perspective on relationships as a whole that was the problem? Kate Bishop, asking all the big questions. Didn’t stop her thinking about Yelena’s body in that suit though, and it didn’t stop her feeling a little bit bad about it when she did. Should she be objectifying her potentially asexual girlfriend? Her word, not Yelena's. And even if it turned out to be ethically okay, was it just going to slowly but surely create problems for them further down the line?

    “Kate!” came Yelena’s urgent voice, pulling her from her thoughts. Busted. “Stop thinking about how much you’d pay to have me do that to you, and let’s go!” Double busted.

    “I was kind of hoping you’d do it for free?!” Kate called, down the hall, and Yelena gave her a bemused smile. Kate smiled back. Yelena thought she was being cute, so maybe not so busted.

    “Are you kidding, I can get good money for that.”

    “I could make a charitable donation?” Kate shrugged, it seemed like a reasonable suggestion, but the Russian could only roll her eyes and gesture that perhaps, Kate should think about joining her in getting the fuck out.

    The brunette sprinted down the corridor, bundled into the back of Yelena and pushed her through the double doors, back into the corridor with the service elevator. The alarms still rang in their ears as they made their final sprint to the elevator, or what they thought was their final sprint. Just as they reached their escape route, blast doors slammed into place. The elevator was sealed shut. Oh, shoot.

    Yelena groaned in dismay for the seventy fifth time that morning and tapped her earpiece to open up a channel back to base. “A decommissioned uranium mine. Really Carol!? Does this look like a decommissioned uranium mine to you?”

    “I mean, I can’t see what you’re looking at.”

    “What uranium mines do you know with blast doors and hangar bays?” Yelena was practically growling now. Kate would have found it strangely attractive if they weren’t facing possible capture or death behind enemy lines.

    “Are you really complaining to me about the hangar bay filled with escape plans?” Carol asked, incredulously. Kate risked a glance at her girlfriend, who was chewing the inside of her mouth animatedly. Carol had made a valid point, and Yelena had quite clearly gone from disliking their current situation very much, to certifiably hating it – because Carol had been right.

    “Cyka.” Yelena muttered, not nearly quiet enough for it go unheard, and Kate was pretty sure that had been the intention.

    “Sitrep in five,” Carol chimed. Carol didn’t give a fuck, and really, would you if you could carve spaceships in half with your energy beam hands?

    “If you don’t hear from us, it’s because we’re dead,” Yelena bit back, and killed the line.

    “We’re not gonna die right?” Kate asked Yelena, her voice a little more panicked than she’d meant for it to be. She suddenly felt it. The realness of the situation. They were on foreign soil, they were most likely outnumbered, and they were almost certainly trapped, for the time being anyways. Kate did have a few things going for her though. Firstly, she had Yelena Belova with her, trained super assassin. Secondly, she had Yelena Belova with her, trained pilot of literally everything. And thirdly, she had Yelena Belova with her, her girlfriend and teacher and when their eyes met, she saw resolve. And it flooded her with confidence.

    The alarms blared and a voice echoed through the halls. “What are they saying?”

    Yelena grinned. “Yoga is at five in the main hall, code of conduct training is overdue for anyone who is yet to take it and they’re expecting a couple of visitors in the hangar bay, anytime now actually.”

    “Really?” Kate asked, a smile tugging at her lips.

    Yelena shrugged a signature shrug. “Something like that,” she quipped, her voice low, and Kate was flooded with something else entirely. “Come on,” Yelena grabbed Kate’s wrist and began to drag her through the complex. Through one door, through one guard, two guards, through another door, through a third and fourth guard. They ducked for cover as the gunfire started, and quickly barrelled into the next room. Yelena’s eyes lit up, she’d found what she’d been looking for.

    “How do you know where we’re going?!” Kate shouted, over the ear-busting sound of semi- automatic weapons.

    It was a question Kate knew the answer to. She most certainly could. In a split second, an arrow was between her fingers, in her bow, and then fired. It struck the door and a quick drying purple gunk expanded rapidly across its surface and the walls, effectively sealing the door shut.

    “Get down!” Yelena shouted, as Kate felt her girlfriend’s arms engulf her, and drag her down to the floor. The blast shook the room, and shook her bones as her ears protested.     “Hold on,” Yelena urged, her voice in Kate’s ear and her lips pressed firmly against her temple. It was a gesture that was supposed to fill Kate with confidence, but all it really said to the young Avenger was Yelena was about to do something incredibly dangerous and desperate, like hurl them both out of a window from a great height, on one thin wire designed to hold one person’s body weight all the while probably being shot at from the hangar bay below.

    But hold on Kate did. She screwed her eyes up tight and held on to the woman who had so quickly won her heart back on that rooftop in New York City, a time and a place that seemed so very far away at that moment. Kate suspected that she probably looked more like a very frightened koala.

If they weren’t irreparably damaged after the explosion in the room above, they were now. Oh god, I don't want to end up like Clint, Clint is old. More guards streamed into the hangar bay and began to take up vantage points. The partners ducked behind a set of sturdy looking metal storage boxes. They needed to move, before they were flanked.

    Yelena’s eyes danced around the hangar, evaluating threats, cover and opportunities. Her gaze fixed upon something over Kate’s shoulder. They were getting out of there.

Yelena couldn’t wipe the smile from her face as she fired a few more covering shots in the guards’ direction, she looked far too casual and way too hot. But now was not the time, Kate reminded herself, as she bundled up the hatch and into the back of the jet.

    Kate looked at Yelena, like she’d grown two heads. This kind of seat of the pants behaviour she expected from herself, but not from Yelena Belova.

    “What? I missed you. You were like, really far away for like, forty seconds or something.” The brunette could only shake her head and laugh as Yelena clambered into the driving seat and fired up the jet’s engine, seemingly non-plussed by the bullets beating down on the glass just in front of her face. “Sometimes, I can be a little impulsive.”

    “A little?!” Is that what she called a little? “What would a lot look like?” Kate asked, not really sure she wanted to know the answer, especially as she knew it probably didn’t involve railing her.

    “Avalanches,” Yelena answered, as if it were the most obvious thing in the world. Huh, Kate was not expecting that. The blonde hit a couple more buttons, set thrusters to burn and pulled back on the yoke. They had lift off.

    “Remind me to ask you about it if we get out of here.”

    “Darling, we’re getting out of here, but you might want to hold onto something,” Yelena said, as Kate grabbed onto the back of one of the chairs. As the jet lurched upward at breakneck speed and shot out into the desolate Siberian landscape above, a warning blipped on the HUD, and two red dots appeared on their radar, closing in quickly behind them.

    “Of course, they’ve scrambled fighters,” Yelena muttered, from upfront. “Kate, can you go back there and fetch two chutes?”

    “Yeah, good thinking.” Fetching things was absolutely something Kate could do. She hurried through the jet, searching beneath seats and in overheads. The sound of aircraft fire scattered against the fuselage and Yelena was forced to take evasive manoeuvres. These weren’t semi-automatic weapons anymore. These were weapons of the armour piercing variety. The Russian banked from right to left and Kate almost lost her footing, as she slammed her knee, painfully against the seating that lined the walls.

    “Sorry! You doing okay back there?”

    “All go-”

    “Hang on!” Came another shout from Yelena, as she weaved low across the flat and barren Siberian desert. And therein lay their problem. No peaks, no trees, no valleys, nowhere to hide. Kate fell forward but managed to keep herself upright by grabbing onto some material webbing that divided the area for people from the area for cargo, and that’s where she found her prize.

    Kate clambered back to the front of the jet, threw herself into the passenger seat and a chute in Yelena’s direction. The Russian grabbed it and tucked it between her legs so she wouldn’t lose it in the case of further evasive manoeuvres.

    ‘Good work!” Yelena had to shout over the sound of the onslaught. They were taking heavy fire now, but there was no time to think. For now, the jet’s shield was taking most of the damage. For now. “Put yours on! Now!” Yelena instructed, and Kate did as she’d been told.

    “Aren’t you gonna put yours on?”

    “I’ll manage. I’d prefer to be strapped in for this,” Yelena explained, indicating that perhaps Kate should also think about securing her seatbelt. Again, she followed Yelena’s instructions. The blonde flinched as another barrage of aircraft fire streamed past their left and right bows. They had nowhere to go, nowhere to hide and the Yelena was quickly losing patience.

    Another peppering of fire hit their bow and Yelena swore heavily in Russian. An alarm blared and the lighting on the ship dimmed. A red warning flashed up on the HUD and a female voice sounded through the speaker system. This couldn’t be anything but bad, right?

    “What did she say?” Kate asked.

    Yelena’s brow furrowed, darkly. She was debating whether to tell Kate, debating whether to worry her, debating how to keep her safe. Kate could practically see the cogs turning and it was then that she realised what Yelena had been trying to avoid. They could escape, they could be safe, they could return to their life together, with their soon-to-be two dogs, and their IKEA bed and their cutlery and their spooning, but it would come at a price; and that price would be these pilot’s lives. Yelena was trying to protect Kate, she was desperately trying to protect her from one danger, by exposing her to another, and time was running out.

    The jet took another hit and Kate felt it physically lurch in the sky. Fuck. The warning sounded again.

    “Yelena, what did she say?”

    Yelena swallowed. “Shield integrity is low,” she explained, solemnly. The blonde chewed her lip. Her eyes seemed as if they were somewhere else, as if her brain had wandered to a new plain of consciousness, but her body still responded to its instructions; gracefully turning and deftly weaving the jet through the air. This would have probably been another rail me worthy moment, if death hadn’t felt so close.

    "I need you to shoot them down,” Yelena spoke, abruptly.

    “What?” They were the words Kate had been expecting, but not the ones she’d wanted to hear.

    “There is an aiming module,” Yelena tapped a few buttons to her right without taking her eyes from the landscape ahead. A control stick rose from the panel in front of Kate, and the HUD reconfigured to show a crosshair and two jets dancing around it, like two moths dancing around a flame. “I need you to take their ships down.”

    Kate panicked at Yelena’s words. She felt her heart drop and her stomach flip flop, and not in the good way that she’d grown accustomed to with Yelena. She couldn’t kill these pilots. She wasn’t a killer. She was a hero, heroes weren’t killers. But Kate knew that was a fallacy, Kate knew that her own hero had plenty of blood on his hands. She knew that the woman next to her, that the woman she... cared deeply for had killed an incalculable amount of people, many of them completely innocent. She knew that being a killer was part of the Avenger equation, so why had she never seen this for herself? Why hadn’t Yelena warned her? “But…

    “He will have a chute, Kate,” Yelena tried to reassure her, but her voice was desperate. She needed Kate to do, not think, and Kate knew that at this point, Yelena was only protecting her conscience from a few harsh realities.

    “Kate! Kate! Look at me, Kate!”. Despite her existential panic, Kate did. “You can do it, Kate.” Yelena’s eyes were soft and certain, and Kate felt the tiniest bit of confidence begin to creep into her. It wasn’t much, but it was enough.

    “Okay. Okay.” Kate cracked her knuckles and cast her eye over the turret controls. “This all seems fairly simple”

    The jet took more damage and the warnings blared.

    “Five percent Kate!” Yelena warned.

    “I got it, I got this,” Kate muttered, as Yelena wove and barrel rolled to avoid the next shot and the next shot, as their next could be their last. The brunette gripped the control stick and dragged the crosshairs across the jets, firing as she went, but she couldn’t account for Yelena’s dips and dives, and she missed.

    Yelena gritted her teeth. “Get it quicker.”

    “I would be able to if you would just…” She lined the first jet up. “Hold…” her thumb released the safety. “Still...” and her trigger finger fired a burst of significant firepower.

    “Holding still will get us-” The first jet spun and struck the second and both careened out of view. A distant explosion rippled through the jet’s large hull and Yelena took her hand hands from the yoke to strain her neck and catch a glimpse of the two crafts.

    The blonde stuck the jet in cruise and the two breathed heavily, in a desperate attempt to claw some oxygen back into their lungs to replace the adrenaline that was coursing through their veins.

    “Was there a chute? Did you see a chute?” Kate asked, her voice desperate.

    “I don’t know.”

    “I need to know.” Kate pleaded with Yelena. And she did, she needed to know if she was a killer, because it was something she’d have to live with. Ignorance wasn’t bliss, ignorance would tear you up inside, worse than the truth.

    “Okay,” Yelena spoke, softly, with the deftest of nods. She understood.

    Yelena turned the jet back around and began to scour for the fighter’s remains. They passed over a pilot unbuckling herself from an ejector seat in the snow. Well, at least she survived the tail spin, whether she’d survive the weather was another question entirely.

    Two miles further North and Yelena came across the wreckage of the fighters. Thick black smoke burned dark against the pure white of the frozen desert and Kate’s heart thumped against her chest. Please be okay, please be okay, please don’t make me a killer. A little further North and Yelena spotted another ejector seat, Kate saw it too. They’d got out. Their parachute was sprawled out behind their seat and they were lying prone, just a few meters away. Kate threw a hopefully look to Yelena, but the blonde didn’t reciprocate. Her jaw was set, her face dark and her eyes troubled. The hope Kate had managed to scrape together was quickly escaping her.

    Yelena set the jet down in silence and unclipped her harness. “Stay inside,” she said to Kate who threw her a questioning look.

    “What, why?” Kate needed to see. She needed to know. They had managed to eject from the wreckage, surely, they would be fine, surely that’s what ejector seats were meant to do. They were meant to keep people safe, they were meant to save lives, not take them.

    Kate unclipped her harness and began to rise to her feet, but a forceful hand pushed her back down into her seat. “Stay inside.” Yelena said, once more. Her eyes were filled with sadness. No, not sadness, pity. Her girlfriend knew, she knew the truth, and she was protecting Kate from it. But they’d ejected, they’d got out, surely they were safe. If Yelena would just let her go outside, see them, help them, she would prove it. That’s what ejector seats were meant to do. That’s what she was meant to do, she was meant to help. She was meant to save lives, not take them.

    Yelena pressed the button to release the hatch and turned her back on Kate as she steeled herself and marched down out into the frozen tundra. The wind swept violently around her and the blonde had to work hard to stay on her feet. Kate dashed from her seat and chased after Yelena, the wind bit at her hands and her face and she had to brace herself against its pushes and pulls.

    Kate’s eyes widened as she saw Yelena approach the prone pilot and unholster her gun. “Yelena, what are you-,” Two gun shots rang out into the wilderness. Kate’s words of protestation caught in her throat and she immediately had to work to resist the urge to vomit. Yelena had shot him, twice, in the head. Deep red blood began to pool, bright against the white of the snow. It would have been beautiful if it hadn’t been so heartbreakingly horrifying. “What... what,” Kate tried but failed to find the words. “What did you do...? He was alive,” she despaired. He was alive.

    Yelena didn’t meet Kate’s eyes. She didn’t turn to comfort her. She didn’t offer her a word of sympathy. She simply stared down, to where bright red met bright white. “One in three people suffer spinal injuries when ejecting. One in ten die. No one was coming for him. No big ship in the sky. People like him are just collateral damage.”

    “But you said…”

    Yelena holstered her gun, turned and finally met Kate’s eyes. “That they had a chute? I know, and they did.”

    “But you didn’t tell me the odds,” Kate said, emotion in her voice, as it broke and creaked under a fresh wave of guilt and grief. But it was a selfish grief, she wasn’t in pain for him, for the pilot, it was her own pain, her own guilt. She was mourning her own loss of innocence and reality hit her square in the face.

    “Would you have taken the shot if I had?” Yelena asked, a sad smile painted across her features, because she knew, she knew the answer. Kate wouldn’t have. She would have hesitated, she wouldn’t have pulled the trigger, and she would have gotten them both killed; and that was the reality of being an Avenger. Kill or be killed. Yelena had tried to protect her from that, she had tried to keep her safe and ultimately, she was the one who had pulled the trigger. But Yelena had only really dealt the pilot mercy, it was Kate who had condemned him to death for the greater good. And just like that, Kate understood what it really meant to be an Avenger.

    Metamorphosis: Two Chapter Summary Kate and Yelena return from their mission in Siberia, with far too much baggage. Chapter Notes Here we go! The comfort I promised you all. You deserve it, as do our heroines. Thank you for the kudos and the comments. I love reading them and responding in kind. And thank you to Kristin and Hawk Simps for all their invaluable input. Enjoy!

    Kate sat, alone, outside the war room. She was exhausted. Exhausted from crying, exhausted from broken, un-restful sleep, exhausted from re-living the last twelve hours in her head over and over. The pursuit, the alarms, the panic, the adrenaline and the tailspin. The bitter cold, the gunshots and the blood against Siberian snow. She was exhausted from the guilt, so exhausted she was worried that no amount of sleep would ever be able to extract every single drop of it. Kate pinched her nose as tears threatened to fill her eyes once more. She just wanted them to stop shouting at each other, she just wanted everything to stop. “You’re not telling me that you didn’t know about this!?” Yelena was angry. Yelena was so angry.

    “I knew as much as you did,” came Carol’s curt response.

    “Bullshit! You think I’m going to believe that the almighty S.H.I.E.L.D made an oversight this fucking big. You knew what you were getting us into, you knew this was Government.” Yelena had been calm on the flight home, so calm. Only two things had mattered; Kate and getting Kate home safely. She’d held Kate when she’d needed it, she’d given her space when she’d needed it, she’d listened when she’d needed it. She’d been perfect, but as soon as they’d touched down, as soon as Carol had shown her face, she’d broken. Whatever she’d been holding in, whatever she had been holding back to protect Kate, all of that had begun to spill over, and of course, Carol was having none of it.

    “It doesn’t matter who it was, that asset needed securing.”

    “At whose expense, huh? It was supposed to be simple. Safe. This was her first job.” It certainly had been. And for the most part, it had been wonderful, it had been everything she’d hoped it would be, especially with Yelena. Before they’d met, oh man, had Kate wanted to be an Avenger. She’d wanted it more than anything. But after meeting Yelena, after learning from Yelena, after falling for Yelena, all she wanted to do was go where she went, fight who she fought and make her smile whilst doing it. In reality, it was never going to be as idyllic as that, and maybe all of this was her fault, because maybe, she should never have let herself think like that in the first place.

    “And it sounds like she aced it, maybe you should have more confidence in her.” “That is not what this is about and you know it.”

    There was a pause, a heavy pause, and Kate hoped upon hope that the two had stopped fighting. She’d had enough conflict for one day, and even if Carol had admitted to knowing more than she’d let on, something Kate knew she would never do, it could never change what had happened in the previous twenty-four hours. It was done.

    “Yelena, I’m sorry that things went south and we can offer Kate whatever support she needs going forward.” Carol’s voice was quieter this time, more sympathetic, and Kate could hear Yelena audibly sigh. She sounded pained, she sounded tired, and above all, she sounded sad. “She’s a kid, Carol.” Yelena said, softly, and Kate’s heart broke all over again. Of course. Of course, that’s what Yelena thought of her. She wasn’t mature enough to choose between their life and his death, she wasn’t experienced enough to know the risks of ejecting during a firefight, she wasn’t hardened enough to fire two nine millimetres into a dying man’s head. She wasn’t any of those things. She was a kid. A kid that needed sheltering and protecting. A kid that she was happy to go home and play house with though, a kid that would hold her and kiss her and comfort her when she awoke from one of her more horrifying nightmares, a kid that was teaching her how to be a real adult.

    “No, she isn’t. She’s an Avenger. She needs to learn that people will die and that our actions have consequences. Some people will suffer so that an overwhelming number may live. That’s the burden of being an Avenger. Your sister understood that and Kate will too, just give her time”. It was unkind of Carol to speak about Natasha, but she knew what she was doing. Any suggestion by Yelena that the opposite was true would be to diminish her sister’s memory, so Yelena fell silent. Kate could feel the tension, the unease and general disrespect the two held for each other. Carol didn’t like Yelena’s way of doing things, she didn’t like her general disregard for authority, showing no understanding of Yelena’s years of subjugation. And Yelena didn’t like Carol’s way of doing things. She didn’t like her overwhelming power, she didn’t like the autonomy that was granted her, she didn’t like that she would come and go as she pleased, and she hated that it was her sister who had to save the world, when Carol wouldn’t.

    But here and now, Kate knew deep down, that Yelena agreed with Carol. Kate did need to learn, she did need to understand, and if she truly wanted to be an Avenger, she’d have to come to terms with that. Kate would have to embrace that part of her, she’d have to embrace the killer in her.

    After today, Kate had wondered if Yelena was running from the exact same thing. Yelena had committed to a life with the Avengers for Kate, and she’d committed to using non-lethal force, not because she represented the Avengers, not because she was now a beacon of hope and light, but because she was setting an example. No, it wasn’t even that, it was because she didn’t want Kate to see her as a killer, because there was so much good in Kate. But Kate knew that the assassin was part of Yelena, it was a necessary part of her, it was sewn into the very fabric of her being, and it wasn’t going away, but it also wasn’t her everything. She needed to show Yelena that that part of her, wasn’t something she needed protecting from. She loved her for it, not despite it, because she loved every part of her. Even the part that thought she was just some kid, yep, she loved that part too. “I’m taking her home, we can debrief tomorrow,” came Yelena’s voice. All Kate wanted to do was go home and hug her dog, cry into his beautiful soft fur, and fall asleep with him. “I’d prefer it if you both stayed here overnight, in case you need any-” “We’re going home.” Yelena’s voice was stern, and final. Kate could practically imagine Yelena, standing defiantly in front of the taller, and much more powerful, woman. But Yelena was powerful in her own right. She was strong in her convictions, selfless in her actions and loved far more fiercely than she would ever want you to know. The door to the war room slid open and Yelena marched out. Upon seeing Kate her hardened expression softened. She crouched in front of the brunette, and placed a comforting hand on her knee.

    “Are you ready?” Yelena asked softly, as she tried her best to hide the anger and frustration in her eyes.

    Kate gave a small nod. Oh man, was she ready to go home. “Yeah.”

    “Then let’s go see Lucky”.

    The drive home had been quiet. Neither really had much to say to each other. Everything Yelena knew how to say had already been said, and she’d gotten the distinct impression that Kate had just needed quiet, so she’d given her just that. She’d also given Kate her large, oversized hoodie so she could sit with the hood up and just get lost in it. Kate had stared out the window as Yelena guided them from the darkened country lanes of upstate New York, to the fairground attraction that was Manhattan Island. The rain that had fallen that evening had caused the bright lights of the City to run into each other, like an oil painting. What a contrasting morning they’d had. It almost seemed like they’d lived it in another life. Yelena supposed that they kind of did. Their life together in New York sometimes seemed so distant from their life together as Avengers. Up until this point, their New York life seemed precious, untouchable, unspoiled. It was sacred. They could come home and come together to hide from the stresses of training or politics, to comfort each other, to distract each other to enjoy each other, and to forget. But tonight, that would change.

    Yelena pulled up, put the car in park and grabbed both of their bags from the back. She’d called ahead with a pizza order, so quickly dashed into Herman’s, paid, thanked him, and dashed back out again. Kate was waiting for her, seemingly lost. Waiting for Yelena to open the door to her own apartment. Normally Yelena would take an amiable swipe at Kate. Do you have hands? What are you, a princess? I’m not your fucking doorman. But that night, Yelena simply shifted both bags into the crook of her right elbow, the large pizza she balanced precariously on her right hand, and dug in her back pocket for the keys she’d just deposited there. She gave Kate a small nod and a smile, and gestured for the brunette to follow her.

    With an impressive show of strength, agility and perseverance, perhaps her most impressive of the day, Yelena managed to get Kate, their bags and their pizza into the apartment, whilst being accosted by an incredibly excited dog. Kate sank to her knees and held him. He calmed in her arms and she pulled him in tighter, buried her face in his beautifully glossy fur, and breathed him in. She sure loved that dog, and who could blame her. She held him quietly for some time, it seemed like he was the comfort that Kate needed. Something completely separate, something completely innocent, something that loved her unconditionally. Was it normal to be jealous of a dog?

    “Should I get you some pizza out?” Yelena asked, as she dumped the pizza on the slightly charred table and set their bags down next to it.

    “I don’t want any food,” Kate mumbled into Lucky’s fur.

    Yelena frowned, not because she’d bought pizza and Kate didn’t want it, but because Kate always wanted pizza. She’d even gone for full pineapple, a gesture that would now go unnoticed. Yelena guessed it really wasn’t that important in the grand scheme of things. “Okay. No problem. It’ll be here in the morning.”

    Kate gave Lucky a quick kiss and then dragged herself to her feet. “I think I just want to sleep.” Yelena couldn’t agree more. If Kate could just get some sleep. Even the worst pain could be in part quelled by a decent night’s sleep, the brain just needed time to process. Of course, sleep could never entirely cure pain such as this, but it could at least give someone the tools to cope, for just a little bit longer at least.

    “No problem,” Yelena said, softly. “Do you want me to come with you?” Kate didn’t look at her, she just tugged on Lucky’s collar and began to take herself to bed. “No, you do whatever you want.” And with that she was gone.

    Yelena sighed and chewed the inside of her lip. “Okay,” she said quietly, into the silence. If Kate needed space, she would give it to her. She’d give Kate anything she wanted. Well, nearly anything. She wanted to at least.

    For a little while, she heard Kate shuffling around upstairs. Taking off sweatpants, presumably putting on a different coloured pair of sweatpants. Taking off her long-sleeved t shirt, to replace it with a short-sleeved t shirt. Taking off her bra and replacing it with, well, no bra. Yelena shook her head, sadly, settled into a chair that was tucked under the table, and threw open the pizza box. Look at all that pineapple. Yelena shook her head once more and started to pick pieces off, systematically, before she covered a couple of slices in a healthy amount of sriracha. Bet it still tastes like pineapple, you are far too whipped. And it was true. She was totally and completely whipped, whether she liked it or not, and whether Kate had intended it or not. It was so ridiculously stupid. She’d spent most of her adult life in captivity, and what did she do when she finally regained her independence? Spent three years freeing other women, five years not existing, and then subsequently chained herself to a woman called Kate Bishop. She was quickly learning that she had an irrational desire to do whatever it took to protect Kate Bishop, to do whatever it took to make her happy, and it was fucking stupid, but she couldn’t shake it, and she didn’t want to. Yelena thought back to the night before, thought back to her dream. She’d woken with the familiar dread that she’d always felt, with that sense that she was walking down a path that wasn’t meant for her, trying to find a door that would never reveal the one thing that she’d been looking for. She’d killed someone for Kate Bishop today, without thinking, without question. She was compelled to, and that worried her, because it was all too familiar. But she’d do it again, and she’d do it again, and again, if it would protect her, and protect what they had, and for that, she felt shame. Kate was so good and so pure, and had so much brightness in her, and Yelena had been desperately trying to hide the darkness in herself. Today it came out. She was the killer, not Kate, and once Kate came to realise that, they would be over. But that wouldn’t be tonight, she needed time to process first, she needed time to sleep.

    Although the light over Kate’s bed had been switched off some time before, Yelena could still make out movement coming from upstairs. Kate was tossing and turning, she was restless and she certainly wasn’t sleeping. Yelena massaged her forehead, gently and tried to unclamp her jaw that had been gradually getting tighter and tighter since she’d awoken the night before. She closed the pizza box, found some space for it in the fridge and quickly washed her hands, before she kicked off her sneakers and padded upstairs. Quietly, she approached the bed. Kate lay still, as if asleep. Sadly, for Kate, Yelena was pretty good at knowing when someone was asleep or not, and when someone was dead or not. She settled down next to Kate, perching delicately, on the side of the bed. “Is it okay if I sleep up here with you? Or would you prefer me to go back downstairs?” Yelena asked, gently.

    There was a moment of silence, before Kate let out a small sigh and opened her eyes ever so slightly. They were tired, heavy and red, but despite this, Kate was struggling to find sleep. “I’m not a kid you know?” Yelena blinked, that wasn’t what she’d expected to be keeping Kate up at night.

    “I know you’re not a kid.” Said Yelena, plainly. Of course, she wasn’t a kid. Sure, she was happy-go-lucky, lacked a little real-life experience and certainly didn’t have as much street cred as she thought she did, but she wasn’t a kid. She was a beautiful woman. “Then why did you say it?” Oh... Yes, Yelena had said it, and no, Yelena hadn’t meant it that way “I’m sorry. I did not mean it like that.” And she hadn’t, but she could understand why it had stuck with Kate, and she could absolutely understand why Kate might find it hurtful. She looked up to Yelena, learned from Yelena, wanted to be taken seriously by Yelena and sometimes shared a bed with Yelena – you do not want that that person to see you as a kid. You want them to see you as a peer and a partner.

    “Then how did you mean it?” Kate asked, quietly. It wasn’t a challenge, it wasn’t indignant, it was soft and it was vulnerable and it took all the control Yelena had, not to reach out and pull her body to hers. Instead, she reached for Kate’s hand and took it within her own, just liked she’d done many times that day. Her thumb brushed over the broken skin of Kate’s knuckles, broken from multiple well-placed punches.

    “I have been killing people for over fifteen years, Kate. You started today. I just meant that...” Yelena sighed and rubbed her temples with the hand that wasn’t entwined with Kate’s. “You’re new to this and it was our job to prepare you for it. My job.” Kate chewed on her bottom lip and her eyes darkened, Yelena knew where she’d gone. She was back in that moment, back out on the snow. The Russian pulled at Kate’s hand, demanding her attention, demanding that she turn her eyes towards her. Kate swallowed, her eyes fixed on Lucky, sleeping and still at the end of her bed.

    “Hey,” Yelena tugged again, a little more forcefully this time, and Kate dragged her eyes up to meet the Russian’s. “Hey,” she said again softer this time, with an even softer smile. She needed to show her. She was going to show her. “Can I kiss you?” Yelena asked and Kate blinked. That wasn’t what Kate had been expecting. “We do not have to, if you do not want to,” she said, soothingly, as her thumb continued to play across Kate’s knuckles. After a moment’s consideration Kate shuffled in the bed, and scooted over ever so slightly to make room for Yelena to slip underneath the blankets. The Russian gladly accepted the invitation and crawled in next to Kate, where her arms immediately found the brunette’s waist and pulled their bodies close. She was so warm, and long, Yelena had to work not to let her cold feet touch Kate’s shins. Even in sweatpants, Kate always insisted she could feel Yelena’s ice-cold toes; it was something she often got a swift telling off for. Kate’s eyes were all over Yelena now. “Are you actually going to kiss me? Or was this just an elaborate ruse to steal the warmth I’ve worked so hard to cultivate?” And there it was, a glimmer of Kate’s spirit. The number of times she’d heard those words, or words like them. Yelena couldn’t help but smile as she leaned into capture Kate’s lips. She started how she always did, being the smaller of the two. She took Kate’s bottom lip between her own and drew it gently into her mouth, letting it graze against her teeth as she went. Her hand left Kate’s waist and moved to frame her jaw, as Kate’s tongue sought to move against her own. She felt Kate sigh into her as her body began to relax into the Russian’s touch. Yelena broke their kiss, just for a moment, as she brought both hands to frame Kate’s face now. One thumb played across an eyebrow, as the other danced deftly across her lips. “If you want to, you can carry on hating yourself. And I will love you enough for the both of us, just for one night, okay?” Kate’s lips parted, as if to speak, but she never found the words. Her eyes danced in the light from the room below, as they searched Yelena’s. Wow, she was beautiful. So incredibly beautiful. Kate Bishop had eyes that even the toughest international women of mystery could get lost in, and it had turned out that Yelena Belova really wasn’t really that tough. In fact, she’d learned quite recently that she was disconcertingly soft, especially when it came to Kate Bishop.

    “What do you mean?” Kate whispered, her eyes still searching Yelena’s. That was quite the question, what did she mean? In reality, Yelena wasn’t sure. She didn’t know what an expression of feeling was for her, she didn’t know how to appreciate beauty in the way that she wanted to, and up until that point, she’d been too afraid to articulate it to Kate. But what she did know was that it was time Kate felt what she felt. It was time that Kate felt as beautiful as Yelena saw her to be, because right in that moment, Kate needed to feel it most.

    “I...” Yelena shook her head. Words, Yelena, for the love of God, use your words. Speaking openly and honestly was never something she’d been good at, never something her family had been good at, and there was certainly no chance of her starting now. But actions, she could do actions. “I... I don’t know yet. I was kind of hoping to make it up as I went along.” Kate smiled, affectionately. “But I want you to know how beautiful you are.” Kate’s smile grew more delicate as her eyes glistened softly. “Okay,” she nodded. Yelena’s heart felt warm, and tight and soft and light, all at the same time. She was nervous, nervous because she had no idea what she was doing, nervous because she was far too aware of the potential significance of what she was about to do, and nervous because somewhere at the back of her mind, the devil on her shoulder was telling her that however much she did, however loving her touches were, however tender her kisses were, it was never going to fulfil that need in Kate.

    She had to say, she had to talk about it. She couldn’t keep Kate guessing any longer, and she also couldn’t keep Kate in a relationship that wasn’t going to give her what she needed. Perhaps she could love her tonight, love her enough that it wouldn’t matter. “But I should be honest, I don’t think I can -”

    “It’s okay,” said Kate quickly. Her hands moved to Yelena’s cheeks and they lay there, mirroring each other, one tall, one small.

    “But I want to...”

    “All I need you to do is kiss me.”

    Yelena smiled a small, flirtatious smile. “I can do that,” She nodded. “Where would you like me to kiss you?”

    “Everywhere,” Kate said, a little breathlessly.

    Yelena found herself nodding, once more. “I can do that,” she said, as she reluctantly prodded at Lucky, to encourage him off of the bed, with a small pang of guilt. Their lips met again, just as purposefully as before. Her hands pulled at Kate’s waist to keep her close and then slipped underneath the cotton of her t-shirt to find warm smooth skin. The feel of it under her rough fingertips was sublime and she felt Kate’s breath hitch at her touch. She was just so beautiful.

    Her tongue caressed Kate’s as her touch danced across the sensitive skin of her stomach, and pushed the cotton of her t-shirt up to rest just below the curve of Kate’s breasts. Her hands lingered there. Go any further and it was further than they’d ever been before. Their eyes had wandered, their kisses had wandered, and their hands had wandered, but never further than this. The Russian felt Kate moan at her touch and pull softly at her hair. She knew what Kate wanted, and she knew that in that moment, she could give it to her. “Take it off,” Yelena whispered, and Kate acquiesced, breaking their kiss momentarily to lift herself off the bed and pull the t-shirt over her head to reveal a flushed chest and smooth skin. Yelena noticed Kate shiver slightly as her warm skin met cool air. “Are you cold?” Yelena asked, quietly. “Because we can-”

    Kate shook her head, as quickly as the question had been asked. “No, no, I mean, yes, I am cold but that is absolutely okay.”

    Yelena swallowed with a nod. There was a half-naked woman in front of her, an incredibly beautiful half-naked woman. The lines of her body, the curve of her waist and her breasts, the depths of her eyes, the fullness of her lips, the warmth of her smile and her skin. She needed to appraise it all and then praise it all. She went in search of every freckle, to gift it a kiss. Her fingers traced every bruise, and every dip. Her lips found the line of her jaw, and the soft, sensitive skin of her neck. They found warmer skin on the inside of her elbows and the inside of her thighs. Kate’s hands found her hair and every now and then Kate’s lips would find her own, as Yelena’s fingers played delicately across the brunette’s ribs or the backs of her arms.

    “You’re so beautiful,” Yelena whispered, as she peppered sensitive kisses across the sensitive skin that lay just below Kate’s ear. “So, beautiful.” She heard a quiet hmm of satisfaction escape Kate, and felt the brunette smile into her adulation. Beautiful. Yelena had lost count of the times she’d used that word that evening. After every murmur from Kate, she’d tell her, after every sigh she’d say the words, after every freckle she’d repeat the admission. “I feel more beautiful than when we started,” Kate whispered, her fingers playing in Yelena’s hair, which had somehow escaped its own messy ponytail.

    The Russian couldn’t keep the cocky grin from her face. “A resounding victory then.” “Oh indeed,” Kate drew Yelena in for another kiss and her fingers played at the hem of the Russian’s shirt. Kate bit her lower lip, ever so slightly, and Yelena could practically see the cogs turning.

    “Yes, you can,” came Yelena’s voice, before Kate could even ask the question. “I won’t perve or anything,” Kate said, innocently.

    Yelena found herself laughing. Of course, Kate would perve. She’d spent half the day perving at her. “You can perve,” she said, amiably. And she was serious, if Kate wanted to perve, it was no skin off Yelena’s nose. It was Kate who’d have to deal with the consequences, and Yelena knew she looked good. When she looked in a mirror sure, she might not feel sexy per se, but she felt confident and really, wasn’t that just the same thing but seen through a different lens?

    The blonde pulled off her t-shirt, kicked off her sweatpants, and wrestled the sports bra that she was wearing up and over her head. She couldn’t help but smirk as her girlfriend malfunctioned at the sight. Her girlfriend. That was weird. Maybe. Maybe her girlfriend. With two strong arms she pulled Kate close, and their bodies pressed warmly together, no risk of cold toes offending Kate’s shins any longer. Their foreheads rested gently against one and other’s, and they found themselves smiling at the comfort they both afforded each other. Kate bit her bottom lip once more, but this time with just a hint of trepidation. Yelena’s eyes searched hers to ask the question, what was wrong?

    “I just... I have loved every moment of this. I just don’t think I can forget that easily.” Yelena smiled and traced a finger, gently across Kate’s shoulder blades. “You don’t have to. You shouldn’t forget. That’s what keeps you you.”

    Kate frowned and her eyes grew darker still. “Hey,” Yelena’s forefinger found Kate’s chin and forced the brunette’s eyes to meet hers. “The first person I killed was a journalist in Belarus. She was writing stories that the government didn’t want published so they hired a fifteen-year-old to kill her,” Yelena smiled ruefully, it was all she could do. “The official line was break in gone wrong but I didn’t leave any sign of a break in. I shot here,” Yelena touched Kate gently, just to the right of her sternum, “And here.” She traced a line softly, from Kate’s chest to her temple and tapped lightly there. “And I felt nothing. No remorse, no guilt. Why should I?”

    “Yelena, I-“ Kate wanted to offer her some kind of sympathy, sympathy that she didn’t need. That wasn’t why she was telling Kate this.

    “What I’m saying is, it’s good to feel something, even if it hurts. It proves you’re human,” Yelena placed another soft kiss upon Kate’s lips and pulled her even closer. “You’re human too you know,” Kate whispered, trying her best to make Yelena see herself through Kate’s own eyes. But she didn’t have to convince Yelena of her humanity. Yelena knew that she was painfully human. She was flawed, insecure, angry and lost. She felt things fiercely and sometimes not at all, she vacillated on her feelings, and she was so totally afraid of trusting anyone with them. Surely that was the most human characteristic of them all. That and loving someone, truly loving them. She’d said the word love that night, but was she falling in love? She knew the answer, but she wasn’t ready for it. “What? You are human,” Kate reassured her, as the brunette’s hands cupped her face. Yelena hadn’t realised that she’d fallen quiet, and Kate must have interpreted her silence as doubt of her own humanity. “This feels pretty human,” Kate said, quietly, as she pressed herself impossibly close to the Yelena. Kate’s skin upon hers felt beyond good. It felt like electricity, like an unsatisfiable ache, and like the most earnest comfort all at the same time. Yelena smiled and pulled Kate in for one last kiss, the last before she knew sleep would take them. “I know,” Yelena said quietly. “I’m the most human when I’m with you.” BISHOP SECURITY. TRANSCRIPT LOG. FN 19932. 12/14/25.

    The hot water beat down heavily on Kate’s aching shoulders. The heat worked and relieved the tight muscles that it found there, but caused Kate to hiss and inhale sharply as it chased across the broken skin, just below her ribs. Water met blood as red streamed down Kate’s legs, and danced its way into the drain below. She would have to treat that wound again once she was out of the shower, that was for certain. She sighed, heavily, rested her head against the cool, wet tiles of her shower, and released the breath she’d been holding. Whose idea had it been to send her on a mission the day before her big charity benefit dinner? Oh right, hers. Her skin was painted black and blue and tender to the touch, her arms were scratched and her legs had been fighting to keep her upright since she’d dragged herself out of bed and away from her very warm and comfortable girlfriend to crack on with her long list of chores. Kate felt another sigh come and go as her mind wandered. The heat eased her body, the steam her lungs, and the gentle drumming of water falling upon porcelain eased her mind. Kate hoped Yelena would be up by now, but the likelihood was that the blonde was still in bed. Neither woman was really that into mornings, but for Kate, today wasn’t a regular day. Today was the Bishop Family’s annual Christmas Benefit, and also happened to be a year to the day that she’d met Yelena. Not that Yelena would remember.

    Yelena Belova, what a life changing revelation she’d been. If you’d have told Kate a year ago, that in a year’s time she’d be sharing four different beds with that woman, she’d have firstly told you you were crazy, and she’d have secondly asked you how and when she could make that happen. She could never have imagined she’d be training with her, fighting by her side, sharing her life with her, kissing her, loving her, being loved by her. Not that Yelena would ever admit to loving Kate, not anytime soon, and Kate knew that was a reality that she’d have to live with, perhaps for quite some time. She was okay with that, because she didn’t need to hear the words. She felt it. She felt it in her looks, her touches, her kisses. The way her voice softened for her, the way her eyes softened. And her smile. Kate had started to see something in her smile, a flicker of something she hadn’t seen before. She found herself seeking it out, she needed to find it, needed to see it, because whenever she did catch a glimpse, it tipped her world on its head.

    She’d seen it the previous night when Yelena had been very gently re-cleaning the wound that lay just below her ribs. Her touch was warm, her hair loose and messy, and her cheeks were flushed, as they’d both decided they were deserving of a glass of red and the heating turned up to eleven, and that’s when she’d caught a glimpse of it again. The look. Soft, hopeful eyes, small, delicate smile. Kate had wondered momentarily if it was worth getting shot or stabbed on every mission, just for a chance to see that look again. The fairy lights that they’d decorated Kate’s apartment with together twinkled and danced in Yelena’s eyes as she’d chided, ‘Next time, don’t ask the man with the knife if he’s going to stab you, just shoot him, please?’ Kate had agreed, reluctantly. Getting stabbed hurt, even if the wound had been fairly superficial, and surely there would be other opportunities to catch Yelena’s soft, hopeful gaze once more.

    Soft looks had melted into soft kisses and even softer touches across sore skin and bruised flesh. Kate had gasped in equal parts pleasure and pain as Yelena’s grip on her hip had tightened, just that little bit too much. Her girlfriend had apologised but Kate simply pulled her closer and captured her lips a little more fiercely than before. Her fingers had lost themselves in Yelena’s thick tousled hair, and she’d hooked her leg very gently, up and over her girlfriend’s waist, a position both had gotten very used to, but a position that Kate had found was becoming increasingly frustrating for her. She knew this was, at best, a process for Yelena, or at worst something worth managing to be with the woman she loved. And showers were her way of managing. Really long showers.

    Kate released another breath, shakier now than the one previous, as she imagined her girlfriend’s hands on her. Grasping her hips and her thighs. Nails gently digging into the flesh there. Her teeth bit firmly into her bottom lip as she rested her body against the achingly cold tiles, to give her already battle-weary legs a break as the muscles in her thighs and calves grew tighter and tighter as every second passed. If Kate let her mind wander far enough, each droplet of water that peppered across her chest felt like a kiss from her girlfriend’s lips. Each flash of unexpected heat from the shower felt like the grazing of teeth against the sensitive skin of her neck or hips. Each fevered touch of her own felt like her girlfriend’s strong, tactile hands, urging her closer. Fuck, Yelena. Oh fuck. You feel so- The sound of the bathroom doorhandle being turned and then released jolted Kate from her self-indulgences. A chaotic bundle of bed head blonde bulldozed her way into the bathroom, and Kate’s hands quickly found their way from herself to her shampoo-less hair. Smooth Kate. “Fuck, Yelena, what are you...?” Kate asked, through laboured breaths. Had she noticed? And if she hadn’t, would she? Kate’s skin was flushed, but the shower was hot, and she could pass off her shortness of breath as shock right? RIGHT?

    Yelena glanced up from behind her unruly hair with a frown. She was confused, and a little taken aback, like she was the one who’d just been caught out.
