The blonde was quite clearly brushing off the cobwebs left by the thousandth snooze she’d taken. “What are you doing in here?” Kate asked again, as she finally regained the ability to put words into sentences that made sense.

    The blonde simply shrugged. “Brushing my teeth. You told me to get ready.” “Uh huh, I did,” Kate nodded, breathlessly, as she tried desperately to locate the shower gel. “I did tell you that.”

    “And I want to brush my teeth first so I don’t get any toothpaste on myself, because I’m always doing that.” Yelena was not wrong, that was something she was always doing, and it was something that Kate always told her to mitigate by brushing first. This was the very first time that she wished Yelena would discount every piece of advice Kate had ever given her. “You do do that.” Kate’s hands found the shower gel and she rapidly begun working it into a flush disguising lather.

    “But you’ve been in here so long and I want to-”

    “Uh huh, okay, sorry about that, but when you’re fighting international terrorist groups on the Thursday but have to host your family’s annual Charity Fundraiser on the Friday, sometimes you deserve as much hot water as your body can take. So, do you mind just waiting until I’m out?” Was Kate being short? Because she felt as if she was being short. She also felt as if she really needed that orgasm to face the day ahead of her, and currently there was a Yelena Belova sized road block between her and her oxytocin hit.

    “Why?” Yelena’s frowned deeper. She knew something was off.

    “Because I’m in the shower,” Came Kate’s rather knee jerk response.

    Yelena simply shrugged. “Well, it’s not as if I haven’t seen you naked before.” The blonde was not wrong, but Kate was not in the market for rational reasoning at this point. “Right, but...” Kate started, and quickly stopped as Yelena nonchalantly walked over to the sink, picked up her toothbrush and stuck a generous helping of toothpaste on it. Kate sighed at her very stubborn and clueless partner. So much for her prescribed natural pain relief. “Right, okay. You’re still going to brush your teeth.” Kate was not surprisingly a little exasperated, but was also not at all surprised.

    Yelena hunched herself over the sink and stuck her toothbrush in her mouth to start brushing. “Are you going to actually shower?” she asked, as she eyed a bumbling Kate, suspiciously in the bathroom mirror. it was a fair question. Was Kate actually going to shower. In actuality, Kate had showered quite some time ago, but she wasn’t going to tell Yelena that as that would open her up to even more questions.

    “I was just....” Kate sighed, she was going to have to bide her time and wait. She could wash again, there was no harm in that. It would be worth it. It would be so very worth it, even after the interruption.

    Kate huffed and hunted for the shampoo. Once she found it, she emptied some into the palm of her hand and began to work it through her hair. Maybe one day, she’d be able to entice Yelena into the shower with her, maybe one day. “I’ll wait.” Kate whispered, wistfully, as the shampoo began to lather in her hair.

    Yelena’s eyes flickered to meet Kate’s once again, in the mirror that hung above the sink. The blonde frowned, her eyes a little darker than they were a moment before. She was thinking, deliberating, calculating. Shit. Realisation slowly dawned on her girlfriend and all Kate could do was look away as her girlfriend blinked at her epiphany. Fuck. The Russian pulled the toothbrush from her mouth, unceremoniously, and splattered her black t-shirt with a mist of toothpaste. If Kate hadn’t been so mortified, she’d have tutted and rolled her eyes. “Wait a minute, were you-?”

    “Nope.” Kate cut in quickly, as panic betray her voice.

    “Mastur-”

    “Don’t say it,” Kate begged, but Yelena was too far gone.

    “-bating...?” Kate winced as a word she never thought she’d hear her girlfriend say, and hoped she’d never hear her say again, fell out of her mouth. Yelena looked perturbed, awkward and suspiciously sweaty all of a sudden. Kate felt the same way. She needed to leave. She needed to find the nearest patch of dirt, dig a Kate Bishop sized hole, bury herself inside it and erase herself from existence.

    There was an awkward silence, when all Kate could hear was her heart beating disconcertingly loud over the rhythmical drumming of water against porcelain. Yelena’s eyes darted around the bathroom in a desperate attempt to look anywhere but Kate. “Umm. I’m sorry,” the Russian managed, as she hastily rinsed her toothbrush off and placed it back in the beaker that held Kate’s and the toothpaste. She was leaving, and despite any outcome being awful, Kate couldn’t help but feel a small pang of relief. “I should...” Yelena started, eyes down, as she gestured towards the door awkwardly. “I should leave,” she finished, before she turned on her heel and made her escape.

    Kate groaned and hit her head once, twice and then a third time against the wet tiles of the shower. Of course, this was probably a reality that they were going to have to face up to at some point, but hours before the annual benefit? Fate was a cruel mistress. No, scrap that, Fate was an absolute bitch.

    “Fuck”.

    Kate had emerged from the bathroom to a quiet flat, it seemed as if Yelena had taken herself upstairs, which, once up there, Kate could confirm she had. Kate had found the rather beautiful blonde sat in bed, arms around another blonde of comparable adorableness, Lucky the golden retriever. Yelena had offered Kate a small and slightly unreadable smile, before she had given Lucky one last squeeze, hopped out from under the covers, kissed Kate lightly on the cheek and padded downstairs to the vacated bathroom. Presumably to finish brushing her teeth. Was everything okay? Kate couldn't tell. Sometimes Yelena was a woman of few words, sometimes she was a woman of many, and sometimes she was simply a woman of action. Here, she’d offered Kate a small kiss, on her cheek and her cheek only. Kate had frowned, and told herself not to over think it, something that was more easily said than done, but she had too much to do and far too much to think about to have her brain dominated by one kiss, or lack thereof.

    She’d spent the next half an hour calling contacts, answering supplier queries, patching up the wound below her ribs, blow drying her hair and wondering what was taking Yelena so long in the bathroom. There was next to no chance that she’d been getting up to what Kate had been getting up to, or maybe Kate was foolish to assume that, but either way, half an hour was a long time for someone as efficient and fuss free as Yelena to spend in the bathroom, even if Kate had heard the shower spring to life twenty minutes previous. Kate sighed and pinched her nose just between her eyes in frustration, as she crossed a couple of tasks off of her list of things to do.

    Get ready, was the next task that stared back at her. She sighed again, as she knew that anything involving moving her arms above shoulder height would result in considerable pain. Kate jumped in surprise at the sound of the bathroom door downstairs clicking open. She had emerged.

    A wet haired Yelena padded back upstairs and fixed Kate with a smirk. This wasn’t what Kate had been expecting. She had been expecting quiet, brooding Yelena, not playful, flirty Yelena. “Shouldn’t you be getting ready?” She asked, teasingly. She knew Kate was stressed, she knew she had a thousand things to do, and she knew that so far that day, she’d been zero help. The lie in, despite being incredibly welcome, had also cost Kate an incredible amount of time.

    But Kate smiled. The smirk was a peace offering and the tease was Yelena’s way of saying that they could move on. Whatever long ass pondering her girlfriend had done in that shower, seemed to have worked for the time being, and Kate was thankful for it. The brunette got up from her spot on the bed and stretched painfully, in a desperate attempt to work out the clamping tension that was threatening to reclaim her shoulders after being ousted by the super-hot water of Kate’s shower.

    “I cannot believe I got myself blown up yesterday,” She groaned as she shuffled to her wardrobe and retrieved the black suit, white shirt and black tie that she’d had pressed especially for that evening, as Yelena shrugged off her towel and shrugged on a short, tight red dress. The blonde looked fantastic even then, with wet hair and no make-up. Kate dreaded to think what she’d looked like when her heels were on, and her hair was done in two hour's time. The brunette would most likely expire at first glance. “And stabbed, don’t forget stabbed,” Yelena helpfully reminded her. As if Kate could forget. Kate slid the white shirt off its hanger and began to unbutton it. She tried in vain to shrug the item of clothing on, as her muscles screamed at her and protested fervently. Small, but strong hands took the shirt from hers and eased her arms into the sleeves. It was a small gesture, but one that made Kate’s heart a little giddy.

    “There’s still a thousand things to do and I can hardly move my arms.” “You’re regretting saving those hostages?” Yelena asked with a cheeky smile, as she stepped back to let Kate step into her suit trousers. How had it gotten so easy with them? So perfectly easy. Kate had to admit, she was surprised by how quickly Yelena had managed to shake off their run-in in the bathroom.

    “Look, you don’t know these people. They’re vampires.” And Kate was not wrong. They were energy sucking arseholes at the best of times, and blood sucking leeches at their worst, but these were her people, or at least they were her mother’s people. Sadly, without her mother to run the family, it fell to Kate to maintain decorum, and therefore, she was condemned to them.

    “So, let me get this straight. You’re saying you wish you hadn’t saved those people, because you’re now not in a position to adequately service some rich prick who donates point five of a percent of his annual earnings at the Bishop Family Benefit and calls it charity?" The blonde asked, with a playfully raised eyebrow.

    “Oh absolutely,” Kate said, with a wink as Yelena threaded the brunette’s black tie around and underneath her collar.

    “Said like a true Avenger,” Yelena teased, as she pulled on Kate’s tie and pulled her in for a short but firm kiss. Kate couldn’t help but smile, this felt fine. Good even. Things were fine, right? It was totally normal to brush something like this under the carpet, right? Because that’s where it belonged, right? Not biggie, RIGHT?

    “Amen, baby.”

    Yelena smiled a smile that didn’t quite reach her eyes and patted Kate gently on both shoulders. Kate frowned. That was odd. “If it helps at all, the caterer called whilst you were in the shower, and they’re already at the venue.”

    “Oh really?” That was early, but good. Better early than late.

    “Yep. Said everything looked really good,” Yelena explained as she began to scrunch and towel dry her hair. “So that’s one thing less to worry about.”

    “Good, thank you for sorting.”

    “No problem,” Yelena smiled up at her, before she threw the towel that she was using to dry her hair down, onto the bed and pulled Kate in for another kiss. This time her lips lingered on Kate’s as Yelena’s fingernails dug gently into her shoulders. The Russian held her close, ran her tongue across the brunette’s lower lip, and breathed her in. “And also,” Yelena broke their kiss to whisper, as her hot breath tickled Kate’s skin, “I think you look very handsome in your suit”.

    “You do?” The brunette asked, a little taken aback. It was the first time Yelena had called her anything but beautiful. Of course, she loved it when Yelena called her beautiful, but being called handsome, that just hit different. Her stomach flip flopped and she felt the familiar, hot pull a little lower, at the sound of Yelena’s words. She felt strong, and she felt desired. Just a little. And that’s when it hit her. Something was wrong. Things were wrong, because Yelena had never called her handsome, only beautiful. Always beautiful. Yelena had never cradled her face in the way that she was doing now, she’d never pressed herself flush against her, never dug her nails painfully into her flesh so consciously and purposefully, not like this, not like this felt. Something was different.

    “Mmm hmm,” came Yelena’s answer as she captured Kate’s lips once more. It was like kissing a different person. Like someone else had walked out of that bathroom. Like someone else was in Yelena’s skin. Kate’s stomach lurched involuntarily, but she knew she could handle this. You can handle this right? This wasn’t the first time Yelena had shut down on her, and it probably wouldn’t be the last time either, but this time did feel different. This time she wasn’t dark or brooding, she wasn’t letting her emotions get the better of her. All her previous reactions, despite being eternally frustrating, were all honest and uncalculated, but this time, Yelena wasn’t being honest, this time she was playing a role. This time she was wearing a mask.

    “I mean, you look...” Kate drew back from her girlfriend’s embrace and put her hands to Yelena’s waist, admiring the woman in front of her. Role or no role, she was a sight to behold, and maybe if Kate just persevered, she could ride this wave. This was just Yelena coping right? Kate could cope with that, and her first port of call would have to be flattery. Unabashed, unrepentant, honesty flattery. It wasn’t as if it would be that hard when the woman looked that good, and it wasn’t as if Yelena was particularly skilled at resisting Kate’s dorkish charm. Soon, they would be laughing, joking, kissing and dancing. Soon they would be back to the easiness and comfort that they afforded each other.

    “I don’t even know how to describe you. You just take my breath away.” Kate said, as she tried to say as much with her eyes as she did with her words.

    Something flickered across Yelena’s face. Was it doubt? Hope? Kate couldn’t tell. “Really?” the blonde asked, and Kate wondered how of this Yelena that stood in front of her was real and how much was this new role.

    “Yes,” Kate said, with a soft, encouraging smile, as she drew the blonde towards her again. “I’m just so proud that you’re with me.” Kate leaned in to kiss Yelena once more, in an attempt to exorcise whatever fears or insecurities were bubbling just beneath the surface. But she needed to do more, she needed to say something, she needed her to know that she was enough.

    Yelena had just seen a side of Kate that Kate had kept hidden, and she’d been an idiot to keep it so. But hindsight was a funny thing. Kate needing to let off some steam wasn’t something they’d ever discussed. Foolishly, it was something they’d decided was better left unsaid, but it was something that was surely an inevitability with the type of relationship they shared. Kate drew Yelena even closer and grazed her nose gently against her girlfriend’s. She had to know, she had to know that Kate wanted Yelena above anything. Loved her above anything. The value she put on the comfort Yelena brought her was incalculable, and difference between Kate’s wants and needs wasn’t even worth the debate. She wanted Yelena, and that was enough. Anything else, Kate could manage herself, because it was so much more than worth it. “This is more than enough for me, Yelena. You are more than enough, and I am so proud to be able to say that you’re even just the slightest bit mine.” There was suddenly distance between Kate and her girlfriend, as Yelena strode over to the dresser and began to search through her jewellry, and Kate felt as if she’d been punched in the gut, or stabbed. Either/or. The brunette felt a pang of frustration as her earnest and heartfelt efforts went ignored and unrequited. It won’t last, just keep doing the right thing and you will get through it. But what was the best approach? Was it to reassure her, to be there if she came to her, or was it to leave her alone entirely and well, sweep it all under the carpet?

    “That reminds me,” Yelena said, over her shoulder. “What’s my story?” Kate frowned in confusion. “What do you mean?”

    “I’m very good with rich people,” Yelena explained, as she swapped out some of her usual earrings for a few fancier pieces. “But I’ll need a story. I’m used to entertaining rich Europeans, but I’m sure your rich Americans are just as vapid. They will love a good story, I’m sure.”

    “I don’t know,” Kate shrugged. She didn’t like where this was going. “These people are pretty awful.”

    “Kate, I went to Evil Russian Assassins school for girls. You don’t think they taught us how to be charming?” Kate had never really thought about it, but suddenly Yelena’s whole act made sense. Her girlfriend knew how to play people, she knew how to make them feel wanted, knew what buttons to press and how hard, knew how to turn someone on and turn them around. Of course, she would. And so, when hit with an inconvenient truth that you don’t have the emotional capacity to process, like your girlfriend masturbates in the shower because you can’t satisfy her sexually, instead of shutting down and trying to start a fight with Kate, she’d fallen back into a much subtler and harder to recognise set of behaviours, all because she’d made a promise never to fight with Kate again. She’d also promised to get better at vocalising her thoughts and feelings, but Kate suspected that might take years for Yelena to achieve, not months. But she was making progress, right?.

    “Do you know how many events I attended as an escort that were just like this one?” Yelena asked, nonchalantly. What?

    “They sent you as escorts?” Kate couldn’t quite believe what she was hearing. Of course, they those poor women as escorts. If you’re going to lay complete and utter claim on a woman’s body to take people’s lives, you might as well take their dignity as well whilst you’re at it.

    “Well, I was normally there to escort some rich oligarch into the afterlife.” “You’re terrifying.” Kate kind of meant it. Unbrainwashed Yelena was a force to be reckoned with. She was the most skilled fighter Kate had ever seen. Sure, she was fun to spar with but get her out into the field and she had five or six more gears. Brainwashed Yelena must have been truly scary. Match her skill and efficiency with apathy and ruthlessness and it was easy to see why she was the best and most feared assassin on the planet.

    “Oh, we could say I’m your escort,” Yelena said, excitedly, with a mischievous glint in her eye. That was the real Yelena, sending Kate’s heart into palpitations as usual. “I’m certainly dressed like one,” Yelena looked down at the short cut of her dress that just about grazed her mid-thigh, and appraised her golden rings and her t-bar chains. “Well, a pretty fancy one,” she said with a shrug. “I think I make a pretty high-quality es-”

    “Please don’t tell anyone that you’re my escort,” Kate blurted out, as she waved her hands in front of her in an attempt to erase the notion entirely. That could not happen. Even if Yelena were to say it in jest, Kate would be done. That would be it for Kate Bishop and her benefit dinner. They’d be into her like a pack of rabid dogs with a bone.

    “Not even a fancy one?” Yelena asked, hopefully.

    “No, no, no.” Kate insisted, and added a final, “No,” for good measure. “Well then what is my story?” Yelena asked with a frown. “Why am I there? I’m not a posh New York City socialite.”

    It was Kate’s turn to frown; she shook her head a little in confusion. “Well, you’re my girlfriend, so...”

    “I’m not your girlfriend, Kate.” Came the five words that cut deeper than her assailant’s knife had the previous day. And Yelena always went for the heart. The blonde’s voice was calm, matter-of-fact, and non-negotiable. She was serious and Kate felt herself begin to unravel, quickly and, painfully. What a simple sentence, and what a hurtful one. There was no malice in Yelena’s voice, but no softness either. There was no sympathy or empathy, and Kate wondered if this just her playing another role, how she hoped it was. But in reality, Kate knew that this was just another one of those unspoken things. She knew that it was something she’d been afraid to push for, a topic she’d be afraid to breach, and she knew the reason why. This was the reason.

    Suddenly Kate thought back to the night before. The kisses, the softness, the tenderness and the look. Yelena’s new look. She’d let herself hope that it was something more, and indication that the feelings Kate held for the Russian, the Russian held for her too. She’d let herself hope it was love or something close to it. She hoped Yelena was falling and her heart had felt warm and light and full but now her heart felt pained and tight and emptier with every moment that snuck by. .

    Kate blinked, and for a moment, she found it very difficult to piece together exactly what her brain was telling her. What? “You’re not?” Kate asked, before her brain had made a rational attempt to communicate effectively with her mouth. It was feeble and pathetic but it was all that would come out. “You’re not. Of course, you’re not.” Oh no, there were more words, “Why would we say that?” Kate was surprised by the bitterness in her own voice, but either Yelena hadn’t been or it had been lost on her entirely.

    This was all fine though, Yelena could just ignore it. Ignore the hurt she’d caused, ignore Kate’s embarrassment from getting caught in the shower earlier, ignore her battered ego, ignore the fact that she had to host a charity dinner. Just ignore it all. “Oh! I could be your mysterious Russian cousin.”

    Kate felt something unfamiliar, deep in her gut. It wasn’t desire or lust or love. It was anger. Anger at Yelena’s jokes, at her cluelessness, anger at her complete and utter inability to look up at her goddam girlfriend and see someone in pain. All the brunette could do was shake her head dejectedly. “All these people have known my family since the early nineteen-hundreds, Yelena.” She said and did her best to fight back a grimace of pain as she threw her jacket on, unaided.

    “Escort is the only explanation then.”

    “Could we please drop the escort thing?” Kate pleaded, with a groan, as she slipped on her boots. She was done.

    “What? There’s nothing wrong with being an escort.”

    “I just wanted...” Kate started, this time in anger, before she caught herself. She was mad, and sad and she needed somewhere to put it all. Yelena blinked back at Kate, and it dawned on the brunette that perhaps this was the first time Yelena had ever seen Kate truly lose her cool. “I was just hoping that...” Just hoping that what? That she would be proud of you, the way that you were proud of her? Kate thought. Had she been hoping that Yelena might come with her to Barton’s for Christmas, as her girlfriend? Sure. Had she known that Yelena would turn her down? Also, affirmative. Had she been hoping that Yelena would agree to telling Carol about them so they didn’t have to feel as though they were living a double life? So that they could be open and free and happy? Absolutely. Had she been hoping that Yelena would dance with her this evening, in front of all those fucking rich idiots who thought she’d amount to nothing? Had she been hoping that the very same rich idiots would realise that it really didn’t matter if she never amounted to anything because all that mattered was the little slice of happiness they’d managed to forge together? Sadly, yes. She had. She’d been dumb enough to hope. What a fucking idiot.

    “You know what, it doesn’t matter,” Kate continued. Vitriol had crept into her voice. “I work with you, I invited you, we’re friends. That’s all it needs to be.” Because seriously, just fuck it. Kate didn’t have the time or the headspace to go there. Yelena liked her, Yelena thought she was beautiful, Yelena kissed her and held her and cared for her and comforted her, and yes, Yelena was obviously going through a crisis of confidence right now that frankly, Kate just didn’t have time for it. So, fuck it. Kate finished angry tying her laces and got to her feet.

    “Right,” Yelena agreed, with a cool shrug. “Let’s not over complicate things.” Kate knew that the blonde wasn’t referring to the charity dinner, she was referring to them and their relationship. All she could do was smile, wryly, and park her unravelling thoughts. She could feel her phone buzzing and fighting for her attention in her pocket, as guests, entertainment and florists were no doubt trying to get ahold of her. She didn’t have time to fall apart, and she didn’t have to piece her relationship back together. Because no matter how hard Yelena pushed back, that’s what it was. It was a relationship. And even if she picked it back up again in the morning, battered and bruised, much like her body, it could be fixed. If something went wrong with the dinner now, well, that couldn’t be.

    Kate shook her head. She wanted to find something snappy to say, something that told Yelena she wasn’t going to concede that easily, that she was going to have a fight on her hands once the evening was over, but she couldn’t find the words, or the energy. “Cool,” was the most apathetic thing that could have tumbled from her mouth, but tumble it did, as she waltzed passed her non-girlfriend, down the stairs and threw herself onto the couch to make about a thousand overdue phone calls.

    “Oh boy,” came Yelena’s voice, as it floated down from the upstairs balcony. Her tone was a familiar one; it was the tone she reserved for only for Lucky, and Fanny of course. He’d been sleeping quietly at the end of Kate’s bed since she’d emerged from the shower and had continued to sleep, undeterred by the attempted dissolution of their entire relationship. “Looks like I’m in the dog house today, hey?”

    Understatement of the year, Yelena Belova, understatement of the year.

    Once Bitten and Twice Shy Chapter Notes Sorry. You keep leaving such nice comments and I follow it up with this? Thank you to Kristin for being a brilliant sounding board and beta, and thanks to you as always, you guys are awesome and you don’t deserve this kind of treatment, but here it goes. You did want them to have that all important talk. Be careful what you wish for. See the end of the chapter for more notes

    The rest of the afternoon had gone by in a blur. It had been crisis after crisis to deal with for Kate, leaving no time for her to deal with her own current personal crisis. Lucky hadn’t wanted to be parted from them, probably something to do with the fact that his moms weren’t talking. The florist had gotten lost and had needed retrieving from 94th and 5th instead of 49th and 5th, which had been an absolute schlep up Maddison Avenue and then back down. What florist takes Uber XLs to venues?

    Thankfully everything had started to come together with a little time to spare before guests had started to arrive. Wine was on tables, the string quartet was warmed up and raring to go, as string quartets always were, waiting staff were milling about and looking dapper as fuck and the caterer had kicked off proceedings in the kitchen. Everything seemed to be coming together, and of course, that’s when disaster had struck. The MC texted, of course they had, calling would have been far too much of an imposition, especially for someone with laryngitis. LARYNGITIS. Just a little spot of laryngitis. Just a person who gets paid to speak for a living, with a little spot of laryn-fucking-gitis that they failed to mention until thirty minutes before guests arrived! Kate felt murderous and at the same time, completely apathetic. She was done, cooked, over. That was it. She couldn’t just pull an MC out of her ass, three nights before Christmas in New York City, thirty minutes before her event kicked off. It just wasn’t going to be possible. She’d had all the suppliers booked for months, months. Kate wanted to laugh, and cry and vomit, and the one person who could usually stop her from doing all of those things was making her want to laugh, cry and vomit. So, there she was, in front of all her guests, holding back the tears and the vomit and the despairing cackle with a microphone in hand. The room was big, silent and expectant. With an extremely nervous smile, Kate’s eyes scanned the room for a diminutive blonde in a red dress, but came up empty. She hadn’t seen Yelena since her trip to rescue the florist, something else that she’d been left to handle by herself, and since returning she had really hit the fan, so seeking Yelena out, despite being high up on her list of things to do, had sadly fallen by the wayside.

    At this point in the day, Yelena’s absence despite being disappointing, wasn’t entirely unexpected, and Kate had to now shift her focus onto surviving the evening. Survive tonight and save her relationship tomorrow, because under this kind of pressure, there was no way that any conversation was going to be constructive, or have the time it needs. Her hand was tight and clammy around the microphone. These were her mother’s people, and her people really. She’d grown up around them, at their events, their fundraisers, their parties their bachelorettes. It was the kind of crowd that knew very little about you but seemed to know everything about you, often before you did. Your grades, your love life, your family’s financial dealings, which had always left Kate wondering how much the people around her in that moment knew about her mother, and before her, her father. She knew that they had very little sympathy for her family’s current situation, despite the kind words and the pleasantries, because one rich family’s loss was another’s gain, and if one rich family went down, a tonne of bad shit could be pinned on them. Which is why Kate’s position was unique.

    Her mother was almost certainly on her way down, for how much, Kate wasn’t sure, but Kate was totally in the clear. Not only because she was the one who turned her mother in, and completely innocent, but because there was almost no way S.H.I.E.L.D. would now let anything happen to her. She had protection, and so did Bishop Security, because unsurprisingly, her mother had her fingers in the government contract pie too. So Kate was an untouchable. She was rich, she was powerful, and she was a threat to these people. That didn’t make them any less terrifying. They were old, they were rich and they were powerful, and the disdain they felt for Kate was palpable. She’d turned in her own mother, what would she do to them? If she had her own way, she’d run for cover and never see these people again. No galas, no benefits, just give it all to charity and do away with it, but that’s where the family lawyers had disagreed, as had her mother. Kate had to reestablish the Bishop name amongst the elite of New York City, amongst the politicians and the law makers. Kate was young, beautiful, and just, and a mother who raised a girl such as that couldn’t possibly be all that bad a person right? The lurking Russian assassin probably wasn’t a testament to that.

    But it was time, time to address the succubi of New York City, and hopefully convince them to part with a good chunk of their cash. Kate could do it, for sure. Kate was charming. That was her thing. Only problem was, she was just a little concerned that the nerves and the sweaty palms weren’t a symptom of stage fright but a symptom of heartbreak. “Hi everyone. Erm…” Kate tapped, nervously into the mic. “Is this on? Is thi-” A sharp, high-pitched wailing out through the elaborate, high-ceilinged dining room. There were a few awkward laughs as Kate cracked a face-saving grin. “Well, it is now. Just as well as I gotta get this thing going right?” The question hung in the air and Kate realised she’d given it too much space. This wasn’t a call and response. She quickly persevered. “Okay. Um, hello everyone. I guess a quick welcome from me, for those who haven’t had the pleasure of meeting me, or for those who last saw me in diapers um, I’m Kate Bishop.” There was a smattering of polite applause, and she was sure that if Yelena was in earshot, she’d be laughing at her expense right now.

    “Obviously my mother couldn’t be here tonight,” Kate smiled, a little awkwardly, and tucked a stray hair neatly behind her ear. “I kinda told her I wouldn’t bring that up, but ah, I guess it’s the elephant in the room right…?” There was another small silence, it certainly was. “But although she can’t be here tonight, and although we probably all know the reasons why, these fundraisers were and still are something that she cares very deeply about. I know that she probably did a lot of bad, verdict pending, but with your help these events have always found a way to do an awful lot of good.” A murmur of approval travelled the dining room, it was good that bad people enjoyed making themselves feel better so much. “So, I just wanted to thank you for your continuing support of the Bishop Foundation. Not everything is perfect right now. In all honesty, you might be looking at us and thinking, Jeez Louise, what a car crash. But you’re here, and I’m grateful for that.” And she was, because sadly, the charity dinner would have been so much worse without the vampires of Hell’s Kitchen. “Although we might appear a little dysfunctional right now, things really aren’t as broken as they seem.” Another round of courteous applause rang around the dining room, as some of Kate's guests cracked well-mannered smiles or mumbled what she hoped were words of agreement or encouragement. Her rambling yet surprisingly coherent speech had already gone on for far longer than even she had anticipated. Unsure if that was a positive, Kate decided that it would be wise to tie things up. “So, I hope you all enjoy yourselves tonight. Again, thank you so much for coming. Please dig deep this evening, it’s all for a number of wonderful causes, and of course, Merry Christmas”. A bigger cheer erupted now, as guests were delighted to be able to get back to their drinking and merry making, and Kate let out a relieved sigh as the prying eyes of New York City’s rich and powerful removed her from their scrutiny.

    She had survived, for now. Soon she’d have to network and socialise, and to do that, she would need an incredibly large glass of scotch. So, to the bar she went, navigating table after table, saying polite hellos and goodbyes, taking compliments and giving them in return, accepting people’s sympathy but insisting it wasn’t needed. Literally, every interaction with these people was shallow.

    “Scotch, please. Neat, and make it a double, at least.” The barman nodded and quickly got to work. Kate slumped against the bar and huffed, loudly, sending her bangs into disarray. “Kate?” A familiar voice came from behind her. She turned quickly on her heel to come face to face with, quite surprisingly, the one guest she was looking forward to seeing that evening, Jack Duquesne.

    “Jack!” Oh, how Kate was relieved to see a friendly face. Her ex step-father to be was beaming back at her, moustache as coiffed and as jovial as ever. He was dressed sharply, Kate would expect nothing less, but his red bowtie betrayed how excited he was feeling about the holiday season.

    “Kate! My dear!” He bellowed, pulling her into a welcome but quite unexpected hug. “Jack, it’s so... good to… see you!” And it absolutely was, but Kate struggled to get the words out, as Jack’s arms crushed her against him and every single aching muscle screamed to be released. Her ribs burned, arms protested passionately and the stab wound to her midsection began to burn fiercely. “How… are you?”

    “Wonderful Kate, just wonderful.” His hands found her arms and drew her away from him, much to Kate’s relief. “But all the better for seeing you of course. What a feast for sore eyes.”

    “Right…” She laughed softly, at the failed idiom, after all, it was Jack’s trademark, and a rather endearing one at that, but she couldn’t hide her wince.

    He frowned, immediately concerned. “Are you okay?”

    “Oh yeah. Absolutely. A-okay. Right as rain,” Kate lied. She was a wreck, physically and mentally.

    “There is nothing right about rain, Kate.” Jack said, with a soft, concerned smile. “Always so wise,” Kate smiled, affectionately.

    Jack’s eyes narrowed suddenly, he looked around the room conspiratorially and leaned in, with hushed tones. “A little sore from all that crime fighting?” His eyebrows quirked, excitedly. “I bet the other guy couldn’t have scrubbed up quite this well after going a few rounds with you, eh?” He gestured to Kate’s suit and black-tie combo. “I would love to hear all about it.”

    “Something like that, for sure,” Kate whispered back as her phone buzzed in her inside pocket. She groaned inwardly. Every time her phone had buzzed that day, she’d hoped it would have been an apologetic message from her not-girlfriend. Sorry, I’ve been a big meanie, please forgive me. But every time she glanced at her phone, she’d found it to be a supplier or guest with no Yelena in sight. “Sorry, one moment,” Kate smiled apologetically as she delved into her pocket, retrieved her phone and glanced down at the message on the screen. Fuck. “Look, I gotta go. I have some hosty stuff that I need to deal with.” Jack’s smile dropped a little, he was obviously enjoying their reunion. “But I’ll be back, okay? I would love to catch up,” she smiled earnestly.

    “What kind of stuff? Can I be of service?”

    “No, no. Don’t worry.” Jack was sweet, but Jack was not her father, and out of every guest there, he was the only one she actually wanted to enjoy the evening, despite her needing everyone else to.

    “Come on Kate, if things had been different, you’d have had my help this evening.” He was not wrong, how different life might have been. But shit changes when it turns out your mom slash fiancée is embroiled in organised crime. “What do you need? A little charm offensive?” He grinned and his exuberant eyebrows were at it again.

    Charm offensive. Of course. There was no way in hell that Jack could rescue the dumpster fire that was that text message, but there was something else he could take off her hands. “Well, actually, now that you mention it, there is one thing.” It was the turn of Kate’s eyes to dance conspiratorially.

    Kate scoured the side rooms as Jack’s voice boomed through the dining room’s speaker system, and reverberated through the old sandstone building. She can’t have gone far. Yes, Yelena had been avoiding her most of the afternoon and well into the evening, but she also wouldn’t have the audacity to leave the event entirely. Yelena just enjoyed shadows, and skulking in them.

    The acrid smell of cigarette smoke caught her attention. There shouldn’t have been anyone smoking back there, that’s what the smoker’s balcony was for, and there was far more food and drink on hand there. Kate nosed a little further down the lavish corridor of the early twentieth century building, to the room at the end of the hall. It was dark, but Kate could feel a cold December chill emanating from the door that had been left ajar. Slowly and carefully, she nudged the door open, to find Yelena perched on the balustrade of a small balcony, through a set of French windows on the side of the room, with a cigarette pressed to her lips. If the Russian knew Kate was there, she did little to give the game away, as inhaled deeply and held her breath to feel the burn in her lungs. After a moment, she exhaled, and the smoke billowed from her mouth and into the cold wintery night. She must have been frozen, was Kate’s first though, but Yelena showed no signs of discomfort. She simply stared at the traffic below, her eyes unconsciously flicking from car to car, as it moved on by in the late Christmas rush. She looked beautiful there. Still and contemplative, in the lights of New York at Christmas time. Much like the night they’d first met. She’d taken her breath away then, and she certainly took her breath away now. Sadly, she was also the current cause of her impending palpitations, and not in a good way.

    Kate sighed. She wanted to not be angry, she wanted to be able to let it go. She knew that her not-girlfriend was dealing with something, and she knew that she had escaped out here for a reason, but she also knew that she needed help, and when she needed help, she turned to her partner.

    “What are you doing?” Probably not the best way to start. Did she mention that she was angry?

    Yelena was still, her eyes didn’t leave the traffic. “Smoking,” she offered. It was an offer that Kate was not impressed by. Not only was had she been completely absent, but she was out here smoking of all things. Her not-girlfriend smoked. And not only did her not- girlfriend smoke, she could only assume that her not-girlfriend had concealed the fact that she smoked from her.

    “No, I mean, there are a thousand things to do and you’re here.” If Kate sounded exasperated, it’s because she was.

    “I’m just taking a break,” The blonde shrugged, with a nonchalant wave of her cigarette. Kate had to bite down a retort. A break? A break from what exactly? It had been Kate who had been fielding calls, doing chores, entertaining the guests. It had all been Kate. “I need your help, please. I can’t do this by myself.”

    “Yes, you can,” Yelena said, softly, and perhaps a little sadly, as she took another draw from her cigarette. She was sad, Yelena was sad, and it made Kate take pause. She needed to calm down, she needed to soften, and she needed to try and understand.

    Kate closed the distance between her and the woman who she lived with, slept with and who she massaged incredibly often, but was not her girlfriend.

    With Yelena sitting, Kate towered even higher over the smaller woman, she too decided to perch on the balustrade as she endeavored to find Yelena’s eyes. Her mission was unsuccessful, although she had successfully managed to freeze her butt off in .36 seconds. Motherfucker this thing is cold. “You told me that we would do this together. That we’re a team and that we could survive this as a team, like we always do. So...” Kate reached out her fingers found the cool skin of Yelena’s thigh. She squeezed, in what she hoped was a reassuring manner, and offered her a kind smile. “I would really appreciate it if-”. Yelena’s eyes finally met Kate’s. They were dark and uncertain, and didn’t match the smile that was desperately trying to coerce the corner of her lips. “You are doing a great job, don’t worry.” That wasn’t the response Kate had been looking for, but it should have been the one that she’d expected. Despite that, she pressed on.

    “It would just feel a lot easier if you were in there with me,” Kate gave Yelena’s leg another gentle squeeze. Even if Yelena didn’t consider them girlfriends, they were partners. Yelena gave her confidence, strength and balance, and Kate felt so much more equipped to deal with whatever else the night threw at her, if she had Yelena by her side. “So, can you finish up here, please, and then come help?” Kate threw her the warmest of smiles possible, and her eyes practically screamed the anguished please, that she didn’t have to say. There was a moment’s silence, as Yelena weighed up her options. Kate got the distinct impressed that her not-girlfriend wanted to hide away indefinitely, perhaps until the end of time. But she also knew that Yelena found it incredibly hard to resist Kate Bishop. Especially when she smiled just like she was smiling in that moment. The blonde’s head tilted, almost inconceivably. She’d come to a decision. “Okay,” Yelena whispered softly, as she stubbed out her cigarette and deftly flicked it into the cigarette bin that was stood a few feet away. “Nasty habit anyhow,” she added flippantly.

    Kate sighed with relief, but it didn’t do much to relieve any of the anxiety that she had placed elsewhere, because she currently had a disaster on her hands. “Thank you, because the caterer is being an absolute nightmare. They’re saying we didn’t order any vegan options which is ridiculous.”

    Yelena frowned with confusion. “We didn’t.”

    “What, why?” Kate blinked, getting to her feet. Of course, they’d ordered vegan options, of course they would have done that, because vegans exist.

    “Because you said not to,” Yelena shrugged.

    “No, I didn’t.” There was no way she said that.

    “Yes, you did.” The blonde rose to her feet now, in an attempt to claw back a little bit of the height differential and a lotta bit of the dominance.

    “Why would I say that?” Kate’s hands were on her hips.

    Yelena’s hands were on hers. “You said there weren’t any vegans”.

    “No I said I WISH there weren’t any vegans”.

    “Well, that’s not very inclusive,” Yelena shrugged, smugly. It was a joke, and not a very well received one. In fact, in only went to make matters worse.

    Kate pinched the bridge of her nose. How could this have happened? There were five vegans, five, and one was gluten intolerant. Currently, they had nothing to eat, and currently one of their dads owned half of New Jersey. “I literally asked you to do one thing. Deal with one person. If you were confused you could have just asked.”

    “Me dealing with people normally involves two bullets in their brain so I’m sorry if I messed it up.” Yelena threw two hands up in the air, as if she didn’t know what else to say. Perhaps not alluding to their mission in Siberia a few months before would have been wise in that moment. Kate could only groan and turn away from her not-girlfriend in exasperation. “Jesus H Christ. You should come with a trigger warning.”

    “That’s funny.”

    Kate turned back to Yelena and fixed her with a look that said she was done. “No, it’s not. This is serious for me. So, when you’re done here, doing whatever you’re doing, could you please come out and help me. Even if it’s just to talk to people. Rich people love you right?” A muscle twitched in Yelena’s jaw. “They do,” she nodded, coolly.

    “Then please,” Kate clasped her hands together. She was literally begging Yelena to do as she asked. She was having to beg this stubborn, relentless, infuriating asshole, that she loved. She loved her. It would be hilarious if it wasn’t so tragic. After everything Yelena had done for her, everything she’d taught her, the care she’d taken with her, the affection and tenderness she’d shown her, was making sure that the caterer had food for the five vegans attending Kate’s benefit dinner the straw that broke the camel’s back? Kate suspected not. The straw had just landed at the most inopportune moment. “Please,” she said, one more time, “Just humour me.”

    “I said okay,” Yelena said, stoically. Which was true, she had, it didn’t make her response any less annoying, but she’d said it, and Kate just need to take it, suck it up, and get on with sorting out Yelena’s mess. Their mess. Her mess.

    “Okay. Can you just go tell the caterer that we need five vegan meals and I’ll pay double for them? Or triple, or quadruple.” Kate Bishop would pay whatever it took, sadly for Kate, the caterer probably knew that.

    “You could just go get some Bombay Mix from World Foods Store a block away,” Yelena suggested with a small, mischievous grin. Do not take the bait, Kate. “I am not serving Bombay Mix at my mother’s charity fundraiser.”

    “Wow. Kate Bishop,” And the familiar lilt was back in Yelena’s voice, as if nothing had ever happened. “I didn’t know you were such a snob.” DO NOT TAKE THE BAIT. “I am not- you know I love Bombay mix” Kate practically growled as she shoved a finger in Yelena’s smirking face. She took the bait. “You know what, I’m not going to rise to it,” Kate declared, as if she hadn’t already. “Nope. Not today.”

    “Okay.” Was Yelena’s only response. It seemed to be her favourite word of the evening. The summation of her complete and utter apathy. Okay. Kate had to resist the urge to push her not-girlfriend off the balcony.

    Unsurprisingly, it turned out that Yelena Belova could be quite persuasive when she wanted to be. Who’d have guessed it? The caterer had magicked up some vegan delicacies for starter, main and dessert, and had only charged Kate their normal rate and so the dinner had gone off without a hitch. The food had been wonderful, the speakers fantastic, and a LOT of money had already been raised. And much to her surprise, Jack had really shone as MC for the evening. He was totally and completely in his element, and she couldn’t help but grin stupidly, despite everything, as he took to the floor.

    Her boozed filled guests had moved on from the table wine and were now chatting, networking and floating around the dance floor with stronger offerings in their hands. This should have been music to Kate’s ears of course, or her eyes at least, as all the bar profits went straight to the Foundation, but it wasn’t because of her. Yelena was doing exactly what Kate had asked her to do. She was laughing and flirting and dancing and hanging off older men’s arms. Actually, Kate hadn't asked her to do that last one, but let’s face it, it wasn’t a stretch. Yelena was always in control of the situation, of course. When was there ever a situation where she wasn’t? This morning, Kate thought. Oh. OH.

    Nevertheless, the previously out of control blonde was very much in control now. In fact, she had a particular group of men eating out of the palm of her hand, which wasn’t surprising. She was charming, beautiful to an extreme, intelligent, foreign and mysterious, small and petite and perfect for any tall person, and last but not least, she was wearing that dress. Kate sighed, she was beautiful, and she should have been in Kate’s arms in that moment. She wanted nothing more than to march over there, tell the old dudes where to stick it, and pull her close, in front of everyone. She wanted to feel Yelena’s body pressed against hers, she wanted to feel the music together, she wanted to tell her that she loved her. But she knew she couldn’t, not now, and maybe not ever. Not anymore. And that hurt, that hurt an awful lot. “Who’s the blonde that you can’t take your eyes off of?” Kate was pulled, suddenly, from her catastrophising by the sound of her resident MC’s voice.

    “Erm…" Kate hesitated. Who was Yelena, if she wasn’t her girlfriend? Kate’s mouth found the words before her brain did. “She’s someone I work with,” Kate explained, despondently. Jack settled down next to her and filled her glass with a welcome glug of scotch, from a bottle he must have purchased from behind the bar. Ring up them profits. “Oh, so she’s an Avenger too” he whispered impishly.

    Kate took a healthy sip of her Ardbeg. Was she drunk? No, never. Was she merry, absolutely, it was Christmas. Was she happy? Absolutely not. “Don’t let her hear you call her that but yeah, she kinda is.” And it was true, Yelena had signed a contract of sorts, and they certainly wore the really sexy uniforms, but calling Yelena an Avenger was a sure-fire way to lose your head.

    “How come I’ve never heard of her?” Jack asked, and it was a fair question. Most Avengers were marketed to shit, or had pretty unignorable abilities. You know like, they get angry and turn big and green, or they’re a big blonde god, or they have even more money than Kate. “She likes to keep a low profile, you know? One of those ‘works in the background whilst the flashy guys swoop in and take all the credit’ Avengers.” Kate frowned for a moment, which begged the question, which one was she? Sure, she was Hawkeye, but that didn’t mean she had to be Clint’s Hawkeye, but until that point and until she just pretty much confirmed it to Jack, no one else outside of the facility knew about her Avenger status. “Oh, I see I see.” He tapped his nose and winked. Again, despite feeling awful and heartbroken, Jack managed to draw a smile from Kate. What a difference a year made. Kate glanced up at Yelena, who was still laughing at old man vampire jokes and sipping her White Russian with satisfaction. What a difference a year made, indeed. A year ago, they were up on that roof. A year ago, Yelena threw her off said roof and a year ago, Kate marched back up there stubbornly. Still the best shot she’d never taken. “Well, she’s double o seven, and just as dashing”.

    “Yup.” Kate said, as she folded her arms. Didn’t she know it.

    “It’s a lovely dress,” Jack continued, innocently.

    Kate snapped. “Look I know she looks practically edible okay. You don’t need to point it out.” And just like that, Kate Bishop came out to Jack. Kind of, not that she felt like there was much to come out as. She was in a relationship with a person, who happened to be a woman, and that relationship was probably over, despite it being the most beautiful and fulfilling relationship she’d ever had.

    “Does she know how you feel?” He asked, softly. Kate smiled and shook her head ever so slightly. Kate would have been lucky to have him as a step-dad.

    “I don’t know. I don’t think it would be a good thing, not right now.” Telling Yelena that she loved her would only terrify her even further, and maybe she needed to be honest, maybe she needed to tell Yelena the truth and risk losing her. Then at least she’d know that she’d done everything and said everything. Then at least Yelena would know that she was capable of being loved. What she wanted to do with that information was up to her. “What? Tonight would be the perfect night,” Jack said, with a twinkle in his eye. “It’s Christmas, the venue is beautiful, the hostess even more so.” He winked and Kate rolled her eyes. “Come on, what have you got to lose? I’m sure we could find you some mistletoe”. His eyes searched the venue, feverishly.

    Kate sighed. Jack was adorable, but ultimately completely and utterly clueless. “We live together Jack. I’ve kissed her before.”

    “Oh. Really?” He glanced up at her in surprise.

    “Yes. Many times.”

    “Well,” he got to his feet a little unsteadily, reached for the champagne bucket in the middle of the table, and retrieved a not-quite-empty bottle of bubbly. “I suppose congratulations are in order!” He beamed, clearly not reading the situation all too well. At least he was making an effort, which was more than most that evening. He poured Kate and himself a glass, and handed the sparkling liquid over. Kate gladly accepted with a smile and a clink of crystal. Exactly what she needed, more booze!

    “You should ask her to dance,” he offered, as he settled back down next to Kate, both of them now staring out, a little forlornly onto the dance floor.

    Kate would love that. “She’d hate that.”

    “Why would she hate that?” Jack asked, clearly confused by the whole situation. In his mind, love was very simple. Be charming and debonair, and females would succumb to your gentlemanly charms. In a non-creepy way. He was a romantic, in the old-fashioned sense of the word, and it was all rather lovely, but it really wasn’t them. So often, being with Yelena was the most romantic thing. The no-sex thing seemed to unlock so many other wonderful ways to impart love on someone. Everything seemed to gain so much more meaning and purpose. Cooking for romantic meals for each other, surprising each other with small tokens or takeout and blankets on a cold evening, caring for each other with kisses and massages and soft and gentle touches, waking up pressed against each other, Yelena’s skin on hers, Yelena’s hands in hers, Yelena’s lips on hers. Everything she’d taken for granted with other people meant so much more with Yelena, because all these things were the ultimate expression of affection for her well, not-girlfriend. And there was the rub. Kate frowned. Her very affectionate not-girlfriend. Kate really was well and truly fucked.

    She sighed and sipped at her champagne. “I don’t know, Jack. I just don’t think she wants to be seen with me tonight”.

    “Oh”. He tsked quietly. “What a shame. Trouble in paradise?” You have no idea buddy. “Yeah,” Kate nodded, forlornly. “It’s just all been a bit of a surprise. I didn’t… think,” She sighed with another glance over to where Yelena was now dancing with one of the younger gentlemen in the room. Actually, Kate was probably related to that younger gentleman, in some complicated fashion. “I should have seen this coming.” And she was right. She should have. She shouldn’t have sprung the girlfriend thing on Yelena, she should have seen this run-for-the-hills reaction coming from a mile away. Of course Yelena would react like this, of course she’d stop communicating. She’d happily indulge you with a story about her first kill or the time she almost bled out in a Turkish swamp, was rescued but caught typhoid. But when did she ever talk about Natasha unprompted? When did she talk about her parents? Like, really talk about her parents and their time together in Ohio. It was very rare, and it was either preceded or followed by some kind of dissociative behaviour. Kate should have asked her, weeks ago, when she’d first told Yelena about the dinner, when she’d first invited her. It had just seemed too soon at the time, maybe the whole thing was too soon. Maybe she loved her too soon.

    “Kate,” Came Jack’s soft voice, filled with concern. “She would be an absolute fool to say no to you,” he said earnestly, and he wasn’t wrong. Yelena would be a fool, look at her. But fools do a lot of things for a lot of perfectly valid reasons, Kate should know. He paused for a moment of contemplation, and then asked, “Do you want to ask her?”

    Yelena was laughing, quite genuinely now, at someone’s seemingly hilarious anecdote and Kate’s heart felt warm and heavy. She was so beautiful when she loved. If there was one thing Kate loved more than the physical touches and kisses, it was making Yelena laugh. She couldn’t hear it, not over the tumultuous dining room, but she didn’t need to, she knew exactly what that laugh sounded like. Rasping, warm, uninhibited. There was a magic quality to it, that no matter how bad a day Kate was having, that laugh could turn it on its head. Kate sighed a wistful sigh. Of course, she wanted to ask Yelena to dance, she’d been thinking about it for weeks; what she’d feel like in her arms. How she fit so perfectly. Would Yelena be a good dancer? Would it be romantic or goofy or some adorable amalgamation of the two? “I want to ask her. More than anything,” Kate said, with a wistful sigh.

    “Then ask her,” Jack said, a little more enthusiastically, and gave Kate a gentle nudge to the ribs with his elbow. What a terrible idea and fuck that hurt, but Jack was too merry and too preoccupied with the dancers to notice Kate’s wince. However gentle and how unintentional Jack’s nudge had been, Kate’s side was now burning.

    The music came to a natural stop and Kate took a deep, steadying breath. She was going to do it. Fuck it, she was going to ask Yelena to dance, because at this point, what did she have to lose? Being rejected on the dance floor was no worse than the girlfriend rejection, and surely a dance wasn’t too much to ask. It wasn’t a life-long commitment, it wasn’t even a short-term one, it was momentary. Just like their relationship. Maybe if she could just hold her close and show her how she felt, rather than using words, if she could just speak Yelena’s language rather than her own, maybe Yelena would want her back. Maybe Yelena would be proud of her too.

    Kate placed her glass of champagne on the table, gave Jack a confirmatory nod, rose to her feet and smoothed down her tie and dress shirt. Her blazer was still hung across the back of her chair, it had grown far too hot inside the benefit, despite the blizzard that had taken up residence outside.

    “Go get her,” Jack said, softly, as Kate stepped out towards the dance floor. She weaved in and out of the revelers, towards her target. She wasn’t easy to lose in a crowd, despite her height. There was no way Kate could lose sight of Yelena Belova in that red dress. The crowd cheered as the band came to life, with the intro of yet another Christmas classic, and couples began to move and sway in time with the music. Kate deftly sidestepped one couple, then ducked underneath the flailing arms of another, who were dancing a little too exuberantly. With one more twist and another turn, she’d arrived at her destination.

    Yelena who was talking still talking to their friend from New Jersey, had her back to her, whether that was intentional or not, Kate didn’t know, but she was quite sure that Yelena was aware of Kate’s whereabouts at all times. The brunette swallowed, gave herself and moment, and gently tapped the blonde on the shoulder. Yelena turned ever so slightly, confirming what she already knew, it was Kate. She turned back to her every growing group of admirers and excused herself, incredibly politely, and then turned to face Kate. She was smiling widely, her face a little flushed from the heat of the dance floor and the double vodkas in her White Russians.

    “Hi,” Yelena said, a little breathlessly. She looked her happy, her eyes alight in the warm holiday hues of the Benefit Dinner.

    “Hi,” Kate said, a little hesitantly.

    “Vegan crisis sorted?” Yelena asked, genuinely, her attitude from earlier in the evening seemed absent. Kate’s hesitancy waned slightly. Maybe Yelena would be more receptive than Kate had originally thought. Maybe.

    “Yeah, whatever you did seemed to work like a charm so, thanks.” Kate smiled widely, hoping that it would mask the worry and apprehension undoubtedly evident in her eyes. “Good,” She smiled. “I told you we could handle it.” Her voice was smooth, and low and reassuring and for a moment Kate felt like things were normal. Like Lucky had vommed on the stairs and they’d stemmed the flow, or a ten-story building had started to collapse and they’d managed to evacuate all the residents. That kind of normal. The kind of normal where they could pretty much boss anything life had to throw at them if they worked together. The kind of normal that Kate loved.

    “Yes, you did, and I should have listened to you on the Bombay Mix. I could smash a kilo of that stuff right now, and it would certainly help with the whisky.” Kate grimaced a little awkwardly and drew a sympathetic smile from her not-girlfriend.

    “You didn’t eat?” She asked.

    “No, I was just so busy and-”

    “You haven’t eaten all day?” Yelena asked, with genuine concern. Of course, Kate hadn’t eaten all day. She’d been busy and also completely and utterly petrified that she’d lost you. “I’m fine. Really. I can eat when I’m dead, right?” Kate smiled but still couldn’t shake her awkwardness. This wasn’t the conversation she wanted to be having. She should just ask. Just do it. Just ask. “Umm, I was wondering something actually...” Do it Kate. “Umm, if you would…” Breathe. “I mean you look…” Incredible, say the word incredible. “And I would really love to…” Ask you... “umm…”

    Yelena raised a slightly perturbed eyebrow, and instinctually reached out to place an easing hand on Kate’s arm. “Darling, you are malfunctioning,” she whispered. Darling. That word from that mouth should come with a public health warning. May cause cold sweats, palpitations and heart attacks.

    “Really? I…” Heart attack, impending.

    “It’s very sweet,” Yelena smiled, but Kate could only frown. As lovely as it was to hear the endearments fall from Yelena’s lips, they only served to confuse Kate. “Oh, well that’s good to hear, considering,” the brunette scratched her head a little, suddenly this seemed like a bad idea. They were both a little drunk, and although she was slightly disinhibited now, with her language and her muscle memory, Yelena couldn’t escape years' worth of trauma at the bottom of a few White Russians.

    “Considering what?” Yelena asked. It was innocent, too innocent. Yelena knew exactly what Kate was referring to. The incident in the bathroom, the girlfriend conversation, Yelena’s extended absence in the day and then their argument on the balcony.

    “Nothing. Nope.” Kate shook her head fervently.

    “Kate...” Yelena’s other hand went to Kate’s elbow, and the brunette noticed a few New Jerseyan eyes fall upon them.

    “It’s really fine, actually, I just thought that maybe you wanted another drink.” “Kate, you’re sweating.”

    “It’s hot.”

    “What is it?” Yelena asked softly as her eyes searched Kate’s. This woman will destroy me. She could do this, she fought aliens for a living, she could ask a girl to dance. She could ask a girl with soft eyes and soft lips and soft skin she’d been so lucky to taste so many times previous. What was a dance, compared to that. There was a moment of silence as Kate’s breath caught in her throat. She swallowed it down and smiled hopefully at Yelena, heart pounding in her ears.

    “Do you wanna dance?” It was practically a whisper, but Yelena heard her. If she hadn’t heard her over the noise of the band, Kate was pretty sure that Yelena could read lips. Yelena’s soft eyes faltered. “Right now?”

    “Yes,” she bit her lip. She should have said no, because she already knew Yelena’s answer. “Just you?” Yelena’s eyes left Kate’s.

    “Yes.” She pulled her hands away.

    “In front of all these people?”

    Kate felt hot and cold at the same time. A shot of pain filled her chest and she tried desperately not to wince. “Yes, in front of all these people.”

    Yelena looked up at her, there was regret in her eyes. It was the first time Kate had seen it. She knew her words hurt Kate, she knew how they affected her and she wished that she could give her a different answer. At least that meant something.

    “No. I’m sorry, I just-”

    “No, it’s fine,” Kate cut in. Of course, it wasn’t fine but the quicker their conversation would be over the better. She winced again but tried to breathe through it. “Kate...” Yelena started.

    “I’m fine. Maybe a little embarrassed.”

    “Kate…” She said again, her tone different. It sounded like a warning. “Maybe a little hurt but um, nothing I can’t handle right? Carol sent me on that resilience training for a reason.” She was talking now, spiraling and doing her darndest to cover it up. You couldn’t be having a mental breakdown if you appeared to be completely and utterly lucid.

    “Kate,” Yelena grabbed her arm and shook. “You’re bleeding.” She gestured to the spot just underneath her ribs. Oh shit, Kate was bleeding, and through her white as white shirt no less. “Oh, hey would you look at that. I should uh...” Kate glanced apprehensively around the dance floor, checking for prying eyes. Considering the shirt was supposed to be a cover for the bumps and bruises she gained whilst Avengering, it would be best to try and keep it that way. Kate Bishop, daughter of Eleanor, could not be seen, bruised and bloodied at her own benefit dinner. The Vampires would be circling, for sure. “I should do something about that,” Kate continued. “I’m going to go and do something about that.” She turned on her heel and started to make her way back across the dancefloor to where she and Jack had been sitting. “Kate!” She heard Yelena’s voice call, from somewhere in the throng behind her.

    “I’m fine, it’s fine, I’ve got this,” she called behind her. At this point, she didn’t care whether Yelena had heard her or not. She didn’t need her help. She didn’t need her help with dinner, she didn’t need to patch her up, she didn’t need her to dance with her, or train her or teach her anymore. Kate could do this by herself.

    The brunette scooped up her jacket, waved off all of Jack’s concerned noises and marched towards the quieter corridor, where she had found Yelena a few hours previous. “Kate, let me help you.” A firm hand caught her by her elbow and turned her around, but Kate shrugged it off.

    “You have been no help this evening, why do you want to start now?” There was a bitterness in her voice, one that she’d managed to elude all evening up until that point. She was bitter now. Bitter, frustrated and sad. How had one twelve-hour period been such a fucking disaster? But of course, it wasn’t really twelve hours, was it? It had been so much more than that. So much time spent avoiding the most difficult subjects, the ones that you were afraid to talk about, because sometimes honesty didn’t always lead to resolution. Yelena stood in silence. She’d known this was coming. Kate could tell, simply from her glum acceptance.

    “Would it have been too much to ask for my girlfriend to actually give a shit?” Kate could hear the emotion in her voice, she could feel the tears threatening to betray her. “I’m not your girlfriend, Kate.” Yelena said, sadly. The Russian looked as dejected as Kate felt, and maybe, just maybe, Yelena regretted not being able to give her what she wanted. Maybe it was even something Yelena wanted too, but it was too much to ask of herself. Too dangerous to ask.

    “Yep, too much to ask,” Kate whispered, and turned to find the women’s bathroom that she’d spied down the deserted corridor. It would be quieter there. She could clean herself up there, she could cry there, and then she could recover there, enough to go back out there and face her guests.

    The bathroom was empty, just as she’d hoped and Kate quickly got to stripping down. She threw her jacket behind the faucets, yanked her tie from around her neck, and began to unbutton her shirt. Kate looked down at the offending stab wound. The gauze that she’d treated it with earlier was completely saturated, the wound itself must have bust open somehow. Wow, she’d been an idiot.

    She ran the cold water and carefully placed the blood-stained part of her shirt underneath it, then she rummaged around in her jacket pockets to retrieve a few supplies that she’d made sure to pack in case of emergencies such as this. She really did have all bases covered that evening.

    Kate whined a little as she peeled back the dressing to revealing an angry looking stab wound. Fuck. She tore open an anti-septic wipe and began to dab at the area, trying to clean away as much of the blood as possible. The door swung open and Yelena walked in, a determined look on her face. Kate couldn’t do this; she just needed the stillness of the bathroom and the coolness of the water. She just needed Yelena to not be around her anymore.

    “Please, let me help you.” Was Yelena begging her? Surely, she wasn’t begging her. Well, it didn’t matter, because she didn’t need anyone’s help.

    “Nope.”

    “Kate.” Yelena insisted.

    “You’re not my girlfriend. Why would I let you help me?”

    “Because you are bleeding.”

    “Absolutely not. If you can’t help me with a caterer, you can’t patch me up when I’m bleeding. This is real life; this is part of my life and you can’t pick and choose which part you’re comfortable with.” Kate shook her head and continued to clean her wound, as she flung a saturated wipe into the trash and tore another one from the packet angrily. “That’s not what I’m doing. I am not choosing to be dif-” But Kate didn’t want to hear it. "Oh really? You train me, you fight next to me, you patch me up when I’m hurt, you kiss it better; literally. We’re in this Avengers bubble and it’s intense and incredible, but then it gets to real life and I can’t- I can’t depend on you.” She threw another wipe into the trash and threw her hands up to gesture to the building that surrounded them, and the people within it. “This is my life, Yelena. This is my public life and I wanted you to be a part of it.” Suddenly, Yelena looked small in her dress, and her shoes and her jewellery. “You can depend on me,” she spoke weakly. It was the first Kate had ever heard Yelena speak in that way.

    “Sure. To buy me pizza when I feel like shit or take Lucky to the vets but-” “I’m sorry about the caterer,” she apologised, quietly.

    Kate shook her head and placed two hands upon the porcelain of the sink. Their eyes met in the mirror for a moment until Kate tore hers away. She was mad, and Yelena’s eyes were soft and filled with trepidation. How could she be mad when that’s what she was faced with? How could she spout her vitriol when the woman that she loved was looking at her like that. This was the most honestly Yelena had ever looked at her. The mask was slipping, in the harsh artificial light of the early twentieth-century bathroom. Kate sighed and closed her eyes. “I’m not upset about the caterer”.

    There was a moment’s silence, Kate couldn’t even hear Yelena’s breathing over it. “I’m learning how to do this. This real-life thing.” Her voice was closer than Kate had expected, and it was heavy too, heavy with emotion. Kate felt rough fingertips touch her hip, delicately. “Please, just let me hel-“ But Kate pulled away. It was awful but she had to break the pattern. Kate got hurt and Yelena made it better. It was how Yelena showed that she cared, but Kate needed more now.

    A flicker of frustration showed on Yelena’s face, but the ex-assassin buried it. “Please do not be mad at me.”

    “I am mad, and I’m hurt.”

    “I’m sorry for hurting you. It is not what I want,” Yelena’s eyes couldn’t meet hers. Her hands were tense, and her brow furrowed. Kate realised that this was the most vulnerable she’d seen Yelena. It hadn’t been when she’d killed for her, it hadn’t been when she’d stripped her and adored her, it hadn’t been when she’d shopped for tampons for her, or told her about her first kill. It was this moment, by far. “You mean a lot to me,” it was only a whisper.

    “It hasn’t felt like it today,” Kate murmured. In fact, it had felt like quite the opposite for a majority of it.

    “But it has felt like it on other days?” Yelena asked, hopefully.

    “Of course, it has, Yelena. There are times when I’m with you that I...” Kate caught herself, she wanted to say everything and nothing. She wanted to be honest but was so afraid of pushing her away even further. They were on a knife’s edge, and they both knew it. “But, I just don’t understand what it was all for, if you don’t want me like that.” “Kate.” Yelena was shaking her head.

    “As your girlfriend, not the other thing, I don’t care about the other thing.” And she didn’t, she could manage it, she would manage it; for Yelena it was worth it.

    “Yes, you do.”

    “No, I don’t.” She needed to make her see, somehow, she needed to make her understand. “Yelena-”

    “You might not now but you will and what if I can’t give you it?” Their voices weren’t hushes anymore, their voices were raised and desperate.

    “I get to say that, I get to say what I want.”

    “But things change, Kate.” Yelena was sad and exasperated. She ran her hands through her hair in an attempt to quell the unhelpful energy that was building inside of her. “Do you know how afraid I am of that?” Her eyes met Kate’s. “Of change? Yesterday I wasn’t your girlfriend. Today I am? Just like that? I’m too much of a pussy to dance with you in public, I’m not made to be anyone’s girlfriend.” There were tears in Yelena’s eyes now as Kate bit back her own.

    “You dance with Russian oligarchs.” It was a dumb argument but Kate felt as if they were slipping, slipping from that knife’s edge.

    “But this is real life, Kate!” Yelena’s voice was well and truly raised now. It was tearing and breaking, like just like Kate’s dumb little heart.

    “You jump out of planes, you fight twenty dudes at a time, you walk IN to exploding buildings. Those things are all real and all fucking terrifying. What is so scary about this?” But Kate knew the answer. She knew that for Yelena risking her life was way less scary than risking her heart. So, Kate decided to ask the question.

    “Is this about this morning?”

    For a moment, Yelena stood in silence, her eyes watching the water pool and then disappear down the sink. “No. It’s not about this morning.” She swallowed and shook her head a little. “It’s about every time you’ve had to do that.” Yelena’s breath caught a little and Kate suddenly, Kate got the feeling that this was too much for her. Talking like this, about this, in such a charged way. “I never thought…” But she couldn’t finish her sentence. Kate groaned with frustration, and then closed the distance between herself and the woman she loved. This was the most she’d ever seen of Yelena, of the real human being. And despite being enraged and hurt and upset, Kate’s heart found warmth in the realisation that there was so much more of her to love. So much more of her that deserved it. “Yelena, that doesn’t matter to me. I’ve been doing that over you since...” This is going to be embarrassing. “God, since before you even came back to New York City.” She took another step towards the beautifully broken woman in front of her and drew her into her arms. It felt so good to have her there. Yelena didn’t resist her. “It does not matter.” “Of course, it matters. It matters to me. That I can’t make you feel the way that you deserve, that I’m broken in this way.”

    “No. No, no.” Kate’s hands cradled Yelena’s delicate features and brought their foreheads together, gently. “You are not broken, Yelena.” She needed to make her see somehow, she needed to make her understand. “Do you know how proud I am of you? How excited I was to come here with you? I have been dreading this dinner for weeks, but the idea of being able to come here with you, with the strength that you give me, that’s how I’ve faced up to this.” Kate drew Yelena even closer, like she was breathing the woman in. Merging every part of herself with every part of Yelena. “You’re so… God, I can’t even find the words. Just the idea of dancing with you, in front of all these people, fills me with so much pride.” She felt hot tears meet warm cheeks, as soft lips met hers. They kissed desperately for a moment. Yelena’s strong hands grasped at her shoulders, and Kate’s arms pulled the woman impossibly close. it was devastating. After a moment longer Yelena broke away from Kate and shook her head, sadly.

    “This idea of a person that you have in your head, I want to be it for you, very much,” She shrugged a little in Kate’s embrace. “But it is just not me.”

    “But it is. It can be.” Kate tried to pull her closer once more but Yelena resisted. “I cannot promise you that. And I am so thankful that you are proud of me, and I am so thankful too, for the love that you show me, but I am not proud of me and I don’t think that I will ever be.” Kate felt Yelena slipping away, slipping through her arms. “I can be proud enough for the both of us. Remember, remember what you said?” Kate was back to that night, that first night after her first mission, back to what Yelena said. That she would love her enough for the both of them. “I can do that. Yelena, I...” It was her last chance, maybe her last ever chance to make Yelena understand, that she could be loved, she deserved to be loved. “Yelena, I… I love you.”

    But the Russian went stiff in her arms, and Kate knew her chance had gone. “You don’t mean that.” Yelena’s voice had changed again, it was more even, dismissive almost. Kate released her.

    “I do,” she said, solemnly. There was no use raising her voice, no use fighting, because she had done all she could. The ball was in Yelena’s court, and Yelena had absolutely no idea what to do with it.
