    “You love this thing that we might have together in the future but-”

    “No. I know myself. I know what I want and I want you. You don’t get to judge me like that until you know yourself. I love you, and you will not make me feel ashamed of that. I’m not a kid who doesn’t know her own feelings, I’m not like you.” It was harsh, and maybe a little too blunt, but she needed to say it. She needed Yelena to know that she wanted it, Kate was ready.

    “I want the whole package, Yelena, and I know exactly what I’m signing up for. Your beauty and your empathy and your gentleness. Your patience and your strength. All these things that I never expected of you, and I never asked of you but you gave them so freely.” Kate took a step towards the woman she loved and reached out, to gently brush a thumb over a tear-stained cheek. Their eyes met. “If that’s not a reason to love someone, then I don’t know what is.” Kate’s words echoed through the tiled bathroom. Both women understood their significance.

    Kate tore her eyes from Yelena and sighed sadly. She grabbed her shirt from the sink, and threw it back on, making sure to double up on the gauze over her wound. With a small, rueful laugh, she wiped away her tears, wrestled her jacket on and buttoned it up; effectively cover the blood and now water-stained shirt. She smiles sadly at Yelena. The woman looked broken, but it wasn’t her job to fix her, not any more. “Now, I have to go back out there and pretend, in front of all those people, like we didn’t just break up.”

    “Kate, I just need-”

    “Come back to me when you’ve decided to stop being the biggest, most stupidest idiot of all time.” And with that, Kate strode back across the bathroom, and passed Yelena. “Kate,” Yelena caught her arm in quiet desperation as she tried to pass. “I don’t know how to do that without you”. Her eyes were panicked and lost and it took all the strength Kate had not to pull her back into her arms. Not to try and love her and fix her and comfort her. Yelena needed some time without Kate, without the pressure, without the good distractions to mask the bad.

    Kate smiled and said something she truly, whole-heartedly and painfully hoped was true. “You’ll work it out.”

    She stared at the spiraling water as it made its inevitable journey down the sink. Yelena took comfort in the inevitable, at least she knew what to expect. If she cut you, you’d bleed. If she punched you in the right spot on the sternum, your heart would stop. And if she slid a knife into your chest, up and under your ribs, and twisted, you’d die, there was no stopping it.

    This between her and Kate, this had been inevitable. She’d been an idiot to try and avoid it. But even though the knife had been twisted, and even though she knew that there was no going back, it still hurt. She could feel the blade beneath her ribs, the blood rushing from her body, the cold taking over her senses. Really, this was her just returning to normal. She’d only really entered the world of the living the day she met Kate. Since Natasha’s death, Yelena had been sleepwalking through life. What harm would there be in simply going back to sleep? She wasn’t made for this life anyway? Not for Kate’s life, that was for sure. Kate was too good, and too gentle, and too beautiful. Yelena would never be enough, whether it be physically or emotionally. Kate needed more, she deserved more. Someone who could illicit even more beauty from her smile, someone who could appreciate the depths of her gentleness and the heights of her goodness. She deserved someone who could make her feel and scream and yearn, someone who could fulfill the tiniest want and need. And Yelena wasn’t that person. That was evident now.

    She caught sight of her own eyes in the bathroom mirror. They were dark and empty and Yelena knew it was time to leave. She pushed against the door and made her way back down the hall. The party was still in full swing as she entered the dining room, and stuck to the shadows. Her eyes found Kate immediately, they always knew where to find her. She was laughing with a group of well-dressed socialites. One of them must have just told an incredibly funny joke, because Kate’s hand was upon his arm, trying its level best to convince him that she too found him hilarious, but her smile never reached her eyes, and her other hand never left the spot just below her ribs. They loved her, evidently. Everyone in this room did. Yelena knew that Kate was terrified of them, terrified that she’d never be good enough, that she’d never have their backing or approval, but there was no need. No one could resist falling in love with Kate Bishop. With her charm and her warmth, and her smile. Yelena had tried.

    Yelena took one last look at Kate, she wanted to take her all in. She wanted to remember her joy and her passion, her weird combination of smarts and enthusiasm that somehow translated into her wild over-zealousness. But she couldn’t, because Kate was sad. Her smile was sad, her body was sad, her frame was smaller than it normally was, and that was Yelena’s fault. She’d spoiled it, she’d spoiled them and she’d spoiled this final moment that she’d have to take in the woman that she loved so much.

    So, she left. She went home, she packed a bag, and she held Lucky tight for longer than she could remember. She didn’t want to leave, but she needed to, and besides, Kate no longer needed her. She’d been truthful earlier, when she’d said that she wasn’t proud of herself, she probably never would be. But she was proud of Kate. Not for tonight, not for pulling off the dinner, but she was proud of the agent she’d become, proud of the Avenger she’d become. Yelena had come to New York City so that Kate could lead the life she’d wanted. Now Yelena would leave New York City so that she could lead the life she deserved.

    Chapter End Notes Yikes. So… we’ve hit our lowest. The only way is up from here. AND, Christmas is just around the corner. Right on time to deliver a much needed Christmas miracle. Don’t worry guys, our faves have got this. Expect a guest appearance or two next chapter, to knock some sense into them.

    I’ve just one wish on this Christmas Eve…

    Chapter Notes So this was a long one. It’s Christmas Eve and our two idiots finally talk. Prepare yourselves.

    Thank you all so much for your comments, your readership and your patience, and thank you to Kristin for offering me so much support with proof reading and the like. You da best.

    What was it that they said about Christmas? Oh yeah, that it was the most wonderful time of the year. What absolute bullshit. Kate had decided that she would be writing an angry letter to the writer of that song, before realising that the writer had in fact passed away thirty years previous. That wasn’t to say that she wasn’t still considering suing someone somewhere for false advertising, despite the eggnog, the Christmas sweaters, the roaring fire and the warm, smiling and happy family; all things that she’d usually associate with awesome fun holiday times. This year was different however. This year Kate was not feeling awesomely fun. She was trying desperately to find that thing within her, that untameable, unrelinquishing Christmas Spirit that could normally shine bright through thick or thin, but today, Kate was finding things particularly trying. She could deal with arguing relatives or demanding mothers, she could deal with missing her father at times like this, despite being surrounded by people she considered family, but this Christmas Eve Kate was dealing with something she’d never had to deal with over Christmas before, she was dealing with a break-up.

    You know, people didn’t normally break-up over Christmas, that was just mean. You’d tend to spare each other the pain until New Years, and then act surprised when it happened to avoid exactly this. The Holiday Blues. And of course, as no one knew about Kate and Yelena, which turned out to be one of the biggest sticking points in their relationship, Kate couldn’t offload to anyone. So, she was doing her best to keep a lid on her chagrin in front of the Bartons. If she wanted to patch things up with Yelena it wouldn’t be the best idea to let the cat out of the bag, especially with Clint.

    Clint had kind of been another one of those unspoken off topic questions. Of course, Clint knew Yelena had been training Kate. He hadn’t been too pleased when he’d first found out. A complicated mixture of protectiveness, worry, jealousy and fomo. He’d been on the phone to Kate, to Carol, and by the sounds of things, people a lot higher up, but he’d been given reassurances from all involved. Reassurances that hadn’t necessarily alleviated any worry, but had made it quite clear that there was really no point pushing any further. Yelena was staying, and that was that. And anyways, she was only teaching Kate those softer and more board-friendly assassination skills, like non-lethal takedowns and threat recognition, rather than the more brutal assassination skills like neck snapping, heart stabbing and life ceasing. There really was nothing to worry about.

    Did he know that they’d been living together? That was a no. Did he know that they slept together, ate together and dated together. Also, a no. Did he know that they were in some kind of not-relationship which involved lots of kissing, massages and hair brushing? Absolutely not, and it was clear to both of Kate and Yelena, that they had wanted to keep it that way until they were absolutely sure it was the right time to tell him. Which in Kate’s mind was never, and in Yelena’s mind was ‘I’d rather be fucking dead’. Kate had always thought that Yelena’s resistance over Clint knowing about their relationship had come from her wanting to avoid his lectures and judgement, which perhaps in part was true, and was almost certainly the reason she’d asked to not be invited to the Bartons’ for Christmas, but now Kate knew that Yelena wanted to avoid everything and everyone, not just Clint.

    So, there she was, sat in the most festive jumper she could find, tucked into Laura's side with a blanket shared between them and sipping on a heavily spiked eggnog at far too early an hour. Kate wasn’t going to lie though; she needed that eggnog- words that probably no one else had ever thought ever, in the history of woman-kind. Laura’s arm was draped over Kate’s shoulder, and every now and then the older woman would give her arm a small squeeze or comforting touch; Laura’s momma senses were tingling, like mad. As soon as Kate had walked through the door she’d known something was up, even if Clint had been none the wiser. The woman had been all over Kate since she’d arrived. Extra blankets, cookies, cake, cups of hot tea; you name it, Laura had provided it. Her hugs had been warmer and her brows more furrowed, and Kate had to work hard to smile brighter and cover the puffy redness surrounding her eyes from another tearful night, curled up with Lucky but no one else.

    No Yelena. No furnace with cold feet to keep her warm on chilly winter nights. No one to talk to, vent to, no one to hold her until her tears were spent, no one tell her that bitch wasn’t good enough her and someone else even more fantastic was just around the corner, no one to buy her Ben and Jerry’s and mix them together if the store was out of her favourite flavour. No best friend. The first night without her had been difficult, to come home and find her gone; it shouldn’t have come as a surprise but of course it still hurt like hell. But the second night was so much worse, once the booze and the vitriol had melted away. The second night was when Kate had felt the significance, the weight of perhaps never having Yelena back, and it had weighed heavy, so heavy that she hadn’t really slept. Of course, this was something Laura had picked up on almost instantly, as Kate slouched her way to breakfast that morning. She was without the woman she loved. Her heart felt empty and cavernous with loss of the one thing that had filled it so immeasurably over the past five months, but her mind was chaotic and overloaded with an incalculable number of thoughts, affirmations and regrets.

    Regret. Did Kate regret anything that she said two nights previous? No. She’d said what she needed to, and she knew she had been brave to do so. Did she regret the outcome? Absolutely, but she also knew that it was brave to face up to that. She knew telling Yelena she loved her was a risk, she knew that pushing her had been too. What she didn’t know yet, however, was whether it was a risk that would pay off. She’d been the one to ask Yelena to leave, it was Yelena who had to want to come back. Which is why, despite her heart’s protestations, her brain hadn’t let Kate message her or call her. It hadn’t even let her track her location. She just had to let Yelena come back to her when she was ready. Because it was Yelena who needed to fight for them now, not Kate, and that lack of control felt like it was trying to physically murder her. She felt sick, she felt tired, and cold, and her brain felt like it was going to melt. And of course, even if Yelena did come back, what if she didn’t say the right things? What if she didn’t want what Kate wanted, what if their differences were, well, irreconcilable? Kate couldn’t even bear to think about it. She took another generous sip of her eggnog, she needed as much eggnog as her body could physically consume without vomming.

    “Kate, honey?” Laura’s gentle voice yanked Kate from her thoughts.

    “What? Sorry, I- er- I zoned out there for a second.”

    “It’s okay,” the older woman smiled softly and gave her arm a reassuring squeeze.

    “Elf or The Princess Switch?!” Came Nate’s voice, demanding Kate’s attention from across the room. Wow, she really had zoned out.

    “The Princess Switch: Her Royal Five-ness,” Lila corrected, clearly irritated with the lack of respect her younger brother held for Vanessa Hudgens’ most recent Belgravian holiday escapade. In all honesty, Kate hadn’t even realised that they’d gone beyond ‘The Princess Switched Again’.

    “There have been five of those movies?” Kate, asked incredulously. Normally, Kate would probably be a little disappointed that it had taken her that long to realise. There was nothing better than watching shitty Christmas movies whilst stuffing your face with milk chocolate buttons, but right now, she didn’t know whether she really wanted to watch a movie about falling madly in love with a mysterious Eastern European.

    “Your vote decides it, Kate.” Said Clint from across the room, with a wry smile and a sparkle in his eye that said, sucks to be you. He was not wrong, being Kate Bishop really did suck. Especially as somehow, she had the deciding vote when there were only six people in the house. That was not fair.

    “How? There are six of us.”

    “Lucky voted!” Nate shouted gleefully. Kate groaned, inwardly, and did her best to smile brightly. Her mood wasn’t Nate’s fault and she was trying desperately hard to remember that in that moment. Besides, even though she’d seen Elf seventeen thousand times during her life, she’d take it over some vapid Christmas love story. Oh, but Elf was a love story, set in New York City... at Christmas.

    “He did?” Kate asked, with a smile that she hoped reached her eyes. “And what did Lucky vote for?”

    “Elf, of course! Because he’s the best.” Nate raised his arms above his head in triumph, much to Lila’s annoyance, because let’s face it, a dog shouldn’t have a vote, as adorable as the idea was – especially when that vote was being taken and interpreted by a young boy with an ulterior motive.

    “But mom, we’ve watched Elf like, five hundred times already this month,” Lila tried desperately to appeal to Laura. “Please, can we watch something else?”

    “Kate gets to decide and Kate is our guest.” Kate got the distinct impression that both Clint and Laura were enjoying having another adult in the house, and Kate was not overly impressed. Then again, if she’d had to deal with three kids in the run up to Christmas, she’d be taking any opportunity to offload responsibility for the day, and so, the pressure was thoroughly on Kate. And she was feeling it.

    “I mean, er, both films are legendary obviously,” She looked at both Lila and Nate, a little apprehensively. They both were offering her incredibly expectant looks. “Despite me only just hearing about the second one, but let’s face it, who doesn’t love a Vanessa Hudgens Christmas classic?” This comment was met with a nod of approval from Lila.

    “Vanessa Hudgens sucks,” Nate said, arms crossed and without remorse. Lila could only roll her eyes.

    “I actually think her comedy is underrated,” Cooper chipped in, softly, and Kate found herself really smiling now. Cooper was too nice a kid.

    “I do too Coops, I do but...” Kate sighed a little awkwardly, and she saw Lila’s face drop a little. She felt bad. Lila was like a little sister. Of course, Kate was close to the boys, but she and Lila had grown closer. She was a badass archer, and a great kid, and she was quickly turning into a pretty awesome young woman who looked up to Kate immensely, but now Kate was about to commit the ultimate betrayal. Kate was going to choose Elf. She knew that she could tune out the romance and enjoy the comedy and the reindeer and the Christmas spirit. With Princess Switch, there was a risk of her annihilating the Bartons’ television, or devolving into a pathetic, drivelling mess. It really could go either way, and it wasn’t a risk Kate was willing to take. With another pained exhale, Kate continued. “I’m just not sure I wa-“

    The sound of Lucky barking stopped Kate in her tracks. He shot up from where he was sat with Clint and made a beeline towards the window behind where she and Laura were sitting, as he continued to bark furiously. Kate inwardly sighed with relief; she’d been saved by the bell, and what a good bell he was. Maybe Kate could forgive him for dropping her in it with his vote.

    The sound of Lucky barking continued, but it was quickly joined with the foreboding rumble and gurgle of a motorcycle drawing closer to the homestead. Clint rose to his feet, quickly. He was tense and alert, in stark contrast to the relaxed figure he’d cut just moments before. They weren’t expecting any more guests for Christmas, and no one outside of S.H.I.E.L.D. knew the location of the Barton homestead.

    “Expecting any company?” Laura asked, her body stiffening against Kate’s as she rose in her chair.

    “No,” came Clint’s tight-lipped response. With a look, Laura was on her feet, dragging Kate with her.

    “Get the kids into the back room,” she ordered, and Kate nodded quickly. Although Kate was the Avenger, there was nothing more fearsome or formidable than a mother protecting her kids, and she certainly didn’t fancy refusing Laura in that moment.

    Of course, Lila did. “We’re not kids,” argued the middle Barton.

    “Right now, we are,” hissed Cooper, as he grabbed Nate and helped Kate usher her charges through the homestead and into the back room, once they were there, Kate turned back to find her other charge, Lucky.

    Clint grabbed his bow and quiver from the coat stand and Laura deftly palmed a knife from the kitchen drawer. Lucky’s bark had gone, to be replaced with a desperate whine, as he began to scratch against the door.

    “Come on boy, let’s go,” Kate called from a crouched position in the kitchen, clapping her hands slightly in order to gain his attention. “Lucky, boy. Come on. Come on boy, come to momma.” But Lucky wasn’t playing ball. His whines grew louder and more desperate, as he jumped and clawed at the door. Clint tried and failed to grab his collar, and he threw Kate an exasperated look that said ‘will you come and sort your dog’. Clint was right to be frustrated at that moment. Lucky was incredibly loyal and certainly tenacious but intimidating and dangerous, he was not. Which begged the question, what had got him so riled up? He never behaved like this. The only time he would ever scratch or whine was when she came home, or when... oh. Oh. Oh shit.

    “Wait,” Kate said, weakly at first, as she stood up awkwardly in the hall.

    “What?” Clint asked, sharply.

    “Wait, stop.” She said a little stronger this time.

    “Kate, what are you doing? Get some cover, sweetheart,” came Laura’s concerned voice.

    Kate sighed, and shook her head a little, despairingly. Why was she there? “It’s not anyone…”

    “It sounds like someone,” Clint tried to reason through gritted teeth, willing her to grab Lucky and head back into the backroom with the kids.

    Kate couldn’t believe it. If she hadn’t ruined Christmas enough for Kate already, here she was, to really twist the knife. Or apologise? No, it was too soon. Kate didn’t let her brain even go there and she didn’t let her heart hope. She shook her head once more. Clint was going to kill her. “It is someone. It’s Yelena.”

    He frowned a little in confusion, but Kate could see that he visibly relaxed, ever so slightly at the mention of the ex-assassin's name. Of course, for most people, a Black Widow turning up at your home on Christmas Eve was a particularly bad omen, but for Clint, at least it wasn’t the worst thing that could have happened. “Are you sure?”

    “He is,” Kate pointed to Lucky who was still whining and scratching away at the Barton front door. His barking had totally ceased and it was blindingly obviously that all he longed for was to get to the person on the opposite side of the door. Clint frowned but couldn’t argue with her logic, whoever was on the other side of that door was a friend. Well, that depended how loose your definition of friend was.

    “Yelena, as in Nat’s Yelena?” Laura asked, a little taken aback. Kate didn’t know how much Laura knew about the Black Widow assassin who was sent to kill Clint the previous December, but she could imagine that the things she had heard probably weren’t all that good.

    “Yes,” both generations of Hawkeye answered, in unison.

    “Yelena who tried to kill you last Christmas?” Laura was clearly a little confused, and still incredibly tense. She wanted to understand why they were both standing down with a Black Widow practically on their doorstep.

    “That was just a misunderstanding,” Clint explained, quickly.

    “It didn’t look like a misunderstanding,” countered Laura, clearly thinking back to when her incredibly patched up husband just and so made it back home for Christmas. He had taken a beating on that ice.

    “I was fine, honey,” he tried to reassure his wife but she was having none of it. A small raised eyebrow showed him as much.

    “She kicked your ass!”

    “Because I let her!”

    “I kicked her ass, just so you know,” Kate interjected, thinking that this tense and incredibly undesirable scenario could only be helped with humour.

    “Because she let you!” Clint’s face was flush with frustration and exasperation as he turned to Kate. “How does she know where we live, Kate?” Oh shit. Oh shit, I’ve done something bad and I didn’t even know it. Kate hadn’t meant to; she hadn’t even told Yelena exactly where she’d be going... had she? No, surely not.

    “I mean, we’re friend but I didn…”

    “So, you tell all your friends the secret location of my family home?” Clint’s eyes had narrowed, his temper had been well and truly stoked. Only the ones I share a bed with, Kate thought without filter.

    “I didn’t tell her anything, I swear,” Kate held her hands up in defence of herself, “She probably found it on the S.H.I.E.L.D. database.” She must have, right? Kate was known universally as an oversharer, but not with the stuff that really mattered. And although she loved Yelena, when she wasn’t being a complete and utter douchebag, she’d never betray Clint’s trust by telling her the location of his home and his family. That was his and Laura’s information, and only theirs to share.

    “She doesn’t have the clearance,” he said, through gritted teeth. Clint was quickly losing patience. He knew that his family was no longer in immediate danger, that wasn’t why he was angry. He was angry because he thought his trust had been betrayed, by Kate of all people. If it was possible, Kate started to feel worse than she had just minutes before.

    Clint was right, Yelena didn’t have clearance, so how did she...? Ah, that’s how. Shitballs. Of course, that’s how she did it. That or she already knew. She was very proficient in finding any and all the information that she needed. “I mean, there might be a chance, just the tiniest chance...” Kate took a moment, she knew she’d fucked up, she knew that in all that had happened, she’d forgotten. She’d forgotten about her phone. Just say it you coward. “Just the tiniest chance, that she has a track on my phone.”

    Clint blinked. “A track on your phone?!”

    “Yeah, you know, in case I get in trouble? Which we both know has happened before and will happen again.” Clint looked thoroughly concerned, Laura looked thoroughly confused. “What? She’s protective. I know it might be hard for you to believe. You’re not telling me you don’t track my phone as well.”

    “I don’t...” Clint spluttered a little at Kate’s accusation. “I don’t have a track on your-“

    “Of course you do,” interjected Laura, clearly done with this irrelevant argument. “Look, Clint, if Nat’s Yelena is a friend of Kate’s and is conscientious enough to track her phone in case of emergencies, then despite her kicking your ass last year, and despite it being a little odd that she tracked Kate all the way to Missouri, I’m pretty sure we’re safe.” Thank goodness for Laura Barton. But wait, that sounded like they were going to let her in. They couldn’t let her in, Kate wasn’t ready for that. Her hair was unwashed, her eyes were red and her face puffy, and her heart had wounds that were still fresh. “You guys came to an agreement, right?” Laura asked Clint.

    He shrugged, clearly not sold on the idea of letting the Black Widow into his family home on Christmas Eve. “Something like that.”

    “Then I think we should let her in,” Laura said, with a breezy, warm smile. It was as if the last few moments hadn’t even happened; the tension, the panic, the confusion, it had all been forgotten. It was Kate’s turn to frown now. Why the sudden change of heart? Was it because Yelena was Nat’s sister? Was it because she couldn’t turn away a third stray at Christmas? Or was it because she was beginning to piece the clues together? Moms could be terrifyingly intuitive in that way.

    “Come on, it’s Christmas,” reasoned Laura, light-heartedly. Exactly, it was Christmas, and the ruiner of Christmas was stood on the other side of that door. But, let’s face it, it wasn’t really Christmas that Kate was concerned about. If Yelena ruined Kate’s Christmas, then okay, there would always be other ones, but if Yelena came here and ruined their relationship, Kate wasn’t sure she’d ever find another like it. Why did she have to come? Why did she have to arrive, like in a fucking Christmas movie, at her doorstep on Christmas Eve? Why? Because you told her to you idiot, you literally told her to. Kate just never expected it to be so soon.

    A silence hung in the Barton household. It was Clint and Kate now, who shared looks of concern. She wasn’t ready for this, Kate couldn’t deal with this, she wasn’t ready. She hadn’t even sorted her own brain out and now she had to deal with Yelena’s? “I-“

    A knock sounded against the door, and rang out through the hall. Kate wasn’t ready to talk, she wasn’t even ready to see her. Seeing Yelena in her mind’s eye hurt, and she was concerned that seeing her in the flesh would well and truly finish her off, and not in a good way.

    “Am I opening the door?” Laura asked, impatiently.

    “I don’t… I,“ Kate stuttered and Clint shrugged.

    Laura sighed impatiently and shook her head at the two useless superheroes stood before her, “I’m opening the door”.

    “Wait-“ Kate, lunged forward but it was too late. Laura had pushed her way past Clint and had thrown the door wide open.

    There she was. Her cheeks were flushed and her hair mussed and tousled from hours inside her motorcycle helmet. She had her black, fleece lined leather jacket zipped up as far as it would go to protect against the cold, and her worn, grey jeans and aged boots were peppered with mud and spray, presumably from the road. Her eyes were anywhere but Kate’s, which was probably for the best because goddamn, did she really have to turn up looking that ridiculously hot when Kate looked that ridiculously bad? It was only in that moment that Kate realised how absurd they must have all looked, stood in the doorway to the Barton homestead, all in vaguely matching, cheesy as fuck Christmas sweaters. They looked like the fucking Brady Bunch, and Kate wanted to crawl somewhere and die.

    To add to her dismay, her own dog threw himself at the Russian before her, whining and licking and wagging his tail. The betrayal. But of course, he loved her unconditionally, and the blonde loved him. Yelena bent down to greet the dog that was accosting her and couldn’t keep the dumb and happy smile from her face. “Okay, boy. Yes, it is me, you have got me. You are a very smart boy.” Kate’s heart felt hot, her two blondes together again.

    “Hi!” Laura beamed from the door. Oh yeah, something was going on with her. Yelena being Yelena was quickly put on the back foot by the older woman’s cheeriness, and she rushed back to her feet, stuffed her gloved hands back inside her pockets to protect them further from the cold and shifted awkwardly from foot to foot.

    “Hello… Mrs Barton?”

    “Call me Laura, please. You should come in.” And in any other circumstance, Kate would completely agree. It was freezing, and another snowfall was due in the hour, but this wasn’t normal circumstances. This was a ‘the object of my unrequited love and the cause of my heartbreak was stood in front of me’ situation and Kate wanted to do anything but invite her inside. Her heart felt as if it was beating out of her chest, and she was sure Yelena could hear it. She always knew.

    By the looks of Yelena’s slightly sheepish reaction, actually entering the Bartons’ home had never made it onto her ‘to do list’. Kate’s not-girlfriend shook her head politely, “Oh no, that is very kind of you but no, I am not here to intrude on your Christmas.” Her eyes flashed to Kate’s and then darted away, quickly, back to Laura’s. “I am just here to speak to Kate, if that is okay?”

    Was she asking permission to speak to Kate? Why didn’t she just ask Kate herself? Why didn’t she just look her in the eye and-

    Clint cleared his throat, loudly and purposefully from behind the two brunettes at the door. Oh, that was why. Yelena offered a stiff nod to the man just over Kate’s shoulder. Kate didn’t dare look round, but she knew that Clint’s eyes were fixed on Yelena, because Yelena’s stare was unwavering.

    “Clint,” she said, tersely.

    “Yelena,” came his rather frosty response. Any other day of the year, and perhaps having been invited, Yelena might have been welcome on the Homestead, but it was Christmas and the uninvited guest was technically trespassing.

    Her eyes shifted to Kate’s once more, and this time, she held her gaze. Yelena’s face softened as she took in Kate’s features. A smile pulled at the corner of her lips, it was tired and sad and yet hopeful and Kate felt her stomach lurch. “Kate, I-” But Yelena’s eyes were pulled from Kate’s yet again. Loud footsteps from behind the brunette told her that the kids had appeared. Great, even more matching sweaters, what a fucking loser.

    “Um,” Yelena hesitated. Kate didn’t think she’d ever seen her not-girlfriend that awkward ever. But then again, who wouldn’t be, faced with the entire cast of the Brady Bunch? “Nice sweater”.

    “You hate it”. It was the first thing that came out of Kate’s mouth, and it was very ‘speak first think later’. She’d meant for it to feel familiar, it hadn’t. Instead, it had betrayed how jaded she really felt.

    “I don’t…” Yelena was quick to stop herself from telling an all out lie. Insincerity out of desperation to please probably wouldn't have made for the best of starts. “I don’t hate it”

    “Sweetie,” Laura chimed, as she grabbed Clint by the arm and began to yank, “I think maybe we should leave these two at it for a little bit huh?” An over-protective Clint was reluctant to leave, despite knowing that Yelena had trained Kate for nearly six months without murdering her or leaving her for dead, but it was quite clear to everyone currently gathered by the door to the Bartons’ home, that something was up between the two young partners.

    With another tug on his arm, Laura managed to pull Clint away. Another shepherding arm grabbed Nate and Lila and cajoled them back into the lounge. Of course, Laura could rely on Cooper to make his own way there, and grab a reluctant Lucky on the way. “Aaaand, seeing as Kate is tied up and really wanted to watch Elf, how about we watch the Princess thing.”

    “It’s the Princess Switch: Her Royal Five-ness, mom” Lila had to explain, again, clearly for what she felt was one too many times.

    “But Lucky had voted! He really wants to watch Elf. There are no take backs mom.” Came Nate’s disappointed tones.

    “Come on buddy,” Kate could hear Clint say, as the Bartons’ began to settle in the lounge, “Lila has been waiting since November to watch this. Grab your blanket and let’s sit together.” With that, Nate’s protestations were quelled and the youngest Barton joined the eldest on the couch. He was a good dad. No, scrap that, he was a great dad.

    “Kate, umm, I’m sorry if this is a surpr-”

    “What are you doing here?” Kate asked, in hushed tones as her eyes flicked between Yelena and the Bartons. “You’re not supposed to be here.”

    “Well, I rode all night to see you,” Yelena appealed, hopefully. “Probably broke quite a few state laws, in quite a few states actually.” She laughed a sheepish little laugh, but was only met with silence.

    Kate didn’t know what to say. What was she supposed to say. Thank you? She wasn’t exactly feeling particularly grateful in that moment. How about, you should have messaged first? Well, she’d probably have told Yelena not to bother and knowing Yelena, she’d still have turned up on the Bartons’ doorstep.

    “I thought that we could talk?” It was a question, a hopeful one, and a question that filled Kate with so much hope and yet so much trepidation. She so wanted to talk with Yelena, she so wanted for Yelena to talk to her, to open up to her, to be honest with her, but right at that moment? There was no way, she needed time to get her head back together, to put her pieces back together in a way that meant she could function again effectively.

    “On Christmas Eve? Here?” Kate asked. “Do you know how ruined my Christmas already is?” Yelena tore her eyes from Kate’s almost instantly. It was an instinctual reaction, and a defensive one. It was clear that Yelena knew, and it was clear that Yelena knew how big a role she’d played in that in that one woman show.

    “Probably not as bad as last year,” the Russian shrugged and Kate wanted to shut the door in her face.

    “You think that’s funny?” She hissed, with another anxious glance over to the Bartons’ who all seemed too engrossed in the opening few sequences of The Princess Switch: Her Royal Five-ness to pay the two women at the door much attention.

    “No,” Yelena swallowed, hands in pockets. “I just make jokes sometimes when things are… awkward”. Her eyes met Kate’s again. They were dark, bloodshot and restless with lack of sleep, after more than a night’s worth of concentrating on the roads and highways. It was a long way to drive, and suddenly Kate wanted to draw Yelena to her. She was exhausted, and what she’d done was dangerous, ridiculously dangerous, and all to do something that they could have just done over the phone or at least in the new year back in New York City. Yelena must have been desperate. Well, good.

    “I can go if you want me to, and I don’t need to come in, I don’t want to intrude, but I would like to talk to you if would listen”.

    “What could you possibly have to say?” Perhaps that remark had been a little flippant, considering its recipient had travelled for sixteen hours across seven states, simply to talk, all the while stood out in the depths of a Missouri winter. She must have had a fair bit to say. Wasn’t that what Kate wanted anyhow? To know Yelena’s feelings, to know her truths? Didn’t she want Yelena to come to her?

    “Well,” Yelena continued, unperturbed, “Maybe we could go on a walk and you could find out?”

    Kate sighed, dejectedly. “I don’t want to walk, Yelena. I just want to enjoy Christmas with my family”.

    Yelena took a steadying breath and nodded in acceptance. “Okay”. She was disappointed, she’d come a long way and it was clear that Kate’s rejection hurt her, but she wasn’t going to beg, and to her credit, she certainly wasn’t going to guilt Kate into talking to her. “I was going to book into the guest house down the road so, maybe I can come back later or after?”

    Someone must have caught Yelena’s eyes from over Kate’s shoulder as the blonde threw a casual, reassuring smile to someone in the Barton lounge. The brunette’s best guess was Laura, who had been throwing the couple secretive glances since settling down to watch the movie. She also doubted Yelena would offer Clint a smile so freely.

    Perhaps they could talk later, or maybe after Christmas. Or perhaps Kate should tell Yelena to go home, but where was home for her now? Was it the Avenger complex, or would she go further? Kate felt her stomach lurch once more at the thought of Yelena leaving the country, at the thought of Yelena being out of her life completely.

    “Kate,” Yelena leaned closer, out of the wind and into the homestead’s door frame. “You said that I should come back to you when I knew what I wanted”. Two pairs of sleep deprived eyes met, and a rush of anticipation flashed through Kate’s body, because there it was, Yelena’s new smile. Small, delicate and hopeful. A smile that Kate thought she might never see again. The Russian lowered her voice further and spoke as earnestly and honestly as she could. “I know what I want”. And with those words, those eyes and that smile, Kate’s world turned upside down, again. Fucking fuck, just talk to her you fucking idiot.

    With an audible groan, Kate chose to relent and Yelena’s eyes grew brighter. “I’ll just change into some jeans and get my coat. Come inside for a second, we’re letting the cold in”. Kate stepped back to let Yelena inside the homestead, quickly closed the door behind her and disappeared upstairs.

    Yelena stood, awkwardly, alone by the door, hands still firmly tucked into her pockets. Laura met her eyes once more and threw her another kind smile. Nate, who had very little interest in the political machinations of Belgravia was staring happily at Yelena, whilst his siblings were engrossed in the movie. He smiled and offered the Russian a tiny wave with his even tinier hand. Yelena extracted a gloved hand from her right pocket and waved back, sheepishly, but not without the smallest smile, before Kate came thumping back down the stairs, boots laced and big coat on.

    "I'm ready,” Kate declared, as the Russian frowned at her, incredulously.

    “Are you still going to wear that jumper?” she asked, with a raised eyebrow. It was Kate’s turn to frown.

    “That what?”

    “Your sweater,” Yelena clarified, pointing at Kate’s chest.

    “Yes. It’s Christmas.” What did Yelena expect?

    “I- okay,” the Russian sighed and shook her head. If this was Yelena starting how she meant to go on, it was not a good sign.

    “Is that Russian, ‘jumper’?” The smallest smirk began to pull at the corners of Yelena’s mouth, and Kate realised that her not-girlfriend was flirting. She was actually flirting.

    “No idiot, it’s English.”

    Thankfully, once they’d gotten outside, the bitter wind that had been blowing relented ever so slightly. The day was stiller now, which always meant snow was just around the corner. They walked through the yard, passed Santa’s Workshop, and through into the fields behind the Homestead. The snow that had fallen a few days before was thicker there, and Kate was thankful that she thrown on her biggest pair of boots and her thickest pair of socks. Heads of trodden down, unharvested corn could just be seen, struggling for breath under the thick layers of compacted white snow, and they walked slowly, and in silence, along a path carved by the family a few days before.

    “For someone who wanted to talk, you’re being awfully quiet,” Kate mused, as she pulled her coat tighter around herself to ward off the cold.

    “Sorry. I- I’m not very good at this.” Wasn’t that the truth. But in reality, who could blame her? Talking wasn’t something that was encouraged where Yelena grew up, and Kate could only presume that things like feelings, were actively discouraged, god forbid she’d have independent thought.

    “I’m aware,” Kate nodded, with acceptance.

    “But neither are you,” said Yelena as she glanced momentarily in Kate’s direction, and then quickly away.

    “That is not true. I am an excellent talker; I could talk all day.” The smallest of laughs escaped Yelena and Kate felt her temper flare. What was so funny?

    “About inane things, for sure,” Yelena countered. Inane? Kate was not inane; Kate’s thought and feelings were not trivial.

    “Is insulting me your idea of talking? Because if it is, I’m going back inside right now.”

    “No, no,” Yelena rushed to clarify, the last thing she probably wanted after a seven state motorcycle ride was to have the person she came all that way to speak to shut her out. But if she was going to remedy the situation, she needed to explain herself, and fast. “I just mean that we both talk a lot but we do not talk, you know? About the things that we should talk about. We are not always honest, when we talk.”

    Kate pulled her coat even tighter around herself, as Yelena’s words struck a chord. There were things she’d avoided saying, there were things she’d avoided doing, in fear that it would cost her their relationship and oh how she felt called out on it. “I think I’m very honest,” the brunette said, quietly and if not a little stubbornly.

    “Of course you are”. Yelena tried to find her eyes but Kate was resistant. A gloved hand tugged at her arm, extracted her cold hand from her left pocket and then clasped itself tightly around it. Yelena was demanding her attention, and Kate gave it. Their eyes met and Yelena’s were earnest. “Hey, of course you are. You are the most painfully honest person that I know. Sometimes, it is even to your detriment, truly.” Yelena smiled sincerely. “But, sometimes, we both withhold some truth to avoid a little pain. Or maybe a big one”

    Kate didn’t know what to say. Yelena’s words reflected rang true, too true. She could only ‘hmm’ her agreement, tighten her hands around Yelena’s, and continue to walk as finally, the long forecast snow began to fall.

    “I uh- I nearly left the country yesterday morning.” So, she really had tried to leave. It was something that Kate knew might happen. Without Kate, what was keeping Yelena in the United States? If Yelena had decided to run, she’d run as far as her fake passports could take her. “I had decided that we were over”. Kate nodded. It was what she’d been so worried about, but then why if Yelena was so afraid, why had she changed her mind?

    “What changed?” Kate asked, she needed to know.

    Yelena smiled to herself and shook her head, ruefully. “My mother kicked my ass.” Kate couldn’t help but smile too. Melina was a formidable woman, and a terrifying one. Kate would have to remember to thank her, if this all worked out.

    “She told me to come and speak to you.” Of course.

    “So, you’re doing this because your mother told you to?”

    “No, I am doing this because she was right.” Yelena stopped suddenly in her tracks, and stubbornly tugged on Kate’s hand as she tried to keep walking towards the tree line. Kate couldn’t escape her resolute little face, or fiercely determined eyes. There was so much emotion caught up in those eyes, that Kate didn’t know what or how to feel. The Russian seemed frustrated and angry and hopeful, all at the same time. She frowned, tore her eyes from Kate, and looked down to find both their hands now fully entwined. She seemed to be wrestling with herself and with her words. She’d come an awful long way to say them, but that didn’t make the saying of them any easier. In fact, it probably made it harder. They had to be perfect.

    “I should not have told you how to feel.” As far as words go, they weren’t actually too bad, because Yelena was right.

    “No. You shouldn’t have.”

    “But at the same time, it would be very useful for me to know what you want, so I can understand better, what you do feel and why.”

    “I want you. I think that’s pretty obvious.”

    “Darling, it is not just that though.” Oh goodness, she used the word. It had only been two days since she’d last heard it, but to Kate, it had felt like an eternity. Part of her had wondered if she’d ever hear it again, in her beautiful, rasping tones. “Do you want to carry on living together indefinitely? Is this long term or marriage or babies?” Kate swallowed, because she knew she’d had these thoughts. She knew she’d imagined their future together; she knew that she’d let herself dream of it. She also knew that that future did not involve babies.

    “You want babies?” Kate, her voice slightly higher and far more terrified than intended.

    Yelena smiled softly and drew Kate closer. “This is just an example, no? But it is a very good example that we do not know what the other person wants. When have we ever talked about it?”

    Kate shrugged. “Never.”

    “And yet we live together.”

    Kate frowned. It was Yelena who had told Carol she didn’t intend on living at the Avenger’s complex, which Kate now suspected was more to do with being as far away from Carol as possible, rather than as close to Kate as possible. “That was your fault.”

    “Yes, I suppose it was. And I like living with you. It’s convenient and-”

    “Convenient. Great. I’m convenient.” Yelena fixed Kate with a penetrating stare.

    “I was planning on expanding if you had let me.” Kate quickly caught her tongue.

    “Sorry, I’m just…”

    “A little emotional? Me too. There is no need to apologise.” Yelena’s eyes were calmer, more assured, and Kate felt warm despite the snow that was beginning to fall more heavily. “Do you want to carry on walking? There is a small lake just the other side of these trees.”

    Kate’s brow furrowed. “How do you know that?”

    “Google Earth.” Yelena chimed, as if it was the most normal thing in the world, and if it was possible, Kate’s heart felt even warmer than it had a moment before. The woman she loved was such a fucking nerd. “I like to know the lay of the land before I travel somewhere, just in case something was to happen, I would be ready.” Yelena narrowed her eyes and pulled Kate closer. “I am always ready."

    “Smart but a little creepy.”

    “Ha,” Yelena laughed, sarcastically, as she pulled away from Kate and dragged her in the direction of the tree line. “That is what my last girlfriend used to call me.”

    Kate blinked in confusion. She’d never mentioned anyone previous, in fact, she’d always made it quite clear that Kate was the only person she’d ever been romantically involved with. Yelena’s reason, word for word? ‘Everyone else I have ever met is so fucking vapid I want to shoot myself in the face’. Delightful. But still, her last girlfriend? “You’ve had another girlfriend?” Kate asked.

    “No, Kate!” Yelena said with a grin as her tired eyes still somehow danced in the modest winter light. “Do you listen to anything I say? Come on”.

    Kate let herself be dragged along the path. Their boots crunched and made new footprints in the fresh snow. Wait, if Yelena said last girlfriend, then who was her current girlfriend. WHO WAS HER CURRENT GIRLFRIEND? No, no, Kate had to keep it together. She was joking, certainly about the previous girlfriend, and even if she wasn’t joking, just because she used the word ‘girlfriend’ didn’t mean that everything was forgiven. Yes, Kate, that’s why you’re following her into a romantic winter wonderland.

    And what a winter wonderland it was. It only took the couple a few minutes to reach the partially frozen lake, but it was so picturesque, despite the winter ravaged trees and the absence of life. There was so much beauty in its stillness and so much solace in its silence. After taking a quiet moment together at the foot of the lake, they settled down in the shelter of a few evergreens. Kate’s thick coat protected her butt from the cold, Yelena was just well, Russian and tough as fuck.

    Yelena took a steadying breath and retook Kate’s hand. The brunette had got the distinct impression that to find the strength to say anything today, Yelena would need Kate’s hand in hers. After all, Kate was teaching her how to live, it would make sense that she might need a little moral support during the most human conversation she might ever have, even if that conversation was with Kate herself. “So, I kind of had this all worked out in my head. Twelve hours on a bike is a long time.”

    What the fuck. “Twelve hours?! Did you even pee?” Kate didn’t think she could go twelve hours on a flight, let along twelve hours on a bike.

    “I am trying to pour my heart out to you Kate,” Yelena reminded her, with just the slightest exasperation.

    “Sorry, you were saying”.

    “Well, I thought that I should tell you how I feel… About you.” This was it; this was what Kate had been waiting for. The confirmation that she needed.

    “I would like that, yeah. I would like that a lot, actually.” As long as it was good news. Oh god, please let it be good news. “It’s good right?”
