    Thank you all for your patience on this one. Work is only getting busier but I was determined to deliver on this incredibly belated Christmas gift.

    Again, thank you to all those who are commenting and liking etc and sorry if I haven’t gotten back to you as much as normal from the last chapter. Things got a little manic, but this time, I promise to be a little more on the ball.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Her head rang, her mouth was dry and her pride was hurt. Yelena was willing to admit that British vodka packed more of a punch than she had originally thought, she just hoped that old man Clint would be suffering more than her that morning. If he wasn’t, that would really compound her problems, and do even more damage to her alcohol-weakened ego.

    With a groan of discomfort, Yelena turned in bed and reached for her water that she’d sensibly provided for her bedside table. It had been refilled since she’d emptied it in the early hours of the morning. Either the Bartons had house elves, which boded well for Christmas Dinner, or her girlfriend had very dutifully refilled her glass.

    “Good morning,” came the amused tones of Kate Bishop, from the other side of the bed. Speak of the devil.

    Yelena stretched and let out the most pathetic little whimper. She had really hit a new low. What would her mother say? This was a dark day for Black Widows everywhere, but she was determined not to be defeated, especially by the British.

    “Good morning,” she murmured back whilst taking a few gentle sips of water with one eye open.

    “How are you feeling?” Kate asked as Yelena fought to prop herself up in bed. At least the Bartons had plenty of cushions. One could say a suspicious amount of cushions.

    “I am fine,” Yelena lied. She would not be conceding to this hangover, absolutely not. Especially not to Kate, as Kate would only tell Clint, and Clint would not let her live it down. He would cling to this victory as he knew would lose to her in a battle of wits or brawn. Even if he was hungover himself, he would take a huge amount of pride in the knowledge that he got the Russian drunk, on vodka no less, and Yelena was sure that she would never hear the end of it.

    Kate smirked disbelievingly. “Sure. Okay.” The cheek of this girl. “Do you need anything?

    “Just a coffee,” she grumbled, and turned over to hide her head firmly into the pillows she’d just propped herself up against. And a Burger King Breakfast Croissant. Yelena would kill for one of those too, although she would never admit it.

    Her girlfriend’s lips grazed gently against the soft skin of the backs of her arms. It was warm and comforting and normally it would quite easily entice Yelena into turning round and meeting Kate’s lips with her own. Not today. Kate’s hands gripped her hips gently and pulled her blonde girlfriend closer. Kate’s breath tickled her neck and Yelena felt a soft kiss fall, delicately, upon the soft skin at the nape of her neck. “And a shower,” came Kate’s whisper. The CHEEK of this girl.

    “Hey,” Yelena protested, rather weakly, her voice hoarse. “What are you trying to say?” She shifted uncomfortably to meet Kate’s amused eyes.

    “That you reek of alcohol,” Kate explained and Yelena found that she did not have the will to argue, for Kate was right, there was a particular stench about her. “How much did you drink?” The brunette asked, innocently.

    The blonde shrugged meekly. “I do not know. Like, four and a half fingers?”

    Kate raised two incredibly bemused eyebrows. “Wow. Four and a half?”

    “Yes, four and a half.” Yelena huffed stubbornly, as she rolled back over to glower in private. “I’m going back to sleep.”

    “That is not an option. It’s Christmas,” explained Kate cheerily. Americans and their Christmases. They were practically obsessed; unhealthily obsessed. Why was ‘good will to all men’ reserved for just one day in the year? Why was kindness and generosity exclusive to December 25th? Why did they only care about quality time with their family when their capitalist society told them to? Asked the ex-murderer with the completely dysfunctional family unit.

    “It is not Christmas,” she said as she buried herself further into the soft pillows and pulled the comforter around her. Americans.

    Yelena felt the bed dip and move as Kate shifted her weight. A soft kiss brushed gently upon the top of her head and deceptively strong arms found their way beneath the covers and around her waist.

    “I take it your talk went okay?” Kate asked quietly. Yelena knew it was only a matter of time until she asked, and it was perfectly natural to be curious. That didn’t mean that Yelena felt like talking about it much, and it certainly didn’t mean that she had the capacity to do so.

    “Mmhm,” came the Russian’s beleaguered response.

    “You’re still alive and you didn’t come to bed with blood under your fingernails so I’m guessing Clint is too.”

    “I would not be so sure. I am very good at cleaning up after myself.”

    “Really?” Kate asked skeptically, as she propped herself up on one elbow and threw a purposeful look at Yelena’s clothes from the night before. They lay, strewn across the floor, right where Yelena had left them, after she had discarded them unceremoniously on her way to bed.

    Yelena’s chagrin deepened. “When I have not been tricked into drinking, yes.”

    “Oh, you were tricked?” Yelena did not like Kate’s teasing tone. The blonde needed aspirin, not sass. And maybe a little sympathy too, just a little. “Weird,” continued Kate as she gently pressed another kiss against Yelena’s hangover-flushed skin. “I didn’t think anyone could pull the wool over Yelena Belova’s eyes, but obviously I’ve been proved wrong.”

    The blonde rolled her eyes and rolled herself onto her back to fix Kate with a most unimpressed look. “A rare moment of weakness after being up for forty hours straight.”

    “Well then,” Kate said, unable to keep the mirthful smile from her face, “I’m going to get up.” Yelena was glad that at least one of them could extract some humour from her current predicament. Her girlfriend was practically beaming. The Russian guessed it was kind of Christmas after all.

    Kate placed a firm kiss upon Yelena’s lips and breathed her in. Why anyone would want to breathe in hungover Yelena Belova was behind her but she guessed that maybe that’s what loving someone meant, you take them any which way they come. Suddenly Yelena’s chest felt warm, her heart light and her head was slightly less poundy. Could she bottle this feeling for every time she was hungover? Yelena was pretty sure Kate Bishop could make a pretty penny with those kind of skills. Not that Yelena wanted to share, not at all actually, she wanted Kate Bishop all to herself.

    “I’m going to get you a coffee,” Kate whispered before planting another kiss upon the blonde’s very receptive lips. “And some water,” she said before their lips met again. “A couple of Clint’s super strong painkillers for old dudes backs.” Yelena actually laughed into their next kiss, because Clint was old, and it was funny. “And then,” Kate’s voice dropped just a fraction lower as she placed on final, punctuating kiss upon Yelena’s lips. “I’m going to meet you in the shower.”

    If Yelena had already been drinking her future coffee, she would have choked. “Oh really?” She asked, coolly. She was totally cool. The coolest. Why wouldn’t she be? It wasn’t as if her heart had skipped a beat, or two, or five. Nope.

    “Uh huh,” Kate nodded slowly with a knowing smile. “Do you think your head can handle it?”

    Yelena was absolutely sure her head could handle it. And for the first time, she realised that her heart and mind could handle it too. She knew where they stood, and Kate knew what she wanted. She knew where Yelena wanted to be touched and kissed and held and loved, and Yelena knew that Kate was excited to give her all of that and nothing more. There were no expectations of anything else, no implications because they’d be naked together, no awkwardness or fear of misunderstanding, that had all gone. Yelena felt freer than she had the day before, freer than she ever had with Kate, and quite bizarrely, it was because they had set boundaries.

    Nervousness and apprehension had so easily morphed into anticipation. Anticipation to touch and feel and connect. Yelena felt her heart rate steadily increase, and she was sure it wasn’t the hangover. “I can handle it,” Yelena spoke, quietly but confidently, as Kate’s lips found hers again. Arms pulled her close and she stretched into their kiss, savouring every moment of soft lips, upon soft skin amongst soft pillows.

    Yelena could feel Kate smile into their embrace as she whispered, “Well, happy Christmas to me.”

    Turned out Yelena’s head couldn’t handle it. The coffee hadn’t done much to take the edge off, Clint’s painkillers had been oversold, and as lovely as her shower with Kate had been, Yelena couldn’t help but feel it could have been so much better if she’d been able to keep her eyes open for more than fifty percent of it. Kate hadn’t minded of course, because it meant that she could pretty much have her way with her. She could style her hair in dumb ways, give her bubble Santa beards, and force her to exfoliate, like all over. It was awful, and Yelena had frowned and grumbled her way through all of it. Kate thought it was cute and hilarious. For sure, Yelena considered herself hilarious, very much so, but cute, the Russian did not adhere to that school of thought. It hadn’t all been bad though, Kate had been beautiful and gentle and caring with her rather delicate girlfriend and for all the frowns exchanged there had been double the amount of kisses, and surely that was remedy enough for four and a half fingers of vodka on top of half a bottle of red.

    Breakfast was light, and perfect for a day where you planned to stuff your face with a dinner that rivalled American Thanksgiving, but it wasn’t really of the hangover-curing variety. The pastries were beautiful and the gallon of coffee Yelena consumed was finally starting to banish the pounding in her brain, but she really just needed pizza. Pizza, bed, Netflix, dog, girlfriend. Not in that order. Yelena glanced up at where Kate was helping Laura tidy away the plates from breakfast. They both caught her gaze and grinned knowingly to each other. Okay, maybe in that order, or maybe just strike the girlfriend off the list altogether.

    “Ow!” Yelena yelped all of a sudden as a small, vicious hand slapped against the back of her own.

    “You’re not even trying!” Moaned Nate, who was sat opposite her, crossed legged on the floor.

    “I am trying,” Yelena explained, stubbornly. It was a lie. She really was not trying. “I am trying very hard.”

    “You’re a terrible liar,” he said, with another tiny handed slap, across the back of her left hand this time. Yelena winced. The boy was simply wrong, Yelena was a brilliant liar. She was so good, she even managed to deceive herself most of the time, so these kind of accusations were completely unfounded. Especially from a child.

    Another slap and the back of both of her hands were beginning to turn red. “Ouch!”

    Nate rolled his eyes. “That didn’t hurt,” he said with disdain. The kid was merciless, Yelena loved it.

    “Yes it did,” she said with a smirk. “You have little kid hands. They’re sharp.”

    Nate frowned in confusion. She wasn’t trying to slap his hands, she wasn’t trying to defend his slaps, and yet there she was, happy to sit there and take the pain? “That doesn’t even make any sense.”

    Yelena simply shrugged. “English is not my first language,” she explained, nonchalantly.

    “Where are you from then?” Nate asked.

    “Ohio,” Yelena answered, coolly. Nate’s eyes narrowed and Yelena’s smirk grew wider. Another slap landed across her right hand and Yelena out and out grinned. Good, it was now an interrogation. Natasha would be proud.

    “Russia,” she said, simply, offering him a slither of information

    “Where in Russia?” This kid was on the ball.

    “I do not know-ow!” Another slap rapped against her now very pink knuckles and this time, Yelena flinched. “I do not know, kid, jeez. This is not an interrogation,” Yelena said with a broad smile, her words clearly not marrying up with her actions. Nate huffed with frustration and confusion. Every kid loved a game of slapsies, but this was not how the game was meant to be played and, although Nate was winning, by a clear margin, it was clear that he felt as if it were the opposite.

    “Then fight back,” he said, through gritted teeth.

    “Never,” Yelena grinned.

    “I think you’re afraid of me,” Nate said, and it was quite sweet really, that he thought that.

    “I am not afraid of you, Nate,” Yelena smiled. “I am not afraid of anything.”

    “That’s a lie!” Came Kate’s voice from the kitchen. Well, well. Not only had Kate and Laura been passing judgement on them earlier, turns out her girlfriend had been eavesdropping too. Yes, strike Kate off the list, Yelena would be more than happy with Lucky, bed and Netflix. In fact, she was pretty sure that Lucky was up there right now, waiting for her. “You’re afraid of your mother!” The word ‘commitment’ was probably left unsaid, which Yelena was grateful for. Kate caught her eyes and smiled the warmest, purest smile and Yelena shook her hooded head happily.

    Clint, who was sat comfortably on the couch, nursing a coffee and looking incredibly worse for wear, chuckled a little to himself and Yelena threw him a glare. She was taking great pleasure in his level of suffering, however.

    “Do not listen to her,” Yelena appealed to Nate, trying desperately to hide her happy smile. “I am not afraid of anything. One time I got thrown off this big ship all the way up in the sky.”

    Yelena had kind of presumed that Nate knew his dad was a superhero. It wasn’t exactly a secret, there was a musical about it, but she did wonder if he knew the types of threats her father had dealt with on a daily basis, the ones that weren’t immortalised on stage. She wondered if he knew what Kate did, or what she did. She wondered if he knew that her father had killed for a living. Of course, Clint had ‘retired’ by the time Nate was born, so he never had to live with the fear that his father might never return to him, he may never have really been old enough to understand that in the first place, but surely he was old enough to know how much Kate put her life at risk, and surely he was now just about old enough to understand Natasha’s sacrifice. Dealing with kids and being a superhero must have been a difficult balance, with Lila and Cooper in the mix. Yelena thought that she had it bad with just Kate to worry about.

    Yelena had half expected the kid to shrug her story off, but Nate’s eyes widened at her words. “A big ship in the sky?”

    “Yes. Very high up. There was a very bad man up there, with really bad cologne. He would have hurt people if we let him get away. Lots of people, so I had to stop him.” Clint took another sip of his coffee, and smiled knowingly. Clearly Natasha had recounted this story to him, and clearly he knew that Yelena had done something very, very stupid.

    “And did you?” Nate asked, suddenly enthralled.

    “Yes. But to stop him I had to do something scary, but I was not scared.”

    “You weren’t?” Nate was on tenterhooks. Clearly big ships in the sky were peak superhero, and for someone with no considerable superhero powers, that made Yelena pretty fucking happy.

    “No,” she whispered, with another glance in Clint’s direction. He frowned momentarily, as he realised he couldn’t hear her whisper over the chattering coming the kitchen and the noise of the tv. Yelena smiled with satisfaction and turned back to Nate. “It would have been a pretty cool way to die though,” she whispered again, gleefully. “But then of course my sister had to save the day,” Yelena concluded with a dramatic eye roll.

    “My mom says that Auntie Nat was your sister.” It was more of a question than it appeared.

    “Yes, she was,” Yelena nodded. “Is, I guess.”

    “But you don’t look anything like her.”

    “I don’t?” Yelena teased, a little meanly. She could have just told him they weren’t blood related, or legally related for that matter. They had shared a powerful bond, and three years of their lives, for sure. They also had shared trauma, shared similar losses, they shared the rare ability to empathise with each other, shared the ability to offer each other true understanding. But of course, in many ways, they were nothing alike.

    “She had red hair,” the kid pointed out, and Yelena couldn’t help but laugh. It earned her a slap on the hand and a very real reminder that technically they were still playing slapsies, and she was still losing.

    “Ah. Her red hair, one of Natasha Romanoff’s greatest deceptions.”

    Clint chuckled this time, probably knowing full well how often the older Black Widow had to dye her hair to maintain her iconic look.

    Nate went for another slap, this time sizing up Yelena’s left hand, but to his surprise she deftly moved her hands out the way of his incoming attack.

    His eyes went wide once more. “Woah, that was quick!”

    Yelena narrowed her eyes conspiratorially, smiled a small smile and whispered, “I am very quick.” Nate smiled back.

    The Russian glanced up from the floor as her exceptionally tall looking girlfriend shuffled through into the lounge. She took a small moment to marvel at her. Her dumb Christmas sweater, her comfortable Levis that were turned up at the ankle, her thick, warm socks. Her long, dark hair that Yelena loved so much was pulled back into a messy bun as her bangs framed her beautiful and eternally happy-go-lucky features. She lit up whatever room she walked into and Yelena was more than happy, simply to exist within her orbit.

    “Hey, Babe,” Kate smiled, innocently unaware of the effect she had on Yelena. Nate tried to take advantage, with a well-aimed, vicious slap, but Yelena moved with instinct, evading his attack without ever taking her eyes from Kate. The young boy was left open-mouthed.

    “Hey, darling.” Clint shifted uneasily, despite their conversation from the night before, and Yelena made a note to use the word ‘darling’ as much as humanly possible.

    “Laura could do with some help with the chopping, if you can tear yourself away from here.” Yelena frowned for a moment and appraised her hands. Perhaps taking a break from being glutten for punishment was for the best, and besides, if she was going to benefit from Laura Barton’s exceedingly generous hospitality, she should probably help out a little in return, even if she was still feeling a little sorry for herself.

    “Sure,” Yelena smiled. “You want to tag in, darling? Nate is a formidable adversary, I warn you.”

    “I think I can take him,” Kate grinned and rubbed her hands together at the prospect of slapping a small child. Maybe Clint had a point the previous night, maybe Kate really was still a kid. But if that was the case, where did that place Yelena’s mental age?

    “Yes!” Nate celebrated with a little fist pump. A second victim.

    “Don’t get too cocky,” Yelena warned Kate as the brunette helped her up to her feet. “The kid has clearly had some training.”

    “I got this,” said Kate as she took Yelena’s place on the floor, opposite Nate, and got comfortable.

    Yelena surprised herself as she left the smallest of kisses on the top of Kate’s head before she left for the kitchen. It earned her an instant smile from Kate, who quickly flinched in pain as Nate landed his first decisive blow.

    Once in the kitchen, Laura brought Yelena up to speed with what was left to prepare for the dinner. There were lists and timing plans and colour coded flow charts, the thing was being run like a military operation. No wonder Clint fell for this woman, the efficiency was, well, it was simply stunning.

    After a moment, Yelena had a knife in her hand, and was chopping. She knew what board to use, what measurements to cut to, what pan each vegetable needed to end up in, and in what amount. This was something Yelena’s hungover brain could handle. Most people would maybe feel the need to sit down, but Yelena’s mind found sanctuary in this level of order.

    “You doing okay?” Asked Laura, quietly and quite unexpectedly. Her smile was gentle and her eyes were soft with an edge of concern.

    “Me?” Replied Yelena, a little taken aback. “Oh yeah, just a little rough around the edges.”

    Laura nodded, ruefully. “You and him both. I’m pretty sure he was up in the night.”

    “Really?” Yelena asked, perhaps a little too happily. She couldn’t help it, the thought that Clint Barton had vomited when she hadn’t was just too delightful. “I knew it. I knew he could not beat me.”

    “Oh, that was never in doubt,” Laura smirked a little. Yelena liked this woman. “But I actually wasn’t asking about the hangover, I was asking about you. You drove a long way to put a lot on the line. You’ve been interrogated, and you’ve put yourself way out of your comfort zone by accepting our invitation to stay. Are you doing okay?”

    Yelena was a little stunned, she hadn’t expected the question, and she certainly hadn’t expected Laura to care that much, despite having a sneaking suspicion that she had been trying to talk Clint out of his plans to interrogate Yelena the night before.

    So, was she doing okay? Probably as well as could be expected. She was happy, especially as her headache was easing, and she was growing more comfortable with the idea of being under Clint’s scrutiny. Every time she caught him watching, every time Kate and Yelena caught his attention, was just another opportunity to prove him wrong, to prove to him that she was good for Kate, and not a fuck up waiting to happen. And besides, Christmas could be fun right? There was alcohol, when consumed in responsible amounts, there was good food, dumb movies and good company, because the kids were alright, and getting to watch Kate be this happy for an entire day was even better. To know she had played a small part in that happiness was enough to dampen any worries lingering at the back of her mind that she might have over speaking to S.H.I.E.L.D.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded, with a small reassuring smile, as Laura’s concern was appreciated. “I am doing okay, truly.”

    “I know this is probably a lot. The kids, the music, jazzy sweaters.” Laura grinned and Yelena couldn’t help but grin back.

    “The sweaters are awful,” she laughed, “Very tasteless. But I can see the appeal.”

    “I’ll take that as a ‘you’re not entirely hating it’”

    “I am enjoying it. More than I thought I might,” Yelena explained, earnestly as her eyes found Kate and Nate, both sat cross legged in the middle of the lounge. They were both desperately trying to out slap and out trash talk each other. Yelena spotted Clint tap his hearing aid, and relax back into the couch. “Certain things have been easier than I expected.”

    “Kate seems happy,” Laura said, warmly.

    She really did and Yelena’s heart felt full. “Good.”

    “Are you happy?” The older woman asked.

    Yelena took a moment. It was a big question, and Laura wasn’t just asking it casually, Laura really wanted to know; this wasn’t a pleasantry. The ex-assassin stopped chopping and placed the knife down. Her eyes found Kate, who smiled at her happily before being slapped back to reality by a battling Nate. Lila and Cooper were sat at the dining room table, excitedly discussing the rules to a brand new board game they’d just opened, as they were setting it up. Lucky had slunk downstairs, probably awoken by the cacophony that was Kate and Nate, and was settling down heavily on top of a willing Clint, as the sights and sounds of Miracle on 34th Street played out across the TV in the lounge and the smells of the Christmas Dinner emanated from the Bartons’ kitchen. Yelena smiled a little, to herself. For the first time, in such a long time, she felt still, like she could afford to stop and look and smile and love. She felt at home, because this was exactly where her heart was. And it wasn’t just with Kate. This was Nat’s family too, and perhaps that meant that they were hers also.

    Yelena looked up into Laura’s warm eyes. “I am happy.”

    The older woman smiled and drew Yelena into an unexpected hug. For a moment the blonde stiffened, but in the next moment she felt herself relax. The only person she ever hugged was Kate, and that was a very different type of hug. This was warm, and all encompassing. If a hug could protect you from the world, it would be this hug. It was something Yelena had never experienced before, it was a mother’s hug, and Yelena didn’t want it to end. For her own mother never held her like this, not for lack of love or desire to love, but Melina was still learning how to be Yelena’s mother, Melina was still learning empathy and much like Yelena, Melina was still learning that she could be loved herself, but Laura Barton was all love. Love on instinct, love without question. Perhaps Yelena’s mother needed to be hugged by Laura Barton.

    After a moment more, Laura freed the younger woman from her embrace and smiled. “Good, you deserve a little happiness. Us and the kids still have a few presents to open. You can join us if you like?”

    Yelena appreciated the offer, but with no presents to give, her offering needed to be made in meticulously chopped and sorted veg. “I am okay here. Thank you though. I don’t have anything to give.”

    “If you say so,” Laura shrugged and raised a small, teasing eyebrow, before she grabbed her two older kids from the dining table and led them through to the lounge.

    Nate declared victory over Kate as Clint told them to wrap up what they were doing and the family settled across the couches and the chairs in the lounge. Gifts were distributed and kids waited impatiently, fingers itching to unwrap them. Yelena watched Lila’s eyes light up in delight, as she opened a gift from Kate. It was the archery target that had hung in Kate’s apartment. They’d had to remove it when Yelena had moved in and taken up residence underneath the duplex. The blonde remembered that way back then Kate had mentioned how much of a great gift it would be for Lila, Yelena remembered agreeing. Kate had been correct. Both young women hugged tightly and then sat for a little while, in each other’s embrace. It would have been endearing if it hadn’t been so sickeningly sweet. Yelena rolled her eyes from afar, with a smile she couldn’t keep from her face, and continued to chop as the Bartons and the Bishop continued to exchange gifts.

    “Wow, these vegetables are regimented,” came her girlfriend’s voice. Arms found their way around her waist and lips pressed against her temple. How had she gotten so close? And how had Yelena not seen or heard her coming? The ex-assassin had taught her charge far too well.

    “Small, neat vegetables are the best kind of vegetables, you know that. That way everything cooks quickly and evenly,” Yelena explained, not making any attempt to escape Kate’s encircling arms.

    “You are too cute sometimes,” Kate whispered into her neck, as she placed a kiss there, gently. Yelena’s eyes went to the Bartons, all who were still happily opening presents. No eyes were on them, but still Yelena felt herself stiffen, just a little, but Kate knew exactly what she was doing, as her eyes were on the Bartons too, watching for any sign that their attentions were wandering. Yelena really had trained Kate well.

    “I am not cute. Do not tell anyone that I am cute,” Yelena insisted, whilst emphasising her point, gesticulating her knife.

    “Oh, you’re way too late.”

    “Ugh,” Yelena shivered dramatically and shook off Kate’s embrace. She couldn’t hide her smile though.

    “Laura thinks you’re cute too.”

    “Oh really?” Yelena smirked and raised a suggestive eyebrow.

    “Not like that,” Kate explained, a little too quickly.

    “That is a disappointment,” Yelena said, with a little frown and a downturned smile. “She would make a very good wife in Russia.” Yelena wasn’t joking, Laura would make an excellent wife in Russia. She had birthed strong children, she was strong willed, kept her beautiful home beautifully neat, was the perfect hostess and from the incredible smells coming the oven, was almost certainly an incredible cook.

    “What about me?” Kate asked, clearly threatened by the competition, despite making it quite clear less than twenty-four hours before that she despised marriage.

    “You would make a terrible wife – ow! Nahui!” Blood flashed angrily against the kitchen surfaces as Yelena dropped the knife and clutched her left forefinger, tightly.

    “Language around my kids Yelena!” Came Laura’s voice, loud and clear from the lounge. By her tone, she wasn’t messing around. Did she speak Russian? What the fuck? And ow, what the fuck. Ow, her finger hurt. What a fucking idiot.

    “Is everything okay?” Called Clint’s concerned voice.

    “Everything’s fine!” Explained Kate as she waved off inquiring looks and grabbed Yelena by the hand to drag her to the kitchen sink. Kate turned on the cold tap and thrust Yelena’s hand under it. The blonde’s blood flooded the sink at first, and mixed like watercolours as it spiralled lazily down the drain. Very quickly though, the wound grew less angry and after a few more mumbled expletives and a few more forehead kisses, Kate took Yelena’s hand from under the tap and applied pressure with a clean tea towel.

    Kate tutted and shook her head. “Poor thing. For someone who’s supposed to be good with knives, you really fucked it.”

    “You are very distracting,” Yelena simply scowled.

    Kate smiled, a little too proudly, and removed the tea towel as she turned Yelena’s hand in hers, inspecting the tiny wound on her finger that had been effectively calmed.

    “Still think I’d make a terrible wife?” Kate asked, with the biggest of shit eating grins.

    Feeling ever so sorry for herself, Yelena could only pout. “Zhizn’ ebet meya,” she grumbled, quietly.

    “What did I say, Yelena?!” Came Laura’s voice from around the corner in the lounge.

    “How?” Yelena asked, completely confounded by Laura’s hawklike hearing. “How?!”

    A few more hours of helping Laura with the food prep had managed to shift Yelena’s hangover entirely. Clint had managed to haul himself from the sofa and was in the kitchen following Laura’s strict timeline of instructions. He had to put things in the oven when they needed to go in, and then remove things from the oven when they needed to come out. It was a very vital role.

    Yelena had been put on table setting duty and then serving up duty; transferring food from oven dish to serving dish. Not a job she could have managed without the band aid Nate had provided for her. It had been a sweet gesture, until she’d realised he was trying to attach Avenger band aids to her, and she wanted to be a little sick in her mouth. Yelena had made a mental note to tell Carol that she never wanted to be on any band aids, ever. Or on any other merchandise for that matter.

    Everything was looking good though, and in a few short minutes, the family would probably be settling down to eat, but of course, one guest couldn’t wait for that. One guest was hovering, like a scavenger, and that guest was Kate Bishop.

    “No,” Yelena chided, as she slapped away Kate’s searching hand, and not for the first time.

    “But I’m hungry,” the brunette moaned. She was trying everything. Giving her the eyes, tugging shamelessly at the belt hoops of her jeans, she’d even tried to convince Yelena that the cheesy dinner roll she was attempting to make off with was for Lucky.

    “Sweetheart,” chimed Laura. “You can wait a little longer.”

    “Exactly,” agreed Yelena, “You can wait a little- hey!” Kate snatched at a roll but in the blink of an eye Yelena had hold of her wrist. “What are you a kid or something?” Yelena asked, a little put out that her meticulous arrangement was now not so meticulous looking. “You can’t follow simple instructions?”

    Lila ducked into the kitchen to collect a dish of potatoes destined for the dining table. “Us kids can follow simple instructions, don’t tar us with her brush,” the middle Barton quipped with a smile.

    Kate simply grinned, snatched her wrist from Yelena’s hand, tore the steaming doughy goodness into two pieces and handed one to Clint who smiled conspiratorially. “Thanks Kid.”

    “Clint, sweetheart,” Laura appealed, but it was too late. Her husband had fallen to Kate Bishop’s corruption.

    Kate stuck the rest of the bread in her mouth with aplomb and all Yelena could do was roll her eyes. “What are you gonna do?” Kate asked, through the half-chewed bread in her mouth. Delightful, you’re falling for this? “You can’t stop us.”

    “Nothing. I am not going to do anything,” Yelena said, stoically, her arms folded across her chest. “But you should know that I could, if I wanted to.”

    “You’re plotting your revenge aren’t you?” Kate said, but it wasn’t really a question.

    “Naturally,” Yelena grinned. This earned her a laugh from Lila who was back in the kitchen for the green beans.

    “You two are so dramatic.”

    “Don’t get in my way, Lila Barton,” Yelena warned, smile evident as her eyes narrowed and finger pointed in the teenager’s direction.

    “Like you scare me,” Lila said as she retrieved the green beans, flicked her hair, quite dramatically if Yelena had to put a word to it, and headed back through to the dining table.

    “Wow,” was the only thing Kate could manage.

    “Did you hear that sass?” Yelena asked, disbelievingly.

    Laura and Lila high-fived as the beans reached the table and laughter rang through the Barton household as Lila earned a congratulatory slap on the back from her father, who then proceeded to steal another cheese roll and shove it unceremoniously into his mouth.

    Kate grinned at Yelena and Yelena grinned back. Suddenly everything felt natural, suddenly everything felt right. Yelena had never been in a place where love had felt so palpable. She’d have called it sickening if she hadn’t secretly liked the feeling so much.

    The brunette pulled on Yelena’s sleeve and drew her closer. The blonde knew Kate wanted to kiss her, she could see it in her face, but she knew that she wouldn’t. That could wait until later.

    “How’s your fragile ego?” Kate asked, she was so close.

    Yelena shook her head in mock dismay. “I have never been shown such disrespect.”

    Dinner played out in much the same way as the rest of the day had. Filled with love and laughter and weird conversations with Nate about Russian Santa. Yelena had told him that Santa delivering presents to every kid in the world on one night was fake news; Russian Christmas was two weeks later, so he had a pretty long break to rest and go again. Nate had then asked that if he came to visit her for Russian Christmas, would he get two lots of Christmas presents? The blonde had reluctantly told him that she thought Santa would know, and he’d reluctantly agreed.

    They’d also agreed that Lucky could spend the night with Nate that evening, as it was Christmas and Lucky would be going home the next day. Yelena was grateful for the space it would afford her feet. Kate was grateful for the lack of an additional body of heat. The Bartons’ homestead was beautifully cosy, but also exceedingly warm once Kate had added furnace Yelena into the mix, on top of Lucky’s fluffy self.

    Yelena rummaged around in her rucksack as Kate changed into a pair of shorts and a baggy Avengers t-shirt. She really was a nerd.

    Hands found her hips as Yelena found what she’d been searching for. Kate pulled on the blonde’s ever so slightly oversized jogging bottoms.

    “These are so big on you,” Kate said, as Yelena turned in her arms. It was true, the pants were huge on her, and they were huge because they were Kate’s. When Yelena had been packing her rucksack for her trans-American tour, she hadn’t really had a tonne of space to pack any pyjamas, and sadly having a girlfriend and being able to share all their clothes wasn’t really something their size difference afforded them. But she was willing to admit that she did look just a little bit cute when she tried to share Kate’s wardrobe, and Kate certainly didn’t mind it. The brunette’s hands found their way to the blonde’s ass and drew her closer. Yelena was pretty sure Kate had been waiting all day to do that.

    “They are big because my girlfriend is a giant, so…”

    Kate stooped a little, as the brunette’s lips found Yelena’s and the blonde dropped the rucksack she’d been holding, to the floor. A small moan escaped Kate as Yelena’s hands pulled their bodies flush. They then tugged at the hairband tangled up in dark, dark brown hair. The messy bun was released and Yelena’s fingers almost got completely lost amongst the waves, along with her senses. With reluctance, the blonde placed a delicate hand upon Kate’s chest, broke their slightly fevered kiss, and pushed, gently.

    “What?” Came Kate’s worried look. But her worry was quickly quelled by Yelena’s warm smile and her eyes that danced in innocent excitement.

    “So, umm,” Yelena stuttered slightly, as she retrieved her rucksack from the floor. “When I was riding here, I had to stop at the gas station, quite a few times actually. Bikes are not efficient and gas tanks are not really that big.”

    “Okay,” Kate said, her curiosity piqued.

    “I thought that whilst I was there I could get you some really cool Christmas gifts. You know, in case you accepted my apology.” At the time it had seemed like a great idea, and the more Yelena thought about the gifts she’d managed to pick up, the more she thought it was the best idea she’d had in quite some time.

    “From a gas station?” Kate asked, incredulously. Just you wait, Kate. Just you wait.

    “Yes and they are very cool, considering I bought them at 3am. It not like Tiffany’s was open,” Yelena reminded her with a chiding shake of the head and a playful smirk.

    “Okay okay,” Kate held her hands up in repentance. “Sorry. It’s very thoughtful and I’m ready to be blown away,” Kate said as she perched herself down upon the end of their bed.

    “Good. Because you will be,” Yelena said, a little smugly, as she produced a brown paper bag from her rucksack and handed it to her very confused looking girlfriend. “Happy Christmas.”

    If possible, Kate’s confusion grew as she delved into the bag and withdrew the first item. “Corn?” She asked, a little bewildered.

    “Yes,” said Yelena, matter-of-factly. Surely it was obvious. “Corn. Ohio is very famous for corn. This corn is dried,” Yelena pointed to the packet in Kate’s hands, “And there are a lot of different varieties inside.”

    A small smile pulled at the corner of Kate’s lips. The brunette was thinking about how cute she was, Yelena knew it.

    “I can tell you love it. I do too, but do not worry, I will not ask you to share.”

    “Oh thank god, I was worried.”

    “I will buy more on my way home,” Yelena reassured her clearly concerned girlfriend.

    “Good, because try and stop me finishing all of this.”

    “Do not worry, it is for you, it is all for you. Now, come on, what is next?” Yelena grinned and Kate could only shake her head as she delved back into the brown bag of gas station surprises.

    “What have we got here…?” Kate asked as her fingers found purchase on something and pulled. Yelena had to fight to keep a straight face as Kate’s eyes scanned what lay before her. It was a bumper sticker, and it read: BABY AVENGER ONBOARD.

    “For when you pass Drivers Ed,” Yelena explained with the smallest of smirks. She felt so smug. When she’d bought the sticker she hadn’t known if Kate was going to take her back, now she’d given it to her, she didn’t know whether Kate was going to break up with her all over again.

    Her girlfriend glowered at her. “Fuck you,” were the only two words she could manage. Oh how sweet this was. It really was the perfect gift.

    “It was just too perfect, I could not resist,” Yelena said, giddily. “Because you are an Avenger but you are like a baby and you are new so-“

    “You don’t have to explain it,” Kate insisted, with her jaw set, but her eyes betrayed her. She was counting the ways she wanted to pin Yelena down and make her pay, and for the first time, Yelena was okay with that, and it made flirting fun, really fun.

    “I do, I do have to explain it, because it is funny.”

    Kate sighed and shook her head dramatically. “Considering you got this at 3am, you’ve actually done pretty well,” she conceded.

    “Thank you, I thought so,” Yelena said with a shrug and a small downturned smile. “I was going to get you a lottery ticket but then I thought that you had already won the lottery with me so…”

    “What? Come on!” Kate pouted. “I would have loved a lottery ticket! You got dried corn but not a lottery ticket?”

    Yelena simply raised an eyebrow and indicated that Kate should delve a little deeper into the bag, and so the brunette did just that.

    “You got me a lottery ticket,” Kate said with a smile.

    Yelena crossed her arms. She was incredibly satisfied with herself. To see Kate smiling, to see her happy, to hear her laughing, all the things Yelena worried she’d never experience again when she’d been buying these small gifts at the gas station, it was the greatest Christmas gift Yelena could have hoped for

    “You got me a lottery ticket and used our birthdays for the numbers,” Kate said, softly and Yelena nodded. It was gross and cute and not at all her, but when she’d picked those numbers out, she hadn’t known if Kate was going to take her back, she hadn’t known if this risk, this gamble, was going to pay off, and to put their birthdays down on a lottery ticket like that, it felt as though she was rolling the dice, and once she’d put everything on the table, it was going to be up to the fates to decide. Of course, that was totally irrational. It had been up to them, and only them, but at that moment, at 3am in a gas station in Ohio, she’d have taken all the help she could get.

    “I love you,” Kate whispered as she reached for Yelena, wanting her girlfriend to be closer. The blonde acquiesced and drew the brunette into the strongest of hugs. Kate buried her head into Yelena’s chest and the Russian placed a soft kiss upon the top of her girlfriend’s head.

    “I know,” Yelena whispered her response, as her arms grew even tighter around Kate. They both knew that Yelena couldn’t say it back yet, they both knew she wasn’t ready, but Yelena was so grateful to hear those words from Kate, and she made a note to make sure that Kate knew how grateful she was, every time she uttered them.

    “I am just thankful that I am able to share these small things with you. When I was buying the stuff, I was- I did not know…” Yelena signed and placed another kiss on Kate’s head. The blonde felt Kate’s hands tighten around her waist, she felt so good. “I did not know whether you were going to want to see me again. So, this is nice.”

    Kate pushed back slightly to look up into Yelena’s eyes. She smiled, warmly and happily and her eyes danced in the muted glow from the old light fitting that hung over their bed. “It is,” she said, gently, just before their lips met once more, softly this time. It was chaste and tender and for a moment it felt as if time stood still, because soon, soon she would open the card.

    Yelena broke their kiss and rested her forehead against Kate’s, just for a moment, before she settled down next to her upon the edge of the bed. The Russian gave her girlfriends a small nudge in the arm and nodded towards the bag. “There are some Twizzlers in there too, and a card.”

    Kate’s eyes lit up. “Ooh Twizzlers,” she said, clearly delighted, and Yelena couldn’t hide her smile as Kate immediately began to open the packet of candy and then caught herself. She looked up at Yelena, clearly a little embarrassed at her over-exuberance. “You want me to open the card?”

    Yelena swallowed. “Yes, please.”

    “Did you write this at 3am too?” Kate asked.

    Yelena shifted, nervously and Kate couldn’t hide her small, confused frown. “Maybe,” the blonde said, apprehension evident in her voice.

    Kate’s hand squeezed Yelena’s thigh reassuringly before she tore at the envelope, extracted the card, and began to read. Yelena studied Kate’s face as her heart pounded in her chest. Not at the contents of the card, not at the question that she’d posed inside, but at the implications of what could come next.

    Kate’s eyes widened as they took in the words that were written there.

    After a beat she looked up into her Yelena’s eyes. “Really?” She asked, a little breathless.

    Yelena nodded.

    “You want me to come with you?” Kate’s expression was one of bewilderment. It hadn’t been the greetings card that she’d been expecting. In all honesty, it hadn’t been the greetings card Yelena had been intending on writing, until a night previous.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded, earnestly. “I have been thinking about going for some time,” she explained. “Since having you in my life, I have felt strong, I have felt strong enough.”

    Kate’s hand found hers and her fingers became instantly entwined amongst Yelena’s. “Do you know where to start?” Kate asked and Yelena nodded. She did, she knew exactly where to start. Sarajevo.

    “Then, I would feel very privileged to come with you,” Kate said, with a tight squeeze of Yelena’s hand.

    There was a moment, when the significance of what they’d just agreed settled upon both of them. They weren’t just going travelling together, this wasn’t a holiday. Yelena had asked Kate if she would join her in finding her mother, and Kate had said yes. This wasn’t a declaration of love from Yelena, this was a declaration of absolute trust, and for Yelena, that was so much more significant.

    Kate tried and failed to blink away the disloyal tears that had threatened to escape her eyes as she smiled brightly and happily.

    “So we get to go to Europe?” Kate inquired with a small grin, in an attempt to spare her embarrassment.

    “Uh huh,” Yelena smiled, broadly.

    “I’m thinking like, Med Cruise, a few nights in Rome, oh or Venice.”

    Yelena couldn’t help but laugh. Kate Bishop was a total dork.

    “Maybe some Greek Island hopping. Oh maybe Paris.”

    Yelena shrugged. “I have kind of done Paris.” She knew Kate would hate that. Turns out, she was right.

    “But you haven’t done Paris with me.”

    The Russian decided to tease her girlfriend some more, because why the hell not? “I do not want to do Paris with you. You will get all swept up in the romance of it.”

    “Wouldn’t that be nice?” Kate asked as she drew Yelena into slow and heated kiss. Turns out Kate knew just how to counter Yelena’s teasing.

    “That is if Carol lets us go,” Yelena muttered as she broke their kiss, most disappointed that her mind had jumped to Carol Danvers mid-kiss with Kate Bishop.

    Kate placed a reassuring kiss upon Yelena’s lips. “She will.”

    Yelena frowned now. What if she didn’t let them go? What if she asked why they were travelling together? Would she have to come clean that soon? Suddenly Yelena had a lot of worries, mainly about Carol Danvers. “She might not. Carol can be a bitch.”

    “Well then,” Kate chewed on her lip for a moment, considering her words carefully. “Fuck Carol.”

    A surprised and delighted laugh escaped Yelena Belova. “Kate Bishop, you are incredible,” she said unabashedly.

    Kate grinned mischievously. “Really?” Kate Bishop secretly loved being bad. She considered herself rebel, a badass. Of course, in reality, she was neither, but it was wonderful to see her dream.

    “Uh huh,” Yelena nodded before she captured her lips once more. Kate’s tongue grazed gently against her own, and the brunette moaned softly into her mouth as Yelena’s fingers played across the soft skin of her stomach that was hidden just beneath the hem of her oversized t-shirt.

    Suddenly, Kate captured Yelena’s hands in her own and removed them from underneath her shirt. Yelena found herself frowning.

    “I’m sorry, I just…” Kate tried to explain but struggled to find the words.

    “I’m turning you on.” It wasn’t a question. Of course Yelena was turning her on, that was kind of the point wasn’t it? For Kate anyways.

    Kate nodded, sheepishly.

    “Well, do you want to try?” Yelena asked, and Kate blinked in confusion.

    “You mean… with the- with me doing the…” Yelena could sense Kate’s brain spiralling. She placed a calming hand against her cheek, and played her thumb slowly across the soft and slightly flushed skin there.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded assuredly. “If you want to.”

    Kate’s cheeks really were flushing now. “But we’re at the Bartons’.”

    Yelena shrugged, calmly. “What better place to try? If it does not work and we do not like it that much our bed is still sacred, no?” She reasoned, in an attempt to reassure her girlfriend. “But of course, if you do not want to then we absolutely don’t-“

    “Woah, woah, woah,” Kate interjected, quite suddenly. “I didn’t say that I didn’t want to. I said that we were at the Bartons’, so you’re going to have to help me forget. As long as you’re happy with that?”

    Yelena smiled, she absolutely and irrefutably was. “I am,” she nodded. Of course, her heart was beating off the charts and her brain was telling her that she was completely out of her depth but she knew that this was something she wanted to do. This was their first step towards compromise, towards a long term way of working, towards a long term relationship.

    Kate took Yelena’s face within her hands and made her meet her eyes. “If you’re ever not, at any point-“

    “I will say,” the blonde reassured her.

    Kate took a moment, a moment to deliberate and moment to contemplate, before she nodded her agreement. “Okay,” she said, quietly, as a hint of excitement entered her voice.

    “Okay,” said Yelena, as she took a deep steadying breath.

    “Okay,” whispered Kate one last time, quite breathlessly, before their lips met and they fell back into the multiplicity of pillows that adorned the bed.

    Yelena started slow, just like she had the first time she’d put her lips to every inch of Kate’s soft and freckled skin. They removed each other’s clothes, slowly and deliberately, revealing new areas to kiss and touch and caress. Yelena peppered soft, adoring kisses across Kate’s chest as the brunette’s hands lost themselves in unruly blonde hair or clung just a little desperately to her strong shoulders, drawing her lips closer.

    Yelena’s breath caught as their eyes met, for she was met with a look of such vulnerability yet such excitement and exhilaration. Kate was ready and her eyes were asking if Yelena was still as ready as she was. The blonde answered with a small nod and fierce, reassuring kiss.

    It was odd in a way, as at first, it felt like nothing had changed. Kate’s lips still grazed and bit at hers, her tongue still played with hers, her hand still tugged and pulled at her hair. But soon, Kate was moaning into her mouth, her hips flinched and bucked, and her movements grew more erratic, her breathing more laboured.

    Where before Kate’s eyes had been open, to study every movement and every inch of Yelena, they now struggled to stay open, as she bit her lip and gasped in pleasure. Her chest was heaving as her body grew more and more tense. Yelena didn’t know where to touch or whether to kiss her or where to kiss her, but she knew that she didn’t need to. She just needed to be with her. So she held her as close as she could, she stole kisses across her chest when she could and pressed her lips into the palm of the hand that was clutched at her shoulder. And then Yelena told her how beautiful she was, how unbelievably beautiful she was, as Kate came in her arms for the first time with Yelena’s name on her lips.

    The next morning, Yelena and Kate awoke in each other’s arms. They exchanged kisses and laughs, and helped each other pack their bags as they sipped on coffees and snacked on bagels and Pop-Tarts. Yelena marvelled at the amount her girlfriend had packed for a three- night stay and to her surprise, Kate had accepted the blonde’s criticism happily. Yelena suspected that she could have said anything to Kate that morning and the brunette would have simply smiled and told her that she loved her.

    After a final coffee in the lounge, the two Avengers said goodbye to the Bartons. Yelena thanked them for their hospitality, and paid special tribute to Laura’s kindness and welcome. Hugs were exchanged and Nate had to be physically extracted from Yelena’s side as Kate’s taxi arrived.

    After that, Yelena reluctantly left Kate and Lucky at the airport. With a kiss for both her girlfriend and her girlfriend’s dog, she started the long journey back to New York City alone, on her bike. As the early winter sun was setting, Yelena made the short walk through the gravestones, to her sister’s snow covered grave. She diligently cleared some of the dead flowers away, but there were still an abundance of recent floral offerings that had been left by grateful families of those lost in the Snap.

    Yelena settled down on her haunches and laid the nicest bunch of gas station flowers she’d ever seen down upon her sister’s grave. She stood again, in solace, for a moment and tried to push back thoughts of Christmas times together, and Christmas times that could have been. “Merry Christmas, Natasha,” Yelena whispered, “Your family missed you.”

    Chapter End Notes Okay. Don’t cry.

    Knock on Wood Chapter Notes Hello! So… welcome to Europe. This is the first of a three part escapade and I hope you enjoy.

    Thank you all who are reading and commenting and kudosing. We went to Rome and came back with covid and your encouragement really motivated me to get back on it after a few days in bed. Thank you to my beta Kristin who, once the fog cleared, really encouraged me to get back on it. I hope you enjoy.

    Kate’s curiosity had been piqued, in a major way. She’d only just made it off of the plane from London when Yelena’s text had come through. It read but two words. I’m sorry. Followed by the obligatory kisses that girlfriends must leave one another. What the hell had she done within the space of just a few short hours? It couldn’t have been something too serious right? Otherwise her girlfriend would have been phoning her as soon as wheels had touched tarmac. No, she hadn’t done anything too bad. Unless it was so bad that it was far too difficult to put into words. Best avoided altogether, that sort of thing. Kate had messaged back, of course, whilst running through London Heathrow. She had Lucky in one hand, was furiously typing away with her phone in the other, with her carry on bag thrown over her shoulder and her large winter coat billowing behind. She’d worked up a serious sweat on that airport dash. Of course, Yelena had never seen her message as she had been on a flight of her own. They’d arranged it so that Yelena would arrive into Sarajevo, with Fanny, an hour or so before Kate and Lucky were due. Smart. But not so smart when your girlfriend sent you cryptic messages with zero explanation and then disappeared into the dizzying heights of a thirty seven thousand feet cellular dead zone.

    The anticipation was killing the young Avenger. Thankfully it was killing her figuratively, not literally. But it wasn’t killing her as much as the anticipation of seeing Yelena again. Her girlfriend, Yelena. It had been too long. After spending a pretty fantastic and completely lazy New Year’s Eve together, Kate had gone back to Avenging and Yelena had gone to see her family for Second Christmas, just outside of St Petersburg. It had been nearly two solid weeks since they’d seen each other in person. Nearly two solid weeks since she’d seen her elusive smile, nearly two weeks since she’d breathed her in or kissed her lips or heard her rasping laugh. Nearly two weeks since she’d felt the benefit of her unwavering optimism. Okay, that last bit was bullshit. Yelena Belova, although sometimes a little ‘seat of her pants’, could not be called an optimist, but there was something about having the Russian around that made Kate feel strong or better yet, capable as an Avenger but more importantly in their life together.

    And very shortly, that life together would resume; she was on the brink. Kate stood silently with a tired Lucky sat happily next to her, as the conveyer carrying everyone’s luggage but hers limped its way around the baggage carousel. “Come on, come on, come on,” she muttered to herself as she tapped her foot impatiently and checked her phone for the thirty seven thousandth time. Nothing yet from Yelena. Kate didn’t know what she wanted more, her luggage or contact from her bae. Side note, when Kate had discovered that Yelena hated the word ‘bae’ it was entered into the brunette’s common vernacular with immediate effect. Kate Bishop didn’t mess around.

    After a few more minutes of foot tapping, phone checking and general impatient mumbling, Kate caught sight of her case and her bow case as they were spat out onto the conveyer. With a mini fist pump and a quiet, “Yes!”, she hurried over to where the cases had just appeared and dragged them from the carousel with next to no form. With Lucky at her side, she hastily made for the exit as fast as her feet would take her without looking as if she was trying to avoid declaring anything she really should be declaring.

    Kate glanced down at her phone again but nothing. Ah well, it was too late now. She was in Bosnia and Herzegovina. She was sure that Yelena would be there. She was sure that she would see her ridiculously wonderful face as soon as she turned into the- “Kate!” Came a bellowing, familiar voice from her right. She was blindsided before she even had time to lay eyes on her assailant, and pulled into a crushing hug. Lucky yapped happily at her side and pulled on his lead as his pawed feet tapped and clacked happily on the tiled airport floor. His other momma was nearby and he knew it, which meant this must have been… oh god, this must have been…

    “Alexei!” She spluttered into his shoulder as he held her as tight as his super solder strength allowed. Unsurprisingly, that was pretty tight. “Hi, I uh…” Kate was lost for words, and was also quickly losing the feeling in the lower half of her body.

    “Papa, let her go”. There they were, Yelena’s dulcet tones, as optimistic and enthusiastic as ever. But where the hell was she?

    “It is so good to meet you!” Alexei exclaimed, practically lifting Kate off her feet. He had a distinct musk, one that wasn’t necessarily unpleasant but certainly not something you’d want to sit next to on a flight for longer than forty-five minutes. It was an odd mixture of Smirnoff, presumably from the flight, chewing tobacco and a knock off version of Boss by Hugo Boss.

    “Wow thanks. I....” Big arms released her and drew her back to get a better look. She was met with the broad smile of a man in his early fifties, a smile that she recognised from the few times they’d seen each other face to face through the power of encrypted video calls. His beard was neat and trimmed to his jawline, and his thinning hair was swept back scruffily, in an unintentionally fashionable manner. His sunken eyes were bright and happy and although the man they belonged to towered above even her, which the brunette would normally find hella intimidating, Kate couldn’t help but smile through her bamboozlement. This was not the welcome she’d been expecting, but all of a sudden, Yelena’s cryptic text made complete sense. Her parents were coming, and they were coming for her.

    Kate beamed back at Alexei. “It’s good to-.” But the brunette didn’t manage to complete her sentence, as she’d already been drawn into another fierce embrace.

    “My darling girl,” Melina said softly, before she pulled back, took Kate’s face between her hands and appraised it. “Beautiful,” Yelena’s mother said, as if appreciating a fine wine or work of art. Kate felt the heat begin to rise in her cheeks.

    “Oh, thank you. I…” Kate’s eyes did their best to try and locate Yelena, but the head they were residing in was still being held firm by Melina Vostokoff and her evaluating grip. Yelena, now would be a good time to show yourself, babe. Kate knew that her girlfriend’s parents meant well, and this was just them showing their excitement and enjoyment in meeting her, but at the same time this was unlike anything she’d ever experienced before. “She’s beautiful, isn’t she beautiful Alexei?” The incredibly striking, and incredibly intimidating ex Black Widow insisted of her partner. Now, Kate’s ego would have you know that she never doubted Alexei’s response, but only because Kate’s ego would never recommend disagreeing with a very insistent Black Widow, unless you wanted trouble. “Very beautiful my dear,” he agreed enthusiastically, as expected. Big tick for Alexei. Were they going to check her teeth too? Because she had great teeth and she would be open to that.

    Melina smiled warmly before she released Kate from her grip and caught sight of the cute ball of golden retriever goodness that stood to attention next to her, sniffing the air curiously. The older woman gasped in delight as she went to greet him with a generous ear scratch. “And Lucky! What a wonderful boy!”

    “Sorry if he’s a little grumpy, he’s probably pretty tired,” Kate shrugged, and in all honesty, they both were. It had been one long day. They’d boarded about six pm New York time, and it was now four am New York time. Sure, they’d both slept on the flight, and yes, Kate had treated them to business class so they could get a little shut-eye on the way to London, but her body was still telling her it was four am, and her body could not be convinced otherwise. “He is beautiful,” Melina said as she gave him a gentle kiss on the forehead. “He really is. He...” Kate trailed off, because there she was. Finally. Yelena not-Avenger, Black Widow, corn-lover Belova. Yes, that Yelena Belova. She was stood a little further away than Kate had expected, with Fanny in hand. Her yellow tartan winter coat hung open despite the cold outside. Underneath she wore a thick black turtle neck, some faded Levis and a pair of black DMs. To top it all off, Yelena was wearing something Kate had never seen her wear before, and almost instantly it became something Kate wanted to see her wear every single day of her life; a purple beanie. A purple beanie. Did she do it on purpose? Kate hoped she did. Kate also knew that this was completely wishful thinking on her part, but now in her mind, it was canon. Straight up canon. Yelena was telling the world that she was the property of Kate Bishop, the greatest archer in the world. Oh, what could Kate do to say the same? Something spider themed seemed a little Halloween, and she wasn’t exactly a spider person, not that she’d ever admit to it. Perhaps they could get matching black widow mark tattoos, or dog mum T-shirts. Or Kate could walk around with a snapback that said ‘I survived the Black Widow’s Bite’. That would be totally cool and not nerdy in any way. Although, had Yelena ever actually bitten her? Nibbled, perhaps, but bitten? Kate couldn’t think of an occasion, probably for obvious reasons. But maybe, just maybe, Yelena would, if she asked nicely enough... at a later time, not at the airport, in front of her girlfriend’s parents. Kate, you really need to stop thinking about Yelena biting you right about now. Jeez, the effect a purple beanie could have on a girl, but gosh darn it, did it make her feel possessive. In a totally appropriate, respectful way. They were in a monogamous relationship, after all. The blonde smiled and waved awkwardly from a distance. Why did she have to be so far away? Of course, Fanny. Yelena was keeping Fanny away from Lucky, which made total sense but was also incredibly disappointing. She began to slowly approach with her american akita, letting her dog sniff and evaluate the situation in front of her. “Surprise!” Yelena called from across the way, her voice dripping with sarcasm. “They wanted it to be a surprise.” Kate could summate that her girlfriend was not happy. “Isn’t this surprising? What a great surprise.” Oh no, not happy at all, but Kate couldn’t help but smile. To see her furrowed brow, her stubborn, downturned lips, her small turned up nose; it was wonderful and it was making Kate giddy with happiness.

    “I mean, it is a great surprise I’m just a little…”

    “Lost for words?” Yelena asked, with an exasperated smile.

    “Surprised!” Kate answered, with a smile of her own, as Lucky took a few apprehensive steps forwards and the two dogs began to sniff at each other’s snouts. Kate knelt down and very carefully supplied both dogs a couple of treats for their good behaviour. A little positive reinforcement went a long way with Lucky, and she hoped it would do the same for Fanny. Kate gave the akita an affectionate head ruffle and then slowly brought her into her arms. She was warm, despite the cold outside, and like the absolute good girl that she was, she rested her head lightly on Kate’s shoulder. Lucky was going to have some competition. “Hey, Fanny,” Kate whispered into her fur, “It’s so good to finally meet you.” “Do I get a hug or…?” came her girlfriend’s slightly put out voice. Kate knew that Yelena’s tone was for effect, but it couldn’t mask the fact that the blonde was most definitely getting jealous of her dog. She had needs, and being hugged was one of them.

    With an eye roll and a shake of the head, Kate stood and pulled Yelena into a long-overdue hug. Her girlfriend’s head tucked neatly under her chin, her hands clutched at the thick material of Kate’s coat and pulled the brunette as close as was physically possible, and the two partners breathed each other in. It was the first time Yelena had let herself be held so intimately in public, which was ironic seeing as they knew Sarajevo wasn’t exactly the place for public displays of affection, same sex or otherwise.

    Kate placed the smallest, and subtlest of kisses on the top of Yelena’s beanie and whispered, “I like this, it’s purple.”

    “I found it at the dollar store,” Yelena mumbled. “But they had to pay me to take it from them.”

    “Fuck you,” Kate grinned.

    “You wish,” Yelena smirked, as she pulled back to take in her girlfriend. “Sooo original,” Kate laughed quietly and shook a chiding head before turning back towards Yelena’s rather giddy parents. They’d been watching them hug, and it was kind of cute, but at the same time Kate was suddenly feeling the pressure. They were really here, Melina was really here; Melina who knew all about their falling out before Christmas, Melina who convinced Yelena to stay in the United States with Kate. All of a sudden, Kate felt like she needed to justify that decision, to prove that it was a gamble that was going to pay off. After all, Melina could have had her daughter back forever if she’d just let Yelena follow through with running away, but she hadn’t.

    “It’s so lovely to meet you both, and an even lovelier surprise,” Kate offered. That was good right? That said conscientious, kind and polite. It must have been somewhere in that ballpark as Melina and Alexei smiled back at her.

    “When Yelena told us you were coming to Sarajevo, we just had to see you,” Melina explained. Oh, so she did tell them.

    “We got on the first flight,” Alexei added. Oh, so she only just told them. OH. “They got on my flight,” Yelena grumbled. She clearly wasn’t happy, but she wasn’t just unhappy with the intrusion. There was something else. Because after all, this trip was never a secret trip to meet Kate, and the secret certainly wasn’t Kate herself. The secret was the reason they were in Sarajevo specifically, and that was something Kate had been pushing Yelena to reveal to her parents, quite incessantly, most days since Second Christmas. “You told them?” Kate asked, apprehensively.

    “I did,” Yelena nodded, tight lipped, and Kate frowned. Her girlfriend was not being forthcoming with information.

    “That I was coming to Europe?” Kate asked again, for she definitely needed further clarification before she put her foot in her mouth and revealed more than she should. “Yes,” Yelena answered, with another little nod. This was like pulling teeth. Kate eyed Yelena shiftily. “What else did you tell them?”

    Yelena shrugged, as if it were obvious. “That we are going to look for my biological mother.”

    When Yelena put it like that, she didn’t quite believe it. “You did?” Kate asked sceptically. “Yes,” Melina interjected, coolly, “She did.” The older woman’s expression was unreadable, which gave Kate fair reason to worry. If Melina was totally cool with the idea that Yelena was about to prance around Sarajevo on the hunt for her biological mother, not ‘real mother’ just to make that clear, that was language that Kate stressed Yelena never use under any circumstances, Melina’s answer to Kate’s question would have been given with a small smile or a laissez-faire attitude, but no expression whatsoever meant something entirely different. No expression meant that Melina was pissed off to some degree, and that would mean that Yelena would be pissed off too. Wonderful. What a wonderful way to begin their romantic, fact-finding mission. Angry parents, complex feelings and to top it all off, it had been Kate’s idea to tell Melina in the first place.

    “You listened to me?” Kate asked, a little awkwardly as she shifted from foot to foot. Somehow, she had already managed to put her foot in it, without even putting her foot in it. That was some proper high quality Kate Bishop skill right there.

    “Yes, and although it is not your fault,” Yelena was quick to clarify and make sure they all understood where the blame lay, (hint: it was firmly with her parents), “I am starting to wish I had not,” she finished, with a sideways glance at her mother.

    “Do not listen to her,” Alexei told Kate as he took Yelena by the shoulder and pulled her into his side. The blonde frowned and pouted but didn’t pull away from the contact. After all, as much as she tried to convince you otherwise, Yelena Belova loved her father, deeply, and her stubborn resistance was as sweet as it was futile.

    “I try not to make a habit of it,” Kate joked. Humour. Humour was needed. “A wise move, Kate,” Melina said, shrewdly.

    “She is just upset that they did not serve kissel on the flight,” Alexei shrugged. As much as Yelena loved kissel, Kate highly doubted that this was an accurate summation. Although, sugar deprivation could certainly exacerbate Yelena’s poor mood.

    “That is not why I am upset,” she said as she folded her arms defiantly. “I am not even upset.” Her mother threw her the most sceptical look imaginable and Yelena threw her hands up defensively. “What? I am not.” No one believes that, babe.

    Melina sighed haughtily and shook her head. “You wanted a romantic week away with your girlfriend in Sarajevo, you wanted to do a little detective work, and eat and drink and do whatever you do,” the older woman waved her hand dismissively. Yelena’s jaw twitched with annoyance and a faint but undeniable blush rose on her cheeks. Kate swallowed. Either Melina was confused by woman-on-woman sex or knew exactly how much woman-on- woman sex they weren’t having. Wow, is it warm in here? Melina must have been really pissed to be so flippant about Yelena’s sex life, now that really was telling. “But it was never going to be as easy as that Yelena. So, stop frowning and be grateful your family are here to support you.” Yep. Pissed. And maybe a little bit right… or a lot right. Surely four heads were better than two, especially if those heads were well connected.

    “I never asked for your help,” Yelena frowned and huffed and puffed. Kate had created a monster, but she could see this from both sides. This was Yelena’s thing. It was her past, her journey, her missing connection and she wanted the freedom to explore that unburdened and selfishly. She’d had so much taken from her, hidden from her, and if she sought it out with her mother in tow, however well intentioned that mother was, could she really find the honest truth on her own terms without the worry of undermining or hurting the woman who ‘raised’ her? And for Melina, it was hard to relinquish that control, to let your daughter go out and potentially discover someone you worry could have greater claim over her, greater sway over her, someone your daughter could inexplicably love more than you. Especially finding out moments before her daughter was to leave, she’d had no time to come to terms with it, to rationalise it, and Yelena had no time to reassure her. Both were justified in their behaviour but both were also being really, annoyingly stubborn. Like mother, like daughter. The older woman turned to Kate and smiled warmly. “Come on dear,” she said, putting an arm around the young Avenger. “Alexei will take your bags, won’t you darling?” It wasn’t a question. The big man released his daughter a little too quickly and jumped to, easily relieving Kate of her heavy bags. Melina offered him a playful wink and he couldn’t keep the smirk from his face. Yelena visibly shuddered in disgust but followed her family, Fanny in tow.

    “Wait, wait, wait,” Kate said, suddenly, before they got too far from arrivals. “Can we get a picture? All of us together?” She knew it was a lame request but also, this was a pretty momentous occasion, despite the drama. She and Lucky were in Europe, with Yelena and Yelena’s parents and Fanny. A picture was a must. Not for the gram, but certainly for the memories.

    Melina beamed. “Of course, Alexei?”

    Again, in a crazy show of strength, the super soldier piled all of Kate’s bags under one arm, extracted his phone from his pocket and snapped a selfie in record time. It took a moment for Kate to realise that photo had been taken, she’d only just managed to smile, and of course, Yelena hadn’t even made it into the shot.

    “You have replaced me. Just like that,” Yelena huffed in exasperation. “It’s okay,” Melina called over her shoulder. “We will find you your other mother.” Stone. Cold. But it made sense. Don’t say how you really feel, don’t admit that you’re hurt or worried or feel insecure; just be passive aggressive about it.

    Kate tried to glance back at her girlfriend but found herself being forcibly removed from the airport, under Melina’s strong coercion. She heard Alexei’s quiet voice say, “Come on little one,” from behind her, and her heart felt warm and tight and happy. Yelena was such a daddy’s girl, in the most innocent and joyful way possible. The father and daughter duo came up alongside Kate and Melina, and a glum Yelena was already tucked, snuggly, back under her father’s arm. Alexei kissed his daughter gently atop her head and smiled into her beanie. “She will be mad for a little while but she will come round,” he said, quietly. “I am not mad,” Melina clarified, sharply, before she unlocked the car and gestured for Alexei to put Kate’s luggage into the trunk. Yelena made for the passenger seat but was very quickly demoted to the back with a single, withering look from her mother. “I feel like there’s more going on here than I realise. I just can’t put my finger on it.” Kate whispered to her girlfriend as she felt around for the seatbelt. For the life of her, she couldn’t find it, and Lucky being in the back with them really wasn’t helping. With a shake of the head, Yelena handed Kate her seatbelt, and then secured hers.

    “I will explain everything,” the blonde said, with a squeeze of Kate’s hand, “When we get a little privacy.” That final word was not for Kate. If Melina could be passive aggressive, so could Yelena. Kate was thankful in a way though. She would take passive aggressive warring Black Widows over active aggressive warring Black Widows any day of the week. “There is nothing to explain,” Melina piped up from the driver’s seat as she put the car into gear. Gears, yikes. Kate really was in Europe. “Yelena keeps secrets, Yelena is forced to tell secrets, Yelena has to face the consequences of said secrets. It is quite simple really.” Kate could see the older woman shrug matter-of-factly, and caught her eyes starring daggers at Yelena in the rear-view mirror. She really was quite formidable.

    Yelena ‘tsked’ and folded her arms. She threw herself back into her seat dramatically and let out an audible sigh. “Welcome to the family,” she grumbled.

    After a very quiet drive to the hotel, which mainly consisted of a lot of hand holding and dog patting, Kate, Yelena and her parents got checked in. Much to Yelena’s chagrin, the hotel wasn’t particularly busy, so the reception very helpfully managed to place Melina and Alexei right next door to them. Kate had thought it kind of cute at first, until she realised that it had been a couple of weeks since they’d done whatever it was that they did, as Melina put it, and then Kate did not find it cute. Kate did not find it cute at all.

    There would be a dog per room, which was probably the big advantage of having Yelena’s parents around. It meant that if Fanny or Lucky needed a cooling off period during their getting to know each other adventure, they could be afforded it, which was just better all round. It also meant Yelena’s parents got to spend a little more time with Fanny before she left for the USA, something that they greatly appreciated.

    Despite booking a double, their hotel room came with two twins, so the first thing the partners did was push the beds together. The second thing they did was decide to make out on them.

    “Ow!” Yelped Yelena dramatically. Kate had backed her into the bedside table. “Sorry. I’ve never been here before,” Kate shrugged nonchalantly, before she got back to relieving her girlfriend of her coat and her turtle neck. The beanie could stay though, the beanie could definitely stay; even if it meant that it had to come off and then go back on again.

    “Neither have I,” Yelena protested as she rubbed a sore spot on the back of her thigh. “But I can see with my eyes that there is a bedside table there.”

    “Poor thing. Does it hurt?” Kate teased.

    “No,” Yelena said, stubbornly, but she was pouting all the same.

    Kate gently took her girlfriend’s face in her hands and kissed her softly and chastely. “Maybe you should take a lie down. Just for a sec,” she whispered before she placed a hand square on Yelena’s chest and pushed. It was more forceful than Kate had anticipated and her own confidence took her by surprise. It must have taken her girlfriend by surprise too as Yelena ended up back flat on the bed. The blonde smirked and raised a challenging eyebrow. Kate had just raised the stakes, but was she bluffing? Absolutely not.

    The brunette crawled on top of her girlfriend and settled happily in her lap, knees either side of her hips, before she pressed their lips together once more. Everything deepened so quickly, from breathing to kisses to touches. God, Kate had missed Yelena so much.
