Her taste, her warmth, her touch; the steadying hand that framed her face, the fingers that got lost instantly in her hair, the tongue that moved lazily and longingly against her own. She’d missed her smiling against her kisses, she’d missed her adoring whisperings and words and she’d missed the sound of her breath catching when Kate surprised her with a new touch or sensation. She wanted to touch her all over, put Yelena’s skin against hers, put Yelena’s mouth against hers. She needed Yelena’s mouth on her skin, and being the most empathic self-proclaimed sociopath Kate had ever met, Yelena naturally acquiesced.

    It came at a price though. Within the blink of an eye Kate had conceded her position, she’d been weak, not that she was complaining. Yelena, beanie and all, placed tender kisses against the soft skin of her neck as Kate’s hands played just beneath the hemline of the blonde's small, white T-shirt and across the sensitive and ticklish skin of her ribs. Kate felt Yelena sigh happily at her touch and the blonde’s hot breath tickled pleasantly, the brunette couldn’t help but smile happily at the universe. Her girlfriend always took so much comfort in small, soft touches. Who knew Yelena Belova, badass ex-assassin could be undone with such a simple and loving caress? This girl did.

    Eventually, Kate had to accept that the beanie needed to go. She couldn’t effectively run her fingers through her girlfriend’s ridiculously lovely hair with the beanie there and so it was cast aside, along with most other items of clothing apart from tees and briefs and big socks, because it was cold as fuck. And because it was cold, they very sensibly worked their way to the top of the bed, pushed down the comforter with their feet (because why use hands?), slipped beneath it and then pulled it up tightly around them once more. There they settled into each other’s embrace, foreheads gently resting, noses grazing, eyes searching and smiles pulling at their lips.

    “Hi,” Kate whispered quietly.

    “Hi,” smiled Yelena.

    “I’ve missed you,” Kate said, as her arms tightened imperceptibly around the woman she loved.

    “I have missed you too,” Yelena murmured before she pulled her closer and placed another kiss against Kate’s very grateful lips. The blonde’s frowns and furrowed brows seemed to have melted away and had been replaced by soft eyes and gentle smiles and Kate was just a little bit proud of herself. Without really realising or meaning to, they’d become each other’s sanctuary over the last six months that they’d spent together. Comforting touches and embraces beneath the covers, simple moments with even simpler forms of communication. They were safe in these moments, safe from their positively outlandish lives, safe in their togetherness.

    Kate’s fingertips gently wandered up and over Yelena’s thighs, to the soft curve of her hip, to the soft cotton of her boxer briefs, where they rested and played absentmindedly. “I’ve missed this,” Kate said, softly.

    Yelena quirked a playful eyebrow. “My ass or this?” She asked as she pulled a little on Kate’s waist.

    “Both for sure. Both equally,” the brunette grinned which elicited a wide smile from the blonde.

    “I have missed this too. This quiet. Things feel quieter when I am with you,” Yelena explained earnestly, bringing her forehead back to rest against Kate’s. “Happy to be of service,” Kate said with another lingering kiss.

    “I love them, I do,” Yelena went on, “But life with them can be a little…” she searched for the right word. “Chaotic.”

    “Sounds like life with me,” the brunette shrugged, and it wasn’t a joke. She knew that she could be a little chaotic at the best of times, but chaotic good at least. “No no,” Yelena shook her head gently. “Life with you is balanced, when you know, we decide to effectively communicate,” she smiled a little self-deprecatingly. “You are strong when I am not, you can offer a smile when I cannot, you have humility when I cannot look past my pride. You turn to creativity when I am too practical or too stubborn to change. You are my foil.” For someone who wasn’t known to be particularly loquacious, sometimes, just sometimes, Yelena Belova came out with the most astounding and affecting things. Kate felt her heart tighten again in a wonderful way. This was the side of Yelena that only she saw, this was the side of Yelena that Kate would lay down her life for.

    “Always happy to be your foil if you promise to always be mine”. Kate knew that Yelena would make no such promise, not yet anyways, however much she wanted to. That didn’t stop Kate from prodding her though. It was irresponsible but irresistible, and Kate knew as long as she didn’t pressure, Yelena would smile and roll her eyes or do something as equally cute, so it was totally worth it. “Not foil of the aluminum variety, right?” Kate asked, keeping it light. See? She could do ‘no pressure’. It was just good to remind Yelena, every now and then, that Kate was in this for the long haul, just like they’d agreed. “No,” Yelena shook her head ever-so-slightly. “You are not light weight or durable.” Wait, hang on a second, had Yelena decided to do some prodding of her own?

    “Woah, woah now,” Kate said with a gasp. What was she implying?

    “But you are a good heat conductor,” Yelena continued, matter-of-factly, unphased by her girlfriend’s growing dismay.

    “What’s this about not being lightweight?”

    “Well, first off,” Yelena started, plainly, “You are currently lying with half your weight on top of me so I am open to you trying to change my mind on this.”

    “Just my legs.”

    “And secondly,” the blonde continued, “You are a superhero, you should not be light weight. You should be strong and dense and powerful.” Okay, in fairness to the Russian, that made more sense, and Kate was a little irritated that she hadn't thought of it herself. Of course, that’s what Yelena had meant. Yelena doesn’t work out to lift the most, or run the furthest or look the hottest, she worked out to be effective, and she was very effective. Kate’s brow furrowed questioningly. “I am, right? Strong and powerful?” “And dense, yes,” Yelena nodded, with a twinkle in her eye.

    The brunette gasped, open mouthed before giving her girlfriend a playful slap on the thigh. “You are such a little B!” All Yelena did was laugh, which only went to make the situation worse. “You are such a little B.”

    “And you are a little sensitive,” Yelena teased.

    “I have flown a long way,” Kate huffed, “I am very tired, and this is the treatment I get? Unbelievable.”

    “What kind of treatment were you hoping for?” Yelena asked, with a speculative eyebrow. “Well, you know,” Kate shrugged, “I’m a little stiff from the flight...” She stretched and moved against her girlfriend. Kate knew exactly what she was hoping for, as did Yelena. “You know I flew this morning too, right?” Yelena asked, knowing full well that she was being difficult, and knowing full well that Kate would take the bait, because of course she would.

    “Mine was longer,” Kate argued stubbornly, with a little frown. She knew that she looked cute, she would get what she wanted.

    “True,” Yelena said, with an appraising look. The blonde was very good at resisting, but she wouldn't win.

    “And it’s six am at home right now. What time is it in St Petersburg?” Kate added. The cheek to even suggest that they were the same level of tired. She was the more tired, she had proved it and she would get what she wanted. And just like that, she did. Yelena rolled her eyes and nudged Kate with her knee. “Fine you win. Get up.” Kate clapped a little clap in delight at her victory before she scrambled out from under covers and threw off her T-shirt. With a final check that the air-con was in fact turned to max heat, she rooted around in her bag for some body moisturiser that could sub for massage oil and chucked it at Yelena who deftly caught it. With a kiss to Lucky, who’d curled up at the foot of the bed, she jumped back onto their make-shift double and settled with her back to her girlfriend, who had propped herself up against the headboard.

    Yelena gently gathered Kate’s hair into a messy bun before getting started. She tried her best to warm the moisturiser in her hands, but Kate still shivered instinctually every time it graced her skin. Small kisses followed strong hands, as Yelena tried to make up for the angry red marks she was painting across Kate’s porcelain skin. Kate didn’t mind, however, as every touch eased a tension and every kiss teased a smile.

    “Your mom seems pretty upset,” Kate ventured, into the comfortable silence. Time for Kate to work some magic. If she didn’t, there was a good chance that tensions would be high for the rest of their trip. This was not what she wanted.

    “Yup,” came Yelena’s voice from behind her. This was going to take a little work. “Do you think it’s going to be like this all trip?”

    “She will calm down,” the blonde said, dismissively. Yelena sounded like her father, they really were alike.

    “Do you think it would help if you apologised?” It was a controversial suggestion, one that she knew wouldn’t go down well, but it was probably the right thing to do. “Why?” Yelena asked, a little disgruntled, as anticipated. “I have nothing to apologise for.” Kate raised a sceptical eyebrow and twisted her body to give her girlfriend the stare. “What? I don’t,” the blonde protested.

    “She thinks you weren’t going to tell her. She thinks you only told her because you were backed into a corner.” Even if that wasn’t true, that was Melina’s perception, and nothing was going to change that.

    “I was going to tell her I just…” Yelena sighed, “I did not know how so I put it off.” Of course, that’s what Yelena did; Kate knew all too well how avoidant her girlfriend could be. “Sounds oddly familiar,” she said, with a smirk.

    “I am not the only person who avoids awkward conversations for fear of hurting other people. Get off your high horse, Kate Bishop.” The brunette couldn’t help but laugh. Yelena’s words were provocative but her tone was light, even if her touch had got a tad rougher, but Kate was not complaining. No ma’am.

    “Well, then,” Kate said, as Yelena’s hands worked through some particularly stubborn knots in her neck causing her head to nod back and forth rhythmically. “Apologise and just say that. Exactly that. All you need to do is tell her the truth.”

    “The truth?” Yelena asked, as if ill-acquainted with the concept.

    “Yes, the truth. Tell her you were worried about hurting her and that you didn’t know how to tell her without doing that. Say that you know you messed up but you had always wanted her to know.”

    There was a silence as Yelena contemplated this suggestion. Her strong fingers worked up and down Kate’s neck and across her shoulders. It was weird to think that probably Kate Bishop, and only Kate Bishop had ever benefited from having Yelena Belova's hands around her neck. In fact, she was probably the only person who had ever lived to tell the tale. Was it weird that she wasn’t worried whenever they did this? Maybe. Was it weird that it only made her want Yelena’s hands around her neck more? Most certainly. Oh, no... what if murder is MY kink?

    “That kind of sounds like a lie,” Yelena cut through the silence and through Kate’s spiralling thoughts. “I did not want her to know, I just knew she probably had to, at some point.” Kate shrugged, as if it were obvious. “Okay well lie a little then.”

    “You are telling me to lie to my mother?”

    “Just a little. A tiny little lie.” That was fine right? A white lie to save someone’s feelings and make their romantic little European getaway infinitely more enjoyable was ethically sound, right?

    “Wow, Kate Bishop, I am telling Carol,” Yelena joked, and Kate knew that she was quickly trying to shift the focus of their conversation.

    “Just think about it, please?” Kate asked. She deserved this, they deserved this, this time away, and Melina deserved the comfort too.

    “Okay,” came Yelena’s less than enthusiastic response.

    “And whilst you’re thinking about it,” Kate turned suddenly with a mischievous smile and placed both hands upon Yelena’s shoulders. “Do you want to jump in the shower with me?” “Not really,” Yelena answered, disinterestedly.

    “Wow, rude.”

    “I would prefer to think about you and not my mother whilst we are naked,” Yelena countered with a wry smile. She had a point.

    “Oh, well that is more reasonable,” Kate agreed, as she flounced off the bed and grabbed a couple of the towels from the wardrobe. “So, is that a ‘yes’?” She asked as she turned back to Yelena with a raised eyebrow, “Because travelling makes me feel gross.” “That is a yes because you are gross,” the blonde grinned.

    “Harsh,” Kate pouted.

    “But true!” Yelena shot back as she hopped off the bed and captured Kate within her arms. She drew her in and peppered kisses along her collar bone. Yelena’s hot breath tickled and Kate found herself giggling like an idiot. She was quite unsure whether they’d ever been this giddy together. Breath tickled the soft skin of her neck, just below her ear. “I am going to wash you so hard,” Yelena teased and Kate was caught between finding the proposition completely hilarious, which it was, and finding it a complete and utter turn on, which it also was. And she was seventy-five percent convinced that Yelena knew exactly what she was doing, and what she was doing, was taking the piss.

    Kate simply laughed a cursory, “Ha ha,” before she shrugged off Yelena’s embrace, as well as what was left of her own clothes, and made her way into the bathroom.

    She switched on the water and quickly retracted her hand, as the cold water flew from the shower head. Always, always so cold. It was the price one had to pay for a hot shower. Once the water had warmed, Kate stepped under a steady stream of glorious, life giving, soul cleansing hot water, just as Yelena shuffled into the bathroom with a few toiletries in hand. She looked down at her bounty and then up at Kate, smiling gleefully.

    “You are going to be so clean.”

    “You’re right, I do feel particularly clean,” Kate said as she pulled on an oversized sweater. It was fresh out of her bag and still smelled like their laundry. “And maybe a little dirty,” she grinned as she flopped down into the overstuffed hotel room chair. Just like that, the trip to Sarajevo had been worth it, for pretty much the best shower she’d ever experienced. They’d laughed, they’d kissed, they’d got clean, she’d got off. She was putting that shit on Trip Advisor, ten out of ten would do again.

    “That was all on your own volition, not mine,” Yelena pointed out with a small, bemused smile as she strapped a small combat knife to her ankle.

    “Are you taking a knife to lunch?” Kate asked casually as she grabbed her phone and began to take random photos of a sleeping Lucky who was still flat out at the end of their bed. “Yes,” she nodded matter-of-factly.

    “Is that for your mom or…?”

    “Ha. Very funny,” Yelena said, as she pulled down her jeans to conceal the weapon. “It’s just lunch though, right?” Did Yelena need weapons at lunch? Kate worried that this was a stupid question.

    “You know I like to have at least one weapon on me at all times,” Yelena reasoned, and yes, it was true, Kate did know that.

    “But at lunch though?” And with four highly trained ass-kickers?

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded, as if it were obvious.

    Kate frowned. Something didn’t add up. Yes, she knew Yelena liked to carry weapons, her bracelets were weapons for god’s sakes, but a knife strapped to her ankle? That was a mid- fight type of weapon. That’s not just a ‘I’ll have this on me just in case’ weapon. That’s a considered weapon of choice, and Kate didn’t like it. “Is there something you’re not telling me?”

    “No,” Yelena said plainly, her mouth a little downturned.

    Kate raised an extremely unconvinced eyebrow and fix her girlfriend with the most searing of disapproving stares. Yelena’s eyes narrowed and began to scowl with displeasure, she was about to renege on her answer and she hated herself for it. She hated that she was so weak when it came to Kate Bishop.

    “Yes,” the blonde said through gritted teeth.

    “Spill,” Kate instructed as she gestured towards the other overstuffed chair that was sat next to hers.

    Yelena sighed and reluctantly sunk into the chair. There was a pause, then another sigh and then an explanation. “I may have assassinated a leading member of the Serbian Mafia here....”

    WHAT? “What?” Why hadn’t she mentioned this earlier?

    “It is fine,” Yelena waved it off dismissively, “And totally nothing to worry about.” “You’re not worried? That’s not why you’re strapping a knife to your leg?” Kate asked in disbelief.

    “Kate, if you think this knife is the only weapon I have strapped in places, then you are clearly not as handsy as I thought you were.”

    “You’re avoiding the question.”

    “Darling,” Yelena leaned forward, captured her hand and began to brush her thumb soothingly across Kate’s knuckles. “I am not worried. I am simply being prepared.” “Prepared for what? Would they recognise you here?” Kate asked. How was this something that hadn’t been mentioned? Sure, Yelena’s sense of danger was completely out of whack in comparison to most other people’s, but surely she had been aware of the risk. She’d strapped a knife to her ankle for pity’s sake.

    “Oh, for sure,” Yelena nodded enthusiastically, “I am kind of a big deal.” Forever modest this one.

    “Why didn’t you tell me this before?” Kate asked. She felt as if she were losing her mind, or at least a few marbles.

    “Well, I do not like to brag,” Yelena teased with a grin, which earned her a glare from Kate. The blonde sighed and an over-confident grin was replaced with a more earnest smile. The blonde squeezed Kate’s hand reassuringly. “Because it is nothing to worry about.” “Nothing to worry about?” Kate was finding it hard to take Yelena’s word for it. Killing a mafia boss and then not expecting any dire repercussion seemed like absolute crazy talk, even for her girlfriend.

    “No. The guy now in charge,” Yelena explained, “He is the one who hired me for the hit.” Well, that made a little more sense but didn’t do a huge amount to reassure the brunette. “Oh, so totally trustworthy then.”

    “Oh, totally,” the blonde nodded with a smile, “Hence the weapons.”

    “I… “ Kate shook her head, a little lost for words, “Sometimes I just despair.” Yelena could only smile widely. She was finding Kate’s histrionics endearing but that had never been Kate’s aim. Kate had meant for them to be taken seriously. The ex-assassin pressed a soft kiss against her knuckles. “Are you ready to go?” She asked. “Sure,” Kate sighed in frustration. Was there any point fighting this? No. Were they going to lunch? Yes. With weapons? Also, yes. Would shit hit the fan? Maybe. Would the four of them be able to handle whatever the criminal underground of Sarajevo threw at them? Most certainly.

    “Good,” Yelena smiled happily. It was going to be their first lunch as a family. Their first outing, and Kate could tell that despite the tensions and the fights, Yelena was just a little bit excited to be sharing it with her. “It is going to be a nice chilled lunch. We will eat some great food, have some nice pastry, I will get them to make me a kissel,” she said with a grin as she jumped to her feet and pulled Kate with her.

    “Please ask nicely.”

    “And,” Yelena continued, clearly happy to ignore Kate as and when it suited her, “I will speak to my mother now so that we can all have a nice time when we get there. No arguments.” Turned out she didn’t need Kate’s input at all, as that actually sounded quite sensible.

    “Yes, please do that,” Kate said as she grabbed the key-card and followed Yelena out into the corridor with Lucky in tow. “Because I am desperately trying to make a good impression and you’re kind of cramping my style,” she explained unapologetically as the blonde called the elevator.

    “I will meet you and Lucky downstairs in the foyer, okay?” Yelena said before she scanned the corridor, ensured all was quiet, and then leaned in for a lingering kiss. Kate was being silenced but she didn’t mind too much, not if it meant kisses like that. The elevator pinged and the couple broke apart, just in case the elevator had a passenger. To their relief the doors to an empty elevator slid open and Kate slipped inside.

    “You are going to apologise, right, Yelena?” She asked, as she pressed the button marked ‘Reception’.

    “Oh, absolutely,” her girlfriend reassured her, with the least reassuring smile she’d ever bore witness to. Yelena’s eyes somehow dance in the lights of the dimly lit corridor. At least she was having fun now.

    “Yelena?” Kate asked, her tone a little higher than it had been moments before. The doors to the elevator slide shut. “Yelena?” Damn it.

    Much to Kate’s delight, lunch was just that, delightful. No mobsters had crashed their party, no ghosts of mafia bosses gone by had ruined their pastries, no family arguments had soured their coffees; everything had been pretty much perfect. Lucky and Fanny had gotten along so well, they were such good dogs. Alexei had regaled them with ridiculous tale of battles from before their time. Yelena had rolled her eyes and chided him, but had smiled and laughed and secretly hoped that there was truth in his words. Melina had told stories of Yelena as a child, and Yelena had blushed and told her mom to stop and sulked but grinned stupidly whenever Kate’s eyes fell upon her, or whenever Kate’s hand gently squeezed her thigh underneath the table.

    Kate had discovered that Alexei could practically eat and drink his own body weight, and they’d discussed the possibility of him becoming a competitive eater. He’d loved the idea of course, as it was a great idea, but Melina had thought it might bring too much attention to the family. They were a household that liked to keep a low profile. Alexei had been understandably disappointed but they’d still decided that it might be a cool idea to set up a Red Guardian Instagram account so that he could reach out to his modest fanbase and set some records straight.

    After two courses of mezes and then meats, Kate was certifiably stuffed, much like the dolmas she'd gorged herself on. The bill had been asked for and Melina and Yelena were having their first argument of the afternoon, over who would pay it. A stupid argument really as Kate would be paying. She was one of New York City’s most eligible lady bachelors, remember?

    Whilst the two were distracted, she thought it the perfect time to unlock her phone, open Pokémon, spin the Pokéstop that was in fact the restaurant they were sat in, and scan the local area for any geo-locked Pokémon that she couldn’t catch in North America. Much to her chagrin, there were none in sight. I’ll get you Zangoose, even if you are an ugly son of a bitch.

    “Of course,” came Yelena’s pained voice. Kate quickly snapped her phone shut and looked up. Busted.

    “I told you,” said Melina, admonishingly. Oh shit, not Melina’s disapproval too. “I’m sorry,” Kate said before realising that she had not in fact been busted, the two Black Widows weren’t even looking in her direction. “What?” She asked, just a little confused. Was everything okay?

    Yelena was sat with the bill between her fingers and a troubled brow. She passed the small slip of paper to Kate who scanned it with a frown. What was she supposed to be looking for? "It has been paid for,” Yelena explained. Wow, already paid for? Who would have done that? Not that Kate wasn’t grateful. She knew she’d been intending to foot the bill but damn could Alexei eat. Would you look at that total?

    “I knew we were being watched,” muttered Melina, her eyes narrowed and her lip twitched. “When the Red Guardian walks into your restaurant you notice,” Alexei boomed and Yelena practically groaned in exasperation.

    “Yes, I felt it from the moment we walked in,” The younger Black Widow agreed with her mother. Thank goodness they were back on the same page. Never doubt the power of a simple ‘I’m sorry’. The blonde shook her head in frustration. “I thought this place was clean.” Her eyes began to scan the room in search of any suspicious sets of wandering eyes, but she found none.

    “Things change quickly around here,” Melina shrugged, “You know that.” So, Melina knew about the assassination too, good to be the last one in the loop.

    Yelena weighed up her mother’s words and nodded in reluctant agreement. “So much for a nice quiet meal.”

    “There is no such thing when you are with a celebrity,” Alexei quipped with a grin. At this point, Kate was almost convinced that Alexei played the fool to lighten the mood. There was no way someone could be so... well, dense, was there?

    Yelena couldn’t hold the eye-roll back; it was like a reflex when it came to her father, an unstoppable impulse. “They have never heard of you Papa. This is not the Motherland.” He frowned. His bottom lip shot out and his chin crinkled. “Why do you hurt my feelings this way?”

    “Why do you say stupid things?” Yelena’s voice went up a few decibels, or ten. She was practically out of her chair. Her nice lunch, the first meal her family and girlfriend had ever shared had gone from pretty much perfect to creepy and potentially dangerous within the space of a few seconds. They were being watched and it had already crept under Yelena’s skin. Normally it was Yelena who did the watching, it was never a good idea to give her a taste of her own medicine. The blonde found it particularly bitter.

    “Now, now children,” Melina warned, tersely.

    “She started it,” Alexei pointed in Yelena’s direction, doing absolutely nothing to help his case. “Showing me no respect.”

    Yelena simply shrugged. “Okay.”

    “I will have you know the Red Guardian was a hero to all the Yugoslav people.” “Whatever you say papa,” the blonde said, disinterestedly. Yelena had clearly chosen the high road. The one signposted ‘I don’t give a fuck’.

    “Darling,” Melina placed a gentle hand upon Alexei’s arm, as if she was about to deliver some painful home truths. “Half the people in this room weren’t alive before the Balkan Wars.” The big man’s brow crinkled in confusion, as if a time without the Red Guardian was a time beyond comprehension.

    “It is true,” Yelena nodded, serious as anything. “You are old, Papa,” she deadpanned, but Kate knew she took a huge amount of pleasure delivering those words. This family had some weird dynamics, but then again, what family didn’t?

    Alexei’s confused frown turned into an obtuse scowl as he grinned mischievously. “Who did pay for our meal then, your sugar daddy?” He asked, throwing in some air quotes to really emphasise those last two words. Kate couldn’t help but laugh, because he meant her. He was calling Kate a Sugar Daddy and Yelena hated it. He’d really struck a chord. The blonde's jaw was fixed and ticked, her little hands balled into little fists and then flexed. Oh, she hated it so much. So much for the road named ‘I don’t give a fuck’.

    “No, Kate did not pay for this,” the blonde bit back at her father, as she tried her absolute hardest to appear completely and utterly un-phased, “And Kate is not my sugar daddy, although...” Yelena took a steadying breath and flicked her eyes to Kate. The blonde offered her a small smile. “She does pay for more things than I would like.” Noted. Kate was an instinctual payer, it was just something she did without thinking, something she was used to. She wanted it? She’d buy it. It needed paying for, she’d tap it. Now she’d made a mental note to rein it in. Kate smiled back at her girlfriend and nodded ever-so-slightly to let her know she'd heard her. Wow, they were getting good at this mature communication thing. “So, if the bank of Kate Bishop did not pay for our meal, then who did?” Asked Alexei, and at that point, Kate really did kind of want to know too.

    Yelena glanced once and then twice around the room, to ensure they didn’t have any obvious overlookers. Once she was satisfied, she took the bill from Kate’s hands and handed it to her father. “Benny Lecić,” she explained, quietly.

    Alexei frowned, but other than that, his face was unreadable. “How do you know that?” "Look at the bill. I don’t speak Bosnian but I can read that,” Yelena explained, plainly. His frown grew darker. “It says ‘With love’?” There was a pause and then a moment of clarity, where realisation spread across Alexei’s face. Suddenly he was grinning. “Oh! Oh, that guy? You killed his partner.”

    “You wanna shout it any louder or...?”

    “When was it?” Alexei thought to himself, “Two thousand and seventeen?” “I mean, he paid me to so I do not think he minded that much but-”

    “Oh no he did not mind. At all.” Alexei clarified, taking another sip of his third coffee. “With love?” Kate asked. That seemed a little odd coming from a mafia boss, but she guessed it was fittingly vague and aloof. It certainly said the whole ‘I know you’re in my city and I’m watching you attentively thing’. Kate seriously hoped it wasn’t a crappy James Bond reference because if it was, someone needed to tell that guy that it really didn’t work. Yelena had been the one to fly from Russia with love, and not the other way round. Idiot. “He likes Yelena very much,” Alexei said with a grin and a wink over the top of his coffee. Wait, what? This was new information. So, Yelena had brought them to a city where she had killed a mob boss, which was a hit ordered by the mob boss who succeeded him, who ‘liked her very much’. That sounded like bullshit. Yelena, tell me it’s bullshit. “That is bullshit,” she said with complete and utter disdain. I love you so much. “Benny and I have a professional relationship and Benny is old.”

    “You are old,” Alexei teased, and Kate had to admit, he had a point. If it hadn’t been for the blip, Yelena would have been more than a decade older than her girlfriend, which made Yelena practically ancient, or something even worse; a millennial.

    “No, he is antiquated old. Like Red Guardian old,” Yelena retorted with a smirk. Her jibe landed.

    “Would that make me antiquated too, darling?” Melina asked her daughter sweetly. Her jibe backfired.

    “Benny Lecić is a thug and nothing more.” Yelena had clearly decided that for her own safety, her mother’s question was better left unanswered, but Melina’s sweet smile never left her face.

    “Benny Lecić is a very powerful man,” the veteran Black Widow countered calmly, “With a temper and a lot of names in his ledger.” Her smile was soft but her eyes were dark and sharp and full of warning. Kate did not like this. Kate did not like this at all. As much as Yelena reassured her, and as much as she wanted to believe her girlfriend’s reassurances, Kate couldn’t help but take Melina’s warning to heart.

    “Well,” Yelena said as she got to her feet and threw on her yellow winter coat defiantly, “If he decides to pick a fight, he has met his match in me.”

    “That,” Melina nodded warily, “Is exactly what I am afraid of.”

    The snow had started to fall again once they’d separated from Melina and Alexei. Melina had told them to be careful, and Yelena had reassured her mother that they would be. Despite all the back and forth in the restaurant Kate wasn’t surprised to see them now hug and kiss warmly and enthusiastically. That was the kind of family they were. Melina had given her daughter’s hand one final squeeze before they’d parted ways, and with a final wave and a final ‘be careful’, Yelena and Kate set out on their exploration of Sarajevo. They walked and talked and laughed, and Fanny and Lucky walked happily alongside them. Kate was so happy to see that their two fluffers were getting on so well, it would have been a bit of a disaster if they hadn’t been.

    The city itself was stunning, especially in the snow. Yelena had told her that it was one of those pretty, magical places where cultures came together, and Sarajevo was certainly a city of East meets West. Turn down one street and you’d find yourself in some grand square of buildings with colourful facades that exemplified the height of Austro-Hungarian architecture. You’d turn down the next street and be met by the winter hustle and bustle of the bazaar, with small coffee places and vendors selling freshly roasted chestnuts. They smelled amazing by the way. It was also a city where the stark reminders of its recent history were never far from the surface. Some buildings still wore battle scars, streets had been renamed in commemoration, and memorials and tributes to those who had been lost could be found on every other corner.

    As the wind whipped up and the day grew colder, the pair linked arms and huddled together, and no one blinked an eye. Yelena smiled up at Kate happily. It was that smile, that smile that was new, or had been. Perhaps it would always feel new. It still managed to send Kate’s stomach into outer space whenever she saw it. Kate kind of hoped that feeling never left. She certainly didn’t think she would ever tire of seeing Yelena smile like that. They trudged up quieter cobbled streets where snow had settled. They shrieked and laughed as the younger and lankier of the two took a tumble, but of course, the shorter woman was there to catch her. They kissed softly atop a deserted Yellow Fortress that overlooked the city and checked the dogs’ paws to make sure they were still doing okay in the cold before they began their decent back down towards Baščaršija in the Ottoman Old Town. “This city is beautiful,” Kate said, as she sipped her thick, dark coffee. It was like no coffee she’d ever really experienced. It was gritty and earthy and a little odd, but she was certainly getting a taste for them, and quick. Although that didn’t come as a surprise considering how much caffeine was in them.

    Yelena ‘hmmed’ thoughtfully, her eyes glazed as they roamed the street outside. Stalls were closing as the night was gradually drawing in and the snow was growing heavier. “Especially in the snow,” Kate added, hoping to drag her girlfriend’s eyes away from the street vendors. Yelena seemed distracted, as if something was weighing on her. She glanced momentarily at her watch and then back out, towards the lights of the stalls, and the fountain at the centre of the Ottoman style square.

    “Do you think this could be your home?” Kate asked.

    There was a moment’s silence as Yelena brought her coffee to her lips and sipped. After a moment more she nodded solemnly. “Yes, I do,” she said, quietly, never taking her eyes from the square. Kate wished that she could take Yelena’s hands in hers, take her lips with hers. “It’s sunset,” Yelena spoke, suddenly.

    “Already?” Kate frowned. “Wow, I knew it was getting late, but I didn’t realise it was that late.”

    “The muezzin will start soon,” Yelena mused and Kate frowned in confusion. “The what?”

    The blonde placed her coffee cup back onto its saucer and their eyes met. Yelena’s eyes were unreadable, but at the same time, completely at sea. “The call to prayer. From the mosques,” she explained.

    “Oh, I’ve never heard it in person,” Kate said, and it was true. There probably weren’t that many Americans who had. Sadly, most people’s experience of a Muslim call to prayer probably came from watching Claire Danes run around a fake and washed-out Afghanistan in Homeland.

    “It is very beautiful,” Yelena smiled softly. It wasn’t often that Yelena denoted beauty to anything, or anyone other than Kate. She put a high value on true beauty and so her comment was quite wonderfully revealing. Kate loved finding out these little parts of Yelena. The small, unassuming, hidden parts of her, that completely defied your expectations. She was complex and challenging and Kate was so extremely grateful that Yelena was a discovery that was just hers for the making. “It is one of the few things I remember,” Yelena said, quietly.

    Their eyes met once more. The blonde’s were still at sea but didn’t lack conviction. “That you remember?” The words had left her mouth faster than she’d even managed to think them. What a dumb thing to say, of course that’s what she meant. What you were supposed to say was, ‘thank you so much for sharing that with me, I think I fall even further in love with you the further you let me in’.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded, but she seemed apprehensive. About what? Kate didn’t know. “At least I think it is,” the blonde said, and then paused for a moment. She was weighing something up in her mind, finding the right words, finding the right amount of courage. Instinctually Kate’s hand found her girlfriend’s. Yelena didn’t pull away, it seemed as if it was the contact that she needed. “I have a dream,” Yelena spoke quietly as Kate’s fingers intertwined with hers. “A recurring one”. Yelena sniffed a little and then swallowed. She gave herself a moment. Kate offered her a warm smile and Yelena sent a half smile back. It was laced with sadness. “When I hear the muezzin, I know the dream is nearly over.” Kate swallowed the small lump in her throat. “That sounds a little bittersweet.” “It is,” Yelena nodded with a sigh just as the scratch and crackle of a loud speaker coming to life echoed around the square. A melodic, amplified voice rose through the Old Town, and cut through the sounds of life that still surrounded them. The man’s voice was euphonious as it wavered with untamed vibrato and soared emotively across the rooftops and out into the city. The sound was enchanting, and somehow resonated inside of Kate. Despite being in a language she didn’t understand, pertaining to a religion she didn’t practice, it moved her. “You’re right,” Kate said, reflectively, “It is beautiful.” Yelena smiled and then nodded to the other side of the square, to the place her eyes had been unable to tear themselves away from just moments earlier.

    “The address is just round the corner.”

    Kate frowned. The address? Were they going there now? Was that why they’d gone there, to that square? The brunette suddenly had a lot of questions, very few of which she should have been bombarding her girlfriend with, so she chose just one.

    “Do you think this address could be... you know... your home?” Kate asked, a little sheepishly.

    Yelena shrugged and sighed. “I do not know. I doubt it. The guy who gave me the tip told me he picked up three girls from an apartment here in nineteen-ninety-two. One of them fit my description,” she took a final sip of her coffee and screwed up her face a little at the bitterness of the final dregs and the grittiness of the sediment. “I found him sheltering an ex-widow.” That made sense, and perhaps if someone still lived at this address, someone who had living memory of Yelena or any girls being there, they might be able to tell them how the girls got there in the first place. “So, you think this might be where they kept you?” Asked Kate, as her thumb still worked gently across Yelena’s knuckles.

    The blonde met her eyes and shrugged with a small, rueful smile. “For a while perhaps. But there is only one way to find out.”

    They left money for the coffees and then some, tucked under the decorative saucers, before they braced themselves for the cold, and ventured back out in the Sarajevo’s wintery streets. Arm in arm, with their dogs at their sides, they made the short walk from the café to the address marked on Yelena’s phone. Handily, as Yelena had been given the code for the building, she didn’t need to do any fancy espionage and the two Avengers were very happy to bundle in and escape the cold once more.

    Once inside, Kate could see Yelena’s eyes searching. Searching for what, she didn’t know. Her eyes roamed the walls and the doors, maybe looking for something familiar, something that would trigger a thought or spark a memory. From the frown and the look of consternation on Yelena’s face Kate was willing to bet that the corridor was triggering very little for her girlfriend, but as they both knew, Yelena was old, and a lot could have changed in thirty plus years.

    The pair took the steps to the third floor as Yelena mumbled something about old buildings with even older elevators. As they walked down the corridor to apartment twelve, Yelena’s fingertips played across the walls, as if she was feeling her way. Her eyes flicked to the overhead lighting, and then to the door at the end of the hall. She was quiet, which was to be expected given the circumstances, but her mind wasn’t. Her mind wasn’t quiet at all, for Kate could hear it.

    “You ready?” Kate asked as a hopeful smile pulled at the corner of her mouth. Yelena swallowed but nodded resolutely. The blonde looked up into her eyes and Kate’s heart broke in that moment, in the most wonderful way, for she found such hope and trepidation and fear and thankfulness. All these things that Yelena couldn’t vocalise, that she didn’t know how to vocalise, but Kate could see. She could see them all as Yelena’s eyes danced brightly in the harsh, artificial light of the corridor.

    “Good,” Kate whispered after a moment lost in hazel. “Can I tell you something?” she asked. “Yes,” Yelena said, quietly.

    “You’re the strongest person I know,” Kate said sincerely, and it was the truth. To have the strength to overcome the subjugation and to not run, to not turn her back on those that were like her when it would have been so easy to escape that life. To have the strength to continue after Natasha, to have the strength to show restraint and mercy with Clint when all she felt was grief and anger. To have the strength to seek the truth about her past when she knew that the answers she might be faced with could cause more hurt than never knowing at all. Yelena smiled a small, heartfelt smile and Kate couldn’t help but smile back as a look of love pulled at the corner of her mouth.

    There they both stood, just for moment longer, lost in each other’s eyes. Kate wanted to savour the moment, to savour the hope in Yelena’s eyes, to capture the beauty and optimism in her smile and lock it away within the vaults of her mind, because they were about to jump from the precipice. One knock on the door that stood in front of them and Yelena’s world could come crumbling down. But with that one knock could come answers, and answers were what they came for. Answers were what Yelena needed and deserved, and so together, they knocked.

    Metamorphosis: Three Chapter Notes This is a journey. I’m sorry. But stick with it and it’ll all be worth it. I’m not going to do you like I did at Christmas.

    As always, thank you for reading and commenting etc. I do love our chats. Thank you Kristin!

    Yelena paced back and forth at the end of the bed. She chewed the inside of her lip as her hands rested on her hips.

    “She is being silenced,” she said grimly as a cross-legged Kate grabbed another slice of her pizza from her spot on the bed.

    “She could just be scared,” the brunette offered, “You did say you were kind of a big deal, what if she’s heard of you? I’d be scared too if an infamous assassin walked into my apartment and started questioning me about missing kids.” It was a logical argument which normally Yelena would be in support of, however, Yelena was not in the mood for logic or reason. Yelena was frustrated.

    “Not if it were me.” It was a stupid argument and she knew it, but she made it anyway. She knew quick and simple answers were never going to be easy to come by, that didn’t mean that not getting them quickly and easily was easy to stomach.

    “No, but I’ve seen you day drunk trying to steal Pokémon plushies from Build-A-Bear, she just thinks you murder people,” Kate explained as Melina rolled her eyes fondly and Alexei grinned from the overstuffed chairs opposite the bed whilst devouring his pizza whole. “That plushie was for you. Don’t complain, you love Squirty.”

    “Squirtle. It’s Squirtle.” Kate’s eyes flicked nervously to Yelena’s parents and back again. The blonde couldn’t keep the knowing smirk from her face. She liked to tease Kate about her Pokémon and she was learning that she really liked to make Kate squirm in front of her parents; it was certainly a way to appease some of her frustrations. “Please don’t ever say that word again?” Kate asked, a little too desperately.

    “Well, who would you be more afraid of? Me or the Mafia?”

    “That is a question that I am not even going to think about going near,” Kate said before she tore off a slice of greasy pizza and fed it to Lucky. Yelena was scary right? She could kill someone with a paper clip, that had to count for something.

    “Yelena, you don’t know it is Benny,” Melina chipped in as she sipped at her Coke Zero. Of course it was Benny, who else would it have been? Who else had that influence? Who else scared the city shitless?

    “When pushed, she said that men would bring girls to the apartment. She said that there was a woman there who they were in contact with, who would look after the girls. This is human trafficking, this is what they do. This is what half of them are in prison for, mama,” Yelena argued and there was no way she could be wrong. Human trafficking was the Mafia’s life blood, and it was rife during the early Nineties, right about the time Yelena would have been taken from her parents.

    Melina paused for a moment as she considered her response. “Darling, I just think that you should think very carefully about involving Benny Lacić. You are safe in this city because of him and the power that he holds.”

    Yelena frowned and continued to pace. Her mother was correct, to an extent. Killing a mob boss normally put a target on your back, but of course, when the guy who hired you to do it in a grab for power ends up being the new mob boss, you’re afforded a little reprieve. However, the thing that would keep Yelena and safe in Sarajevo wasn’t her association with Benny, it was the fact that they were highly skilled fighters. She had no doubt. “You are safe in this city as long as I am here, little one,” Alexei smiled happily as he fed Fanny a little pizza crust and ruffled her ears affectionately. He was going to miss that dog. “Thank you, Papa,” Yelena nodded earnestly. “I know.” They both exchanged small little smiles. Having a super soldier on your side was certainly a benefit but having a super soldier with no sense of subtlety on your side could almost certainly be a hindrance. Melina’s hand closed around Yelena’s wrist, bringing her pacing to a sudden halt. With a small tug and a gentle touch she demanded her daughter’s eyes. Yelena gave in. “I am just worried about you,” Melina said gently.

    Yelena’s shoulders relaxed a little as she sighed. “I know, I know,” she said as she pulled her wrist from Melina’s grasp and replaced it with her hands. She squeezed gently. Her mother was experienced and she trusted no one, apart from more recently her family. It had got her this far in life and she wasn’t about to change. If her instinct was telling her that Yelena should be cautious, her instinct was probably right, but now was not the time for caution, now was the time for answers, and in actuality, when had Yelena ever taken a cautious approach?

    “I want this for you darling, I do.” Melina reciprocated Yelena’s squeeze of the hand in order to emphasise her point. “But is it worth your life? Or the life of the people you love?” The blonde’s eyes shifted to Kate who had managed to choke on her pizza at Melina’s words and then back to her mother with a look that said, what the hell are you thinking? “It really is not that big a deal mother,” Yelena shrugged, in an attempt to keep things casual. Because love was casual. Casual love. Not that kind of casual love but you know, generic love that didn’t refer to any particular person but just friends in general. Friends and girlfriends and family. That kind of non-binding, chilled, no-pressure love. “I am sure we can work something out with Benny that keeps everyone safe. And besides, we’re all pretty capable.”

    “I am incredibly capable, thank you very much,” Kate piped up from the bed as she tackled another slice of pizza after having cleared her airways. “You’ve taught me pretty well and let’s face it, I wasn’t too bad to begin with.” She was right, but Yelena would not give her the satisfaction. The blonde raised a sceptical eyebrow and her girlfriend rolled her eyes. Their relationship was pretty perfect. How had she managed to get it so good? “I think you should speak to him,” Kate said, with a mouth full of dough, cheese, and processed meat. “Calmly,” she made sure to clarify, with a twinkle in her eye, “And ask for his help.” Was Kate suggesting that Yelena had a temper? Surely not.

    Melina's brow was furrowed in consternation. She didn’t like that plan, even if it was one that erred on the side of caution. “You would be in his debt. And that’s not to say that he would even tell you the truth.”

    “Well, do we have any better leads?” Kate asked, forgetting herself slightly. She wasn’t in the Avenger’s war room, she was in a hotel room with Melina Vostokoff.

    “What is she going to do?” Yelena’s mother asked, setting Kate in her sights, “Walk in there and charm him into giving her the information?” To her credit, Kate didn’t blink. “No,” the younger brunette smiled sweetly, “That’s my job.” Melina was overcome. She could only smile back affectionately. What had Kate Bishop done to her? How had she been so sassed and yet been so happy to take it. How had she not bitten back? Kate needed to teach Yelena her secrets. Although Yelena had a sneaking suspicion that it had something to do with the fact that Kate was not Melina’s searingly sarcastic daughter, and of course Kate Bishop was also a ray of fucking sunshine. A ray of fucking sunshine that was going nowhere near Benny Lacić.

    “One, I can be very charming when I want to be,” Yelena retorted. These were facts. “And two, absolutely not. You are not going. He is not going to see your face. He is not going to know your name. He is not going to know who you are to me. Do you understand?” “But-”

    “I have to agree with Yelena on this one,” came her mother’s voice. It was about time they agreed on something. They hadn’t even agreed on pizza toppings that evening. At least they could agree that Kate Bishop was worth protecting. “I know you came here to support your girlfriend, and Kate darling, I think you are very talented and very beautiful and are far too good for this idiot that I raised-”

    “Ha, raised. Whatever,” Yelena rolled her eyes.

    “But for all these reasons,” Melina continued, ignoring Yelena, which tended to be standard practice, “Tomorrow morning, you will be staying in this hotel room with Alexei.” The look on Kate’s face told both Black Widows that she was not best pleased; both had very little sympathy for her. “Yelena and I will go,” the blonde’s mother met her eyes and the two nodded in agreement. “You two can take photos of the dogs for the Instagrams.” “But I’m more useful than that,” Kate reasoned. She didn’t whine, she didn’t pout; she simply wanted to be taken seriously and usually, Yelena was the first person to advocate for her, but that night, it just wasn’t happening. There was no way.

    “No buts,” Melina retorted with a wave of her finger. “I am the mother here. Do you know the first thing the Mafia will do if you piss them off?” The older Widow asked as she leaned forward in her seat.

    Kate shifted uncomfortably on the bed next to Lucky. “I’m going to pretend I didn’t just watch John Wick.”

    “Hurt the people you care about,” Melina said, coolly. It was clear to Yelena that her mother had never watched John Wick. Probably for the best really. She’d enjoy the action but would be left reeling by the inaccuracies. “You are too much of a precious commodity,” Melina continued. “Thankfully, Yelena and I hold nothing but contempt for each other.” “Total contempt,” Yelena nodded to her mother, straight-faced, “In fact, I hate you.” Melina threw her daughter a saccharine smile. “I hate you more.” Of course, everything was a competition.

    “I love you both,” said Alexei, uncharacteristically softly.

    “We know Papa,” Yelena grinned at her loveably idiotic father as she sat down on the bed next her girlfriend and gave her a consoling pat on the knee. She knew Kate would be dying to go with her to see Benny, she knew she wanted to be with her every step of the way, but there was always going to be parts of this journey that Yelena would have to do alone. This was one of them, even if Melina had decided to tag along.

    “I kind of love you all,” Kate mumbled into her soda, as she took a long, loud sip on her straw. Yelena wrapped her arm around Kate and rolled her eyes affectionately. “I know darling, I know,” she soothed, sounding a little too much like her mother for her own liking. “That is why you are such a precious commodity,” she added teasingly as she made a grab for a slice of Kate’s pizza. Her searching hand got what it deserved, a swift slap away. “You said you didn’t want any pizza,” Kate reminded her girlfriend, stern faced. “What if I asked nicely?” Yelena asked and smiled sweetly. She knew she was irresistible. Even when Kate was pissed off with her, the brunette simply couldn’t resist. “Yeah, it’s just not working for me,” Kate said bluntly, as she shoved another slice of pizza into her mouth and chewed with relish. Okay, maybe not as irresistible as a slice of Pepperoni Passion.

    Yelena scratched desperately at her reflection, head muddled from the bombardment, from the shock and awe, from the sensory deprivation and total saturation. Her nails dug into the linoleum as blood streamed from her nose and mixed with the water that pooled there languidly. She balled her fists in frustration and hammered them into the floor as she found she could dig no further. She could go no further. She could see no further. Nothing but her own face.

    The sweet, metallic scent of gas mixed with the sweet metallic taste of blood as fumes clouded her her mind and obscured her vision. Now, it wasn’t even her own face she could see as darkness hung around.

    Strong arms clutched and grasped at her, strong fingers dug into her arms and prised at her ribs, pulling her backwards with a strength that was irresistible. She flailed with her hands for purchase. Purchase on something. Anything. Anything that would keep her here. Where she needed to be. Where she would be. Her face, her eyes, her smile, her voice, her scent. But there was no purchase to be had.

    The soaring melody echoed and reverberated around the small apartment, made all the more penetrating due to the assassin’s failing vision. A hand covered her mouth to quell her own chorus, one that matched the muezzin’s passion but not his sentiment, for Yelena was afraid. Afraid that she would never find the face she was searching for. The smile, the eyes, the voice, the scent, the touch.

    Touch.

    Within a second her hand had captured her assailant’s wrist.

    Twist.

    She twisted the wrist clockwise, violently. The hand that was pressed up against her mouth released her in an instant and she heard a cry of pain.

    Strike.

    A sharp strike with her free elbow sent her abductor reeling and staggering backward. Lunge.

    A lunging knee slammed into the chin of her enemy who was already doubled over in pain. They slammed into the fire exit door and the back of their head cracked painfully against the reinforced metal.

    Fall.

    They fell forward as Yelena closed the distance between them, their hands on the floor, blood streamed from their presumably broken nose onto the carpet. Red met red. Pull.

    The assassin’s hands dug into their scalp and pulled and yanked at their hair as she brought a face out of shadow and into the cold hue of flickering, artificial light. Poise.

    Yelena’s right hand was poised to strike a final, levelling blow. Her assailant’s nose was indeed broken and misshapen. Her violet eyes rolled back into her head as she wrestled against her unconscious.

    Blink.

    The blonde blinked through her own blood and clouded vision. Blinked through the years of uniform, unwavering and never ending repetition. She blinked to see her. Her. Her Kate. Kate.

    “Kate?” Yelena woke suddenly, her chest heaving. She was covered in a cold sweat and it felt as if her pulse was absolutely racing. This wasn’t normal. She’d had that dream a thousand times before. It was always the same. Always. And she always awoke without a start. No cold sweat, no fear, no panic, because her dream had always been the same. Nothing scared her anymore, nothing surprises her. Until now.

    Yelena shrugged off the covers and quickly put distance between herself and the woman from her dreams, the woman who lay breathing softly in her bed. Lucky mewed and shifted at the end of the bed as if he’d been rudely disturbed and the blonde gave him a unconscious pat as she found her bag and began to dig around for her cigarette packet.

    With her winter coat wrapped round her, Yelena slipped out onto their hotel room balcony. Her shiver was instant as the January cold hit her like a sheet of ice. The stone beneath her feet almost burned it was so cold as it penetrated her body like a Siberian winter. This was it. This was what she needed. Pain, feeling, searing distraction. Fuck, she thought as she sheltered her cigarette from the wind and after one, two, three attempts successfully lit it and took a deep and steadying inhale.

    It was a dream. It was only a dream. A dream that had never changed for thirty years. A dream that was only changing now, surely, because she was close. There was new information, or the possibility of new information tantalisingly close. Yelena could practically reach for it. That was why her dream had changed. Not because she was afraid. Surely she couldn’t be afraid. This was everything she wanted, the truth was everything she wanted. Her face. Just to see her face. Both of their faces.

    Yelena took another drag on her cigarette. The hot, acrid smoke burned her lungs and punched back against the freezing temperatures and biting wind. All this was was simply her brain processing. She wanted to keep Kate safe, and in going down this route of searching for her mother she might be putting Kate at risk. It was a simple as that. Her brain was processing this information and that was that. It wasn’t prophetic, it wasn’t meaningful and it didn’t mean that she was in danger, it simply meant that Yelena should cut down on the mozzarella before bed.

    But she’d hurt her. In her dream, she’d hurt her. Yelena had been the one to do it, not Benny. Yelena had inflicted pain upon her. She’d drawn blood. She’d broken bones. She’d broken her. Yelena’s fists balled and tensed uneasily as the cigarette hung between her lips. She drew on it again as she tried to rid her mind of the image of a bloodied and broken Kate, knelt in front of her, battling with her own consciousness as the sun rose over the minarets of Sarajevo and the muezzin began his rousing call to prayer.

    Yelena sighed heavily. She could see her breath in the freezing cold, morning air. They had been right. They had been right to keep Kate out of this. As much as she pouted and asserted, as much as Yelena had complete trust in Kate’s capabilities, she was starting to have very little trust in Benny Lacić’s ways of working.

    After a few more moments on the balcony, Yelena stubbed out her spent cigarette and silently padded back into her room. She dressed quietly, so as not to wake the woman she cared so deeply about, kissed Lucky on the head and let herself out of the room. The breakfast hall was empty apart from the reclusive brunette that had taken up residence in the corner of the room. She nursed a coffee and nodded to Yelena to join her. The blonde helped herself to a coffee of her own before she settled into the chair opposite her mother. “Ready to drink your body weight in tea?” Melina asked as a small smirk played across her dark features.

    Yelena sighed at the thought of violet eyes and blood red lips. “As ready as I will ever be.”

    He made them wait. Of course he made them wait. It was just another way of showing his power. First the bill at the restaurant, then the woman in the apartment, now this. Anywhere influence and power could be exerted, he would. That’s what it meant to be the top dog, and it was important to remind everyone that they were powerless against it. Yelena sat with her mother at the back of the café. The breakfast rush was over and the staff were busy clearing tables and readying them for lunch. A waiter spotted that Yelena had finished her tea and in moments it was refilled and piping hot. This was the dance. The traditional tea dance. Finish the tea and they’d assume you wanted more, don’t finish the tea and you would run the risk of implying that your host was inhospitable. So, naturally, you would finish your tea, to not offend, and it would be refilled again and again and again until your bladder was screaming at you and your body composition was ninety-seven percent tea. The blonde smiled a small thank you to the waiter for condemning her to yet another cup of scaldingly hot liquid. He meant well and that was without the pressure to appease Benny’s guests. Could you imagine being accused of not providing enough tea for your guests? It was unthinkable. Melina nibbled on a dry biscuit that had been on her saucer since they’d arrived. With a small, unimpressed sniff she discarded it, only to have it quickly snaffled up by a hungry Yelena. She should have eaten more pizza the night before, she’d been waiting hours to collect on Melina’s last biscuit. Her mother simply rolled her eyes at her. The biscuit was tasteless and dry but it was sugary and would go some way to soaking up the five gallons of tea in her stomach.

    After another half an hour of waiting, a pretty shifty looking guy stepped out of the back office. He was large and brawny, and looked like he thought he was the shit. He had slicked back black hair, a neat, dark beard and much to Yelena’s disgust he wore big brand label clothes slapped with gaudy, loud logos. The blonde was willing to bet her life that he was really fucking stupid. He would probably be willing to bet his life that him and his muscles could end her in seconds. He would lose that bet.

    Muscles nodded toward the office behind him and Yelena and Melina moved on through. Neither could escape a once over from the guy and the blonde practically hissed at him on her way past. Benny was sat at his desk, as he always was. It was another way he could demonstrate his power. He had a desk, you didn’t. Well, Yelena had a Carol Danvers if all else failed, but she wasn’t exactly the blonde’s first choice of crisis aversion solution. Benny Lacić was everything you wouldn’t expect from a mafia boss by the looks of him. He was tall and wiry and had a thing for woollen sweaters, especially in the winter. He liked baklava with his coffee, had a real sweet tooth and unlike most mafia bosses, Benny had a distinct appreciation for cats. A small grey shorthair was prowling his desk, rubbing its face against his laptop and his knuckles. He gave it an affectionate scratch before he shooed it away and closed his screen. He smiled wildly, a smile that didn’t reach his eyes. Sure, Benny Lacić didn’t look like a mafia boss, but his mind certainly operated like one. It was as ruthless and effective as the handgun he had strapped on the underside of his desk. “Yelena Belova,” he greeted warmly, “What an unexpected pleasure.”

    “Benny,” she nodded with a restrained smile. She had to offer him something. They were on good terms, or as good terms as an independently contracted ex-assassin could be with a mafia boss.

    “And Melina too, well, it has been quite some time.” He gestured for the two women to sit, which of course, they did. “You have not aged a day my dear,” he said with an appraising look. Yelena was worried she was going to be a little bit sick in her mouth. They were fortunate that they’d left her father back at the hotel otherwise their tense meeting would have already devolved into shouting, punching and Yelena coming away emptied handed and with a target on her back. “As for you Yelena,” he said as he turned to take her in, eyes looking her up and down. “I can see that the superhero life agrees with you.” Did it? Did she look better for it? That was what he was saying right? It’s certainly what his eyes were saying which was deeply troubling and worryingly vomit-inducing. It was starting to look as if leaving Kate back at the hotel had been a good idea for various reasons.

    “It pays the bills,” Yelena shrugged coolly. She even managed a smug, self-important smirk. Benny would like that.

    “Oh, I’m sure it does much more than that.” Yelena had to physically restrain herself from frowning. Benny always liked to speak in riddles and half-truths. He liked to hold his information close to his chest, he liked knowing what you wanted and having what you needed. “You’re not here to drag me away to some American court of ‘justice’ are you?” He asked with a playful twinkle in his eyes. Playful-ish.

    “You know I am not really interested in justice Benny. I just do the job,” Yelena said, matter- of-factly. It was the truth for the most part. Yelena liked justice for the right people, but with the Avengers she was just a tool. She didn’t get to decide what was right and what was wrong, she was simply pointed in the right direction. Or what she hoped was the right direction. “And besides,” the blonde continued, “You know that is not why I am here.” “Then why are you here?” He asked innocently as he took a sip of his thick, dark coffee. Prick. Of course he knew. Nonetheless, Yelena glanced at her mother, seeking her approval. It felt right. Melina nodded and gave her the smallest of controlled smiles. If her mother was feeling vulnerable she didn’t show it, which was probably for the best in present company. Yelena turned back to Benny. “We are looking for my biological mother.” “That is why you are in Sarajevo,” he said, before taking a bite of his baklava. It crunched satisfyingly and Yelena felt the smallest flash of jealousy. She’d been subjected to dry, tasteless biscuits whilst he’d kept the good stuff for himself. That wasn’t how you treated guests. “But that is not why you are here.” He was wrong and right all at the same time. He wanted Yelena to be more direct and Melina thought it best to humour him. “We have a lead. An apartment that we believe was used to traffic children,” Melina said. “The woman is too afraid to speak, why is that?” Yelena asked, perhaps a little too aggressively, but Benny had always said he loved her confidence.

    “You should have come to me first, Yelena. I could have helped,” he said with a small downturned smile. His fake sympathy was unbecoming.

    “And you can’t?” Yelena retorted, knowing full well that she was pushing the ticket but this was the way that he worked. He wouldn’t give up information easily, you had to work for it. “Yelena,” Melina chided, the warning clear and obvious in her voice, but Yelena knew what she was doing, despite her mother clearly thinking otherwise.

    Yelena leaned forward in her chair and smiled easily. “I know you have information. What is it that you know?”

    “The question you should be asking is how much is this information worth, no?” He said as he dusted pistachio crumbs from his fingers nonchalantly. They really were going to do this. “There are people out there who are more than capable of killing to protect the integrity of the Red Room, to protect their own integrity. I can protect you from that.” “The Red Room is dead,” she said dismissively. He smiled a knowing smile and she rolled her eyes. She wasn’t there to play games. “And besides, I am more than capable of protecting myself.”

    “In my city?” He asked, sceptically.

    “Yes,” she said plainly. Where else did she mean? She could protect herself any time, in any place and from any angle. Benny nodded, he didn’t doubt her capabilities, in fact, he valued them very highly but he was quietly confident that if he wanted to take out the two Black Widows before him, him could. He may need to take extreme action, but he could. Benny failed to realise that in Yelena’s new line of work, Benny Lacić was small fry. “How about your girlfriend, can you protect her?” He asked as his eyes flicked to hers. She didn’t flinch, not outwardly. Inwardly she wanted to scream. How had he known? She could have sworn they hadn’t been followed the previous night. She’d been so careful when they’d kissed. Had he had someone at the hotel? Maybe, but they weren’t sharing a double and they’d been careful to be discreet anywhere else but their room. What if he didn’t actually know anything, what if he was bluffing to get a rise from her or prove a hunch? She had to be careful not to give him anything.

    “Stop with this Benny,” she said with a confident wave of her hand. “I want information. You will give it to me,” she smiled.

    “What if I said that I do not have the information you seek, hmm?” He quirked a questioning eyebrow and leaned back into his chair as he crossed his legs.

    Yelena’s small smile grew into a full-blown smirk. “I would say that is bullshit.” Melina rolled her eyes at her daughter’s petulance. Yelena’s mother clearly thought that her charm offensive was lacking, and thought it best that she took the reins to steady the ship. “Benny, even if you were not involved-“ “Which I was not,” he cut in sharply, “Human trafficking is abhorrent and not something my organisation has any dealings with.” For someone who thought human trafficking was abhorrent, his tone certainly was light, if not a little dismissive.

    “Sure,” bit Yelena sardonically.

    “There are members of your organisation who are serving time for this crime,” Melina retorted civilly with a tight smile. “Would they have information that could help us?” It was a good question from her mother, Yelena was willing to admit it. It shifted focus and blame from Benny and put it on those who went before. In reality, they were just the people stupid enough to get caught.

    Benny’s brow furrowed in thought, as if he was giving the idea conscious and careful consideration. It didn’t need any consideration. Most Bosnian jails were filled with ex-Mafia, and most of those inmates would have been involved with human trafficking if they were members during the Nineties. “There is the possibility I suppose,” he shrugged. The cheek of this man.

    “Yelena only seeks her mother Benny,” Melina reasoned, trying to appeal to his sense of reason. Whether he had any was up for debate. “She does not seek retribution.” “Is she not an Avenger?” He replied.

    “I am on vacation.”

    “There are a lot of people I know who would pay a lot of money to get their hands on an Avenger,” he said coolly as he took another sip of his coffee. Of course, he was going to try and play her this way but he was forgetting that she did not give a fuck. “Especially ex-Black Widows who break into top secret facilities and steal classified assets. These people do not care that you are on vacation.”

    “If the Russian government wanted Yelena they could have taken her at any time,” Melina offered, and she was right. Yelena had been in St Petersburg for weeks which meant one of three things. The Russian government also did not give a fuck. They’d decided it would be easier to take her when she was apart from her parents in Sarajevo, a plan that was thwarted at the last minute with Melina and Alexei’s impromptu trip. Or it wasn’t the Russian government that Kate and Yelena had acquired the asset from. From where the blonde was sitting, the latter seemed the most likely, which was curious to say the least. “Hmm. I suppose they could have,” Benny nodded. Yep, definitely the latter. “What about Kate Bishop? Now she’s out of America can you really keep her safe?” Yelena’s jaw twitched. He said her name, it wasn’t a bluff. Whatever it was, however much he knew about their relationship, it was certainly a threat. Whether he meant to act on it or not. The blonde blinked away the image that plagued her mind from the night before. Violet eyes rolling back into her head.

    “Enough of this talk,” Yelena said as casually as she could muster. “What is it that you want Benny? I am sure we can come to an arrangement.” She smiled as his eyes lazily traced her figure. Yelena would have found it grotesque if her mind hadn’t been so preoccupied with swirling worries over Kate’s safety.

    After a moment longer Benny smiled to himself ruefully and then met the blonde’s eyes. “There is a man, an ex-associate of ours. He may have the information you are looking for.” “What is the catch?” Yelena asked, for it was never going to be that simple. Benny shrugged as if the catch was next to no catch at all. That was never going to be the case. “He is in protective custody. They have offered him a deal to roll over on us. I have his location but I lack your...” he paused for a moment as he searched for the right word. “Subtlety.” Yelena had to agree, subtlety was definitely something Benny lacked. “You want me to silence him,” she said, plainly. It wasn’t a question. “Yes,” he nodded.

    Yelena smiled and shook her head. There was only one answer here. “No.” His eyes narrowed, as did Melina’s. Yelena’s mother didn’t hide her surprise well but the blonde’s refusal shouldn’t have come as one. The younger Widow was an ex-assassin for a reason. “Well then,” Benny said as his smile faltered, “You will not get your information.” “What is stopping me from agreeing and then not honouring my end of the bargain?” Yelena asked, curiously.

    “Kate Bishop. She is beautiful, no?” Their eyes met and Yelena’s stomach dropped. He really was going to threaten her, he was going to use Kate to manipulate Yelena, and she wanted to gut him for it. “What is she? Twenty four, twenty five? I have heard she is very talented with a bow and arrow but other than that, has no real otherworldly gifts.”

    “Benny, that girl has nothing to do with this,” interjected Melina.

    “You see, there was a time when all you cared about was money,” He continued as he rose from his chair and came round to rest against his desk in front of them. “The more money you had, the more of your little friends you could free.” The way he said the words ‘little friends’ made Yelena want to punch him in the face whilst she gutted him. “But now... now you care about someone.”

    She tried to stay cool, she tried not to give him the power that he was so desperately trying to eke from her. “You know that if you hurt her, it is not me that you answer to.” He laughed a cyclical laugh. The conversation had turned, it was no longer civil. There was no pretence anymore, no rapport, only business, and it was business on Benny’s terms. “You think your Avenger friends scare me Yelena? Avengers cannot simply raze cities to the ground anymore, they have been stripped of their prerogative. Castrated like the dogs that they are. But I can raze this city to the ground and I will if I have to.” His dark eyes bore into her and she felt the dread begin to pool within the pit of her stomach. This was a situation that could escalate quickly if Yelena didn’t keep herself in check. There was nothing she wouldn’t do to keep Kate Bishop safe, but she had changed for the better because of her. By pursuing the information she wanted it was she who was putting Kate at risk. It was her need and unwillingness to pay that debt. Could she kill a man in cold blood to keep Kate safe? Of course she could. Could she look Kate in the eye after? She wasn’t so sure.

    “Do this for me, Yelena,” Benny said, almost caringly, as if they were on the same side, pulling for the same team. “Kaşim will give you the information you need, I guarantee it.” He took a card from his desk, noted down what must have been an address and held it out within reach before her. Where the fuck did he get off?

    Yelena pursed her lips and shook her head. “I do not do that anymore.” He smiled, almost sadly, with an air of inevitability.

    “Yes you do,” he said quietly. “And do not worry, no one will tell your little girlfriend. It’ll be our secret.”

    Yelena looked at the card held between his fingers with consternation. Her heart began to race as she chewed the inside of her mouth and clenched her jaw. On that card could be everything she’d been hoping for. It could unlock the mystery of her past. Where she came from, who her parents were, where her parents were. It was everything. Everything she’d questioned since she was a child. Everything she could never bring herself to hope for. Without thinking she reached, she reached for the card. But as she reached it was pulled away, just out of her grasp.

    “Ah, ah, ah, do we have a deal?” Came Benny’s mocking voice.

    Her eyes flicked to his and then back to the small, almost insignificant looking piece of card that rested between his fingertips. “We have a deal,” she whispered. Her heart had spoken and the deal was done.

    The guards were relatively easy to pacify, as was the security system. Police tech was bad at the best of times and these certainly were not that. Yelena and Melina’s mark was holed up just outside the city, in the hills to the south. It was a small property amongst the trees that grew in the shadow of Trebević. Too easy to find and even easier to infiltrate once identified. Some idiot cops had been lighting up outside as Yelena and Melina had approached. They had very quickly been taken care of. Yelena pocketed a packet of Camels from one of the unconscious cops, much to her mother’s dismay. She shrugged, she really didn’t give a shit. When Melina had the types of dream Yelena had and still stayed off the nicotine, then she could pass judgement.

    The sun had only just set but the house was dark apart from the familiar glow of a tv at the end of the corridor leading to what must have been the lounge. It was a two story winter chalet and the two Widows had made sure to sweep both floors before they made a move on the mark. The muffled chatter of sports commentary made its way towards them. Željo were playing that afternoon, Kaşim was clearly a fan, and was clearly unaware of the two Black Widows inching closer to his position on the couch as he mouthed off at what Yelena could only assume was the referee. That’s what football fans did, right?

    The sound of the tv and their mark’s objections grew louder as both mother and daughter approached the door cautiously. They both paused for moment, listening intently. Their eyes met. They had both heard it. A heavy sigh that didn’t belong. There was someone else in the room with Kaşim, most likely an armed officer assigned to go wherever his charge went. He would be there to protect the snitch for sure, but he would also have been appointed to ensure the ex-Mafia member didn’t do a runner.
