With a nod Yelena pointed to her chest, she would take the guard, Melina would make sure Kaşim didn’t escape. The blonde’s mother nodded back to signal she understood. They would go on Yelena’s mark.

    The ex-assassin, perhaps soon to be current-assassin, took a deep, steadying breath. This was it. This could be it. Within just a few moments she might have the information she’d been searching for. Within just a few moments she might know where she’d been taken from or even who she’d been taken from. She gave her mother one final nod before she burst through the door to the lounge.

    In shock, the armed guard sprayed the door with bullets from his semi-automatic rifle that he had held against his hip. Yelena deftly sidestepped the assault as the guard struggled to his feet. He was so slow the blonde felt as if she were waiting for him. She grabbed the barrel of his gun and threw it backwards into his nose. He screamed in pain as his nose broke and his blood showered the carpet with vibrant, red, oxygenated blood. For a moment Yelena blinked as she saw Kate’s face before her. Violet eyes and blood red lips.

    “Yelena?” Came her mother’s slightly trepidatious tone. Kaşim cowered upon the couch, Melina had him at gunpoint.

    The blonde blinked again. The armed guard was raising his rifle once more. In one fluid motion she kicked the gun forcefully from his grasp and then continued her momentum round to sweep his legs. His head cracked forcefully against the carpeted and by then very bloodied lounge floor. He was out cold.

    Before joining her mother by the couch she turned the non-armed guard onto his side to encourage the blood from his broken nose to pool onto the already well decorated carpet, rather than down the back of his throat and into his lungs. Never let anyone tell you that Yelena Belova wasn’t a conscientious creature of the night. With two fingers the blonde checked the man’s pulse. It was a little slow but steady and not going anywhere fast. Now to her target.

    Yelena got to her feet and turned to Kaşim. Their eyes met and he started screaming for his life, screaming in hope that one of his cop protectors might hear him. Sadly for the ex-Mafia member, all of his protectors were out cold. She drew the pistol that was holstered just inside her jacket, closed the space between them with three quick steps and pointed the gun to his head.

    “Molim te! Molim te! Ne pujac!” He pleaded. His brow was already dripping with sweat. He was was terrified for his life, and justifiably so, for her knew who she was. “Engleski,” she demanded as she pressed the barrel of her gun into his forehead. “Molim!” he continued.

    “Engleski!” She shouted as she pressed harder with her gun.

    “Please. Please do not shoot,” Kaşim begged, this time in English. A wise choice as the younger Widow had already begun to lose her patience. “Did Benny send you? How much did he pay? They can pay more.” No they couldn’t but it was a nice try, even if Yelena was in no mood for that kind of bargaining. She wanted answers, not money. Not anymore. “I will make this quick,” Yelena said as her mother settled casually in the chair Kaşim’s police friend had vacated moments before. “I am looking for information. Rumour has it you are a real fountain of knowledge.”

    Their mark frowned in confusion. He expected to be dead by now. “Who sent you?” “I’m here for myself,” Yelena answered.

    “I would never give him up. You need tell him that.”

    Yelena sighed and shook her head. This was proving harder than it needed to be. “What happened to you paying me all that mone-“ “I was only going to give them Xhaka. You have to believe me,” his hands were pleading with her but Kaşim was way off the mark. She was going to have to cut to it. “They wanted me to but I-“ “In Nineteen Ninety-Two, you were involved in the trafficking of children for a man named Dreykov.”

    Kaşim blinked. “W-What?”

    “Dreykov, do you know the name?” Melina asked as she inspected her gun. Even Yelena’s mother was getting impatient.

    “Yes, I-I do…” His confused eyes darted from Yelena to Melina and back. “But, I do not understand.”

    “There were girls kept in an apartment near Baščaršija,” Yelena continued. Clearly she was going to have to spell it out for him. “They were taken from there to Budapest for Dreykov and then on to Russia. Where did the girls come from?”

    “I don’t know…” Kaşim shrugged and yelped a little as Yelena pressed the gun against his temple more firmly to help jog his memory. “Bosniak families. Families who lost fathers, mothers who were sold into labour. They could have come from anywhere.” Yelena swallowed firmly. She knew there was a high probability she was orphaned by the war. She knew there was a high probability her mother may have been trafficked. She knew there was a high probability her parents were dead or worse, not even remembered by anyone. It still didn’t make it any easier to hear.

    “There was a blonde girl in Ninety-two,” came Melina’s voice. It was much closer than she’d expected it to be. In fact, Yelena jumped slightly as her mother’s hand gently squeezed her shoulder. “She would have been three years old. Do you remember?” Get your shit together Yelena.

    “There were a lot of kids,” he shrugged. He was getting a little too confident. Melina was entirely unimpressed. She narrowed her eyes and raised her voice.

    “Do you remember?” She asked, forcefully.

    It did the trick. “There might have been a blonde from Mostar. She was young. We picked her up during the first siege I think.” Mostar, she was from Mostar. Maybe. It was practically a border town in the south of the country and had been heavily besieged more than once in the Nineties. It made sense, Yelena was sure there were a lot of orphans from Mostar from those days.

    “Who were her family?” Yelena asked. The hand holding her gun was steady, but her voice was beginning to reflect the emotions that were swirling beneath the surface. “You expect me to fucking know that?”

    “If you want to live, yes.” Melina said calmly as she began to pace the room casually. This hadn’t been part of their plan although in all honesty, they hadn’t really had a plan. Go in, take out the cops and get answers. What happened after that hadn’t been discussed. Yelena knew that a year previous she wouldn’t have hesitated. She would have taken Kaşim’s life, no questions asked. But now, things were different.

    “Woah, woah, woah. It was a long time ago, okay? What do you remember from Ninety- two?”

    Yelena shrugged. “A shelled apartment. Broken dishes. Gun shots. How about you?” She said provocatively and his eyes widened. He’d finally clocked that she was the girl. That he might have been the one to take her. That after being on the brink of achieving it, he could never really escape his past discretions. It was a sobering moment for him. He seemed to swallow and nod. He knew he had to give in to her. He knew he owed it to her. But whether he could remember was something else entirely.

    “There was an apartment we were looting that had taken damage. We took a girl there, sure.” “Blonde girl?”

    “I-I think she could have been blonde.” Yelena knew that he was trying but she was getting impatient. She gave him a clip on the side of his head with her spare hand and yelped in pain. Melina smiled, cleverly amused.

    “What do you expect?!” He appealed.

    “Information,” Yelena grabbed him by the collar and brought her gun up beneath his chin. “Everything you can remember,” she growled, “And I will let you live.” There, she’d said it. Her mother caught her eye from where she was pacing across the room. Yelena didn’t like what she saw but Yelena also didn’t think she had any other choice. She couldn’t just kill because it was convenient, that’s what killers did, and she wasn’t a killer, not anymore. She would get the information she needed, have Melina stay with Kaşim until she’d put Kate on a flight back to the United States and then have her mother turn him back in. She couldn’t return to Kate a killer, if she planned to, well, she shouldn’t return to Kate at all. “Really?”He asked with equal parts scepticism and hope.

    Yelena sighed. She was at ease with her choice, although by Melina’s face, it was clear that her mother wasn’t. “Yes,” the blonde said matter-of-factly as she pulled the gun away Kaşim’s neck and gestured from him to sit on the couch. He very quickly did so, aware that he had little to no chance of liberating her weapon from her.

    “Where was this apartment building? In Mostar?” Yelena asked.

    “Yes,” he nodded. “Just west of the river.”

    “Give me the address.”

    “I don’t have it. I-I think it’s a hotel now, after it was rebuilt. I- the whole place was torn apart.” Yelena nodded. That sounded consistent. It felt as if they were making progress, real progress. Kaşim’s voice was steadier and more certain, he was remembering. “Was it near the old bridge?” She asked.

    “Yeah, by the mosque near the bridge.” He frowned for a moment, as if trying to draw from a memory that was just out of reach. “Hadži … Hadži…”

    “Kurtova?” Came Melina’s voice. It was an unexpected intervention but not unwelcome, as Kaşim’s eyes lit up.

    “Yes! Kurtova, that is the one.” He was suddenly incredibly enthusiastic to help, now he thought his life was guaranteed. “There was a kid, her mother had been taken.” “Taken?” Yelena frowned. Taken. It was hard not to let her mind run away with itself. Taken meant maybe alive? But also who fuck took her? How would she find them? And how could she make them pay?

    “Yes,” he nodded.

    “By who?” She asked. She needed to know.

    He shrugged a little too casually. He’d gotten comfortable and it made her want to scream. “By who?!” She shouted as she brought the gun closer to his face once more. “Look, you have a gun pointed at me. If I knew, I would tell you. I just did the clean up job. We went in and looted these places, took anything of value.”

    “And that included kids?” Melina asked, clearly disgusted.

    “Of course. The Dreykov stuff was just money on the side but he paid well.” “So it was Mafia? Mafia took her?” Yelena asked insistently. She wanted to get back to talking about her mother.

    “You will not find her.” He said, stoically. “Thousands of women were taken, not just by us. The man in charge of it all is dead, you made sure of that.” Yelena swallowed. Benny’s old partner, Emil. The man she’d killed for Benny. She’d killed before she knew, before she even had an inkling that her parents could have been Bosnian. Was he responsible for the human trafficking out of Mostar? She supposed that it would stand to reason. But surely there would be another lead, someone who would know, someone Benny would know that… But of course she couldn’t go back to Benny, not if she handed Kaşim back to the police. She would burn all bridges.

    Yelena’s mind started to get the better of her. The man before her was a monster. He profited from war, he stole children from their families, and families from their children. He showed no empathy or remorse, he couldn’t even muster any loyalty. He was a monster who deserved the justice that she’d been told to deliver because he took her. He took her. Yelena had to swallow the tears that threatened to betray her. “You took me,” her voice broke as Melina brought her hand to gently rest upon Yelena’s arm, willing her to lower her gun. “You took me from my mother.”

    “Your mother was gone by the time I got there,” he explained and she knew it was true but she wanted to hate him. “I saved your life.”

    “You have no idea what you’re talking about,” Yelena bit back. Saved her life, that was rich. She survived because of her family, because of her sister, and because of herself. “There is a woman I know in Mostar,” Melina said quietly as she placed a supportive hand across Yelena’s lower back. “She might be able to help us.” Mother and daughter locked eyes. Yelena wanted to hope and Melina wanted to give her that hope, despite both of them knowing the chances of finding the blonde’s mother alive were so incredibly slim. Yelena had to fight to keep the tears from her eyes as her mother smiled sadly.

    “Okay,” Yelena whispered.

    “I would not hold your breath,” said Kaşim dismissively and almost cruelly. Now he’d guaranteed his safety he’d obviously decided to be a heartless prick again. “She is just one woman in thousands.”

    Yelena’s jaw clenched tightly. She wanted to beat the shit out of him. She wanted to be brutal. She wanted to be everything he thought she was. But she couldn’t, she wouldn’t, because that wasn’t who she was, that wasn’t Kate Bishop’s Yelena Belova. So instead, she asked a question.

    “In Sarajevo, in that apartment, were there other children like me?” Melina’s eyes narrowed, perhaps at her daughter’s question, perhaps at the evenness of her voice. “Yes,” Kaşim nodded.

    “How many?”

    He shrugged at if kids were a commodity. Give or take a couple, it didn’t really matter. “At least six, they were not all mine.” None of them were yours, prick.

    “Six, wow.” Yelena smiled dangerously and shook her head. Kaşim began to look a little uneasy. A Black Widow’s smile was something that usually proceeded a bullet in the brain. “And how many children did you collect for Dreykov do you think? In total?” She asked, smile never leaving her face.

    “Maybe fifteen, sixteen.” His eyes darted to Melina and then back to Yelena. He was nervous.

    The blonde’s smile dropped. “Do you know that only one in twenty make it through the training?”

    Kaşim audibly gulped. Fucking coward. If she couldn’t kill him, she could at least destroy fucking conscience for at least a couple of hours. “You might have saved my life, but you condemned the rest. I hope your conscience can live with that.”

    He looked down for a moment and chewed the inside of his mouth, his face unreadable. He was going over his next move, considering his next words. He clearly thought that they could be the difference between life or death, but Yelena was never going to kill him. She wouldn’t give him the satisfaction, he could rot.

    Finally Kaşim’s eyes rose, not to meet Yelena but to meet her mother’s. Something passed between them and he smiled, almost cruelly. The blonde went to speak again, to tell Kaşim that he was going back to the police, to tell him he could rot in a jail cell, but she didn’t get to. It all happened so fast.

    Muzzle flash filled the room and Kaşim’s brains sprayed across the coach. Yelena had recoiled instinctually at the sound of sudden pistol fire to her right. Her mother had shot him, she’d killed him in cold blood. Yelena stood open mouthed as she struggled to find the words.

    “Mama… mama, what did you do?” She couldn’t quite believe what had happened. It had happened so fast, and out of nowhere.

    “I saved Kate’s life,” Melina said coolly. “Something that you seemed unwilling to do.” Yelena shook her head in disbelief. She was never unwilling to protect Kate, she would give her life to protect Kate but she wouldn’t stoop to this, not anymore. She wouldn’t become a murderer for her, there were other ways.

    “I made a promise, mama. I could have protected her.”

    “You made that deal, I would not have,” Melina retorted, clearly disappointed at her daughter. “It is my job to keep you both safe,” she pointed angrily at her own chest, her eyes dark and dangerous. “And I will kill anyone that gets in the way of that.”

    Yelena sighed and shook her head. Being a Black Widow, being through the Red Room so many times, didn’t mean that her mother couldn’t be anything else. It didn’t mean that she was condemned to this life. “But mama, you don’t have to kill for me.” “He was a piece of shit, Yelena. He hurt you. He hurt countless children like us,” she smiled sadly, placed both hands upon her daughter’s shoulders and looked deep into her eyes. She needed Yelena to hear her. She needed her to understand. “I wish I could kill him a thousand times over.”

    The car ride back to the hotel had been quiet. Too quiet for her liking. Her mind was a mess and she would have preferred to argue all the way back into the city with her mother than be subjected to it, but she had been out of luck. Melina drove calmly and carefully, as not to attract attention, and it had taken them a full half an hour to reach where they’d been staying. Half an hour was too long. Her hands were still covered in blood, but she hid them firmly in her pockets as she strode across through reception to call the elevator with her elbow. Thankfully the artificial light overhead didn’t betray the blood that hid in plain sight on her black turtle neck. Day light and it would have been a different story. The elevator doors closed and mother and daughter stood in silence as the old machinery jolted to life and hauled them to the lofty heights of the fourth floor. It juddered to a halt and Yelena was quick to exit. She heard her mother’s defeated sigh from behind. They would talk, and they would be okay, but it wouldn’t be tonight. Yelena needed to get the blood from off her. It wasn’t even Kaşim’s but she needed it gone. She needed it out from under her fingernails, out from the cracked skin and callouses on her palms and out of her pores.

    She took the key card from her pocket and let herself in. It wasn’t late enough for Kate to be asleep, but it was certainly late enough for her to be worried. Without a look to the surprised brunette who was pushing herself quickly from her bed, Yelena made her way to the bathroom.

    “Hey, oh thank God you’re back. Are you okay?” Came Kate’s voice. She felt awful but she shut the bathroom door behind her, ignoring Kate’s words. She couldn’t let her see the blood.

    Immediately Yelena pulled the turtleneck over her head. Parts of it peeled off of her, as the cop's blood had soaked through to the grey vest below. Both articles of clothing ended up in the shower as Kate knocked lightly on the bathroom door.

    “Yelena?” She called, concern evident in her voice.

    “I am okay!” Yelena managed, despite not sounding very convincing. The last thing she needed was for Kate to come into the bathroom, and if she didn’t want that to happen, she needed to do a better job of alleviating some of her worry. Yelena turned on the hot tap, grabbed the soap and began to scrub feverishly at her hands, knuckles and wrists. “Yelena,” came Kate’s voice again, “I’m coming in.” No, no, no, she couldn’t come in, she couldn’t see her like this. Why the fuck didn’t she lock the door?

    The door swung open and hazel eyes met violet in the mirror. Yelena swallowed. “What happened?” Those violet eyes traced her reflection quickly, taking in the blood-stained skin of her stomach and her chest. Yelena suddenly felt very exposed, despite still being in her sports bra and jeans. Kate’s eyes widened in realisation. “Oh my god.” The brunette rushed to her, panicked. She turned Yelena to face her and inspected her skin, in worry. The blonde captured her girlfriend’s frantic hands with her in own in an attempt to calm her.

    “It is not mine, Kate,” Yelena said as gently as she could manage. “It is not mine. I am okay.” Yelena tried to offer her a reassuring smile but she knew that her smile would never reach her eyes. Not tonight.

    “Oh, thank god," Kate said with relief as she pulled the smaller woman into a fierce hug, clearly not realising that she was probably getting someone else’s blood all over her ‘dog mom’ T-shirt, or simply not caring.

    Yelena inhaled deeply, trying to even out her breathing. She could feel her chest, it was tight, and not in a good way.

    “Is your mom okay?” Kate asked a little apprehensively.

    Yelena nodded into her girlfriend’s embrace and then pulled back, putting her at arm’s length. “Melina is fine,” she nodded, “You should go to bed.”

    The blonde turned back to the sink and continued to scrub. She had to get underneath her nails, she simply had to. There was still so much blood there. Thin, angry, red lines stood in stark contrast to her fair skin and she had to get them out. The blood swirled and mixed with the flowing hot water in the white porcelain sink. Iron and water, like water colour. Images of linoleum tiles flashes before Yelena’s eyes. She shook her head to rid herself of the image but it was no use. She had to grip the edges of the sink as she felt the tiles beneath her fingernails, the blood beneath her fingernails. Her mother’s blood. So much of her dream had been reality, was her mother’s blood reality too? Her mother was gone, her father was dead. That’s what he’d said. That’s what he’d said.

    Supportive arms snaked round her waist as small tender kisses adorned her shoulders. Kate was so tender, so soft and gentle, so beautiful. It was just too much. “Please, go back to sleep,” Yelena begged. It was painful to say but she needed Kate gone. This wasn’t meant for her.

    “You’re not going to tell me what happened?” Kate asked, her tone one of disappointment. She wanted to be let in, not kept out. That was how they worked now. They talked, they communicated, but not even Yelena’s brain could make sense of the thoughts she was thinking and the feelings she was feeling.

    “No,” Yelena shrugged off Kate’s touch. “It is best that you do not know.” There was a silence as Kate searched for Yelena’s eyes in the mirror. “As long as you’re okay,” Kate said softly with a small sad smile. She was hurt but she understood on some level. She knew Yelena needed to deal with this and she knew that maybe later she would talk about it, when things became clearer and less vivid.

    She was just too good, too perfect. Too soft and kind and generous. How could Yelena have been so stupid? She knew before she invited Kate to Sarajevo that she had history in the city. She knew before she came that there was potential risk involved. She knew all of it before she came and yet she still invited Kate Bishop. All because she wanted to share something with her, something important. She wanted to show that everything was them going forward. She wanted the woman who made her feel like a different person by her side. But it was stupid and it was selfish and she saw that now.

    Yelena turned off the tap with her back still turned to Kate. She shook her head and braced herself against the sink. “I should have never invited you here. Exposed you to this,” she whispered. To this. To this life, to her part in it, to this side of Yelena that she was hoping her girlfriend would never have to see.

    “Whatever it is,” Kate said resolutely, “I can protect myself. Greatest archer in the world, remember?”

    “That is not what I mean. I-“ Her tears caught in her throat. They had been coming but they had still some how managed to take her by suspense. She bowed her head and gripped the sink, her breathing ragged.

    “Hey. Shh, shhh.” Kate’s arms were around her, pulling her from the sink and into her embrace. Tears stained Yelena’s face as she tried to resist. “Whatever it is, we’ve got this okay? You and me.”

    “No, no,” Yelena pushed her girlfriend away dismissively. “You should go home,” she said as she marched out the bathroom. Yes. That was it. Kate had to go home. Away from the danger and away from her.

    “What?” Kate blinked in disbelief as Yelena strode past her with a new sense of purpose. “You can fly home in the morning. If there is no flight I can arrange something,” she said, searching the room erratically.

    “I’m not going home,” said Kate disbelievingly as she too marched out of the bathroom. “It is safer,” Yelena insisted, her eyes dark and wild. “It is safer for you to not be with me,” she explained as she grabbed Kate’s case and threw it down onto the bed. “What do you mean to not be with you?” Kate asked incredulously.

    “This is not something you should be involved with,” Yelena said as she opened Kate’s case and began to throw her belongings inside. “ I am not someone you should be involved with.” “I think I get to decide that for myself.”

    “Nope,” Yelena shook her head matter-of-factly. Finally she’d found clarity, finally she knew what had to be done. “Not anymore.”

    “Well too late Yelena, because I love you,” Kate retorted stubbornly. She was wrestling with her voice to keep it together as it was so close to breaking.

    “You are an Avenger,” Yelena explained as she began to search the wardrobe for Kate’s things. “You do good.”

    “And so do you!” The brunette appealed, desperately, tears now shining in her eyes too. Lucky came to her from his place at the end of the bed. He was confused and scared and he nuzzled Kate’s hand to find some comfort.

    Yelena used the distraction to continue her hunt. She threw a pair of heavy DMs into the case.

    “Yelena,” pleaded again. Her voice did break this time. Again, her appeals went ignored. Kate huffed audibly and put her hands to her hips. “Yelena Belova, I swear to god if you do not put my bag down, I will fucking make you.”

    There was a moment’s pause where silence fell in the hotel room. All that could be heard was Yelena’s increasingly laboured breathing. She was struggling. The tears were still coming. She threw down a handful of Kate’s shirts and stepped away from the bed. Tears turned to sobs as she fought for air and she sank down against the magnolia painted walls of their hotel room. Kate was instantly by her side.

    Sobs wracked Yelena’s body and Kate placed gentle hands upon her girlfriend’s knees. “Look at me,” she soothed, “Look at me, okay? Breathe with me sweetheart. Just breathe.” Kate’s fingertips ran slowly and comfortingly up her arms as Yelena tried to wrestle back control of her breathing. Her chest was so tight, it was just so tight. She tried to breathe deeply but every time it just clamped backdown around her lungs like a vice. “Breathe with me Yelena,” came Kate’s voice. She sounded so far away but her touch felt so close. Yelena tried to focus on Kate’s voice as she counted up to five over and over. The blonde’s hands found her girlfriend’s and she clung on for dear life. In, two, three, four, five. Hold, two, three four, five. Out, two, three, four, five.

    Arms encircled her and light kisses peppered her hair, forehead and her cheeks, tasting her tears. Violet eyes met hers and they smiled back. “I’ve got you,” Kate whispered. She meant it. It was something she’d never thought about before. The idea that Kate had her. Yelena was always the protector. She was the older one, the more experienced fighter, the impure one. The one that had less to lose, the one that would be less of a loss if something bad did happen. Yelena could be sacrificed and it would be worth it but nothing could ever be worth Kate’s life. But right there, Kate’s hands were her anchor, her kisses her comfort, her words her lifeline. Kate was her home. Not the city they were in, not Mostar. Kate. “You do know I’m not going anywhere, right?” Kate said with just the tiniest bit of attitude. She had reason to be a little put out and Yelena was more than happy to deal with a little of her sass. It was cute.

    Yelena nodded, she wondered at this point what she’d have to do to get rid of the woman. “Good,” Kate said obstinately but with a smile.

    “You are stupidly stubborn,” Yelena said. “Like bad-for-your-health stubborn.” “You’re damn right I am,” Kate replied, “Lucky for you.”. Okay, maybe she was more angry than put out, but Kate Bishop angry was even cuter than Kate Bishop put out. “Do you want to talk about what happened?” Kate asked. Yelena wasn’t sure she could. “No,” the blonde whispered. Nervousness wasn’t something she felt all that often. The feeling was almost unrecognisable but it was there. She wanted to tell Kate everything. She would have to tell her about Kaşhim, she would have to tell her about her choice that put Kate in danger, she would have to tell her about her mother. It just all felt like so much and that’s why it had to come out.

    “Are you sure?” Kate asked gently.

    Yelena’s eyes found hers. “No,” she replied, and so she told her. She told Kate everything. From the conversation with Benny to Melina pulling the trigger. There had been more tears and more soothing words as well as words of affirmation. Kate had told her she’d made the right choice to not kill Kaşim. She’d told her that was how they protected each other. Each other. There it was again, the idea that it wasn’t just Yelena who protected Kate, it was a responsibility that they shared, one that went both ways. Yelena had to admit that although it was a completely foreign concept to her, she liked it. She liked the way it made her feel. She couldn’t quite work out what it was but she liked it. She liked it when Kate took her back to the bathroom and showered her clean. She liked it when she took her back to bed and gently towel dried her hair. She liked it when she kissed her stomach and grazed her ribs with her teeth. When she nuzzled her neck and tickled the sensitive skin behind her knees. She liked it when she asked permission with her eyes to kiss the insides of her thighs delicately and she liked it when she’d pulled the blankets around them tightly as if protecting them from the dangers of the world outside their hotel room window.

    They lay together for some time, exchanging delicate words and even more delicate kisses. Without her telling her, without Yelena even being conscious of it, Kate had given her exactly what she’d needed. She’d given her sanctuary.

    “Do you remember the first time we did this,” Kate whispered as she traced Yelena’s eyebrow with the tip of her finger. “You told me how you felt nothing the first time you took someone’s life?”

    “Yes,” Yelena whispered back. She remembered. She remembered a night very much like this one, but how the tables had turned.

    “I know it’s awful, but feeling the way that you do is so much better than feeling nothing. You told me that.” Yelena nodded silently, her brow furrowed. “You are so far away from the person they tried to make you,” Kate continued, searching for her eyes. “And whilst I’m here, there is no chance in hell that I am letting them make you think anything different.” Kate’s took Yelena’s chin in her hands gently and turned it so that their eyes could meet, so that Yelena couldn’t look away. The love that Yelena found there made her want to laugh and cry and scream.

    “So, you cannot get rid of me. Tomorrow we’re packing our bags and going south,” Kate announced confidently. She smiled a little stubborn smile and Yelena couldn’t help but smile back. Kate’s good moods were always irritatingly infectious and Yelena struggled to mount any type of defence against them. You would have thought that after all this time she would have managed to build up some level of immunity.

    Yelena raised an eyebrow and drew Kate closer for one final kiss before the blonde insisted on sleep. “I think you are already packed.”

    “I think you should quit whilst you’re ahead.”

    Yelena Rigby Chapter Notes Hello! Sorry this one has been a slightly longer wait. Life finds a way doesn’t it? This is the penultimate European chapter so enjoy it! Next up we have a phone call that has been a very long time coming. Try not to get too excited. Guesses on who it’s between in the comments please.

    Thank you all for reading and being generally awesome!

    Yelena woke gently, Kate’s arm still draped around her waist, her slow and rhythmic breathing tickling softly against the back of her neck. Crisp winter sunlight cast light and shadow across the room and the sounds of a city coming to life floated in through the open window. It must have been well gone nine. Good, they deserved the rest. Lucky sat, gently nosing at her hand that was hung over the edge of the bed. Maybe she hadn’t woken as gently as she’d thought. The dog was clearly hungry and restless but didn’t want to wake his mother, so he’d opted to disturb his other mother; the one he loved less. Yelena couldn’t fault him for loving Kate more. He was Kate’s dog and she was infinitely more loveable.

    A little reluctantly the blonde slipped out of her girlfriend’s grasp and trudged over to Lucky’s food and water bowls. She rinsed them, filled them and then quietly set them down for a very thankful dog to dig in. Whilst he was enjoying himself she threw on some sweatpants, boots, a sweater, her winter coat and a beanie and found Lucky’s lead. After placing a gentle kiss upon her girlfriend’s cheek she grabbed Lucky’s lead and took a very grateful dog for a very wintery walk.

    The family had arrived in Mostar the afternoon before and checked into a hotel just east of the Neretva. Alexei had chosen to take out Melina to see the city, rather unsubtly hinting towards his desire for a romantic evening between the two of them. Yelena had made all the expected disgusted daughter remarks, it was practically her job, but had smiled and waved them off happily. The love her parents had found in each other, the love they’d all found in each other, during such a testing and supposedly artificial time never once left her feeling anything other than warm, happy and grateful. Yelena also found herself very grateful for the gift of alone time with Kate.

    And that alone time consisted of dog walking in the snow, hot baths, rewatching their favourite episodes of the American Office whilst they brushed out each other’s hair, sharing a bottle of red over dinner at the hotel restaurant and getting meat sweats before falling asleep in each other’s arms with Yelena moaning about how uncomfortably full she was. All in all, their day had been pretty spot on, and quite the contrast to the day before. Lucky pulled happily against his lead. Yelena had thought about taking both dogs out but she’d had zero desire to sneak into her parents' hotel room that morning. She shivered slightly in thought of what her poor darling might have witnessed the previous night. It’s okay Fanny, mama will liberate you soon enough.

    Doggie paws pitter-pattered against the stone cobbled streets of Mostar as Yelena and Lucky walked past restaurants and bars serving breakfast to tourists out of medieval townhouses. Yelena politely declined their requests for her to come inside and sit down for a Bosnian style breakfast, despite her appetitive having returned, and instead persevered up and round to the left, to the Old Bridge. She would cross it and turn to the right. It was as simple as that. The hotel would be there, it was on the map, the one next to the mosque.

    Yelena stepped foot on the bridge as Lucky tugged enthusiastically, willing her forward as her apprehension willed her back. The snow-covered white stone was slippery beneath her feet and even her impeccable balance was struggling to adjust to the different forces that were pulling and pushing against her body. As the two blondes made it to the crest of the bridge Yelena dug in her heels and held fast on Lucky’s lead, bringing him to an unceremonious stop. She mumbled a small apology as he u-turned back to sniff confusedly at her feet. Yelena sighed and looked out across the river to the south. Café patrons still sat in the small courtyard gardens that lined the river with their teas and cigarettes. Lucky pulled Yelena to the north side of the bridge where she could see back towards the centre of the minaret- adorned City. It was crazy to think that just over thirty years earlier the bridge beneath her feet had been almost completely destroyed. Now it stood as a symbol of reconciliation. The significance wasn’t lost on Yelena.

    With a bracing intake of breath the Russian trudged onwards, much to Lucky’s delight. The descent was steep and slippery but Yelena negotiated it easily with a little more certainty in her step. She hung a right at the bottom of the bridge and passed some more cafés. A little further up there was a mosque and then a hammam on the right. Yelena made a mental note to book herself and Kate in for a treatment once all this was over, and then checked the name of the mosque. The bronze plaque read ‘Hadži-Kurtova džamija’, ‘džamija’ being the Bosnian word for mosque. She was in the right place, she was on the right street. Her street. She will have walked these cobblestones before, probably with her mother or father or both. She would have maybe played out here, or maybe in the courtyard of the mosque with the cats that undoubtedly patrolled there. Yelena smiled to herself a little as she caught sight of a free little bowl of kibble that the mosque’s staff must have left out for the feline friends. Maybe her father had prayed in this mosque, Yelena thought, maybe her mother too, she didn’t know. She did know that if they had, it had done them no good. Not in life anyway. Her small smile turned sour as she tried to shake her darker thoughts from existence. She would have to keep a clear head from here on out, it was imperative. She couldn’t spiral again as things may only get harder and she knew that at one point, there was something she was going to have to do by herself.

    Lucky pulled the ex-assassin a little further down the street until they reached it. There was a small amount of covered decking at the front. A few late stragglers were taking their breakfast of pastries with meats, cheeses and olives underneath the outdoor heaters. One couple caught her eye and offered Yelena a polite smile. She smiled back before breaking their gaze and taking in the rest of the building. Above the decking hung a sign. ‘Hotel Gümüş Restaurant & Bar’. It was clearly once a residential building, Yelena could see that from the structure of the place. Her hand tightened unconsciously around Lucky’s lead as he sat patiently, clearly sensing that now was not the time for a repeat of his earlier impatience. This was it. This could be it. Her home. Or something that had been, for a small part of her life, for the most formative part. It was funny how the most formative years were the ones that were lost to faded memories and shrouded dreams. Yelena’s eyes roamed. The first floor of the building was lined with sandstone, as was traditional. But it wasn’t old sandstone, it was relatively new, clean and bright. The second floor was painted white and each double- glazed window was lined with a wooden frame. Yelena assumed the wood theme probably continued inside, which was fairly usual in these types of hotels. From what the blonde could see from under the snow, the roof was new as well, with the bright, rusty orange of the terracotta tiles making itself known. The hotel was a far cry from the one she and Kate were staying in, where the windows were still single pane and the stone was still medieval, but that’s what shelling did to a building.

    Yelena retrieved her phone from her coat pocket. She’d messaged Kate just as she was leaving to tell her she’d left with Lucky for a walk. Now she’d message her to request she meet her for breakfast. Now was as good a time as any to revisit the past, but there was no way she was doing it without Kate.

    The blonde headed past the couples on the decking and stepped through into reception. She’d been right. There was a lot of wood. Wood panelling and white walls, it was a thing. After checking with the woman at reception if it was okay to have Lucky inside, they were led through to the indoor dining room which was a lot warmer and almost completely deserted. Why tourists insisted on taking their breakfast in the snow was beyond her, but she supposed if she were a romantic then maybe she’d think otherwise. Because she wasn’t a romantic at all. No ma’am. And she certainly wasn’t hopelessly in love.

    Once they were seated Yelena checked her phone again to find a message from Kate. She was twenty minutes away. She could kill twenty minutes easy right? Twenty minutes with her own thoughts and very little stimuli. Easy. Totally fine.

    First, she ordered some tea. Then read the menu seven times until her tea arrived. She drank her tea, tapped her foot incessantly, drank some more tea because they had filled her glass as soon as she’d consumed the last drop, avoided small talk with the receptionist-come-waitress who might have been coming onto her (did she give off some sort of vibe because she needed to find the off switch), all interspersed with giving Lucky the love and attention he deserved. The golden retriever started to shuffle excitedly and look towards the reception as his paws did a happy tippy tappy dance on the tiled floor. Kate was there. Thank god, Kate was there, and not just because she wanted to use her as human shield between herself and her server. “Good morning,” Kate smiled warmly and leant down to deliver the softest kiss to Yelena’s cheek. Kate’s cheek was cold against her own, but her lips were warm and Yelena wanted them against hers.

    “Good morning,” she smiled back as Kate gave Lucky the biggest, tightest hug before she removed her coat, hat and scarf and sat opposite Yelena.

    “I see you found the place okay?” Kate asked. Although she smiled fondly, Yelena easily detected the concern in her eyes. She really wanted to know if Yelena was feeling okay, which she was. Or as well as could be expected.

    Yelena nodded reassuringly as her warm hand found Kate’s cold one. “Yes. It was exactly where he said it would be.”

    “Well, that is good to hear,” Kate said as she took a sip of Yelena’s tea. Tea was probably the only thing Yelena didn’t mind sharing with Kate, considering there seemed to be an infinite supply of it, but it was probably polite to order the brunette her own. A few minutes later the now slightly put out receptionist re-appeared. She was either disgruntled by Kate’s appearance and the way that Yelena hung on her every word, or the way that Kate had consumed all of Yelena’s fourth glass of tea. The blonde very quickly ordered Kate her own beverage, and breakfast for the both of them.

    The couple chatted happily whilst they feasted on breads, fruits, cheese and olives. They’d confirmed that Lucky enjoyed sudzuk, which made sense because who didn’t? Well, vegetarians and vegans, but that was beside the point. Having Kate was such a wonderful distraction. Everything she did she did with such passion and zeal. Every olive was possibly the best olive she’d ever eaten. The bread was the freshest, the cheese was the tangiest, the tea was the most comforting. In anyone else, Yelena would find this unrivalled level of enthusiasm grating, in Kate she found it spellbinding. She reminded her so much of herself in a way, the few years she had after escaping and destroying the Red Room. She’d wanted to try everything and anything. Whatever music she could get her hands on, she would listen to. Any artists, any genre, any period; she’d just wanted to fill her ears with it. She’d wanted to taste everything and discern her own tastes. She’d wanted to wear crazy clothes and try different styles to find her own. She’d simply wanted to consume as she’d be deprived for so long, and of so much. Back then, those years, those were her real formative years. Those were the years that made the woman sat before Kate that morning. But then Natasha had died and that zeal had left her. She didn’t care for the taste of anything. She found no pleasure in the way she dressed, it didn’t match what she felt inside anymore. And all the music she’d learned to love reminded her of her sister in some way so she’d simply stopped listening. Kate had changed that from the moment they’d met. Her passion and her zeal, the pure unadulterated joy she could take from the simplest of things. She was showing Yelena how to live again, how to feel again and how to love again without the fear of losing, again. They finished their meals with a coffee each, because caffeine was incredibly important, and Yelena wondered out loud about how many breakfasts she’d actually had in the building in which they were sat.

    Kate smiled sadly. “Not enough. Are you ready?”

    Yelena took a steadying breath. “I think so.” Of course, she wasn’t ready. She would never be totally and completely ready, but she was prepared enough for what might come next, especially with Kate by her side.

    “Do you want me to wait downstairs?” Her girlfriend asked.

    “No, no. I want you with me.” The blonde reached forward and captured Kate’s hand. She glanced at the waitress who was busy collecting dishes on the decking out front, and placed a gentle kiss upon Kate’s knuckles. The brunette smiled and Yelena smiled back. Kate’s eyes contentedly in the light of the dining room and Yelena’s breath caught momentarily. Yelena always thought she’d never make it into her forties, she never thought her cause of death would be beautiful, Manhattan socialite. More like a bullet to the brain. She certainly knew which one she preferred and it was most definitely the more slow and painful one. With a check to make sure the waitress was still occupied on the front decking, the two Avengers got to their feet quietly, and with Lucky in tow, snuck further into the quiet hotel. Round to the left of the reception room was a flight of wooden panel stairs that presumably led to the rooms above. Yelena led the way.

    Just as she reached the top she felt Kate’s hand close gently around her wrist. The blonde turned at the touch. Her girlfriend stood two steps below, her violet eyes looking up at her with concern.

    “Just take your time, okay?” Kate said as her thumb played across the skin of Yelena’s wrist. “I’m here,” she reassured softly. Kate was worried about her and justifiably so, as Kate had been with her two nights previous. She’d seen how the truth had affected Yelena. Not even that. She’d seen how the potential for truth, the potential for gut-wrenchingly, painfully hard truth had affected her. And she’d seen how their methods of extracting the truth had sent her spiralling. Sure, meat sweats, hot baths, soft kisses and nice wine had gone some way to allaying her anxieties, but that kind of reaction to stress was not something Yelena was used to, and it was not something that even the most well-trained of minds would bounce back from completely unscathed.

    Yelena smiled warmly in an attempt to dispel some of her fears, brought her arms to rest upon Kate’s shoulders and clasped her own hands together to draw her girlfriend closer. It wasn’t often that her girlfriend stood a few inches shorter than her and it something she needed to take full advantage of. Yelena brought Kate’s mouth to hers, forcing her girlfriend onto her tiptoes, and softly captured her lips with her own. Kate’s arms snuck inside her winter coat and clutched at the material of her hoodie, pulling the blonde down onto her lips intently. Kate’s body pressed against her own and Yelena could feel her girlfriend breathing her in, willing her closer in an attempt to make her feel her words of reassurance, in an attempt to will any fears or anxieties away. After what never felt like quite long enough, Kate broke their kiss and whispered, “I’m here and I’m not going anywhere”. Her voice was breathless but determined, and Yelena knew she meant every word.

    “I know,” Yelena whispered back as she placed a gentle kiss upon Kate’s forehead. She gave Kate’s hand a grateful squeeze before she turned and persevered to the top of the steps and through a door that read ‘Rooms 1-5’ with her girlfriend’s hand still held firmly within her own.

    The first thing Yelena noticed were the walls. They were all bright white. The floors, that were hard, cold travertine, were covered in Anatolian rugs of deep reds and royal blues. The wooden panelling continued upstairs with wooden door frames and wooden doors scattered across the walls. The rooms weren’t positioned along a corridor as with a built-for-purpose hotel, these rooms were laid as if they were used to be rooms off one central living space, the space they were stood in now. Across from where they stood, on the other side of the central space was room five. To their left was a small hallway and off of that were four doors, presumably rooms one to four; two on the left, one on the right, and one at the end of the corridor. Yelena swallowed, she couldn’t take her eyes from it. Two rooms to the left, one on the right, kitchen at the end. They’d shared with two other families. How did she know that? There had been a kitchen, a bathroom and a communal space that they’d shared. “You recognise it, don’t you?” Came Kate’s voice.

    “It feels familiar,” Yelena explained. And it did but something wasn’t right. Her eyes darted to the window of the communal space and before even thinking her feet had taken her to it. It wasn’t the right view. In her dream she could see to the city outside, her view had been higher.

    “It definitely used to be a home. You can tell,” Kate spoke again but Yelena didn’t hear her words. Her mind was working at a million miles per hour.

    “I think we should go up again,” Yelena said before striding back past Kate and out into the stairwell. She strode up another flight, her rather short but powerful legs taking two steps at a time. Yelena paused momentarily at the top, ‘Rooms 6-10’. The blonde shook her head. It couldn’t be the second floor, the view simply wasn’t high enough. She could see the other side of the river clearly from their window, it had to be higher. Yelena dashed up another flight of stairs to the third floor. She’d made it to the top floor of the town house. ‘Rooms 11- 15’, it said on the door. A breathless Kate and a highly amused Lucky joined her at the top of stairs.

    “This is it.” Yelena said quietly as her eyes fixed on the door handle. She could feel her heart pick up its pace, she could hear it beat an anxious tattoo against the inside of her rib cage. Beyond that door, what would she see? White washed walls and travertine floors? Or would she see shelled interiors, flickering fluorescent lights and muzzle flashes? Brass cooled her fingertips. Yelena looked down. Her hand was grasping the door handle but she didn’t remember her feet carrying her to the door. She needed the truth, more than anything, and to find it she needed to know that this was the place. That this was the place where she lost her mother. She needed to know so that maybe, just maybe, she could find her again. She turned the handle.

    A cold sweat crept across the back of her neck despite the cold. The third floor was a carbon copy of the first. White walls, rugged floors and an identical layout. Yelena’s gaze immediately fell to the end of the corridor. Room fourteen. She had to blink away the ghostly visions of dark corridors. Her eyes unwittingly found their way to the ceiling, something that wasn’t as intact the last time she’d set foot down this corridor. There was no cold evening rain to penetrate her skin, there was no piercing glass to rain down upon her and penetrate her bones, just white ceilings and modern spot lighting. All white. All fresh. Paint over it and it’s like nothing ever happened. Paint it bright enough and no one will see the stained walls and blood red floors that were there before.

    Yelena’s fingers flexed and then clenched tightly into fists. Her breathing had shallowed and she was caught between resisting the need to run or vomit, or on press on. She felt a gentle touch in the small of her back and soft lips brush her temple. Yelena closed her eyes and leaned into the touch, just for a moment. She let it ground her and pull her back into the moment. Again, Kate was her anchor, her harbour, her sanctuary. After a few moments more the blonde opened her eyes slowly and she was back to reality. White walls and travertine floors. The urge to bring up her recently consumed breakfast and five litres of tea began to recede and she found that she could focus on the door at the end of the corridor with far more purpose.

    “This corridor,” Yelena whispered, “This structure was damaged”. She pointed to the room on the right-hand side. “And much of the ceiling was gone. These rooms were for other families but the apartment at the end, I think that was mine.”

    “How do you know?” Kate asked, clearly surprised at the clarity with which Yelena could recall her supposedly lost childhood. The blonde simply shrugged.

    “I see it most nights.”

    Kate brow furrowed as if trying to piece stories together. She knew about Yelena’s dreams but not in great detail. Maybe it was about time Yelena shared that detail, preferably over a vodka or ten.

    “The apartment was like a studio. It had a small kitchen diner, and we shared a bed that was against the far wall,” Yelena explained as she moved down the corridor, her fingertips brushing against the walls and the door frames, taking in the textures that felt so familiar yet so abstract and foreign. She had done it so many times before in her dreams but it had never felt like this.

    She took a few more steps. Her body was tense as if bracing herself for the inevitable concussive blast that would throw her to her knees. Of course, the blast never came, but she still felt its echoes.

    Within the blink of an eye Yelena had reached the end of the corridor. This was it. The door from her dreams. The door she’d spent thirty years trying to walk through. “This is it,” she said matter-of-factly, “Room 14”.

    “Do you want to go in?” Kate asked.

    “We can’t,” Yelena said quietly.

    “What? Why?” Her girlfriend was clearly confused. She could understand Yelena not wanting to, but not being able to just didn’t make any sense. The blonde smiled ruefully at their bad luck. Wait thirty years, travel thousands of miles, risk their lives, and the room was occupied. But of course, it was a hotel.

    “There are people inside,” Yelena explained. “The shower is running.” She’d heard it the moment she stepped onto the floor.

    She placed a gentle hand against the lacquered wood of the door and then rested her forehead against it. It was so close, it could wait. She didn’t need to go inside to confirm the address with her mother, she didn’t need to go inside for any reason other than to be able to claim back some agency from her demons, to be able to find some semblance of closure. That could wait until a time where it could be done on her terms, finding her mother couldn’t. Yelena breathed in the smell of the wood and the varnish. She took comfort in it. The rush of running water stopped and Yelena took a step back from the door. “We should go.”

    “We can look around more if you want, you’re doing so well babe.” Yelena smiled. Kate being the ultimate cheerleader was very on brand and just as delightful. “We have what we came for,” Yelena explained. Kate frowned, clearly still concerned. “But-“ “Kate, darling,” Yelena interjected, as she placed soothing hands upon Kate’s arms. She squeezed. “I’m okay,” she reassured with a smile. Worried eyes searched hers for any tell-tale sign that Yelena was not quite as okay as she claimed. “Hey,” Yelena whispered and her voice softened even more. “I really am okay. I will tell you if I’m not. There are no more answers here Kate, only ghosts. The ghosts can wait.”

    Yelena and Kate left the hotel swiftly. They did their best to elude the waitress-come- receptionist on their way out and took the immediate left back up to the Old Bridge. By the time they’d paused to take in the beautiful wintery scenes of snow-capped domes and terracotta tiles, Yelena had texted her mother.

    ‘It’s the place.’

    The limestone beneath Yelena’s fingers was cold to the touch, but she enjoyed the visceral nature of the sensation. It centred her. She stared out across the river gorge and watched the deep green waters of the Neretva flow languidly through it. In a few weeks' time, when the snow has melted, the river would flow far more furiously. Kate’s hand came to rest on top of Yelena’s, and the partners stood together in silent solidarity, Lucky amusing himself with passers-by.

    Her mother would be speaking to Kate’s contact at Interpol, probably at that very moment. They had the address, they had a favour owed and soon they would have the names and faces of those registered to that address at the time that Yelena was taken. If her parents had been living there legally, her mother should be able to find their names. If they held driver's licences or identification cards, she’d find their faces. From there it wouldn’t be too difficult to find birth certificates, or death certificates for that matter. There was the very real possibility that once Yelena arrived back at their hotel she would be faced with some very harsh realities, but harsh realities were better than false hopes she supposed. Kate’s fingers tightened around Yelena’s. “We don’t have to go back right away,” she said, sensing Yelena’s apprehension. “We can just spend some time here or wander about a little and get some lunch. Whatever you want. There’s no rush.”

    Yelena couldn’t keep the smile from her face. Kate had tried to feed her more times in the last twenty four hours than any other day on record, and it was becoming clear that Kate’s method of caregiving consisted of sitcoms, duvets, kisses and a thirteen-course tasting menu. The blonde shook her head at the thought of all the snacks they’d accrued from their three hour drive the day before, snacks that were now stockpiled in their hotel room. Undoubtedly Kate would want to return with more snacks before the morning was out, despite them literally having eaten twenty minutes prior. Yes, Yelena could eat, she was her father’s daughter after all, but after a night of meat sweats and a morning of tea and feta, her stomach wasn’t exactly calling out to be satiated. In fact, it was doing quite the opposite. “I am okay,” she shrugged good-naturedly, “I am not really hungry.”

    “Not even for those little kebabs?” Kate teased lightly and Yelena audibly groaned. She was about to have flashbacks, and unlike the ones from the hotel earlier, she wasn’t sure if her stomach could handle them. The trauma was just too fresh.

    Yelena slowly squared up to her girlfriend. Her eyes narrowed as they took in Kate’s amused little grin.“If you tell anyone that I didn’t finish that, I will kill you, do you understand?” The brunette’s grin widened and her eyes danced with delight. This was not the effect Yelena Belova was used to having on people. She was supposed to be scary and intimidating. People were supposed to quiver whenever they heard the utterance of her name. Of course, Kate Bishop was immune to Yelena’s intimidation tactics, that wasn’t to say the blonde couldn’t make her girlfriend quiver though.

    “There’s no shame in it,” Kate shrugged nonchalantly, “It’s a lot of meat.” This was actually true, it was a lot of meat. Not that it had been an unexpected amount but Yelena had decided that what would normally be a meal to share with say, your very willing partner, would actually be a meal that she wanted to enjoy for herself. So, Kate had ordered her own meal and Yelena was left without any help and subsequently Yelena had failed to finished. Not only had she moaned about being uncomfortably full for the rest of the evening, but she had also sulked about not having enough room for any sutlijaš. That was perhaps the biggest tragedy of them all.

    “There is shame,” Yelena sulked, thinking about how disappointed her Daddy would be. “There is a lot of shame. And soon I might have two families to bring shame upon.” Kate rolled her eyes and shook her head. “We could have just shared,” she reasoned. Reason was not what Yelena needed.

    “Zatk`nis” Yelena grumbled as she huffed and turned to look back out over the gorge, resting her elbows against the limestone.

    “That is just rude,” Kate proclaimed.

    Yelena shrugged and ‘tsked’ quietly with her tongue. “You don’t even know what I said.” “Yes, I do actually,” Kate said, a little haughtily. She was currently at her most Hermione Granger. “You told me to shut up,” she explained, clearly very pleased with herself, for she knew she was correct.

    Yelena’s lips quirked into an little downturned smile of appreciation. “I am impressed Kate Bishop.” And she was. Just a few weeks prior Kate knew next to no Russian. The brunette smiled a smug little smile. “I Youtubed Russian curses and insults, as they’re your kind of go-to.”

    “Idi na hui,” Yelena said with a smirk in an attempt to call Kate’s bluff. It only earned her a mirthful look and a swift slap on the arm. “Ow! Pizdets!” Yelena moaned with a frown and a pout as she rubbed her arm for dramatic effect. Kate Bishop had a slap on her, that was for sure.

    With another eye roll Kate threaded her arm through Yelena’s and dragged her away from the side of the bridge, towards the eastern side of the river and their hotel. “Where are you taking me?” Yelena asked suspiciously. The smirk on Kate’s face had not gone unnoticed. .

    “To your mother,” the brunette explained, “So she can also slap some manners into you.”

    The walk back to the hotel had been unexpectedly lovely. Most things with Kate Bishop turned out to be unexpectedly lovely. American Christmas, pizza with pineapple, The Avengers to name a few. But considering this walk should have been filled with severe worry, anxiety and trepidation, unexpectedly lovely should have been beyond even Kate’s capabilities, shouldn’t it? Yelena should never have underestimated her. She was the master of distraction. First, she continued her tease about Yelena’s failure to finish her dinner the night before. Then, she moved onto the roasted chestnut seller and insisted that, even if Yelena couldn’t manage any, it was about time she made the leap and tried some herself. You know? Really experience the culture. Then she dragged Yelena into a small independent souvenir store filled with hand blown tea sets and water-pipes, wooden carvings beautifully painted Arabic calligraphy. One painted dish had the word ‘Lucky’ painted on it in Arabic script. Yelena had even found herself joking that they should ask for a custom one to read ‘Fanny’, so they could have a matching pair, and the couple had snorted and giggled a little too loudly in the quiet store. With a slightly embarrassed smile, Yelena picked up some lokum for later, not to be shared, and met Kate back outside.

    The two then wandered the medieval streets at their own pace, Kate with map in hand as she pointed out old sites and read little anecdotes about their history. Suddenly Yelena found herself wondering how many years her family might have gone back in Mostar. Had they walked these streets? And for how many years? Could they have been traders or crafters, or did they come to the city from the nearby villages in the Austro-Hungarian period? There were so many questions, so many possibilities and instead of being overwhelmed by trepidation Yelena felt just the slightest bit of hope.

    That hope faded quickly however, as she opened the door to her hotel room to discover her parents’ stoney faces. The laptop was closed, which meant that they had finished their search, which meant one of two things. They hadn’t found what they’d been looking for, or they’d found exactly what they’d been looking for and it wasn’t the best news. The cold sweat Yelena had felt at Hotel Gümüs returned in an instant, almost as quickly as Kate’s fingers had entwined themselves in hers. Fuck you anxiety, Kate Bishop has got your number. Whatever the news, they could deal with. Yelena had a family, she had a mother, she had a father, the only thing she was missing was the truth. She wanted it and she was ready for it.

    “Darling,” Melina sprung to her feet and pulled Yelena into the fiercest of hugs. So, they’d found something and it wasn’t all good. Yelena wouldn’t let her heart sink, they’d found something and that in itself was more than she had the day before.

    “You found them?” Yelena asked.

    Melina drew back from their embrace and took her daughter’s face delicately between her hands. Her face was pained and her eyes were swimming with emotion.

    She nodded solemnly. “We think so.” She took a steadying breath and blinked back the glassiness in her eyes. She was trying to draw upon her cool, stoic, Black Widow demeanour but she was failing, which in a way was a comfort. If she was going to be delivered bad news she wanted it to come from her mother. “There are passport records and census information that links a young couple and their daughter to that building in the early Nineties.” She swallowed, the older widow was withholding information.

    “And?” Yelena asked, a little impatiently.

    Melina took Yelena’s hands in her own and breathed a steadying breath. After a moment, she confirmed Yelena’s suspicions. “There is a death certificate for the father.” Yelena’s legs felt heavy. She took a breath and then another as she tore her eyes from her mother’s. There was too much softness, too much sympathy, too much pity. She needed to sit down. She took her hands from her mother’s and took herself to the end of the bed where she sat quietly. Her biological father was dead. She would never know him, never hear his voice, never know what made him smile or laugh or cry. She would never know him. Alexei shuffled quietly across the room and settled down next to her on the bed. A large, tattooed hand closed around hers. She knew that he wouldn’t know what to say, but of course he didn’t need to say anything, not really. She was just so lucky to have him. To know him, to know his voice and his laugh and his smile. With her other hand she traced the letters that adorned his knuckles and she felt his hand tighten around hers.

    Melina settled in the chair opposite the bed and reached out to place her hand upon her daughter’s, completing the set. “He was killed in action. There is no certificate for the mother or the daughter.”

    “Are there names?” Yelena asked. There were passports, surely there were names. “Yes,” Melina nodded. “Karlo Delić and Nadija Delić. There is a birth certificate for their daughter Elena, born July First, nineteen eighty-nine.”

    Yelena’s breath caught in her chest as a sudden rush of warmth filled it. Her heart tightened as the realisation hit. They had named her. The name she had was the one they gave her. Elena.

    Her eyes found Kate’s. She smiled warmly. It was as if she knew what Yelena was thinking and feeling. Ever since they’d let their walls down at Christmas, ever since they’d let each other in, it was as if they’d struck a connection that was getting deeper by the day. “They named me Elena?” Yelena asked, vocalising her thoughts. She couldn’t quite believe it. Melina nodded and kissed her hand gently. “Yes darling,” she whispered. There was emotion in her mother’s voice, emotion she hadn’t heard since the time she returned to them, since the time they discovered they’d traded one daughter for another.

    “I have the name they gave me. I’ve always had it.” Hot tears stained her cheeks as she struggled to find her next words. Strong arms encircled her and she was pulled into her father’s crushing embrace. She felt him press his lips atop her head and she gave herself up to the comfort he was offering her. Melina never let go of her hand. She brushed her thumb across Yelena’s knuckles soothingly and the blonde clung on for dear life. “They were with me this whole time,” she said quietly as her father held her.

    Once her tears had subsided and her breathing had evened out, Yelena gave her father’s hand a small squeeze and he released her from his embrace. Lucky had been let off his lead and he was sat with his chin resting gently against Yelena’s thigh. She couldn’t help but smile, and part of her couldn’t wait to be back at home in New York curled up in bed with Kate, Lucky and Fanny, eating shit, chatting shit, watching even worse shit on Netflix. When it all came together, it really was going to be quite something.

    “There are photographs too, on the laptop,” Melina explained quietly and Yelena’s eyes met hers. Photographs. She was going to see their faces. She was going to see her face. The face she’d spent over ten thousand nights searching for. She’d clawed at vinyl, clawed through blood and water, clawed at the arms that tore her away, but she wouldn’t have to claw any longer, all she would have to do was open that laptop. Her heart started to pound again, but not in trepidation. “We will leave you for a little bit to look yourself,” Melina continued, pulling Yelena from her thoughts. “This time is for you.” The older widow gave her daughter’s hand one final squeeze before she relinquished it. Alexei stood up from the bed and gave his daughter a reassuring smile.

    “We are just next door,” he said, his voice uncharacteristically earnest. “I know,” Yelena said softly. How grateful she was for him and her mother. Kate stepped forward and knelt before her. She smiled tenderly and kissed the palm of her hand tenderly. It was intimate and in front of her parents, but at this point Yelena was beyond caring. “I’m going to go too, just for a little while,” Kate said delicately. She wanted to give Yelena some space and some privacy. Kate knew that this was Yelena’s moment, and as long as the blonde didn’t think she’d need the support, it was best left that way. This was Yelena’s journey. Sure, Kate had tagged along for the ride to support her girlfriend, Yelena had wanted her there, but the ex-assassin had been on this road herself for over thirty years and it wasn’t all dual carriageway.

    Yelena’s thumb gently grazed across the soft skin of Kate’s cheek. She smiled and nodded gently. Kate smiled back. She rose to her feet, took Yelena’s tear-stained cheeks between her fingertips and kissed her chastely and tenderly. The brunette broke their kiss. Her eyes were still closed as she rested her forehead against Yelena’s. Kate was finding it difficult to drag herself away. She was torn between being a supportive girlfriend and actually being a supportive girlfriend. Everything in her heart was screaming at her to stay with Yelena but everything in her head was telling her to give her the time and space she needed to feel and process. The blonde felt Kate sigh as her heart relinquished.

    “You message if you need us, okay?”

    Hazel eyes met violet and Yelena gave Kate her best and most assured smile. “I will.” “Okay,” Kate said, more to herself than anyone else. “Okay.”

    With a final kiss to one of Yelena’s flushed cheeks, Kate said goodbye and the familial entourage filed out of the room and into the one adjacent. The door closed with a soft click and then Yelena was alone. For a moment she simply sat. There was no rush, she told herself. She’d waited thirty years, what was another thirty minutes? After a few minutes she got up and threw off her big winter coat and boots so she was left in her sweatpants and hoodie. Much better. She boiled the kettle and made herself a hot cup of tea, no milk, and took it over to the bedside table. She then grabbed the laptop and placed it on the bed before getting comfortable underneath the comforter.

    Yelena settled back against the headboard and sipped at her scalding hot tea. She tutted to herself as she burned her tongue, what happened to ‘if she could wait thirty years, blah blah blah’? After a few minutes the tea had cooled to a satisfactory temperature so Yelena dragged the laptop onto her lap and continued to sip. All this new information had come so quickly. She had parents, they had names and very soon they would have faces. She had a surname that wasn’t Belova, that was weird as hell. And they’d called her Elena. They’d actually given her her name. Had it been a coincidence? Or had the Red Room simply changed it to the Russian spelling? Either way, she was still Elena and that made her feel a whole host of things. To have something that was still with her, something they gave her that survived her trafficking, her abuse in the Red Room, her subjugation. Something that wasn’t erased by countless days, weeks, months of conditioning and brain washing, to have something so significant as a name, Yelena couldn’t quite articulate how she felt about it. But it made her heart full and tight and it somehow made them feel almost tangible. They weren’t just the people who gave her life any more, she didn’t just share their genetics, she was a person to them, she was their person. She was their Elena, and that hadn’t changed. Fighting back the tears that threatened to overcome her, she took a deep, steadying breath and then exhaled with purpose. She took a final sip of tea, placed it back down onto the bedside table and then clicked the laptop open. The screen took a moment to flicker to life before the geometric scanner recognised her face and gave her access. Kate had said it was one of the most secure ways to protect a laptop, Yelena had argued that if she could take someone’s head off and use it to access their most private of information, the geometric scanner wasn’t nearly secure enough.

    For a brief moment a blue loading circle spun around the cursor as the laptop worked to load up Kate’s profile. Suddenly Yelena regretted downloading so many different Sims 2 expansions. After a few seconds more the blue Windows screen was replaced by Kate’s desktop which had several browser windows open. Two black and white faces, side by side, stared back at her. Both had dark eyes, probably exacerbated by the lighting of the Nineteen Eighties photobooth the images would have been captured in.

    Yelena tapped and pulled at the screen, zooming in on the images that she’d found there. Her father’s hair had a lightness to it despite the shadows of the photograph, it must have been a light brown or dirty blonde. His nose was strong and broad, unlike her small and slightly upturned one but the curve of his mouth, the arch of his brow and the angle of his jaw were all familiar. Yelena went to trace the lines of his face but the touchscreen contorted her view. She cursed modern technology as she zoomed back out and corrected her mistake. He didn’t look like a soldier, but then again, most men didn’t. He probably hadn’t touched a rifle before the conflict and Yelena found herself wondering if he’d been a teacher or a car salesman or a grocer before a gun was put in his hand, and for the first time Yelena knew that she would probably be able to find out, with just a click of a button. It was an odd feeling, knowing so little for so long and now suddenly having nearly everything at her fingertips. Everything except her parents themselves.

    The ex-assassin swallowed as she summoned enough courage to look at the other photograph on the screen. It was clearly taken in the same photobooth and Yelena smiled a little sadly to herself. They’d gone together. It was like a moment captured in time. A couples’ trip to the store for passport photos, maybe even a family trip. Yelena could almost see it in her mind’s eye and she took comfort in it. It was like a memory that wasn’t and the blonde revelled in it. She wiped away mutinous tears as she tried to focus on the young woman in front of her, on the face that had eluded her for so many years. It was odd but she had to force herself to look, as if putting a face and a name to her dreams, her memories, made them real. If her mother was real then the reality of her being dead or missing was all the realer too. After one final intake of breath Yelena forced her eyes to look, to really look. She’d had thirty years to imagine her mother’s face but it had been something she’d never managed. She’d never expected to see herself staring back at her. Her eyes, her nose, the delicate shape of her face; it was like staring back in time but this photo wasn’t taken ten years ago, this photo was taken nearly forty years earlier. This was her mother, there was no doubt. She was so beautiful, and it was weird because Yelena never really looked at herself that way, she was a tool, but this woman in front of her who shared her eyes and her smile and the colour of her hair, this woman was so beautiful, because she was her mother.

    Yelena snapped the laptop shut as her emotions threatened to take over. She had to look away, for now, she had to look to away. It was so much after so little and as wonderful as it was, there was only so much the blonde had capacity for. She knew she was on the edge, she knew that her chest was tight, that her heart was racing and that her breathing was irregular. Yelena pushed the laptop away and stared blankly at the leafy landscape painting that hung upon the far wall of her hotel room facing the bed. Landscapes were supposed to be calming, right? After a moment she closed her eyes and remembered Kate’s words from a few nights previous. Breathe, two, three, four, five. Hold, two, three, four, five. Out, two, three, four, five. If she focused hard enough, she could feel Kate’s arms around her, her lips pressed against her temple, her breath against her skin.

    The comforter felt rough against her skin as she threw off her sweatshirt and crawled underneath it. She drew a pillow to herself and held it tight, it wasn’t something she’d ever done before but it felt comforting in that moment. She focused on her breathing once more, hoping that sleep would take her. She needed to switch off, just for a while. She needed her brain to stop and rest and process, if she could just do that.

    Breathe, two, three, four, five. Hold, two, three, four, five. Out, two, three, four, five. She felt her mother’s arms around her, her lips pressed against her temple and her breath against her skin.

    Soft fingertips ghosted across the smooth skin of her stomach. Although her eyes were still closed, a lazy smile pulled at the corners of Yelena’s mouth. Kate was with her. The blonde snuck one eye open to spy on her girlfriend. Her violet eyes were alive in the light of the winter sunset that had infiltrated the room and were rather indulgently marvelling at the sight of her girlfriend’s bare midriff. Yelena must have been asleep for hours if the sun was painting such shades across their hotel walls.

    “Hey,” Yelena said quietly. To Kate’s credit she didn’t quite jump out of her skin, but her face certainly betrayed her. She’d been caught.

    “Oh, h-hi,” She stuttered. Yep, she got caught perving alright.

    “You just let yourself in?” Yelena asked a little sternly, her eyebrow quirked. She wanted to make Kate squirm, just momentarily. Payback for turning her into such a soft bitch. “Err, yes...” Kate managed, eyeing Yelena keenly, desperately trying to work out what the right answer should have been. “No?” she corrected. If she said both words perhaps Yelena would interpret them the way she wanted rather than the way that Kate actually meant them. “Well,” Yelena began as her hand captured Kate’s. She was drawing this out and it was unfair but it was also fun. “This,” she continued as she turned into her girlfriend and pulled the brunette’s arm around her, “Is a very nice way to wake up.”

    “Oh,” Kate visibly relaxed as Yelena pulled her close with a grin. “That was mean,” the brunette added with a pout and the blonde thought it would be rude to do anything else but attempt to kiss the pout away.

    “How are you feeling?” Kate asked as Yelena settled into her embrace, head tucked gently in the crook of her neck.
