The blonde nuzzled the warm skin that she found there and closed her eyes to focus on the feel of Kate, the sound of her breathing, the scent of the conditioner that she so religiously applied.

    “I am okay,” Yelena whispered. It was the truth. She’d seen her mother, seen her face, and she hadn’t dreamed about. Yelena would categorise that as a win/win. Of course, winning never came easily. To be a winner you needed to apply yourself, put in the hard work and make sacrifices; Yelena knew a lot about that.

    “It’s a lot to take in,” Kate reflected as the hand that had been tracing patterns across Yelena’s shoulder blades decided to change tack and proceeded to lose itself in the blonde’s sleep mussed locks.

    “I suppose,” Yelena shrugged, “But it’s more information than I had yesterday.” She pulled absentmindedly at the elasticated band of Kate’s pyjama bottoms and then released. It snapped back gently against Kate’s hip. The blonde found herself smiling. Kate had not only let herself back into their hotel room and snuck into bed with her, she’d made sure to get into her pyjamas for ultimate comfort. Yelena was in no way surprised; it was a very Kate Bishop thing to do.

    Kate responded with a small, “Hmm,” and then placed a delicate kiss atop Yelena’s head. “I’m so sorry,” she whispered after a moment longer and Yelena nuzzled closer, breathing her girlfriend in. Kate had nothing to be sorry for. She wasn’t responsible for her father’s death, her mother’s disappearance or Yelena’s own abduction. She wasn’t responsible for the years of subjugation or for Natasha’s death. The only thing she was responsible for was giving Yelena the strength to seek the truth.

    “Do not be sorry,” Yelena whispered as she played with the hem of Kate’s sweatshirt. After a moment she drew back slightly and hazel eyes met violet. Kate’s eyes were unsure, worried. She had seen Yelena break down only two nights previous, what was to say the same thing wouldn’t happen again? Well, the difference was, Yelena knew she wasn’t doing it by herself anymore. Sure, she’d invited Kate to come to Bosnia and Herzegovina with her, but once there, as soon as things became difficult, she’d shut down. She’d decided that she needed to take things on herself, to protect Kate from her past, who she had been and who she really was. But since then things had changed, because Kate was her future, and that future was going to be spent together, tackled together, discovered together.

    After that realisation Yelena’s burden had felt lighter, and she’d come to another decision, one that Kate wouldn’t necessarily be all pleased with. “I am just grateful you are here,” Yelena continued before she captured Kate’s lips with hers. She tugged on Kate’s sweatshirt to draw her close, giving her girlfriend permission explore with her hands and her mouth and her fingertips. Yelena liked giving Kate this, she liked giving her a way to love her that came instinctually to her. She didn’t want to deprive her of that or repress it. She wanted to feel close and intimate, and she wanted Kate to be able to express her love, not keep it hidden. The couple kissed and talked and smiled and laughed. They undressed each other before they jumped in the shower, and then helped each other pick out their outfits for dinner before towelling each other off. Kate checked her phone as Yelena was towel drying her hair, the brunette’s eyes went wide.

    “What? What is it?” Yelena asked, her brow furrowed with concern.

    “I um, I kinda asked someone at Bishop Security to run some searches for me, just in case something came up,” Kate revealed sheepishly.

    Yelena paused her towel drying and frowned curiously. “What kind of searches?” Kate shrugged a little awkwardly. “Census type stuff. Previous addresses, living relatives?” Their eyes met. Yelena’s brain hadn’t even got that far. Sure, she’d thought about ancestors and romanticised in her brain about having medieval agricultural lineage, who didn’t? But living relatives, actual living relatives... could there be? She swallowed. “Relative like… family?” The blonde asked disbelievingly. Her heart was racing but not like it had before. It was pounding out of her chest and in her ears, it wasn’t overwhelming, it didn’t have its own gravitational pull. No, it was excited, hopeful and suddenly she needed to know the contents of the message on Kate’s phone. She needed to know with every fibre of her being. Kate nods.

    Kate nodded as she glanced back down to the message she’d received. A smile crept to her lips and Yelena’s heart skipped a beat. “A grandmother,” Kate said softly. “You have a grandmother on your mother's side.”

    For a moment Yelena thought her heart had stopped altogether, she thought that she might just expire. A grandmother, a grandmother who might just have her eyes and her nose and the share the shape of her face. Kate dashed forward to catch her as Yelena felt the overwhelming need to sit down, clearly concerned that she was going to end up on her ass. She didn’t though. Her ass found a way, and she sat smiling broadly at the foot of the bed. “A grandmother?” Yelena asked disbelievingly. She needed to make sure she’d heard Kate right. After all the painful news, all the tragedy, all the struggle to get to this point, Yelena had to make sure that her mind hadn’t strayed into some defence-mechanism-triggered alternate multiverse.

    Kate came and knelt before her, much like she’d done before Yelena had been left alone with the laptop earlier that day. She gripped the blonde’s knees and nodded up at her with the softest and brightest of smiles Yelena had ever seen. “Yes,” was all Kate needed to say. Yelena leant forward to rest her forehead against Kate’s and then grinned idiotically at each other. The blonde was practically giddy which was not a term that was often used to describe her. “Does she live in the city?” Yelena whispered, her brain already working overtime to formulate a plan.

    Kate shook her head a little against Yelena’s and the Russian’s heart sank ever-so-slightly. “No,” Kate said softly, her tone a little guilty, “A place called Počit-elj?” Yelena’s stomach dropped. It was a place less than thirty minutes out of town, she’d seen it on brochures and coach tour itineraries. It was close enough to drive, they could go the next day.

    Was it too much? Maybe. Would her grandmother even want to even see her, the woman who looked so much like her daughter? Would she bring her only painful memories? To lose your daughter must be life shattering, to lose her and not have closure must have a constant hold over someone’s life. But she’d lost a granddaughter that day too. Had she wondered, just like Yelena, for the last thirty years? Had she dreamt and questioned and yearned like Yelena had? Undoubtedly. So, really whatever pain her grandmother still felt, it was a pain shared and perhaps rather poetically Yelena herself could be the one to bring her some semblance of closure.

    The blonde nodded with a new found sense of purpose. “We will go tomorrow. But there’s one thing I need to do first.” She would have to go to the room. Room fourteen. Because she needed some closure of her own, and she knew that however difficult it might be, how painful, she would find it there.

I want to thank her for exhibiting some semblance of self-control when I couldn’t and I want to tell her that if she takes you for granted I’ll find another Black Widow who’s better at following orders.

    212-528-6138: I… I… okay. She’s like, the best Black Widow though.

    E. BISHOP 12875: I’ll hire as many as it takes.

    212-528-6138: Whatever you need to do mom, just don’t get frivolous, funds are tighter than you're used to.

    E. BISHOP 12875: Ha. Ha. You’re hilarious.

    212-528-6138: I think so. So, are we gonna talk about the fact that Yelena is a woman or…? E. BISHOP 12875: No, why would we do that?

    212-528-6138: No reason. Just checking.

    E. BISHOP 12875: I mean, it was a little unexpected but you wear a lot of suits dear. And boots. You like boots.

    212-528-6138: I do like boobs. Boots. I like boots.

    E. BISHOP 12875: And besides, she went down very well at the party.

    212-528-6138: Oh, so if she didn’t flirt her tits off with your old vampiric friends she wouldn’t be quite as big a hit?

    E. BISHOP 12875: That’s not what I mean.

    212-528-6138: Then what do you mean?

    E. BISHOP 12875: She made the effort. For you. To speak to those old fellas for an entire evening, good Lord, she’s practically a saint.

    212-528-6138: I thought you didn’t like her.

    E. BISHOP 12875: I didn’t say that. I just think she needs to get her priorities in order. 212-528-6138: Well, that’s one of the reasons we’re in Europe I think. She has some stuff she needs to sort out.

    E. BISHOP 12875: Looking for her family?

    212-528-6138: How’d you know?

    E. BISHOP 12875: She’s a Black Widow.

    212-528-6138: Hmm. I guess.

    E. BISHOP 12875: Have you found anything?

    212-528-6138: We have names and faces. Her father was killed in action back in the Nineties and her mother is missing. Has been for some time so it doesn’t look hopeful, but we have some leads.

    E. BISHOP 12875: That’s a shame, I’m sorry. I can’t imagine how hard it must be for her. 212-528-6138: She’s doing okay. It’s been difficult at times but she’s a lot stronger than she gives herself credit for.

    E. BISHOP 12875: You really do love her.

    212-528-6138: I do.

    E. BISHOP 12875: I’m glad to hear it.

    212-528-6138: It’s just... can you imagine being taken away from your family? Sold to men who want to turn you into a weapon? She saw her mom’s face for the first time today, on a computer screen. A computer screen.

    E. BISHOP 12875: I can’t imagine. Is this why you called, Kate?

    …

    212-528-6138: Yes. I miss you, and you’re just a phone call away and I choose not to make it?

    E. BISHOP 12875: I don’t blame you. What I did wa-

    212-528-6138: Mom, apologise when you’re out of there okay? You can make it up to me then.

    E. BISHOP 12875: Okay. I have to go now. My ten minutes is up.

    212-528-6138: Okay.

    E. BISHOP 12875: Please stay safe. No more stabbing.

    212-528-6138: I will. I miss you, mom.

    E. BISHOP 12875: I miss you too, Kate. Thank you for calling. I love you so much. 212-528-6138: I love you too.

    E. BISHOP 12875: Goodbye Katherine.

    *call ended*

    Metamorphosis: Fin Chapter Notes This chapter will tie up our favourite duo’s European caper. It was originally the end of last chapter but I decided it deserved a little chapter of its own. I know this one is a little shorter but there’s plenty to come. I hope you enjoy.

    As always, thank you so much for reading and commenting. It’s always lovely to hear from you all.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes

    The room was dark when Yelena awoke. It had been dark when she arrived. She’d paid double to move its occupants to a different room; she hadn’t minded. She’d have paid whatever they asked if it meant securing the room for the night.

    Yelena hadn’t taken much with her. No toiletries, no girlfriend, no dog. Only a change of clothes and something to pull over her head to sleep in. The room had been very much how she’d expected it. Wooden floors had replaced vinyl, new interior walls had been erected so that the room could offer an en-suite bathroom, a small sofa sat in the far right corner where their shared bed had been and a now a broad king-sized bed was sat proudly on the site of her old kitchen table. The room was practically unrecognisable. It was only betrayed by its view, a view that was becoming clearer and clearer in Yelena’s mind.

    Traumatic flashbacks hadn’t greeted her on arrival, her visit hadn’t triggered a tight chest or spiralling heart rate. That had never been the intention. The intention was to dream and so the ex-assassin had undressed, crawled into bed and stared at the ceiling. She thought about how many times she’d dreamed there as a child. Had she had nightmares? Had her mother held her through the shelling and vowed to protect her from the vampires at the door? Probably, that’s what mothers did.

    Before sleep took her, Yelena had flicked open her phone and looked long and hard at the faces before her. She swiped back and forth between her father’s dark stare and her mother’s delicate features and smiled. On her phone she could properly zoom and take in as much detail as a photo of a computer screen would allow. It was time to exorcise some demons, if her subconscious would allow.

    She tossed and turned as music from the street below invaded her senses. She could hear the gentle murmur of voices coming from the street below. There must have been some kind of party in one of the cafés that backed into the river. Every now and then someone would whoop or cheer, presumably as some idiot decided to give the belly dancer a run for her money. The belly dancer would always win.

    She glanced back at her phone one final time. She took in her mother’s small smile and found herself smiling. There were no smiles allowed in passport photos, and assuming this was one, it allowed Yelena the smallest of insights into who her mother was. A small rebellion in the face of authority, how oddly familiar.

    Yelena turned onto her side and pulled her knees up towards her chest. The windows were closed but the evenings were still bitterly cold, even though they’d travelled further south. She started to regret not bringing any sweatpants to wear underneath the bed’s comforter. The sleeping pill she’d pilfered from her mother was taking its time. Sure, she knew they weren’t a be all and end all, but she’d hoped she would be asleep by now. The thumping music from the party outside probably wasn’t helping matters. The pounding beat seemed to penetrate her skull and into her brain, the vibrations felt as if they were rattling her bones. The windows shook within their frames with each blast from the speaker. It was as if the music was getting louder. It rung in Yelena’s ears and the Russian’s hands clamped around her ears, partly in an attempt to protect them, partly in an attempt to block the sound out altogether.

    The rhythm of the music was becoming erratic. It came in short bursts of concussive beats getting louder and louder. The windows shattered.

    Yelena’s hands and knees pained her as razor sharp glass sunk into her flesh. She crawled forward in a desperate attempt to reach the doorframe a little further down the corridor before the next blast shook the building and rained more piercing glass down upon her. If she could just reach the end of the corridor, if she could just touch the brass of the handle, if she could just breach the threshold in time, she could see her face. Yelena knew that she could, that she would. There was something different this night, something new, but she couldn’t place it. The overhead lights flickered and muzzle shots cracked out into the night. With every ounce of strength, with every fibre of her being, she dragged herself to her feet and picked up the pace, throwing herself down the dark corridor and toward her destination. Unlike so many times before, her legs didn’t fail her. The door was getting closer, it was almost within touching distance. All she had to do was reach, just reach. Fingertips touched brass just as she collapsed forward onto the door itself. Her breath was laboured, her chest was tight and sweat seemed to permeate pore, every crack in her skin. She rested her forehead against the lawyered pine to catch her breath and pressed her palm up against the wood. There were voices behind the door, murmurings, undefined chatter from an open window and the sound of rushing water pulled gently at the back of her mind. Open the door. Just open it.

    Yelena tore her eyes open. A muzzle flash flooded her senses and as quickly as it had been there, it receded, to be replaced with a vision of her right hand was clasped tightly around a bright brass door handle. She turned it and it clicked open, and all the guns fell silent.

    The room was still dark when she woke. She must have sensed the movement. The opening and closing of the single pane window, the silent yet detectable footsteps across the hardwood floors. The intruder was sat in corner of the room, her shadow thrown against the white painted walls.

    Yelena’s breathing never changed, her heart rate never quickened, because she’d know that silhouette anywhere. She could practically feel them. Their energy, their rigidity, their forcefulness.

    Sparks flew as a lighter scratched and fizzed to life, illuminating her mother’s dark and dangerous eyes.

    “Cigarette?” Melina asked, clearly aware of her daughter routine. She’d seen it often enough. Dream, wake, smoke and try desperately hard to forget. This time was different though. This time a Yelena didn’t want to forget.

    “It’s no smoking,” Yelena with a smirk that was barely visible through the darkness. Her mother laughed. “Have you been here all night?” Yelena asked, knowing full well what her mother’s answer would be.

    “No, but you know that. I wanted to get here early. Kate is coming is she not?” Melina drew upon her cigarette once more. Her hand shook ever-so-slightly and Yelena frowned. Her mother was smoking to quell nerves, but nerves for what?

    Yelena nodded. “Yes. Kate is coming for breakfast. We’re heading to Počitelj.” “To see your grandmother?” Melina asked in surprise, her voice betraying her. Her mother was usually so collected, it was odd seeing her this way. It was subtle, and perhaps not noticeable unless you studied body language for a living. Of course Yelena did, or at least used to, and she was probably one of the only people in the world who could read the enigma that was Melina Vostokoff.

    “Yes,” Yelena said as she sat up in bed and leaned back against the headrest. Wasn’t it obvious?

    “It all seems very fast Yelena.” Ah, her mother was deflecting. So there was something wrong. Why else turn up in the dead of night? And why sneak in for that matter? Logic would suggest that perhaps Melina didn’t want to wake her, but any normal person would just use the door. Melina hadn’t wanted to wake her, she wanted to watch her. “I do not see why I would wait,” Yelena shrugged matter-of-factly. Why should she wait? “I suppose you’ve waited long enough,” Melina said stoically. She was still. She didn’t offer her daughter a nod or a smile, she simply sat. The younger widow shook her head in admonishment, slipped out from under the comforter and padded across the hotel room. First to the window. She opened it, allowing some of the smoke from her mother’s cigarette to escape the room. She then made her way into the bathroom. She grabbed a glass in the darkness and filled it with water from the tap, then padded back through and sat down upon the end of the bed. Melina merely watched her. The atmosphere was strange, almost frosty and unfriendly. Was her mother threatened by this new potential mother figure in Yelena’s life, most likely, but the young Avenger had a suspicion that her mother’s insecurities weren’t the reason behind this visit. The visit was fuelled by guilt.

    “Why are you here, mama?” Yelena asked quietly, her patience clearly waning. After all, she’d intended on sleep for a good three hours more.

    “I wanted to speak to you before you left,” Melina whispered, her voice measured. “Are you not coming?” The blonde said with a frown. Her mother had insisted on being with her nearly every step of the way since they’d left St Petersburg.

    “No,” she said abruptly with a small shake of the head. The sudden movement, the directness of her voice, surprised the blonde. “This is for you. I should have respected that from the start.”

    “You are my mother. I understand that you would want to-“ “I know, but I did not follow you here to support you like family should, not really.” Through the darkness Yelena could just about detect the rueful smile that pulled at the corner of her mother’s lips. She took another drag on her cigarette and was careful not to meet Yelena’s eyes as she did. Guilt, indeed. “I followed you here for myself.”

    Yelena’s narrowed and her brow furrowed. She hadn’t been expecting this, not really, but perhaps she’d hoped. Her mother paused as if working through the words, debating how much to give, how much to show. Melina Vostokoff was a strong woman but that didn’t often translate to strength through vulnerability.

    “I followed you here because I was afraid,” Melina said sadly. It was practically a whisper. “Afraid of what?” Yelena asked softly.

    Her mother shook her head. A reaction to her own internal discourse. Her stoicism was failing her and her mask was slipping.

    “Mama, afraid of what?” Yelena pushed harder. She needed her mother to speak, she needed to hear her mother’s own words. Melina took a final drag on her cigarette and then stamped it out on one of the saucers that sat next to her on the hotel room table. “Afraid that you would find out what I did.” Melina swallowed as two pairs of dark eyes met. Yelena’s mother was afraid, terribly afraid. The younger widow had never seen her mother this way before. She’d seen her broken and inconsolable after Natasha’s death, but never so paralysingly afraid. But of course it made sense, as she was on the brink of losing another daughter. Again.

    “You were at the apartment?” Yelena asked. Her voice was even. Emotionless. “Yes,” Melina managed. It was barely a whisper. “I did not want to. I had no power to-“ “You took me?” This was now an interrogation.

    “I chose you,” Melina’s hands reached out and clutched at Yelena’s bare knees. Yelena’s frown didn’t budge as her mother searched her eyes. “We were under instruction to only take the strongest girls. You were so small but so strong willed.” Her mother smiled sadly as if remembering three year old Yelena. Small, blonde, strong willed and hazel eyes. Melina’s hands went to Yelena’s cheeks and her mother was now kneeling in front of her daughter. “Is that why you killed Kaşim, because he recognised you?”

    “No, no,” her mother shook her head, adamantly. “I killed him to protect you and Kate.” “Before he could say anything,” Yelena cut in quickly. She’d seen the look they’d shared, she knew it was true. Perhaps it was opportunism but it wasn’t a purely selfless act. Melina’s eyes flashed with frustration. She knew Yelena was right and she knew that denying it would only drive her daughter further away. Her mother was desperate. ‘I thought if I came with you to Sarajevo I could prevent you from ever finding out but…I...” Her mother shook her head as if trying to rid her mind of battling words and intentions. “You came here for the truth and the truth is what you deserve,” Melina said with grim resolve. Yelena couldn’t look at her mother, despite the older widow’s searching eyes. She simply ‘hmmed’ her response as she processed Melina’s words, thought about their implications, their ramifications. Should she feel betrayed? Should she feel as if her trust had been irreparably broken? Or should she pity the woman falling apart in front of her. The mother who was risking everything to give her daughter the truth. A mother who was in desperate hope of forgiveness as she clutched at her daughter.

    Words were beginning to tumble from her mother’s mouth. Words to fix and mend and persuade. “I am the reason you went to the Red Room. I chose you. But you would have been sold otherwise, to god knows who.”

    “So you think you saved me?” Yelena asked cooly. Her mother blinked, she was taken aback. Kaşim had thought the same. He thought he’d saved her by taking her away from a war zone, by giving her purpose, by selling for cash. Was what her mother had done any different? “No Yelena, I … I was not myself then.” Her mother took Yelena’s hands in hers and clutched them tightly. Desperation began to mar her words. “You must believe me. I believed what I was doing was right. I was trained to follow, not question. I was told I was saving you.”

    Yelena looked at the hands that were so tightly woven around hers. They were hands she knew well. Much like hers they were scarred from multiple split knuckles and defensive wounds, and misshapen from breaks and dislocations. They’d lived much the same life. Taken as children, trained and turned into weapons. Yelena was lucky to escape when she did, her mother had to endure so much more.

    “I-I asked your name in the apartment,” Melina whispered and Yelena’s eyes snapped to hers. Her mother’s face had softened and her eyes were glistening with unshed tears. “You were so quiet at first, you hardly spoke a word but I asked you your name and eventually you told me.” A small, affectionate smile pulled at the corner of Melina’s lips as she thought back to the first time she met a very young blonde with hazel eyes and a turned up nose. “You had crawled into my arms on the back seat, two hours outside of Budapest, and I asked, ‘what is your name baby girl?‘, and you told me.” For a moment, just a moment, Melina’s face flooded with unbridled happiness. It was as if she was back there, hearing Yelena’s voice for the first time, hearing her name, having her safely within her arms. Was that the first time Melina’s walls had been breached? Was Yelena the reason the mask had slipped? Was Yelena the first person to make Melina feel? And really feel. Not what they wanted her to feel, but what her heart and her brain and her chemistry felt. Had she felt that, at the sound of her voice, at the sound of her name?

    “You knew my real name?” Yelena asked disbelievingly. It was the first time she’d spoken in some time and to her surprise, her mother laughed ruefully.

    “No, no,” she shook her head and sniffed a little. “I-you were very upset. You’d been crying for most of the journey. You had a little blocked nose.” Melina smiled up at Yelena and ever- so-gently took her daughter’s cheek within the palm of her hand and caressed the tip of her nose with her thumb. Yelena always knew that her mother had the ability to be an affectionate, loving mother despite her rather frosty demeanour. Melina’s love language was tough love and defending you with her life. This level of vulnerability wasn’t something Yelena was used to seeing from her mother and without even thinking about it, the blonde unconsciously leaned into her mother’s touch.

    “You told me your name,” Melina continued, “I heard Yelena. I suppose from then on you were Russian, and you were mine.” The older widow brushed her thumb across the flushed skin of Yelena’s cheek. “You wouldn’t leave my side. I was only supposed to take you as far as Budapest but if I let you go you would cry and cry, so I went with you all the way to St Petersburg.”

    Yelena couldn’t keep the small smile from her lips. “I’m surprised they didn’t throw me into the Danube. I would have.”

    “You knew what you wanted and you found a way to make it happen,” Melina shrugged, as if it were simply par for the course for Yelena, which of course it was. “I thought that after Ohio I would never see you again and then you walked back into my life. I couldn’t believe my luck.”

    “Strong willed,” Yelena said with smirk.

    “The strongest,” Melina replied, her eyes brimming with love and pride and tenderness. “I should have told you then but I was afraid, I’d only just got you back. We were a family; all of us together. But then….” Her mother’s smile faltered and Yelena knew what her next words would be. “Then the Snap happened and you were taken away from me….” Both of her mother’s hands were now clasped either side of her face. Melina exhaled heavily as she tried in vain to quell the tears that were flowing freely across hot cheeks. “And when I got you back I couldn’t risk losing you again. Losing you the first time broke me in ways that I cannot even begin to explain, and then Natasha…you were all I had left.” Her mother’s eyes pleaded with her to understand. To understand her loss and her fear and her regret. Yelena nodded slowly. It was so much to take in, so much to process, but she did understand. She understood her mother’s pain, as she’d felt it herself. The loss of a sister, a daughter, a mother. Their pain was shared and intertwined. When Yelena had returned to her parents five years after her disappearance, the happiness she had witnessed from her father had been so visceral and raw but her mother had been quietly thankful. She’d held her and kissed and doted on her, and she’d weep happily when she believed no one was watching. This was before they’d discovered the truth about her sister’s sacrifice. Once news reached them of Natasha’s death Melina’s happiness waned, as did Yelena’s. Both felt guilt and loss, both felt robbed of a love that they had never truly explored. For a while both had needed time apart to be able to live fully when they were together and Yelena knew that whatever trauma they’d endure together, whatever the future had in store, however much they might pull apart and push away, they would always find their way back to each other, because they were mother and daughter. Brought together by hate and greed but held together by love and pure stubbornness.

    With a small reassuring smile Yelena softly pulled on her mother’s hands, asking for Melina to release her. Her mother acquiesced. The blonde went to her rucksack and pulled out a postcard from the front pocket. It had an illustration of the Sarajevo skyline on the front and a brief message scrawled on the back. It was signed ‘With love’.

    Yelena handed the postcard to her mother who took it from her in confusion. “This was in my hotel room, waiting for me when we checked in yesterday.”

    “I-I don’t understand,” Melina said as she turned the postcard over in her hands and scanned the message that had been scrawled there.

    Yelena shrugged. “Benny gave you up,” she explained matter-of-factly as if it were obvious. Melina’s eyes flashed to hers. “What?” She asked in disbelief. “But he said that he-“ “You are my mother,” Yelena interjected as she plucked the postcard from Melina’s hands, “But you are more than that. We are sisters too.” The blonde tore the postcard in half and then half again before throwing it into the wastepaper bin where it belonged. Furious hazel eyes met Melina’s. They cut through the darkness of the hotel room.“You were taken from your parents like me. They sterilised and violated you like me. They brainwashed and coerced you over and over. They were violent with you, manipulative, and they exploited your intellect to exploit even more women like you.” Yelena drew her mother to her. She clutched at her sides and Melina lowered her head to rest her forehead gently against her daughter’s. How dare a man such as Benny try to turn them against each other. How dare he manoeuvre them like play things. How dare he manipulate them and pit them against each other. Yelena refused to be at the mercy of men who sought to control her. She would not bow to their influence and she would never allow them to come between her and her mother. “We were both victims of the Red Room, mama,” Yelena whispered. She felt her mother nod gently. Melina’s hands were cradling her cheeks and her thumbs were grazing across the baby hairs upon her temples. The blonde looked up at her mother. Her eyes were closed and her forehead crinkled. She sighed softly in relief and then pulled Yelena into a fierce hug. The young Widow smiled contently into her mother’s shoulder.

    “Do you remember you used to take me to the hairdresser and I would cry and cry?” Yelena asked, her words a little muffled.

    “I do,” Melina replied fondly.

    “You must have been so embarrassed. But you held my hand and bribed me with strawberry Twizzlers.”

    “You were only ever having an inch off, you were such a drama queen.”

    “Only because papa encouraged me,” Yelena mumbled.

    “Don’t get me started.”

    “Do you remember the time that I fell at school playing football with the older kids? You brought me home and made me macaroni.”

    “Yes. And I’ve regretted it ever since,” Melina bemoaned.

    “Ha,” Yelena laughed into her mother’s shoulder. “You set a very dangerous precedent.” “And you were quite demanding,” Melina countered.

    “And do you remember when I used to have bad dreams?” Yelena asked quietly. Melina’s hand came to cradle the back of her daughter’s head. She softly stroked the mussed blonde hair that she found there and kissed her Yelena’s temple.

    “I do,” the older Widow said solemnly.

    “You would hold me close, stroke my hair like this and call me your baby. You would tell me that I was safe with you.” And she was, until the two had been torn apart by cruel circumstance and even crueler men.

    A small, rueful laugh escaped Melina. “I always thought I never wanted a child. I think it was to cope with my choice being taken from me, but then you walked into my life one day and I could not help but love you as my own. You were mine, you and your sister.” Yelena could feel her mother smile into her hair as her grip on her daughter tightened. Moments ago Melina was terrified she was going to lose her daughter forever, she gripped her as tightly as possible. She never wanted to let her go, just in case she really was to slip through her fingers.

    “You are the reason I survived. You and daddy and Natasha. Being united with you, being a family again was the one thought that would keep me going. The one thing that kept me going. I will not turn my back on that,” Yelena reassured her as she freed herself from her mother’s tight embrace and drew back to make sure Melina met her gaze in the darkness. She needed her to hear her next words, to really hear them. “You were a victim of that man, mother, as much as I was.”

    “But I should have said something, I kne-“ “No,” Yelena cut in. There would be no more talk of that. No more guilt, no more apologies. The conversation was over. It was in the past and that’s where they were going to leave it, especially when their future held so much promise. “My father was dead, my mother was gone. You gave me a family. You are my family. Remember,” Yelena said as she took her mother’s hands in hers. “It was real to me. I know it was real to you as well.” Melina smiled brightly and her eyes glistened in the early morning sunlight that was just beginning to break across Mostar’s dark winter sky.

    “From the moment you crawled into my lap in that car, it was real.”

    Kate wasn’t scheduled to arrive until later that morning so mother and daughter crawled back into bed and traded stories of Yelena’s brief childhood. Melina held her daughter until sleep took them both and by the time Yelena awoke to a bright winter’s morning, her mother had successfully delivered on a promise she’d made more than thirty years before when a small blonde girl had crawled into bed beside her after dreams of war-torn corridors and silent abductors; she’d vanquished her of her demons.

    Alexei and Kate joined them for breakfast and they enjoyed another morning of feta, breads, olives and honey at the Hotel Gümüs. Yelena was going to miss feasting like this when she was back in the States. She made sure to tell Kate that they were going to have to recreate a Bosnian breakfast on a regular basis. Kate very enthusiastically agreed. Breakfast was polished off with a coffee that the Avenger could practically chew, and once the bill was paid Yelena checked out of the hotel. It probably felt like a bigger moment than it was, but it was significant to her. It felt like a line in sand. As if one chapter of her life was closing and another was beginning. Soon she would put distance between herself and that place and never look back. Could she know for sure that she would never dream of that room again? No, of course not. But Yelena knew that if she did, it would be different because she’d be there. They’d both be there.

    She hugged her mother and father goodbye fiercely. Melina told her that she would reach out to her contact in the city again today today to see if any progress had been made on the location of Nadija. They’d traded hopeful smiles and her mother promised to get in touch as soon as she heard anything. Yelena knew that the chances of ever tracking down her birth mother were unlikely but if anyone could manage it, it would be Melina Vostokoff. Alexei kissed her fiercely on the forehead and then hugged Kate warmly. Finally he hugged Fanny and wiped a solitary tear from his eye. Melina gathered her daughter into her arms one final time and clutched her tightly. She didn’t want to let her go but she knew she must. She knew she needed to let her daughter go, let her explore her past and her future, and so she let her go with a final flurry of kisses. Yelena eventually managed to bat her mother away but not before a sheepish blush crept across her cheeks. Kate couldn’t help but smirk at her girlfriend’s clear embarrassment as she loaded their bags and their dogs into the car. With a few final goodbyes the two young Avengers put their car into gear and left Hotel Gümüs behind them. Počitelj was just thirty minutes outside of Mostar through the picturesque, snow-covered Bosnian hills and much to Yelena’s chagrin, as she was behind the wheel, Kate was in charge of the music. It was probably for the best, as if Kate had been the driving, for one it would have illegal and for two Yelena’s mind would have wandered. She was on her way to meet her grandmother, a blood relative. Would they look similar? Would she share her daughter’s eyes much like Yelena did. Would she remember Yelena? Would she want to see Yelena again? Would she even believe that Yelena was in fact her granddaughter. After all these years, Yelena hardly believed it herself.

    But something weird was happening. Something Yelena had never really experienced before. The feeling of hope. Hope that maybe this was the start of something new and exciting, hope that it was the start of something good. She glanced across to the passenger seat to see Kate happily scrolling through Spotify. Her nose scrunched in joyous mischief every time she added a song to the queue that she absolutely loved and knew Yelena would absolutely hate. Just over a year ago, Yelena would have turfed someone out of the car and left them at the mercy of the cold Bosnian winter for less, but not Kate Bishop. Somehow she’d managed to creep into her dark, cold heart and light a fire. Yelena hadn’t managed to build the walls quick enough and in the end she’d had to simply stop trying to put them up. Resistance to Kate Bishop was futile. Resistance to her smile, her violet eyes, her shit jokes, her fervour for life. Resistance to the comfort she provided, the beauty she exuded, the love she gave so freely. A smile pulled at the corner of Yelena’s mouth and a tight, warm happiness filled her heart. Yes, she was sure of it. This was the start of something good and Yelena didn’t hate it. In fact, she was pretty sure she loved it.

    Chapter End Notes And so concludes our European escapade.

    We’re on the home stretch now. Ish. But we’ve not quite reached Destination Happy Ending. Next up is a Valentine’s Day phone call and then it’s time for Miss Bishop’s birthday. It’s going to be a good one.

    It Takes Two: Part One Chapter Summary So, in true Alex fashion I took one chapter and I’ve made it two! My literary eyes are far too big for my belly which means things have taken longer but also means you get more stuff.

    Enjoy Kate’s birthday!

    Thank you for your kind comments as always. I love our discussions.

    The penthouse was deathly quiet when Kate awoke, hidden high, up and away from the busy streets of New York City. Unlike her own place, the Bishop’s family home was built like a tomb with its marble walls, columns and high ceilings. It was the perfect place to come when Kate wanted to increase the possibility of her getting a full night’s sleep, and despite the macabre, it was also the perfect place when Kate wanted to treat herself. Yesterday she’d made the decision to head back to the Bishop Residence for the first time in months, for one reason and one reason only. Today was Kate’s birthday, and she’d decided that she deserved a treat so, she’d let herself in, ordered a pizza and ran herself the biggest, hottest, bubbliest bath she’d never had the cheek to run when her mother had been around. It had been one hundred percent worth it and nearly, just nearly perfect. There’d been just one thing missing, and that one thing was her Yelena Belova.

    Yelena Belova sat between her legs with a glass of wine in hand, covered in bubbles with the sound of her hoarse, characterful laugh echoing around the marble bathroom. That would have been absolute perfection. But alas, her girlfriend was in rural Bosnia and Herzegovina, chillin’ like a villain with her grandmother. Of course, that hadn’t stopped Kate thinking about her girlfriend being sat between her legs with a glass of red wine. It hadn’t stopped her thinking about a multiplicity of things her girlfriend could have been doing between her legs. A girl could dream, right? And dream she did, a few times over.

She’d fallen soundly asleep surrounded by her two most faithful companions, Lucky and pepperoni pizza, and slept like a log. Baths, pizza and orgasms tended to do that to a person.

Lucky breathed quietly and Kate found herself smiling. She loved her Pizza Dog. He would be feasting on pizza for breakfast that morning, because she would be feasting on something else entirely. Waffles. The brunette threw on a robe and padded down to the kitchen. The marble was cold underfoot, despite the woollen socks Kate had pulled on to protect her feet. New York in March was cold but the Bishop penthouse floor was cold all year round, a blessing in summer but a curse in winter, and there was no way in hell they were replacing the slabbed antique flooring with modern underfloor heating, no matter how in-keeping with the style they tried to make it.

Of course, that’s ignoring the bigger reason she’d stayed away. Her mother. Everything within the walls of the residence reminded Kate of her. Of course it did, Eleanor had decorated the entire place. Every touch, every detail, every ornament was Eleanor’s doing. Even the styling of her own bedroom had been heavily influenced by her mother. The room hadn’t changed since she was young, and pink and floral wasn’t exactly her thing, but there was no way her mom was painting her room purple and letting her cover the walls head to foot with posters, she’d had to fight for the ones that were already there. That being said, the poster of Clint could probably come down now he was literally at the end of the phone.

She’d picked up some fruit and syrup at the store and took great pleasure in neatly presenting the fruits of her labours on one of her mother’s fanciest plates. The brunette made sure to take a photo to show her mother once her visitation permission had been approved. Jen had explained that because of mother’s association with organised crime, each visitor had to be thoroughly checked and vetted. That included her own daughter. What Jen hadn’t expected was for the wait for sign off to be so long. It may have been something to do with her living and romancing with an ex-Black Widow assassin. Maybe. Perhaps. Despite Carol insisting that Yelena’s record was clean. Kate didn’t hang much hope on Yelena getting permission to meet her mother.

They were booked in for a bottomless brunch at 2pm at some fancy- ish hotel and Kate thought it best to make sure the journey back to her hotel was already in her Google Maps search history, just in case.

It must have been from Yelena, it must have been, and oh how excited she was to open it.     “Dammit,” Kate cursed. She needed more dresses like this in her life. More of Yelena in dresses like this in her life, specifically.

    Yelena laughed a low, rasping chuckle. “You will like it, I promise. Now, go put some clothes on.”

    Kate blinked. For what? Were they not just going to take their clothes off? “What kind of clothes?” Kate asked, confused. She wasn’t interested in clothes apart from this wonderful red dress that clung so wonderfully to her girlfriend. Did she mention she loved her? She loved her very much.

    Yelena shrugged innocently in Kate’s arms. It was hot. “Clothes you feel good in,” the Russian explained coolly.

    Kate narrowed her eyes. This was a plot, Yelena was plotting. “Where are we going?” The blonde grinned with mischief. “It is a secret.”

    “But I want to know. How can I get dressed if I don’t know where we’re going?” Kate gripped Yelena’s hips and brought her closer. “Come on tell me. Please?” Kate begged, working her puppy dog eyes. Yelena would didn’t stand a chance. She had a tough exterior but Kate Bishop was her weakness. Kate needed tampons from the store? Puppy dog eyes. Kate wanted Thai over Italian? Puppy dog eyes. Kate wanted to know classified information that only Yelena and Carol should have access to? Puppy dog eyes. It worked. Every. Single. Time.

    Yelena sighed, she knew she was about to give in. “Fine. We are going dancing.” Kate’s stomach dropped. She immediately felt the significance. “Dancing?” She asked in disbelief.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded warmly. “Two months ago you asked me to dance and I said no. Tonight, I was hoping you would dance with me.” Wow. Kate didn’t know what to do or say. She was holding the most beautiful woman in her arms, a woman who wanted to dance with her, in public, in THAT dress. She wanted people to see them together. Kate couldn’t believe it.

    “You wanna-you wanna dance?” Kate asked as she found Yelena’s eyes. They were dancing joyously in the low light of the lounge. She had to be sure before she really let her heart get carried away with itself.

    “Yes,” Yelena smiled as her arms tightened around Kate and pulled her even closer. The brunette finally let her heart soar as the blonde’s eyes twinkled bewitchingly. “I would like nothing more than to dance with Kate Bishop on her birthday.”

    It Takes Two: Part Two Chapter Notes Gooood evening. Well, it's been a while. Sorry for the delay. I had a pitch at work, then a pretty crap illness (don't get ill in America) and then just about enjoyed the rest of my vacation. What was lovely though, is when I was away I managed to visit a few pretty incredible locations (Amherst and Concord) and have come away feeling very creatively replenished.

    As a warning, this chapter starts to move into the very top of end of the M rating. Take from that what you will, but I think it's worth saying ahead of time.

    Thank you all for your patience on this one, and thank you to all who are still reading and commenting and kudosing. You're wonderful.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes It was beginning to dawn on Kate that she had made some poor decisions. A crop top had seemed smart when getting ready to go out for the evening. Cool enough for a night out dancing, showed a little skin but not too much and looked fantastic with a pair of Levis. Yelena had always been very complimentary of her chosen lewk. She’d offer compliments if Kate wore one in the gym or around the apartment. In fact, tonight’s look had already gained Kate some incredibly kind words, and even kinder kisses. So yeah, all in all, the crop top had been a strong choice. That was until they’d stopped at Shake Shack in Hell’s Kitchen on their way to the bar. Seemed sensible right? But there was only one problem, and it was a doozy; Kate Bishop could not control herself at Shake Shack. She'd told herself, and her girlfriend, that her order of crinkle fries, chicken bites, a ShackMeister and a churro and chocolate shake was necessary, to line her stomach for the alcohol that was to come. After all, Yelena had told her to get whatever she wanted, so Kate had simply complied. Sadly for Kate, for her Levis, her crop top and her dignity, whatever she wanted was actually quite some distance from what she actually needed, and even further from what she could fit in her stomach. So, there Kate was. Sat, sad and defeated by fried food, with a grinning Yelena Belova delightfully picking at her fries. Of course, Yelena had eaten just as much as Kate and more, but Yelena could put it away and then some.

    The brunette was grateful that she hadn’t heard the words, ‘I told you so’ yet, and was even more grateful when her girlfriend rose from her side of the booth and settled down next to her. She was grateful for Yelena’s hand upon her thigh, grateful for the lips that ghosted across her cheek, grateful for the fingers that found their way between her own. It was then that Kate realised the eyes upon them. There was no way that Yelena hadn’t noticed them, Yelena noticed everything, every look, every glance. Yelena even knew if someone was thinking about looking, but tonight she was choosing to ignore all those things. The significance wasn’t lost on Kate and she felt her heart get tighter as her girlfriend sipped happily on what was left of the brunette’s shake, her red lipstick leaving its mark on the wilting paper straw. But sadly for Kate, it wasn’t just her heart that was feeling tighter. Why the fuck did she have to look like that? Why the fuck did Yelena have to look so good? With the lipstick and the dress and the hair. How was it legal in the State of New York for someone to look that edible? Kate clung a little tighter to her girlfriend’s hand. Sure, Kate was full of carbs but she was very much hungry for something else that evening.

    With an excited grin and a tug on Kate’s hand Yelena pulled the brunette and her Huaraches out of the booth and straight out of Shake Shack. The blonde quickly tucked herself into Kate’s side and the pair chatted happily as they made their way to the club that lay about two blocks over. To say Kate was excited to spend the night dancing with Yelena was an understatement. It was something she’d wanted for so long. Not just because of Christmas and the want to be seen and acknowledged, and the validation that came with that, but because it was another way to be physical with Yelena, you know, without getting physical. It was a way to let their hair down together, relax together, laugh together, move together, be a regular couple together. The brunette couldn’t wait.

    Kate actually heard the bar before she saw it, which shouldn’t have come as a surprise, especially in this part of town. The bass permeated through the neighbourhood, making the air shiver and pulse as Kate clung to her girlfriend for warmth in the cold March air. Somehow, Kate’s little furness still managed to radiate heat in what was really just a slip of red material, but the brunette was not complaining- about her personal heating system or the dress.

    With a nod from the Russian to the doorman, the two Avengers bypassed the long queue at the door, earning them a few disgruntled looks from those who had been waiting. Yelena paid them next to no attention. She’d earned her right to stroll into almost every club in every major city, and really, who was going to stop her? It came with the ex-Black Widow territory.

    Once inside, the couple headed straight for the bar. Yelena’s eyes instinctually surveyed the inner workings of the club; exits, bottlenecks and shadowy hiding places. Revellers dominated the dance floor as they moved organically to the dip and grind of the music. The pounding bass, that had only been a shiver on the air outside the club now assaulted Kate’s ears as they moved closer to the dance floor. It really had been some time since the young Avenger had been out. Like, out out. All the training, physical and otherwise, had become so consuming of her time and for good reason. Kate wanted to be the best Avenger she could be, and that didn’t mean going out, getting drunk and dancing herself into an early hip replacement. It meant hard work, training and focus.

    Yelena’s hand tightened around Kate’s and the brunette found herself at the blonde’s mercy once more. It was a place she very much liked to be, not that she would ever admit that to her girlfriend. The couple negotiated their way around the edge of the dance floor, deftly moving between couples seeking a little more privacy or loud groups of gesticulating friends who weren’t quite ready to commit to a night of dancing. Eventually the two Avengers found their way to the bar, and Kate settled happily behind her girlfriend, arms hooked loosely around her waist, her stomach pressed flat against Yelena’s back and her chin rested gently upon her shoulder. Being the taller of the two, it was a position Kate often had the pleasure of assuming, and she never wasted a chance to place a delicate kiss or two upon the soft, hot skin of Yelena’s neck. Tonight was no different.

    Although it was, wasn’t it? That night was completely different. Yelena wanted to hold her and be held by her, in public. Sure they’d held hands in Sarajevo, but this was a completely different kettle of fish. Showing an attachment to someone in public in this way was like showing your hand at a poker game, or signposting your next move in a fist fight. It made you vulnerable, it showed your enemies your weakness. Kate was now that weakness, which also made her a target, but still Yelena welcomed Kate’s lips, she welcomed her embrace and her touch, and she welcomed it with no fucks given. Something had changed. Something had changed for the better.

    Once at the front of the bar Yelena ordered herself a White Russian, Kate a margarita, and a double vodka for the both of them. Kate grimaced slightly at the thought of the clear, burning liquid tearing at her throat. She also grimaced at the prospect of overdoing it. She would have to be sensible. The last thing she wanted to do on her first ever night out with Yelena was spew half the Shake Shack menu, it was already sat a little uncomfortably under her breast bone. She also wanted to enjoy herself, at the club and perhaps a little afterwards, and she intended to remember every second of it because Yelena, in that dress, dancing with her… the prospect was making her delirious. Up until that point she didn’t even think Yelena really danced. The ex-assassin was precise, and efficient, not free and uninhibited. Kate’s arms tightened around the blonde as her girlfriend paid the bartender. She fit so perfectly, especially in heels, and Yelena’s ass felt otherworldly pressed against her. Kate didn’t know if she was going to survive the dance floor if this was how she felt when they were simply standing still. Fuck me.

    Yelena turned in Kate’s arms and handed her a vodka shot. The brunette gingerly accepted but downed it with aplomb because a girl had pride, and she was pretty sure that wussing out of vodka with a Russian was grounds for arrest in rural parts of the country. Kate screwed her eyes shut and hissed in discomfort as the burning liquid coursed down her throat. Her girlfriend’s amused little smile was unmissable, and completely adorable. Kate exhaled a ragged breath. One double was perfect. It was just enough to settle her but not too much to send her into a night of drinking, partying and passing out face first into a Pepperoni Passion. The blonde handed Kate her marg and clinked her glass against the brunette’s happily. “Happy Birthday!” Yelena shouted loudly against the music with joyful abandon.

    “Thank you!” Kate yelled back. She couldn’t help but grin unabashedly. This was what it was meant to be like, the whole girlfriend thing. The whole normal life, “partying like a twenty- something with a girlfriend” thing. Kate felt giddy because look at her, just look. She was so at ease, so happy, so beautiful, and in fairness to the bar’s clientele, many had been looking. Was it bad to internally objectify your asexual girlfriend this much? Was it objectification if you knew that she’d dressed this nice as much for you as she did for herself? Was it bad to want to rail your asexual girlfriend this much? Probably. Kate swallowed thickly. She was a bad person. Her thoughts were getting out of hand. She needed that vodka to kick in, stat. That would help, surely? Yes. Vodka would help. It wouldn’t make her even more handsy, no ma’am. Not a chance.

    Yelena’s smirk widened at the sight of her malfunctioning girlfriend - the Russian was pleased with herself. It was clear that Kate’s internal thoughts hadn’t been as internal as she’d had hoped and with a nod to the dance floor, Yelena triggered what might just turn out to be the beginning of the end for Kate Bishop. If her life was about to be drawn from her inch by inch, breath by breath, touch by touch upon a grubby dance-floor in Hell’s Kitchen then so be it, as long as it was Yelena doing the taking. The prettiest Russian agent with the even prettier smile. Clint would be so disappointed but Kate wouldn’t mind, her death would be worth it, just for the chance to touch and dance and feel and connect. It would all be worth it. The music rolled and dropped and Kate’s feet followed Yelena in time with the music. At this point they would pretty much follow her anywhere. Once they were in the crowd there was no turning back, the tumultuous mass had swallowed them. They were jostled and pulled with the ebb and flow of the music, and once they had found a small opening in the crowd that they could call their own, neither of them could see beyond the sea of bodies to the shore.

    With a pull upon Kate’s waistband, Yelena demanded Kate’s gaze back upon her. The blonde almost seemed displeased that the brunette’s eyes had roamed in the first place, and Kate really had no excuse. With her drink in one hand and one of Kate’s belt loops in the other, Yelena began to move to the music. Kate watched as her girlfriend smiled happily to herself, letting the rhythm take her, move her, free her. Suddenly Kate regretted only having one spare hand but Yelena pulled her close and kissed her tenderly and made her forget. The song seamlessly fell into the next track and the pace picked up. It was a song they both recognised, a club classic from the nineties. Of course, Kate wasn’t born in the nineties and Yelena didn’t exactly have access to ‘Now That’s What I Call Music Nineties’ growing up, but that didn’t mean they’d never danced to ‘Freed From Desire’ before and it certainly didn’t mean Kate didn’t know all the words. Words that she was now singing at the top of her lungs along with the rest of the club.

    With a sip of her margarita she hooked an arm around Yelena’s waist and pulled her close. The blonde couldn’t help but laugh at Kate’s sudden enthusiasm. They were both grinning from ear to ear as they swayed in each other’s arms, pointed to the sky and screamed the iconic words tunelessly into the night.

    Once their drinks were finished they were quick to the bar for a couple more shots and then back out onto the dance floor. They laughed together when Yelena discovered Kate was the goofiest dancer on the planet, they swooned together when Kate spun Yelena in her arms and held her close, and they smiled happily together when they realised that even in the loudest, busiest, noisiest of clubs, if they had each other, everything else simply faded into the background. It turned out that dancing with Yelena wasn’t to be the end of Kate Bishop at all, it gave her life.

    But, as always on nights such as this, there came a time when the unthinkable had to be done. It was an inevitability, a necessary evil. Kate didn’t want to, she never did, but Kate needed to. She needed to break the seal. With a quick kiss and an agreement to meet at the bar, the brunette reluctantly tore herself away from the blonde and negotiated her way through the crowd and to the toilets.

    Naturally, they were grungy as fuck but nothing that couldn’t be rectified with plenty of soap and hot water and so there Kate was, scrubbing at her hands, stood over the cool metal basins. Kate needed to be clean for her lady.

    “I know you,” came an unfamiliar voice from the basin next to her. Kate glanced up into the well graffitied mirror and her eyes were met by a piercing blue pair, staring straight at her. “What?” Kate blinked, clearly taken aback. She glanced to her left to take in the woman next to her and their eyes met once more. She wore a black band T-shirt and dark tartan pants. Her red shoulder length hair was purposefully mussed and messy, and she had a pretty impressive sleeve of dot work on her right arm. The smallest of smirks began to pull at the corner of her lips.

    “I do know you,” the mystery woman said, more confidently this time. “That bow and arrow thing?” The red-head smirked more broadly, it was almost a smile. “Cool trick,” she said with an impressed little nod, and then turned on her heel and made her way back into the heart of the club.

    “Huh,” was all that a very taken aback Kate could manage. She’d been recognised, for the very first time and it was like her brain had short-circuited. Was this a good thing? It felt like a good thing, or at least a pretty cool thing. Was the improved personal branding paying off? The Hawkeye brand had certainly had an upgrade since Clint passed the baton. Did everyone recognise her? Or just this woman? Maybe the red-head was just an Avenger stan, someone who followed their missions a little too closely, scoured Getty for the most recently papped images, you know the type.

    The still gushing faucet snapped Kate back to reality. She quickly quelled the running water, dried her hands and decided that the best course of action was to hurry back to the safety of her insanely badass girlfriend.

    “Hey!” Kate called as she got to the bar and found her girlfriend’s waist. Yes, safe, this felt safe. “Someone just recognised me in the toilets! How crazy is that?” Did Kate sound excited? Because she was excited, maybe rather foolishly, but she was excited all the same. Excited but scared.

    Yelena could only shake her head affectionately. “Crazy is definitely one word for it.” Kate had no time for her sass, she was buzzing. “I knew the purple would really pop. I knew it.”

    “Do you want another drink?” Yelena asked as she smiled that smile that was for Kate and Kate only.

    “Yes!” Came the brunette’s resounding response. “It’s my birthday, I’m a famous superhero, and I have the most beautiful, funny, smart, deadly girlfriend in the world.” “I am incredibly deadly, yes,” the Russian nodded, happily, clearly very pleased to be called deadly above all the other compliments thrown her way. Kate didn’t think it was possible to love Yelena Belova anymore than she already did, but she’d just been proven wrong again. Kate was wrong a lot it seemed. “Vodka or something else?” The blonde asked. “Beer I think,” Kate said with a nod. Yes. It was time to be sensible. And she was a responsible superhero. She saved lives.

    “So we are mixing?” Yelena asked, eyebrow raised. Her tone implied that she thought that to be an incredibly bad idea, and was very much advising Kate against it. What was going on? Kate shrugged and fixed Yelena with a look. “Beer isn’t strong, beer is fine.” Yelena shrugged and threw Kate her signature downturned smile. Kate narrowed her eyes suspiciously. “Have it your way superhero,” the blonde said as she nodded towards the bartender who was ready to take their order. That victory was far too easy, and normally Kate would question her girlfriend but it was her birthday, and why would she even dream of looking a gift horse in the mouth. Besides, she was being sensible.

    “Two Bud Lights please?” Kate asked as Yelena wrinkled her nose a little in displeasure. Kate rolled her eyes. “And an Espresso Martini for the lady, of course.” Yelena raised an appreciative eyebrow and whispered a quiet thank you into Kate’s ear. The blonde’s hot breath prickled and teased the sensitive skin there and sent shivers through Kate. This woman was deadly as eff. What had Kate done in a previous life to deserve her? “Hey! Hawkeye!” Came a sudden shout from across the bar. Kate’s eyes found familiar blue ones, it was the red-head from the toilets. Shit . Yelena’s eyes shifted dangerously to the mirror behind the bar to take in the red-head unseen and Kate sent up a small prayer for the woman’s soul. “Drinks are on me!” She called merrily and the blonde at Kate’s side stiffened. It was one thing being recognised in the grimy toilets of a Hell’s Kitchen club, it was another thing having your Avenger’s alias shouted across said club. Very loud and openly. “No no no, you don’t have to! It’s okay!” Kate called back with a smile and a gentle wave of her hand but the red-head wasn’t to be deterred. In fact, she quickly closed the distance between herself and the pair of Avengers. Yelena’s jaw clenched. This could get spicy. “Come on, let a girl buy an Avenger a drink.” The red-head smiled a little coyly as she rested her hand deftly upon Kate’s forearm. Before the brunette even had time to choke out a response Yelena’s arm had found Kate’s waist and the red-head withdrew. Kate’s heart turned inside out. Her girlfriend was being possessive. Possessive of Kate. She had instinctually reached for her and it took all of Kate’s self-control not to scream in absolute jubilation to the high heavens. Praise be to those bisexual deities for making all her dreams come true twice in one night.

    Instead of screaming with delight though, because Kate was a cool customer, the coolest of all customers in fact, the brunette very coolly threw Yelena a single teasing eyebrow. Because she was totally cool. One hundred percent cool. Call her fucking Kelvin. Yelena’s eyes went wide, and her face softened. Within the space of just a few seconds she’d managed to go from downright deadly to downright angelic. “What?” The blonde whispered innocently with no sign of a smirk. Perhaps Yelena had surprised herself, but then again, perhaps she was just a really good liar.

    Kate could only sigh in happy bemusement and so turned back to the mystery Avengers stan. Or was she a mystery Hawkeye stan? Kate had fans. Fans who thought she had cool tricks, fans who wanted to buy her drinks… which was flattering and certainly stroked her ego, but completely inconsequential as she only had eyes for one person in the world and that person still had her in a death grip. She had such strong hands. Such tiny strong hands. “It’s very kind of you,” Kate said with what she hoped was her nicest most approachable ‘leave us alone’ smile, “But we’re good. Thank you.”

    The red-head frowned a little but quickly brushed off Kate’s very delicate rejection. “Suit yourself. Who’s your friend?” Wow, she was persistent.

    “She’s my partner,” Kate explained succinctly yet vaguely enough. She knew Yelena wouldn’t want Kate giving out her name to some rando, especially some rando who knew a little too much about Kate’s identity.

    “Can I buy her a drink?” The red-head grinned and Kate could only laugh at the woman’s brazenness.

    “I mean, I have no issue with that. Makes her a cheap dat-oww.” Did Yelena Belova just jab her with a finger? And how did one tiny finger hurt so goddamn much?

    “What?” Kate whispered incredulously as her eyes snapped to the Russian’s, but her girlfriend’s eyes weren’t fixed on hers, they were coolly fixed upon the red-head. “I think you should buy us both a drink,” Yelena said, a little too ominously for Kate’s liking.

    “Alright,” said Kate’s biggest fan with an even bigger smile. She really wasn’t getting Yelena’s ‘fuck off or die’ vibe. To make matters worse she leaned into Kate and whispered loud enough for the blonde to hear, “She’s scary.” Nope, not getting the vibe at all. Kate supposed it was easy to under-estimate the ex-assassin, especially when she was in the slightest of red dresses and six-inch heels.

    “I will have you know that I am very scary,” Yelena said, her voice lower and softer than it had been. An unnerving smile crept across her butter-wouldn’t-melt features and Kate’s hand found its way reassuringly to the small of Yelena’s back. She wouldn’t do anything would she? No, of course not. Kate knew Yelena better than that. She was simply pissed and wanted the girl to leave them to their night. Sadly for Yelena, her message just wasn’t getting through.

    “Sure,” nodded the red-head indulgently. Was she patronising a Black Widow? Good Lord. First she makes a play for some Black Widow property, then she comes for the Widow herself. Rookie mistake.

    But to Kate’s surprise she felt Yelena’s body relax in her arms. “Oh, Otvali ,” the Russian groaned into the fresh Espresso Martini that had magically appeared before her. Yelena was done. She wasn’t going to fight, and she wasn’t going to spoil their evening, and so she deferred to the ‘ignore it and it will go away’ approach. Kate quietly let out a breath she hadn’t realised she’d been holding.

    “You European?” Asked the red-head and Yelena could only blink at the girl’s persistence and complete lack of self-awareness.

    “ Eto pizdets,” The Russian mumbled as she took a generous sip of her vodka and coffee concoction. Kate found herself grinning at how disgruntled Yelena had become. It was a grin she’d surely pay for later as her girlfriend eyed her grumpily. “You can do one too,” she mumbled in Kate’s direction. The brunette’s grin only grew wider.

    “What brings you to New York?” The stan called over the top of the music. “I take it by ‘partners’ you mean you’re an Avenger too, right? Not just her girlfriend?” Yelena’s eyes narrowed further and the red-head broke out into smile that lit up the club, for the blonde had confirmed her suspicions.

    “That is so cool! Two Avengers in one night.”

    “I am not an Avenger,” Yelena lied dismissively with another sip of her drink. “I came to New York for her,” The blonde nodded in Kate’s direction matter-of-factly, but no amount of Yelena Belova stoicism could stop the flip-flop that Kate’s heart did in that moment. She knew Yelena had come to New York to train her, but did she mean what Kate thought she’d implied? Did she mean she’d come to New York for Kate? Did she have feelings for Kate before they partnered up in July? Had she been pursuing Kate from the start? Her mind was racing and her heart was pounding. Kate Bishop was all kinds of giddy. “Smart choice!” The red-head smiled earnestly as she handed over some bills to the barkeep. “Enjoy your drinks and have a good night ladies,” she said as she tipped them an imaginary hat and then disappeared into the crowd. “Thank you for your service!” She called over her shoulder before getting lost completely.

    “Well…” Kate said in a rather bewildered fashion as she looked at the two Bud Lights in her hands. “That worked out well.”

    Yelena rolled her eyes and leant back against the bar, keenly scanning the dancefloor for more potential threats, new and old. “She wanted to rail you.”

    Kate almost sprayed her girlfriend with shitty light beer. “N-no she didn’t. She just thought it was cool that we were Avengers.”

    The blonde ignored the brunette’s protestations and shook her head dismissively. “She wanted to rail you.” Yelena’s grip was firm upon her dainty martini glass. Kate was filled with a sense of sweet satisfaction.

    “And you got jealous,” she said with relish.

    “I got possessive,” Yelena huffed, not taking her eyes from the sea of Kate’s potential new suitors, and the blonde’s potential new rivals. “Two different things.” “Uh huh, sure,” Kate grinned and leaned in to place a lingering kiss upon Yelena’s sullen lips. She was unsuccessful however, as the blonde brought her glass to her mouth and threw back the rest of her drink. It was Kate’s turn to pout unhappily as she leaned heavily against the bar and rested her chin sulkily upon Yelena’s bare shoulder. The blonde glanced down at her smugly. It was a look that Kate couldn’t resist. She just had to get this woman back onto the dancefloor, as soon as possible. So, Kate downed her first beer, pushed herself from the bar, took the blonde’s hand with unbridled enthusiasm and gestured to the dancefloor dramatically.

    “Another dance m’lady?” Kate asked with the most gallant of bows. With an affectionate shake of the head and a roll of the eyes Yelena accepted Kate’s hand, and for the first time that evening, it was Kate who led Yelena into the throng.

    Much to Yelena’s delight, the nineties tunes continued through the night. Kate recalled her girlfriend telling her how after coming out of the Red Room she’d wanted to experience everything. Every taste, every fashion, every type of music; everything she’d been missing. Part of that was a deep dive into what should have been the music of her childhood, and so Kate suspected that she’d been brought to this particular club for a reason. It felt familiar, it felt fun, and it felt safe. Safe enough to dance wearing whatever the hell she wanted, with whoever the hell she wanted, as stupidly or suggestively as she pleased. Safe enough to forget who she was for three and a half minute intervals.

    Kate was just happy to be able to hold Yelena close and feel her body against her own. To laugh with her and dance like a dork with her, to scream lyrics at the top of their lungs at each other. The look of sheer, unreserved delight on Yelena’s face when a track came on that she recognised was something Kate wanted to imprint indelibly onto her visual cortex. She’d never seen her girlfriend so carefree, and so free of burden. It was as if, when she was dancing, the weight of the Red Room, the weight of her childhood and her trauma, the weight of her losses had been lifted from her shoulders, and it filled Kate’s heart with a euphoria that she’d never felt before. Who knew Yelena could be this way? Kate certainly didn’t, but it was now Kate’s mission to help Yelena feel this way daily.

    A dying outro rolled effortlessly into a familiar intro and the crowd went wild. Kate frowned a little. She knew the beat, the riff, it resonated somewhere at the back of her mind but she couldn’t place the song. Of course, Yelena had, and she drew her Kate closer into her embrace. Their foreheads rested tenderly against each other’s and they swayed gently to the cool electro rhythm.

    “Do you know the song?” Yelena asked softly.

    Kate shook her head. “I know it but I can’t place it.”

    The blonde smiled happily. “You will know it,” she said as she placed a delicate kiss upon Kate’s lips. The brunette couldn’t help but smile giddily against her lips. This was possibly the best birthday she’d ever had in her life. Waffles, surprise girlfriends, fist fights, coming out brunches with the bestest of friends, naps, red dresses and now this. This was beyond anything she could have imagined at the start of the day. Man, she was in love. She was so in love. It was dangerous. Kate Bishop would literally do anything for this woman, especially when she would kiss her so softly, or hold her so gently, or ‘inadvertently’ rub her ass against certain places whilst they were dancing. Assassins were deadly, never forget that. A rich melody coursed through the club as the vocals kicked the track into life. Kate did know this song. Of course she knew it. Her suspicions were confirmed when the chorus hit and, without a thought she found herself singing the words back at Yelena who was already serenading her enthusiastically.     Her girlfriend’s words, no, her voice, her low rasping voice, was Kate’s only lifeline. It was the only thing that was stopping her from going under completely. Intimate, breathless words, tender praises, eager encouragements. Kate had never felt so unbelievably lost but so indescribably present as the gentlest of pressures began to build within the pit of her stomach and the tumultuous seas of her pleasure began to fill her lungs. She was doomed. All she could hope to do was to cling to her lifeline, to cling to the one thing that mattered most to her in all the world.     Kate could feel the blonde’s eyes on her, studying her as she gasped and clutched and kissed and loved. Yelena was applying cause to effect, action to reaction, Yelena was learning and evaluating in real time and it was so very her.

    Kate pulled her girlfriend closer, tighter, deeper. She wanted to be close to her when the time came. She wanted to be held by her, she wanted to be able to kiss her and tell her how loved she was and how good she felt. She wanted everything and all of her. She wanted her there in the moment of stillness and quiet, the moment on the precipice before the ocean would claim her and consume her senses, before she drowned in its all-consuming vastness, and she needed her there to guide her back to calmer waters and rouse her back to blissful consciousness when all was said and done.

    Rubbernecking Chapter Notes I'm sorry for the stress. I'm sorry for the wait. I'm sorry for what's to come next! Not really. It's going to be a ride but with a lovely ending I assure you.
