    Thank you so much for reading and enjoying and telling me you enjoy it. Much love. See the end of the chapter for more notes Everything hurt. Everything. From the end of Kate’s toes to the tip of her nose, and then some. That’s what happened when you were a non-super superhero. Whilst her friends were going out, getting tanked and enduring two-day hangovers, Kate Bishop was going out, kicking ass and enduring four days of debilitating muscles aches and hematomas.

    A groan escaped her as she struggled onto her side, to tuck herself into the arms of her sleeping girlfriend, but to Kate’s surprise she found Yelena already awake and watching her with increasing levels of amusement.

    “How long have you been awake?” Kate mumbled as she continued to bury herself into Yelena’s side.

    “Good morning to you too,” came Yelena’s stiff response. She was deflecting.

    “A little stiff?” The blonde hissed as Kate wrapped an arm around her.

    “No. Not stiff.” Yelena managed through gritted teeth.

    “Is that why you haven’t moved a muscle yet?” Kate whispered mischievously as she placed the softest of kisses against the skin just below Yelena’s collar bone. Kate always took competitive comfort in the fact that no matter how much better Yelena was at hand-to-hand combat, no matter how much more skill or experience she possessed, she’d always return from a mission with more aches and pains than Kate did.

    “I’m just tired,” the Russian grumbled.

    “No,” Kate grinned against soft skin and placed another gentle kiss there. “You’re just old”.

    The comment clearly hit a nerve and the old girl sprung to life. Well, relatively. With a grimace, Yelena stiffly turned her head to glower at the younger Avenger.

    “I have really missed this. Waking up to you and your charm.” Her voice was thick with sarcasm but Kate smiled sweetly, because she knew that no matter how grumpy her girlfriend was that morning, she really had missed Kate, to a disgusting degree, something that only added to the blonde’s grumpiness.

    “I know you have,” the brunette smiled sweetly and took her opportunity, aching body be damned. She pushed herself up on her elbows and captured her girlfriend’s lips with her own. Yelena’s demeanour softened instantaneously as she let Kate dictate to her the terms of engagement. The brunette could feel the tightness and stress gradually release from the blonde’s body as she slowly and tenderly praised her top lip with her tongue and her bottom lip with her teeth. Maybe when the two weren’t so ridiculously achey it was a ritual she could perform delicately upon every inch of her girlfriend’s body. Kate made a mental note to plan in some post romantic meal canoodling. Tomorrow evening couldn’t come soon enough.

    “I do not miss waking up feeling like I’ve been hit by a car though,” Yelena mumbled disgruntledly.

    “Being hit by a car will do that to you,” Kate smiled as she placed another gentle kiss upon her girlfriend’s lips.

    “It was an armoured vehicle and it didn’t hit me, I hit it,” Yelena insisted softly yet stubbornly and Kate thought back to their ‘peace-keeping’ mission in South Sudan, less than twenty-four hours earlier. Her girlfriend was factually correct, it had been an armoured vehicle, which was far more formidable than a regular car, and yes, Yelena had in fact driven her vehicle into it as opposed to the other way round. Only problem was, Yelena had been on a motorcycle and the armoured vehicle weighed more than two tonnes.

    “You hit it with a much smaller vehicle,” Kate reminded her with a look that said, ‘maybe don’t next time.’

    “It worked didn’t it?” Yelena appealed. The blonde would normally have shrugged too, to really labour her point, but today it would have been far too painful. And in reality, she didn’t need to labour her point because of course it had worked, because she was Yelena Belova. Everything worked when you were Yelena Belova. The ex-assassin had identified a weak point in the Humvee’s armour, she’d timed the impact perfectly and she’d caused the driver to deviate just enough around the tightest of bends to throw the vehicle off course entirely. It was crazy, it shouldn’t have been possible, and it certainly shouldn’t have been something any normal person would even consider, but Yelena pulled it off. Because of course she did. That didn’t mean that Kate wanted to see a repeat performance though. The way the impact threw her from the bike, the way her body hit the ground, the way she took just a little too long to get back up; it wasn’t something Kate wanted her to make a habit of, ever.

    “Are you friends or something?” Kate asked incredulously. Did they talk? Did they talk about Kate?

    “Yes…” Yelena said plainly, offering Kate little to no explanation. Her hazel eyes were fixed firmly on the attendant. “Is that woman going to touch me?”

    “Yes, babe,” Kate confirmed with a gentle nod and a soothing hand to the small of her back. She supposed she could question Yelena about Laura later. Her girlfriend clearly needed a little soothing, and she certainly wouldn’t appreciate an interrogation. “I think she’s probably going to pat you down.”

    “And I have to let her?” Yelena asked, stubbornly. The older Avenger was not used to having to bend to authority, she normally was the authority. It was only when she butted heads with Carol that she would bend but that’s because she understood that Carol had earned the right to ask her to do things she didn’t always want to do. Also, Carol could also shoot energy beams from her fists so, who’s really going to argue with those? But these security guards hadn’t earned Yelena’s respect, and they certainly hadn’t earned their authority over her.

    “If you want to get in,” Kate answered sympathetically.

    “Can I reconsider?”

    “Do you wanna reconsider this relationship?” Kate’s eyes snapped to Yelena’s. She was met with the biggest of grins. For gods’ sakes stop being cute. Kate couldn’t resist the smile that pulled at the corner of her lips.

    “I’m not kidding sweetheart. The amount of hoops I had to jump through to get you in here,” Kate said quietly.

    “Which I appreciate,” Yelena assured her earnestly.

    “At least you officially don’t exist,”Kate explained.

    “Oh yes, thank goodness human trafficking,” Yelena deadpanned. This time it was Kate’s turn to ignore Yelena’s sass.

    “Any actual record of you and you’d never get in this place. Say what you want about Carol but she did us a solid. And no questions asked.”

    Yelena shrugged. “I like Carol,” Yelena said plainly. She what? She likes Carol?

    “Where’s my girlfriend and what have you done with her?” Kate joked.

    “You’ve condemned her to a day of unwelcome touching and cross-examinations.”

    “Angela isn’t going to cross-examine you. Hey, Angela.” Kate waved happily to the attendant who was beckoning Yelena forward.

    “Your mother, Kate. I meant your mother.”

    “Oh. Oh yeah, she’s probably going to cross-examine you.”

    “Hi Yelena, I’m Angela.” The happy-go-lucky middle-aged security attendant smiled warmly at the blonde. Yelena visibly recoiled at her cheeriness. She also definitely hated that the woman knew her name. “I just need to swab your hands, doll.” If it was possible for Yelena to recoil even further upon hearing that particular term of endearment, she did.

    “What? Why?” The blonde asked, eyeing the instrument that Angela was holding with disdain.

    “For chemical agents, allergens, that type of thing,” Angela explained casually. You know, the usual.

    Yelena threw Kate a wary look, she was nervous and it was understandable. In reality, her girlfriend only trusted a few people and when Kate actually thought about it, her girlfriend only really touched three people in her life. Kate, her mother and her father. She didn’t hug, she didn’t shake hands, sure, she’d hit you in the face, but that’s where it ended. Yelena had spent more than half her life being used and violated and now a woman she didn’t know wanted to stroke her with a weird looking wand. It was understandable that she was wary. Kate offered her girlfriend what she hoped was the most encouraging and thankful smile that had ever graced Gaea’s green earth, and she watched, grateful, as Yelena tentatively offered her hands to Angela for swabbing.

    “Thank you,” Angela said as she put the sample into the machine and pressed a button. “And now just your mouth.”

    Yelena’s eyes widened. “My mouth?” She asked disbelievingly.

    “I need to see inside your mouth,” Angela explained, unfazed. She was clearly used to dealing with difficult customers. It was a prison after all. “Just say ‘ah’,” she smiled sweetly.

    “Do you want to bend me over too?” Yelena snapped and for a moment Angela was fazed. She was very fazed. And so was Kate. The brunette could feel the electricity radiating from her girlfriend’s body, like the ex-assassin had flipped a switch. Kate often joked that Yelena was the perfect combination of cute and deadly, but right now, there was nothing cute about her. There was a palpable tension in the room as Angela’s eyes were held by hazel. She was trying to determine if she was in real danger. Kate found herself worrying the same thing and she immediately felt awful for doing so as her girlfriend broke out into the widest of smiles.

    “I’m sorry, bad joke. I am Russian, I’m just used to being treated like crap at customs.”

    Angela laughed a little nervously but waved away altercation as a misunderstanding. “It’s okay, it is a little invasive. You ready?”

    “Absolutely,” Yelena smiled and opened her mouth so Angela could have a good poke around.

    The machine whirred behind her and after a moment it gave Yelena the all clear. Angela waved Kate goodbye and a new prison officer, Carl, joined them to escort the couple from security through to the solitary visiting area. With Eleanor’s trial just around the corner, and the possibility that some of her testimony could cause problems for the rest of the New York Crime Community, security had been heightened. A few weeks ago Kate was visiting her mom in the regular visitor's area with the rest of the families, now they had to meet in a separate part of the prison in what felt like an interrogation cell. In fact, most days it probably was used an interrogation cell.

    “I feel violated,” mumbled Yelena as they followed the prison officer down what felt like the fifth or sixth corridor.

    “You’re very dramatic,” Kate teased.

    “I am not.”

    “You are. You’re dramatic.” This time Kate wasn’t teasing. It was more of a statement of fact.

    “Just through here,” Carl said as he tapped his ID card against the security terminal to release the blast proof cell doors. “You’ve got ten minutes. And I know you never listen,” he said as he fixed Kate with the look of a man who’d been ignored a thousand times before, “But I really mean it this time. No touching.”

    Kate cringed a little. She’d made a name for herself as a serial rule breaker in the short time she’d been visiting her mother in jail. At the beginning she’d found it hard to resist a mom hug. Especially when she was touch starved and missing her girlfriend, she’d revelled in its comfort. Now her mom was under high security though, things would have to be different. “Sure,” Kate nodded, “I got this. Thank you.”

    “Uh huh,” Carl glowered, completely and utterly unconvinced, as he yanked the heavy metal door open and revealed a very tidy but a little tired looking Eleanor Bishop. Kate’s mom was sat behind a very broad metal table on which sat a jug of water and a few glasses. Kate noted the metal loop welded to the table itself, a metal loop handcuffs could be attached to. Yes, this place really did double up as an interrogation room.

    “Kate!” Eleanor exclaimed with delight. The metal chair she was sat in scraped loudly across the concrete floor as Ms Bishop instinctually rose to her feet, clearly wanting to close the distance between herself and her daughter. Kate wrung her hands as she found herself wishing she could do the same.

    “Hey, mom,” Kate smiled gladly. She felt giddy. Who would have thought that seeing her mother could send her giddy?

    “Kate, sweetheart,” Eleanor said softly. Her mother’s eyes danced with happiness and Kate’s heart lurched. “I’ve missed you.”

    “I’m sorry,” Kate sighed guiltily. “With the tighter security it’s taken much longer to get clearance and if it means that you’re safe...”

    “I know, it’s okay,” Eleanor smiled warmly. She understood. It didn’t stop Kate from feeling completely and utterly frustrated by the whole thing, but it sure did help, and she sure was happy to see her mother. How things had changed in such a short amount of time. It seemed as if her and Yelena’s trip to Sarajevo and Mostar had changed them both. “And besides,” Eleanor continued, “You’re worth the wait.”

    Kate’s heart felt tight and happy and anxious all at the same time. There was nothing normal about visiting your mother in prison, but visiting your mother with this amount of security just didn’t feel right. Sure, it told her that someone somewhere in the justice system felt Eleanor Bishop was worth protecting, which gave Kate hope that maybe her mother’s testimony could do some good, and see her mother go free or serve a reduced sentence. But it also told her that someone somewhere would prefer Eleanor Bishop dead and for the truth to die with her.

    “And you must be Yelena,” Eleanor said, tilting her head slightly to see past Kate and to the blonde beyond. “I’m surprised they let you in here,” she said with narrowed eyes. Yelena didn’t miss a beat.

    “I am surprised they might be letting you out of here,” The blonde retorted. Kate swallowed, thickly, but to her surprise, Yelena’s remark earned herself a small laugh from the elder Bishop. It was just the kind of quick witted, scathing retort Eleanor Bishop would have attached value to in the boardroom. Sure, the interrogation room wasn’t quite as glam or expansive, but there was still water on the table and it was still filled with cut-throat women. Yelena smiled back comfortably.

    “It’s good to finally meet you in person Yelena. I’ve heard a lot about you,” Eleanor said magnanimously as she settled back down into her chair. A boardroom indeed, and she Eleanor Bishop was still the queen of it.

    “From Kate or…?”

    “From Kate,” Eleanor nodded, “And… others.” Kate’s mom eyed the one-way glass that dominated the wall left of the entrance. They were being observed, or at least, it was a real possibility.

    “All good things, I am sure,” Yelena smiled as she poured Eleanor some water, and then filled a glass for herself and Kate before she settled into one of the metal chairs opposite Eleanor. Kate joined her.

    Eleanor paused for a moment before taking a sip from her glass. She was sizing Yelena up, getting a measure of her. Kate was sure that Eleanor had indeed heard a lot about the ex- assassin from elsewhere, and there was no way that any of it was good if you worked in law enforcement. If you were in Eleanor’s line of work, however, she’d probably heard a whole host of wonderful things, useful things, and then some. Kate’s mother smiled to herself. Her eyes grew warmer and less reproachful. “It probably depends on your point of view,” Eleanor said with a smile. Damn, Kate’s mother liked Yelena already, and the younger Bishop didn’t know whether to be delighted or incredibly put out. New favourite daughter alert anyone?

    Yelena shrugged coolly. “Probably,” she agreed.

    “I’m hearing that you make my daughter very happy as well”. Eleanor’s smile grew even warmer.

    “Was that from Kate too or…?” Yelena grinned. They were joking now. They had jokes. Already. What was happening? Hours before Yelena was grumbling about having to meet the damn woman and now they were sharing jokes? How was this happening? Of course, Kate knew exactly how this was happening. They were far too similar and suddenly Kate felt gross. Yelena used to be the person who would do whatever took to protect her family and the people she loved. She’d even kill to keep those she cared about safe, and now she was on a path to redemption. Eleanor Bishop trod a similar path. Fuck, am I dating my mom?

    “Sounds like she had quite the surprise on her birthday too,” Eleanor added conversationally.

    “What?” Yelena choked. What?! Kate hadn’t told her mom about the sex, the surprise sure, but not the sex. Kate would have never told her mom about the sex, or the underwear, and she especially wouldn’t have told her about the fifteen-minute-long fight through the penthouse.

    “You surprised me, remember?” Kate nudged her girlfriend very gently, conscious of her Frankenstein ribs, in an attempt to snap her out from her panic induced spiral. The brunette was pretty sure Yelena had already started to sweat profusely and not in a sexy way. “You were supposed to be in Bosnia but you came home to surprise me on my birthday?”

    It took a moment but eventually Yelena’s brain pulled itself out of its ass and back into the real world. “Oh...yes. I surprised her with... that. With being...home?” Great use of the English language, babe.

    “I’m sorry I couldn’t be there for your birthday, sweetie,” Eleanor reached across the table as if to take Kate’s hands but stopped short. It was an act that spoke to Kate, she didn’t need Eleanor’s touch, but to know her mother wanted to hold her was enough. “Two birthdays,” Eleanor shook her head ruefully, “I’ve missed two birthdays.”

    “It’s okay mom,” Kate said softly in hope of comforting her mother. “There’ll be more and we can make up for it when you’re out of here.”

    Eleanor’s blue eyes met with Kate’s violet, and she sighed sadly. “I have a lot of making up to do.” The older woman’s eyes then moved to Yelena’s and grew harder, more assured, more certain. “I know that.” Eleanor was making them both a promise, as she clearly knew that if she fucked up again, it was Yelena Belova that she would have to be dealing with before she even had a hope of apologising to her daughter.

    “Everyone deserves a second chance,” Yelena said, surprisingly softly. “You were only protecting your family.” Wow, she really was dating her mom. And to think, Kate thought she had daddy issues.

    “Don’t let her off that easy,” the younger brunette said with a roll of her eyes.

    “What? I have to impress right?” Yelena protested with a shrug. She wasn’t wrong. “And we’re not too different, your mother and I.” She really wasn’t wrong, damn.

    “Listen to your girlfriend Katherine.” Oh, that was how it was going to be? Suddenly they were best pals huh?

    “Firstly,” Kate held up a solitary finger in defiance, “Gross. And secondly,” Kate turned to face her mom, “My girlfriend is wrong, often.”

    The blonde gasped melodramatically. “I am no such thing. Where I come from, they train the ‘wrong’ out of you. In more ways than one.”

    “Then how do you explain that jacket?” Kate asked audaciously pointing at Yelena’s much- loved yellow and black chequered coat.

    “I quite like Yelena’s jacket,” Eleanor pitched in, high and mighty as always.

    “See, your mother likes it,” Yelena shrugged.

    “That is not a good thing,” Kate pointed out.

    “Coming from the girl who wears black, grey and purple exclusively?” Eleanor chimed.

    It was Kate’s turn to gasp, and she had to admit, she was enjoying the drama. It distracted her from the concrete walls, metal doors and impending trial. It almost felt… normal. “Wow. Mom. What are they teaching you in here? That was savage.”

    “This place is full of white-collar women,” Yelena said as she shook her head and grimaced at the prospect of going toe to toe with some of prison’s most heinous offenders, “They are all savage.”

    “You have no idea,” Eleanor leaned across the table conspiratorially, an excitable grin lit up her sleep-deprived face. It had been too long since she’d just talked. “Two weeks ago, a woman in for suspected inheritance fraud had two members of the cafeteria staff fired because they refused to let her leave with the entire kitchen’s supply of Himalayan rock salt.”

    “You have Himalayan rock salt here?” Kate asked disbelievingly.

    Eleanor nodded quite seriously. “The women would riot without it.”

    “I can’t tell if you’re joking or not,” Kate laughed.

    “But what would she want rock salt for?” Yelena asked, completely enraptured by the white- collar madness.

    “To soak her feet,” Eleanor explained, taking on a frivolous air, “To balance her minerals...”

    “In prison?” Kate asked incredulously.

    The blonde shook her head in disapproval. “Prisons are very different is Russia, even for the wealthy. No rock salt, just rocks.”

    “Worse than this metal box?” Kate asked, although she kind of knew what the answer was going to be.

    “Much worse,” Yelena nodded. “In fact, the wealthy do not really go to prison at all in Russia, but if they do, they have made some pretty powerful enemies.”

    “And I’m sure most of them never leave, am I right?” Eleanor asked, clearly hoping beyond hope that wouldn’t be her fate.

    “Hmm. Most of them do leave, but mainly in boxes,” Yelena explained sombrely before offering Eleanor the smallest of smiles. “But we are not in Russia.”

    “True,” Eleanor sighed, “But I’ve made some pretty powerful enemies.”

    Kate reached for her mother this time but stopped short of taking her hands. “You’re doing the right thing, mom. Remember that.”

    “What? Turning over to save my own ass?” Eleanor asked, her voice fraught. It was the first time she’d seen her mother show any kind of weakness or worry during their visiting times. Sure, she’d evidently missed Kate but that wasn’t what Kate meant. It was the first time she’d shown fear of what was to come, and doubt over whether she was making the right choices.

    “Yes,” Kate insisted, because Kate believed she was. “If it can bring these people to justice and offer you your freedom, then yes.”

    Yelena leaned across the table and captured Eleanor’s eyes intensely. “Do you think these people would show you an ounce of loyalty? They would not,” The blonde said with a sneer of disdain for the system that raised her, used her, and would have discarded her without a second thought.

    Eleanor’s eyes grew dark to match the fraught nature of her voice, and nerves began to flutter disconcertingly in Kate’s stomach. “There’s a rumour, Kate, going round.” Eleanor took a deep steadying breath and glanced back towards the one-way glass. She lowered her voice. “A rumour that... that he survived. That it’s the real reason behind the tighter security. Have you, or your… friends heard anything?” Eleanor asked. Her voice was quiet and steady but Kate knew that her mother was scared. Unfortunately, Kate didn’t have the answers that Eleanor sought, and had no way of comforting her, or quelling her own fears that were quickly gathering momentum in her mind. Kingpin alive? That would be a whole load of bad, for a whole lotta people.

    “No, I’m sorry,” Kate shook her head softly. “I mean, we haven’t, have we?” She glanced to Yelena with a questioning look.

    “No, no,” Yelena shook her head, her brow furrowed, “But if anyone was going to survive a bullet to the brain…”

    “Yelena,” Kate chided. Of course, her girlfriend was right, and of course her girlfriend always thought that it was better to be aware of all threats and live than to die in ignorance, but of course, Yelena could also be painfully socially unaware at times.

    “I’m sorry, it’s true!” the blonde appealed, “But I have not heard anything and normally it is the kind of thing I would hear”. Yelena looked to Eleanor again with an apologetic smile. “I can reach out to a few contacts if it would help allay your fears.”

    “It would, thank you,” Eleanor smiled gratefully. “Tracksuit Mafia, I can handle. Yakuza, far less intimidating than they would have you believe, but him...” Eleanor let out a body- wracking sigh, “He’s different. He’s ruthless, like no one I have ever known. Ruthless and suffocating,” Eleanor said, darkly. There was a moment of silence as the grim reality of the situation hit home. If Kingpin was alive, then Eleanor really was in danger.

    “Mom, we’re super-heroes,” Kate said, with a hopeful smile, “If anyone can protect you, we can. Plus, we have some pretty powerful friends.”

    “One man can make himself very tiny,” Yelena quipped earning a smile from Eleanor. Her mother’s face brightened for a moment and Kate had to concede that perhaps her girlfriend wasn’t entirely socially unaware.

    “And he controls an entire army of ants,” Kate added enthusiastically.

    “That does not sound as good as you think it does, darling,” Yelena teased. Eleanor’s smile grew upon hearing Yelena’s endearment for her daughter.

    “Scott is a cool guy, okay?” Kate objected. She refused to adhere to this narrative. Scott was cool, even if he was just the ant guy. It took a lot of training and a hell of a lot of bravery to do. what he did.

    “Scott is not a cool guy and what use is an army that I can kill with anti-perspirant?”

    “You wouldn’t!” Kate gasped in dismay. Yelena simply shrugged. She totally would.

    “Kate, being cool won’t protect me from a vengeful crime lord,” Eleanor appealed. It was clear that she thought it best to get her daughter back on track, irrespective of how much delight she was taking in the couple’s evident happiness.

    “It’s okay Mrs Bishop,” Yelena said.

    “Please,” The Bishop matriarch interjected, almost placing a hand upon Yelena’s before thinking better of it. “It’s Eleanor,” she said with a warm smile.

    “Well, Eleanor,” Yelena corrected herself, “You do not need people with superpowers to keep you safe. Your daughter is more than capable. I promise you, she is very good at what she does.”

    Kate’s heart felt hot and tight, she knew what Yelena was doing. Her girlfriend knew how much Eleanor had doubted Kate, how hard she’d worked to dissuade Kate from following her heart into superhero-dom, how much she’d regretted putting that bow in Kate’s hands for the first time. Yelena was very gently telling Kate’s mother that she was wrong by asking her to have faith.

    “I’m guessing you’re responsible for that?” Eleanor asked matter-of-factly. And they were back to their normal bullshit. It hadn’t taken long.

    “Not really,” Yelena shrugged. “Kate is very talented. I mean, she knows it but…”

    “Hey!” Kate slapped Yelena’s arm playfully and immediately regretted it but to her surprise her girlfriend didn’t flinch.

    “What? It is true.”

    “That’s rich coming from you.”

    “I was paying you a compliment.”

    “Bullshit.”

    “Girls, girls, if you could stop your flirting momentarily…,” Eleanor cut in with a smirk. Kate felt a blush creep hotly up her neck and across her cheeks. They had been flirting, shamelessly flirting, and they’d been doing it in the most ‘them’ way possible right in front of her mother. The older Bishop gestured to both of them, open palmed. “I have a few requests.”

    Kate nodded sincerely. “Whatever you need.”

    “I would be very grateful if you could reach out to Marcus at work. I want the apartment security completely updated, hardware and firmware,” Eleanor explained plainly. She’d clearly thought this through. Kate supposed she’d had plenty of time on her hands.

    “I can do that,” Kate nodded.

    “Now,” Eleanor continued, “I want you to speak to Marcus and Marcus only, okay? It’s important,’ her mother stressed.

    Kate nodded again, more vigorously. “Of course, I understand.” Well, she kind of understood. She didn’t know Marcus in accounting well, but it was clear that her mother did, and her mother trusted him.

    “And then Yelena,” Eleanor Bishop turned to the smaller woman and fixed her with a stare. “I know we’ve only just met but I need something from you as well.”

    Yelena took a moment to consider her response before she gave it. “Okay,” she said, slowly.

    “Good, I want you to get me names. A list of...,” Eleanor eyed the one-way glass once more. “A list of security people who are loyal to you.”

    “You want my girls?” Yelena asked, eyebrow raised. The request had clearly come as a surprise to her and it had come as a surprise to Kate too. Eleanor was asking for Black Widows and she was putting all her trust in Yelena’s basket.

    “I do. Your girls, not his. For protection.”

    The Russian took another moment to consider Eleanor’s request. Could Yelena guarantee that? Could she guarantee their loyalty? Kate knew that her girlfriend had liberated many of the women who were subjugated by the Red-Room, but beyond that, she knew nothing about them. Whether they were still working, whether they were loyal to Yelena, whether they could be trusted. The blonde began to nod slowly, clearly Yelena knew some of the answers to those questions. “I can do that,” she confirmed quietly.

    “I’ll pay them whatever they want,” Eleanor whispered.

    Yelena pursed her lips. “It will not come cheap.”

    “I’ll worry about that,” Eleanor reassured the Russian and Yelena seemed to accept her answer. Not Kate though.

    “But for how long mom?” Kate appealed. “I mean I get it, but if you testify, it’s done. You can’t go back on that. Wouldn’t something like witness protection be more effective?”

    “You want your mother to go into witness protection?” Eleanor snapped.

    “No, I-l"

    “Never to be seen or heard from again?”

    “That’s not what I meant, mom.” There was no way Kate wanted to lose her mother when she was so close to getting her back, but if it meant keeping her safe, surely her mother could see the merit in that.

    “I will not fade into obscurity, Kate,” Eleanor spoke, emotion thick in her voice, “I will not have these people dictate to me how I live my life any longer, and I will not be leaving my daughter ever again. Not after I’ve only just got her back.” There were tears in Eleanor’s eyes and Kate had never wanted to reach for her mother more than she did in that moment. But she couldn’t, and it made Kate want to scream and cry and throw the jug of water at the one-way glass. She wanted to obliterate it into a million pieces. So instead, she settled for a change of tack, because the only other option was to tell her mother how much she loved her, and neither of them had ever been very good at that.

    Yelena must have sensed Kate’s unsatiated need to take her mother’s hands in hers, so she intertwined her fingers with the brunette’s and placed a gentle kiss against her knuckles. Eleanor smiled, clearly touched by Yelena’s gesture, touched that her daughter had someone to comfort her when Eleanor couldn’t.

    “Jen’s still confident then?” Kate asked after a moment.

    “More so than ever,” Eleanor nodded.

    “Two mins left ladies!” Came Carl’s booming voice over the loud speaker.

    “Dammit why are these times so short?” Kate sounded exasperated.

    “For my protection apparently,” Eleanor rolled her eyes and Yelena did the same.

    “If I wanted to kill you,” The Russian said, “I wouldn’t need ten minutes.”

    “Can we not talk about murdering my mom?” Kate pleaded.

    “She’s right though, it’s laughable,” Eleanor seemed to be at the point where if she didn’t laugh, she’d cry. “Ultimately they just want to get back to their crosswords. Speaking of, have you brought my sudoku?”

    “Yes,” Kate exasperated expression very quickly turned into a far more sheepish one. “There’s Sudoku XL and there’s a new Avengers Adult Colouring book which I know you’ll love.”

    Eleanor pulled a face. One of those faces parents made when their kids were really proud of something they’d made in class, but in actuality it was totally underwhelming and yet the parents had to pretend to be super impressed by their dumb kid, because parenting was hell. “Are you in it?” Eleanor asked apprehensively, unsure whether she really wanted to know. At least it was an attempt to show interest.

    “Not this one, but soon maybe,” Kate said with an excited grin.

    Eleanor sighed with relief. “Thank goodness. I love you but I have no interest in colouring you in.” Kate tried to be offended, but in the grand scheme of hurtful things Eleanor Bishop said to her daughter, this was probably only a three out of ten

    “I would colour you every colour but purple,” Yelena said playfully, with a wiggle of her eyebrows.

    “Why would you risk your own life like that?” Kate asked reproachfully. Now she was offended.

    “Girls…” Eleanor interjected before they got into another flirt –filled back and forth. “Two minutes remember.”

    “Shit, yes,” Kate refocused. “Okay, there’s also the latest Margaret Attwood aaaand…” The younger Bishop rapped her hands against the metal table excitably to build anticipation.

    “Yes...” Eleanor encouraged her daughter to continue, with the patience of a saint.

    “Some cannoli from Mike’s.” Kate pulled a face, a face that said she was incredibly impressed with herself and her own genius.

    Eleanor’s face softened and the smallest of smiles pulled at her lips. “Really?” she asked with face of someone who’d been eating canned fruit for eighteen months. Eleanor Bishop really did love Mike’s cannoli. It was her one weakness. If Kate ever did anything dumb as a kid, Mike’s cannoli would lessen the blow, for a time at least.

    “Uh huh,” Kate nodded smugly. Yep, she’d done good. “God knows if they’ll reach you. The lady said she couldn’t make any promises. Unsure whether that was for security reasons or whether she just intended on keeping them for herself.”

    “Well, whether they reach me or not, I appreciate the thought sweetheart,” Eleanor smiled. “Maybe when this is all over, we can go to Mike’s together. Yelena too.” Kate’s heart felt fuzzy again, warm, hopeful. Mike’s with her mom and Yelena, it was almost too good to be true.

    “I’d like that,” Kate said softly. In fact, Kate would like nothing more. She just hoped above hope that her mother stayed safe and that whatever threat was potentially out there, stayed out there. They deserved a little bit of happiness, and if someone wanted to come and take that away, they’d have to go through Kate first, as well as her utterly terrifying girlfriend.

    “Is it sad that I can’t wait to hug my daughter?” Eleanor asked, her eyes brimming with unshed tears.

    “No, it’s not sad,” Kate smiled and swallowed the lump that was forming in her throat. “I kinda can’t wait to hug my mom.”

    Kate’s breath caught in her throat as she pressed the clean, damp cloth against the gnarly scrape that lay across the top of her thigh. With Yelena gone for the evening, it seemed a good time to redress her wounds from the day before, accompanied by a generous glass of red and a few episodes of Below Deck.

    Yelena had treated Kate to a Sonic on the way home and had then received a text from an old associate, a Widow associate, with a tip off asking to meet. Yelena’s ask for information had yielded answers quickly it seemed. Kate didn’t know whether that was a good or bad thing although she knew what her gut was telling her. If there was nothing to know, why the urgency, and if there was no risk to Eleanor Bishop, or perhaps Kate herself, then why did Yelena insist that Kate stay home?

    Of course, the queen of distraction had told Kate that the ex-Widow she was meeting wasn’t one of those that were loyal to her. She’d said she wanted to keep her hand, and information on who she shared a bed with, close to her chest just to ensure everyone’s safety, but Kate couldn’t help but be suspicious of the entire situation. She was certainly suspicious of this new Widow.

    Since speaking with her mom earlier that day, everything had seemed suspicious. The cab driver who tried to beat Yelena off the green light, fat chance. The woman getting pizza downstairs who’d paid a little too much attention to Kate kissing Yelena goodbye on her fact- finding mission. Whoever stuck the ‘Hell’s Kitchen DnD: Journey into Hellfire’ flyer under the doorway; instantly suspicious. What was it? Some kind of threat?

    With another grimace, Kate decided that she’d adequately cleaned her glorified scratch and began to redress it, just as the door flew open and a blonde charged through, thoroughly frightening Kate for the second time that day.

    “Hey, babe!” Kate called from the sofa. Did she sound concerned? Because she wasn’t

    “Hey, darling!” Yelena called back cheerily and headed straight for the bathroom. Kate felt the concern slowly leave her body as she heard the shower spring to life. She still frowned unhappily however. Was she not even going to get a kiss?

    “What are you doing?” Kate asked, accusatorially.

    “I’m just jumping in the shower,” Yelena explained as she stuck her head around the door. She was clearly half naked, and yes, still looking like she’d been used as a human soccer ball. Couldn’t she just come out of the bathroom to answer Kate’s inquisition, so Kate could get a better look? She’d had a traumatic afternoon and all she wanted was to see her girlfriend naked, was that too much to ask?

    “Didn’t you shower earlier? I want a kiss.” Kate appealed.

    “The club was smoky,” Yelena grumbled, “Ugh I can just feel it on my skin."

    Kate frowned and thought to the packet of Camels hidden in Yelena’s underwear drawer. “But I want a kiss,” Kate said, this time more insistently. She may as well have asked if she’d fucking stuttered.

    In an instant a half-naked ex-assassin was hurtling across the apartment at breakneck speed. She practically clattered into the brunette and pressed a fierce yet disappointingly fleeting kiss against Kate’s lips.

    “Hi,” she grinned, a little breathlessly.

    “Hi,” Kate beamed back. Did Kate mention cute at all?

    But no sooner had she arrived, did Yelena leave. The blonde turned on her heel, hopped out of her black jeans and hopped into the bathroom, sprained ankle be damned.

    “You don’t smell smoky!” Kate called, “You smell sexy!”

    "Very funny!” Came Yelena’s voice through the heavy drumming of the shower’s downpour. Kate definitely considered herself pretty amusing, especially after a generous glass of wine. The brunette got up and strolled over to the kitchenette.

    “You want pizza?!” She asked as she grabbed downstairs’ menu from it’s prestigious spot on the fridge. As if she didn’t know it like the back of her hand.

    “What?!”

    “PIZ-ZA!? For dinner!”

    “Sure!” Yelena yelled back, “Whatever you want!” Despite knowing exactly what she wanted, Kate browsed the menu like she always did and leant against the door frame to the bathroom. She was seriously having to resist stripping and joining her girlfriend, even if she had just patched her leg up again. One glass of wine and she was legit up for anything.

    “What did your Widow have to say?” Kate asked curiously as she dropped their order into a text to the fellas downstairs.

    “Nothing really,” Yelena explained as she scrubbed at her skin. “Just gave me a name at New York Presb.”

    Kate frowned. New York Presb was a hospital, surely not where someone like Kingpin would be, even if he was still needing treatment. But he could have potentially ended up there that night. Kate would have to check S.H.I.E.L.D’s incident report again. “That’s not very forthcoming,” Kate grumbled.

    “She never was.” Kate heard Yelena sigh loudly over the sounds of water cascading from the shower head to the basin below, and the brunette made a mental note to ask Yelena about her mystery Widow that caused her to sigh so enthusiastically at some point in the future. Another Widow in New York City could mean trouble, or useful alliances. Moments later the sound of water ceased and was replaced with the sound of the shower door opening and a small yet deadly woman climbing out.

    She thought to steal a glance at her very naked and dripping girlfriend but was rudely interrupted by her ringing phone. She sighed loudly, what part of ‘all the meats but not ground beef’ did Herman not understand? Kate grabbed it from the side and picked up. “Yo, Hermano, my man, you’re killing me here.” But the voice on the other end wasn’t Herman’s, it wasn’t anyone’s she knew in fact.

    “Yes, this is Kate Bishop.” It was the prison and Kate felt cold. “I’m sorry, what?”

    Yelena appeared from the bathroom, still wrapped in a towel, concern etched across her face. She must have known from the sound of Kate’s voice that something was very, very wrong.

    “How? I don’t understand.” Yelena closed the distance between herself and Kate and settled her hands gently upon her hips. Hazel eyes search violet. All they found were unbridled panic.

    Yelena mouthed a gentle, “What?” to Kate but the brunette didn’t even register it.

    “Where is she?” Kate asked urgently. “I’m coming. I don’t care!” Panic turned quickly to frustration and anger. “Then I’ll wait, as long as it takes.” Kate hung up. She couldn’t feel her legs. Yelena’s arms where around her in an instant, offering her the support she didn’t know she needed.

    “What’s happened?” The blonde asked, eyes searching Kate’s once more. What had happened? Kate didn’t know. She had so many questions, so many. How, when, who? And why them, why her family? Why her mom? But only one question really mattered in that moment... Was her mom going to be alright?

    Kate took a breath and steadied herself. If she said it, she spoke it into existence, right? That’s how it worked. As soon as she said the words it would be real. But it was already real, and it had all happened so fast.

    “Mom is ill,” Kate whispered, and she felt Yelena’s arms tighten around her instinctually. “Really ill. I don’t- I don’t know what-”

    “Hey, hey, hey,” Yelena soothed as she pulled Kate into the tightest of embraces. They stood there for moment as Kate let the shock wash over her body. Her heart was racing, her chest tight and her breathing erratic but Yelena’s strong arms held fast and her low, comforting voice whispered gentle words in her ear. Slowly, slowly, Kate felt the tightness in her chest recede just enough. Just enough to breathe in that moment. “Let me get changed, okay?” Yelena whispered as she found Kate’s eyes once more. The brunette found so much solace in those eyes, so much strength, so much comfort. “You stay right here. I won’t be a second.”

    With a kiss to her cheek, Yelena dashed into the bathroom and gathered her discarded clothes. She then hurried up to the duplex balcony, threw on whatever clothes she could find, quickly brushed out her wet hair, and dashed back down to where a shell-shocked Kate stood still and silent in the kitchenette.

    “Where have they taken her?” Yelena asked as she searched one of her coats for her car keys.

    “She’s at Hackensack. That’s New Jersey, right?” Kate asked. Surely, they couldn’t have taken her mom to New Jersey, that was a totally different state.

    “Yes, but it is not far. Thirty minutes?” Thirty minutes?! Thirty minutes could be the difference between life and death, and it was so far. What if she didn’t get there in time. What if-

    “Hey, hey,” Kate felt Yelena’s hands capture hers. “I will get you there, okay?” She said softly. “Let’s go.”

    Kate took a breath and squeezed Yelena’s hand. If anyone could get her there it would be Yelena. If anyone could come to Kate’s rescue, it would be her. The woman she loved.

    The two Avengers grabbed their coats, and Yelena led Kate downstairs to the parking lot. The Russian never let go of her hand.

    “Do you think… do you think she’s been poisoned?” Kate asked, her thoughts swirling. If she was sick, surely she was poisoned. Unless she was just... sicK, but that seemed so unlikely. She was perfectly fine earlier, happy even, although a little tired. Anyone would be, sleeping in prison bunks.

    Yelena’s face was stony. “I think it is a possibility,” she said gravely.

    Kate swallowed and asked the question she’d been dreading to ask. “Do you think it could have been the cannoli?”

    Yelena couldn’t help but smile a small sad, affectionate smile. She drew Kate to her once more and held her tight. “No,” she shook her head, “I don’t think it was the cannoli.” But what if it was? What if it was the cannoli but she didn’t even know it? What if someone at Mike’s had spiked the pastries? What if-? “Kate,” Yelena said, softly, as if she could hear the brunette’s spiralling thoughts, “This is not your fault.” Hazel eyes gazed wholeheartedly into violet, trying so desperately to quell the panic that they found there.

    Suddenly Kate’s phone sprung to life again. Its shrill tone echoed through the parking lot and Kate froze. What if it was more bad news? What if they hadn’t made it in time? What if she’d wasted so long worrying that her mom had...

    “I can’t-” Kate shook her head, as she dug her phone out of her pocket and held it out towards Yelena, begging her to answer. “I can’t answer it.” She was scared, so scared. She was back to that day, that day in the penthouse, the day everything changed. Fear filled her lungs, and dread flooded her limbs. She was frozen to the spot but her phone just kept on ringing. She needed Yelena to answer it, she needed it stop.

    A moment more and Yelena took the phone from her hands, looked at who was calling and glanced back up to Kate with a small, reassuring smile. Maybe it wasn’t the hospital, maybe it wasn’t bad news, not yet anyways.

    "Hello, America,” Yelena started, but as soon as she had, her smile faltered. “America, stop. You are not making sense.” Immediately Kate felt the panic rise within her again. What the fuck was happening? “Okay, okay,” Yelena said, as she retrieved her own phone from her pocket and began to punch in a URL. "What site, CNN?”

    It took a moment for the CNN homepage to load but once it had Kate knew exactly why America had been calling. She knew exactly why Yelena’s face was no longer the reassuring, soft, comforting picture it had been just moments earlier. And she knew exactly why her mother was ill.

    The top headline on the homepage read, ‘Notorious Hell’s Kitchen crime lord Wilson Fisk, a.k.a. Kingpin, broken out of Long Island high security hospital.’ Kate’s stomach lurched. She needed to sit down, she needed to vomit, she needed to get to her mother.

    “Pizdets.” Kate heard Yelena mutter quietly in disbelief.

    “Yelena, Yelena,” Kate reached in desperation for her girlfriend and small but strong hands found hers. Her mother was ill, most likely poisoned and Kingpin was at large, most likely somehow the perpetrator. How had things gone so badly wrong, and so quickly. “Yelena,” Kate whispered as hot tears finally found their way down cool cheeks. “What the fuck is happening?”

    Chapter End Notes Oops.

    Solovey Chapter Notes Thanks to all your comments from the last chapter. All your brilliant theories and speculations. This chapter, you'll get some of the answers you were looking for, but answers only really lead to more questions, eh?

    All I'll say is, trust the process.

    The hospital had been quiet by the time Kate and Yelena had made it there. The evening rush was over and day shifters were slowly being replaced by the drip, drip, drip of night staff. The couple had rushed to reception, only to be told to wait; a police officer would be with them shortly. The receptionist’s definition of 'shortly' didn’t quite match up with Kate’s, and it certainly hadn’t matched up with Yelena’s. The Russian had gotten increasingly, and quite visibly, agitated as the minutes had gone by. Yelena had never been the most patient. The longer Kate waited, the more she had to sit and be still, the more she realised that this was a situation she had absolutely zero control over. Her mother was ill, seriously ill, and no amount of storming into the ER was going to change that. Nothing she could do could change anything. And so, fear and panic settled within her. It became something heavier, more definite, more crushing. It became dread. She dreaded the worst, but the worst was yet to come.

    After plenty of hand holding and hugs, contrasted with plenty of angry Russian words and even angrier Russian pacing, a police officer opened the door to the Relatives Room and entered, alongside what the two Avengers learned was Hackensack's leading toxicologist. Her face had been troubled but not sombre, and Kate had almost fallen back down into her chair. Eleanor Bishop had stablised, but yes, she had been poisoned. The toxicologist’s troubled look began to make more sense the more she spoke, as she revealed the details, or more specifically, lack of details around Eleanor’s condition. Kate’s mother had been taken ill about an hour after she and Yelena had left Bay View. Her initial symptoms were vomiting and some breathing difficulties, but they’d then escalated. Rapid heart rate, dizziness, low blood pressure followed by severe shock. That was the point at which she was rushed to the specialist at Hackensack, the point that it had become a suspected poisoning. The only problem was, the so-called specialists had no idea what had poisoned her. There was nothing in her symptoms that could point to any one type of poison, nothing in her stomach, nothing in her blood. For the last two hours the prison staff had been searching her room and her personal belongings, but to no avail. No one had any idea as to what Eleanor had been poisoned with and that made her near impossible to treat.

    Thankfully, Eleanor had somewhat stabilised by herself. Her blood pressure had increased, her heart rate was still high but back to below one-twenty, and with intubation, she was at least alive. It was something Kate was incredibly grateful for. However, her mother’s prognosis was still not good. Without knowing the toxin, and without knowing how it was administered, it was incredibly difficult to make any judgement on her health, and all the toxicologist could do was apologise gently and advise that Kate should get some sleep. Kate’s heart had sank then. She wasn’t being allowed to see her mother, but she’d known why. Kate herself would be under suspicion, Yelena would be under suspicion too and that would probably be the case until they could find the source of the toxin and rule them both out. Kate’s suspicions were confirmed as soon as the toxicologist left the room, leaving them alone with the Police Officer.

    He’d introduced himself as Detective Grant Perrina and had smiled sympathetically. Yelena still hadn’t liked him. He seemed apologetic, almost uncomfortable. Perrina clearly didn’t want to be interrogating Kate whilst her mother lay dying just down the corridor, but he’d had to. He’d asked about the security search, about their conversation, about the food and puzzle books they’d delivered. He’d even asked Yelena about the water she’d poured for Eleanor, they’d clearly already studied the CCTV footage from the visit. The blonde had simply shrugged and said she’d poured Eleanor some water from the jug on the table. There wasn’t much more to say. They’d each had a glass, they’d each drunk from their glasses and the prison staff had clearly found nothing in the water, otherwise the toxicologist would have known what they were dealing with, but they didn’t. Two hours later and they still didn’t. Eventually, after much encouragement from Yelena, Kate conceded that she needed sleep. Although Eleanor was still unconscious and probably would be for quite some time, the Russian had managed to persuade her girlfriend to let her drive her home, and the two Avengers had crawled into bed, and into each other’s arms, at around five am. Naturally, Yelena had found sleep first. Despite her often restless dreams, the ex-assassin could find sleep anywhere at anytime, it was all part of the training. So, after she’d placed a few gentle kisses atop of Kate’s head, and whispered a carefully curated collection of even gentler words, the blonde drifted easily off to sleep, leaving Kate to her thoughts. Everything had been so perfect just twenty-four hours previous. Sure they’d been a little broken, most definitely bruised and certifiably achey, but they’d been happy. Yelena was home from Mostar and back in her bed, Jen was positive about her mother’s case, and Wilson Fisk was safely behind bars. Now Fisk was at large, her mother was in the ICU and despite Yelena still being back in Kate’s bed, the brunette was nowhere near in the right headspace to enjoy it in the way that she wanted to.

    Kate tightened her arms around her girlfriend and the smallest of sighs escaped the sleeping blonde. It was cute and wholesome and so very loveable and Kate felt her battered heart grow just a feather’s weight lighter. How grateful she was for her girlfriend. Her taxi driver, her emotional support human, the woman who would show her anger for when Kate didn’t have the willpower to fight, the woman who would move mountains for her and fight her monsters for her. Kate wondered how she would have dealt with her mother’s poisoning without the now sleeping blonde. Would she have dealt with it at all?

    Kate let the tips of her fingers graze gently across the soft skin of Yelena’s stomach. She’d usually trace lines across her ribs, sternum and bare chest but with Yelena’s injuries still fresh from their ‘peace-keeping’ mission to South Sudan, Kate thought better of it. Instead she let her fingertips roam, down across Yelena’s hips, and then skate across the tops of her thighs. It was a comfort, the feel of her. To know she was close, and safe, and warm; her little protector that she would protect with her life. Kate supposed that was the definition of a great partnership.

    The only thing Yelena couldn’t protect Kate from, at least in that very moment, were her swirling thoughts. It was the dread; Kate just couldn’t shift it. It sat heavy in her stomach and pressed tightly against her rib cage as her thoughts became harder and harder to navigate. In the early hours of that morning her mother’s death felt close, it felt like an inevitability, and there was nothing Kate could do to stop it. She was powerless, and that wasn’t something she was used to.

    Kate needed to shut off her thoughts and cross out the images of her mother lying lifeless in a hospital bed that her brain had so helpfully conjured in the absence of real-life memories. She needed to silence the worry, but she couldn’t. The brunette found herself regretting every word spoken in anger, every time she’d disappointed her mother, every time she’d wished she could have traded her mother’s life for her father’s. She regretted it all. “Net…,” came Yelena’s sudden and fevered whisper. Kate was dragged violently from her catastrophising as her girlfriend gasped and thrashed in her sleep. “Net, pozhaluysta,” the blonde implored, her voice louder and laden with panic. “Umolyayu tebya, net, net!” The blonde’s eyes flew open with a gasping breath and for a moment Kate thought she saw those beautiful hazel eyes flash with a similar dread to the one that had laid anchor within Kate’s chest. But no, it wasn’t dread, it was fear. Yelena’s eyes had flashed with fear, but only for a moment, and no more. The fear subsided as quickly as it had come, and the blonde blinked once, twice and then a third time as Kate’s apartment ceiling came into view. Their eyes met.

    “Kate?” Yelena whispered as she searched for her girlfriend’s hand. She was disorientated. They’d danced this dance many times before so Kate knew it well. She took Yelena’s searching hand within hers and pressed it to her lips.

    “You were having a nightmare,” Kate soothed.

    “I-I….” Yelena’s eyes darted around the apartment. She sat up with a start but Kate placed a calming hand against her chest and encouraged her to settle back down into Kate’s many pillows and blankets.

    “Hey, it’s okay. You’re okay.” Kate’s hand moved to Yelena’s cheek and gently turned her gaze to meet her own. “You’re with me.”

    With her hands pressed against Yelena’s chest, Kate could feel the blonde’s breathing begin to sooth. “I am sorry, I’m okay. I did not meant to wake you,” Yelena spoke quietly. “You didn’t,” Kate smiled a tired smile. “Bad dream?” She asked. Probably the stupidest question she’s ever asked.

    Yelena sighed a little despondently. “The same as always.”

    Kate frowned in confusion. “I thought you hadn’t had that for a while.” Yelena frowned too, clearly as surprised as Kate. Yelena hadn’t dreamt about the corridor since before meeting Baka and usually when she had, she’d calm her racing heart with a sneaky cigarette. Kate could feel Yelena’s heart, it was no longer racing. “I haven’t,” the blonde confirmed with a small nod, “But I am sure it’s nothing to worry about.” Yelena grazed her thumb across Kate’s knuckles. The brunette tried to take some comfort in it. “Probably just a symptom of everything that’s happening…,” the Russian shrugged. Yelena didn’t need to say much else. It made sense, with Kate’s mom being so ill, that Yelena might dream of hers. “Have you managed to get any rest?” Yelena asked, as she placed a gentle kiss upon the back of Kate’s hand.

    “No,” Kate answered, glumly. She was tired, exhausted even, but her thoughts would not give her a moment’s peace. “I just can’t stop worrying.”

    Yelena smiled sympathetically. She understood. “I know,” the blonde said softly, “But they will call, okay? And my phone is on loud. You need your sleep,” Yelena implored Kate to listen with a simple squeeze of her hand. Kate was so out of control. She had to wait for their call, she had to wait for something to change, for something to get worse. She was at their mercy and she hated it, much like her mother was at the mercy of this indecipherable poison. They were both so out of control.

    Kate felt her chest heave as a sense of helplessness flooded her body. It tore through her veins, constricted her chest and clutched at her heart. A sob wracked her as helplessness met dread, deep within her stomach. In an instant, Yelena’s strong arms were around her. Kate let herself be pulled into the Russian’s warm embrace.

    “Come here,” Yelena whispered before she placed a tender kiss against Kate’s temple. “I’ve got you. Nothing is going happen whilst I’m here, okay?”

    “You can’t promise that,” Kate said quietly as silent tears continued to make their hot descent down her cheeks. Oh how she wished her girlfriend could promise that. How she wished she could rescue her from these spiralling thoughts and these debilitating, choking feelings, but she couldn’t. No one could. It was senseless. “You can’t control everything,” Kate whispered dejectedly. She felt Yelena’s arms tighten around her once more. They tightened with resolve.

    “I can try,” Yelena said stubbornly. Kate almost smiled despite everything. Trust Yelena Belova to think she could control the uncontrollable. Although if anyone could, it would be her.

    Another half an hour of soothing words and gentle kisses, and Kate’s tears had eventually been vanquished. Her breathing had become regular and her eyes heavy and soon she would be asleep, finally, held tightly within her girlfriend’s arms.

    Kate didn’t wake from her dreamless sleep until just after midday. She was greeted downstairs by a bleary eyed Yelena who was desperately trying to bleed the coffee machine dry. She’d been to Grills’ to drop off the dogs. It made sense as at least he could offer them regular walks and love. Between the hospital visits and the tears, regular walkies could not be guaranteed.

    Once Kate had been suitably cleaned, kissed and caffeinated, Yelena bundled her back into the car and across the Hudson in the hope of seeing Eleanor. To Kate’s relief, she got her wish.

    The room was silent, apart from the quiet buzz of machinery and the regular sounds coming from the heart monitor that told Kate her mother was still alive, or at the very least, her mother’s heart was still beating.

    The brunette clutched her hands together tightly. They were already feeling Yelena’s absence. The blonde had been asked to wait outside, Perrina’s orders. It made sense. Eliminate as much risk as possible by admitting family and only family, but of course Yelena hadn’t wanted to let Kate to go in there by herself. She’d argued her case and laboured her point, but the police officer on the door had no intention of budging. So, after a reassuring hug that seemed to last a lifetime despite being nowhere near long enough, Kate had turned the handle and entered her mother’s room, alone.

    Yelena, in typical Yelena fashion, hung stubbornly just outside the door like a shadow, watching Kate closely through the glass, watching for any sign of danger, or for Kate’s complete emotional breakdown.

    Kate’s eyes went to the chair in the corner of the room as they worked to avoid the prone woman in the hospital bed at its centre. There were tubes and wires and drips, all running in and out of their subject, and Kate didn’t know if she could bring herself to look. It was like something from a movie, not real life. But, she supposed, that was kind of what her life had become. Maybe it was just the next inevitable twist in Kate’s super-hero story. A trial, another challenge, the end of Act Two. But of course, the end of Act Two was always the moment the hero hit rock bottom, and the dread that still sat heavily in Kate’s stomach was telling her this particular twist ran deeper.

    Kate picked up the chair from the corner, placed it next to her mother’s bed and sat. She sighed a heavy, steadying sigh and summoned the courage to look up at her Eleanor. Kate’s stomach lurched. Her mother’s skin was flushed and not pale as Kate had expected it to be. In fact, when the young Avenger reached for her mother’s hand, she found it hot to the touch. Eleanor Bishop had a fever. Kate closed her hand around her mother’s even tighter and pressed her lips to her knuckles.

    She could hear muffled voices coming from just outside the room. One was certainly Yelena’s, Kate would recognise her deep and pretty sexy tone from a mile away, even if she was muttering angrily under her breath. Was she speaking Russian? Kate glanced up to see Yelena practically hissing at a nurse in blue scrubs. Clearly her annoyance at not being allowed to accompany Kate had escalated into frustrated and non-sensical Russian ravings. To Kate’s surprise though, the young woman responded in kind to Yelena. She’d responded in Russian, Kate was sure of it, despite the hushed tones. Was this the other Widow? The one who told Yelena about New York Presbyterian. It would stand to reason. The question was, what was she doing at Hackensack in New Jersey and why was Yelena so clearly pissed with her?

    The blonde jabbed a finger in the nurse’s chest and muttered something unintelligible. The young woman fell silent immediately, nodded her begrudged agreement, and swiftly left. Well, that had told her, whatever that was.

    For a moment, Yelena stood brooding and motionless in the corridor, unaware of Kate’s gaze upon her. A moment later, she cast her eyes back towards Kate and hazel met violet. The blonde was surprised to see Kate staring back at her through the sliver of glass in the door. A split second later and Yelena’s surprise was replaced by a familiar mix of concern, softness and frustration. Kate had a nagging feeling that Yelena wasn’t quite telling her everything. She’d seen it happen twice before. Once at Christmas when Yelena thought Kate had needed protecting from her feelings, and once in Siberia, when the ex-assassin thought Kate had needed protecting from the harsh realities of being an Avenger. This felt like the latter. Had they’d gone backwards after their breakthrough in Sarajevo? Probably not, but in time of stress and worry people did unsavoury things to protect the ones they loved. Kate offered Yelena a forlorn smile and her girlfriend offered one in return. Her eyes were warm and danced brightly in the artificial light of the corridor. She was so beautiful. So supportive. So… strong yet gentle. Whatever wrong and unexpected shit was coming their way, Kate knew that if they faced it together, head on, they could handle it. That’s what partners did.

    “Mom. If you can hear me,” Kate whispered, as she pressed another kiss against the fever flushed skin of the back of Eleanor’s hand, “We’re going to find who did this, we’re going to make it right, and you’re going to be okay.”

    There was nothing to do. Kate had finished Below Deck, she’d finished her rewatch of Love is Blind, she’d finished Australian Love Island, she’d finished Witcher Season Four and she’d finished the latest series of Ahsoka. Why did she binge everything she wanted to watch immediately on the day release? How could she possibly get her mind off her mother’s situation without trash to watch on television? She’d even resorted to tidying her bedroom and picking her clothes up off the floor, but alas, Yelena had already emptied the wash basket and put a darks wash on before heading out to pick up Fanny and Lucky. So couldn’t even do chores if she tried!

    There was really only one thing for it, Kate would have to cook. That had always been the plan anyways, right? The surprise dinner? It was the perfect thing. She could keep her brain occupied and her hands busy, plus she could thank Yelena for everything she’d done for her thus far; taxi service, dog ferrier, body pillow, human tissue. She really had been wonderful, if not a little over protective, but it was in her nature, and she certainly had a track history when it came to Kate.

    Kate gathered her laminated cheat sheet and her ingredients and set to work. She diced onions, tomatoes and minced a ton of garlic. She prepped her wings in flour and spices, and she brewed her coffee for the tiramisu. She just needed to keep busy.

    After Kate seared her lamb amongst the onions, garlic and aromatics, she added her chopped tomatoes and a generous portion of green chilli. Damn this dish was going to blow her brains out. That said, it was all starting to smell pretty fucking good, even if she did say so herself. Perhaps if her mom made it through, Kate could show her that she wasn’t a total disaster in the kitchen. If her mom didn’t, she’d die thinking Kate was a total failure. Nope, nope, nope. That was the dread talking. Kate needed to keep on track. She raided a cupboard for the gallon of rapeseed oil she’d hidden behind the tinned vegetables and the various pastas just as the lock to her apartment turned and Yelena Belova strolled in, dog- less.

    Kate frowned. She wanted her fluff pillow. She needed her fluff pillow. “Where are the dogs?” She asked. She may have sounded a little unhinged. That’s because she was. “Hmm?” Came Yelena’s vague response. Kate’s frown deepened. That wasn’t the response she was hoping for.

    “I thought you said you were getting the dogs on the way back?” Kate asked once more as the light bulb of realisation pinged behind her girlfriend’s eyes.

    “Oh, yes. I did, I did say that.” Yelena nodded enthusiastically, just to confuse Kate even more. “But I thought Grills could keep them for the night. Let you rest properly,” she explained as she strode over to Kate and placed a small kiss upon her lips on her way to the fridge-freezer. Kate huffed a little in disappointment. She missed her Pizza Dog, she missed the comfort he brought her, but she didn’t exactly miss him clambering all over her in the night, or waking her up at seven am for breakfast. So perhaps Yelena had a point. “Actually, I stopped for some ice cream instead,” Yelena grinned as she revealed a tub of Half-Baked from the black plastic bag she’d been carrying. The blonde had clearly made a stop at the local corner-store on her way back from Avenger’s HQ and Kate couldn’t love her more for it. Yes, she was making tiramisu, but that was more Yelena’s thing. Half-Baked was positively Kate’s thing, and not just because she always leapt feet first into every situation with only a Half-Baked plan.

    Kate smiled warmly and for the first time in twenty four hours, her stomach’s resident butterflies were of the happy variety, and they were all a-flutter. The power of ice cream and the power of a wonderfully thoughtful girlfriend.

    “Aaaand,” Yelena teased, oh she wasn’t finished there, “I bought some wine. I think you deserve a glass of….” Yelena’s smile faltered into a bemused expression. She glanced around the kitchen and took in the sight. Chopping boards, discarded knives, discarded vegetable skins and much much more. Yes, there had certainly been signs of… a struggle, of sorts. “Wait… what are you…?”

    “I’m cooking,” Kate announced, with half pride and half hysteria. It was totally normal to be cooking when your mother was on her death bed. People needed to eat, even stressed people. If anything, stressed people needed to eat more, to feel better about all the stressy shit that was going on around them. So this was fine, cooking a three course meal was totally fine. “It was going to be a surprise,” Kate shrugged sheepishly.

    “This was the surprise?” Yelena asked as her face softened. She had the look of a woman who wasn’t often treated to a surprise, or a happy surprise at least. It was Kate’s heart that was a flutter now. Perhaps the dread could be lifted, even if it was only for a moment. “I had it all planned,” Kate said, her heart feeling tighter, hotter and happier, and suddenly her voice cracked. It wasn’t her heart that felt tight, it was her chest. The dread had lifted alright, and once it had, Kate had been found wanting. She was running on fumes, and the tears began to fall. “Chicken wings, Indian food, dessert. I wanted…,” she sniffed and tried desperately to wipe away the tears, “I know it’s a little crazy but I wanted to do something nice for you. You…you…” she sniffed once more and was quickly enveloped within Yelena’s arms.

    “Kate this is…,” Yelena searched for the right words as the brunette clung to her. “Wow, this is so very sweet of you darling, and yes maybe a little crazy but you do not have to do any of this right now, okay? All you need to do is rest.”

    “I know. I know I don’t have to but I need to,” Kate drew back from Yelena’s embrace in search of her hazel eyes, awash with concern. “I need to keep my brain away from…,” Kate sniffed again and turned on her heel in search of a large pan from a cupboard beneath the stovetop. “I just need to keep moving. If I stop I…”

    “We can keep moving,” Yelena soothed as she placed gentle hands back upon her girlfriend, “We can absolutely keep moving by ordering some take out and finishing that Australian Love Island, you don’t need to-.”

    “No. I do need to,” Kate snapped and shrugged out of her girlfriend’s grasp. Yelena immediately pulled away, her brow furrowed. She was hurt, Kate had hurt her, and immediately the young Avenger felt a sharp pang of guilt. “I’m sorry, I’m sorry,” the brunette apologised, heartfelt and urgently. She needed to breathe, she just needed to breathe, if she could just explain then Yelena would see. “Please, please just let me,” she said earnestly, finding Yelena’s eyes once more. “I want to make it nice for you. I went to classes dammit, I planned it all, I’m not going to let whatever prick poisoned my mother ruin my romantic dinner plans too.”

    Not only did the hurt fade from Yelena’s expression, but a small, happy smile began to pull at the corner of her lips. “Is that where you were yesterday?” She asked. “Yes,” Kate whispered apprehensively.

    “Learning how to do this stuff?” Yelena’s small happy smile grew into the one smile that always made everything worth it.

    “Uh huh,” Kate nodded, now with a smile of her own.

    Yelena couldn’t contain her happiness now. “Can I try it?”

    The brunette grinned. Romantic dinner plans were well and truly on the menu. Fuck you, prick.

    Kate grabbed Yelena an Upphjod teaspoon and passed it to her girlfriend. She waited with baited breath as the blonde poked about a bit in the curry and then fetched herself a small taster of the sauce before depositing it in her mouth. A moment went by as Yelena let the spicy gravy wash over her pallet. Kate was sweating, actually sweating with nervous anticipation. Yelena frowned a little, as she always did, and then she flashed Kate a downturned smile of appraisal.

    A moment later, and the curry lover gave her verdict. “That is actually not bad.” Kate’s heart soared. “Really?”

    “Really, I can taste the onions, the cumin,” Yelena’s arms snaked around her waist and her eyes flashed teasingly. Yelena was being a flirt. “Perhaps a touch of coriander?” She asked as she pressed a kiss against Kate’s lips and then took a hearty sniff. “Oh and a lot of garlic,” she grinned, clearly happy with her detective work from the day before. Kate rolled her eyes and playfully slapped Yelena away. “Idiot.”

    “Maybe sometime soon you can teach me,” Yelena suggested as she settled to lean against the kitchen sideboard.

    “I’d like that,” Kate said as she stuck her head back under the stovetop in search of a large pan for the wings. She really would like that. Her teaching Yelena something beyond how to be a real human being for a change, she relished the idea. The blonde had taught her so much, Kate would love to return the favour.

    “I’ll get you some wine and set the table, hmm?”

    “Sounds perfect. Yes, please.”

    And with that, Yelena got to work. She poured the wine and stuck Kate’s ‘Good Chart Shit’ playlist on over the kitchen Sonos. Both Avengers swayed around happily, each stealing kisses along the way. Every now and then Yelena would pinch a taste of food and make excited and satisfied noises. Kate would laugh and chide her but on the inside she felt giddy. This was it. This was exactly what she’d needed. Wine, food, dancing and her girlfriend. A girlfriend that was eyeing her carefully as she set tried to light the flame beneath the gallon of rapeseed oil.

    “I can handle it,” Kate said accusatorially.

    “I did not say anything,” Yelena shrugged, but she almost certainly smirked. “Your eyes said something. I know what I’m doing.” Yelena’s eyes narrowed and Kate couldn’t keep the giddy grin from her lips. “What? I do!” she appealed. Yelena looked seriously unconvinced, so it was only right that Kate took it upon herself to convince her. She abandoned the gas stovetop and set her hands upon her hips, defiantly. “You have to cook them through first on a lower heat and then put them in again but higher so they crisp up.”

    “Mmm. Who knew you were such a wing aficionado?”

    “Not me,” Kate was happy to concede, because credit where credit’s due, right? “Martha Stewart,” she explained with a cool shrug.

    “Well, thank you and Martha for making this effort. You didn’t have to.” “Yes I did,” Kate said as she drew her girlfriend to her. “I want to show you how much I love you. How special you are.” Yelena could only smile. Even after six months of being together Yelena still struggled to take a compliment unless Kate was admiring her Systema. Kate supposed that was what happened when you were treated like a weapon that could be discarded and thrown away for most of your life.

    “You’re taking such good care of me,” Kate whispered before she kissed her girlfriend softly. Her tongue found Yelena’s bottom lip and the blonde sighed contentedly as Kate drew her closer. They stayed like that for some time, getting lost in each other. Lost in every kiss, every tender touch. So lost that for a moment chicken wings were all but forgotten. “You could just tell me how much you love me,” Yelena whispered against Kate’s lips. “You don’t need to go to all this effort right now.”

    “Easy as that is it?” Kate mused. As easy as those three words. I love you. Three simple words that meant so much. And in a way, Yelena was right. An ‘I love you’ could mean so much more than a dinner or a gift, said at the right time to the right person. Then again, sometimes an action said more than words ever could. That didn’t mean that Kate didn’t want to hear Yelena say those words. It didn’t mean she wasn’t desperate for them. Sure, she should be happy with the love Yelena showed with her actions, her support, her strength. But selfishly, Kate wanted to hear those words more than anything, even though she knew she should wait until Yelena was ready. Until the time was right.

    “Yes, it is as easy as that,” Yelena whispered and her hot breath tickled the soft skin of Kate’s cheeks.

    “Telling you I love you?”

    “Yes.”

    “Well, I’d have thought if it were that easy-.”

    “I should have said it by now?” Yelena asked, eyebrow raised and Kate was stunned. She shouldn’t have said anything. Yelena had caught her, she’d caught her pushing. Something she’d swore she’d never do. But to Kate’s surprise, Yelena didn’t seem angry or irritated, she seemed bemused.

    “Okay,” Yelena shrugged, “I love you.”

    Kate’s brain almost fell out of her gaping mouth and onto the tiled floor. She what? She loved her? Just like that? It was that easy? Those three words just fell out of her mouth as if she’d said them a thousand times before. No paralysing anxiety, no grand gesture, no sweetness; just three words.

    “Er…” Kate blinked, “You- just like that?” Was she being an asshole? Was it an asshole question to ask? Too easy. Kate was blindsided, she was in shock. It just seemed so… easy, but not like she’d rehearsed, easy as if… easy as if she hadn’t rehearsed at all. As if she hadn’t meant it at all. But why would she say it if she didn’t mean it? And why would she do that to her now? Yelena had been so conscientious about those three words. So conscientious about Kate’s feelings. She wanted to say it when she knew, when she was she was sure, so that there was no risk of Kate getting hurt. But here they were and she’d said it, and she hadn’t fucking blinked.

    “Just like that,” she smiled coolly, as if everything was fine. This was all totally fine and not at all weird.

    “After all this time…?” Kate asked. She’d waited so long. She’d fantasised about hearing Yelena’s beautiful voice say the words. Pictured how it would be, where it would be, what they would do after. None of those fantasy scenarios played out like this. None of them felt empty like this. Had she built it up too much in her mind? Was it really just three words? “What did you expect, a marching band?” Yelena smiled warmly. She held Kate tightly and captured her eyes. Yelena wanted Kate to see. “I love you Kate Bishop. It is that simple.” Yelena’s arms tightened even more and Kate felt the dread creep back into her stomach, where it sat, heavy. She was holding Kate so much, comforting her, exerting her strength, her grip, her control. Yelena was never like this with her, never this physical, never this dominating. Kate needed comforting but this didn’t feel right, it didn’t feel like comfort at all. In fact, it was starting to feel like something else entirely. It was starting to feel like coercion. It was so well judged. Whatever Kate needed, even the things she never knew she needed, Yelena had supplied.
