    Kate’s stomach dropped as her mind wandered to the what ifs. What ifs that she should never ever consider. What ifs that if true would… well, they would shatter her reality. As well as her heart and her soul. But she had to ask them, because it was the only way to get to the truth and perhaps the only way to keep her mother safe.

    Yelena must have noticed the brewing storm behind Kate’s eyes as her grip grew even tighter. “I am sorry it has taken me so long. I guess with everything that is happening I… I don’t see the point of wasting any more time.” Kate swallowed. She was saying all the right things. All the things Kate wanted to hear. “I love you, Kate. More than anything. You’ve changed me in-,”

    “Who were you talking to? At the hospital?” Kate blurted out. The question came before she’d even really had time to process it.

    Yelena frowned. It was the right question, the test would be whether Yelena answered it truthfully.

    “A nurse,” she shrugged nonchalantly. Well, that first part was plausible enough. “The doctors wouldn’t tell me anything, not being family, so I asked one of the nurses. Aren’t you going to tell me you love me back?” She asked with what she must have thought was her most dashing smile. Yelena was deflecting and Kate’s dread grew once more. “I love you, so much,” Kate uttered, but her voice wavered and suddenly the atmosphere changed. The apartment felt as if it had grown at least five degrees cooler and suddenly Kate realised that she may well be in quite some danger. If Yelena was deflecting, if Yelena was lying, then what else had she been lying about?

    Kate desperately tried to hide her faltering smile as she wriggled from Yelena’s grip. “I just need to make a call, I… I have a feeling about this nurse.”

    “Kate I’m sure it’s nothing.”

    “I’m sure you’re right.”

    “You’re worrying over nothing, like you said. Let’s get back to dinner and get your mind off it.” Yelena was bargaining with her. This wasn’t comfort. This was manipulation. “After I make this call,” Kate insisted, in the most light-hearted, casual, ‘totally not going out of her fucking mind’ voice she could muster.

    “Kate,” Yelena smiled easily, hands on her hips. “You know you sound a little crazy, right?” Fuck. This was manipulation. It was gas-lighting one-oh-one. Yelena wasn’t just lying, Yelena knew that Kate was asking the right questions. Kate was right about the nurse. Which posed the question, what else was she right about? Those what ifs?

    “Why would you say that? That I’m crazy.”

    “Because it seems a little crazy.” Yelena was too calm. Too collected. “I’m not crazy,” Kate insisted. Fuck, it really unravelling. Had the whole thing just been a massive manipulation? “I just don’t think you’re telling me everything.” “I think you’re tired babe, you should rest,” Yelena said soothingly as she reached for Kate once more. She called her ‘babe’. Yelena never called Kate ‘babe’. Their eyes met. It was a slip and they both knew it. No, this hadn’t been a manipulation from the start, but Kate could take no solace in that, because this wasn’t Yelena. There was no way this could be her Yelena. She was sure of it now.

    Kate pulled away from the blonde’s grasp, violently rejecting her touch. Hazel eyes flashed with hurt. “Do you not trust me?” Yelena asked, her voice thick with emotion. “Kate…?” She appealed once more.

    The answer was no, Kate didn’t, not anymore. Was she going crazy? Because this was crazy right? If all the what ifs turned out to be some insane reality. She couldn’t really be considering it, could she? She couldn’t really be considering the idea that Yelena was in some way responsible for the gut-wrenching chaos of the last twenty-four hours? Yelena, the woman she loved.

    Maybe she really was going crazy. Maybe the grief and the stress and the sleep deprivation had sent her imagination into overdrive. Perhaps Yelena was right, maybe she really did need her rest. But she couldn’t rest, not yet. If the nurse was a Widow and was still at the hospital with her mother, she needed to make a call, because those what ifs had consequences she didn’t want to begin to imagine.

    “I just need to settle my head. Even if it does sound crazy, it’s only one call.” Yelena shook her head in disbelief. “I don’t know why you would not trust me on this?” “I do. Okay?” Kate did her best to de-escalate. If she was going to get through this, she just needed Yelena to let her make that call. She could make that call and this would be over. “I just have a feeling. A feeling about this nurse and I can’t shake it and I just need to make a phone call,” Kate rambled as she dug her phone out of her pocket.

    “I told you, they’re a staff nurse,” Yelena implored her but it was no use, Kate was determined. She couldn’t risk anything else happening to her mother. “After everything… you think I’m involved in this!?” Yelena raised her voice and Kate flinched. She’d never heard Yelena shout in anger before. It was different, she was different. It was visceral and violent and terrifying.

    “No, I don’t, I-.”

    “After I tell you how I feel. After I tell I love you?” Yelena’s voice broke and her anger gave way to hurt.

    “No, I-.”

    “After Bosnia. After Christmas? After I made love to you?”

    After they made love. They were in love. And then something changed. Kate’s heart began to ache.

    “You know how crazy that sounds right?” There were tears in Yelena’s eyes, tears rolling down her cheeks. She looked so desperate, so lost, so hurt. Kate couldn’t stand it. She couldn’t stand seeing her this way. It was almost enough to make Kate stop and put her phone down. To make her reach for her girlfriend.

    “Sweetheart, I just wanna call the hospital. Will you let me call the hospital?” Kate was pleading with Yelena now, hoping beyond hope that she could somehow reach her through whatever this façade was.

    Yelena’s lip trembled as she took a steadying breath and attempted to calm the sobs that threatened to take take control of her body. Was there some internal battle happening inside her girlfriend’s mind? Was her Yelena still in there somewhere, pulling for her, fighting for her in Kate’s corner. “Yelena, will you let me call the hospital? Please?” Kate appealed once more but softer this time, pouring into it all her love and all her affection. Surely Yelena could be reached. Whatever was happening, surely, she could see reason. Surely this wasn’t how it would all end.

    Bloodshot, violet eyes met hazel and something changed in that moment. Kate was frozen to the spot. Yelena sniffed reticently as her eyes grew darker and her face harder. “I’m sorry Kate Bishop,” Yelena spoke softly, but her voice was completely devoid of softness or sympathy. In fact, Yelena didn’t sound sorry at all. The blonde crinkled her nose and shrugged apathetically. “I cannot let you do that.” And there it was. The lies had stopped, the tears, the theatrics. The mask had fallen away and all that was left was the cold, visceral assassin that lay beneath. “I have orders and as you know, I am quite the perfectionist.”

    It took every ounce of strength in Kate, every inch of willpower, not to buckle. To not simply give in, despite her body being on the verge of betraying her. Surely her heart had stopped beating in chest, and yet it raced. She felt breathless, tight, trapped even, and yet her lungs ached from use. Her legs were rooted to the ground, unmoving, and yet all she wanted to do was run. Run as far as she could. Away from this nightmarish alternative reality that had so suddenly become real life. Away from this spectre of a woman who stood in place of her girlfriend. Away from this car crash and into her mother’s arms.

    And that’s when Kate knew. It had been Yelena all along, and she’d allowed it to happen. “You poured her a glass of water,” Kate whispered in disbelief. She heard the words but didn’t even remember taking a breath to speak them. “I took you to see her and you poured her a glass of water.”

    Kate had never wanted to be so wrong about something in her life, but she knew… she knew she was right.

    “I did.” Yelena nodded coolly. She was even smiling, a smile Kate had seen so many times before. It was serene, and Kate knew.

    “But they screened you.” They swabbed her, they scanned her, they searched her. It made no sense. None of it made any sense.

    “They did,” Yelena’s smile grew. “Like a knife through butter, remember?” Kate felt sick. Yelena, this person, this assassin, whoever she was, was gloating about poisoning her mother.

    There had to be some explanation, some reason for all of this. This wasn’t Yelena, this wasn’t her Yelena. Kate tried to cast her mind back, desperately scraping and scratching around her recent memories. Had there been signs?

    “I don’t understand… I…how long have you….”

    “Give me the phone, Kate.” Yelena wasn’t asking, she was demanding. The way she called her ‘Kate’, so familiar and intimate, made Kate’s skin crawl.

    “Oh my god,” Kate breathed in disbelief as she felt dread give way once more to panic and helplessness.

    “Kate, give me the phone now. Or I will take it from you.”

    “I don’t understand.” Kate felt frantic, her thoughts fighting against each other, desperate to be heard. Her world was crumbling. Everything was crumbling. The last nine months, her life, their life, their home, their trust and love and safety. Kate swallowed as one thought beat out the rest. It was an awful thought. “And… and Fisk?” She stuttered. Yelena simply smiled. She looked grimly satisfied. This smile was new. This smile was not her girlfriend, and Kate suddenly felt a very different flash of emotion. She was angry. Angry at whoever this was that stood in front of her. Angry at whoever gave her orders. Angry at whatever or whoever it was that thought they could fuck so royally with her life in this way. She wasn’t helpless, Yelena and her training had made sure of that, and if she was going to help save her mother, she was going to have to fight.

    Kate’s tears fell still upon her cheeks and she inhaled with resolve. Yelena’s eyes flashed with delight. “You were never visiting that Widow, were you? You had no intention of helping my mom.”

    The blonde continued to smile, happily this time. She was having fun, and it only fuelled Kate’s fire.

    “It took you longer to see through me than I thought it would. You must really love me, huh?”

    “I don’t love you.” Kate gritted her teeth. She loved her Yelena and she was going to fucking fight for her too.

    “Hmm. True. The Yelena you love was weak, and gone now, I think. Good riddance.” The blonde sneered. What did she mean, ‘gone’? Where did she go? Did they take her somewhere? Was this not Yelena stood in front of her?

    “What do you mean, gone?”

    “Now, now. That would be telling.” Whoever this asshole was, they were a cocky fucking piece of shit. Kate needed answers, damn it. Kate needed to know. Where was she? How long had she been gone for? Sure, maybe Yelena had been acting a little weird for the last day or so but beyond that… had she been hiding things from Kate? The showers, the deflection, the going off by herself… Kate wracked her brain in a desperate attempt to somehow work out when it all started. Was it even Yelena that had returned to her from Mostar? Kate’s stomach dropped. Was it even Yelena that…. Sure it had been unexpected but it had felt so real. So intimate. So loving. It had to have been after that, oh god please tell me it was after that. “How long? How long has it been?”

    “Long enough,” Yelena smirked and Kate wanted to scream, to tear at her, to beg her for the truth. Her smirk grew at Kate’s obvious distress. She was having fun “Not that long though, I know what you’re thinking.” Yelena visibly shivered at the thought. “So sentimental, such a disappointment.”

    “She’s human,” Kate hissed, coming to the defence of her girlfriend. What an absolute mind- fuck.

    “No, no,” Yelena shrugged dismissively. “I am not human, I am a killer. It is what I was built for. Oh,” Yelena gasped in false realisation. “What if your Yelena was just a figment of your imagination, huh? A little wishful thinking.”

    “Fuck you,” Kate spat.

    “You wish,” the blonde teased. It was one of their jokes that they shared. A dumb, stupid joke, but hearing it from this Yelena’s lips completely enraged her. Kate was done fucking around.

    “What did you do?!” The brunette demanded.

    “Woah, woah, woah,” Yelena held up her hands defensively as an amused laugh escaped her. “It’s okay,” she soothed, “She has everything she has ever wanted now.” The jibe should have hurt her but it didn’t. Kate didn’t think much else could at this point. She was past that. “How did they get to you?”

    Yelena shrugged casually. “It doesn’t matter. The only thing that matters is that they did, to liberate me from this domesticated mediocrity.” Yelena took a glance around Kate’s apartment. From the duplex balcony, the kitchen to the beautifully laid out dinner table. “Can you imagine me, here with you, for the rest of my life?” The assassin shivered again. Kate swallowed. That one had hurt. That one had hurt more than anything else because she’d allowed herself to dream, to hope. She’d had so much hope, so many plans, so many dreams for the future. Yelena had always tried to manage Kate’s expectations because it wasn’t as if their jobs were risk free but she’d dreamed enough for the both of them and she knew Yelena had too. Retirement, if Yelena made it past forty. A little place in Ohio near Natasha. Christmases with the Bartons. Lots and lots of dogs. It’s what happiness looked like for them. But even if she got Yelena back, the real Yelena, could they survive this if her mother didn’t? It was a question Kate didn’t have the courage to answer.

    “Oh but you had imagined it. Poor thing,” Yelena pouted and it was like a fucking arrow to the heart, because she knew. Somehow she knew. This person, whoever it was, had her girlfriend’s memories, her body, her eyes, her lips. She felt the same and tasted the same and kissed the same and Kate had a sinking feeling that it’s because she was the same. She was all Yelena, apart from one thing. “This must all be pretty difficult for you. Your mother, your girlfriend. I can only apologise, but you should know, it is nothing personal.” Nothing personal? Nothing personal!? It felt pretty fucking person. Kate Bishop had her heart carved out, stamped on and cast into the fiery pits of mount doom, twice in the last day. It was being twisted and played with and distorted and she was so done with it all. Because you know what, her mother wasn’t dead and her girlfriend was still very much alive and kicking. So, she allowed herself to hope. She would fuel her fight on hope.

    Kate smiled with grim satisfaction. “You’re a pretty shitty assassin, you know that? The doctors say that-.”

    “Give it time,” Yelena interjected stoically.

    But Kate didn’t have time. She needed to make that call, now. She had Carol on speed-dial. If she could just dial-.

    “Do not make that call, Kate,” Yelena warned. It seemed odd for a brand new, reinstated assassin. If she didn’t want Kate to make the call why not just kill her? Was it against her orders, and if so, why? Did they need Kate for something, or did this ‘Yeleno’ have reservations about killing her? Was her Yelena still in there? “Do not make me show you what a shitty assassin is capable of.” Welp, perhaps not, but surely it was worth it. If she could just make the call, if Carol would just pick up, if she could get a message to her somehow, then it would be worth it.

    “She is dead already Kate,” Yelena doubled down. It was almost sympathetic. Almost. She wanted Kate to think that any effort she made would be futile, that her mother was a lost cause, that no matter what she did, Kate would be too late. But Yelena was forgetting that Kate Bishop was a mother-funking Avenger. “Do you really want to join her?” The Russian asked and their eyes met.

    Yelena could see Kate’s stubbornness and she knew what her next move would be. She was going to call Yelena’s best-friend Carol, and then the ruse would be up, but Kate was going to have to put Yelena down first. As non-lethally as she could.

    The blonde sighed with regret. “I did not want it to come to this. I hope you can believe me.” “I don’t,” Kate said with disdain.

    “Well then, let us hope I trained you well,” the blonde smirked.

    “I guess we’ll find out,” the brunette shrugged nonchalantly. This isn’t Yelena, just remember, this isn’t Yelena.

    “Ready for round two?” The Russian teased, an eyebrow raised.

    “Ready for me to kick your ass?” The young Avenger bit back.

    “Be careful, I might like it,” Yelena said with a wink, her voice rasping, low and alluring, and it made Kate’s skin crawl.

    Kate was done, she was so done. Done with the theatrics, done with their ridiculous tête-à- tête, done with Yelena’s time wasting. It was time to fight, and Kate Bishop wasted no time at all.

    She hurled her phone first. If Yelena wanted it so much, she could have it. The blonde easily deflected the flying telecommunications device but it had bought Kate enough time, time to close the distance between herself and the assassin. She threw the first punch, close quarters as was her style, but the blow met the same fate as her phone. Then an uppercut. It was deftly navigated as the blonde arched her back instinctually to curve away and elude the strike. Kate’s next blow, a standing kick, was parried with pure, unabated nonchalance and Kate’s fourth attempt to contact the assassin was plucked out the air with the guile of a someone who was three steps ahead. Yelena’s hands wrapped tightly around Kate’s wrist, twisted and threw her down to the floor violently.

    Kate landed with an “Oof,” as all the wind was knocked out of her.

    “At least make it a challenge, Kate,” came Yelena’s taunting voice. Well, it wasn’t as if she wasn’t trying. But Kate needed to focus, she could do this, she just needed to take the emotion out of it. She needed to not think about who she was attacking, who she was hurting. Or trying to hurt. The only thing that mattered was that whoever this person was, they were standing in the way of Kate making a phone call that could save her mother’s life. The brunette was back on her feet in an instant and then quickly spun away from the assassin, to put distance between them once more. She needed room to catch her breath. Their eyes met and Yelena threw Kate an exacting look. She expected better. “Again,” the blonde commanded. Fuck her.

    Kate came again. She hit harder, faster, stronger but every blow was deftly parried or dodged with an agility Kate had never seen Yelena exhibit before. This wasn’t training anymore, it wasn’t play time, this was real life; despite Kate getting the distinct impression that the Russian was almost certainly still playing with her.

    The brunette ended up on the floor again and this time Yelena didn’t show any mercy. She punished Kate with a thundering kick to the stomach. Every atom of oxygen rocketed out of her lungs and every rib screamed out in excruciating pain. Kate gasped for air as two strong hands grabbed her by her shirt and hauled her to her feet.

    Crockery shattered and the cutlery that they’d so carefully picked out together rang loudly against the tiled floor as Kate was thrown into the air and then slammed down violently onto the table. Her neck snapped back and her head cracked viciously against the laminated surface. Light exploded behind her eyes and for a moment all was nothing and nothing was everything. Her head was slammed again. Once, twice, three times and Kate began to see more of nothing and much less of everything.

    Strong hands released her and she rolled like a rag doll from the table and onto her cool apartment floor. Kate took solace in the feel of the tiles against her flushed cheeks. Their coolness cut through the darkness and she knew she had to get up. Just get up. Keep fighting, keep fighting and win. Her mother’s life depended on it, and at this point, her life probably did too.

    Yelena was brutal, punishing and unforgiving. It was clear that Kate had never sparred with the real Yelena, it was clear she’d been holding back and it was clear now, why Yelena Belova was so revered. She was suffocating. She showed no mercy and she could beat you in a moment. Like she’d said, she didn’t need ten minutes, she just needed ten seconds. Kate placed a palm against the cool tiles and began to peel herself off the floor. She pushed hard and forced her chest upwards with a groan. Pain hit with force. It tore through her. But she had to push through it, she had to force herself.

    “Stay down, Kate.” Yelena said. The blonde pitied her, Kate could hear it in her voice, but it only served to fuel her more.

    Fuck her. Kate was going to win. She’d always been a winner, she knew how, and Yelena had taught her how to win under any circumstances. She’d given her the tools. Kate just needed to think. Think Kate, think. Why was she playing the Russian at her game? Why was she trying to take on a hand to hand master in hand to hand combat? She was being too emotional. She needed to level the playing field, she needed to do what Kate Bishop did best. She needed to let some arrows fly.

    With another pained groan, Kate hauled herself to her feet, but far too quickly. Her world spun and she almost found herself back down on those cool black and white tiles of hers. The brunette felt sick but she had to keep going, she had to reach her bow, but as if by magic, in some sort of twisted version of wish fulfilment, Kate’s bow appeared in front of her. It was right there, all she had to do was reach out and take it, but as her vision cleared Kate soon realised that her bow was in the hands of the woman who was trying to kill her. Yelena was offering it to her, freely. Surely this was just another tease, another taunt, another mind game. Well fuck her, Kate was going to take her bow because it was hers. She might not be able to see straight, but Kate Bishop was the best in the world. She could always shoot straight. Kate’s hands wrapped around the carbon fibre contraption. It felt familiar and she took comfort in it. Yelena smiled with satisfaction, she was enjoying whatever sick game she was no doubt playing, and then threw Kate’s quiver down onto the floor unceremoniously. “You really are a terrible student you know? Come on, I’ll give you a free shot.” Smug, patronising, little shit. In another world it was probably a comment that Kate would have smirked and fluttered her eyelashes at. She’d have made some terrible, punny quip about making Yelena pay, but not today. Today, she was feeling far more to the point. “Fine.”

    In one swift motion, Kate flicked an arrow from the floor and into the air using the curved tip of her bow. Instinctually she plucked it from its path, loaded it and fired from close range. Kate heard the impact; a sick thud as the arrow found its target. Yelena staggered backwards from the power of the projectile that hurtled into her body. Kate felt sick all over again. She wanted to vomit. She’d just shot her girlfriend. She’d just shot her fucking girlfriend. What the fuck was happening? Less than fifteen minutes earlier Kate was cooking Yelena curry and now she was filling her with arrows. She was going to be sick. The sound of it, the way her body absorbed the impact, the velocity. The way she was thrown back and then lurched forward violently.

    But no sooner had Yelena been thrown off course by Kate’s arrow, had she righted herself again. She didn’t even grimace as she wrapped her left hand around the arrow lodged deep within her right shoulder and pulled. The assassin didn’t even flinch as she drew the carbon and aluminium composite through her flesh and bone, and then discarded it apathetically to the floor. All as if it were nothing. There was no pain or discomfort, almost as if Yelena didn’t even feel it at all. Like her synapses weren’t firing or the messages weren’t getting through. It explained the injuries. The morning before Yelena had ached to the high heavens, but that evening she’d moved with ease. Did that mean that something had happened to Yelena between the time she’d dropped Kate in the Village and before the brunette had returned? It seemed crazy but it made sense. It made really scary sense. Yelena shook her head and tutted loudly for dramatic effect. “Oh Kate. Come on, you can do better than that.” Sadly, it was the truth. Kate had found the arrow and fired the bow but she hadn’t put the assassin down. She’d hoped she wouldn’t have to. She’d hoped that an arrow to the shoulder at point blank range would have been enough to incapacitate the blonde, but this was Yelena Belova they were talking about and Kate had been a fool to think it. In truth, Kate wasn’t brave enough to take the option. She wasn’t brave enough to put Yelena down, because she still had hope that she could get her back. She’d risked her mother’s life on that hope, and she may have just lost.

    The Russian shook her head further at Kate’s hesitation. She took the bow from Kate’s hands and threw it to the floor. Kate swung but found only air and was rewarded with a swift, biting kick to the ribs. The brunette doubled over in pain just before Yelena’s strong hands found Kate again. This time they were around her neck. They dragged Kate upright and threw her against the wall, hard. Fingers tightened and Kate felt pressure build against her windpipe. Yelena was going to choke her out. The brunette lashed out desperately with knees and elbows and fists but nothing could relinquish Yelena’s vice-like grip. Hazel eyes bore into hers. They were on fire, alight with the thrill of the fight, the thrill of the kill. Kate gasped for air but her lungs came up short. Lack of oxygen meant her desperate limbs became uncoordinated and her blows lacked any real venom. Kate had to break free, she had to. For her mother, for herself, for the woman who’s hands were slowly but surely choking the life out of her. There was only one thing left to do. Beg and hope. Hope that her Yelena was in there somewhere and was ready to fight for her.

    “Yelena…. Please,” Kate choked as she stared into those dark, thrill-filled eyes. She felt as if she was getting lost. Lost in their darkness as darkness threatened to claim her. “Yelena… I… I love… you. This isn’t yo-.” Yelena had lost patience with Kate’s ploy. She slammed the brunette against the wall and released her, letting her fall into a crumpled mess of a person on the floor.

    Kate gasped for air. She felt giddy as the oxygen repopulated her lungs and for once she was grateful for already being on the floor. If she’d been stood upright she was pretty sure her knees would have betrayed her.

    The brunette pushed against the plasterboard and dragged herself up the wall, slowly. Every inch hurt, every part of her body was on fire, but she had to get back up. She had to keep on getting up.

    “Yelena,” she whispered and then spoke her girlfriend’s name once more but louder. “Yelena, we can help y-.”

    Searing hot pain flashed through her thigh. It felt as if she’d been punched, hard. The impact almost sent her to her knees and at the very epicentre of her pain was a black composite arrow. She’d been shot.

    “I think it is you who needs help now Kate Bishop,” came Yelena’s voice from the other-side of the kitchen.

    “Yelena,” Kate breathed through the pain as Yelena loaded up another arrow. She had to keep trying, she couldn’t give up. “Sweetheart, I-.”

    The assassin released another thundering arrow and Kate felt her heart skip a beat. Blood rushed in her ears and breath caught in her throat. The arrow had pierced her chest, and pinned her to the wall behind her.

    “I would not move if I were you,” Yelena warned and she was right. The arrow was close to her heart, Kate knew it. She could feel it. If she moved she could bleed out in seconds. Yelena only needed ten.

    “Hearts are very easily broken, and I believe I may have broken yours, hmm?” Yelena mused. Kate couldn’t think anymore. She couldn’t be mad or angry or scared. She could only hear the rush of blood flooding her senses. She could only feel her heart wrenching and undulating with every beat. But she could only think of her girlfriend, of the woman she loved. “Yelena…” Kate choked. It was all she could do. All she could do was hope because it was all she had left.

    Yelena strolled over to where Kate’s phone lay useless on the floor. She picked it up from its resting place and looked at it curiously. For a moment, the brunette thought her girlfriend was about to offer it to her, after everything that had happened, but no, Yelena placed Kate’s phone down next to her, excruciatingly out of reach. The young Avenger was pinned. Move to make the call and she could bleed out before she’d even hit speed-dial. Don’t move and don’t make the call, and live with the decision your entire life.

    The blonde swung Kate’s bow over her shoulder, picked up her car keys and made for the door. Her work was done, but she couldn’t leave without firing a couple more parting shots.

    “Say hello to your mother for me,” Yelena leered. “Oh, and Kate, you really should be more ruthless.”

    Shum Chapter Notes Welcome to Exposition City! Population, this idiot.

    Here are some answers, and a few more questions. I think I've already apologised enough times for the previous chapter, but I'll do it again, just one more time. I'm sorry! But come on, it was kind of fun.

    The tone reverberated dully around the space between her ears. It was pure and and unvarying and Kate took comfort in its regularity, for it meant that her heart was still beating. She didn’t know how and she didn’t know why she needed to care, but she did. Kate’s eyes were heavy, in fact her whole body felt as if it were slipping and sinking through whatever lay beneath her. She felt skin upon skin as rough yet gentle fingers grasped her hand. The touch pulled at her and all her senses seemed to sharpen on that one spot, that one point of physical contact. Rough fingertips were replaced with soft lips and Kate felt the comforting pressure of a kiss pressed against the skin on the back of her hand. Her blood seemed to pulse ever-so-slightly against the pressure from those lips, and it was then that Kate became aware of her heartbeat. Strong and steady as it beat out its tattoo against her ribcage.

    Suddenly hot pain flashed across her sternum and Kate’s eyes flew open with a start. She gasped in agony but the mystery person who who held her hand in theirs didn’t so much as flinch. They were but a blur as Kate’s eyes struggled to adjust to what felt like blinding, artificial light. Brown hair, pale skin, dark eyes.

    “Mom?” Kate muttered breathlessly.

    “No, darling,” came a thick, accented voice. Kate knew that voice. She blinked furiously to try and pull her eyes into focus and eventually her efforts paid off as the worried face of Melina Vostokoff gradually came into view. A concerned frown framed tired eyes, eyes that softened once Kate’s settled upon hers. “Your mother is still in the hospital, she is a fighter. Of course, being your mother, this comes as no surprise, hmm?” Melina’s lips formed a tight smile and yet could only frown. Hospital?

    Kate’s brain was foggy, her memory patchy, and she quickly became aware of the dull, heavy pain at the back of her head. Her mother was in hospital? It felt familiar, although unwelcome. Wasn’t she in prison? Eleanor had been awaiting trial, Kate had visited her recently and... and “Yelena?!” Kate gasped as realisation hit her hard, right in the fucking heart. She sat up with a start and her chest immediately tightened. A sharp, penetrating pain struck her and Melina’s soft touch ushered her back down onto the bed.

    Oh god, Yelena. What had she done? Her mother, Fisk, her. It was a nightmare, surely it was just a nightmare. But her pain was real. Her leg pulsed and her heart ached and she knew that those arrows intended for her had been real, and they'd hit their target. “Shh, shh, it’s okay,” Melina’s soothed, but her voice betrayed her. There wasn’t one thing about this situation that Melina thought was okay. Her daughter had turned, or been turned, and she was very much not okay with that.

    “Melina... I....” Kate couldn’t find the words. This was so completely and utterly messed up. The woman she loved- Yelena was the woman she loved. How could this have happened? So quickly, within the blink of an eye. Everything that they had, everything that they’d built, together. Was it really gone?

    “Kate, darling, you’re safe. Your dog walker found you, you are safe, your dogs are safe,” Melina whispered as tears began to threaten Kate’s cheeks. Darling. It was the word Yelena so often used for her, a word she’d picked up from her mother, just like Kate had picked up sweetheart from hers. Kate’s chest ached even more. She didn’t care about being safe, she needed answers and suddenly all the words came at once.

    “Where’s Yelena? Something’s happened to her. She’s hurting people, I don’t understand.” Melina’s eyes were troubled, but her thumb continued to work across Kate’s knuckles. “We are yet to locate her, or understand her motives."

    “That’s not entirely true,” Came a voice from the doorway. It was Carol Danvers, a very tired looking Carol Danvers. She was in a pair of sweatpants and a loose-fitting white t-shirt and she looked as if she’d been up all night. Her face was grim, sad even, and Kate got the distinct impression that she’d had a night of it. A turned S.H.I.E.L.D. agent gone AWOL and another in the hospital wasn’t the best look for her. “How are you feeling?” she asked. Much like Melina’s, her voice was soft and delicate, but it wasn’t enough to quell the flash of frustration and anger that took her.

    “Do you want me to answer that?” Kate bit. It wasn’t fair, and Carol had no way of knowing how truly hurt Kate was, but she wasn’t in the business of sparing anyone’s feelings right now. "My…,” Kate paused for a moment. How far did she take this? How much should she tell Carol? It was a decision she’d wanted to make with Yelena, together, but it was too late for that now. Way too late. “My partner just- Yelena she....” The young Avenger had to take a breath. She was going to say it out loud, she needed to, but once she did, that was it, it was real. There was no putting it back in its box, but after a moment more, Kate swallowed m, readied herself and opened the box. “I think she poisoned my mom.”

    The two older women looked grave. They thought so too, and Kate’s unshed tears began to roll unabashedly down her cheeks.

    “I think that is highly likely,” Melina said grimly. “I am so sorry, Kate.” “I don’t understand, how could this have happened?” Kate sniffed as she felt it again. That feeling of panic and helplessness and dread swirling desperately within her stomach. Her eyes found Carol’s, pleading for some kind of explanation, some comfort in the knowledge that they knew what was happening. If they knew, they could come up with a plan, they always did. That was their job. “Kingpin too?” Kate asked, and Carol nodded solemnly. “Our agents on the ground are saying they have very little to go on. No clear entry or exit point at the facility where he was being held, no alarms raised, no immediate forensic evidence.”

    Melina nodded as she processed Carol’s offering of information. “Sounds like a Widow,” she muttered.

    “It doesn’t make sense,” Kate whispered, none of it made sense. Widows were effective, they were killers and they were very good at it. But Kate’s mother was still alive, she was still alive, but Fisk is free. If Fisk wanted Eleanor dead, and if the Widows were working for Fisk, then surely she would be dead already. It wasn’t like Yelena to botch a job. Carol pushed herself off the doorframe and made her way to Kate’s side. She pulled up a chair opposite where Melina was sat and settled into it. She smiled softly. “You’ve been very lucky Kate. To go up against a Widow and live.”

    “She could have killed me if she wanted to,” Kate said quietly, and it was surely the truth. She rather foolishly hoped that Yelena had spared her because deep down there was a part of the Russian that was still in there, but Kate knew that this hope was beyond foolish, it was dangerous. Her hope was dangerous. “She was just playing.”

    “Well, either way,” Carol continued, “The surgeon said if the arrow had penetrated just a half inch to the right you would have bled out. Lucky she’s not as talented as you with a bow, huh?”

    “I would not be so sure,” Melina said, darkly.

    “You think she meant to miss?” Kate asked with just a little too much hope. Don’t hope, Kate.

    “Almost certainly,” Melina nodded, her hands still tightly wrapped around Kate’s. “I would not take any solace in it though. Yelena took pleasure in pain as a Widow.” The older woman’s eyes grew darker, sadder, and Kate’s heart broke an impossible amount more. Melina had lost so much. She’d lost her daughters to the regime she served. Lost Yelena in The Snap, only to lose Natasha in exchange. And now she was having to face the grim possibility that she’d lost Yelena again, for a third time.

    “I’m sorry Kate, but if we’re going to find Yelena and make this right, I’m going to need to ask you a few questions,” Carol said gently. “Time is of the essence I’m afraid.” Carol was right, time was of the essence. Goodness knows long Kate had been out. Yelena could be on the other side of the world by now, or worse yet, still in New York, bringing even more havoc down on the city.

    Kate swallowed. Her brain was still foggy and her mind felt addled with grief and confusion, but she would do her best, she had to. “Okay,” the brunette nodded her agreement and Melina squeezed her hand reassuringly. Kate took so much comfort in her touch, and she suspected that clinging onto Kate, proof of her daughter’s humanity, brought Melina great comfort too. Carol looked at Kate directly now, it was all business, and Kate felt ready. “Yelena took an incoming Skype call two days ago, around twelve pm. It was encrypted. Do you know who she was calling?”

    The brunette nodded. Two days meant she’d lost a day. “Yes. Her grandmother,” Kate said matter-of-factly.

    “Just outside Mostar, yes?”

    “Yes.”

    Carol’s eyes fell to Melina’s and they shared an exchange. Knowing looks passed between the veteran fighters.

    “What? What is it?” Kate asked. If they knew something, they needed to tell her. She deserved to know. Carol clearly agreed.

    “We have reason to believe that Yelena’s grandmother has been…,” She paused to search for the right word, clearly not wanting to cause Kate too much alarm. “Compromised.” Because that wasn’t alarming. Kate’s stomach lurched, what did ‘compromised’ mean? “You mean Baka? Is she… dead?” Kate asked. Surely not Baka too. The brunette wasn’t sure she wanted to know the answer.

    Carol shook her head. “We don’t know. We had her under surveillance, for her security. Yelena’s request. But she’s no longer on the grid as of three days ago.” “ Fuck , Baka.” Kate said in disbelief. Yelena had only just got her WiFi. Did it really go that far back? It couldn’t have, but if they’d been followed to Yelena’s grandmother’s house, there was no way of knowing how long this had been in the works. Was this linked to Benny? It felt too sophisticated. Benny was a thug, not a master manipulator, but someone somewhere had used Baka to get to Yelena, and there weren’t that many people in the world who knew of her existence. Or at least, Kate hoped now. “You think Yelena was receiving instruction on the call, don’t you?” she asked.

    “Yes, in a way. We think she was triggered.” Triggered. What a word, and what an implication. Triggered. It meant that something was already inside of Yelena, waiting to come out. Whether it was conditioning, brainwashing, micro-chips... It meant that someone had been waiting for the perfect moment, and then turned her girlfriend against her. Against her will. Into someone else?

    “Triggered? How is that possible?” Kate asked as she began to feel her resolve give way. “Key words, phrases,” Carol offered.

    “No, I mean- are you saying that Yelena isn’t Yelena? That she was-she is someone else? That she’s been brainwashed?” Surely if someone had been brainwashed, they could be un- brainwashed? That was a thing. Was Kate clutching at straws? Perhaps. Was hoping dangerous? Yes. Was she going to continue to do so? Most certainly.

    “Subjugated,” Melina interjected darkly. “It is what we call it.” It was what Yelena had called it too. Not a brainwashing, nothing that intensive. A simple tactic to bring someone under control, a chemical that infiltrates and suffocates the senses. But they had a cure for something like that, and with the Red Room destroyed, surely Yelena’s of chemical subjugation should have been over.

    Carol cut in and pulled Kate from her thoughts. “We don’t know anything concrete at this point.” Captain Marvel’s eyes met Melina’s momentarily before she sharply pulled away. Melina’s eyes narrowed. There was a tension here that Kate couldn’t put her finger on. Clearly since Kate had been discovered by Grills plenty of time had passed. Enough for Melina to travel to the United States, enough for both women to have had plenty of discussion. They clearly both knew more or at least they both clearly suspected more than they were letting on.

    “That’s why we need to know if she told you anything,” Carol continued earnestly. “Anything at all that would point towards some kind of external control, or something that could tell us her next move.”

    Suddenly, Kate’s stomach flip-flopped. She’d forgotten something, or someone. She’d forgotten her phone, the phone call, the nurse . How could she have been so stupid? Had someone got to the nurse in time? Melina had said that her mother was still alive, but how could that be?

    “M-Mom,” Kate stuttered urgently, “The nurse at the hospital. I need to tell the hospital that-.” Carol laid a hand on Kate’s shoulder.

    “A female nurse was apprehended by S.H.I.E.L.D. agents last night trying to gain access to your mother’s room. She’s yet to talk.”

    Kate exhaled and although her chest pained her, she felt so much better for it. “Thank God. Yelena was talking to her in the hospital. I couldn’t hear their conversation and-,” “Did she say anything else?” Carol urged. It was abrupt but Kate understood. One problem solved, onto the next.

    “No, I don’t…” Kate paused, because Yelena had. She’d been elusive, more so than she ever had been before. After they visited her mother in prison she’d gone to visit someone and returned incredibly desperate to remove her clothes for her shower. Looking back, it was such a red flag, but at the time she was happy. So naïve. So distracted by her girlfriend’s body. Kate nodded slowly. “Yelena said she visited another Widow last night when Fisk escaped, but that was just a lie, wasn’t it?” Kate didn’t really need an answer, she knew the answer.

    Carol and Melina shared another knowing look and then the ex-Widow encouraged Kate to continue with gentle squeeze of her hand.

    “She was acting like herself but… not. She was more, everything .”

    “Controlling in her affection?” Melina asked. “Increased physical contact? The solution to all your problems?” It all sounded so familiar. How Yelena had held her, so tightly. How she’d been there for every need, ever want, every whim. How she’d let Kate lean in and depend on her warmth and support. Kate’s eyes flicked to Carol. Her expression hadn’t changed at Melina’s words. She was still concerned, her brow furrowed, her hand gently resting against Kate’s shoulder. If Kate said yes, she was admitting to a relationship, surely, but weren't they all past that now? There were more important things to worry about than the declaration of an intra-office relationship.

    Kate swallowed and then nodded solemnly. “Yes,” she said quietly and Carol’s hand tightened ever-so-slightly around her shoulder. Kate’s boss smiled with an understanding the brunette hadn’t expected. She was comforting her.

    “It’s subjugation Carol, it’s chemical ,” Melina maintained. She seemed so sure, so certain. She was the expert after all.

    “It’s not chemical,” Carol countered, with absolute certainty. But if she was certain, they why not simply tell them. Why not explain exactly what was happening? Kate wanted answers, she wanted to know why and how her life had been torn apart, and she wanted to know now. “Then what is it?” Kate demanded, losing the very little patience that she’d started this conversation with. Her head throbbed, her chest ached and her heart felt as though it had be torn almost completely in two. “Because I-I’m freaking the fuck out right now. I-I....” Kate’s breath caught in her throat; it was too much. It was all too much.

    “Katherine Bishop,” Melina whispered. A strong hand delicately captured Kate’s cheek and turned her face to meet the ex-widow's eyes. It was an action, a gentle but strong touch that reminded Kate so much of Yelena. “The person who did this to you is not your girlfriend and she is not my daughter.”

    “Then who is she?” Kate demanded, her voice drowning in emotion. If Yelena wasn’t her girlfriend right now, then who was she? Who was controlling her? Who was responsible for everything that was happening? Was it Fisk? He had the means, and surely the motive, but it felt so cruel and personal. Kate couldn’t shake the feeling that there was something else, something that was beyond their field of vision.

    Carol’s jaw clenched. The tight muscles there ticked with indecision and Kate could see her brain chewing over something through hazel eyes. The blonde took a breath and found some resolve. Their eyes met and Kate knew that everything was about to change. “What I’m about to say cannot leave this room. Do you understand?” Yep. Everything was about to change.

    Kate swallowed. She needed to know, no matter what. “Yes, tell me, please?” Kate realised she sounded as if she were begging, she supposed she probably was, but it wasn’t the time to feel shame for wanting answers.

    “It’s not chemical,” Carol reiterated with a sigh, “Because it’s biological, it’s personalised .” “Personalised?” Kate asked, what did Carol mean, personalised ? “You mean it was made for Yelena?”

    Carol had the look of someone who had said too much, but she was determined to speak the truth. Kate had a sinking feeling that this was just the tip of the iceberg. “Yes,” the blonde said quietly. Melina’s hand tightened around hers.

    “Who would do that?”

    Melina’s face was stony with disdain as she chewed over the possibilities. “Someone who wanted to control her. Someone who wanted her back. Someone who wanted revenge.” It seemed as if her implication was clear. Who would have targeted Yelena’s grandmother? Who would have wanted payback against a perceived betrayal? Who wanted her for himself?

    “Surely someone like Benny Laçic doesn’t have that kind of technology,” Kate reasoned. “No, he doesn’t,” Carol confirmed. She seemed certain. “The serum is made with Skrull DNA.”

    Skrull? That was alien right? Aliens that could replicate other people’s appearance. Did that go as far as being able to change some kind of molecular structure dependent on who a substance was targeting?

    “Alien DNA?” Kate asked in disbelief. Alien. Alien . Why did this all feel so familiar? “It sounds crazy but yes,” Carol nodded.

    There was an alien asset last year...an alien asset that a Russian ‘terrorist cell’ had acquired. An alien asset that she and Yelena secured at great personal cost. It couldn’t be the same, could it? Yelena hadn’t been tasked to secure a mind control serum. That would have been unethical, surely.

    “That asset that we retrieved from Siberia,” Kate began coolly, but she was not feeling anywhere near cool. In fact, she was starting to feel rage simmer beneath the surface. “The alien asset we almost died for, the asset Yelena almost died for, was a mind control serum?” The brunette asked incredulously. The idea was almost laughable. Sending an ex-Black Widow to acquire some kind of chemical subjugation technology, it just felt so, so wrong. Carol shook her head resolutely. “I didn’t know what it was at the time.” “Bullshit!” Kate hissed. She was shouting at Carol Danvers, she was swearing at Carol Danvers, and she did not give a shit.

    “Kate,” Carol tried to appease her,” I understand that you’re angry-,” “You could not possibly understand,” Melina cut in dangerously, but Carol wasn’t there to debate the moral ambiguity of their mission, she was there to solve the problem in front of her.

    “All I knew was the technology could be incredibly dangerous in the wrong hands and we were tasked with retrieving it.”

    “And whose hands are the right hands?” Melina bit. “Americans? So much for the Land of the Free, huh?”

    “Don’t pretend you’ve never broken a few eggs to make an omelette Ms Vostokov,” Carol smiled nonchalantly and Melina’s eyes grew darker. The ex-widow was unhappy to say the least but chose to bite her tongue. After-all, it wasn’t as if Carol was wrong. Melina had actively been involved in subjugating Widows in her past, and despite Yelena being her daughter, Carol clearly didn’t think Melina had the right to judge her. “Who is this ‘ they’ ?” Kate asked, wanting to get to answers. Perhaps answers could lead to solutions and solutions could lead to Kate being able to piece at least some of the shattered fragments of her heart back together. “It was never a terrorist cell, I think we all know that.” Terrorist cells didn't have an aircraft hangar containing a dozen QuinJets. “No, it wasn’t.” Carol sighed with a grimace. She’d grown uncomfortable, frustrated even. It was clear Carol wasn’t being fed all of the information, that there was a level of clearance above her that she wasn’t privy too. “I suspect it was Leviathan.”

    “ Pizdets ,” Melina hissed with venom. She released Kate’s hand to stand from her chair. The sound it made as it scraped across the floor was almost visceral. Yelena’s adoptive mother then stalked towards the shadowy corners of the room to brood gloomily. Well, that couldn’t be good.

    Why would Melina have such an extreme reaction to the name? Leviathan….It was so familiar. Leviathan, Leviathan… of course. Yelena had spoken of them. Closely associated with the Russian government with super shady goings on but totally defunct, or so they thought.

    “Leviathan as in ‘the group who controlled the Red Room’ Leviathan? The group Dreykov worked for?” Kate asked.

    “Yes.” Carol nodded regretfully. That couldn’t be right, that would be ridiculous, because that would mean..

    “Are you saying that the Red Room have her? That they took her back?” This was fucking crazy, they can’t just take women back. They can’t just take women in the first place. They were supposed to be safe. Yelena was supposed to be safe.

    “The Red Room is defunct but Yelena is still a valuable asset,” Carol explained. Kate felt sick at the word. Asset . Is that what they were? Someone’s property? Property of S.H.I.E.L.D. or Leviathan or the Red Room or Hydra?

    “They have taken back what they think is theirs,” Said Melina from the shadows. Kate’s temper flashed white hot. “Yelena is not property to take,” she’s my girlfriend , Kate thought despairingly. My beautiful, generous soul of a girlfriend . A soul trapped . “Yelena is a woman not a weapon,” Kate doubled down through gritted teeth. She was ready to kill someone, or at least maim them really badly.

    “I know,” Carol said gently. “But that’s not how these people work.”

    “You speak as if your own government is different from mine,” Melina seethed from across the room.

    “I am under no illusions, Melina.” Carol laughed the smallest of laughs. It was regretful, rueful and tired. She seemed so tired. Tired of bureaucracy, tired of secrets, tired of her people getting hurt because of them. And there was something else, she seemed ashamed . And that’s when Kate knew. She remembered the details of the mission. They were retrieving something. Something that had been stolen from S.H.I.E.L.D. It had crash landed near Russian territory and been taken from the crash site. If it was possible, Kate felt sicker. “We made it, didn’t we?” Kate asked in dismay, her voice shaking. “It was S.H.I.E.L.D. who made the mind control serum. Leviathan stole it from us. We just stole it back.” There was a moment of silence. Melina’s wrathful eyes were now fixed firmly upon Carol. The tension chewed into Kate. The blonde simply nodded. “As I understand it, yes.” “Was the serum field ready?” Melina asked, much more coolly than Kate would have expected. The ex-widow probably wanted to destroy the entire facility they sat in, but she also wanted her daughter back and to do that she needed as much information as she could glean.

    “That’s above my privileges.”

    “Bullshit,” Kate hissed and their eyes met. She’d just sworn at Carol, Carol Danvers, and not even in a nice way, but Kate was beyond caring. Kate was mad. Had Carol known about this from the start? Had she known about the Serum? Had she put Yelena in danger? “You think I’d tell you this much but not the rest?” The blonde reasoned calmly as she raised a solitary eyebrow. It was a challenge. A challenge to Kate to think otherwise, and it worked. Carol was trying to tell them everything she knew, Kate just needed to listen, but patience was a virtue that she was quickly running out of. “I know we were working on a way to trigger it with frequency,” Carol continued. “Something to do with the agent’s atomic structure.”

    “Resonance. That is smart,” Melina mused darkly.

    “So if it can be triggered, surely it can be un-triggered, right?” Kate asked. Was it naïve to think that? Surely a switch can be switched off.

    “It depends,” Melina spoke quietly as she slowly returned from the shadows. “Most chemical reactions are irreversible.”

    Irreversible? What did she mean, ‘irreversible’? They’d reversed the Widows’ subjugation, surely that was possible here as well. There was no way that Kate was settling for irreversible. Yelena was not irreversibly lost to her. That simply wasn’t acceptable. She wouldn’t stand for it.

    “So, what you’re telling me is, the woman I love was exposed to some kind of ‘Skrull- powered’ biological agent made by S.H.I.E.L.D. of all people, that has irreversibly changed her into a- back into a murderer?” Kate couldn’t believe it. It just sounded so ridiculous. How could S.H.I.E.L.D. make such a monumental fuck up? How could they even think that meddling with mind control was not only ethical but safe? Rather upsettingly, Kate had a sneaking suspicion that those at the highest echelons of S.H.I.E.L.D. didn’t give a shit about either of those things.

    “It might not be reversible but we could use an antidote instead,” Melina said as she sat back down next to Kate. Her eyes weren’t as dark, they were alive even, because suddenly she wasn’t faced with a problem, she was faced with an opportunity to solve one. “An antidote that can break down nitrogen bases in the agent’s DNA.”

    “But it’s alien DNA,” Kate said. She didn’t know much about the Skrull but she knew their biology was like nothing they had on Earth.

    “Yes,” Melina nodded with a sigh, “We are not talking GATTACA I am afraid. We are not even be talking nitrogen.”

    Melina’s eyes were still alight with possibility but Kate’s heart began to sink. Even if they could synthesise an antidote, how long would something like that take? Surely too long to stop Yelena from being lost to them entirely. There must be another solution. Capture perhaps? Trap and detain until they had a fix? It wasn’t the most ideal approach but if it saved Yelena and mitigated disaster, it was one hundred percent worth it.

    Carol’s demeanour changed suddenly. She looked sheepish and shifty? Uncomfortable in her own skin. She eyed both Kate and Yelena and exhaled heavily. She was about to do something that she really shouldn’t do but knew she wanted to.

    “There is a S.H.I.E.L.D. science facility in Alaska. Off the books. It’s where they were working on the synthesis of the serum.”

    Kate’s heart skipped a beat. Carol Danvers, you absolute rebel.

    “You think if they were manufacturing it there, they might also be working on a way to reverse it?” Kate asked. The hope was back. Oh dear.

    “It would make logical sense,” Carol nodded matter-of-factly. And it did. Of course. You wouldn’t make a mind-control serum that wasn’t reversible. It would be like making a love spell without and antidote. A little spill and all hell could break loose. “Great,” Kate chimed, sounding more like herself than she had for some time.“Let’s get ‘em on the phone.”

    Carol pursed her lips and glanced apprehensively in Melina’s direction. The practically invulnerable superhero was afraid of the Russian. “It’s not that simple,” Carol explained a little too quickly and Melina fixed her with a withering look. A look that the blonde tried her best to shrug off.

    “Of course it’s that simple,” Kate said plainly. Clearly it was that simple. If they had an antidote they could hand it over. They caused the problem and they were going to fix it. “You ask, they give, we cure Yelena.”

    “This is above my privilege.”

    “I don’t care about that,” Kate snapped, and she really didn’t. They risked their lives for S.H.I.E.L.D. Working for S.H.I.E.L.D. made them targets, defecting to S.H.I.E.L.D. made Yelena an enemy, and because of that, everything had fallen apart. “My mother is dying in a hospital bed and my girlfriend who has been brainwashed by some mysterious splinter division of the Russian government put her there. You really think I give a fuck about your privilege.” Woah . Kate swallowed. Yes, she just said that. And okay, sure, she swore at Carol earlier, maybe gave her a little sass but this, this was downright insubordination. She was fucked, surely she was fucked. She’d gone too far. Carol didn’t deserve it. Carol was Carol. She was by the book, military, and stifled by hierarchy. Kate loved Carol, idolised her, and suddenly felt the overwhelming need to grovel. “I’m sorry. I’m just-.” “You have nothing to be sorry for,” Carol cut in. Her hand tightened against Kate’s shoulder once more, and yet was face was awash with regret. “But I can’t help you,” she said quietly with contrition.

    Kate knew she never should have hoped. Never should have thought a solution could be so simple. Carol was supposed to be her hero. Her superhero. But Yelena had been right. Carol was so often absent when she was needed most. So tied up with duty and obligation, so tied up with the greater good that she was blind to helping fix the bad that was right in front of her.

    “How do you do it?” Kate asked quietly, her eyes boring into Carol’s. “How do you just stand by and watch these things happen? You have so much power.”

    Carol couldn’t hold Kate’s gaze but to the brunette’s surprise, it wasn’t guilt that she found in the blonde’s eyes, it was a great and profound sadness. Carol gave Kate’s shoulder one final squeeze before she rose from her seat.

    “I pick my battles, Kate,” she said softly as a small smile began to pull at the corner of her lips. “You should learn to pick yours.”

    With that, Carol turned to make her way to the door. Kate’s brow wrinkled in confusion. There was something she was missing, something significant. Her suspicions were confirmed as the senior Avenger paused and turned to look back. Her eyes were twinkling now. Twinkling roguishly and Kate’s stomach flip flopped. If things were different and she wasn’t in hospital, her mother wasn’t on her deathbed and her girlfriend wasn’t brainwashed, Kate might have thought it was her heart that fluttered, not her stomach. But just a little. “When I was a kid,” Carol spoke with a wistful smile, “My father would take me camping just north of Fairbanks. In the winter the roads were impassable, but by April we were able to take the 2 and then the 6 east until we reached the Chatanika river.”

    Fairbanks was in Alaska. She was telling them where to look in Alaska. Carol Danvers was breaking the rules.

    “We’d fish and we’d camp and make s’mores. He loved my brothers you know?” Carol’s smile flashed with sadness, just for a moment and then continued. “But once a year, it was just me and him. I really cherished those times with him. Often he talked about how wonderful it would be to have our own little lodge, just over the ridge to the North West.” Carol ‘hmmed’ with nostalgia and Kate wondered if Carol and her father really had dreamed of a place together, out of the city. And suddenly Kate found herself wondering how many other people Carol had left behind when she’d disappeared. How many loved ones, how many relationships she’d sacrificed those that greater good.

    “I’ve never seen a more beautiful sunset,” Carol smiled fondly at the false memory that clearly wasn’t entirely false to begin with, and Kate felt a strange comfort in it. They were going to find that base, they were going acquire that antidote and they were going to cure Yelena.

    “Never did catch any fish though,” Carol mused and she smiled warmly at Kate. “Maybe you’ll have better luck.”

    Kate wanted to scream and shout and punch the air and shake Carol Danvers for all she was worth but instead she simply smiled gratefully at the woman she was proud to call her hero. “I’ll see if I can locate Yelena,” Carol said, back to business. “You concentrate on getting better,” the blonde winked.

    “I will. Thank you,” Kate said earnestly.

    “Good,” Carol nodded as she looked from Kate to Melina. “I’ll let you know as soon as we find her,” the blonde assured the ex-Widow and Melina offered her the smallest of smiles in gratitude. From Melina, that meant a lot.

    Carol turned to leave but paused momentarily. She looked back at Kate, pale and propped up in her hospital bed. The brunette could see her conflict, she wanted to take action but Carol wasn’t subtle, she was smart, because Kate and Melina could be. Kate and Melina could sneak in, unnoticed. They could retrieve the antidote without compromising the Avengers programme, Carol couldn’t promise the same. Energy beams for hands, remember? “Good luck,” Carol said, hope unbound in her expression. Carol had hope. And if Carol had hope, and if Kate had Melina by her side then surely, even with her injuries, and even with the odds stacked against them, it wasn’t too dangerous for her to hope too, was it? Kate allowed herself to laugh ruefully. They say that it’s the hope kills you, but whatever idiot came up with that had clearly never faced up against a Black Widow.

    The corridor was dark. Silent. She felt the crunch of shattered glass beneath her feet but heard no sound. She felt the girl’s wet blonde hair between her fingers and clenched within her right fist, but she couldn’t hear her whimpers. She couldn’t hear her pleading or her begging.

    Yelena looked up and saw it. It was right where she’d left it. The door. Her door. Yes, Yelena knew, she knew she had to reach it. Just like before, just like every time before. Light flashed brightly and a whole universe of stars burned her retinas, but the lightning was missing its thunder, and so the assassin persevered towards her goal.

    The woman in her grasp struggled against her relentless tide. She pulled and lashed around, she threw herself backwards and to the floor. Her mouth moved in protestation but her words fell upon deaf ears. Yelena simply continued to drag her forward. There was no going back. Her hand touched brass. It was smooth and cool. It was familiar and Yelena took comfort in it. She was close now. She couldn’t hear her mother, she couldn’t hear tune that she hummed, but she could feel the vibrations of it, the murmurings. Familiar, yes, that was the word. It felt so familiar. An old memory reignited after so many years. Lost but now found. Heard but no sound.

    Yelena’s hand tightened around the handle and turned. The door fell open and Yelena felt relief, warmth, belonging. Yelena was home. She would be pleased.

    She barrelled the girl into the kitchen and threw her down onto the wet linoleum. It was violent and it was necessary. She stayed there, her chest heaving as she tried to draw agonising breath after agonising breath. She was slumped, beaten and beyond hope. Yes, it was more than necessary if things were to stay this way.

    The assassin picked up the kitchen chair that lay upon its side and righted it as a gentle hand claimed her shoulder and two warm lips pressed themselves tenderly against her cheek. “Well done, Elena,” came her words. They were soft and light and melodic. Like a warm breeze through a field of golden lilies, like a nightingale’s call signalling the end of a long and unforgiving winter and the beginning of a new and glorious spring. And she could hear them. She could hear its song, she knew that it was beautiful, and she knew that it had called her home.

    Шум Chapter Notes Hello! Apologies for the delay on this one. My gf is back from her time in the States and she's been a bit of a distraction, in a good way. I've also been oddly sociable recently, who knew I had it in me?

    This is probably not the update you were hoping for, but it's an important one, and was an interesting write for sure. I hope you enjoy it!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes The woman struggled in vain against Yelena’s firm grip. Although she was much taller than the Russian, Eleanor Bishop was no match for her strength. The blonde dug her fingers in tightly as she dragged her girlfriend’s mother from the back seat of her car and out into the deserted parking lot.

    Yelena’s captive cried out as she was shoved roughly into the elevator. She fought against the cable ties that tightly bound her hands behind her back and tried desperately to somehow rid herself of the bag that was obscuring her view.

    “What is this? What is happening?” Came Eleanor’s muffled protestations. “Who are you goddammit?” Yelena smiled wryly as she inserted her key and prodded the button that would take them all the way to the penthouse suite. The elevator lurched into life and Eleanor staggered backwards. The blonde grabbed the older woman by her sleeve to stop her from falling and cracking her head upon the varnished Art Deco interiors. Mother would not be happy if Eleanor Bishop brained herself on the journey up, that was not part of the plan. The blonde grabbed Eleanor by the cable ties and dug her pistol uncomfortably into the small of her back. The woman immediately stiffened and her breath hitched at the feel of cool steel. She knew there was a gun barrel aimed directly at the base of her spine for this wasn’t the first time Eleanor Bishop had been held at gunpoint, and it probably wouldn’t be the last. Yelena smiled with grim satisfaction as the Bishop matriarch became instantly more agreeable. Hopefully this was a sign of things to come. She would certainly have to be agreeable going forwards if she wanted to live, and borderline charming if she wanted to spare her daughter’s life. But charming was never an area in which Eleanor struggled, that’s how she’d found so much success. Eleanor was a charming yet ruthless woman, she would be absolutely perfect.

    The elevator came to a staggering halt and dinged brightly. The doors rolled open to reveal a wide marble lobby, much like the Bishops’. The marble shone elegantly in the ambient lighting of the penthouse. It was deep and green and for some reason it filled Yelena with strength and purpose as her boots clipped satisfyingly across it. It was odd. She’d never set foot here before, but as she urged Eleanor Bishop out of the elevator and deeper into the penthouse she was hit with an overwhelming sense of familiarity. She’d known the address, she’d been holding the elevator keys tightly concealed within her pocket since she’d first acquired them at the hospital from Anna, and she knew now where her mother would be. Her heart tightened at the prospect of seeing her again. Seeing her eyes, her smile. Feeling her touch, her gratitude. Receiving her approval. The assassin had completed another of her tasks immaculately and her mother would be pleased.

    Yelena relinquished her grip upon her captive and shifted the gun to her left hand so that she could open the study door with her right. The door handle was brassy and cool upon her fingertips. She tightened her hand around it and took a steadying breath. This was real. It was all real. She could feel the brass, the marble, the metal in her left hand. She could hear Eleanor’s panicked breaths, however hard the woman tried to conceal them. She could even feel her damaged body damaged. Her ribs, her hands, her ankle, but it was no bother to her. She wasn’t trained to feel, she was trained to do, to be a weapon. But then why did the brass feel so cold against her skin?

    Unlike the Bishops, Yelena’s recent ancestors hadn’t built their New York penthouse from the ground up, but they had owned it, eventually. They had taken it from those with power and money, from people like the Bishops, not by force but with coercion and subterfuge. It’s what they were good at, then and now.

    That was all too clear as Yelena gripped the handle tighter and turned it. The door swung open as it always did to reveal a grand mahogany writing desk. Shelves of books lined the walls and an original Repin hung proudly behind the desk. The walls were a deep green to match the marble and one ornate mahogany chair had been quite purposefully placed to face the desk, and the person who sat behind it. A person who shared her eyes, her nose and the delicate shape of her face. That person was her mother.

    Yelena guided Eleanor to the mahogany chair and sat her down abruptly. The brunette huffed a little as ass met seat and Yelena yanked the bag from her head unceremoniously. Eleanor’s already unkempt hair hung lank and in her eyes. She blinked as her vision adjusted to the dimly lit study and tried but failed to flick her unruly bangs away from her face. With her hands still tied, it was a lost cause.

    Yelena frowned for a moment and dug into her back pocket to retrieve her favourite flick knife. It was her favourite for many a reason. It was well balanced, sharp, felt good in the hand, and she’d killed at least a dozen people with it. With the deftest flick of the wrist she released its blade, and with the most precise of cuts she released Eleanor Bishop’s hands. Their eyes met and Yelena could tell that the brunette had gone from scared to absolutely terrified in that moment.

    Eleanor tried desperately to swallow her fear. To regain some semblance of togetherness. Kate’s mother was astute, smart, and whatever Kate thought about her, she was brave too; she’d needed to be. The brunette needed to call upon that courage now. “Yelena,” Eleanor hissed, her voice remarkably steady as she scraped her hands through her hair. “What is happening?” She asked as her eyes dared to take in the woman behind the rather intimidating desk.

    ”Eleanor,” Yelena said smoothly, “You look well.” The assassin was being flippant, because in reality Eleanor Bishop looked like shit, but in fairness to the woman, she was looking a lot better than she had twenty four hours previous.

    “I-I don’t feel it,” Eleanor grimaced. She shook her head as her hands went to soothe her aching temples.

    The woman was alive, what more did she want? “That is the toxin I gave you. It tends to have that effect on people.”

    Eleanor’s breathing hitched once more. This time in disbelief. “ You poisoned me?” Of course she had. Who else would it have been? What kind of idiotic Government agency lets known assassins walk freely into a high security prison facility? Of course she was going to poison someone, that someone just happened to be Eleanor Bishop. “Only temporarily,” Yelena shrugged with indifference.

    “We wanted to have a little chat,” came her mother’s deep, thickly accent voice from behind the desk. She spoke softly without a hint of menace, which if possible, made her even more terrifying. She was formidable and Yelena couldn’t help the smile that pulled at the corner of her mouth as Eleanor’s eyes settled upon the most powerful woman in the room. “A little chat?” The Bishop matriarch whispered in disbelief. “Is that what this is?” “Yes,” the slightly older woman nodded matter-of-factly, her face unyielding. “I believe we have shared interest, you and I.”

    Despite Eleanor clearly being in a rather powerless and potentially dangerous position, she didn’t seem to back down. Yelena respected that, but her mother...her mother relished it. She enjoyed the challenge, the exchange, the battle of words, but most of all, she enjoyed winning, and with Eleanor Bishop exactly where she wanted her, Yelena was certain her mother was going to be one happy woman that evening.

    “And who exactly are you?” Eleanor bit back, “And what gives you the right to-?” “I am a friend,” the older woman said magnanimously. She paused for a moment as her lips pulled into a cool smile. “For now.” It was a warning. A reminder of who was in the driver’s seat, and who wasn’t.

    Eleanor controlled her face well. She didn’t balk in fear or flare with anger, she simply took a moment to appraise her situation. She’d been poisoned, kidnapped and held at gunpoint, but clearly had something to offer, if she hadn’t she wouldn’t be there. So, Eleanor Bishop decided to play ball.

    She sat taller with her shoulders back. A friend could be negotiated with, a friend could be beneficial, a friend could partake in mutual conversation, and that is what Eleanor intended to initiate.

    “Well,” Eleanor started with a touch more decorum, “I’m not sure how you tend to conduct business but from my rather illustrious experience, meetings tend to start with introductions.”

    The mothers’ eyes met and something passed between them. Yelena’s mother had been told plenty about Eleanor, but she had insisted on seeing her in person. She wanted to get the measure of her, to look her in the eye and to know that she was the one. The one who could be trusted, with the right coercion. It seemed as if Eleanor Bishop was passing that test. “Okay,” the older woman said slowly, with an amicable smile. “I am Nadija.” Eleanor looked fairly happy with her progress so decided to persist. “Nadija. A pleasure,” the brunette nodded curtly. “And you clearly know who I am as you wouldn’t have dragged me here otherwise.”

    The older woman smiled knowingly but offered Eleanor no more than that. Of course Nadija knew all the mundane details. The brunette was a widower, mother to one Kate Bishop, CEO of Bishop Security. But then there were quite a few more unsavoury details also. Details that not even the Courts knew. Details that Nadija was very interested in.

    “Who do you work for, Nadija?” Eleanor asked as her eyes narrowed. She was getting bold, something that Yelena didn’t mind. She liked directness. No euphemism or cowardice, she respected that, but Eleanor Bishop was not asking the right questions. Who Nadija worked for was irrelevant. What she wanted and what she was willing to do was far more pertinent. “That is not the question you should be asking, Eleanor,” Yelena interjected smugly. Eleanor’s eyes darted to Yelena’s . They searched for answers, and they found them in the blonde’s satisfied smile. The brunette’s eyes widened with realisation. “Yelena, where is Kate?” Eleanor asked. Bingo . The brunette’s voice betrayed her for the first time and it caused Yelena’s smile to widen further. She couldn’t help it. “Yelen-.” “Kate is fine,” Yelena shrugged with absolute nonchalance, and with her indifference, Eleanor was incensed. Her hands clutched at the arms of the ornate mahogany chair, her nostrils flared and her eyes set alight. It was like a switch had been flicked. Kate’s mother lost all her decorum, all her poise and control, and the assassin loved every moment of it. To watch the disbelief give way to fear, then anger and then unbridled desperation within the space of a few moments, it was art.

    “What have you done with her!?” Eleanor growled. She looked ready to throw herself towards the assassin at any moment. Yelena would not recommend that. Neither would Kate from recent experience.

    “We would not hurt your daughter,” Nadija’s calming voice cut through the calamity and if possible, Eleanor’s vice-like grip tightened around the arms of the chair. She was clinging on in a desperate attempt to hold herself back from a grinning Yelena who’s smiled had just grown even wider. Of course, they would not hurt Kate Bishop. What were a few puncture wounds amongst friends or better yet lovers?

    The smallest of rational voices at the back of Eleanor’s head must have been telling her to stop. It must have been telling her that going for Yelena was a sure-fire way to end up dead, dead dead and not ‘fake dead in a hospital bed’ dead, despite her rising panic for Kate’s safety.

    “Eleanor,” Yelena’s mother quietly demanded Mrs Bishop’s attention. She got it. “We would not hurt your daughter, not if we didn’t have to.” It was a threat, a clear one, and it was more than enough to force Eleanor into line. Her mother’s voice seemed to have that effect. The brunette’s hands relinquished their grip from the arms of the mahogany chair and she sighed dejectedly as she tore her eyes from Yelena.

    How naïve the Bishops had been, to let someone like Yelena into their lives. The blonde almost pitied them, almost, as she thought back to Kate Bishop, alone in that apartment. Pinned and helpless. By now she would probably be with her friends, in relative safety, but she would be heartbroken and angry, ready to do whatever it took to get her girlfriend back, and that’s what Yelena was counting on.

    “I think we could be fast friends,” Nadija continued, “We have a lot in common, you and I. We are both successful women in business, we protect our families and we do what is necessary because we can see the bigger picture.”

    “Like poison...Is poison necessary? You could have killed me.”

    Yelena scoffed at the suggestion. What bullshit was this? “Don’t make me laugh. If I wanted to kill yo-,”

    Eleanor rolled her eyes, and casually waved away Yelena’s comment. “I get it. You would have done it already.”

    “I would not have needed poison.”

    “Right, right, you only need ten seconds, I get it,” Eleanor said dismissively. Yelena grinned. “I can take my time if you’d prefer. How does ten hours sound? I could do your daughter too if-,”

    “You have a beautiful name, Eleanor,” Nadija interjected and it was Yelena’s turn to roll her eyes. It was just harmless fun, but the blonde was quickly learning that her mother liked to be the one to do the talking, the one to make the threats and do the speeches.
