As long as Yelena still got to have a little fun she wouldn’t begrudge her mother that. “A beautiful name,” Nadija continued, “Much like Elena here.”

    Nadija nodded in Yelena’s direction and smiled proudly. Yelena couldn’t help but smile back. She would do anything to see that smile, anything to keep it upon her mother’s face, anything to be looked at with glisteningly proud eyes and spoken to with warm, appreciative words. She would do anything .

    “She is named after Heléne of Troy,” Nadija continued as she stood slowly from behind her desk. Her chair dragged heavily across the floor and Eleanor flinched at the dull yet disconcerting noise it made. Yelena hoped it filled her with a sense of foreboding. It was surely meant to. “Do you know the story of Troy, Eleanor?”

    Eleanor Bishop couldn’t help but glance in Yelena’s direction, the blonde presumed out of some sort of hopeless, morbid curiosity, because of course the brunette did know the story of Troy, she knew it all too well.

    Nadija moved from around her desk and came to stand next to her daughter. The older woman was diminutive in size but broad in stature and powerful in nature, much like Yelena herself. Dressed in a simple yet elegant black A-line dress, Nadija looked as much a CEO as Eleanor Bishop often did. A smart pair of red heels set her a few inches taller than Yelena, and a delicate gold necklace with a nightingale charm hung elegantly around her neck. An identical charm lay hidden beneath Yelena’s black hoodie.

    A gentle hand turned Yelena’s face to hers, and Nadija smiled proudly at her once more. Her mother’s thumb played affectionately across her chin as she appraised her daughter’s features. She was enraptured. Enraptured by their familiarity. The face that wasn’t quite her face. The face she’d only seen when she’d closed her eyes and imagined. The curve of her daughter’s lips when she smiled. Did her cheeks dimple when she did? The arch of her eyebrows, were they full and expressive like her own? Did the tip of her nose turn up like her mother’s or was it strong and broad like her father’s? But of course, now Nadija no longer needed to close her eyes to see, for she was stood in her daughter’s presence. Close enough to touch and hold and kiss gently on hot cheeks.

    “Heléne was the most beautiful woman in the world,” Nadija explained for Eleanor’s benefit, despite not taking her eyes from Yelena. “She was seduced, deceived, and stolen from her people. It is funny how art reflects life, no?” She said with an ironic smile as she turned to face Eleanor once more, and her hand fell from Yelena’s cheek. The assassin found herself frowning at its absence.

    Eleanor frowned too, but with visible confusion. “Yelena wasn’t deceived or stolen, Yelena fell in love,” the brunette said matter-of-factly. As if it were so simple, so obvious. Just like that. Yelena had fallen in love. The idea was laughable. Yelena had been turned against her family. She manipulated by a traitor Black Widow and two washed up Leviathan associates who had the audacity to call themselves her family, and then finally was brainwashed by the US Government into making an emotional connection with an Avenger. They hired her. They put them together. They put them in jeopardy together. They wanted to tether Yelena to them through Kate Bishop and it had worked. She had been weak, she had forgotten her training. She’d sought comfort and contact, she’d sought a cause. She had been selfish. Thankfully her mother had returned to her to break that tether, to be her comfort, her reason, her cause, and now it was just them. Just as it should have been all along, just as her mother had always planned before Yelena was taken from her.

    Nadija leaned casually against her desk and smiled with satisfaction. “And now she is the most a beautiful Trojan horse. They even invited her in.”

    And that’s when it clicked for Eleanor. Not the realisation that perhaps Yelena had been a ticking time bomb in her daughter’s life all along, but the realisation of who Nadija was. “You’re her mother,” Eleanor gasped, “Her biological mother.”

    “I am her real mother,” Nadija bit back with a little more venom than she herself had expected. The word ‘biological’ implied that there was an alternative. There was no alternative. Melina Vostokoff was not Yelena’s mother, she was a traitor. Eleanor’s face softened at the revelation. She thought she sensed a weakness in Yelena but she would not find one. “Then, as a mother, I will ask you again,” Eleanor spoke evenly, powerfully. “Where is Kate and what have you done with her?”

    “Your daughter is fine, Eleanor,” Yelena sighed, this was getting old. Sure, she was probably being a little liberal with the truth, but the newly reinstated assassin had been careful not maim Kate Bishop too greatly. That simply would not do. A little choking, a mild concussion, a few warning shots and a broken heart were just enough to set things in motion. Maybe once this was all said and done, her mother would let her have a little more fun, but Yelena doubted it. There was something about Kate Bishop that made Yelena want to scream. She was so… happy. And even when her mother was seemingly dying in a hospital bed she was so… gentle. She was kind to the staff despite the continuous stream of bad news and lack of progress. She’d sought Yelena’s affection and taken comfort in her touch. And she’d comforted Yelena herself when she’d woken from a bad dream despite Kate being the one in a waking nightmare. Yelena had hated it. She hated Kate Bishop. How could she have been so foolish as to fall in love?

    “By now she will be with her friends, no doubt working on a way to save me,” Yelena grimaced. “She is irritatingly noble like that.”

    Nadija smiled knowingly and Eleanor looked between mother and daughter. “How can I be sure?” She asked. Eleanor wanted a guarantee, which was absolutely perfect. “Because we want your cooperation, Eleanor,” Nadija explained coolly. “Having your daughter killed would not exactly endear me to you, would it?” It would have been fun though. And safer. Yelena didn’t like the idea of keeping the Bishop girl around. Love was unpredictable, it made people do things. Crazy things.

    “Okay, and let’s say Kate is safe, and alive, what is it that you think I can do for you?” Eleanor’s eyes narrowed. “You think I’d be willing to cooperate after you’ve poisoned me? After you’ve dragged me here.”

    “Yes,” Nadija nodded coolly. “I do. For you see, we can offer you something no one else can.”

    “And what is that?” The brunette raised a sceptical eyebrow.

    “Guaranteed safety and absolute power,” Nadija shrugged as if it were nothing, but it was absolutely everything. Especially to a woman who was facing jail time or legitimate threats to her safety if she did the one thing that could spare her time in a prison cell. Eleanor couldn’t help but smile at the absurdity of it all. “No one can offer me that.” Nadija simply pouted in response. Yelena’s mother was mulling something over, calculating her next move. Eleanor needed convincing and Yelena hoped her mother would ask her daughter to do the job. To her absolute delight , her mother turned to her and gave her the smallest of nods. Yelena had permission. Permission to do something she’d been waiting far too long to do. A small smile pulled at the corner of her lips at the prospect and she nodded silently. She’d received her mother’s message loud and clear.

    The assassin turned on her heel briskly and made for the large wooden door on the opposite side of the room. Despite her excitement, she was measured. Her mother would be disappointed if she didn’t show control. It was all about control. Like she controlled Kate Bishop as she poisoned her mother, as she broke Kingpin out of jail, as she pinned her to the apartment wall. Revenge for all those months that Kate had held her under her sway. Yelena wasn’t a girlfriend or a lover or an Avenger. She was a killer, and she would prove it again now.

    Yelena turned the door handle slowly and marched into the darkened room. It was silent, apart from the low, rhythmic murmurings of his breathing. Wilson Fisk was still out cold. He was secured and double-secured to a large metal chair with his head lolled forward due to the heavy sedation he was under. His chin rested against his chest, head buoyed by the rising and falling of his broad chest.

    Yelena retrieved the handgun that was tucked into the back of her jeans and aimed it squarely at the crime lord’s head. His non-existent right eye had healed over since Maya Lopez shot him two Christmases previous, but his body and mind hadn’t been so lucky. The assassin prodded the barrel of her gun into Kingpin’s now empty eye socket and pushed, ever so slightly. It was almost imperceptible, but Yelena caught it. Wilson Fisk flinched. Good, this would make what was to come even more satisfying.

    Yelena skirted around Kingpin’s large body, grabbed the back of his chair and began to heave. “ Blyat ,” she grumbled as she struggled with his weight. She knew he was heavy-she and Anna had struggled to remove him from that high security hospital in Long Island, but what the fuck man? What did this guy bench?

    The sound of metal gouging the wooden floor of the apart filled the study, as Yelena hauled Wilson Fisk through the door and gladly placed him down in front of Eleanor Bishop. The brunette’s eyes were well and truly bulging. She was battling every instinct just to keep her shit together.

    “We can offer you that,” Nadija smiled smugly as Yelena flicked the safety off and pressed her handgun against Fisk’s thick head. The implication was clear. Yelena’s trigger finger was the solution to all of Eleanor’s problems. The blonde only needed to flinch and years of debt and servitude would disappear. She only needed to pull that trigger and Eleanor could testify freely.

    Eleanor’s eyes flicked between the barely conscious Fisk sat in front of her and the two blondes who stood over her. She could see the potential and she could see the danger. Jump out of bed with one crime boss and straight into the sheets with another, one that she didn’t know and couldn’t trust. Eleanor was always going to need a little push and that’s where Kate Bishop came in.

    “Who’s ‘we’?” Eleanor asked darkly.

    Nadija smiled and then pouted once more. She was going to tell her. It seemed only fair that Eleanor knew who she might be having pretty dicey, unprotected dealings with beneath those sheets, even if Yelena didn’t like the idea of showing one’s hand so soon. As a Widow they would die before revealing the names of their masters. Of course, her mother was the master here. She was the leader of the whole gorram organisation.

    “ I, ” Nadija impressed upon Eleanor, “ I am Leviathan.”

    To Yelena’s surprise, Eleanor didn’t gasp or baulk. In fact, she struggled to repress a cold laugh, as if she’d just been told the punchline to one of the cruellest, most hopeless jokes she’d ever heard. “Of course,” Eleanor smiled, cynically. “Of course , you’re Leviathan.” Yelena’s mother almost grinned. The dim light of the study danced and leapt like fire in her eyes. She liked Eleanor Bishop, she liked hearing the name of her organisation upon her American tongue, and she loved the contempt with which she held it. “With Fisk in play, Hydra has had a hold on this city for too long,” Nadija explained, and understanding rushed into Eleanor. An understanding that brought reason and clarity, and above all, possibility. “With you about to testify, we are presented with a unique opportunity.” “Hydra?” Eleanor asked innocently.

    “Yes,” Nadija nodded. “Hydra have an immeasurable influence over Fisk and his associates and have done for many years, but I think you know that,” the older woman smiled knowingly.

    By the look on the brunette’s face, Yelena’s mother was right, Eleanor did have knowledge of the Hydra connection. That would explain her new ‘whatever my money can buy’ approach to personal security, and her knowledge of Leviathan.

    “Pledge yourself to us and my daughter will make whatever remnants of Hydra which exist in this city disappear,” Nadija promised coolly.

    “Just like that?” Eleanor asked, matching Nadija's cool and calm demeanour. The CEO of Bishop Security was distrustful, naturally. Yelena had deceived her, poisoned her and dragged her here against her will. But there was no way this conversation was happening in a high security prison interrogation room, and there was no way Eleanor’s testimony would stand up in court if it had.

    “Yes,” Nadija nodded, matter-of-factly. “You testify, we help guide your business and take a cut of your profits, your Fisk problem goes away and there’s a new Kingpin in New York City.” It was a win, win. Eleanor didn’t die and everyone profited.

    But it seemed too simple, too good to be true. Yelena knew that, her mother knew that, and that’s why it was such a compelling offer. Of course, there were strings attached, there were always going to be with an organisation linked to the Russian Government. There were going to be strings attached with any shady Government organisation. Look at S.H.I.E.L.D. Corrupt, lying, manipulative. They painted themselves as liberators and protectors, when in fact, they were just as bad as everyone else. Only difference was, it was S.H.I.E.L.D. that controlled the narrative, but that wouldn’t matter as long as Leviathan could find a way to control everything else.

    “What happens if I refuse?” Eleanor asked with a speculative eyebrow raised. Yelena smiled. Eleanor Bishop wouldn’t refuse. The offer was too tempting. Money, power, freedom . And of course, saying no to Leviathan would have consequences too. Dire consequences. Yelena’s mother smiled serenely. “If you refuse, Elena puts Fisk back where she found him, we offer you no protection and you are dead as soon as you get into that witness box,” Nadija explained smoothly. “Oh, and there is one other thing of course.” The older woman’s voice grew darker and the smallest of satisfied smiles pulled at the corner of her lips. It was Yelena’s cue.

    The blonde removed her phone from a pocket deep inside her hoodie, flicked it open and held it out for Eleanor to take. The brunette’s brow furrowed in confusion. “What is it?” Eleanor asked as she took her Yelena’s phone in her hands. On the screen was a small red dot. It pulsed brightly and appeared to be moving slowly across a dark background.

    “That is your daughter.” Yelena explained. She didn’t need to say anything else. The message was clear.

    “She loves you,” Eleanor bit back with anger as she forced the phone back into Yelena’s hands. “How could you?” How could she indeed? Quite easily it turned out. More easily than she had ever thought possible. Two days ago, she was in love. Eleanor was right. She hadn’t said it, she was waiting for the perfect time, the perfect place. She’d been trying to find the perfect words. It was funny, how clearly she remembered everything. Kate’s lips, her laugh, the comforting nature of her voice. She remembered kissing her for the first time, crying in front of her for the first time, making love to her for the first time. She remembered all of it, and it had felt so right. They just fit. Connected. But now...now it felt so wrong. When she thought of the softness of Kate’s lips, the gentle nature of her touch, the warmth and fire of her laugh, like a single malt on a winter’s night, she hated it. She wanted to expunge it from existence and purge it from her mind.

    She was simply seeking comfort and connection, that was the only explanation. She was a Black Widow that had come untethered, directionless without her family, so she had lost her way. Latched on. But now she had her family back - her true family, and she had found purpose once more. She didn’t need to find purpose in Kate Bishop any longer. Yet still, she remembered. The hotel room in Sarajevo, she remembered that. She remembered the way Kate had held her, how her touch had given her the strength scream and breathe, and she remembered how weak she had been. An assassin brought to her knees at the thought of killing for love. Yes. Love had made her weak and yet her mother wouldn’t let her destroy the one thing that would end all of that. Yelena was disgusted with herself. She wanted to scream, she wanted to take the gun that was pressed against Fisk’s head and put it to Eleanor’s and she wanted to empty the chamber into her brain for creating such a soul- destroyingly beautiful woman.

    A steadying hand was placed upon her shoulder. Her mother’s fingers squeezed gently and Yelena released a breath she hadn’t realised she’d been holding.

    “Your daughter is in love with a ghost, Ms Bishop,” came her mother’s calming voice. It soothed her. Her heart slowed its heavy rhythm within her chest, her breath steadied and the oxygen that began to find its way back into her lungs brought with it resolve. “What have you done to her?” Eleanor asked Nadija. She was referring to Yelena now, not her own daughter. It was the question that would be on everyone lips. What had happened to Yelena Belova? The loveable rogue, the tortured ex-assassin, the loyal lapdog. “I have liberated her. Freed her so that she can live out her true purpose,” Nadija said proudly. She placed a gentle kiss upon Yelena’s cheek and the assassin leaned into her touch. It had been so long, she had waited so long, all for this. Every nightmare, every time she woke up gasping and thrashing and crying, every heart crushing moment when she realised she could never change the narrative, she could never change her story. But her story had changed, for the woman lost within the very fabric of that room, within the very fabric of her mind, was stood beside her now. She was worth more than a thousand Kate Bishops. “Kate will be heartbroken,” Eleanor said sadly. “Doubly if I take your offer.” “This redemption arc is not a good look on you Eleanor,” Nadija warned. “I -I can’t...”

    “Then I will kill your daughter,” Yelena growled as she lowered her weapon from Fisk and closed the distance between herself and Kate’s mother.

    “I don’t believe you,” Eleanor whispered with conviction. Yelena almost laughed. Eleanor Bishop didn’t even know her. She had no idea what she was really capable of. No idea about her first kill, about her second, about her ninth. The son of an oil baron in Eastern Venezuela. He was five. What made her think Yelena would even blink before killing Kate Bishop? “Right now,” Yelena spoke darkly, “There are bruises on your daughter’s neck from where I almost choked the life out of her. She begged me not to, you should have heard her.” Eleanor swallowed hard. She knew Yelena wasn’t lying, and now her heart was breaking for her daughter. Good . “I watched her heart break; I could see it in her eyes. They are very beautiful but I will take them from her if I have to.” They were violet and penetrating and saw things that they shouldn’t. “But she is alive for now, only because we need her. Do not think that I will hesitate if we ever learn that we do not.”

    Eleanor’s jaw clenched as her eyes searched Yelena’s. She would not find anything. There was no angle she could take, nothing she could say. Yelena would kill Kate if she had to, if she was allowed to. Hell, she was yearning to. To cleanse herself of the young woman that had infiltrated her non-existent heart.

    “Working with us could be incredibly lucrative for you Eleanor,” her mother reasoned. The ‘good cop, bad cop’ routine was a little on the nose, but as the Americans said, if it was not broken, do not fix it.

    “You think money motivates me?” Eleanor seethed as she tore her eyes from Yelena. “Yes,” Nadija nodded plainly. “But not as much as the love you hold for your daughter. That is why you did what you did isn’t? That is why you worked with Fisk? And once you were in, you couldn’t get out. We can get you out.”

    “And into what?” Eleanor asked with disdain. “You’re the same devil with a different name.” The brunette’s eyes bore into her Nadija’s but to Eleanor’s surprise, the older woman began to laugh. It was low and mirthful, and Yelena took comfort in its timbre. “Do you hear this Elena, my love? She calls me a čert , ” Nadija said with a smile, until that smile fell from her face. Her eyes darkened, and her face grew stony and dangerous. “Good,” she said, with not so much as a flicker of a smile. “That is exactly what I am. I only ask for your soul, Eleanor. In exchange, I will give you everything you have ever wanted.” Eleanor’s eyes narrowed. She was stuck. Genuinely stuck. Just as she’d been when her husband had died all those years ago and she found herself indebted to the most dangerous man in New York City. But now she had the opportunity to take that man’s place. “Picture it, Eleanor,” Nadija continued, the fire now back in her eyes. Yelena dare say they were twinkling. “You survive a poisoning carried out by an assassin sent by Wilson Fisk. You are vindicated. You are the victim. And you are so, so brave to get up on that witness stand as you testify against him. Especially as he is now at large. You will be more at risk than ever.” Nadija sowed a powerful narrative as she commanded the attention of her audience. “But really, Fisk is dead. His body in concrete within my penthouse. Or dissolved in acid, I haven’t quite decided yet. Those that you name are taken into custody, waiting for Fisk’s help; help that never comes.” Yelena’s mother tutted in mock tragedy. “You get your business back, your life back, your daughter back. Kate would never know. Kate would think you a hero.” It was a compelling story, Eleanor knew it, and with the brunette’s next question Yelena knew that her mother had won.

    Kate’s mother took a steadying, regretful breath. She was about to jump. “And she would never see you again?”

    Nadija smiled placidly. “No.”

    “That tracker,” Eleanor’s eyes found Yelena. “The tracker on her phone, I want it destroyed.”

    “If you agree,” Nadija said simply, “It would go. Kate will never see Elena again.” Yelena’s eyes flashed to her mother’s. That was not part of the plan. Of course, she wasn’t disturbed at the prospect of never seeing the Bishop girl again, despite very much wanting to choke the life out of her, she was more surprised by the lie. Yelena was very much planning to see Kate Bishop again, very soon in fact.

    “And I have your absolute guarantee, on all of this?” Eleanor insisted. “Yes,” Nadija nodded.

    “How can I be sure?” Eleanor asked hesitantly.

    Yelena’s mother simply shrugged. “I want New York City, Eleanor, and it would please me no end to have a woman in charge of my proceedings here. One that I admire.” “I can’t be bought with flattery, Nadija,” Eleanor said dismissively. Yelena’s mother beamed. It was the first time Eleanor had used her name.

    “Can you be bought with this?” Nadija asked. With a nod to Yelena, the assassin held her gun to Fisk’s head once more. Her hand was steady, she would certainly succeed where Maya Lopez had failed. Especially when she sunk the entire clip into his brain. Eleanor’s eyes were all at sea. There was so much to consider, so much at stake, so much to lose. “Kate can’t know about this,” she whispered, dejectedly. They had won. “She won’t. You will be her hero , Eleanor.”

    “I need your guarantee that she will be safe,” Eleanor insisted as her voice broke, and the tears that had been collecting in her eyes escaped down, across her cheeks. “You have my word ,” Nadija promised in earnest.

    There was a moment of silence as the gravity of Eleanor’s situation seemed to crush the woman. A moment later, and the gravity lifted. Blue eyes took in Yelena and her mother, and then finally Fisk. Eleanor Bishop nodded her acceptance.

    “Then you have my pledge,” Eleanor promised gravely. She knew she’d just sold her soul, but really, she’d simply nailed her flag to another mast. She was never free of Kingpin, she was simply living on borrowed time until he came back to claim what was rightfully his, and Eleanor’s soul was never really free to be given. It had to be taken with force, something Yelena was more than happy to do.

    Her mother smiled, grimly. She had everything she could possibly want. Her daughter was back in her arms, Eleanor Bishop had pledged to serve her and with the CEO of Bishop Security came the keys to New York City itself. Leviathan had a foothold in the United States once more, born from the ashes of Hydra. How sweet life could be, and how sweet death could be.

    “Good,” Nadija nodded contentedly. “Very good, Eleanor. We will look after each other now, hmm? That is what friends are for. Elena?” Her mother snapped her fingers and Yelena felt the grin begin to spread across her delicate features. This was the moment she’d been waiting for. The moment she’d missed most. This was the kill.

    The muzzle flashed and Eleanor screamed as the gunshot echoed loudly around the study, and yet her mother never flinched. Not with the first shot, or the second, or the third even. She simply smiled with unbridled satisfaction as Wilson Fisk’s brains decorated her bookshelves.

    “Good girl, Elena,” Nadija whispered. “Good girl.”

    See the end of the chapter for more notes The mechanical hum of the QuinJet receded into silence as Melina flicked a switch to power the whole thing down. It was for the best, they couldn’t risk being discovered in a sweep of the area even if it did leave them vulnerable if they found themselves needing to make a speedy exit.

    The S.H.I.E.L.D. facility lay within a valley, with steep, imposing mountains either side, and a small, sleepy town two clicks to the south, where the trickling stream became a rolling river. Cold mountain air infiltrated the jet as Melina triggered the door release, threw a large coat in Kate’s direction and with an affirmative nod, marched out into the night. Kate shivered as the freezing cold air found its way into her lungs. She grimaced in pain as the muscles in her chest tightened and contracted and her hand instinctually went to her sternum. Was she emotionally ready for this mission? The chances were slim. Was she physically ready for it? There was no way. But Kate was determined because there was no other option. Losing Yelena would not be an acceptable outcome and Kate would do just about anything to bring her home. With a steadying breath, the Avenger threw on the large winter coat, picked up her retractable bow and her quiver, and followed Melina out into the dark winter wilderness.

    Snow crunched satisfyingly under Kate’s feet as Melina gestured for her to follow. They found their way to the stream but then took a left, to follow the water down into the sleepy town twenty minutes from their location.

    Kate’s brow furrowed. “Where are we going?” She asked as she stumbled in Melina’s wake. Unsurprisingly, the Russian was far more adept in the winter weather than Kate was. “You will see,” Melina called back. Well, that was enlightening.

    “I-I don’t wanna see,” Kate stuttered as she tried to navigate a particularly deep snow drift, “I wanna know.” She tried her best to sound reasonable, because she wasn’t being unreasonable, she too was on a mission to save Yelena Belova and deserved to know exactly why they were walking in the opposite direction of the very thing that could save her, but this was Melina Vostokoff, and she could kick Kate’s ass.

    The Russian turned to take Kate in as the young Avenger struggled through the snow. She smiled a small and reassuring smile through the darkness. “Trust me, Kate Bishop,” she said softly, “You will know soon enough.”

    Melina had certainly been right. After another fifteen minutes of following the river south Kate began to see. It was subtle at first. Red neon light bounced off glossy pine needles and the freezing mist that hung in the air amongst the cedar and the hemlock was thickly stained. As the unlikely pair trudged closer to the tree line Kate could see even more clearly. The red hues that infiltrated the forest came from the flickering neon light of a dive bar on the edge of town. “Wendell’s”, it read. Outside, in the snow-scraped parking lot sat one solitary Humvee, military grade, and Kate immediately understood.

    “Perfect,” Melina whispered.

    “We’re going to steal a Hummer?” Kate asked. She wasn’t gonna lie, the prospect of stealing a Humvee was pretty gosh darn exciting and the prospect of stealing it to infiltrate a top secret S.H.I.E.L.D. facility was even more exciting.

    “Yes,” Melina smiled knowingly. “But first, how about we get a drink?” Kate’s brow creased in confusion, but she was quickly learning that there was method to Melina’s madness. After all, she was plenty experienced. In fact, she’d probably broken into more US Military Bases than Kate had birthdays.

    The two women made their way across the parking lot and into the bar. Kate threw up a prayer of thanks to the goddess of dive bars and holes in the wall - the place was warm and offered them much needed respite from the bitter Alaskan cold. It was small and dimly lit, and not in a cosy way, but despite its size there was enough space for the customary pool table that stood imposingly to the left of the bar. To the right there were a few darkened booths and in the space in front of the bar lay a pair of round tables with some beat up chairs. “What do soldiers do to entertain themselves in a small, cold town in the middle of nowhere?” Melina mused quietly with an almost imperceptible nod to the two men drinking in one of the shadowy booths to their right. Kate’s eyes followed and she began to understand. The two men were laughing and playing cards, both uniformed, both drunk, and Kate sensed the opportunity.

    “Well,” Kate said as she dragged her eyes away from the two oblivious men, “I would watch Netflix, eat pizza and drink frozen margaritas for the rest of my life,” she explained, conveniently leaving out the rather heart-breaking ‘with my girlfriend’ detail, “But I can see your point.”

    Melina smiled earnestly and gestured for Kate to follow her to the bar. The ex-Widow leaned casually against its sticky veneer as if she frequented the place often. She didn’t turn her nose up at the bar’s overwhelming grossness, there was no look of disdain or words of displeasure, Melina looked as if she was propping up her local. She even sounded like a local as she nodded to the barkeep who was playing solitaire on the decrepit till behind the counter and ordered a “double vodka, straight, preferably cold,” with the most impeccable Alaskan accent. “And you will have…?” She asked as she turned to Kate.

    Kate blinked. “Are we actually drinking?” Kate whispered in hushed tones. “Yes,” Melina nodded, matter-of-factly, as if it were obvious.

    “Are you sure that’s allowed?” Kate asked nervously. She was an Avenger. Avengers didn’t drink on the job, that wasn’t a thing. She had to fire arrows and stuff, surely she wasn’t sanctioned to fire under the influence.

    The older woman rolled her eyes and shared a smile with the barkeep. “Darling, tell the man what you want to drink.”

    Okay, Kate, kind of got it. Couldn’t turn up to costume party without a costume, someone would notice. So, with that same logic, you shouldn’t turn up to a dive bar past midnight and order a coke. And you certainly couldn’t hang with some soldiers, render them unconscious to steal their uniforms and their faces without a beer in hand. Anyways, this mission was off the books, right? No one would even know they were there, as long as they were successful. “Umm,” Kate hesitated a moment more before settling on the weakest, shittiest beer she could lay her eyes on. “I’ll take a Bud Lght. Thank you.”

    “No problem,” the barkeep smiled sleepily as he turned to fix their drinks. Kate could feel Melina’s body tighten next to her as the old fella poured her vodka over ice. A travesty of the highest proportions, and yet the Russian could only smile sweetly as he handed her the drink. Keeping up appearances was of the utmost importance; Melina knew that best of all. Thankfully, she was very good at it.

    Once Melina had paid, the barkeep went back to his game of solitaire and happily ignored them. “Well?” The ex-widow asked, “What are you waiting for?”

    “What?” Kate asked incredulously. It had been Melina’s idea to get a drink, it’s not as if she was actively choosing to lollygag.

    “What are you waiting for?” Melina repeated herself and Kate’s brow crinkled in confusion. Was Kate missing something incredibly, glaringly obvious? “You are a girl, they are boys. Go.”

    Okay, that probably was pretty obvious but that didn’t mean that Kate had to like it. There was no way that she would be flirting with boys. For one, she was a terrible flirt. Two, she was the world’s greatest archer, she was better than that. And three, she didn’t accept the notion that girls flirted and guys fell for it.

    “I am not going to do that.”

    Melina smiled serenely and lowered her voice. “And how would you suggest we relieve these men of their vehicle and their identities? Do you have a better plan to save your girlfriend?” Melina was trying desperately to be nice, she wanted to be, Kate was sure, but there was an edge about the woman that would always feel dangerous.

    Kate swallowed. She knew she didn’t have a better plan, in fact, she didn’t have any plan at all besides waiting outside in the cold until the men appeared. And even if they did that, they had no way of knowing how long the men would drink for, and the prospect of spending hours in sub-zero temperatures was not one that Kate savoured. She’d thought about creating a distraction to lure the men out but there was too much risk involved, too much to go wrong. And so she had to begrudgingly accept that Melina was right. She would have to flirt to save her girlfriend, and by the gods, did she flirt her fucking ass off.

    Within thirty minutes the soldiers were thoroughly charmed. They couldn’t believe their luck. A girl, all the way from New York, had stumbled into their sleepy town. There was something weirdly familiar about her for sure, but she was tall, stunningly beautiful and totally into them. And best of all, she was looking for a place to crash. Well, they could certainly accommodate.

    With the smallest of nods Kate signalled to Melina that she and her friends were just about to call it a night. The ex-Widow quietly thanked the barkeep, left a few dollars on the sticky counter-top surface, and slinked out undetected. Five minutes later and the soldiers were out cold, bound and gagged and stored in the relative safety of the bar basement, a place that Melina had accessed with no trouble at all. Twenty minutes after that and the two women were making their approach.

    “Exterior perimeter fence, interior perimeter wall. Guards walking the grounds and a guard stationed at every vantage point,” Melina noted as she peered through the windscreen. Kate’s eyes narrowed. “That’s a lot of security for a bunch of nerds.” “It is almost as if they are hiding something,” Melina quipped darkly, but she was right. No one patrolled the walls of Avenger HQ, but then again, the Avengers themselves were a pretty good deterrent to any prospective infiltrators.

    “So…” Kate began as her mind started to slide back towards the very reason they were in Alaska in the first place. Yelena. They were hiding whatever did this to Yelena. “What are we thinking?”

    “Well, normally I would have schematics, in-ear support and time to put together a really good plan. Today we have none of that,” Melina explained. Well, that didn't sound good. So, what exactly was the plan? Because there was no way in hell that Kate was leaving without this antidote. There was no way in hell Kate wasn’t getting Yelena back. It didn’t bear thinking about.

    “Right,” she nodded, “So, we go in and…we do what? We-we just ask?”

    Melina smiled. “Something like that,” she said softly. Kate wanted to scream. This woman was infuriating. It was almost as if she and Yelena were related in some way. Both put on Earth to terrify her, endear her, and get right under her skin.

    The Russian slowed as the Hummer approached the small security hut that marshalled the access point in the perimeter fence. It looked like once they were through that, they would be able to pass freely into the walled complex. They just needed to make sure they could fool security with their photostatic veils, big winter uniforms, and the cover of darkness. And they needed to hope that no one questioned why they were back so soon after their most recent shift.

    After a quick show of their IDs, a smile and a polite nod, Melina and Kate were waved through, no questions asked. The younger woman breathed a sigh of relief as the ex-Widow's hands tightened around the wheel, her knuckles growing white. Melina knew that the bigger tests were yet to come.

    Once through the perimeter gate, Melina guided the Hummer towards the large blast doors and again, they were waved inside. They found a place to leave the four by four amongst a few other S.H.I.E.L.D. vehicles and quickly hopped out. For a place that looked like a hulking great piece of concrete on the outside, it sure looked high tech and expensive on the inside. Kate was having déjà vu.

    Bright white lights danced across the polished concrete flooring and three thick glass doors led from the garage at nine, twelve and three o’clock, all needing security card access. Behind one of these doors could be the answers to her prayers. Or, well, behind a door, behind another door behind one of these doors.

    “It's nearly three am, so... three o’clock?” Kate proposed quietly to her Russian companion. Melina nodded, there was no time like the present. The young Avenger glanced at the ID that she held tightly within her hands and prayed. Please work, I love her so you have to work. The pair made their way across the garage as inconspicuously as possible and Kate held her breath as Melina casually tapped her ID against the security panel. The panel released a happy little tone and Kate had to work hard not to match it. It worked! They were one step closer. Unless they should have taken the door to the left, then technically they were one step further away, but that didn’t bear thinking about. They’d sweep the entire complex if they had to.

    Once through and into the corridor they moved quickly. Every angle was surveyed, ever turn was on camera. They needed a little privacy and so, they needed to find the toilets. Thankfully at three am, the corridors were empty and no night owl researchers were cooped up in their offices. They found the restrooms and bundled inside where they quickly discarded their outfits and stored them in a utility closet for safe keeping just in case. Melina searched the facilities for any overhead ventilation. They were in luck. A ventilation shaft ran across the ceiling of the facilities, into the next room and beyond. Within moments Melina had negotiated the vent covering away from the metal structure after receiving a leg up from Kate. She hauled herself up and disappeared inside.

    “Are you coming?” Came Melina’s deep voice from inside the vent.

    “A little help, please?” Hissed Kate as the Russian’s amused face appeared out of the darkness above her. “I’m tall but I’m not that tall.”

    “Give me your hand,” Melina offered as she reached down to capture Kate’s hands within her own and heaved. Man, that woman was stronger than she looked, probably all the root vegetables. She’d certainly be able to give Kate a run for her money on a pull up challenge despite the younger woman’s archer status.

    Once inside the vents Melina deftly contorted, turned her body to face away from Kate and began to shuffle deeper inside the complex. The Russian began to check each room systematically but for what, Kate didn’t know. She would get to a vent covering and peer through, and Kate would hear a muffled ‘Net,’ followed by another muffled ‘Net’, and so on and so forth, as Melina continued to come up empty.

    “What is that we’re looking for exactly?” Kate asked as her voice echoed through the ventilation system.

    “Quiet,” Melina whispered, “Your voice carries in here.”

    “Sorry,” Kate whispered back. She was a first-time vent-crawler.

    “I’m looking for a computer terminal,” Melina explained in hushed tones as she continued to move through the vents, “One I can access easily.”

    “Like a laptop or something?”

    “Exactly like th- Ah. Otlichno,” Melina declared quietly from up ahead. “Is that good?” Kate asked.

    “Very.”

    After a quick visual sweep of the office, Melina removed the vent covering and dropped down into the darkness below. Within a few seconds, Kate had joined her. On the desk sat a S.H.I.E.L.D. issued laptop emblazoned with the organisation's banner. Its owner had left it in the office, which was almost always the right thing to do with machines that held private and confidential information, or even military secrets, but tonight was the exception. Melina flicked the machine open and was immediately met with a password prompt. “Sweep the office. Search for photos, mementos, greetings cards, anything that could give us the password.”

    Kate nodded and got to it. She searched high and low, through drawers and across shelves. She searched the wastepaper bin but came up short. There were no personal photos, no trinkets, no holiday souvenirs to reminded the office’s occupant of fonder times away from home, nothing. Whoever habited this office in the day was surely a robot. There was no other explanation. Kate huffed in frustration. They didn’t have time for this. They needed to access to the mainframe now, they needed to find this lab now. In just a few short hours guards would rotate, day time staff would start flooding into the complex and leaving without being detected would become near impossible, but all this person seemed to give a shit about was Twizzlers. Every drawer held a packet of Twizzlers. Strawberry, grape, watermelon, gross, gross chocolate flavour, cherry... They had Twizzlers coming out of their ass. "Any luck?” Melina inquired, her voice expectant as she tapped away at the laptop to see if she could bypass security altogether.

    The young Avenger huffed in frustration. “Not much to go on. Apart from this person having a major Twizzlers addiction. They’re not even nice.”

    “Okay, I’m in.”

    Kate blinked. “Wait, what?”

    “Twizzlers, that was password.”

    Surely not. There was no way. Kate had some bad passwords in her time like ‘hawkeye<3<3’ and ‘Cl1ntB4rton4L!fe’ but Twizzlers, really? And with no special characters? “Really?” Kate asked in disbelief.

    “No, not really,” Melina deadpanned with the smallest of smiles. “I hacked it.” “You’re…,” Kate’s mouth hung open in disbelief, “Can I learn that?”

    “How much patience do you have?” Melina asked knowingly with an affectionate smile. “How much patience do you think I have?” The Russian’s smile grew wider. It was the perfect demonstration of how and why Kate and Yelena worked so well as a pair. Yelena was truly Melina’s daughter, even if they’d spent many years apart, and the blonde had complimented Kate’s way of work so well. She was cool, collected, efficient, and she was ruthless when she needed to be. She could hack security systems, infiltrate the Tower of London, and anticipate a guard’s next move as if she had a fucking crystal ball. Kate could do none of those things, but she would take risks when no one else would, she would protect Yelena with her life, and she was always there to remind her girlfriend of her humanity and her goodness within her. Fuck, she needed to get Yelena back.

    Something in Kate’s expression must have betrayed her thoughts as Melina’s face softened and the ex-Widow threw her a concerned look. “How are you doing?” She asked gently. Now, that was a big question and the answer was complicated. In that moment, Kate was doing good. She was in her element; this was exactly the kind of thing she’d been training for. Outside of this, Kate was a mess. Physically, she’d been beaten, bad. Her leg burned with every weight-bearing step, her chest was tight with pain and she was almost certainly concussed. Could she shoot straight? Maybe, maybe not. Would that stop her? Not a chance, because mentally, she couldn’t afford not to. She would take every shot, every chance, every risk to get Yelena back. She had to. Without Yelena, Kate didn’t want any of it. The Avenging, the apartment, the trash series on Netflix, the bed that they shared, even the pineapple on pizza; she knew that she couldn’t go back to any of it if they didn’t go back together . Yelena had left an indelible mark on Kate’s life. Like a brainwashing toxin with a chemical structure had that been irrevocably changed by the addition of one very important and unique variable. Kate couldn’t go back because this chemical reaction could not be undone.

    But admitting that was too much. Too much in that moment. Kate needed to focus and stay that way and so she battened down the hatches, pasted a trademark Kate Bishop smile across her face and told Melina that she was okay.

    “Kate, darling,” Melina said softly and their eyes met. The ex-Widow's gaze was unwavering and filled with an age-old pain. “I am not losing another daughter.”

    Within a few minutes Melina had the layout of the base up on screen. They managed to identify a lab that seemed to be a good fit for what they were looking for. Plenty of refrigeration, room for live animal testing, and double the security of anything else in the complex. Thankfully, Melina had managed to disable the various laser triggers with just the click of a button. The action would most likely appear on S.H.I.E.L.D. logs in the morning, but by then they would be long gone.

    Melina and Kate hastily hauled themselves back up into the ventilation system and made for the lab. Their route took them three rooms east into a storage cupboard. From there, Kate took out four cameras, all with some newly designed arrows. They were a modification of Yelena’s suggestion, designed to loop the feed of any security camera within a six-inch radius, and she’d fired true. Fitting, Kate thought, that she used them now. Once they’d negotiated the fourth corridor safely, Melina and Kate ducked into a service elevator to the right and took the short but nerve-filled trip two floors up. The young Avenger snapped away her retractable bow, holstered it and then both women pressed their backs against the either side of the elevator doors, ready for what might lie beyond. The two guards didn’t stand a chance. As soon as the doors pinged open the two women were upon them. In an instant Kate had her guard secured in the tightest of grips. She wrapped her left arm around his neck, captured her left wrist with her right hand, and squeezed. Be more ruthless , she’d said. Kate was more than happy to acquiesce.

    Kate used her final modified arrow to help them elude the camera that was making its routine sweep of the corridor to their right, and then both women dragged their now unconscious victims quickly towards the doors of the lab. THE lab. They’d made it. “Any idea what we’re looking for?” Kate asked as she let the guard’s body fall quite unceremoniously to the floor and began to glance around the room, eager to find what they’d come for.

    “Well, you said the original serum had to be stored at low temperature, yes?” Melina asked as she too began to scan the room for any sign of the serum and its antidote. On one side of the lab were cages-animal cages, and Kate felt a red-hot flash of rage. But she couldn't-she couldn’t be distracted. She wasn’t there to liberate a family of rats, she was there to save her girlfriend. The best she could do was be grateful. If the antidote worked, she'd be thanking the lab rats and not the lab workers.

    There was a bunch of super high-tech looking machines that lined one wall, all seemed to have their own individual purpose, and all seemed to be contributing to the almost inaudible hum that permeated the lab. One machine contained what Kate thought could be a centrifuge, another seemed to be some kind of bio-analyser. And her mom had told her that her CSI hyper-fixation had been a total waste of time.

    Kate felt her chest tighten at the thought. Her mom. Fuck, she hoped that her mom was okay. They were off the grid, no comms, no connection to the outside world apart from her phone that she’d put on airplane mode and left, well, in the airplane. There was no way of knowing if her mom’s condition had improved or got worse. There was no way of knowing if her mother was still alive and Kate was not all that good at not knowing. Thankfully, her brain had something really quite important to focus on, and that’s what she needed to do. She needed to focus. Just focus, Kate.

    The young Avenger nodded in Melina’s direction. Biological elements often needed storing at low temperatures to avoid perishing, and the serum had been kept cool using liquid nitrogen, so it made sense to start there.

    Melina cut a determined figure in the low, fluorescent lighting of the lab. She nodded in return, “Then let’s find it,” and the two women got to work.

    Kate checked the cabinet beneath the machinery first. If you were going to test a sample or create something completely new it would make sense to have everything stored nearby, but unfortunately there wasn’t a fridge in sight.

    “Even if we find it, how are we going to know it’s the antidote?” Kate asked, as she turned her attention to the main console table in the centre of the room. There was storage beneath it and the glistening metal doors were warm to the touch. “I mean, I doubt they’re just going to have it labelled ‘antidote’,” she mused as she pulled the cupboard doors open to reveal a series of integrated fridges containing. “Huh,” was all Kate could manage, as she plucked a vial from within the fridge.

    The label read: Antidote D23. Successful. 13/03/26. BB 13/09/26. Store below 40F.

    “Well, I’ll be damned,” Kate said, breathlessly. This was it, or at least it could be. The thing that was going to bring Yelena back. The thing that meant she didn’t have to give up watching trash on Netflix because it was too painful, or pineapple on pizza, or the bed they shared. She wouldn’t have to give up the future that they’d planned together. The dogs yet to be adopted, the bigger apartment in a different city, the trips to Europe and the Christmases as a family.

    In an instant, Melina was beside Kate, her stoic exterior replaced with one of pride and more importantly, hope. She was beaming. “Well done,” she whispered as she gripped Kate’s shoulder fiercely. “Grab everything you can find. I will look for a way to keep them cool.” Kate didn’t need asking twice. She raided the fridge like a drunk chick in her desperate search of carbs after one too many vodka sodas.

    After a moment, Melina reappeared with a handful of Styrofoam cups from the water cooler. They would be perfect. Clearly S.H.I.E.L.D. was happy to pour trillions of dollars into protecting the world from alien invasion, but didn’t feel compelled to provide their staff with sustainable cups. That checked out, Kate supposed. Why change the habit of a lifetime? Kate laid out all the antidote samples on the console table and the two women studied them closely. All were labelled thirteenth of March or later and all were marked successful. There were seven samples in total, that meant they had seven opportunities to save Yelena. Of course, that was only if it was the actual antidote they were looking for, and only if it worked on humans as well as S.H.I.E.L.D.’s lab rats.

    Kate put both hands against the cool metal of the console and stared at the samples with apprehension. So much was riding on this. “How do we know this is going to work?” Kate asked.

    “We do not,” Melina sighed but still offered Kate a reassuring smile. “They valued these enough to keep them though, which I think is a good sign, no?” The ex-Widow wasn’t wrong. These small samples were all they had, but it was more than they had four hours ago. “You're right,” Kate nodded thoughtfully, “Plus,” she said as the smallest of grins began to pull at the corner of her lips, “These labels look pretty offish. Not gonna lie.” Melina’s reassuring smile grew warmer and Kate felt her trepidation ease somewhat. Melina Vostokoff was smiling, because of some dumb joke Kate Bishop made and it felt good. Both of them felt as if they could breathe a little easier because they were hopefully, hopefully , one step closer to getting Yelena back. They just had to trust that Carol could fulfil her end of the bargain in finding her.

    “They certainly do, Kate Bishop,” Melina smiled affectionately, “They certainly do. Now, let’s get these packed up an-”

    A high-pitched blaring pierced Kate’s senses. Shit. Shit, shit, shit, what had she done? She must have done something. Had the fridge been alarmed? Surely the alarm would have sounded as soon as she’d removed the vials. Unless it was a silent alarm but it really didn’t look like there were any-

    “We need to move,” Melina urged, interrupting Kate’s spiralling thoughts, as she grabbed the vials from the table and filled the Styrofoam cups. “These should keep them cool until we are outside, let’s go.” Melina shoved a cup into Kate’s hand and the two women made for the door.

    Suddenly, Kate felt something yank her backwards, and she fell into Melina who held her close. “Wait, Kate, wait,” the older woman hissed into her ear as the sound of heavy footsteps echoed down the corridor just outside the lab.

    “Potential intruder in the atrium,” came the muffled crackle of a walkie talkie as the footsteps clattered past the entrance to the lab and further down the corridor. “Temporarily shutting down access points A through L.”

    The atrium. The atrium was in the centre of the complex, they’d been nowhere near the atrium. Shit, shit, shit indeed. “That wasn’t us,” Kate whispered as Melina’s hands gripped her arms a little tighter.

    “No,” Melina said quietly and Kate knew everything she needed to, simply from the tone of the older woman’s voice.

    The young Avenger swallowed as the hairs on the back of her neck prickled uncomfortably and the muscles within her chest tightened. “She’s here.” Yelena was there. Somehow, she’d found them but she was far too good to get caught. She’d triggered the alarm on purpose which could only really mean two things: she intended to distract them, or delay them in some way. Or, she simply wanted to play with them and Kate couldn’t help but think it were the latter. And it was going to work. There was no way they were driving out of the complex now, they needed a plan B.

    "Let’s go,” Melina said darkly, from behind. Kate didn’t need telling twice. “Yes, ma’am.”

    “Don’t call me that.”

    “No, ma’am.”

    Fifteen minutes prior, the complex had been a ghost town, but now the place was swarming with guards. They were alert and they were moving with purpose. Kate and Melina had to move slowly, much more slowly than they would have liked. They needed to find roof access, as quickly as possible. All elevators had been shut down to limit movement so the only nearby route was a staircase that catered to the east side of the building, and it was at least a few offices over.

    Now, Kate was not exactly the Red Room’s biggest fan. They stole her girlfriend’s freedom, her childhood, her innocence, and her reproductive organs, but they had also trained their women incredibly well in the art of stealth, violence and subterfuge. This had never been more apparent than in that moment. Melina was like a machine. She moved with purpose and with an elegance Kate hadn’t even seen in Yelena, well, not until their most recent face-offs. As the two women were no longer worried about being discovered, Melina left unconscious men in her wake. Time was of the essence. The antidotes tucked inside their combat gear needed that cold Alaskan air almost as much Kate needed to see that smile that Yelena kept, just for her.

    The pair rounded a corner and two more guards came into view. Melina was on the first in a matter of moments. A kick to his solar plexus, a sharp elbow to the temple and then finally a brutal knee to the face to put him down. The other guard reached for her walkie-talkie but cried out in pain as an arrow pierced the hardened black plastic and pinned it to her shoulder. Kate leapt forward and parried an angry blow and captured the offending limb. She twisted and tried to drag the guard to the floor, but she squirmed from Kate's grasp and delivered a winding blow to her stomach. She felt it. She felt the pain in her chest. The wound that it emanated from. It was warm and tight and sharp and for a moment, she couldn’t breathe, but just as the guard was lining up her next strike, strong arms found their way around her jugular and in moments she was unconscious.

    “You okay?” Came Melina’s voice. It sounded so far away. But Kate nodded the best she could. They needed to keep going, she was okay enough for that. Get up to the roof, get out, and get gone. They were nearly there.

    “Let’s keep moving,” Kate grimaced as she rearranged the Styrofoam cup that was tucked inside her suit. She needed to do a better job of protecting it.

    Melina threaded her arm around Kate’s waist and pulled her close. “Okay, I got you,” she soothed, and the pair staggered onwards. They negotiated the next office and the next corridor, alert for guards but also alert for her. What would Kate do? Now was not the time to try and administer some kind of antidote, in a S.H.I.E.L.D. complex on full alert. So, what would they do? Would they fight? Would Yelena gloat about Kate’s mother? What hurtful words would she have prepared for her? And what would Melina do? Kate could feel the older woman’s tension, her worry, and Kate knew that this Yelena would not spare Melina from those hurtful words, or her violence.

    Finally, after leaving another corridor of unconscious guards in their wake, Melina and Kate found the stairs that led to the roof. They yanked open the door and made their way quickly but cautiously upwards. They knew there would be patrols on the roof, how many they weren’t sure, but alerting one would alert them all.

    All of a sudden, Kate bundled clumsily into Melina’s back. The older woman had come to an abrupt stop at the top of the staircase, and once Kate had righted herself, she could see why. There was a body at the bottom of the access ladder. A male guard. He lay, inhumanly crumpled, within a pool of his own blood. He must have been there for quite some time. This was how she’d gotten in. She must have pierced his heart and then thrown him down the access hatch. It was almost as if he’d been put there to greet them.

    “Blyat,” Melina said darkly. Even the ex-Widow was shocked by the brutality. She shook her head in an attempt to stop the vision before becoming permanently seared into her mind. “Oh my god,” Kate whispered, as the Russian took her by the hand and dragged her towards the hatch. Oh my god. Kate felt as though she was going to be sick. The smell of the iron in the blood, the ruthlessness of the act, and the person who committed it. Her other hand found Melina’s and Kate allowed herself to be guided around the soldier, lying prone upon the polished concrete floor. They did their best to navigate around the blood that had collected there, but there was nothing doing, so bloodied footprints painted the ladder red as they climbed.

    Melina cautiously opened the hatch to the roof and peered out. “It’s clear,” she said grimly. Kate knew what she meant by that, and her stomach lurched. Yelena had cleared the roof of any living threat. The Russian threw open the hatch and climbed out into the cold Alaskan night. Kate’s leg burned from where her own arrow had pierced it less than forty-eight hours previous, as she hauled herself up every rung of the ladder and out to join Melina in the cold. It was bitterly penetrating, and without their thick winter coats they would need to find shelter soon, but at least the antidote would be preserved, and that was the most important thing.

    Kate cast her eyes around in the darkness and saw at least six darkly clothed bodies scattered across the rooftop. She was thankful that the spring sun still hadn’t graced them with an appearance, as the cover of night brought with it a comforting ignorance. There was no blood, no detail, no distinct lack of humanity from the trained killer who took their lives, yes, ignorance was bliss in this case.

    “She’s effective,” Melina mumbled. It was the only thing she could say. Anything else would paint her daughter as a monster, but her actions were speaking louder than any words and Kate couldn’t quell the worry that was beginning to pool within the very pit of her stomach. Even with the antidote, even if they could administer it, and even if Kate’s mother survived, would it be enough? Would it be enough for Yelena to recover? To not feel like the monster she always feared she was.

    “Come on, Kate,” Melina urged as she tried to tear the young Avenger away from the scene of her girlfriend’s crime.

    “Wait, why would she come here if she was going to let us get away?” Kate asked. Something wasn’t right. Something really wasn’t right. It made no sense. Sure, Yelena was playing with them, but to come all the way to Alaska and let them get away with the antidote that could stop all of this made no sense at all. Panic rose within her as her eyes searched the darkness. She must have been there, on the roof with them. Surely, she wasn’t going to let them escape. It was only then that Kate noticed. Next to each slumped figure lay a pulsing, red light.

    “It’s rigged to blow,” Kate whispered in sheer disbelief. Fuck. “It’s rigged to blow!” Melina’s eyes immediately snapped to follow Kate’s gaze. It was all the confirmation she needed. The Russian jumped into action. “Let’s go. Now. Get us out of here Kate.” But what about all the people inside? They were S.H.I.E.L.D. employees, most of them were innocent people, they needed to be warned. “There are people inside,” Kate pleaded with Melina.

    Melina shook her head definitely. Her face was steely and resolved. “There is no time, Kate. Get us out of here, now!” Kate knew that Melina was making the only choice she thought possible but what if they could alert the base? What if they could trigger an evacuation. Lives could be saved.

    “We can raise the alarm.” She couldn’t give up. She couldn’t give up on them. On Yelena. Yelena couldn’t do this.

    “Kate! Darlin-”

    “No, if we let her do this, she will not recover. Please,” Kate implored Yelena’s mother. “Please,” she begged. Melina’s eyes were alight with turmoil. She knew they needed to leave, she knew they needed to get the antidote out there. It might be the only chance they had at saving Yelena. But leaving without trying to evacuate the complex, that surely would condemn her.

    Melina sighed loudly and marched over to the first crumpled body. She tried the walkie- talkie. Dead. Kate sprinted to the next one. Dead and dead. Melina made it to the third body and was greeted by a familiar crackle as she tested the piece of equipment. Kate's heart lurched, this time in good way. Melina gave the warning and then Kate fired the arrow that would zipline them to safety. They landed softly in the snow and with a quick check on the antidote, they began to trudge their way back towards the QuinJet, double time. The snow thinned once they reached the treeline and disappeared into the forest. The darkness felt darker in there, under the cover of cedar, and Kate couldn’t shake the feeling that they were being watched, pursued even. She always knew when Yelena’s eyes were upon her, she could always feet her gaze. She felt it now.

    Kate saw the explosion before she heard it. The bright white flash crashed through the forest, casting long wintery shadows against the snow-lined undergrowth. Then, Kate heard it. It beat against her eardrums and consumed her consciousness. And finally, Kate felt it. It collided with the inside of skull. It penetrated her muscles, her bones, her sinews. It penetrated her very being.

    For a while, there was only darkness. Then there was a fuck load of ringing. And then there was Melina, dragging her to her feet. “You’re okay,” Kate heard her sooth. “You’re okay.” Her voice was soft and somehow calmed her ringing ears. “We need to keep moving. Is the antidote safe?”

    Shit. Kate took an unsteady hand and reached inside her combat suit. Fingers closed around the cup and she extracted the would-be cooler. The cup was a little crumpled but thankfully still intact, as were the vials that lay within. Thank god , the Styrofoam must have absorbed most of the impact when Kate had been thrown to the floor. Thank goodness for plastic waste, just this once. “Thank god,” Kate released a breath she hadn’t realised she’d been holding.

    “Good,” Melina nodded, “Mine are intact as well.”

    “What do we do now?”

    “We will let Yelena come to us,” Melina ventured as she cast her eyes darkly about the forest. Fire raged through the complex to the North. No longer did tall, sharp silhouettes cut through the forest. Instead, the flicker of flame sent the shadows into an impish dance amongst the trees making it all the harder to spot any lingering Black Widow assassins. "For the antidote?” It made sense. She’d destroyed the facility for a reason, surely under some sort of instruction. Which meant Leviathan were probably aiming to rid S.H.I.E.L.D. of this new mind-control tech and anything that could stand in the way of them utilising it for themselves. To do that, Yelena would have been tasked to destroy any remnant of the serum and its antidote, so Melina was right she would come, and now they were away from the facility and in the relative safety of the forest, they could confront Yelena with the antidote. It would be two against one, and this time not only did Kate have her own Black Widow, she also was willing to do what needed to be done. She was ready to fight Yelena, no holding back, because there was no alternative to getting her back. None that she was willing to accept anyways.

    “Yes.” Melina nodded stoically, she knew what was to come.

    Thunder cracked viscerally above them. No, not thunder, jets. S.H.I.E.L.D. had scrambled jets. Oh shit. This changed everything. Kate’s eyes snapped to the evergreen canopy above her. She could just about pick out the underside of QuinJets skirting across the treetops. That didn’t mean air support, that meant ground troops, and that meant that their plans had to change. They couldn’t wait around for Yelena, only to be discovered by an entire unit of S.H.I.E.L.D. soldiers. But this was their golden opportunity. This could work. She could have Yelena back that night, she could take Yelena home that night. But the prospect of that was quickly going out the window and for the thirty-seventh time in the last seventy-two hours, Kate’s hopes had been stabbed, maimed, punched, thrown into a ditch and fucking stamped on, along with her heart.

    “Pizdets,” bit Melina in frustration. “The cavalry has arrived. We cannot stay here.” Regretfully, Kate was inclined to agree, that didn’t mean she had to be happy about it. “But… Yelena,” Kate whispered as she cast her eyes back to the flames that licked the burning complex.

    “There will be other opportunity,” Melina reasoned gently, “If we are discovered there will not.”

    Kate swallowed hard as fire danced across violet eyes.

    “Kate,” Melina’s hand closed around Kate’s right arm and willed the young Avenger’s eyes to hers. Dark eyes burned into hers. They were angry, determined, they were grief stricken. They were the eyes of a mother who was on the brink of losing her daughter, of a woman who’d do whatever it took to ensure that didn’t happen, to avoid the heartrending, all- consuming, inconsolable loss. But they were also the eyes of a woman who knew that sometimes to win tomorrow, we had to conceded today. “I promise we will find her again and it will be on our terms,” Melina said, emotion so evident in her voice. “I just…” Kate’s words caught in her throat. What a fucking nightmare. What an actual fucking living fucking nightmare. How could they leave? How could they just leave without her? Kate knew that it had never been the plan, but they were so close, she was so close. She couldn’t bear the idea of leaving without her, of parting ways again, of going home to that apartment or back to her bunk without her. She couldn’t bear the idea of knowing that the woman she loved was out there, not loving her back. Not thinking about her. Not missing her. Not spending every waking moment trying to find her way back to her. I just... I love her,” Kate choked as grief began claw at her throat, tears began to fill her eyes, and the physical pain of it all began to shake her body.

    Quite suddenly, Kate was pulled into Melina’s surprisingly soft embrace. Strong yet gentle arms held her and tender lips pressed the lightest of kisses into her hair. “I know,” the ex- Widow soothed. There was a sadness in her voice, it was inescapable, but there was so much warmth as well. “She loves you too,” Melina said softly, and although Yelena had never said it, Kate knew it to be true. She’d always known it. The first time Yelena had used that smile with Kate, that secret smile, she’d known it, but the young Avenger would be damned if she never heard Yelena speak those words. The real Yelena. But not for herself. Kate didn’t need to hear them, not really. Kate wanted Yelena to speak them for herself. She wanted Yelena to know love and let herself feel love in return. She wanted Yelena to know that her love wasn’t a curse on someone and once all of this was over, Kate would make it her absolute priority to ensure that she understood that.

    Kate took a steadying breath, her face buried in Melina’s long, dark hair, before she drew back from the older woman’s warm embrace and offered her a resolute nod. “Okay, we got what we came for. Let’s go.”

    Despite the burning in her leg and the ringing in her ears, Kate managed to just about keep pace with Melina. The ground underfoot was treacherous, and Kate was caught out more than once by fallen branches or divots in the forest floor disguised by fallen snow. But each time Kate was thrown off course, Melina was there to catch her. The young Avenger couldn’t have been more grateful, and suddenly Kate was hit with one singular and all-consuming thought. Whatever happened here, whatever happened with Yelena, Kate wanted Melina in her life. Kate needed Melina in her life, and Kate suspected that Melina would need her. Kate resolved then and there to make sure that happened.

    Kate’s lungs were screaming by the time the QuinJet came into view, and if things had been different, she would have made a joke about Yelena, cardio training and her own willingness to listen, but things weren’t different. So, Kate stayed quiet and tried darndest to shut the thought down.

    Once inside the jet, Melina fired up the engines, initiated the jet’s cloaking device and guided them up and out of the clearing. Once in the air Kate powered up her phone and pinged Carol an encrypted text, courtesy of Bishop Security, to let her know that they were on their way home with what they hoped was the asset in their possession.

    The young Avenger relaxed into her seat and secured her harness. They had indeed gotten what they’d come for, they’d retrieved the antidote and soon they would able to put it to use. Kate turned the Styrofoam cup within her hands. It was packed with snow from the forest floor and with a little care and attention would stay cool for the duration of their trip home. Kate sighed. Home . Was a home without Yelena really home anymore? There was no way, not really. Her girlfriend had completely and utterly infiltrated her life. She'd given meaning to every part of it. This antidote within her hands would make sure that meaning didn’t fade. Without warning the QuinJet lurched sideways violently. Kate was thrown hard into her harness and her hands tightened instinctually around the Styrofoam cup. There was no way she was letting all that hope slip through her fingers. Her shoulders burned where woven straps dug harshly into her flesh and it was only when she her Melina’s muffled Russian cursing did she realise quite the enormity of what had happened.

    The jet was groaning, shaking and shuddering. Melina’s knuckles were white as she wrestled against the controls with all her strength. Kate must have heard the blast that had severed the left wing, she must have seen it too, but it had all happened so fast. There was no way they were making it home now.

    “Kate!” Came Melina’s voice. They were losing altitude at an alarming rate. “I need you to hang on, okay?!” the older woman shouted over the horrific sounds coming from the Jet. Breathable air was being lost faster than the jet’s failing systems could pump it in, but they’d probably be on the ground in a thousand pieces before it became any real issue. Always best to focus on the positives. Fuck, fuck, fuck, they were going to die. Fuck, they were going to die and no one was going to save Yelena. She would always be this way. This cruel, violent, monstrous killer. They were going to die and Yelena would never know it. Unless... unless she did this. Unless she rigged their Jet to explode.

    A cacophony of noise assaulted Kate’s ears. Wind rushing through torn metal, high-pitched alarms blaring through the cockpit, and the sound of the Earth hurtling towards them at a million miles per hour. Melina desperately pulled at the controls to right the lurching Jet. She was using all her strength and all her determination to will the Jet’s nose upward. She grit her teeth, strained and screamed and fought against gravity. Kate knew that Melina had been here before, countless times, but she didn’t know whether that meant their chances were better or worse.

    “I’m going to try and put it down!” The ex-Widow shouted over the sound of raging winds and twisting metal. Least it was snow, right? Snow was soft. Softer than not snow. They’d be fine... right? Just like Steve Rogers. Steve was fine. Frozen in time for decades but fine relatively speaking.

    The ground was getting closer and closer. No longer could Kate see mountains or trees or rivers, she could only see a blanket of the whitest, purest moonlit snow. But then, suddenly, she could see the midnight blue of a winding river. She could see the snow-capped trees. She could see where valley met mountain and she knew that Melina was winning her arm wrestle with their grim reality.

    The impact came quicker than Kate expected. It was hard, and violent, and cold. Turns out snow was not soft.

    Kate blinked once, then again. She could hear her pulse thumping through her ears. She could feel it, beating its tattoo into her brain. Her shoulders ached, her chest pained, and her head felt as if it were about to explode. Down was up and up was down, the sky was a bright white and the ground was dawning as soft springtime crimson bled across the sky. Kate shook her head, desperately trying to clear darkness back into the corners of her mind. The antidote, where was the antidote? She needed to get out of her harness, she needed to get the right way up, and she needed to check on Melina who was slumped, motionless at the controls. The buckle was jammed and so the young Avenger twisted and wriggled out of her seatbelt’s clutches before she gently lowered her way down to the ceiling. Kate immediately felt inside of her suit, where she’d instinctually secured the precious cup of vials just before they’d crash landed. No, no, no, no. It couldn’t be. Kate pulled the cup from inside her suit and gaped helplessly at the crushed Styrofoam. The vials were shattered and the serum had leaked out into the snow that had been keeping it insulated. This couldn’t be happening. She hadn’t come all this way, she hadn’t pinned all their hope on this, to have it quite literally shatter into a million pieces in front of her. This couldn’t be how it ended. This wasn’t it, this wasn’t their story. Kate felt her chest tighten, fuck, it was hurting so bad. The wound hurt like hell, and her chest was heavy, so heavy, as if someone had placed a heavy weight upon it. The weight of grief and hopelessness and loss. But it wasn’t all lost. Melina had hers. Her antidotes could be safe, they could have survived the crash. They had to have survived the crash.

    “Kate Bishop.” Kate’s heart lurched within her chest. It was her voice. The voice that Kate had so easily fallen in love with. The voice that would send her heart racing when it spoke her name, just like it had in that moment. "What are the chances?” Kate dared not turn round. If she did, and if she was there, then it was true. Yelena had been the one to down the plane. If she turned round and Yelena was there, there was only thing that was going to happen. They were going to fight and out here in the middle of nowhere, either both of them were going home together, or Kate wasn’t going home at all.

    Kate took the deepest of steadying breaths and steeled herself. She would need to be strong and she would need to be ruthless. She closed her eyes, took one final breath and turned to face the woman she loved. Kate gave herself a moment to look upon her. Yelena was so beautiful. The time that they’d had together, it had been so beautiful. The Assassin’s soft blonde hair was neatly braided away from her face. Kate remembered running her fingers through that hair, she remembered how it felt against her fingertips and how she would braid it herself before missions. They would shower and sit together afterwards to watch some show on Netflix whilst Kate would comb it through and negotiate it into whatever plait she felt like that morning. Yelena would always thank her with gentle touches and tender kisses. It was at those times, before missions that Yelena was often at her softest, and then she’d throw on a black combat suit and turn into Yelena Belova, feared Black Widow Assassin. The wind whipped and whistled through a gaping hole in the QuinJet’s fuselage. The back half of the jet been completely torn from the cockpit during landing and left behind, and the famous Assassin, dressed all in black, cut a threatening figure against the bright white Alaskan landscape. This was it then. It all came down to this.

    “I know what you want,” Kate called over the howling wind.

    Yelena smiled and raised an amused eyebrow. “And what is that?” she asked quietly. The Assassin didn’t have to shout, didn’t have to raise her voice. Somehow it carried. “The antidote!” Kate shouted, as held the crushed Styrofoam cup before her. “But you’ve won. It’s gone!” It was a lie, or at least Kate hoped it was. She hoped upon hope that somewhere on Melina’s very unconscious person laid an intact vial.
