    “Antidote?” Yelena spat as amusement was quickly superseded by disgust, “Do not lie to me Kate. I am here to destroy the last of the serum.”

    Kate frowned in confusion. Yelena didn’t know about the antidote, she only knew of the serum. She wanted to destroy the serum. Was that what they had told her? That S.H.I.E.L.D. had been using the serum against her? It was certainly the perfect story, and the perfect motivation.

    “Is that what you think this is?” Kate asked, cup still in hand, “This is the antidote, Yelena. We came here to get the antidote, to free you.”

    Yelena smiled cynically and shook her head. It was then that Kate noticed the ear-piece that was hidden snuggly within her right ear. Yelena was in communication with someone, or someone was in communication with her. “Yelena,” Kate pleaded, desperate for the Russian to not only listen but hear her, “Leviathan, they already have the serum. That’s what they’re using to control you.”

    “You make lies sound so sweet, my love.”

    “Don’t call me that,” Kate hissed. It was too painful to hear. To hear her voice, but to know they weren’t her words. It was far too painful.

    “What would you prefer?” Yelena asked darkly as she tilted her head almost imperceptibly to stare her girlfriend down. Her eyes were dark, intimidating and unshakable but Kate had to match her. She had to be brave, she had to be tough and she had to be ruthless. Be ruthless, Kate, just be ruthless . "How about sweetheart?” Yelena continued with a smirk as she slowly closed the distance between herself and the young Avenger. “Lyubimaya? Oh, I’ve got it!” The Russian smiled charmingly and the brunette’s stomach lurched. She was stunningly beautiful and disconcertingly terrifying all at the same. “Kate, darling ,” her voice was smooth and soothing but oh so dangerous, “Give me the serum.”

    “Whatever you thought was in these vials, it’s gone,” Kate held out the cup to her, she tried to show her. “I swear it.”

    Yelena’s charming mask fell away and all that was left was a face filled with rage and violence. “You’re a liar!” The assassin growled, “Just like that woman who dares to call herself my mother.”

    “Yelena, she is your mother. She loves you.”

    “No,” Yelena shook her head darkly, “Nadija Delić is my mother and she has liberated me from this- from this sham.” What ?

    Kate stood, open mouthed. “Nadija… Nadija is alive?” She gasped. Yelena’s mother was alive, Yelena’s mother was Leviathan. Yelena’s mother was controlling her own daughter. This had just gotten so much worse.

    “Yes,” Yelena smiled, proudly and Kate wanted to reach for her. She wanted to pull her close and tell her how deeply sorry she was. How sorry she was that it had turned out this way. The one thing that Yelena had been missing, the face that she’d lost, the memories her mind had hidden, the woman she loved unconditionally, didn’t love her back. Not in the way that she should.

    “Oh, Yelena. Sweetheart I’m so sorry.”

    “No,” the blonde shook her head as violet met hazel, “I’m sorry.” Yelena held Kate’s gaze for a moment longer before she turned to where Melina’s prone body still hung awkwardly in her harness. Whatever Yelena was fixing to do, there was no way Kate was letting that happen. As soon as the Russian moved, Kate matched her and quickly put herself between Yelena and her mother, her real mother.

    Her girlfriend was so close now. She could see every detail of her face. The small and delicate collection of freckles that resided exclusively upon her left cheek. Her perfect nose, her downturned smile and her full eyebrows. The red flush that always started at the base of her neck and worked its way across her gentle features. Of course, Kate never needed to be this close, all she really needed to do was close her eye as she’d studied Yelena so many times before. With her eyes, her lips and her fingertips.

    “I warned you Kate,” Yelena whispered and her voice low, “Do not get in my way.” It was a statement that was meant to be threatening, and it certainly was but there was something in it that felt off. Kate could tell that her girlfriend was chewing the inside of her cheek. Her breathing was shallow and her eyes couldn’t hold the brunette’s gaze. Perhaps there was more going on in that mind than Kate originally thought. Was Yelena conflicted? It was possible, right? Even if she was under some sort of mind-control. Anything was possible. It was time to challenge that theory.

    “What are you going to do, choke me out again?” Kate gave a cynical smile of her own. “I don’t think you can finish the job.”

    Yelena shrugged nonchalantly. “We needed you then, to lead us here, but we need you no longer.” Something flickered in Yelena’s eyes, recognition at first, and then frustration. The person on the other end of the ear piece was speaking. No, not just speaking, they were giving her instructions. Instructions that she didn’t like.

    “I don’t believe you,” Kate said earnestly. There was something that had stopped Yelena from killing her before in their apartment. She’d missed Kate’s heart for a reason, and whatever it was, whether it was pity, necessity, love or all of the above, Kate knew that it was going to give her a chance, IF Melina’s vials were intact.

    Yelena’s lip curled into a snarl. Kate was getting under her skin, and Yelena knew it. The brunette was onto something.

    “I rigged your ship to blow,” Yelena hissed.

    “Knowing full well Melina would get it under control,” Kate snapped back confidently. Maybe that was a stretch, but Kate was almost sure that it had been Yelena’s stretch and not hers.

    The blonde’s jaw was tight and a muscle ticked there in irritation. She was flushed with cold and rage and Kate could sense something coming. She was losing her temper; she was losing her mind. The voice in her ear was telling her one thing, her head another and her heart something else entirely. Usually, Yelena was so focused, so efficient, so single-minded. She was the epitome of ruthless and it was why she was practically unbeatable. But today, Yelena wasn’t focused, no, she was angry, she was conflicted and surely, she could be beaten. “I will tell you one last time, Kate,” Yelena warned as her hazel eyes grew darker. “Step. Away.”

    As threatening as Yelena was, Kate wasn’t intimidated. She couldn’t afford to be. Instead, she straightened her shoulders, puffed out her chest and met the blonde’s gaze. “No,” she said defiantly.

    Yelena nodded softly, for she understood what would come next. “Okay, so be it,” she whispered and then struck.

    The first blow was hard, brutal. Almost too brutal and Kate parried it with ease. The second was more measured and the brunette had to twist deftly out of its way. Strong hands captured her and tried to drive her down towards a vicious knee that was on a collision course with her chin, but Kate broke Yelena’s grip, grabbed her by the collar and drove her forehead into the bridge of her girlfriend’s nose.

    Stars exploded across Kate’s vision as Yelena staggered backwards and out of her grasp. She’d done it. She’d landed a blow on Yelena Belova. Not the best idea to use her head when she was nursing a concussion but desperate times called for desperate measures. The brunette blinked away the last of the lingering solar bodies that clouded her vision and closed the distance between herself and the assassin. She had to get hands on again and fast, but Yelena was faster. She swayed backwards and evaded Kate’s first kick and then ducked her second. The brunette had to be alert to avoid the subsequent leg sweep.

    Yelena rolled backwards and sprung back to her feet. She smiled with satisfaction as she wiped at the blood that oozed from her nose with the back of her gloved hand. “Impressive, Kate. Most impressive. See what you are capable of when you are pushed? You should be thanking me.”

    Kate rolled her eyes impatiently. “You talk too much, and coming from me, that’s a burn.” Yelena grinned, she was enjoying herself far too much. Of course she was. Wait, Kate blinked. Of course she was. This was what they did. This was exactly what they did. They’d fight and talk trash and fight some more. Yelena would pay Kate a backhanded compliment or two, let her land a few punches and then find another gear to finish her off. Well, Kate Bishop thought resolutely, not this time.

    The brunette charged forward again, she needed to put Yelena down. Knock out or choke out. If she managed that, they could administer the antidote and if not, they could at least hold her until someone somewhere managed to formulate some kind of alternative cure. The blonde parried her advances as they traded blows, but with every blow parried Yelena failed to land one of her own. Kate was focussed, relentless and couldn’t afford to lose. She kicked high and swept low and Yelena was forced to retreat out into the knee-high snow. The Russian’s blood decorated the crisp white carpet as Yelena parried a jab followed by a tight upper cut but missed the elbow. To make it Kate had to compromise herself, she to expose her right side to a kick or low punch, but it was a risk that paid off. Yelena never expected Kate to take risks.

    The Russian staggered further into the crisp Alaskan morning. This wasn’t going the way she’d hoped, but she was still smiling grimly. All she needed was for Kate to make one mistake and it would become a deadly one. Kate couldn’t give her that opportunity, she had to press on. The two Avengers traded kicks and punches and knees and elbows. Yelena caught Kate in the thigh with a ferocious kick and it burned like hell. The brunette wanted to scream as an excruciating fire reaped through the nerve endings that stemmed from the wound there. The wound inflicted by Yelena herself. She knew and she smiled a bloodied smile before she sprung again on her left leg to deliver a knock out kick with her right to Kate’s left ear, but not before the brunette rolled to her right, teeth gritted, as she willed her leg back into action.

    Yelena advanced and Kate evaded. The blonde was having to fight harder against the snow, being the shorter of the two, and she sneered in frustration as Kate escaped her advances. She was leading Yelena further into the wilderness. Maybe a stupid idea to try and fight a Russian in sub-zero temperatures but it appeared to be working. The snow was growing deeper and deeper and Yelena was growing tired. She swung once and Kate parried, twice and Kate ducked, thrice and the brunette had her. She’d overcommitted and with swift kick to outside of her knee which caused it to buckle unpleasantly, Yelena fell with a pained cry. The sound of it tore through Kate, it made her chest tight and her stomach sick, but this was her opportunity to ensure that Yelena’s pain didn’t continue. In an instant Kate had Yelena in a headlock. It was a guillotine blood-choke. If Kate could just secure it Yelena would be out in seconds.

    The assassin instantly recognised the threat and began to fight against Kate’s strong grip, but the brunette was determined not to be bested. She threw herself backwards into the snow and took Yelena with her. She wrapped her legs tightly around the blonde’s waist to secure the hold further, to cling on tighter. With both hands clasped together and her right forearm pressed tightly against Yelena’s neck she squeezed with all her might. Yelena’s movements grew more erratic, more desperate and that’s when Kate knew she had it locked in. Just a few more seconds, she just needed to hold for a few more seconds.

    It all happened so quickly. Yelena’s good leg found purchase in the snow and with her final ounces of strength, she rocked herself forward and loosened the pressure around her jugular. Suddenly strong hands were wrapped around Kate’s wrists and they were pushed to the ground beside her. Yelena’s forehead met her nose, as the blonde returned the favour and once more, Kate’s vision erupted. Hands wrapped themselves around her neck and tightened. Kate tried to fight but her head rang and her body refused to play ball. Oxygen neglected her lungs and her heart bead loudly within her throat. She could hear nothing but the sound of it beating, faster and more erratically than ever before. Nothing but Yelena’s ragged breath, as she heaved and cried out in anguish. She was crying. Yelena was crying. Hot tears fell upon frozen cheeks and violet eyes met hazel perhaps for the last time. But Kate wasn’t looking into the cold, merciless eyes of a trained killer, but the scared, confused and tortured eyes of a woman whose mind and heart couldn’t be reconciled. Kate had wanted to end Yelena’s pain, but in reality, she’d only made it worse, because Yelena really did love her. “Hvah-tit, Elena, hvah-tit!” They were so close now, Kate could hear here. She could hear the woman barking instructions over Yelena’s earpiece.

    Yelena gritted her teeth and Kate felt her heavy breath tickle her cheeks. “No.” “Stop, Elena!” Came the voice again. It was abrupt, demanding; it was used to giving out orders.

    The blonde shook her head. “I can’t,” she said, hopelessly. She was too far gone. They both were. Darkness began to creep into Kate’ consciousness. A grim vignette that grew, becoming more tangible and all-consuming by the second.

    Kate was losing her mind, losing her sense of self, as her brain cells started to shut off one by one. Up was down, cold was hot, and the hands around her neck felt as though they were delivering her to another place in time. Back into the very fabric of her reality. “Elena!” came the voice through the darkness.

    “I need it to stop.” The low voice that she loved so dearly shook with anguish. She needed to hear it, she needed to feel it. She wanted it to be the last thing she tasted before she died. “Elena. Listen to me, I need her, Elena!”

    "Yelena?” Came a new voice. It was one Kate recognised but she couldn’t place it. The comforting tightness around her neck receded and silence fell. Was that it? Was she dead? Kate felt nothing, absolutely nothing. Not the tips of her toes, not the coolness of the snow seeping into her combats, not the split in her eyebrow that was gushing red on white. Nothing. She must be dead.

    “I have what you want,” came the voice again. It was heavy with emotion. Perhaps Kate wasn’t dead after all and somehow, although didn’t know why, her heart filled with hope at the sound of the woman’s words.

    “Give it to me,” that lovely voice insisted.

    “I will but only if you promise to never touch her again.” There was a silence between the two. They were mother and daughter, weren’t they? Their voices were the same but different.

    “You still love her, do you not?” the mother continued. Yes, she was Yelena’s mother and Yelena loved her. Yelena loved Kate Bishop. Feeling seeped back into Kate fingertips as oxygen slowly returned to her lungs and she blinked once and then again. She felt cold, she’d never been so happy to feel this cold.

    "You love her and you cannot bear it,” Melina continued. She was pleading her case with her daughter, pleading with her humanity. “Your mind is telling you that it is weakness. That she is your only weakness, but love is not your weakness, Yelena. Love is what always set you apart. Let me help you.” The older Widow was right. Love had always set Yelena apart. It’s why Melina had chosen her in the first place. It’s what formed their bond. It was Yelena’s love for her family that kept her alive during those many years in the Red Room. It was Yelena’s love for her Widows that fuelled her mission to liberate each and every one of them. And it was Yelena’s love for her sister that brought her to Kate.

    The young Avenger groaned as she hauled herself into a seated position. Her head spun violently and she felt as if she was going to vomit. She really needed to not vomit. Firstly, that would be gross, and secondly, vomiting after a hit to the head was not a good sign. Footsteps crunched in the snow and then came to an abrupt halt.

    “Give me the serum,” Yelena’s voice demanded. She was losing patience because her mother was right. She’d struck a chord and the blonde hated it.

    “Yelena, we can help,” Melina persisted.

    “Give it to me or I will kill you,” Yelena bit back.

    “Now, now, Yelena.”

    “Give it to me!” The blonde raged. She was losing it, she was losing her mind. Her anguish over Kate, the love her mother was showing her. It was all too real, and it was all too different to the truths that Nadija was telling her. Kate could hear Yelena exhale loudly, she was trying her hardest to measure herself, to control her temper. The brunette knew the routine well. She would puff her cheeks and breathe in deeply through her teeth, and her voice would steady.

    Silence fell once more between the pair and Kate’s hands went to where her retractable bow usually clipped to her belt. It was still there.

    “Give me the serum and I swear that I will not touch her again,” Yelena bargained. This wasn’t what Kate wanted but Melina had decided for the both of them. They needed to concede this battle in order to win the war. “You will not see me again,” Yelena continued, “Neither of you will.”

    “I will not give up on you, Yelena,” Melina said softly.

    Her movement was just a blur but Kate saw it clearly. Yelena had closed the distance between herself and mother with a gun in hand. “Give up on me? Cyka,” she spat with disdain, “You gave me to them!”

    “I did,” Melina nodded calmly.

    “And then you let them take me again after Ohio.”

    “If I could have-.”

    “Eighteen years of could haves. Eighteen years, Melina!” Yelena’s gun was in Melina’s face, but Melina had no intention of fighting her daughter. Kate grimaced in pain as she felt behind her for her quiver. She’d be lucky if there was even one arrow left inside after the brutality of her fight with Yelena, but to her surprise, forefinger met feather.

    “I do not pretend to be perfect, Yelena,” Melina shrugged as a sad smile pulled at her lips. “I am far from it. But this woman who claims to be your mother, how is she better? If she is truly Leviathan, she could have spared you from the Red Room, instead she condemned you to it.”

    “No,” Yelena shook her head, disbelievingly. “No, is not true.” Who knows what the voice in her ear was telling her, what lies it was weaving into the recesses of Yelena’s subconscious. “Yelena, do you not see?” Melina said as she took a step forward, towards her daughter, despite the gun barrel that was trained upon her. “She has been grooming you from the start, my darling.”

    “Stop it.” The hand that was holding the gun to Melina’s head began tremble. Yelena was breaking.

    “You are a weapon to her ,Yelena.”

    “That is not my name,” the blonde growled.

    “But to me, Yelena,” Melina continued, unphased by the weapon in her face as the most loving smile brightened her face, and the happiest of tears glistened in her eyes, “To me, you are everything. You are my daughter.”

    Kate turned in the snow and tried desperately to drag her knees underneath her body. “Stop!” growled Yelena.

    “Take the antidote, Yelena. Please.” Melina implored her tenderly.

    “So, you can control me?”

    Melina almost laughed; Kate could hear it. “Is that what she is telling you? The woman in your ear?” Yelena’s silence spoke volumes. “She is the one controlling you. The mind control has an auditory trigger, do you know that? S.H.I.E.L.D developed it but Leviathan stole it from them.”

    “You’re lying!” Yelena cried. “She is my mother!”

    “I know how much she means to you, baby, but-”

    “She loves me! She tells me she loves me.”

    Melina shook her head sadly and reached out to gently capture her daughter’s face within the palms of her hands. It was brave but that’s everything Melina was when it came to her daughters. “We love you Yelena too. Me, Kate, your father. We are your family.” “No,” Yelena shook her head, and Kate didn’t know whether she was trying to beat away her own thoughts, Melina’s words or the words of the malevolent woman in her ear. “I waited...,” Yelena gasped through ragged breaths. She was close. She was so close to giving in. “I waited for her, for so long.” Yelena’s tears broke over cheeks like waves against the shore and she folded into Melina’s arms.

    The older woman held onto her daughter for dear life, antidote still tucked safely in her right hand. “I know, I know,” she soothed gently. “I know darling. And I want so much for you to find what you are looking for, but this is not it.” Yelena’s small frame shook as tears wracked her body. Melina placed a small kiss atop her head and for a moment enjoyed the feel of her daughter’s soft blonde hair against her cheek, before she drew back and rested her forehead gently against Yelena’s.

    The blonde sniffed as her tears started to quell and her lungs began to win out over the sobs that had been so dominating moments earlier. Melina held the antidote within her hands and showed it to her daughter.

    “I need you to let me give you this. I know it is a lot to ask, but it will ease your mind, I promise.”

    Yelena’s eyes searched Melina’s for any reason to doubt her, but they came up wanting. For the longest moment the older woman held her breath until the blonde gave her a small but certain nod. Relief flooded Melina’s face before Yelena wrapped her hands around her mother’s and began to squeeze.

    Melina’s eyes flashed with panic. “Yelena let go.”

    “No,” Yelena said darkly.

    “Yelena, I-arghh” Melina cried out in pain as the vial shattered within her hands, along with her hope. Glass sliced through her skin and blood began to drip, drip, drip upon the snow below.

    The sound of a recurve bow firing was the only warning the two former Widows got. An arrow sailed through the air at lightning speeded, pierced both their hands and lodged itself there. Yelena choked and gasped as white-hot pain claimed her, and Melina cried out once more. But blood mixed with blood, and antidote found its way beneath Yelena’s skin. It had been a dick move, Kate knew it, to strike Melina too, but she had to be ruthless, she had to take the chance that she was presented for it might have been their last. “Cyka,” Yelena spat, as her chest heaved in pain. Kare grimaced at the sight before her. With gritted teeth young Russian slowly but surely dragged her left hand down towards the tip of the arrow and freed it. With one swift motion she twisted to her left, turned her and Melina’s hands skyward and pulled the arrow by its flight, up and out of their interlocked hands. The older Widow slumped to the floor as Yelena threw the arrow down angrily. It pieced the snow, tip first, and stood to attention at her feet. The blonde turned to face Kate with wrathful eyes.

    Come on, work, Kate thought, desperately. Please work, any time now, any time now. Yelena trudged towards her the best she could, favouring her left-hand side. The two were quite the pair. Yelena with only one working knee and Kate with only half a working brain. They were both lucky to be on their feet at all.

    “How have I not killed you already?” Yelena leered. She was tired, exhausted even, but that couldn’t keep the murderous smirk from her face. “No matter,” she said quietly, “I will simply... I wil-” The words caught in Yelena’s throat and she blinked. Her gaze faltered as her eyes flashed erratically to Kate’s and then away. She couldn’t find the words. “I will…,” Yelena swallowed but the words wouldn’t come. Her face ran pale and the smirk that had resided there moments before had gone, replaced by a lost and blank expression. It was working. Whatever was in that mother fucking vial was working . Kate’s final arrow had found its mark and the best shot she never took became the best shot she ever took. Yelena reached for her girlfriend as she staggered forward and collapsed into the snow before her.

    “Yelena!” Kate gasped. She was at her side in an instant. “Babe, can you hear me?” she asked as she hauled at Yelena and fought against the snow to roll the blonde onto her back. “Yelena, sweetheart?” She pleaded as she cradled the Russian’s face in her hands. She wasn’t waking up. Kate checked her pulse. It was a little elevated but that was to be expected. “Come on, Yelena. Wake up. Wake up!” Kate urged, willing Yelena to open her eyes. How Kate longed to see those eyes and the person behind once more, the person she loved. As if by design Yelena’s eyes flickered open. For a moment they were lost in the blood orange hues of the dawn and then they found Kate’s. Realisation struck. Kate could see it happen in real time. Confusion to realisation, to panic and regret. “Kate?” Yelena whispered, “Kate, what have I…? What have I don-.”

    But Kate didn’t let her girlfriend finish her sentence. She drew her into her arms and held her impossibly close. The feel of her against her body, the touch of her fingertips as they clung to her back, her face buried into her shoulder. It was all so precious. “Shhh it’s okay,” Kate said gently. ”It’s okay, it’s over,” Kate said, knowing full well that it wasn’t. Not entirely. Yelena’s mother wouldn’t just give up her daughter like that, but when she came for her they would be ready. By the gods they would be ready.

    The two young women stayed there, clung to each other in the snow for what felt like forever. Neither wanted to let go for fear of losing each other all over again. Kate pressed tender kisses into Yelena’s hair and the blonde’s lips found Kate’s neck more than once. The feel of her lips against her skin brought tears to Kate’s eyes as the magnitude of what had happened hit her. She had Yelena back. But it was more than that. Yelena was her home, her sanctuary, her future, all wrapped up into one perfectly sized package. Kate heard the crunching of footsteps in the snow. She knew that Melina had settled beside her and so she relented her grip upon her girlfriend and drew back. As soon as Melina’s eyes found Yelena’s words of heartfelt apology came tumbling from Yelena’s mouth, but her mother was having none of it. She pulled Yelena into the fiercest of hugs and tried her absolute hardest to squeeze the life out of her. The blonde continued to offer yet more tear- filled apologies but Melina simply shhhed and soothed and rocked her daughter gently back and forth.

    Suddenly Yelena twisted violently in pain and cried. “Yelena!?” Kate gasped as a panic- stricken Melina cradled her daughter in her arms.

    Yelena thrashed in the snow and clutched at her temples before she pushed Melina away violently and staggered to her feet. She was trying to put distance between herself, Melina and Kate but Yelena cried out once more and fell to knees.

    Kate didn’t understand. It made no sense. The antidote had worked. It had really worked. It couldn’t be taking hold again could it? It couldn’t be…

    That’s when she saw it. The earpiece; it was pulsing red. It hadn’t been doing that before and immediately Kate knew that she had to get that earpiece away from Yelena. She closed the distance between them and dived to her knees to cradle her girlfriend’s head in an attempt to quell her thrashing. If anything though, Yelena’s pain was increasing by the second. Kate pulled Yelena to her and held her body tight against hers in an attempt to restrict her convulsions. With one tight hand around her waist the other managed to capture Yelena’s earpiece.

    Kate Bishop glanced down at the small piece of tech that lay within the palm of her hand. Yelena’s breath was heavy against her skin.

    “Throw it Kate!” She heard Melina shout. “Throw it!” It was only in that moment that Kate realised the pulsing red light on the earpiece was accelerating. It was going to explode. Fuck, it was going to explode.

    Kate turned and threw the earpiece away from them, as hard and as fast as she could. But she wasn’t fast enough. It exploded before it even hit the ground, with a blinding flash and a deafening bang, and Kate couldn’t remember what happened next. All she remembered was the cold, and the dark, and her voice ringing in her ears. That voice that she loved so much. That voice that would be the end of her.

    Chapter End Notes Yikes. I think I need a drink.

    Friends Don't Let Friends Kill People Chapter Notes Hello! I'm here to give you the chapter you've all been waiting for but never knew you needed. Does that make sense? It might once you read it.

    Thank you for all the wonderful comments and kudos, and thank you all for reading. I'm sorry I haven't gotten back to a lot of you yet, I'm going to get on that right this moment. Thank you!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Yelena beat her fists against the reinforced glass over and over. Her hands were sore and her knee burned but she continued to pound. “Let me out!” She screamed, her voice hoarse and broken from her relentless protestations. Yelena had been beating, screaming and shouting for the last hour but her desperate demands had fallen on deaf ears. She was alone in the brig, but there was no way that was stopping her. Nothing would stop her. She had to know. She had to know if Kate was safe, if she was alive.

    “Let me out god damn it,” she growled in frustration. “Hello? Hello?!” Her voice reverberated around the inside of her cell, her words and growls bouncing off every hard surface, reminding her that she really was alone. She’d been left there alone. Torn from Kate after hauling her onto the transport and begging for someone, anyone to help them. Restrained whilst she watched despairingly as they worked on her. Shackled and imprisoned as soon as they were back on solid ground. Left to her own thoughts, her fears. She feared the worst of course. Kate’s pulse had gone from thready to practically non-existent within the space of a few moments. By the time she’d got Kate on the transport, it was barely there at all.

    She’d fought back when they’d tried to tear her away from Kate. It had only made things worse. She was disorientated from the blast, her body was cold, spent and exhausted from their fight, and her knee felt as if it were hanging on by a thread. She couldn’t, she just couldn’t do it. When they dragged her away from her, when the baton struck her in the stomach, when she doubled over, when they drove her to her knees and then to the floor, when they bound her hands; she couldn't fight back. Because as much as they could tear her from Kate, Yelena couldn’t tear her eyes away from the pale, seemingly lifeless body of her girlfriend that lay still upon the QuinJet’s floor. She couldn’t look away as they cut through Kate’s combat suit. She couldn’t look away as they started CPR. She couldn’t stop the tears from escaping as Kate’s body moved like a rag-doll under the force of their compressions, an image that would forever be burned into Yelena’s mind’s eye.

    By the time they’d touched down, Kate was on a gurney and Yelena had been bound to one of the chairs at the back end of the jet. All she could do was watch as they took her away. She knew that she couldn’t help her in that moment, but how she wanted to hold her. How she wanted to press her lips against her cheeks, how she wanted to see those violet eyes, hear her dumb American voice. She would do anything to hear that voice again, to see those eyes, to feel Kate’s skin against hers. But she might not, ever. That might have been it. The last of it, their last moments together. And Yelena had to sit in a cell with the knowledge that her greatest fears had been realised. Everything Kate had promised her she wasn’t, she’d become. Everything she’d feared that she could do to Kate, the harm she knew she was capable of causing, she’d caused it. Because she was dangerous, and Kate might have paid the ultimate price.

    Yelena had no idea where she was, where she’d been taken. Presumably to another outpost nearby, but she knew who was holding her. It was S.H.I.E.L.D. Of course it was S.H.I.E.L.D. They would treat her like a criminal, they would pin this on her, and they would use it against her and her family. They would use it against anyone who was different, or didn’t see eye to eye. And they would take no responsibility for what happened to Kate. Yelena growled and hammered against the glass with unspent anger and frustration. She needed out. She needed to be with her, she needed to know. Was she still breathing? Was she awake? Were her eyes open? Was she asking for Yelena? Or had the worst happened? Yelena bit back her tears and hammered harder against the glass. She didn’t know who she hated more, S.H.I.E.L.D. or herself.

    “I swear to god if you leave me in here, I will kill all of you!”

    “Those kinds of threats aren’t going to help your case, I’m afraid,” came a voice from the darkness. It was a voice Yelena knew well. She was used to it sounding off in her ear, but for once, Yelena’s heart soared at the sound of Carol Danvers’ voice. Finally, someone who could vouch for her. Someone who understood that she needed to be with her. “Carol? Carol, how is Kate?” Yelena asked, desperately. “Carol, I need to get out of here.” The Avenger stepped forward and stopped just in front of the glass that separated the two women. Her face was dark, grim. Her eyes were tired and filled with a sadness that scared the Russian. “Kate is in surgery,” Carol said quietly.

    “She-she is?” Yelena just about managed. Surgery, that was good right? That meant that they got her heart beating, that she was saveable. Fixable.

    “Yes,” Carol nodded and offered Yelena the smallest of smiles, “They’ve managed to stabilise her.”

    Yelena felt light headed. She had to lean on the glass as relief flooded her body. Her cheeks puffed as she attempted to ward off another wave of tears that wanted to take hold. She was stable. That was good, that was really good. “I couldn’t find a pulse… I was…” Worried felt like the understatement of the century, so she didn’t say it. Words couldn’t really do the way she was feeling justice, so she simply chose to abandon them.

    “I understand,” Carol crossed her arms and leant against the glass. “I’m sorry I couldn’t come sooner, but I came as soon as I had news.”

    “Thank you,” Yelena whispered earnestly. Thanking the gods for Carol Danvers was not something Yelena did too often, but it was something she was certainly doing in that moment. “I have to be there, Carol. I have to be with her.”

    Carol nodded as if she understood but her soft, apologetic smile told Yelena that perhaps the Avenger wasn’t there to offer her what she needed. “She’ll be in surgery for quite some time, Yelena.”

    The Russian crossed her arms across her chest tightly. To Carol it might have looked like she was simply mirroring the Avenger’s stance out of habit, but really Yelena was trying to hold it all in. Her ragged breathing, her tears, her insatiable need to scream into the void. “But when she is out?” Yelena reasoned, perhaps foolishly, “Maybe I could-.” “You know I can’t,” Carol said with regret. “I’m sorry,” she added softly. Yelena wanted to believe she meant it.

    The ex-Widow rested her head against the glass forlornly. She felt so out of control, she had done for far too long. Under the influence of Leviathan, she’d had so little control but it had felt as if every decision, every want, every urge had been her own. That’s what had made it so potent, so deceptive. In her mind, Kate had been the only thing standing in the way of her total liberation. Kate had been the one thing that still had control over her, and to be truly free, Yelena had needed to sever it.

    “Do they think she is going to be okay?” It was a question that was far scarier to ask than it should have been. The weight of responsibility was crushing as her anger began to subside. “I think so,” Carol smiled gently, her eyes still tired and full of sorrow. She felt for them, for the both of them, and Yelena took comfort in that smile. She had never been very good though, at receiving the sympathy of others. It was a weakness, or at least it felt weak, and Yelena had to swallow, hard, to stop another flood of tears from claiming her. “How is my mother?” Yelena asked, suddenly desperate to change the subject and escape Carol’s pitying gaze.

    Carol’s face lightened momentarily and Yelena found that she could breathe once more. “Just a few minor injuries,” The Avenger reassured, “But she took a pretty big knock to the head so they want to monitor her overnight, just in case.”

    “Good, that’s good,” Yelena nodded hastily. Her mother would be okay, she knew that she would. She’d seen many battles and it was going to take a lot more than a crash landing to finish the ex-Widow off for good. People as smart as Melina died in their sleep. “I can see if she’s well enough to come and see yo-.”

    “No.” Yelena blurted out, a little too abruptly. She wasn’t ready, she wasn’t nearly ready to see her mother. The things that she had said, the things that she had done, they had been awful things. And what had made them worse was that they were things that she had thought in the past, before any of this had happened. Things she’d questioned about her mother, about their relationship. She had felt abandoned, betrayed, unloved. She had felt all those things and she had thought so many times about the ways in which she would tell her, if she ever saw her again. The ways that she would make her mother hurt, like she had. And so, she wasn’t ready, not just yet, for her own words still rang in her ears, and she was sure that they echoed in her mother’s too. “No, thank you. She should rest.”

    “She will want to see you, Yelena,” the Avenger reasoned as she sought the Russian’s eyes, but they eluded her. Carol was attempting to call the blonde on her bullshit. The blonde wasn’t going to let her.

    “She needs to rest,” Yelena murmured and the two stubborn women fell into an even more stubborn silence. The ex-Widow could feel Carol’s eyes upon. They were studying her. Her tear streaked, bloodstained face and her torn and sullied combat suit. She cut a defeated figure as she leant against reinforced glass, grateful for the support it gave her. Now she’d quit her beating and hollering, the adrenaline was beginning to seep from her system, and she was beginning to become more and more aware of her body’s own protestations. Everything ached. Everything was tender. Kate Bishop had really beaten the shit out of her. If the circumstances hadn’t been so dire Yelena Belova would be feeling pretty proud right now. The smallest, saddest laugh escaped her as she felt it. She was still pretty fucking proud. “How are you feeling?” Carol asked after a moment. It was probably one of the stupidest questions of all time. What did Carol expect her to say, ‘fuckin’ great’? Yelena’s gaze flashed to Carol’s and finally their eyes met. “Do you really want me to answer that?” Yelena asked darkly.

    Carol set her jaw and stared right back at the ex-assassin. “I would prefer it if you did,” she said matter-of-factly. Trust Carol Danvers to be the utmost professional. Trust her to think that now was the time to rise above it, to behave as if Yelena meant something to her, as if her wellbeing meant something to her. All she had ever been was a tool, a weapon to bring in line and they had used Kate to make that happen. What an idiotic question. How was she feeling? How did Carol think she would be feeling? Her girlfriend was in surgery, her mother in a hospital, and her real mother had... Yelena had to stop. Her thoughts were spiralling and she had to stop before... She wasn’t ready to think about that, and so Yelena chewed against the inside of her cheek and gave Carol an answer she hoped would be enough to appease. “My knee is not good,” she offered. Carol raised an eyebrow. It wasn’t the answer she’d been expecting but she’d take it. It was something after all.

    “MCL?”

    Yelena ‘hmmed’ quietly. “Most likely.”

    “We need to get that looked at.”

    “I agree but right now you have me in a cage.” Their eyes met once more and this time Yelena did nothing to hide her annoyance.

    To add to Yelena’s building frustration, Carol only offered her empty apologies in response. “I’m sorry,” she said gently, “I am working on getting you out, I promise you.” But to Yelena, they felt like empty words. Even if Carol was working to free Yelena, it meant nothing until she could see Kate, until she could be with her. Until then, it was just time wasted. Where had Carol been? Why hadn’t she been with Kate in the first place? Why hadn’t she helped? Yelena let out a rueful laugh that told Carol she took very little comfort in her promises, and yet the Avenger persisted. “How are you feeling, other than your knee?” “You have no proof the antidote worked, do you? So, are you worried about my wellbeing?” Yelena asked as her eyes narrowed with suspicion, “Or are you worried about who’s in the driving seat?” It was a question Yelena had already asked herself a thousand times. She was almost sure she knew the answer but there was always going to be a small part of her that wondered, what if? There always had been, ever since the Red Room, and it didn’t surprise her that Carol might be questioning it now.

    “Both,” Carol confirmed, it was foolish and yet noble, and Yelena could have smiled at the woman’s honesty if Kate hadn’t been fighting for her life.

    “If I were not me, there is no way I would tell you.”

    Carol smiled back at her happily as the low light of the brig shone brightly in her eyes. “I think you’re you.”

    Yelena couldn’t help the involuntary eye roll. “I think you are naïve,” she muttered. Carol nodded with a pout. “Perhaps. And the other thing?”

    “My wellbeing?” Yelena scoffed? “What is it that you want me to say?”

    The Avenger shrugged. “Anything you want?”

    Yelena had to bite back her anger. “You think that will help me? Talking to you, sharing my feelings? Or is that just therapy for you?”

    “I just want to make sure that you’re okay.”

    “Okay?!” The Russian growled and something in her snapped. She knew Carol meant well, she knew that she was doing her job and she knew that somewhere deep-down Carol just needed to know that her friend was going to be okay, but Yelena just couldn’t take it. “You think that I could be okay?” Yelena stabbed at her own chest as tears caught in her throat. “Kate’s heart stopped beating. What part of that is ‘okay’?” She demanded as she puffed her cheeks and fought against the rage that was rising within her.

    “My mother almost died; I did that, I did that,” She stabbed again violently against her sternum. “Kate’s mother too.” Oh god, Kate’s mother, what was she going to say to Kate’s mother? The deal with Leviathan, her mother, the poison. “I could have killed her, like I killed those people at that facility. Like I killed those guards at the hospital in Long Island. I killed them all, without a care. So, you tell me Carol, what part of this could possibly be ‘okay’?” Yelena’s breath blazed angrily against the glass as her eyes bore into Captain Marvel’s. She’d lost her temper, but she wasn’t done.

    “Yelena, you-.”

    “I am a weapon, Carol,” the Russian spat furiously. “I always have been and I always will be. So don’t talk to me about feelings. I will always be a danger. I will always put people in danger.”

    “You didn’t do anything, Yelena. You’re not responsible”

    “Then why am I in this god damn cage?!” Yelena raged as she hammered her fists again against the reinforced glass that was keeping her captive. She was losing it. Kate could be dead and she was a prisoner. “Why can I not be with her, Carol? I need to be with her.” “I know,” Carol tried to sooth, “And I’m sorry. But until we can categorically prove that-“ “Categorically prove?!” Yelena wanted to fight, she wanted to tear the whole place down. Sure, Yelena was the weapon but it was S.H.I.E.L.D.’s formula that had turned the safety off. “This is your fault! S.H.I.E.L.D. did this. If they had not been-.”

    “I’m sorry Yelena but they don’t see it that way,” Carol explained regretfully. You’d have thought that a woman with earth shattering super powers would have more sway over small men in polyester suits, but god forbid the higher ups in S.H.I.E.L.D. would actually listen to a woman who spoke reason. They only really cared about protecting themselves, and their reputations. A bitter and jaded laugh escaped Yelena. They didn’t even care about what happened to Kate, not really. They simply cared about covering up the consequences of their own ineptitude, and that meant letting Yelena take the fall. She was a weapon after all, just like her sister. The mistake was Carol’s for trusting her in the first place. “Fuck them,” Yelena hissed, “ Fuck them. I should have known. Why did I ever think they could be trusted after the way they treated her? The way they turned on her.” Carol’s face softened as she looked upon the Russian affectionately. “Because you don’t work for S.H.I.E.L.D. You work for her and you work with us. W e’re a team.” Yelena shook her head and sniffed to hold back the tears. A team that let Kate go alone, to Alaska. What kind of team was that? “We are not a team, Carol. You and I are not friends. I would not die for you.” Their eyes met, hazel and hazel. Yelena would have been lying if she’d said that she hadn’t found hurt there, in Carol’s eyes. She’d also have been lying if she said that she didn’t regret inflicting that hurt, but she was angry, and she was so close to breaking she wondered if there was any coming back from this. Even if Kate wasn’t dead, even if she recovered, could they be the same? Could Kate still love her? Even if she didn’t, Yelena could never leave her, it was who she was now, it was who she came to the Avenger to be. Her protector.

    “I came for her, to die for her, Carol. Not you,” Yelena said, her voice quieter than it had been. Yelena was beginning to feel heavy. The adrenaline from the fight was leaving her. Her anger and her rage was exhausting. Her despair, consuming. “And you used that. You used the way that I felt to gain my loyalty. You knew from the start.” Yelena sniffed again. Her head was pounding, her heart and chest were tight and the tears that weighed heavy at the very edges of her hazel eyes threatened to break against her cheeks. “Would you die for her Carol?” Yelena asked as her lower lip trembled.

    Carol simply smiled at her sadly. She wanted to offer Yelena more, but she couldn’t, or wouldn’t. Yelena didn’t know, she didn’t really want to. “We’re not in the business of laying down our lives for each other, Yelena. My job is to make sure we all avoid that.” “And yet you left Kate to do this by herself? When S.H.I.E.L.D. was responsible and now she is fighting for her life, Carol. She is twenty-four years old.” Yelena’s voice broke along with her resolve, “God damn it,” she cried as she slammed her fist painfully against the glass one final time before she slumped against it, her body battered and broken and then slid into a crumpled heap on the floor. Her head lolled and came to rest against the cool glass. It was soothing to the touch, and yet a reminder of her captivity.

    “Kate Bishop is more than capable and she’s going to recover from this. You both will.” “And what if she doesn’t?” Yelena whispered.

    “She will,” Carol said gently, with a comforting confidence. Her powers weren’t the only thing that made Carol Danvers ‘Captain Marvel’. It was her way with people, the way she commanded trust, loyalty, confidence. Entire galaxies entrusted their fate to Carol, Kate had done the same. In a way, so had Yelena when she agreed to Carol’s terms. The two shared a silence for some time. Yelena picked at the material that was pulled tight across her right knee. It had been such a good kick. Perfectly set up, perfectly timed, perfectly positioned. Just perfect. Kate had done so well. She had taken her emotion and channelled it. It had made her ruthless, deadlier, it had given her purpose and she truly had been a marvel.

    The Russian un-balled her hands painfully. They were battered and bruised from the fight, and the arrow wounds where blood had mixed with the antidote throbbed angrily against her palms. She wondered if Kate knew. If she knew that night hadn’t been the first time she’d freed Yelena from herself. With just a look Kate Bishop had reset the trajectory of Yelena’s life. With just a few words she’d challenged her over a pan of macaroni. With blind stubbornness she’d stood in her way, even after being told that to do so would be risking her own life. With her obstinate idealism she’d taken hold of something inside of Yelena and refused to let go.

    For all the times Yelena had risked her life, she’d never been close to death. Never been close enough to feel her serpent’s breath as the darkness took hold. But now that’s where Kate lay, her life hanging in the balance. Would she call her? Would she answer her riddles willingly? Or would she see flashes of her own life? Would she cling onto that place that she’d found inside Yelena, would she refuse to let go just like she always did?

    Were Kate’s thoughts of Yelena herself? Selfishly, the Russian hoped they were. Perhaps they were of the first time they’d truly held each other on Yelena’s birthday. How they’d clung to each other as she’d been overcome by tears. That night Kate had freed from her vulnerability.

    Could she see the moment that she freed her of her indecision as the blonde’s lips had brushed ever-so-gently against every freckle, when she’d adulated over every inch of soft skin and gentle curve for the first time. Or did she remember the moment she’d freed her from her own fears with just three words. Or the moment she freed her from her burden as she held her and loved her in that hotel room. Kate Bishop had freed Yelena countless times over, and Yelena just hoped above all hope that she carried that with her. That she would carry that back to her.

    “I will kill them,” Yelena whispered, her voice brittle with emotion as her heart tightened and her vision grew darker. “If she dies I will kill them. First, I will take away the one thing they love more than anything else in this world, and when they are at the very depths of their grief, when they are wishing for death, I will be there to grant it to them.” Yelena could practically feel Carol’s pained sigh. And really, she understood, she did. She knew that Carol was limited. Sure, she had powers, but did she truly have power? It was never that black or white. Demand entry to the facility, or demand access to science? How long would that have taken? Bulldoze her way in, and how quickly would she become the villain? Yelena knew that Carol would never intentionally choose to harm Kate, but that didn’t make her any less angry.

    The Avenger settled down next Yelena and leaned against the glass that separated them. “Yelena,” she said softly, “Right now, Fury and me are the only things standing between you and a one-way trip to the Raft. Please know that we only want to protect you.” A one-way trip , Yelena mused. “Maybe that is for the best.”

    “Now you’re just feeling sorry for yourself,” Carol smiled.

    “Can you blame me?” Yelena asked with all the exasperation she could muster and the Avenger could only shrug.

    “Not really.”

    Yelena looked to her hands once more. Her leather gloves had been discarded as soon as she needed to feel for Kate’s pulse. In a way she was glad, as they would have been a bitch to take off once the blood had well and truly dried. She had choked Kate with those hands, with her hands. Her strong fingers had closed tightly around her jugular, her palms had crushed against her windpipe as Kate had strained and fought and begged. And yet Yelena hadn’t let go, because of love. She hadn’t let go, because of her love for Kate, not despite it. Her love for Kate was her one weakness and all Yelena could think of in that moment was eradicating it. If she could just make Kate go away, if she could break the hold that the young woman had upon her, then maybe she could have been free. Yes, it was her love Kate that was her only weakness now. Kate had seen to banishing the rest. The fear, the burdens, the vulnerability, the trauma. All that was left was love, but love could be exploited above all, and Yelena knew that it would be. It had been so easy. Benny had done it, her mother had done it, even Carol had. They’d all wanted something from Yelena and they’d all used Kate to get it. What happened when someone came along who didn’t want anything from her, what happened when she came up against an enemy who only wanted her to suffer? What happened then, and what would happen to Kate? Perhaps a one-way trip would be better for the both of them in the long run. It would hurt in the present, but if it might guarantee at least Kate a future, then surely it was worth it.

    “I know what you’re thinking, you know?” Came Carol’s voice, quite unexpectedly, to tear Yelena from her thoughts.

    “Oh really?” Yelena said derisively. Of course, Carol thought that she knew what Yelena was thinking. That was probably the most Carol thing ever. Smug, all-knowing, condescending. Yelena had adjectives for days. “Lay it on me, oh omniscient one.” See? “You’re thinking that you’re going to leave. As soon as she’s well enough, you’re going to leave to protect her when in fact it’ll just make the both of you infinitely more miserable.” “Huh,” was all Yelena could manage. Perhaps Carol really was omniscient. Or perhaps she had a little more experience in this area than she left on. Captain Marvel had lived many lives, in many galaxies. Love and loss were synonymous with a life such as that. “You’ll throw yourself back into everything that makes you unhappy and you’ll slowly become the one thing you were terrified she’d see you as in the first place.” Carol’s voice was soft, and quiet and there something about it that resonated deep within Yelena. It was a voice of experience. A voice of someone who had experienced great sadness and Yelena felt a great weight lift from her shoulders. She was speaking to a friend.

    “Kate knew that I was a killer, Carol,” the Russian whispered sadly.

    “She knew your past and she loved you despite that. She loves you ,” Carol corrected and she was right, Kate did love her. There was no past tense. There wasn’t going to be any past tense. “That’s not going to change because of something you’re not responsible for.” Carol shuffled against the glass and turned to face her friend better. “Do you know how determined she was to save you? There was no way I was stopping her.”

    “You should have,” Yelena muttered but Carol was done fighting with her. “She was so angry. You should have seen her.” Yelena could practically hear the smile that had crept across Carol’s bright features. She could hear it as loudly as the pride in her voice. Her pride in Kate. “She cursed at me, for real.”

    The tightness in the Russian’s chest began to ease ever-so-slightly as the smallest of warm glows tugged at her aching heart. There was no way. Kate Bishop, her Kate Bishop cursing at Carol Danvers? The thought of it completely blew her mind. She really must have been so angry to do something so extreme, to do something so... Yelena Belova. She quickly realised that the warmth spreading through her chest was a heady mixture of pride and affection, and Yelena welcomed it. “At you ? She cursed at you ?” The blonde asked in disbelief as she tried to turn awkwardly to take in the Avenger. Her body groaned its displeasure at her. “Yup,” came Carol’s matter-of-fact response as she leaned her forehead against the glass. “Wow,” Yelena afforded herself the smallest of laughs, “She’s probably been spiralling over that ever since.”

    Carol shrugged nonchalantly. “I doubt it. Getting you back was the only thing that mattered.” Their eyes met momentarily through the glass. Carol was doing it again, giving her that look, that earnest stare that could instil confidence in anyone. Suddenly Yelena felt her chest tighten once more. She should have felt something else, she should have been comforted by Kate’s laser focus on getting her back, but she wasn’t. She couldn’t imagine what it must have felt like, to have the carpet pulled from under you like that. From the grief for her near- death mother, the fear and the anxiety of it all, to then discovering that the person responsible for all that pain was the one person who was supposed to be able to shelter and protect you from it. To discover that you could be on the verge of losing everything, your past, your present, your future. The thought of Kate going through that was no comfort to Yelena. “I know what it’s like,” Carol continued as she commanded Yelena’s gaze with her soft, empathetic tones, “To walk away from someone, to wish you hadn’t.” She smiled sadly and Yelena felt her head rest against the glass of its own accord. They were both there now, just the glass separating two pairs of tired hazel eyes. “Don’t walk away from her,” Carol said, it was practically a whisper. “The next few months will be tough, this is when she’ll need you most.”

    But would she? Or would she simply serve as a constant reminder of all that pain. Could Yelena touch her again with hands that tried to coerce the life from her? Could she kiss her again with lips that had uttered such terrible things? Would the pain not be a hinderance? Kate Bishop was a bundle of sunshine, that was for sure, but she had lived her own trauma before, she just hid it better than most. She could recover from this, she didn’t need anyone’s help, especially Yelena’s.

    The Russian tore her eyes from Carol’s perceptive gaze and chewed upon the inside of her cheek. “She is strong,”

    “She is,” Carol pondered thoughtfully for a moment, “But she’s even stronger with you.” Yelena raised a sceptical eyebrow. “I do not think you give her enough credit. You should have seen her out there, she was…” The Russian took a moment to find the right word. Sure, Kate had been ruthless, brutal, driven, but she had also been elegant, smart and brave. She had been all those things, she had been, “Spectacular.”

    “I don’t doubt it. But,” Carol grimaced a little, as if she were pained to utter her next words, “On top of the internal bleeding, it’s likely her hip was fractured by the blast, the way she fell? She’ll need another surgery and a lot of rehab.”

    Oh. Oh shit. The news hit Yelena like an armoured Humvee hitting a 1200cc Bonneville. If you don’t know, that’s hard. A hip fracture was complicated, recovery was lengthy and full recovery was not guaranteed, even with all the resources S.H.I.E.L.D. had at their disposal. What would that mean? If Kate couldn’t fight again, if she couldn’t fire a bow with the same accuracy as before, if she couldn’t be part of this team that was so integral to who she was, integral to the future that she saw for herself. The recovery period alone would be isolating. Weeks in bed, maybe months until she could walk under her own power again, even longer before she could begin to think about getting back out into the field. All because she put herself between Yelena and her mother. All to protect her. That was supposed to be Yelena’s job and she’d failed. If she left her now, would she be failing her again or would she be sparing her each painful reminder?

    Would Yelena’s touch be a comfort or would Kate remember Yelena’s hands against her windpipe? Would Yelena’s steadying arms at the archery range give Kate strength or would they remind her of how they conspired to drive two arrows into her flesh. And when Kate heard her words of love and gentle encouragement, would she feel Yelena’s meaning or would she question every motive? Would she trust that they were Yelena’s words? Could she trust her fully ever again? It would take a leap of faith, one that Yelena wasn’t sure if she herself would ever be brave enough to make. But if anyone would make a leap, blindly with no thought of the consequences, Kate Bishop would.

    “You’re her partner,” Carol said, “Having you by her side, it’s important, but as her girlfriend it will be invaluable.” Yelena gaze lingered upon her hands once more. Omniscient Carol wins again. Yelena had been an idiot thinking she could keep her relationship with Kate from her boss. That’s why she’d hired her in the first place, right? She’d had it on good authority that Yelena had been in New York several times since her first visit in December. She’d also known that Yelena hadn’t come for any job. There were no contracts, no pay-for-kills. She’d come for Kate. She would book a room near Hell’s Kitchen and wait. Wait for her to put a foot wrong, to overstep, but she never did. She would drink in the shadows as Kate grilled bartenders for information. She would watch her from the rooftops as she kicked-ass in the alleyways below. She waited for the moment that Kate would need her, to keep her safe, but Kate never had. Things changed though, when Kate got her call-up from Carol. The stakes changed, and Carol knew that Yelena had been waiting long enough. She supposed she had Carol to thank for all of this, the good and the bad. The Avenger had given Yelena everything she’d wanted, but at what cost?

    “And you’re going to need her support too you know?” Carol added and Yelena scoffed ruefully at the thought. She was so used to managing her own pain that the thought hadn’t even occurred to her. Pain made you stronger, that was all she knew. It was what she lived by and it had gotten her through so much tragedy. She’d turned so much pain into so much more. Maybe together, she and Kate could do the same, maybe they would be stronger for it. “Because that knee is…wow,” Carol puffed her cheeks and shook her head. She was right, Yelena’s knee was fucked. Like, really fucked.

    “It is pretty big, isn’t it?” Yelena felt a smile pull teasingly at the corners of her mouth. “Big?” It was Carol’s turn to scoff in disbelief. “It’s a beach ball, bro.” Yelena couldn’t help it. She couldn’t help the wheezing laugh that escaped her. It was ridiculous. The whole thing. When you really thought about it, it was crazy beyond belief. She’d fallen in love at first sight. Who did that? Yelena had thrown her off a fucking roof and marched straight back up those steps and pointed her bow at her. Who did that? They’d made fighting their love language. Who did that? They’d almost killed each other in order to save each other. Who did that? They did. It was so very them and Yelena just couldn’t keep the laughter in. It was sweet relief to her bruised body and her aching heart. She just wished that Kate could have been there, to laugh with her, to lean into her, to kiss her tear-stained cheeks. They would have that, soon enough. Yelena had to hope. “What a mess,” the Russian sighed.

    “Well, you’re both alive,” Carol offered. Yes, Yelena had to hope that it stayed that way. “Just,” she whispered as her laughter receded and the visions of Kate’s ribs breaking under the force of the CPR returned.

    “They tell me Eleanor’s doing well,” Carol added. She knew that Yelena was spiralling, what she didn’t know was that Yelena already knew Eleanor was doing well. In fact, Yelena knew that Eleanor was doing more than well. Eleanor Bishop would make a full recovery. But Carol couldn’t know. She couldn’t know about the deal Eleanor made with Leviathan, and neither could Kate. Not any time soon anyways. That would be a mess that Yelena would have to clean up herself.

    “That is very good news,” Yelena nodded stoically.

    “Is it though?” Carol said with a playful smirk and Yelena found herself smiling again “Don’t make me like you, Carol,” Yelena said affectionately.

    “I wouldn’t dream of it,” retorted the Avenger, her smirk now a fully formed grin. “You and Kate, do you make each other happy?” Carol asked, quite unexpectedly.

    Yelena blinked. Bar the last seventy-two hours? And maybe Christmas of course, Yelena was sure their relationship could post some pretty impressive net happiness numbers. “I think so,” Yelena confirmed quietly.

    “Good, you above all people deserve that. Try not to spend the next twenty-four hours convincing yourself otherwise, okay?” There was no way Yelena could guarantee that. “In the meantime, I’m working on getting you out of here. It might be a slow process but I’m going to do my best.” Yelena knew it to be true.

    “Thank you,” The Russian said earnestly, and she was truly grateful. If she had to spend hours on end negotiating Carol’s release with some idiot men in suits, she didn’t think she could do it, and she would surely cause some kind of international incident. “No problem. Oh, and your father will be arriving at 1500 hours,” Carol smirked as she dropped that bombshell.

    Yelena grimaced at the thought. Her father? Here? This was not going to be a good mix. Sure, entertaining for everyone else involved but surely if you wanted a situation to improve, you don’t invite the Red Guardian. “Oh god, and I thought I’d already hit rock bottom.” Carol laughed a little too easily at Yelena’s despair and the Russian scowled. “There was no way I was keeping him away with you in a cell and your mother in a hospital bed. But he's promised to behave and getting him clearance we much easier than I expected.” “Oh really?”

    “Yeah. S.H.I.E.L.D. rate him at threat level zero, so...”

    “Wow...” Yelena balked; he would hate that. This was amazing. “I cannot wait to tell him.” “Please don’t,” pleaded Carol, knowing full well that telling Alexei he was threat level zero would automatically elevate him to a threat level three and a half, at least. Yelena smiled a non-committal, downturned smile. “I’ll think about it.” “You think about it whilst I go and to talk to a few more asshole bureaucrats,” Carol quipped as she hauled herself off the floor with a few more groans than you’d think necessary for a super-powered super-human. "And maybe I can get you something for that knee.” “It is fine.” The Russian shrugged. Pain only makes us stronger, remember? “It is not fine,” Carol insisted scoldingly. “If we leave it much longer that thing is going to have its own gravitational pull so stay down there, okay?” Carol had turned into a parent and Yelena hated. She was pointing and frowning and saying all the irritatingly sensible things that a parent would say. The Russian scowled but made no move to get back up to her feet. Because maybe, just maybe, like any good parent, Carol was right.

    The Avenger paused for a moment and then brushed her fingertip against the glass. “As soon as I have news on Kate, you’ll be the first to know,” she reassured gently. Yelena turned her gaze upward and smiled gratefully. “Thank you,” she said softly. She just had to had to hope.

    “And for what it’s worth,” Carol continued, “I-er-I’m sorry about your mother, Nadija.” Yelena’s eyes fell from Carol’s and back to the wounds that marked her palms. She gritted her teeth and her jaw ticked. “It’s okay,” Yelena murmured indifferently. “She is not my mother.” And that was the end of it. Whoever she was, whatever she was to Yelena, she wasn’t a mother. She wasn’t the woman from that room, she wasn’t the woman from that passport photo, she was someone else entirely. Perhaps Yelena would never know who she was, perhaps Yelena would never see her again, and perhaps that was for the best, because Yelena would make her pay for what she did to Kate, for what she wanted to do to her. Even if she really was her mother.

    The Russian turned again to look up at Carol Danvers, beacon of hope and light for the Universe. She was just a woman really. Flawed and imperfect in many ways but with a goodness at her very centre. Yelena hated it, well, not really, but liked to pretend. “But Carol,” Yelena continued, just as the older woman had turned to leave her alone in the brig once more, “You are my friend”.

    “I know,” Carol smiled gently.

    She had just been so angry. Yelena was on the brink of losing everything, every good thing in her life that she’d managed to scrape back after losing Natasha. She was just so angry, and so very afraid. “I’m just-.”

    “I know,” Carol said again, more firmly this time. She understood. Over the years Carol had grown used to being the person others blamed. It was easy to blame the person with the most perceived power, Yelena had done it countless times. She’d blamed Carol for Natasha’s death when in fact, Natasha had died for her. She had made the choice, so that Yelena may live. So that countless others may live. Kate had made the very same choice that night. “I love her,” Yelena whispered as her head came to rest against the glass gently. It was the first time she’d said the words out loud. She promised herself it wouldn’t be the last. “I know,” smiled Carol. “I know”.

    212-528-6138: And I have a lot of spare time, so consider it taken care of. SHIELDLA273: I will be the judge of that. I am now your official taste tester. 212-528-6138: You’ve been that for a while now babe.

    SHIELDLA273: No, it-

    212-528-6138: Yelena, it’s soccer. Get out of here with your European fancibilites. SHIELDLA273: That is not a word, Kate, that is not a word.

    212-528-6138: It is now.

    212-528-6138: Uh huh, it’s really good.

    SHIELDLA273: Good.

    212-528-6138: So good, that maybe we should do it again some time. Like… tomorrow? SHIELDLA273: If I say yes to the tag tonight, I will be in surgery tomorrow but I will call after.

    212-528-6138: … awesome. I should go, I think they’ve kicked off already but um, this is has been… you sound good and you being good means the world to me.

    SHIELDLA273: I am, I am feeling good. Most of the time I am feeling good. 212-528-6138: I haven’t been able to stand the idea of you not being okay and me not being able to help you and I-

    SHIELDLA273: Kate, it is okay. Sometimes no one can fix you but yourself. And I will admit, I am not entirely fixed but I’m not entirely broken. I think being with you might help put those final pieces back together.

    212-528-6138: I will do anything that you need me to do.

    SHIELDLA273: Gladly. Goodbye Kate.

    212-528-6138: Goodbye Yelena. I love you.

    SHIELDLA273: You too.
