    Metamorphosis: Reprise Chapter Notes Hello! It’s been a little while. Work has been tough and has sapped my brain like no one’s business. But I’m back!

    Thank you for your comments and kudos. Thank you for reading and thank you for your patience. This chapter is a bit of a mixed bag of emotions. Enjoy!

    See the end of the chapter for more notes Kate stared at her phone. She’d been doing it a lot the last few days. Since Yelena had been granted cellphone access, most of Kate’s waking hours were spent waiting with bated breath for her girlfriend’s next message. Of course, Yelena had never been the chattiest over text. She wasn’t prolific with technology as it was. Yes, she could hack her way into the securest of government facilities, but having next to no social media presence had always been a personal choice as well a professional one. ‘I don’t like people,’ she would say, ‘I don’t care about the insignificant machinations of their lives’. Of course, that’s exactly why Kate was on every social media channel available to her. Insignificant machinations were her jam, and so they were the very definition of ‘opposites attract’. Normally Kate loved that, it was their thing, but not today. Today, she wished that her girlfriend had an unhealthy reliance on her cellphone. Today, Kate wished Yelena was a real life addict. But alas, she was not. Sometimes Yelena would respond to Kate within seconds or minutes, if it was mid- conversation or she was taken by the moment. Sometimes hours would pass, sure, but never days. Since Yelena had been granted cellphone rights, a ‘Good morning, Darling,’ had greeted Kate when Yelena woke on the West Coast, and a ‘Sweet dreams,’ would carry Kate to sleep on the East, but now...now it was midday, and Kate’s phone sat undisturbed upon the arm of her chair. No morning greeting, no call, nothing.

    Which perhaps, on a normal day, Kate would be fine with, but today wasn’t a normal day, today was the day that Yelena was coming home. She would finally be home, with Kate, where she belonged. Yes, with a tracker, but she’d be home. When the two had had spoken about the Russian’s return the morning before, Yelena had been a little vague on the details. She hadn’t known when she was leaving or getting in and she hadn’t known if she was being escorted or left to her own devices, but that was yesterday. Surely she must have known something by now.

    Kate had tried calling her but to no avail. She’d texted once, twice and then thrice. She’d tried Carol but the Avenger had been frustratingly unreachable. So, slowly and unfortunately quite surely, what was supposed to be the most exciting day of the grandest proportions, was turning into a rather torturous one. Had something happened? Was Yelena really coming back to her? Carol’s silence worried Kate, for sure, but perhaps Carol had gone to fetch the Russian herself, perhaps they were just in the air with no service. Perhaps everything was fine and she was worrying incessantly for no reason.

    Kate sighed heavily as she shifted in the over-padded armchair and glanced at her phone again. Maybe her signal was bad. Maybe if she turned it off and on again, maybe... she sighed again, heavier this time. She’d been so excited. SO prepared.

    The Eurovision party had been ordered for, and all the food was arriving a little later in the day. She had the recipes ready, timings down, and her little helpers had been prepped. Of course, she’d also done a little preparation of… well, herself, because it really had been a while. Being in bed for weeks kind of strips away your desire for self-care. The willpower to shower goes out the window, let alone the wish to style your hair or put on a little make up, but with Yelena coming home, it felt like the right time. Despite her injuries, despite the pain that more than lingered, Kate above all else wanted to be touched by her girlfriend. She wanted rough fingertips against soft skin, she wanted strong hands in her hair, gentle lips against hers. She wanted to be held and she wanted to feel that connection again. The one that had sparked into life on that rooftop. The one that sustained them, the one that saved them. It burned brighter than her love for anything else. But it wasn’t something to simply be admired from afar, to bask and take comfort in like the high heat of the midday sun, it was something she needed to be consumed by, utterly and completely. And with that in mind, Kate made sure to shave her legs and pretty much everywhere else, because let’s face it, if she wants to be consumed, she’s gotta be a snack.

    Kate sighed another incredibly put out sigh. It was audible and for good reason. Where were her minions? Midday normally meant that America was out of her virtual classes but the multiversal traveler was yet to make an appearance in the rec room, and Kamala, who was normally kicking back with her on the couch or very graciously fixing Kate a snack, was missing in action. Kate shook her head, and grabbed her phone. Her brain needed to be occupied and stat. Left to its own devices, it would almost certainly spiral further than it already had. And so, Kate began to type away into their group chat. It had originally been set up so that the girls could arrange shifts to come keep Kate company, or bring her drinks or snacks or whatever she needed. It was now mainly used to chat shit. Of course, Kate would still demand her minions bring her snacks, and for the most part they agreed. When someone was so decrepit they had to use a walker, bringing them a snack wasn’t too much of a hardship.

    A few absent-minded scrolls through her timeline later and a notification popped up on Kate’s phone.

    America: You rang?

    Katy B: Where are you losers?

    ….

    Katy B: Hey. Minions. My thirst is unquenched.

    America: Then quench it, Princess.

    Katy B: I’ll quench you if you’re not careful.

    America: Kate, you can hardly walk.

    Katy B: It's only a matter of time.

    America: I believe that. But I have a question for you.

    Katy B: Is it... what canst I bringeth you, princess?

    America: No, it’s why the hell are you messaging me when you should be living out your full blown cottagecore lesbian fantasies with your girlfriend?

    Katy B: Err... I don’t have cottagecore lesbian fantasies…

    America: Dude, you showed me your Sims expansions. I’m not an idiot.

    Katy B: Well… I mean…

    America: You have a house, with the dogs...

    Katy B: I don’t know what you’re talking about and even if I did want to live out my perfectly normal and very PG-13 fantasies with my girlfriend, which I don’t by the way, she’s not even here yet and yes, if you hadn’t noticed I am getting pretty tetchy about it. America: She’s not here?

    Katy B: No. I haven’t heard from her at all.

    America: Then why am I digging around in the QuinJet that landed about thirty minutes ago. Katy B: The what that landed what?!

    “I found a cat!”

    Kate Bishop clutched at her chest in fright almost as tightly as she clutched at her walker. “America, jeez Louise, you scared me.”

    “That’s homophobic,” the girl smirked as she sat, reclined lazily in one of the QuinJet’s flight seats, with one large and very content looking ginger cat on her lap.

    “I-I- well, I-.” Kate was stuttering. Why was she stuttering? And how had it taken her that long to realise that the recently turned sixteen-year-old was so clearly queer? That’s what America meant, right? Kate thought that her constant shipping of ‘Bishova’, as she put it, was just a Gen-alpha thing. Turns out it was a gay thing, like a really gay thing. “Relax,” America smiled as she gave her new found companion a generous scratch behind the ears, “It’s a joke.”

    “I know and I kiss girls I’m just-.”

    “Looking for yours?” America asked, with a sympathetic raised brow.

    “Yeah, kinda,” Kate answered with a shrug and sigh that sent a few insolent hairs flying. “You have seen her, right?”

    “Nope,” Kate said, dejectedly. Surely Yelena wouldn’t have opted out of seeing Kate after so many weeks apart. Surely, Kate would be the priority. Surely, seeing Kate was the only reason to actually come home in the first place.

    “She didn’t come to you?”

    “Would I be looking for her if she had?” Kate snapped, a little too aggressively. America wasn’t poking fun, she was at just as much of a loss as Kate was. Being the biggest Bishova shipper around, this discourse must have been pretty devastating for her too. The younger woman raised her eyebrows and mouthed a slightly taken aback ‘yikes’, to the cat. Maybe America had been poking fun.

    “That judgy thing that your face is doing right now, I want it to stop please,” Kate grumbled, and so America sighed and motioned towards the flight seat next to her. She was right to do so, the cripple needed to sit, and fast. The trip from the rec room to the hangar bay was one of ill-advised length for someone who was only supposed to be making necessary journeys, and so Kate hobbled over to the younger woman and let herself flop down wearily. Fuck, her hip was already killing, and she hadn’t even started her daily physio. It would be fucked by the end of the day.

    “Well, from what I observed…” Observed being a synonym for ‘got bored in class and started snooping around on the complex’s CCTV system’, “They got back like an hour ago. You really didn’t know?”

    “No. I didn’t.” A glum Kate sank further into her seat. “Why wouldn’t she tell me she was home?” The brunette pouted. All Yelena had needed to do was reply to one of Kate’s texts. It wouldn’t have been that hard. Just a moment to reassure her had surely been within the blonde’s power, which begged the question. Why? Why hadn’t Yelena told her? America practically recoiled and held her new friend tightly in her arms. “Don’t put me in the middle of this whole thing.”

    But Kate’s mind had already moved on, leaps and bounds. “And wait a hot minute, you said ‘they’. Who’s they?” Kate demanded. America preferred this line of questioning. “Your girl. Carol and er, a guy I’ve never met.”

    Kate looked at her friend blankly. Whole lotta use she was proving to be. “That could be nearly anyone on the planet. You’re not exactly from this dimension.”

    “No shit,” America shrugged nonchalantly and went back to fussing the cat. He/she or they were very into it but all Kate could think about suddenly was this man. Who was he? Where had he come from? Was he S.H.I.E.L.D.? Was he there to make sure Yelena behaved? Was HE her tracker? Did this man have to follow Yelena everywhere she went? What would this mean for their sexy evening times?

    “What did he look like?” Kate asked, with desperation a little evident in her voice. Was she over-reacting? Quite possibly. Did she give a shit? No. She wanted her girlfriend back. She’d waited actual months. MONTHS. Sure, they’d been apart previously but it had been different. Completely different. This had been... hard, to say the least.

    “Bald,” America explained, “Fashion forward fisherman. Gnarly scars on his eye... like a... cat scrat-.” America eyed the fluffball in her arms with sudden and quietly terrified suspicion.

    Bald, gnarly eye... fisherman? “Fury!” Of course, it was Fury. The mystery man from Outerspace. THE Nick Fury. But Yelena had said that he’d been absent, hadn’t she? Clearly absent no longer. That was a good thing, right? Fury must have secured her release along with Carol, but why the hell was he marching Yelena off a jet and away from Kate’s very ready and waiting arms.

    America blinked up at Kate, clearly confused at the mention of the Colonel’s name. “Uhhh, what do you want, a synonym?”

    “No, Mr Fury, I want my goddamn girlfriend back!” Kate bellowed with frustration and America clutched in alarm at her new found ginger friend. It was clear that Kate had lost all patience and become almost one hundred percent non-sensical. She didn’t care though, she only cared about one thing. Yelena. It was her desire to see her girlfriend that dragged her from the flight-seat, despite the growing discomfort in her hip. It was that desire that clutched at her walker and marched her legs towards the QuinJet’s ramp.

    “Kate? Kate, stop.” Came America’s pleading voice.

    “Nope,” the older woman shook her head stubbornly as she hauled herself down the ramp and into the hangar bay below.

    Surprisingly strong and well accessorised hands grabbed her walker as America Chavez put herself between Kate and the hangar bay doors. Kate was met with the warmest and most sympathetic pair of brown eyes. The cat had been left behind and now Kate Bishop was America Chavez’s only care in the world. Fuck this girl was annoying, and fuck it if Kate Bishop loved her a little too much.

    “Kate, just chill, for a second,” America soothed softly, as a hand found hers. “Yelena’s home, okay? And she’s agreed to some complicated shit to make it happen. I’m sure they’re just signing papers or whatever.”

    “With Nick Fury?” Kate asked skeptically. She didn’t like it. Whatever it was, she didn’t like it. Maybe he was saving the day, but maybe he was involving her in some deeper S.H.I.E.L.D. shit that neither of them wanted to be involved in anymore. Deeper shit that could get her in trouble all over again, or worse, get her killed.

    America cringed apologetically. “Again, I have no idea who that is.”

    “Nick Fury doesn’t just sign papers, okay?” And although Kate knew that she might be falling into the realms of hysteria, she also knew that for the most part, she was right. Nick Fury didn’t just turn up on Earth to sign papers. There was more going on here than met the eye, but she’d be ready and willing to forget all that if she could just see Yelena again. Like, now. “If she was coming home early, why didn’t she tell me?”

    “Maybe there’s stuff happening that’s outside of her control,” America reasoned, offering Kate the most sympathetic of smiles. “Maybe she’s just trying to protect you from it.” As logical as that reasoning sounded, Kate did not like the sound of it at all. Because in fact, it only served to compound her worries. Fury wasn’t just here for a paper signing, this was more than that. Maybe a larger deal of some sort, something that was part of Fury’s bigger plan. Natasha Romanoff had always been central to Fury’s schemes, was he pressing for Yelena to be much the same? Perhaps they were hashing out a plan to take down Leviathan together, or maybe in return for her freedom, Fury had demanded Yelena pledge her unwavering service. None of the scenarios bombarding Kate’s already hysterically fragile mind were filling her with much confidence... but there was one thing she was confident about. Whatever the scenario, or whatever the deal, Yelena Belova did not need to protect Kate from it. She was pretty sure she’d already proven herself in that department. “I don’t need protecting,” Kate mumbled her brow furrowed and her lips downturned into an unhappy pout. Had she mentioned that she just wanted to see her girlfriend again? “Hey, Ladyhawk.”

    America smiled softly as she teased a begrudging “Yes...?" from Kate’s lips. America Chavez could be irritatingly endearing for a sixteen-year-old. She was cool and disarming and empathetic, and had her shit together like no other sixteen-year-old Kate knew. In contrast, when Kate was sixteen, sure she was medaling at international competitions, but she was also vomming in the McDonalds parking lot after trying to replicate the Big Mac Challenge. Perhaps if America hadn’t been forced to grow up quite so fast, she could have found a happy medium.

    A grin tugged mischievously at the edges of America’s soft smile as her dark eyes twinkled and Kate didn’t like where this was going. “I hate to break it to you bu-“ “Oh, do one,” Kate snapped as she rolled her eyes and yanked her walker from America’s grasp dramatically. The younger woman’s grin grew and Kate found herself wanting to inflict some kind of punishment upon her. But, of course, she couldn’t because for one, America was still technically a child and two, that would only go to please America more. Her grin would grow and she’d gloat and take a wicked satisfaction in the fact that she’d managed to prod Kate until she broke.

    A cat’s meow caught them both off guard as the ginger cat from moments earlier sashayed its way down the boarding ramp of the QuinJet and joined them in the hangar. “Does the cat have a name?” Kate asked as the ginger fluffball began to rub its face masochistically against the cool, metal legs of Kate’s walker.

    “Name tag said Goose,” America shrugged.

    “Huh. Well Goose, welcome to Avengers HQ. I hope you like dogs. ”

    The hurried clunk of Kate’s walker echoed through the corridors. Was she overdoing it? One hundred percent, yes. Did she care at this moment? Absolutely not. Her unsteady feet would carry her to her girlfriend, if it was the last thing they did.

    Unlike the living quarters, Carol’s office was housed much deeper within the recently built complex; beyond the gym and labs and the war room. It was Carol’s sanctuary at the heart of the compound, hidden behind what felt like miles of corridors and elevators. A sanctuary that Kate was about to invade.

    The young Avenger jabbed at the elevator call button with impatience and leaned wearily against her walker. Everything ached. Sure, her hip pained her like bloody murder, that went without saying, but it was the way that nearly every other part of her body ached to compensate that surprised her. Her hands were on the verge of cramping from gripping her walker so tight, her forearms burned, and her shoulders felt like she’d spent a day on the battle ropes.

    The elevator dinged cheerily and Kate grumbled in deep dissatisfaction. ‘Who gave it the right?’ Kate thought as she shuffled inside the whizzing metal box.

    With a grim determination, she selected the basement level, leaned heavily against the elevator’s brushed metal walls with a puff of her cheeks, and began to descend. Once within the very depths of the complex the elevator doors slid open to reveal Carol’s office at the end of the hall. As with all offices within the Avenger complex, the walls weren’t walls at all, but a thick layer of bullet proof glass. Great for the aesthetic, but not so great for secrecy, especially in this case, because that’s when Kate saw her. Her heart leapt at the sight. There Yelena sat, her back to Kate. Her thick blonde hair, hair that Kate missed losing her fingers within, sat short; just above her shoulders. The Russian had clearly been running her own fingers through the blonde strands, as they sat unkept and unruly. Yelena was anxious and in turn, so was Kate, not just because of her girlfriend’s demeanor but for another reason. It wasn’t Carol that was sat behind Carol’s desk, no, in fact Carol was sat right next to Yelena. The person behind the desk was Nick Fury. The actual Nick Fury, and his gaze met hers. Shit, shit, shit. What was she doing? She knew from America’s description that it had been Nick Fury who’d accompanied Yelena off the QuinJet, she knew and still she’d stubbornly insisted on marching down there. For her girlfriend. Great work Kate, I’m sure Mr Fury will really look kindly upon you putting your desperate need to see Yelena Belova ahead of national security. What an idiot, what an absolute idiot. But now, she couldn’t escape. She couldn’t just let the elevator doors close. She shouldn’t just turn around. He had her in his sights, and so she needed to show conviction. She wasn’t weak, maybe just a little desperate, he could sympathise with that... right? RIGHT?!?

    With a defeated sigh, Kate Bishop gritted her teeth and determined to finish what she’d started. She just prayed that Yelena wouldn’t follow Fury’s gaze and turn to see her struggle. Unfortunately, as Yelena had a perception modifier of ten, Kate’s prayers were not answered as hazel eyes met violet once more, after nearly six weeks of waiting. Kate could have sworn her heart missed a beat. At least one, if not five or six. Because there she was. Yelena’s furrowed brow softened immediately and Kate wanted to run to her. She needed to close the distance between them. She needed to draw the blonde into her arms, capture her mouth with hers, lose her fingers within her hair blonde hair and pull, ever so gently. How Kate wanted to, and oh how she couldn’t, for her legs would never carry her there. No quicker had the Russian’s face softened than it turned to concern. Was it the walker? Kate supposed it was a pretty new sight for Yelena. Or was it Kate’s presence itself? She rose from her seat as fast as her knee brace would allow, tapped the door release button and only with the slightest of limps, stepped out into the corridor.

    “Kate?” Yelena said softly. There it was, her voice. Not a voice beamed from the other side of the country, not a voice that sounded in her head when she couldn’t sleep or when the pain overcame her, but a real-life voice. Deep and warm and comforting, as always, but there was something else there too that morning. Apprehension. It was subtle but it was there, it was unmistakable. Yelena was nervous to see her. This time round, Kate’s heart didn’t so much as skip a bit as stop entirely. Her feet ceased their pained shuffle and her voice caught in her throat. How could one woman be so disarming?

    “Hi-hi,” Kate stuttered awkwardly, whilst internally berating herself for sound so fucking stupid. This is your girlfriend, Kate. Not a high school crush. But by god, did it feel like it. “You shouldn’t have-.”

    “Miss Bishop!” Came a new voice. It was deep, yes, but shrewder than Yelena’s. “To what do we owe the pleasure?”

    Kate blinked. She hadn’t even notice him get up from behind the desk, but there he was, stood before her. And despite the fact that it was Nick Fury, THE Nick Fury, and he was being charming and polite and smiling warmly, Kate couldn’t take her eyes from her girlfriend. What the fuck did she mean by “shouldn’t have”? Shouldn’t have what? And why the hell did he feel as if then was the right time to interrupt? This was between them. Shouldn’t have what goddam it? Shouldn’t have hobbled her way down here, shouldn’t have stuck her nose in? … Calm down, Kate. It was just a lacing of apprehension, remember? Also, Nick Fury just spoke to you, nicely, you should probably open your mouth. “Umm…I umm- .” Was all that Kate managed. Yelena frowned and the smallest of smiles played across her darkened features. Turns out the blonde couldn’t resist Kate’s bumbling charm, no matter the circumstance, and Kate’s heart felt just a little lighter. “Umm-er-you know my name?”

    “You’re a valuable asset, and a bit of a hero, or so I’ve been told.” Was Kate blushing? Because she felt as if she was maybe blushing.

    “Er…erm… I-.” Yep, probably a little puce right about now. ‘A bit of a hero’. Wow. ‘Valuable’. What? ‘Asset’... not so hot. And who told him? Had Carol told him? Did Carol call her a hero? Because that would end her life.

    “We’ll be done in here soon, Kate,” Yelena explained softly. What if it was Yelena that had called her a hero? That wouldn’t just end her life, that would send her soul into hyper-space. “Sure. I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to… sorry.” The apology had fallen out of her mouth faster than she’d meant it. Why was she apologising? Had she really done anything wrong? And if not, why apologise at all? It was mad that with just a crinkle of her brow or with a waver of her voice Yelena could have Kate falling all over herself in such a way. Was Kate just in her own head? And if not, what was causing the animosity? That was something Kate didn’t want to think about, but at the same time, if Yelena was giving her the cold shoulder, Kate would have every right to be annoyed. She ought to stand up for herself and tell Yelena to stop being a grumpy asshole, but instead she could only worry, on today of all days. “I’ll be in the gym, I guess,” Kate shrugged, defeatedly. It was for the best. She wound go, do her exercises, lie on a gym mat, stare at the ceiling and have a existential crisis, and by the time all that was over, Yelena would be ready to be her girlfriend again. If that’s what she wanted, because clearly it wasn’t really a priority for her.

    Carol offered Kate a reassuring smile. It seemed as if the older woman was the only one who could read the fucking room. “She’ll meet you there,” she said with the smallest of glances to Yelena who hesitantly nodded her agreement.

    That was Kate’s cue then. She was politely being asked to leave. She got it. With one glance in her girlfriend’s direction, she resolved herself. She would go upstairs, they would meet in the gym and in just a few moments time, they would have a chance to start again. Kate would forget she’d been sidestepped and sidelined. She would get to put her hands on her girlfriend, hold her, feel her, taste her, and then maybe, just maybe, in the comfort of their own bedroom, and in the comfort of Kate’s arms Yelena would tell her what the fuck was going on.

    “Okay,” Kate nodded as she wrestled to maintain the polite smile that was plastered across her delicate features. “It’s an honour to meet you, Mr Fury,” Kate added respectfully. And it was an absolute honour that was for sure. How many people got to meet THE Nick Fury? Not many. Kate just wished it was under better circumstances. She also wished he hadn’t tried to steal her girl. Kate Bishop would fight him if she had to, walker or no walker. Screw the hierarchy.

    “The honour’s all mine,” Fury smiled earnestly and Kate felt the urge to shake her walker threateningly recede. Okay, maybe she wouldn’t fight him, but she’d give him a piece of her mind, that was for sure. Because ultimately, whichever way you cut it, Fury was S.H.I.E.L.D. and S.H.I.E.L.D. could suck it.

    As always, the gym mat wasn’t nearly as comfortable as her own bed. Kate supposed that was half the point. It wasn’t supposed to be. If physio was easy they wouldn’t call it therapy, because when had therapy ever been easy?

    Kate had been what her mother would like to call “a problem child”. After the death of her father, Kate bounced around therapists like a pinball bounces around a miniature Eighties cult movie-themed gauntlet. Truth be told, Kate had never really needed a therapist at all. She hadn’t needed to relearn ways to take control of her life or manage her grief. She’d needed archery. That was her shortcut, her way of dealing, but with physiotherapy there was no shortcut. It was either do it and get better, or don’t do it and don’t. Which raised the question, what would Kate Bishop do if she didn’t get better. What would she do without archery? How would she relearn control? And how would she grieve?

    Of course, Kate knew some of the easier answers. She had Yelena to support her, as well as the and the little family they’d created. Or at least Kate hoped she had her. She was going through her battles too, that was evident. Although Kate had succeeded in saving Yelena from her mother, as much as she’d tried, she hadn’t exactly saved Yelena from herself. That was something Yelena needed to do, and it was something that Kate was going to have to give her time for.

    Kate exhaled heavily. If only she could will the tension away. She’d been an idiot to think that Yelena coming home would be a day of happiness, celebration, love and fluff. She’d been an absolute idiot. Of course there would be tension, of course it would be weird, and of course Yelena would look at her with apprehension. Last time Yelena saw her in person, she’d been well… dead. Like, heart-not-beating dead. There were going to be mixed emotions, but Kate had just been so excited, so hopeful. To have her and hold her. To make her laugh, God, Kate wanted to make Yelena laugh so bad. To hear that familiar, rasping chortle. To take pride in being one of the only people on the planet who could ellicit it from her. To know that in that moment she was happy. Maybe that’s what she needed to do. She needed reset her expectations. No fluff, no fanfare, no ferocious make-out session, maybe not even any pizza. Just a laugh. To make her laugh would be enough.

    The softest of ‘Hi’s pulled Kate from her thoughts. There she was, Yelena Belova, Queen of Dragsnovs, leant casually against the entrance to the yoga room. In an instant Kate was up on her elbows. Shit did Yelena look good. Colourful patchwork cargo pants with accompanying knee brace, a white t-shirt and black sneakers. The kicker though, the kicker was her hair. What the actual fuck? Kate felt as though she was in a state of perpetual mourning and endless arousal. It was messy but perfectly put together and Kate just wanted to grab fists of it. Good Lord, Kate, remember. Make her laugh. The aim of the game is to make her laugh. Kate eventually summoned a rather breathless, “Hi,” of her own and Yelena smiled all too knowingly from the doorway with her hands dug firmly into her pockets. Could she look any more lgbtqia? If Yelena’s triceps were popping Kate didn’t notice. Not at all. Not one bit. The pair took a moment as they took each other in. It was the first time they’d been alone, truly alone, for a long time. Yelena’s arms still showed signs of their fight, as did her right brow. Kate’s body wasn’t dissimilar. In fact, Kate’s body was a lot worse. Tiny pieces of shrapnel from the explosion had cut and grazed her skin, almost all over. It looked way worse than it was, but it was still a stark reminder of what had happened. There was a reason Kate had chosen a full-length shirt that morning.

    Yelena’s eyes met hers. They were shrouded, despite her smile and Kate knew instantly that Yelena was wearing a mask. She’d come home with her own ideas and expectations of what the day would bring. She was worried, anxious or afraid. Maybe all of the above. But in true Yelena Belova style, she was making a desperate attempt to sweep all that under the rug, to show Kate that she was happy. That they could be happy.

    Before she was even really aware of what was happening, Kate was pushing herself from the mat in an attempt to get to her feet. She needed to hold her girlfriend. Fuck making her laugh if laughing was just for show.

    “No. No, no stay there.”

    Suddenly Yelena’s arms were around her, gently lowering her back down towards the mat. It all happened much faster than Kate would have imagined and any kind of logical thought and reasoning escaped her as Yelena’s lips found hers. It was gentle and yet so desperate and Kate clung to her girlfriend for dear life, breathing her in. Her fingers dug painfully into powerful shoulder blades as she pulled her own shoulders away from the mat to be closer to Yelena, as close as was humanly possible. A strong hand cradled her close as a rather breathless Yelena broke their kiss and softly rested her forehead against Kate’s. The Russian sighed into their embrace as Kate studied her breathtaking features up close. She ran a gentle thumb across her left eyebrow. The backs of her fingers deftly across her cheek. Her forefinger across the delicate tip and curve of her lips. Yelena’s cheeks were hot and flushed with emotion and Kate decided that the best course of action was to pepper them with kisses, furiously, and so she did. And oh how she was rewarded.

    The laugh started deep in Yelena’s chest. So deep it was almost a wheeze. It shook her shoulders as it found its way to her throat, where it because a rumbling and warm chortle. Kate’s heart felt just as warm and twice as giddy at the sound. Yelena Belova laughing should be used as asmr therapy. That shit could cure PTSD overnight. Maybe. Probably not but still, it sounded fucking good. It sounded even better when Kate’s lips found their way to the sensitive skin just below Yelena’s ear.

    “Okay, okay, okay,” groaned Yelena as she fought desperately to escape Kate’s ticklish kisses, “Why are you trying to torture me?”

    Kate reluctantly relented and settle back down into the mat with a smile. “You didn’t tell me you were here.” Of course, in truth, Kate didn’t need a reason to torture Yelena with kisses, but she was more than happy to take the opening Yelena had given her, especially whilst the Russian had a smile in her eyes and not the alternative.

    “I wanted to surprise you,” Yelena shrugged. She knew it was a bad answer. That told Kate that she didn’t have a good one.

    The brunette narrowed her eyes quizzically. “Why don’t I believe you?” “Because I’m not good at surprises?” Yelena ventured. There was that apprehension again. It seemed as if Kate was going to have to get comfortable with being uncomfortable. At least for a little while. And so, she buckled up for the ride.

    “And what is this?” She teased as her fingers found their way amongst thick blonde hair. Yelena cringed a little awkwardly. “Surprise?”

    “I mean, you look hot, I’m not gonna lie,” Kate said with a smirk she just couldn’t hide, for she’d just made the understatement of the century.

    “Thank you,” Yelena smiled softly. “It feels good. Lighter.” And Kate understood. Kate had needed archery to take back control. Yelena had needed to take back control of her body. It must have felt good.

    “But it’s normally the kind of thing you share with someone who… you know. Who cares about you.” Kate felt like an asshole for saying it. She really did. But at the same time, communication now more than ever was going to be important, and hair was probably the least sensitive way of breaching the conversation. That didn’t stop Kate feeling awful as Yelena’s trademark frown pulled at the corner of her rather beautiful lips. “Obviously you don’t need my permission but…” Kate stumbled as she tried desperately to turn that frown upside down. “I kinda feel like….” Find the words Kate, you got this. “I really like touching it and… pulling it.” Those were not the words, although they did kind of have the desired effect for Yelena was now smiling bemusedly at her, as was so often their dynamic.

    “You can still do both of those things,” Yelena soothed. Her voice was low and vibrated deep within her chest. Kate could practically feel it, and it was doing bad things to her. “Right, but I… I-“ “Are you grieving for my hair?” Yelena asked, eyebrow raised, as if grieving for something as inconsequential as hair was speculative at best. Which of course it kind of was because hair didn’t make the person. Yelena could be bald and she’d still be Yelena, but also Kate would die before she cut her hair that short. And she wasn’t being dramatic. Not at all. Nope. “Yes…” Kate confessed. “Just a tiny bit.”

    “I just felt like I needed a change. A fresh start.”

    “I absolutely understand that and you look beautiful and I want you to step on me when my body is ready. It’s not quite ready yet, but it will be.” She was rambling. “And this whole vibe is just very ‘daddy’ and I dig that, you know?” Oh god, she was rambling. The bemused smile that hadn’t left Yelena’s face widened, if that was at all possible. “No… I don’t know.”

    “Probably for the best.”

    “Probably,” Yelena agreed teasingly as Kate’s touch starved hands began to roam. They grazed their way across her shoulders, played with the chunky toggled chain wrapped not twice but three times around her neck. They found their way to the soft skin that lay beneath the hem of the blonde’s T-shirt, and to the warm skin that lay just beneath the waistband of her pants. All the time Yelena simply studied her. Her hands didn’t explore Kate like she was used to. Her lips didn’t search for sensitive spots or freckles or the faded flecks of scars across her skin. They didn’t deepen their kiss when Kate pulled Yelena’s mouth to hers once more. And it occurred to Kate that perhaps Yelena wasn’t quite ready to revisit those sensitive spots. Because there were more now, weren’t there? And there were more scars that littered her body. There was a vast difference between kissing an old pain better and nursing a new pain caused by your hand. Love shouldn’t feel like an apology.

    And so again, Kate resolved herself and persevered.

    “Do you wanna help me with physio?” She asked with kind eyes and the gentlest of tones. When Yelena was like this, she could fool you into thinking she was resilient. But she could be delicate, and so Kate would be delicate too.

    “Is that actually a question? Or is that a demand disguised as such?” Yelena asked, eyebrow raised lightheartedly, disguising the turmoil underneath.

    “It’s definitely the latter,” Kate teased and Yelena smiled softly. Maybe in playing a part in Kate’s recovery, Yelena could heal a part of herself. Maybe they could heal together. “Okay,” Yelena nodded with a determined frown “Tell me what to do.”

    “Yes, daddy,” Kate grinned as Yelena painfully rolled her eyes at her girlfriend. The blonde got to her knees and Kate began to instruct her. Of course, all of these exercises could be completed solo, but having someone support her meant she could achieve a better stretch and a better range of movement, plus the slight resistance that Yelena offered against the inside of her knee or the outside of her thigh would only help strengthen the muscles there. That and maybe turning Yelena’s touch into something functional but also something healing, might at least be a way to reconnect physically. Or at least Kate hoped it might be. It would be remiss for Kate to say that she didn’t use the opportunity to indulge in Yelena’s touch, despite the polyester layer that separated Kate’s yearning skin and Yelena’s warm hands. When the blonde pushed firmly against her knee to stretch Kate’s lower back and glute, the brunette took full advantage, ghosting her fingertips lightly across her forearm and her thumb across her knuckles. This simple contact felt so unbelievably good. It was scratchy yet soft, electric and kinetic, yet as soothing as freshly washed bed linen and freshly shaven legs. It was the skin on skin contact she’d been craving. It was the comforting warmth of her girlfriend’s touch.

    Kate flinched as the pressure from Yelena’s palms became just a little too great and a small hiss escaped her. Before it had even left her lips she wished she could take it back. In an instant their connection was broken and Yelena’s hands deserted Kate. Instead of being on her they were up and open palmed, pleading their innocence. “I-I’m sorry,” Yelena stuttered, panic in her voice and eyes anywhere but Kate’s. “I didn’t mean to-.”

    “It’s okay, it’s okay,” Kate soothed as she captured Yelena’s hands and fought to find her hazel eyes. Cautiously and very gently, Kate guided Yelena’s right palm back down and onto her thigh, whilst she pressed a tender kiss into her left. “It’s the first time,” Kate murmured softly against Yelena’s palm before she placed second kiss against the rough skin there. No sooner had Kate’s lips found purchase, however, had Yelena pulled her hand away sharply. Both hands.

    “I do not think that I can help you with this,” the blonde said hurriedly as she pulled away from Kate and sprung to her feet. Had Kate pushed too much? Maybe laughter would have been the best medicine after all. She didn’t want to push, not too hard. But if it didn’t hurt just a little, it would never heal.

    “Okay… umm, that’s okay we can… we can do something else,” Kate offered but Yelena was already firmly inside her own head. Her eyes were dark. They were everywhere and nowhere all at once as her hands ran agonisingly through her hair. Damn if she didn’t look good. Kate had to remember her girlfriend was having one almighty internal freak out and now was not the time to objectify her. But she’d also been by herself for a very long time. A very long time.

    Kate thought it best to give Yelena a moment. A moment to breathe. A moment to reel her thoughts in and put her own mind at ease. A moment for herself.

    With a herculean effort Kate hauled herself up into a seated position and started to manoeuvre her body so than she could push herself onto one knee, then two, and then to her feet. “Shit,” came Yelena’s admonishing voice. She was angry at herself.

    Two strong arms wrapped around the archer and eased her to her feet. "I'm sorry,” Yelena said, quietly, eyes firmly fixed upon their tightly clasped hands as she helped Kate over to her walker that she’d left next to the edge of the mats. Yelena’s eyes were everywhere but Kate as the brunette grabbed her walking aid firmly with both hands.

    “You don’t like this do you?” Kate asked and Yelena’s startled eyes met hers. “The frame?”

    “Yes...” Kate nodded slowly, “And all of this I guess.” It wasn’t an accusation, mainly to do with the fact that they clearly both knew it to be true. It was a simple recognition of fact. Yelena had a distinct aversion to Kate’s pain and it probably had something to do with the fact that she’d caused it. Not directly of course. Kate had never for one moment blamed her, but she knew that Yelena blamed herself. It was unavoidable really. Her hands had choked Kate with such violent determination, her hands had fired the arrow that almost pierced her heart, and it was Yelena’s life that had been saved when Kate put herself between Yelena and the explosive earpiece. So of course, it was becoming quite clear that Yelena blamed herself. It was also quite clear that she was having a hard time trusting herself. Could the blonde trust that her touch would no longer hurt Kate? Could she trust her hands to do good and not harm? Kate knew that Yelena should, but would she?

    “Seeing you is…” Yelena trailed off as she puffed her cheeks and fought to find the right words. “Difficult.”

    Kate took one hand from the walker and captured Yelena’s. “I thought you were excited.” “I was. I am…” Yelena’s eyes were anywhere but Kate’s, and yet her hand tightened almost imperceptibly around the brunette’s fingers. “But now I’m seeing you... like this. It's difficult.”

    The brunette’s other hand grazed across Yelena’s warm cheek, the walker now abandoned. “I’m okay,” she reassured, “A little bruised and still a little sore, but I’m okay.” Kate turned Yelena’s chin up delicately and sought out her eyes.

    “Seeing you is different. Touching you is...” Hazel eyes met violet. Kate shouldn’t have been surprised by what she found there, and yet still, she was. Yelena was afraid. “There are marks on you that weren’t here before. You think I do not see them but I do.” “Hey,” Kate soothed, both of her hands now gently cradling Yelena’s face. Her thumb grazed the angry scar that split the blonde’s brow. They’d both dealt their fair share of blows that night, some more destructive than others.

    “I did this, right?” Yelena remarked as she grazed her thumb across two bright lines that adorned Kate’s chin.

    “And this?” Yelena clutched at Kate’s hands and studied the now permanently marked skin of her arms. “And these. I’m responsible for every mark.”

    “Hey, no,” Kate clutched tightly at her girlfriend’s, “You’re not.”

    “How can you say that?” Yelena asked, despairingly.

    “These marks,” Kate reasoned fervently as she pulled Yelena close, “They live on both of us. This was an attack on both of us.” Kate placed the softest of kisses upon the scar that marred her girlfriend’s brow, before she rested her forehead softly against Yelena’s. “I want you to help me with this, okay?” Kate whispered. And she really did. She needed Yelena to come on this journey with her, otherwise one of them was going to get left behind and that really wouldn’t bode well for either of them. “I need your help,” Kate continued, “I know you can do it.” If anyone had the strength for this, it was Yelena Belova. It took a moment for Kate to notice the strong fingers that clung to her back. Yelena was hanging on for dear life. It was at times like this that Kate felt how small and diminutive her girlfriend really was. Yelena was the kind of person that took up so much space. She occupied your attention and dominated a room without overburdening it. Sure, she could go completely unnoticed if that’s what she wanted, but her personality was so bright, so confident, so self-assured; it was always odd to see her this way. Small, delicate, almost fragile, and it made Kate want to hold onto the women even tighter.

    A few moments longer and Yelena’s body began to relax. The finger tips that dug deeply into Kate’s back eased their grip and the Russian began to ease into Kate’s arms. “Okay,” Yelena whispered, her soft breath tickling the sensitive skin of Kate’s neck. “Okay. I can do this,” the blonde affirmed as she broke their embrace and matched Kate’s gaze. Yelena’s hazel eyes that were so recently filled with fear now danced with something as delicate as Kate’s emotional state. They danced with hope.

    The brunette smiled affectionately, she couldn’t help it. The emotions Yelena managed to stir in her were beyond anything she could have anticipated, and yet the blonde was still finding ways to surprise her.

    “I have a dumb idea,” Kate whispered conspiratorially as a sudden thought hit her. “What’s new?” Yelena deadpanned and Kate couldn’t help the smile that pulled at the corner of her lips. Yelena had made a joke. She had actually made a joke.

    “Okay I kinda walked into that one but hear me out,” Kate continued as she took her girlfriend by the hands and gingerly lead her back over to the mats.

    “Okay…” Yelena raised a skeptical eyebrow but followed Kate dutifully, a supportive hand around the younger woman’s waist.

    With only a small amount of pain and slightly higher amount of difficulty, Kate lowered herself back down onto the mat and encouraged Yelena to sit beside her. “So what is this dumb idea of yours?”

    “It’s not dumb,” Kate frowned.

    “Your words, not mine,” Yelena teased, hands raised. The significance wasn’t lost on Kate. Just minutes earlier Yelena had recoiled from her, hands raised, scared and defensive. Now, a small smile played across her girlfriend’s lips.

    “Whenever we do this,” Kate gestured to the mat before she took one of Yelena’s hands and placed it back upon her body, “Whenever I do a little exercise, whether you’re helping me or not, you should do one too.”

    “Like with my knee?” Yelena asked, clearly needing a little further explanation. “No, idiot. Not with your knee, with your brain.”

    “That was clear as mud, Kate Bishop.”

    “Whatever,” Kate batted away Yelena’s teasing concerns and persevered. “Whenever we do this you should….” Kate searched for the words. She needed to not sound dumb. “Exercise your thoughts.” Okay, that sounded a little dumb. “When you worry about my body, think about how you’re helping me fix it. And when you’re angry at yourself or scared about what you think you’re capable of, be angry at them. With S.H.I.E.L.D. or with that… that woman.” Yelena’s eyes grew a little darker at the mention of her biological mother. “That way we can get better together,” Kate added with a hopeful smile. “I know it sounds a little cheesy but-“ “It does not sound cheesy,” interjected Yelena quietly. The earnestness in her voice surprised Kate. It was a very happy surprise.

    “No?”

    “It sounds smart,” nodded Yelena in her typically rational manner. “I have to get used to this. To your body being like this.”
