    Yelena’s fingertips danced one last time against Kate’s abdomen. They plotted a meandering course from just below her sternum, across ticklish ribs, taut muscles, soft curves and- “But in the spirit of using words….” Kate’s breathless voice pulled Yelena from her heady revery. It was very easy to get drunk on the feel of her girlfriend. Clearly harder to get drunk on the feel of her.

    “Mmm hmm,” Yelena just and so managed.

    “Are you going to tell me what’s going on with you and Mister Fury?” Ah. Yelena blinked. Really, she was surprised it had taken this long. Kate must have been sitting on this for hours. She’d probably dreamed about all the ways she could ask Yelena about it. Was this one of the ways? Yelena thought it highly likely.

    Two very hopeful, violet eyes were upon her. It wasn’t time. Yelena hadn’t even signed anything yet, she wasn’t even close to choosing herself, let alone inviting Kate into the conversation. Right now, things needed to settle. Once that happened, then Yelena could choose.

    “I could tell you,” Yelena started carefully, “But then I would have to kill you,” she concluded, in the deepest, sexiest, most seductive voice she could muster. It was a voice that always worked. Yelena only needed to raise an eyebrow and mutter a few magic words and Kate would be kicking her feet and twirling her hair, but that morning was different. Kate Bishop wasn’t taking that shit. Pizdets.

    “You tried that already,” she shrugged matter-of-factly in Yelena’s embrace. “In fact, I seem to remember that you were defeated by a superior enemy,” wow, the shade, “So, tell me.” Kate’s chin jutted in stubborn defiance. She wasn’t going to take no for an answer. What a shame that was the only answer Yelena was going to give her.

    “Nope.”

    “Tell me now,” Kate insisted, and Yelena yelped in surprise as the brunette launched a vicious and pre-meditated pinch attack.

    “Ow. I can’t.”

    “Why?” Kate growled. “Why? I want to know why.” This had very quickly become an interrogation. A very Kate Bishop style interrogation, with pinching, frowns and an overuse of the word ‘why’. Quite different to a Yelena Belova interrogation. That normally consisted of lots of shouting, inflicting pain and mind games.

    “Ooow, Why not?” Yelena despaired as a Kate landed a particularly painful pinch on the soft skin of her stomach.

    “Because we don’t keep secrets,” Kate reasoned.

    “I never agreed to that.”

    “You agreed to it when you decided to be my partner.”

    “I don’t remember that being part of the contract.” It was Yelena’s turn to pout but in all seriousness, not keeping secrets was never part of her S.H.I.E.L.D. contract. In fact, she was pretty sure shutting up was one of the most important clauses of the agreement. “Bullshit,” Kate said stubbornly. “It’s part of the girlfriend code. You’re my girlfriend. Girlfriends don’t keep secrets.” Yelena had to resist to the urge to point out that everyone kept secrets, and everyone told lies. That would have been bad for two reasons. First, Kate would have got angry. Second, Kate was the exception to that rule. Kate can’t keep a secret to save her life, and Kate certainly can’t lie.

    “What if this secret was imperative to National Security?” Yelena countered and Kate’s eyes lit up at the possibility.

    “Ooh, is it?” She asked excitedly. This was the reason Kate couldn’t keep secrets. Secrets were far too exciting.

    “No,” Yelena answered stoically.

    “But is it though?” Kate grinned. Her desire to know the truth was insatiable. “Nope.” There was no way.

    “Oh my god just tell me!” Kate was going to burst, like maybe real-life burst. Yelena needed to act and quick. She needed to offer Kate something, at least part of the truth but telling her everything just seemed too much. Kate would jump to conclusions and overthink and worry. But if Yelena told her nothing her girlfriend would ultimately end up doing the same thing. Yelena sighed and gently pulled Kate to her until their bodies were flush. “Look, it’s not a scary secret, okay? The world is not ending, I haven’t agreed to anything I shouldn’t and I’m not signing my freedom away.”

    “No, because you already did that.”

    “And it’s not anything that is going to kill you to not know for a little while.” “It isn’t? Because it feels like it is.”

    “No,” Yelena soothed as well as she could and gazed up earnestly into uneasy violet eyes. “It isn’t.”

    “Really?” Kate was sceptical and she was justified in that. It wasn’t as if Yelena had been the most communicative as of late. Sure, there were reasons and good ones, but the previous days events had shown how inconsistent Yelena could be. How unpredictable she could be with her feelings and her thoughts. Yelena didn’t trust her own mind. How could she expect Kate to when she didn’t.

    “Yes really. I just need to…” Yelena paused for a moment, in search of the words. Words that wouldn’t spark panic but words that were honest enough. “I just need to handle a few things first. You’ve seen how I am. I haven’t been good.”

    “But I thought you were feeli—.”

    “I am. I am feeling better, and you are such a big part of that. I just… there are a few things that I need to work out, for myself. I know you want to help but you cannot change my brain for me, okay? But hugs and warm beds help, plus whatever you did last night. I liked that.” “You did?”

    Yelena nodded contentedly. She more than liked it. She loved it. “Of course. I’ve never felt so close to anyone”.

    “Me neither,” whispered Kate, suddenly quite aware of the significance of the moment. She smiled awkwardly and rolled her eyes. “So now you choose to use your words, I see. Yelena Belova, Queen of distractions.”

    “Oh, I can be very distracting,” Yelena grinned mischievously as she released her hold on Kate and allowed her rough fingertips to graze teasingly from knee to thigh to hip. Whatever strength Kate had in her hips, it urged them forward, keen to feel Yelena’s touch. More definite, more purposeful. Fortunately for the brunette, her girlfriend was willing to acquiesce.

    “Shit. What time is it?” Wait, what?

    Yelena frowned with confusion. Was sex restricted to certain hours of the day? Did Google forgo telling her this incredibly important titbit of information? “Like… ten-ish?” Kate’s eyes went wide. “TEN-ISH?!”

    The blonde blinked. She was not making the connection. Had she broken the most sacred rule of sexual intercourse? Did they teach this in schools? She didn’t go to school! “Move, move, move!” Kate huffed as she pushed her girlfriend away from her, threw back the sheets and began to haul herself laboriously from the bed.

    “Kate, what are you doing? You’re going to hurt yourself.”

    “Eurovision starts in four hours!” The brunette wailed.

    “Right, four hours. I thought you wanted to… you know…?” Yelena gestured a little awkwardly to her very naked body that had been unceremoniously robbed of its covering. “Yes, but there’s a lot to do,” Kate explained as she pushed herself from the bed and hobbled through to the bathroom. Yelena shook her head in exasperation. This girl was going to hurt herself all over again.

    “Like what?”

    “Like prep the food and cook the food. You know? Stuff,” Kate explained as she flipped the light switch to the ensuite and set the extractor fan humming.

    It made no sense. It was Eurovision, not a banquet. And no offence to Kate, but Yelena wasn’t sure that Kate had the attention span to follow a recipe for forty minutes let alone four hours. “What are you making that takes four hours?”

    Yelena heard the shower spring to life as water beat down powerfully against porcelain. “Something that I might screw up first time round!” Echoed Kate’s voice from the bathroom. The Russian shook her head and began to drag her own very naked body from their bed. “You will have my help. There will be no screwing up. I am Russian and I happen to be a very talented-.”

    Kate’s head appeared from around the door frame as she practically barked at her girlfriends, “No! You will not be helping. This is my treat for you, for everyone. It’s a homecoming. You’re not cooking at your own homecoming.” It made sense and normally Yelena would be inclined to agree, but really? Four hours?

    Yelena flexed her knee gently for a moment to ease the morning stiffness and then hopped off the bed in pursuit of her stubborn brunette. She found her in the bathroom. Kate was carefully testing the temperature of the shower as Yelena’s hands found her girlfriends hips. She pressed herself against Kate, bare skin against bare skin, Kate’s ass against the dip of her stomach, careful not to pull against her hips. Her lips danced across Kate’s shoulder and the nape of her neck as the brunette huffed impatiently for the water to heat up. “We could use the next two hours to… I don’t know… maybe rest a little more. Make use of this very comfortable big bed. Perhaps take a shower together.”

    “No can-do babe,” Kate said apologetically as she shrugged off her girlfriend and stepped into the shower. “Got places to be. All of us, all in one place, when does this ever happen? This afternoon has to be perfect.”

    What was happening? Had Yelena stepped into an alternate universe? How was she the one pursuing this? It’s almost as if she conditioned Kate into an almost sexless relationship where doing loving and caring things for each was their love language.

    “No, no it does not have to be perfect. Eurovision is imperfect in every way. It is dumb and over the top and gay as hell. Does that sound like someone we know?”

    “Peter?” Kate shrugged as she began to lather the shampoo in her hair. “No idiot. You, Kate Bishop.” This was absurd.

    Kate stuck her head back under the water dismissively. “I am none of those things.” “You are at least one of those things,” Yelena countered as she shook her head and started her reluctant retreat back to the bedroom.

    “It’s gay, isn’t it?!” Kate called after her.

    “Yep!” Yelena couldn’t help the grin as she collected her sport bra and sweatpants from the floor.

    “Look!” Kate called once more, “I’m gonna finish my shower, then I’m going to cook and then I’m gonna do physio and if you’d like you can help me with two of those three things!” Two of the three? Yelena dropped her bra and sweatpants to the floor and scampered back into the bathroom. Being clothed could wait.

    “Cooking is not one of them, is it?”

    “Nope,” Kate said with a grin and with glee Yelena leapt into the shower to kiss her sudsy girlfriend.

    “Oh, but there is one Eurovision related thing you can do for me,” Kate said through a multiplicity of Russian kisses.

    “And what is that, darling?”

    “I’m going to need ice. Like… a lot of ice.”

    “Ice for what?” Yelena asked quizzically hoping beyond all hope that Kate wasn’t going to say ‘for the vodka’.

    “For the cocktails,” Kate explained as if it were the most obviously thing in the world. “I’m not watching that thing sober.”

    Yelena pulled her girlfriend towards her and smiled proudly. “Now you’re getting it.” “And so I was thinking maybe we’d have a couple of White Russians.”

    “Mmm hmm,” Yelena hummed happily against the wet skin of Kate’s collarbone. “A margarita or two.”

    “Mm a classic. Truly.”

    “And… I don’t know… maybe a cosmo to round out the evening?”

    Yelena’s breath caught and her hands stilled against Kate’s skin. Kate did want her. She’d been planning and planning well. This feeling was new for Yelena, she didn’t really know what it was. She was excited. Not sexually, or at least she didn’t think so, but she was excited all the same. If there was one thing in life that she wanted to do more than anything else, it was to feel close to Kate Bishop. Close, intimate, connected. Kate was at her most open, most vulnerable when they were together like that, and it was only for her. Only something Yelena was about to see. Only something that was shared with her. And Yelena loves that. Also there was no escaping the smugness one felt when a girl as beautiful as Kate Bishop screamed your name.

    “Ice you say?” Yelena asked as hazel eyes met violet.

    “Yes, please.” It was practically a whisper.

    “I can do that.”

    Kate’s violet eyes were dark with exhilaration. She bit her lip and ran her hands through wet blonde hair before pulling Yelena close. “Good girl,” she purred, “Good girl.”

    Yelena was slumped dejectedly at the kitchen counter. Russia were still languishing in the second half of the table and there had been only so much ribbing she could take. So, she’d done something she’d never normally do, she’d extracted herself from the situation. Arguing with children was a pointless exercise, concealing your extreme distaste for them and pretending to like them was even more pointless. Sure, this year’s entry had been particularly weak, and sure, nothing would ever really top the Buranovo Grannies, but had the ridicule been necessary?

    Laughter rang out through the open plan lounge as yet another country’s representative dialled in with a crippling sound delay and absolutely cringe worthy sense of humour. Oh Europe, never change.

    Despite Yelena never having watched Eurovision as a young woman growing up in the Red Room, she found it oddly nostalgia inducing. When she’d learned of its existence after escaping, she consumed as much of it as she could. She scraped and scoured the Internet for copies, all the while desperately avoiding spoilers. She’d spend evenings, just herself and Fanny, eating some random take out that she’d never tried before and indulging in post two thousands Eurovisions. It had been glorious, and quite educational. Nothing taught you more about the political machinations of the European continent and beyond like Eurovision did. Over the years there had been some classics. Many of which had made it into one of Yelena’s many work-out playlists but this year, this year Russia’s entry had left a lot to be desired. That didn’t mean all hope was lost however, quite the opposite, for Yelena had a wild card this year. Bosnia and Herzegovina. And that absolute gem of a country was currently lying in fourth place. Surely being genetically Bosnian meant she had a fair claim if she won? Kate had unequivocally disagreed, as had Kate’s minions, Kamala and America. Of course they had. America had always taken great pleasure in prodding Yelena, and Kamala, well, Kamala just took great pleasure in prodding anyone. Baka had been kinder. Whilst Kate had been cooking, what an absolute mess that had been by the way, Yelena had caught up with her grandmother, who after being inexplicably returned to her modest Bosnian home was now living it up in a S.H.I.E.L.D. funded Istanbul safe house. Unsurprisingly she was keen to give the Russian’s a good hiding, Yelena could only smile and nod. Her pride wasn’t so easily swayed but that’s what years of indoctrination could do to a person. That and an enthusiastic appreciation for the richness of Russian culture, and dumplings of course. And anyways, Yelena’s mother was Russian, and her father, and her sister. The Bosnian could be afforded a little indiscretion.

    “How’s the leg?” Came a sudden voice. It was close, very close, and Yelena had to wonder how she’d let someone get that close whilst remaining undetected. The answer was easy. She was squiffy. Tipsy. Tidily. Not entirely sober.

    Yelena turned toward the voice, it was one she’d heard quite often as of late, a little too often in fact, since the incident with the Leviathan. It was Carol Danvers, undoubtedly come to rub the scoreboard in her face. Cyprus, who until moments ago lay below Russia, had just been granted twelve points from Greece despite their song being absolute trash. Now the bastards lay mid-table and Russia had slumped even further. This was a grim day but at least the vodka was cold, and despite the explosion in the kitchen that was her girlfriend, the food had been pretty good. Tasty, authentic and fresh for soaking up the alcohol she was drowning her sorrows with.

    The ex-assassin sighed and shook her head as she gathered some ice from the machine and deposited it onto the kitchen surface. “Good. Thank you.”

    Carol rested gently against the countertop, her back to the raucous group of friends who were chattering excitedly about the presenter’s lightning fast outfit change, a Eurovision tradition. Yelena smiled to herself as Kate’s voice carried through to the kitchen. She was claiming that she’d done quicker. She’d be right.

    “How’s everything else?” Carol asked quietly as Yelena’s eyes found her girlfriend. The younger woman was smiling so brightly, with Lucky and Fanny at her feet and her friends by her side. She was beautiful, especially when she was so free and happy like this. It suited her. It’s what she deserved.

    Yelena frowned a little at Carol’s probing question as she grabbed a lime to make Kamala a margarita mocktail, or as Kamala liked to call it mockerita. She thought she was smart. Yelena thought she was stupid. Kate just thought it was cute. A laboured sigh escaped the Russian. Kate Bishop. How do you solve a problem like Kate Bishop… if the problem wasn’t really Kate Bishop at all?

    “Better than it was yesterday,” Yelena mumbled discretely and offered Carol the smallest of smiles. It was true. Things were better than yesterday and tomorrow would be better than today. Or maybe not. That’s what healing was right? An undefined timeline of steps forward and backward and adjacent, all in order to reach a completely underdetermined destination. You can never go back to the way things were, not completely, but at least you can make a choice to get to wherever you’re going together. Right?

    “That’s good,” Carol smiled back softly before she turned towards her young recruits and leaned with her palms flat upon the surface. “So, is there a menu or…?” “There are limited ingredients,” Yelena explained as she gestured to the modest collection of spirits, mixers and bitters, “But I might be able to pull something together that’s to your taste.”

    “Hmm,” Carol mused, “What have you got there? Is that scotch?”

    Yelena nodded and gestured with her knife. “Scotch, vodka, tequila, vermouth, Cointreau, some terrible bourbon.” The bourbon in question was Jack Daniel’s. The blonde felt repulsed just thinking about it.

    “Not a bad collection,” Carol mused. Oh, how different they were. “All a little strong for three in the afternoon, though.” Oh yes, quite different.

    “Oh, come on Carol. It’s five pm somewhere in the universe and besides if you can’t drink to cope with the pleasure and pain that Eurovision brings, when can you drink?” “Alright, alright,” the older woman relented good-naturedly. “I have a request, but I won’t pretend it’s going to be easy.”

    A challenge? Well, this was interesting. “Pfft. Try me.”

    “Do you think you could make a penicillin?” Carol asked, eyebrow raised. Yes, it was a clear challenge, and Yelena was eager to prove herself to her newfound friend. It was weird to think that this was their first ever social interaction. They’d never shared a drink, a meal or even five minutes in front of the television together. This was the breaking of the bread and Yelena was in a pickle.

    “What is that? Scotch, bourbon, honey and lemon?”

    Carol’s lip quirked into an impressed little pout, “And ginger.” Ginger… ginger… she had ginger. Peter had gone gingerbread latte mad over Christmas and there was a bottle of ginger syrup in one of the cupboards. Honey was easy, lemon, not so much.

    “I could sub a lime for lemon?” Yelena offered a little reluctantly.

    “When life gives you limes huh?” Chuckled Carol and Yelena’s traitorous lips twitched at their corners.

    “That is a reach, even for you,” Yelena covered, her voice thick with disdain, but Carol couldn’t be fooled, and she grinned at Yelena happily.

    “Yeah, but you smiled.”

    “I did not smile,” Yelena frowned for added effect. “America just hit Peter really hard.” “Whatever,” Carol laughed, “You smiled.”

    “Whatever. You’re a loser,” Yelena bit back light-heartedly.

    “A loser with really great taste in cocktails.”

    “And terrible taste in women,” Yelena smirked. Carol could only roll her eyes. “Not always,” the older woman retorted quietly as Kamala moseyed on through to the kitchen to retrieve her mockerita.

    “Thanks Champ,” she said with an appreciative wink.

    “You’re welcome nerd,” Yelena smiled back with a generous helping of saccharine as she watched Kamala go before delving into the kitchen cupboards in search of Peter’s ginger syrup.

    “So…” Came Carol’s voice as soon as Kamala had left earshot, “Have you made that call yet?”

    Yelena sighed and ceased her searching for a moment. She’d wondered when the interrogation would start. “No, not yet, but I will.” The blonde huffed a little as she spied the ginger syrup. Peter had hidden it all the way at the back of the cupboard because of course he had. With more effort than she’d wanted to expend, Yelena retrieved the syrup and heaved herself back to her feet. Her knee was stiff and her brow gloomy. “I will, but I want to make sure that-.”

    “That’s okay, I understand,” Carol said soothingly. Was Yelena being defensive? Absolutely she was. Did she need to be? Maybe, maybe not. That didn’t take away from the fact that Yelena was almost certainly avoiding picking up the phone to Eleanor Bishop. One thing at a time, one hurdle at a time. Speaking of hurdles…

    “Have you thought any more about our offer? Have you spoken to Kate?” Asked Carol with another cautious glance through to the lounge. Yelena knew exactly what she was looking at. A group of friends.

    Yelena sighed as she sliced into yet another lime and shook her head dismissively. Now was not the time. “I’m going to need some more time.”

    Carol shrugged casually but there was nothing casual about their proposition. “There’s no rush.”

    “I feel rushed.”

    “He’s just a busy guy. He was planet side so he paid you a visit. That’s all.” Yelena sighed cynically and carefully placed her knife down upon the chopping board. “Really?” She fixed her friend with a doubting stare.

    “Absolutely,” Carol smiled back earnestly. At least she believed her own bullshit. That was something.

    “Why don’t I believe that?”

    Carol tried to blink back her surprise. “Are you saying you don’t trust me?” “No…,” Yelena shook her head as she went back to squeezing her limes. “I’m saying I don’t trust him,” the Russian explained with gritted teeth, and she wrestled the juice from the disobedient fruit.

    “Your sister did,” Carol offered. She said it so casually, as if she didn’t understand the significance of her words, but of course she did, and she knew that Natasha’s trust was one of the only reasons Yelena had even entertained an audience with Fury in the first place. “And look how well that worked out,” Yelena growled as she tossed the lime juice into the large shaker and slammed its smaller counterpart down to seal it aggressively. “Believe me when I tell you, you have all the time in the world.”

    “I’m a Black Widow. You and I both know our time runs out eventually.” And with that, Yelena began to shake the cocktail, loudly. The ice rattled and rumbled inside the shakers and Carol cringed as the sound assaulted her ears.

    Eventually the kitchen fell silent and Yelena poured a smooth, lime penicillin over ice and pushed it over the counter towards Carol. The Russian stood pensively for a moment, hands on hips and brow furrowed, before her eyes met her friend’s. “I believe, for the most part, that you believe I can trust him. That is enough for me.”

    “Good,” Carol smiled. They were friends, friends were supposed to trust friends. Carol had trusted her when everyone else within S.H.I.E.L.D. wanted to lock her up and throw away the key. She could trust Carol now.

    “Now drink up,” Yelena urged amicably, “I’ve yet to have the pleasure of drunk Carol Danvers.”

    “There’s no such thing,” Carol grinned mischievously.

    “Whatever,” Yelena shook her head dubiously as Carol ventured for her sip of pen-with-lime- in. A warm smile spread across the Avenger’s face.

    “You know what? That is pretty good. The lime works.”

    Yelena eyes lit up with delight. “I knew it. I knew it would work.”

    “Are you having one?” Carol asked as she settled back against the counter to nurse her drink. “You think I haven’t already?” Yelena quirked an eyebrow.

    “Okay, are you having another one? Come on, it might liberate you from this perpetual cloud you’re insisting on walking under.” So, the interrogation wasn’t over. “I am not insisting.”

    “Then what are you doing?” Nope. Not over in the slightest.

    “Healing,” Yelena shrugged. She did not need this conversation right now. Especially as she was already having it with herself several times daily.

    “Bullshit,” hissed Carol.

    “Wow”. Two sips on her cocktail and Danvers was already getting in her face. “I mean it. You can pretend with Kate, but you can’t pretend with me. I’m immune to your bullshit.”

    “Nevospreeyimchyivaya, pryamo tahm" Yelena grumbled unhappily as she crossed her arms across her chest. She didn’t like being called out. She didn’t like being prodded. And she certainly didn’t like being proved wrong.

    “What are you waiting for? Just tell her.”

    “Carol, if you do not shut up right now, you will leave me with no choice.” It was an empty threat, both women knew it, but Yelena had to draw her line in the sand and she was fucking drawing it.

    “Good luck with that,” Carol shrugged dismissively. Of course, there was no way Yelena could ever take Carol in an all-out fight. Take Carol’s powers away, however, and the super- powered super-human was in deep, deep trouble.

    Yelena frowned as she refilled the ice bucket and threw some tequila into a shaker. She was going to get drunk. It was her only option.

    “I know there’s going to be an adjustment period,” Carol pressed.

    “You don’t know shit.”

    “We talked about this.”

    “No, you talked about it,” Yelena snapped angrily as she jabbed a frustrated finger in Carol’s direction. She caught herself almost instantly. She was getting too loud, too heated. She’d let Carol crawl under her skin, and it had been far too easy. “I’m not ready,” Yelena said dismissively as she shook her drink momentarily and then sieved it into a fresh glass, “We’re not ready.”

    “Yelena,” Carol said gently, “She is. She’s ready.”

    Yelena gritted her teeth and took a long, hard sip of her drink. It was strong. Very strong. Thank the goddess.

    “Look, Yelena,” Carol said as she took a step toward her. The ex-assassin knew what was coming. “I’ve been where you are right now.”

    “Carol, I’ve heard this before,” Yelena protested, and she had, more times in the last month than she could remember. Couples counsellor Carol had been trying force her great wisdom upon Yelena, despite being unable to hold down any semblance of a relationship herself, ever since she’d found out about Kate and Yelena. When it had started out, Carol had would appear and just talk about nothing or everything or whatever was in-between. Despite appearances and some rather vocal protestations, Carol had recognised that Yelena needed company. She’d needed something to fill the silence, otherwise her own brain would. As their rapport grew the topic of Carol’s seemingly random conversations became far more specific and far more Kate Bishop orientated. Was she going back? How did she feel about that? Did she know that Kate didn’t blame her? Maybe she should endeavour to speak to her girlfriend for more than two minutes. And lastly but not leastly, does she know how much you love her? Yelena’s incredibly useful response had been, ‘She knows that I would die for her. Is that not enough?’ According to Carol, the answer to that question had been categorically, ‘no’. Carol sighed with exasperation, pinched the bridge of nose in consternation and a took deep, steadying breath. Yelena frowned as Carol thumbed at her glass with a nervous energy Yelena had never seen in her friend before. Something was wrong. “No, Yelena, you haven’t heard this before.” Hazel eyes snapped to hazel eyes and Yelena found only frown. Carol’s face had grown softer and yet somehow more burdened, as if her years within this universe had quite suddenly caught up with her. Yelena had only seen Carol look this grave once before, on the night Kate’s heart had stopped beating within her chest.

    “Look,” Carol started as she placed her cocktail glass gently upon the kitchen work surface and swallowed with a grim acceptance. “I had someone once, someone I cared very deeply for but I was never honest with her about how I felt. Never truly honest anyways.” Carol spun the glass clockwise and then counter clockwise upon the granite countertop. The noise it made was soothing and Carol’s eyes never left the glass. “Truth be told I was scared of what it all meant. Back then people like us, we couldn’t have careers in the military. And then the whole super powered thing came along and I saw an opportunity.”

    “To do the space thing?” Yelena asked quietly and Carol smiled a small, fond smile. “Yeah,” she nodded gently, “To do the space thing. Turns out putting light years between yourself and your problems doesn’t always work out for the best.”

    “And I thought three thousand miles was extreme.” It had certainly felt it at the time and despite Carol’s arguments against running away from her problems, she’d helped Yelena do it all the same, because that’s what friends did. She got Yelena placed in LA, negotiated the house arrest, and kept up the pretence that her isolation on the other side of the continent was on S.H.I.E.L.D.’s orders. You see, Carol had been on damage control. Sure, she’d lied to Kate about Yelena, but it was for both their sakes. Yelena had needed space, Kate had needed security, hope that her girlfriend was fighting to get back to her. In her mind Yelena had been. In fact, the Russian had been fighting with herself since before she’d even come back to New York last July. Every decision was a battle, an internal wrestling match versus her fears and her rational brain. She’d needed the space, the quiet to piece back to the broken pieces and come back to Kate a whole person again, or as whole as she could ever be. If she hadn’t had that? Well, goodness knows what would have happened, but she couldn’t guarantee she wouldn’t be standing in the kitchen drowning her Eurovision blues with Carol Danvers and stealing glances at the woman she loved. No ma’am.

    “Three thousand miles is plenty,” Carol said with a grin, “But, I’m always going to outdo you, Belova. Higher, further, faster, remember?” The older woman winked and Yelena had to work hard to suppress the involuntary eye roll.

    “I do,” Yelena said with affection, “I do.”

    “Anyways,” Carol continued, not before taking another rousing sip of her drink, “I went off to fight my space monsters and I guess time moved faster than I ever thought it would. Before I knew it, I’d wasted all the moments we never had together.”

    Yelena stole another glance across to Kate. She was reclined lazily on the couch, tucked into Peter Parker’s side. She was insisting on hand feeding him chips and dip over her shoulder and despite being known in wider circles for her pinpoint accuracy, that afternoon her aim was well and truly failing her. To her credit almost all of the chips found their target. The dip didn’t.

    Peter cried out as sour cream and queso rained down onto his flannel shirt once more. Luckily for him, Fanny was in attendance. She sensed her opportunity and pounced, licking his shirt clean as Kate chortled happily. The sound of her laugh was golden. It wrung brightly in Yelena’s ears and clung tightly around her heart, and if you asked the Russian the reason she got out of bed in the morning, it was for that. That very sound. It was for Kate Bishop’s laugh. Because it was the sound of her happiness.

    Kate’s happiness. It was something that didn’t just revolve around Yelena, despite that being a thought that the Widow secretly indulged in. No, Kate took happiness in so many things. It was what made her such an incredible young woman. She could see the goodness in the darkest of places. She could delight in the crispness of a pepperoni pizza, she could dance alone to the worst music at a wedding, and she could take comfort in the company of good people. People that she would never want to be parted from.

    “There we so many things we dreamed about doing when we were younger,” Carol reflected quietly, “But I kept her at a distance. Sure, I was afraid of jeopardising her career, but really, I was afraid she’d choose that career over me too. What if I came and she’d moved on or didn’t feel the same way anymore?”

    Kate caught Yelena’s eye and waved happily. “Russia’s still sucking!”

    “Thank you, darling!” Yelena called back with plenty of sarcasm. It was a slip. Not a catastrophic one, but a slip all the same. Immediately Kamala’s voice could be heard from across the room, bad accent and all.

    “Daaahrrling, daaahrling. That sounds so Russian.”

    America giggled and Kate rolled her eyes as she continued to force feed Peter. Carol grabbed the scotch and emptied a healthy amount over the ice that remained within her drained tumbler.

    “I’m sorry, I love peaty whisky,” The older woman explained a little sheepishly, but of course there was no need.

    “No, no problem. By all means, continue. I’m going to need more to survive the afternoon.” “You are in for a lot of teasing I think.” Carol grimaced on her friend’s behalf and Yelena nodded sombrely.

    “I think you may be right, but I’m sorry, you were-.”

    “Right, right yeah, my sob story,” Carol said, her voice thick with self deprecation. “It’s okay, they are like currency around here.”

    Carol laughed because it was true. Everyone in that room had known pain, or if they hadn’t, they would. It was the sad reality of it all. It simply came with the job. “I mean, I thought about coming home to her, I did, but that asshole part of my brain told me to worry every time. How would I explain why I’d been gone so long? When she needed me, when our family needed me. What if she’d found someone else? Or worse yet, moved on when I hadn’t.” Carol shook her head, mentally chastising herself for decisions made long ago, but then her face softened and her eyes brightened. It was the look of someone who wasn’t simply remembering about reminiscing. “She was so smart and talented and brave and beautiful,” Carol said fondly, eyes dancing with melancholy, and Yelena understood. Carol’s person was dead. This smart, talented, brave and beautiful woman was dead. Much like Kate had been.

    “So, I put it off. I put her at the back of my mind. I put my feelings at the back of mind. And then when I finally came home, years later… I….”

    “You’d waited too long,” Yelena said quietly. It wasn’t a question. She knew the moral of the story, she knew what Carol was trying to warn her against. It was her own fucking brain. “I didn’t even know she was sick, Yelena. Cancer. She lived her whole life, never knowing if I loved her. Never knowing that she was loved. And then she died alone, because I was afraid.” Carol slammed her glass down upon the countertop and met Yelena’s gaze. Her eyes weren’t filled with fondness any longer. They weren’t dancing with memories gone by. They were angry. Angry with herself, sure, but they were angrier with Yelena. “Stop wasting time fighting your space monsters, Yelena,” she hissed. Her voice was quiet but it cracked and popped with unabashed frustration. “No matter what you think or feel, they will never be worth it. They will never be worth not having her. Not loving her. Not feeling her love. They will never be worth the dreams that you have together. So just tell her how you feel.” The words tumbled heatedly from Carol’s mouth and all Yelena could do was gawk in silence.

    “I-I… I’m sorry.” Yelena had no idea what exactly she was apologising for. Was it for Carol’s loss? For her inaction? For her ability to ignore almost every piece of advice Carol had been trying to throw her way because she’d insisted in her own mind that Carol couldn’t possibly understand what Yelena was thinking and feeling? Was it some confused jumbling of all of the above? It was too early to say.

    “Yeah. Me too.” Carol said with equal parts anger, equal parts regret. She downed her drink and slid the tumbler back across the countertop to Yelena.

    “Do you want another?” Yelena asked with apprehension.

    A small smile pulled at Carol’s lips. “Hell yes.”

    The rest of the afternoon went by in a flash. Probably for the best as it turned out Russian hopes couldn’t be saved by the public vote, which saw them sink even further down the table. They didn’t place last though, which was cause for celebration, and the friends had made a merry toast to ‘Being better than the UK at something!’ Yelena has argued that Russia was better than the UK at everything, but Kate wasn’t buying it. Apparently United Kingdom had corgies and One Direction. Yelena had threatened to leave Kate then and there. Kate had thought she was joking.

    After Eurovision had ended they stuck on a movie, that had taken about forty minutes to decide upon, and then all proceeded to veg out in front of it. Kate took advantage of her and Yelena’s recently updated, ‘out’ status and snuggled into the Russian’s side. Much to Yelena’s disappointment Kate announced her retirement from ‘that chip and dip life’ and refused to hand feed her girlfriend what was, by that point, congealed queso and soggy nachos. Perhaps it was for the best.

    Their fingers intertwined as Kate whispered incessant questions about the movie into Yelena’s ear. Why was her nose bleeding? Why weren’t there more killers in the loose? Why were they so afraid of dying when the witch only cared about one frickin’ person. Why didn’t they just drown her in the first place. And why, oh why didn’t they just get her some water? They were in a goddam grocery store. All legitimate questions, none of which Yelena was too concerned about. In fact, the Russian hadn’t been too concerned with the movie at all. Her mind was elsewhere. Lost in Carol’s story. Lost in the feel of Kate’s hot breath against her neck as she asked her questions animatedly, lost in the warmth of her body pressed against hers, lost in the feel of her rough fingertips as they played gently across the soft skin of the back of her hands. Lost in the thought that she felt so safe and so sure with Kate in her arms, even in front of these people who up until recently had been colleagues, not friends. “Hey,” Kate whispered, dragging Yelena from her thoughts.

    “Hi,” Yelena smiled as she turned to face her girlfriend.

    “Whatcha thinking about?” the brunette asked inquisitively. Yelena had clearly been caught. “Just something Carol said,” the blonde shrugged. It was the truth.

    “Oh really?” A small grin adorned Kate’s face.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded happily.

    “You and Carol best friends now, huh?”

    “Something like that,” she said coyly, “What are you thinking?”

    Kate blinked. She clearly hadn’t been expecting the question. “Um… just… how nice it is to be all together.” Yelena ‘hmmed’ thoughtfully. “It feels like it’s been forever.” For a split second Yelena saw Kate’s demeanour change. Her mind went somewhere. Her eyes darkened and her face flashed pensively, and then it was gone, replaced with a contented smile. The smile of a woman who had everything she wanted all in one place for the first time in so long. Then why the sudden sadness?

    “But anyways,” smooth, “I was wondering, as you seem to be paying zero attention to this movie…”

    “Not true.” Yes true.

    “If you could fix me a drink,” Kate asked probably a little more demurely than she’d initially intended, but who was Yelena to say no to such a polite request?

    “Sure. What would you like?”

    Kate pressed her lips against Yelena’s jaw, “You,” she whispered, her hot breath tickling the fairest of hairs that lay upon the blonde’s hairline. Yelena’s stomach lurched and her eyes immediately flashed to their friends with worry. But she needn’t. The merry band of freaks and geeks were all sat gazing up at the big screen. Peter was gripping a cushion in suspense, Kamala was still in mourning the loss of her favourite character and America was too gripped to move.

    “You’re not as smooth as you think you are, do you know that?” Yelena said quietly as she flashed Kate the smallest of smiles.

    “You would be correct,” Kate grinned, “In fact, I pride myself on being dumb, over the top and gay as hell.”

    Yelena laughed warmly which earned her a scathing look from Kamala who was clearly still in her mourning period. “Very good. But you are not dumb.”

    “No?” Kate asked curiously.

    “No. You’re very smart, remember? 3.8 gpa, great at Wordle, world renowned master of Russian delicacies, me being one of them of course. I know everything about you.” “And yet for some reason you stay,” Kate teased as her lips found Yelena’s and the room of people was momentarily forgotten.

    “For some reason, hmm,” Yelena mumbled against Kate’s lips. They were soft and warm and welcoming and yes, they were home. Her home. For many years Yelena had been striving to define what that meant. It wasn’t the Red Room, clearly. It wasn’t in St Petersburg with her parents or with the other Widows in London. It wasn’t any of those places, for Yelena had always felt restless. Whenever she’d tried to put down roots those roots never took. Not until Kate, because Kate wasn’t a place. She wasn’t a city or a job or a home. She was a person, and home was wherever she was. Kate could be in New York, sure, but Kate could also be in LA or in Mostar or in Budapest. Yelena didn’t have to choose between any of them, she just needed to choose Kate. She wanted to choose Kate. But would Kate choose her? “Yelena!” America shouted from the couch opposite, “Can you stop being gross and pass me a fresh bag of ch-ooof.” The requested bag of chips landed a little too forcefully in America’s lap. The culprit? Not Yelena Belova, oh no. Someone far dumber, more over the top and gay as hell. “Thanks but no thanks,” America muttered before she opened her newfound chips and dug in.

    “There is actually something I was hoping you could fix me,” Kate said as she turned back to Yelena and intertwined their fingers once more.

    “Oh really?” Yelena said quietly as she raised a curious eyebrow.

    “Yes,” Kate smirked back.

    “And what is that?”

    “Well, if it is not too much to ask, it feels like years since I’ve had a cosmopolitan.” Ah. A cosmopolitan.

    “And since you’re such an expert in err-,” Kate’s eyes darted across to the couch opposite and then back, “Such an expert in making them, I thought that-.”

    “It is not too much to ask.” Yelena cut in. “Not at all. They’re quickly becoming my favourite to make actually.”

    “Oh reall-.”

    “I’ll have a Virgin Pina Colada please!” Kamala announced from her comfy spot on the couch.

    “I swear to god,” Yelena muttered.

    “What?” Kamala appealed far too innocently, “I thought you were going back over there.” Yelena huffed dramatically. “I was,” Yelena lied, reluctantly. She couldn’t exactly admit that a ‘cosmopolitan’ was code for something very very different. Especially with a minor in the room.

    “Awesome!” Kamala exclaimed excitedly. “I’ll have a Virgin Pina Colado. Extra cherries! Oh! And extra pineapple! I like it tangy, you know? Like they do it in Chilly’s.” “In Chilly’s?” Yelena was at a loss for words. All this effort, all this cocktail making talent on display and Kamala wanted her to do it like they do in Chilly’s.

    “Yeah,” Kamala shrugged, “I love Chilly’s.”

    “You are an eternal disappointment to me, Kamala,” said Yelena as she reluctantly dragged herself up and off of the sofa, away from Kate’s warm embrace and back over to the kitchen counter.

    “You just hate what you don’t understand!” Kamala called after her “Your brain’s too tiny. You have like er, a tiny assassin brain.”

    “And you have a tiny teenager brain. Do you know that it’s not even fully developed yet?” “Gosh! Imagine how much smarter than you I’ll be when it is huh?”

    “Imagine how much smarter than me you’ll be with this pineapple shoved up your-“ “Yelena, babe!” Kate cut in, her voice understandably desperate. Perhaps Yelena was about to go a little too far. “Don’t forget there’s honey cake.”

    Yelena’s ears pricked up. “There’s honey cake?”

    “See?” Kamala’s smug voice floated from lounge. “Smarter.”

    “Pizdets,” the Russian grumbled as she searched the fridge for Kamala’s pineapple juice. Being forced to concede to a nineteen year old was not on Yelena’s list of leisure activities. The blonde’s frown was quickly turned upside down however as Kate Bishop and her walker pottered through into the kitchen.

    “Stiff?”

    “Mmm hmm. But it feels good.”

    “That is very to hear. Truly.”

    Kate joined Yelena on the other side of the counter and let her hands find the Russian’s waist as she tipped some ice into a glass and begrudgingly gave up what was left of her cream, normally reserved for her White Russians.

    “Do you want your Cosmo now or a little later?” Yelena asked as Kate’s finger tips found their way beneath the hem of her T-shirt.

    “It’s a little early, considering the company,” Kate mused as she placed a gentle kiss on Yelena’s right shoulder.

    “I don’t know, I’m getting a little tired of present company,” the blonde muttered. “We can hear you! That’s rude!” Kamala grinned.

    Yelena could only laugh and smile back. How could a kid be so boisterous and yet so conscientious at the same time? Kamala Khan was a dichotomy. Much like the woman who seemed to have permanently attached herself around Yelena’s waist.

    “She’s just grouchy Russia were trash,” America piped up.

    “It was a beautiful song!”

    “It was a train wreck,” added Peter.

    “Exactly! That is the whole point of Eurovision. It’s a train wreck. Stop looking at me like I’m crazy.”

    “But you are crazy!” reasoned Peter.

    “Certifiably!” agreed America.

    “Totally insane,” confirmed Kamala as she padded through to the kitchen to retrieve her alcohol free cocktail.

    “It’s for virgins,” muttered Yelena snidely.

    “Good joke, virgin,” retorted Kamala, unphased.

    Yelena’s eyes snapped to Kate’s. “Don’t look at me,” the brunette squeaked, “I just came for the Cosmos.”

    “Do you guys know that Cosmo is their code for-.”

    “Kamala! I will murder you.”

    Fear Street one had turned into Fear Street Two, with a promise to catch up on the third with their friends the next day, and as day turned to night, Yelena and Kate had retired to their room. Kate had grown quieter as the evening had progressed. At first, Yelena had thought Kate was simply tired from a day filled with cooking, physio and socialising, as she tucked herself into the blonde’s side and rest her head upon her shoulder.

    The questions stopped, despite Kate’s fingertips still grazing gently against Yelena’s knuckles and the brunette’s eyes glazed over, getting lost somewhere between conscious thought and daydream. The Russian had kissed the top of the younger woman’s head every so often, and brought her hands to her lips once or twice during the final act of the movie. Just small acts but acts that would normally earn Yelena a smile, a squeeze of the hand or even a kiss in return nonetheless. Not that evening however, that evening Kate was quietly lost in thought; arguably one of the least Kate Bishop things of all time. Kate had thoughts of course, great ones, smart ones, insightful ones, but Kate was the kind of person to think something and then say that something, immediately. Patient consideration, or dwelling was not her forte, that was more Yelena’s bag, and the blonde found herself wondering if Kate’s ponderings and her pensive moment from earlier were linked. Kate was hiding something, a thought, a feeling perhaps. A fear? Potentially. They had just survived a pretty bleak time of uncertainty, it would be only natural to worry, and so Yelena asked again, “What are you thinking?” The blonde asked gently as she sat upon the edge of the bed that they now shared. A post tooth brush Kate was fussing with hair in the bathroom mirror. “Just how nice today was. Hanging out like a little family? It’s nice.” “Yes,” Yelena smiled, “I enjoyed it for the most part.”

    “They’re good kids,” Kate added as she hobbled from the bathroom, using every surface she passed as a crutch.

    “Spoken like the wizened old woman that you are,” Yelena grinned, but Kate didn’t smile. She didn’t laugh or roll her eyes. She just persevered until she reached the dresser. Yelena’s brow furrowed. Had she done something wrong? Had she not complimented the food enough? Had she not been helpful enough? Or was it something deeper than that? Was it them? Yelena knew she’d fucked up yesterday but Kate had understood, right? They’d been happy. What if it was worse? What if she’d finally listened to Yelena? “Kate, are you okay?” Yelena tried but failed to keep the concern from her voice. “Yeah, yeah, I’m just tired.” Kate wasn’t looking at her. She didn’t find her eyes in the mirror, she didn’t turn to her, she simply shrugged and peeled off that days t-shirt and bra and replaced it with an oversized Avengers T-shirt. Yelena could see Kate’s eyes in the mirror linger on the badge and the same pensive look marred her features.

    “You know earlier today when you asked me to use my words?”

    “And you didn’t?” Kate’s eyes were on her now, her expressive eyebrows raised to reinforce her point. Kate wasn’t angry, she was just stating fact. Kate had asked about Fury earlier and got nothing but reassurances. Kate was simply returning the favour.

    “Okay,” Yelena said, trying her best not to freak the fuck out, “That is fair.” She exhaled thoughtful, considering her next words. Pushing clearly wouldn’t do. She would have to rely on Kate’s ability to talk. She couldn’t keep other people’s secrets, let alone her own. If Yelena was patient, it would come. Unless it was something catastrophic. Yelena swallowed, hard, and relented. “I just want to make sure you are okay. That is all.” Kindness was the tact and kindness prevailed.

    Kate sighed and leaned heavily against the wall. There was a distance between them, a distance Yelena wasn’t used to. She felt compelled to close the distance but instead she sat, her fingers unconsciously gripping the bedsheets.

    “I just… I just don’t think I can do this any longer.”

    “Oh.” Yelena’s stomach dropped. It was worse. It was so much worse.

    “And I know you’ve worked so hard on yourself to get back here and be here together.” What was happening? What the fuck was happening? Kate was breaking up with her. This was a break-up. A break-up out of nowhere that she should have seen coming. She poisoned her mother, she almost killed her and then after all of it she’d held Kate at arm’s length. She’d left her to heal, alone.

    This couldn’t be happening, but it’s what she deserved. Months of her dragging her feet, months of her vacillating, months of her never truly giving Kate her whole heart. She’d taken too long, Carol was right. She’d taken too long and now it was too late. She was about to lose everything.

    “I think I’m going to be sick.” The words tumbled from her mouth but Kate didn’t hear them. She was too busy with damage control. Trying to placate, trying to explain, but she didn’t need to. Yelena understood. Fuck, how could she have been so selfish? So self-involved? So fucking terrified of loving and losing it all that she lost it all anyways. Yelena needed to do something. She had to do something. She couldn’t lose Kate. Kate was the only person who knew her past, who knew every detail and loved her anyway. How many lives the hands that held her had taken but loved her anyway. How many families she’d shattered. How many hearts she’d broken. But Kate Bishop loved her anyways. Like the sun loved the moon. And much like the moon, Yelena would be nothing without the celestial wonder that was Kate Bishop’s light. She would simply fall back into darkness. Where she belonged. “And I don’t want to ruin that,” Kate continued hurriedly, “But I just don’t think th-.” “I love you!” The panicked words spilled from Yelena’s mouth without thought. “What?” Kate blinked. She was stunned to silence.

    “I-I…,” Yelena spluttered, desperately trying to find the words to explain. She needed Kate to change her mind. She needed to prove that she could be better. That started with using her goddamn words. “I love you,” she said again, her voice shaking. “Please don’t. I know that I’ve taken too long, I know that.” Yelena’s breath was ragged, her chest tight, but she needed to get the words out, she had to help Kate see. “And I know that I’ve done things to you, and I know that... I know that I don’t deserve you, but I love you and I can’t lose you. Please don’t. You are my everything.”

    Yelena’s words flowed. Her eyes shone brightly with unshed tears and her lip shook dangerously. She was fighting to keep it together. Fuck, why was she so fucking soft? Kate blinked once more. Yelena needed her to speak. To open her mouth, to tell her everything was okay. Everything was forgiven. She needed Kate to hold her and kiss her and love her, but instead she just stood there, shocked, but then suddenly everything changed. Her eyes went wide, and a flash of panic struck her beautiful features. Kate closed the distance between her and Yelena quicker than should have ever been possible, hip be damned. Kate fell to her knees in front of Yelena, sat upon the edge of their bed. Her hands clutched her face and her lips pressed themselves fervently against her hot cheek. Yelena didn’t understand. Had she manifested that, was that a thing?

    “Oh no no, Yelena, sweetheart I’m sorry, that’s not what I meant. I didn’t mean….” Lips found hers as Kate desperately tried to undo the hurt that she’d caused. “I don’t mean us, at all. I don’t mean us,” she soothed softly. “I love you. I love you. I’m sorry.” Yelena’s eyes searched Kate’s. They were warm and earnest and beautiful and Yelena wanted nothing more than to spend the rest of her life getting lost in them. She meant it, Kate meant it. She still loved her. She still wanted her. She wasn’t lying.

    Fuck, she felt sick. There was the strong possibility that Yelena was still going to vomit. “I’m so sorry,” Kate whispered tenderly before she placed another lingering kiss upon Yelena’s lips.

    “It’s okay,” Yelena managed with a sniff and the smallest of wry smiles. “I asked you to use your words.”

    Kate took Yelena’s hands in hers and pressed her lips against Yelena’s scarred knuckles. “I meant this,” she explained as she gestured to the room around them and the facility beyond. “All of this. S.H.I.E.L.D. I love the family that I’ve found here and today has been such a wonderful reminder of that.” Kate sniffed sweetly and brought Yelena’s knuckles to her lips. “I don’t know what I would have done without them these last few weeks. And I love the sense of purpose that it’s given me but…” Their eyes met and Yelena was met with the same pensive look she’d spied earlier that day, fully manifested. “I don’t trust them.” “S.H.I.E.L.D.?”

    “Yes,” Kate nodded quietly.

    “Do you trust me?” Yelena asked. Her voice was unsure, timid even. It was a timbre Yelena wasn’t use to, but crippling doubt was a feeling the blonde wasn’t use to either. Kate drew her girlfriend into a crazy hug. “More than anyone, more than anyone. You know that.”

    “Despite me trying to-.”

    “Despite everything,” Kate soothed with complete and unequivocal certainty, and Yelena sunk into her embrace. She wasn’t losing her, but with Carol’s words and Fury’s offer… Yelena had got herself so turned around. Kate did love her, but not only that. Kate wanted to leave. She wanted to leave just like Yelena. Yelena wouldn’t be tearing her away from her family, she wouldn’t be giving Kate an ultimatum, she would be giving her a purpose. A shared purpose.

    Yelena felt the tightness in her chest ease as not only did relief flood her heart and flood her sense, but an insatiable joy and excitement raced through her veins at the thought of opportunity. At the thought of a life together.

    “Then trust me when I say I have it worked out. He is working on something for us. If you want it.”

    Kate released Yelena from her embrace and the blonde was met with questioning eyes. No, not questioning, curious. “Mr Fury?”

    “Yes,” she confirmed with a sniff, “He cannot tell me everything, not yet, he is infuriatingly secretive, but he wants to give me my freedom back. My autonomy for my loyalty.” Yelena took a moment to read Kate’s expression. Her brow was furrowed, she was considering Yelena’s words. “I will give it if you say so.”

    Yelena felt Kate’s hands tighten almost imperceptibly around hers. “Do you trust him?” It was a big question. Perhaps not on the surface, but its implications were huge for the both of them. If Yelena said yes, their lives could change, completely, and Kate had always dreamed of being an Avenger.

    Yelena shrugged because in reality she couldn’t be sure. Not truly sure. Any answer was a risk, but Yelena was known for taking calculated ones. “As much as I can trust any man like him and besides, my sister trusted him. That is good enough for me.”

    Kate chewed her lips adorably and Yelena’s heart melted just a little bit more. “Then give it,” Kate said after a moment more contemplation, “Give him your loyalty, and I’ll give you mine.” She sounded so sure, so confident. As if putting her destiny in the hands of an ex- assassin was the safest and soundest thing to do, and Yelena was so, so thankful for it. Kate Bishop was so astoundingly perfect, and brave and loving and kind and funny and smart and intelligent. She was Yelena’s sun, and Yelena was just a tiny bit of shitty space rock that had been pulled into her orbit by some freak event thirteen point eight billion years ago. And somehow, in Kate’s fierce and irrepressible light that shitty bit of space rock had come to life. It had flourished. And it had found its place in the Universe.

    As small, “Okay,” was all Yelena could manage. A sheepish smile pulled at the corner of her lips and Kate could only grin.

    “Okay,” Kate nodded as the two idiots smiled happily at each other like teenagers over a milkshake at Denny’s.

    They sat for a moment longer, content just to feel each other's company. Both knew how significant this moment was. Yelena had said the words, she’d said them and nothing awful had happened. She hadn’t been struck by lightning and Kate hadn’t jumped out the window. No, in fact Kate had doubled down. Kate had taken Yelena’s love and turned it into something real, something tangible. A new life together. Chosen by them, for them, together. Yelena’s sheepish smile grew wider as a stray thought crossed her mind. “Do you er, do you still want that Cosmo?”

    Kate’s grin faltered for a moment. She couldn’t find the words. “I-I er, I mean…” Kate swallowed awkwardly and Yelena took great pleasure in watching Kate fumble and squirm. “I’m er, pretty sure I could go for one drink.”

    “I was hoping you would say that,” Yelena said softly as she drew Kate to her. Their lips met once, then twice.

    “Really?”

    “Mm hmm. Really,” Yelena mumbled against Kate’s mouth before she ran her tongue deftly across her girlfriend’s lower lip.

    “You got a taste for it?” Kate asked, eyebrow raised, as she broke their kiss and with a lot of physical exertion, made it to her feet just in time for Yelena to throw her down onto the bed in bundle of laughter and kiss.

    Yelena was on her girlfriend instantly, carefully straddling her hips whilst making sure she was bearing all of her own weight. She tutted good-naturedly as she placed her hands either side of Kate’s head and grinned. “Don’t be gross.”

    Kate gasped in complete and utter dismay. “That was your joke!” she protested, poking Yelena in the chest.

    “I don’t recall saying anything of the sort.”

    “Well, that’s convenient,” Kate said sardonically just as Yelena captured her lips roughly and breathed her girlfriend in.

    Kate’s hands were on her in an instant. In her hair, across her scalp, under the hem of her T- shirt, hot against her skin. Her fingernails scratched teasingly up Yelena’s sides and the sensation made the hairs on the back of her neck stand up on end. She shivered instinctively as Kate pulled her T-shirt up and over head, and the cool air of the bedroom hit her skin. The brunette’s warm hands soothed her as they gripped her shoulder blades and explored her strong back. Yelena’s teeth captured Kate’s lower lip. She sucked on it gently at first and teased it with her tongue. Clearly Yelena’s intentions had been felt, wherever Kate felt those kind of intentions, as a moan of longing escaped the young woman and echoed satisfyingly through Yelena’s body.

    To Yelena’s surprise though, Kate’s lips left hers as the brunette’s hands found their way into her unruly blonde hair.

    “Say it again. Please?” Kate asked, utterly breathless. “I wanna hear it again.” Violet eyes met hazel and it was if a switch had been flipped. Yelena found the words so easily, as if they’d been burned into her mind the moment they met on that rooftop months before. She’d just needed to find them to learn they’d be there all along.

    “I love you, Kate Bishop,” she whispered, her breath dancing against her lover’s lips. “I love you more than anything.”

    Chapter End Notes Thank you all for reading and continuing to like and comment. Thank you for sticking with me on this journey. We're almost at the finish line. I love you all. Christmas in July Chapter Notes Okay, so. Here we are. Is this the end? For a little while at least. This final chapter was the third of three that I originally planned, now look at us.

    The final scene you see here has always been endgame. It's fluffy and it's dumb but I'm excited to finally share it with you and what a perfect time of year to do that. This has been one weird and unexpected journey. I've learned a huge amount during this process. I've learned so many invaluable things about asexuality, I've learned that I can finish a fic, and I've learned that maybe, just maybe, I'm going to be able to write that novel in 2023.

    I've loved these characters and I'm not really ready to let them go. I won't lie, I'm feeling pretty sad about it. But thank you for sharing them with me, and coming on this journey. Thank you to every single person who's read or dropped some kudos or left a comment. I've loved responding to your theories and stoking the angst. And thank you to the friends I've made along the way.

    A big separate thank you to my beta, Kristin, who's seen this from start to end. I love you.

    Enjoy everyone and have a very happy holidays.
