Wow this woman was soft. She was getting softer every day, and Kate found it quite delightful. What Kate found even more delightful was the fact that the softness was for her and her only. Sure, she tolerated America, and perhaps even liked Kamala, but this side of her was for Kate, exclusively, and it always would be. Because Yelena trusted her.

    “But you know what?” Yelena continued thoughtfully, “Let’s go home. Just for now. We are already planning to go away and until I can locate the tracker S.H.I.E.L.D. have almost certainly placed on the Jeep, I think it best it stays in New York City.” Kate scrunched her nose in disgust. “Little S.H.I.E.L.D. assholes,” she muttered. She was really starting to hate those dudes. “But you have a point. And… I have really missed Herman’s. There’s just something about Herman’s sausage that-.”

    “Kate,” came Yelena’s chiding tone.

    “What?” Kate protested her innocence. She wasn’t innocent of course, she knew actually what she was doing. “The Italian sausage there is top tier. You can’t deny it.” Yelena's eye roll was tangible, but she smiled happily and admitted defeat with minimal qualms, but only because it was Kate. “You’re right,” she sighed.

    “Of course I’m right.”

    “Herman’s sausage is really tasty, really tasty,” Yelena nodded with what could only be taken as genuine enthusiasm and Kate grinned with glee and stamped her feet happily, as she couldn’t clap her hands together.

    “Thank you. That’s all I wanted to hear,” Kate beamed. “Can I kiss you right now?” “No,” Yelena said matter-of-factly. “I’m driving.”

    “It’ll be real quick.”

    “Nope.”

    “But you told me you’d driven an articulated truck own a highway in Belgrade during a snowstorm. If you can do that then you can definitely kiss me.”

    “No,” Yelena said more firmly, “Kate, you can kiss me all you want once we’re home, but let’s jus-.” But it was too late. Kate’s lips were already on hers. Kate had heaved herself out from under the weight of her holdall, captured Yelena’s face and pulled it towards hers. Suddenly the Jeep lurched forward. Kate’s heart was in her mouth as she felt the momentum of the Jeep take her away from Yelena’s lips and sent her sprawling into the Russian’s lap. “Oh my god. Oh my god, what happened? Is everything okay?” Kate’s heart raced as she tried to push herself up and out of Yelena’s lap, with quite some difficulty. “Everything is fine.” Yelena explained, surprisingly calmly. “The dogs are fine, your luggage is fine. You are fine.”

    “You tapped the brake, didn’t you?” Kate said, as realisation hit. Yelena had said no and she’d meant it.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded stoically.

    “And I freaked out, didn’t I?”

    “That also.”

    “Dick,” Kate grumbled as she hauled herself back into her seat and under her holdall. “I prefer 'Italian sausage', spasiba .”

    Between the two of them, it only took two trips to get all their luggage, and their dogs, up the stairs of their apartment building. Kate dug deep into her jean pocket, rummaging for her keys, as Yelena cut an unusually apprehensive figure next to her. Her girlfriend was nervous, plenty nervous, and of course, Kate knew why. This was the first time they’d been back together, back where it all went wrong after Kate’s birthday. Back to broken glass, chairs, tables. Back to walls with more arrow holes than they had before. Back to bad memories, but home to so many more good ones too.

    Kate knew that Yelena had been back to the apartment since, knew she’d replaced the broken dishes and cleaned up Kate’s own blood. She knew because they’d picked out new plates together on the IKEA website, Yelena had insisted on IKEA, naturally. And she knew because Yelena couldn’t stop washing her hands for days after. The blonde would joke that just like Kate, her blood was being particularly stubborn, when in fact all that she was trying to wash away was her guilt. Guilt she needn’t feel in the first place, but try telling Yelena that over, and over.

    “We can get a hotel for the night if you prefer, or go to the penthouse,” Kate offered gently. “No. No, no.” Yelena shook her head dismissively. She was trying to play it cool, and although she was queen bullshitter, when it came to her actual, real-life emotions, she wasn’t that great at masking, not with Kate around. “I’m okay,” she lied, “Just a little…” Yelena took a breath and then exhaled slowly and resolutely. “I’m okay.”

    “It’s okay to be nervous,” Kate soothed as she abandoned her search for her keys and reached for Yelena. “And if we get in there and it brings back bad memories we can come straight back out again. We can go somewhere fancy with a spa and a boujie restaurant.” Kate pulled Yelena close and the blonde folded easily into her embrace. She placed the gentlest of kisses upon the top of her scraped-back blonde hair. “But…” Kate continued, a little more optimistically, “I have a feeling that it’s going to be okay. We got this.” Yelena took a moment’s more comfort in Kate’s arms and then drew back, nodding with resolve. “You’re right. You’re right.” She smiled sheepishly and placed a cool set of keys in Kate’s hands. Of course, she had them all along.

    With a small nod towards the apartment and a final squeeze of Kate’s hand, Yelena signalled for the brunette to open the door, and so, she did.

    The sun had just set and the apartment was strewn in the darkest of summer orange hues. Light came at premium in New York City anyways, and a first floor apartment certainly wasn’t afforded much, so Kate reached for the light switch. In that moment, the room burst into colour.

    Trails of multi-coloured fairy-lights spring to life. There must have been miles of them in the apartment, running over doors, around appliances, across walls. They framed pictures and mirrors and bookshelves and glowed brightly and boldly into the darkness. A tree, a real life Christmas tree stood at the centre of the apartment, lit to the rafters and adorned with all sorts of traditional and not so traditional ornaments. Garlands of pine decorated surfaces, with generous wrappings of red ribbon and Russian ornaments decked shelves and the halls. The apartment was completely aglow. It was unexpected, it was spectacular and it was truly breathtaking.

    “Holy shit,” were the only words that Kate could muster. It was simply so beautiful, and so thoughtful and so…unexpected.

    The dogs’ paws click/clacked around the apartment as they took in new and yet familiar sights and smells. “This is incredible,” Kate said in disbelief.

    Her feet carried her further into the apartment as Yelena stood expectantly by the door. Kate wanted to take in every decoration, every thought, every attention to detail. A beautifully decorated Hanukkiyah sat on the coffee table next to a pair of festive hand- painted nesting dolls. On the fridge the were at least half a dozen snow globe magnets, all from places the two of them had visited together in the last year, whether it be on a mission or for personal matters. There were even stockings with their names on, all their names on, hung in alphabetical order along the handrail that led up to their bedroom. Fanny, Kate, Lucky and Yelena. And a slice of honey cake and a glass of vodka was perched upon the window sill for Santa. The window sill through which Yelena had gained entry into the apartment a year and a half before.

    The apartment was glowing, with love and warmth and spirit. Kate was pretty sure that in that moment, she and the apartment were one and the same. Sure, it was July, but by Odin did it feel like Christmas.

    “You did this?” The brunette asked as she caught Yelena watching her closely from her spot by the apartment door. Yelena nodded and Kate detected just a hint of smugness in her girlfriend’s demeanour.

    “Yes, I did.” Yelena nodded and her small, knowing smile broadened, for Yelena Belova looked truly happy. Completely and utterly. “Happy anniversary.”

    Wow that was romantic. Or would have been if it hadn’t sent Kate reeling. What anniversary? There was an anniversary? Had she missed it? She didn’t miss stuff like this. She was a planner when it came to gifts and occasions. She’d toil over every detail of a gift, of the surprise. She was sure she had their anniversary marked in her diary, in heavy marker, the same day as Yelena’s birthday. How had she been outwitted?

    “Wha-I. Have I missed a thing?” Kate blinked, trying to do the math but coming unstuck. Yelena beamed as she stepped deeper into the apartment to close the distance between herself and Kate. She was pleased with herself, so pleased with herself, it was unbecoming, but also incredibly cute. Kate didn’t think she’d seen Yelena smile this widely since, well, since the night of her birthday. Kate hadn’t realised how much she’d missed it. Her heart felt hot and tight and happy and it only grew happy as Yelena’s strong hands found her waist and pulled her close with a fierce grip.

    “A year ago today, we finally got that ‘Christmas Eve’ drink,” Yelena explained as her hazel eyes danced brightly against the galaxy of fairy lights that adorned every corner of Kate's apartment, “I’m pretty sure that counts.”

    “ I’m pretty sure you told me it wasn’t a date,” Kate countered, perplexed. She one hundred percent said that. Yelena had said that it wasn’t a date, that she didn’t date, so it wasn’t a date. Kate was right, Yelena was wrong.

    Yelena tsked softly and pulled Kate closer, arms looping around her waist. “I said no such thing,” she purred softly and Kate wanted to fold in on herself. Lies just sounded so beautiful when they came out of Yelena Belova’s mouth. “And besides,” the blonde shrugged matter- of-factly, “it was a date to me.”

    Kate had words, she could have sworn she did, but every single one of those words thought it best to elude her in that moment. It was a date to her. She said it so earnestly, so honestly. This wasn’t some Yelena Belova teasing bullshit from earlier in the day, this was her real, honest truth, which must have meant that-

    “When you came back to New York…”

    “I came for you, yes.” Yelena nodded with a smile and searched Kate’s eyes. She knew she’d stunned her, knew she’d blown her away, but wasn’t that the whole point? With the lights, and tree and the fucking stockings? There were stockings, with their names on, IN JULY. “I hoped that maybe…I didn’t really know at the time, I just-.” Yelena’s eyes left Kate’s for a moment as she paused to steady herself and take a breath. She wanted to find the right words, all this work to make this moment perfect, Yelena wanted the words to be perfect too, and once their eyes met again, Yelena continued. “I just knew that I couldn’t get you out of my head. I’d spent years not letting anyone get close and just like that, I felt connected to you in a way that I couldn’t explain. I had never felt that before. And I have to admit I spent quite a few months denying it but…” The blonde exhaled heavily. The weight was lifting, everything was lifting. This was Yelena finally and forever nailing her colours to Kate’s mast. She smiled up at Kate, eyes dancing and sun-kissed cheeks all aglow, and in that moment, she really did take Kate’s breath away.

    “I guess I just couldn’t stay away from you. It’s actually a little creepy when you think about it.” Yelena laughed, a small, self-deprecating laugh that made Kate’s stomach tie itself in knots. “I think I’ve always been in love with you.” Yelena said the words quietly, almost contemplatively, as if it were the first time she’d ever even admitted them to herself. "It just took me a long time to realise that wasn’t a death sentence for you.”

    Kate smiled affectionately. Trust Yelena Belova to take some of the most wonderful and revealing words she’d ever spoken and follow them with a joke about self-loathing and death. Kate found it desperately adorable, but was also in desperate need of a therapist. “Cheery,” the brunette quipped.

    Yelena glanced appraisingly around the abundantly lit room. “I thought so,” she deadpanned with the smallest of smiles as Kate grazed her knuckles greedily up and down Yelena’s forearms. Soon she would expand her area of exploration to take in Yelena’s biceps and shoulders.

    "Still the best shot I never took, though. I stick by that,” Kate assured her as Yelena’s finger- tips dipped beneath the hem of the brunette’s T-shirt.

    “I should hope so. I mean, I would have caught it whatever ,but-”

    “From that range? Absolutely no way.”

    “-the sentiment still stands.” Yelena said nonchalantly, knowing, of course, that it would drive Kate absolutely mad.

    “You’re insufferable.” Kate huffed, which only meant Yelena pulled her even closer. The blonde shrugged with an all too familiar smugness. “And yet you suffer me." “I mean, who wouldn’t? Look at you, look at this?” Kate tore her hands away from Yelena’s very lovely arms and gestured wildly at her apartment that was lit up like Rockefeller. She was pretty sure that if she asked Carol to go have a little look for her, the woman would spot the place from Space.

    “But, oh,” Yelena grinned excitedly, as she grabbed Kate’s hands and dragged her in the direction of the kitchen, “there is more.”

    “Really?” Kate asked with honest disbelief. How could there be more than this? “Herman’s is already ordered, there is pretty much frozen everything in the freezer,” Yelena threw the freezer door open to highlight her point “And I got us the new Scream movie to watch.”

    “You did not. It’s not even out yet.” There was no way. Yelena was bad with technology at the best of times, unless it was designed to sabotage.

    “If I can get a rocket launcher on the black market,” she explained, “I can get Scream, okay?”

    Kate blinked. “You bought a what on the black market?”

    “Aannd I got you something,” Yelena revealed excitedly.

    “Wait, wait, wait, so let me get this straight. You’ve done the most romantic thing anyone’s ever done for me, for this...surprise anniversary, and I’ve got you shit? Is that what we’re saying.”

    Yelena frowned her customary frown and shrugged easily. “Well, it was a surprise.” This was all so wonderful and amazing and generous, and that was all Yelena had ever been since she’d come home from LA, but what the fuck was Kate doing? Where were Yelena’s anniversary gifts and surprises? All that good shit? She’d dropped the ball, majorly. Even if she didn’t think today was their Anniversary, a year of Yelena being back was a big deal, and she’d missed it. Kate sighed heavily. “I just feel-”

    “Don’t feel,” Yelena cut in softly, pulling Kate close once more and searching for her eyes, “Don’t feel, just enjoy, okay? You deserve this. Without you, I…” Again Yelena paused to find the words. Her mind strayed into darkness just for a moment, perhaps thinking of a life without Kate, of what might have been if they hadn’t met up on that rooftop that night. If Valentina hadn’t sent her on that bullshit mission with phoney information. And then her face lightened again. Kate felt Yelena’s fingers cling imperceptibly tighter around her waist as the blonde smiled up at her. “You give me so much...? You give me so much.” “Well,” Kate said, a little in awe and a lot in love, “you changed my life.” Yelena smiled happily. “And you saved mine,” she whispered, and Kate’s heart caught in her throat. “On that rooftop, you saved me. I was so angry. I had been so angry for so long and I thought that killing Clint Barton would make me feel...I guess, I thought it would make me feel. But instead, you did that.”

    Goodness did Kate want to kiss her in that moment. Kiss her and hold her and breathe her in. Breathe in her honesty and her vulnerability, her beauty. She just needed it to be a part of her. But instead, she settled for a few simple words of affirmation. “I don’t think you give yourself enough credit. People don’t change if they don’t want to.”

    Hazel eyes pierced Kate’s. Yelena was working over something in her mind, Kate could practically see it; thoughts tugging her one way and then the other. A moment later and it seemed as though her thoughts had settled, or she had at least found resolve. The blonde released Kate for a moment and dug deep within her left jean pocket. “Speaking of change…” she chimed as she produced a small ring box from her pocket and held it out toward Kate, “I er...that something that I got you.”

    Wait, what? It was a ring box. A RING BOX. Surely not. No, that was just Kate’s mind running away with itself. That, on top of the decorations and the cocktails, the movie and the pizza, no, that was too much. And sure, Yelena had loved her from the moment she’d met her but marriage still seemed a little way off, especially as both of them definitely told each other they weren’t that into the idea. Although, Yelena had just outed herself as a big ol’ liar when it came to the love and dating department so who knew what was true anymore? But it was just a ring box, right? She wasn’t getting down on one knee, although her busted knee was still a little dodgy so maybe...No, Kate! No maybes. No marriage, no babies. Although the idea of Yelena tearing through the apartment with a miniature version of herself was admittedly, an endearing one, but that was a conversation for another year. Or decade. “I know this place is home and it was your dad’s and I don’t want to push you into anything you do not want to do but...,” Yelena exhaled heavily before she summoned the courage and opened the box. To Kate’s surprise, there was no ring inside. No ring at all. Instead, lay a small, silver key. “Will you move in with me?” her girlfriend asked nervously, eyes wide and brow furrowed Kate let out an anxious breath she hadn’t realised she’d been holding. “Honey, I hate to break it to you, but we’ve been living together for nearly a year.”

    “No, sorry, I-.” Yelena pinched the bridge of her nose with frustration. “I am not doing this right.” The blonde huffed with exasperation, gathered herself, and tried once more as she held the ring box out in front of her. “Kate Bishop, will you move to LA with me? A new life, a new home, away from S.H.I.E.L.D.”

    The brunette’s stomach fell through the floor into the pizza place below. LA? Together? Her heart skipped t beat just at the idea of it. Them, together, a new thing that was theirs. Together.

    “Working for Fury?” Kate asked.

    “Yes,” Yelena nodded enthusiastically. She’d clearly had this in the works for quite some time. “The place I stayed in LA, it was his. A new complex under his jurisdiction. A new place for people like us but also for people like Kamala and America. A protected place.” Yelena recaptured Kate’s hand and squeezed it tight. “It’s beautiful there, I promise. It’s right by the ocean and there’d be so much space for the dogs. I love this apartment, I do, it’s the first place I’ve ever settled, the first place that’s felt like home, but it’s a little small for a family of four,” Yelena pointed, she was not wrong. “And it’s probably bugged to hell.” She was not wrong about that either.

    “I have to say, LA does sound pretty lush.” It sounded more than lush, Kate would happily admit.

    “Right? It’s warm all the time, and my daddy says vitamin D is really good for you. Oh!” Yelena exclaimed with unbridled exuberance and Kate wanted nothing more than to wrap her arms around her and press kisses on her cheeks and run her fingers through her hair. "If we wanted snow we could go home, stay back here, or go see Baka, or go wherever we wanted.” The blonde was like a kid in a candy store who'd suddenly realised that it was a place of infinite possibility.

    “I think I’d prefer a little break from snow, for a couple more months at least if that’s okay?” Kate suggested softly, and immediately Yelena cringed.

    “Right, of course. We totally do not have to do snow any time soon. Consider snow completely off the menu.” Yep, she was too cute. Kisses on cheeks and fingers in hair would be happening. As soon as realistically possible. Kate closed the distance between them and took Yelena’s hands, and the ring box, within her own. She gazed down into hazel eyes and found everything she could possibly want there.

    “Sun sounds good,” she whispered and Yelena’s eyes came alive, searching hers for absolute confirmation.

    “R-really?” she stuttered.

    “Yeah, really,” Kate beamed, “Have you seen me. I’m practically translucent.” “And very beautiful,” Yelena said a little breathlessly. Kate was on the verge of saying yes. Yes to something she’d clearly been sat on for goodness know how long. Something she’d been plotting and planning and hoping. The ex-assassin seemed practically giddy. “You will love it. It’s huge and modern and private, until we invite America and Kamala of course. But still, it’s big enough to get lost in.”

    “And,” Kate cut in as she pulled Yelena close, “We’ll finally be able to watch that sunset together.”

    Yelena fell still. “You remembered?”

    Some of the worst and best phone calls of her life? Of course, she’d remembered. How much she’d wanted to be with Yelena in those moments. How much she’d felt out of control and if she could have been there with her, she could have made her see. She could have made everything alright. But it wasn’t the right time. If anything, things could have fallen apart further. But now, now it felt more right than anything.

    “So, it’s a ‘yes’?” Yelena asked, hopeful eyes watching her closely.

    “Yelena,” Kate spoke softly, and dug her fingers into her hips to make sure she heard her, “Of course it’s a yes. Home is wherever you are. Nowhere else will do.”

    Within moments the ring box lay forgotten on the kitchen counter as Yelena drew Kate’s lips to hers. It was romantic and desperate and so full of possibility, much like their very first kiss upon the same spot ten months earlier. Yelena’s finger-tips ran tantalisingly through her hair and brushed delicately at the soft skin that lay beneath the hem of the shirt. Kate couldn’t help but laugh happily against her girlfriend’s lips. Yes, so full of possibility. After spending several minutes pressed up against the fridge-freezer Kate decided that some cocktails were in order. With a devilish grin, Yelena happily acquiesced, and delved inside the rusting contraption for a couple of frozen melon margaritas that were enthusiastically consumed in front of the TV. Kate gasped and screamed at every jump scare and found her way further into Yelena’s arms as the movie went on. Yelena would tease her for being a coward, lay the softest of kisses atop her head and then laugh with sheer delight as yet another unsuspecting loser met a rather grisly end. This was the woman she loved, ladies and gentlemen, the woman she wanted to spend the rest of her life with, the mother of her dogs that were curled up contentedly at their feet. Yes, she may have offered Ghostface feedback after every kill, and yes, she admitted several times during the movie to having ‘done that, oh and that’ which made her a certified psycho, but she was Kate’s psycho and she was hot, so it was fine.

    “I’ll be honest,” Kate confessed, as shifted in Yelena’s embrace and took another sip of frozen margarita, “Eating and drinking too much and falling asleep much earlier than anticipated, it really does feel like Christmas in July.”

    “Well,” Yelena mused as her finger-tips ghosted circles across Kate’s shoulder blades, “maybe we should do this every year.”

    Kate ‘hummed’ contentedly at the idea. “Maybe we should,” she smiled as Yelena leaned down to press a lingering kiss upon Kate’s lips. “I love you” The brunette whispered and Yelena gladly returned the sentiment.

    “Christmas in LA though...” Yelena whispered, smile wide and eyes dancing with possibility, “How does that sound?”

    “You know what?” Kate spoke against her girlfriend’s lips, “That sounds pretty perfect.” “Good,” Yelena said softly and Kate could feel it. She could feel the significance of that moment. She could feel it in her chest, and in the pit of her stomach. She could feel the potential of it. They’d come so far in a year, how much further could they go? They’d grown together, learned from each other. They’d stopped each other from falling apart and helped put each other back together again. Yelena had learned to allow herself to be saved and Kate had learned that she could do the saving.

    “Merry Christmas, darling,” Yelena whispered and Kate knew that she would never get tired of hearing Yelena say that word. Not ever. It wasn’t possible.

    Kate couldn’t help but laugh at the silliness of it all, surrounded by lights and trees and dogs and love. It was mad. If you had told Kate Bishop a year ago that Yelena Belova would have gone to these lengths for her, she would have never believed you. She would have chewed your hand off, sure, but she would never in a billion years have thought she’d be sat in Yelena’s arms celebrating their ‘one year anniversary’. It felt so…so normal. So ‘what everybody else has but they could never’. That was what made it so beautiful she guessed. It was a one in a million chance that they’d met on that rooftop. That their lives would be thrown together in such a way. That they connected the way they did. So instantaneously, so undeniably. But in that moment Kate had known one thing. Not that they would fall for each other. Nor that they would move in or become dog moms or discover they had the same taste in frozen cocktails. But Kate knew that Yelena would teach her how to survive, and Kate would teach Yelena how to live. And so they would. Live. Together.

    “Merry Christmas, Yelena,” Kate said softly, “And here's to a very Happy New Year.” fin.
